개초딩 카드 (비하적인 표현 아님) 을 만들어서 초등학생들의 손목을 비틀고 돈을 뺏어서 더 강한 스티커를 덕지덕지 붙여 기가OP 카드들을 만들어 가는 게임.

My Card Is Better Than Your Card! 는 (약간의 날조를 추가하자면) 게임의 제목 그대로 막강한 카드들을 만들어서 상대방의 카드들보다 내 카드가 더 쩔다는 것을 자랑한 뒤 어린 아이들의 용돈을 빼앗아 스티커를 구매하는 덱빌딩 로그라이크 게임이다. 대부분의 덱빌딩 게임들이 우중충한 테마를 지니거나, 배경 자체는 밝은데 스토리를 보면 특정 존재의 타락이나 망해가는 세상을 다루고 있어서 절대 평화로운 세계관을 지니지 않는다는 걸 생각하면, 이 게임의 경우 초등학생들이 스티커 모아서 서로 귀여운 카드들을 만들고 자랑하는 걸 주요 게임플레이 루프로 삼았으며, 게임 오버를 당한다고 끔찍한 죽음을 맞이하는 게 아니라 그냥 게임 오버 당하고 주인공이 슬퍼하는 게 전부라 아기자기하고 잔잔한 힐링 게임을 플레이하는 듯한 느낌을 준다. 게임 엔딩에 나오는 최종 보스의 경우도, 다른 덱빌딩 게임들은 세상을 멸망시키려고 하거나 주인공을 죽이려 하는 위압감 넘치는 보스들이 나오는데, 여기서는 초등학생들이 나름 강한 카드들을 쓰기는 하지만 전반적으로는 귀여운 스티커를 붙이면서 자랑하는 WWE를 하고 있는데, 그 와중 덱빌딩 게임에 진심인 아이가 나와서 "흠 .... 당신들의 덱은 너무 약하군요 .... " 라는 대사를 치는 혼모노가 UFC를 거는 걸 주인공이 더 강한 개초딩 카드로 이기는 내용이 최종 보스전에 나와서, 게임의 분위기를 암울하게 만들지 않음과 동시에 플레이어들이 "왠지 저 초등학생이 하는 말이 맞는 거 같은데 .... ?" 라는 내면의 반성을 하게 되는 개그스러운 장면으로 끝나는 게 마음에 들었다. 그렇다고 이 게임이 그냥 아기자기하고 쉬운 카드 게임이냐? 라고 하면 긍정적인 답변을 남기는 게 좀 애매한 게, 의외로 초등학생들이 만들어 오는 카드들이 너무 강해서 대충 잡덱을 만들고 덤비면 무자비하게 패배하기 때문이다. 쉬움 난이도에서는 그렇게 사기 카드를 안 만들어도 되지만, 보통 난이도 3주차부터, 그리고 어려움 난이도 2주차부터는 초등학생들이 카드 부스터 팩에 얼마나 현질을 많이 했는지, 덱을 아주 방향성과 시너지가 가득한 버전으로 업그레이드해서 싸우기 때문에, "왜 주인공은 저렇게 현질을 안하는 거야?!" 라고 게임의 구조에 대한 현실적인 불만이 들 수도 있다. 물론 플레이어는 게임 내 모든 컨셉의 스티커를 사용한다는 나름 파격적인 차별점이 있기는 하지만, 반대로 말하면 이 때문에 특정 키워드 중심으로 덱을 쌓아 올려 가고 있다면 다른 스티커들로 인해 풀이 희석되어 자신이 원하는 스티커를 가져 갈 가능성이 낮다는 단점이 있어서, 이러한 특징이 플레이어에게 항상 유리하지는 않다.

하지만 게임의 난이도는 여기까지 이야기하고, 이 게임의 가장 큰 특징은 바로 가볍게 언급한 스티커 시스템이다. 수많은 덱빌딩 게임들이 효과와 코스트가 고정되어 있는 카드들을 쓰는 데 비해, 이 게임은 비어 있는 카드 위 스티커를 붙여서 커스텀 카드를 만드는 게 주요 메커니즘으로 나온다. 물론, 스티커 1개당 1개의 사탕 (마나 / 코스트의 개념이라 생각하면 편하다) 값어치가 들기 때문에, 아무 생각 없이 스티커를 다닥다닥 하나의 카드에 붙이면 사탕이 부족해서 카드를 낼 수 없을 것이다. 간단한 예시를 들자면, 기본 스티커 중 "별" 스티커는 "1개의 별 (데미지의 개념이라 생각하면 편하다) 을 얻습니다" 의 효과를 지니고, 이 스티커를 하나 붙인 카드를 내면 "1코스트 - 이 카드는 1데미지를 줍니다" 카드가 되는 것이다. "별" 스티커 2개가 붙은 카드를 내면 "2코스트 - 이 카드는 2데미지를 줍니다" 카드가 되는 것이고 말이다. 여기까지만 보면 별로 특별해 보이지는 않을 수 있는데, 게임 내 스티커의 종류가 의외로 많다는 점 및 같은 종류의 키워드를 공유하는 것끼리 붙여서 일명 OP 카드들을 여러 개 생산할 수 있다는 걸 알게 되면 그 뒤로 한 장에 400데미지 이상은 기본으로 뽑아내는 카드들을 만들어 놀이터의 초등학생들 손목을 비트는 재미를 맛볼 수 있다. 가장 쉬운 사기카드 예시를 들자면, 게임 내 "벌레" 라는 자원을 이용해 카드를 뽑거나 이를 사탕으로 바꿔먹는 스티커들이 존재하는데, 벌레 생산 + 벌레 수만큼 에너지 획득 + 벌레 수만큼 카드 뽑기 스티커 3개를 합치면 "3코스트 - 벌레 4개를 획득합니다 + 벌레의 개수만큼 사탕을 얻습니다 + 벌레 2개를 잃고 카드 2장을 뽑습니다" 가 되며, 실질적으로는 벌레 자원 2개 + 1마나 + 카드 2장 드로우라는, 욕망의 항아리가 보고 경악할 만한 카드를 스티커 운만 붙으면 대량으로 생산할 수 있다. 또한, 스티커를 이용한 개사기 카드를 만드는 과정에서 각 스티커의 효과 위치 조절을 통해 자연스레 각각의 스티커 활용법에 대해 이해할 수 있고, 몇몇 NPC 들이 쓰는 스티커 콤보를 통해서도 게임에 대해 간접적으로 배워 나갈 수 있다. 예시를 들자면, 위에서 말한 벌레 스티커에서 벌레를 획득하는 스티커를 맨 뒤에 놓는다면, 벌레가 없다면 아무것도 못하는 깡통 카드가 될 것이다. 이처럼 카드 위 어떤 스티커를 배치할 것인지, 그리고 어떤 스티커 효과를 어느 위치에 놓을 것인가를 이해하는 과정 속에서 게임의 다양한 키워드와 콤보에 대해 자연스레 배워갈 수 있다. 그래서 그런가, 게임의 첫 인상은 "의외로 게임이 깊이가 있는데?" 였다. 덱빌딩 게임이라고 광고하지만 실제로는 오토배틀러 장르에 더 가까운 게임이었던 와일드프로스트와는 완전 다른 첫인상이었는데, 비주얼이나 사운드 면에서는 뭔가 유치해 보여서 아동용 게임인 줄 알았음 + 그런데 실제로 게임을 하다 보면 얻을 수 있는 스티커의 개수가 많으며, 여러 장의 카드들을 만들어 나갈 수 있음 + 플레이어가 어떤 덱과 대결할지 정할 수 있고, 이로 인해 불리한 덱은 피해 갈 수 있음 3박자 때문에, 테마 면에서 호불호가 갈릴 수 있어도 게임이 과하게 부조리하거나 덱빌딩 면모가 밍밍하다는 생각은 전혀 들지 않았다. 물론 초반에 상대방이 어떤 덱을 쓰는지 모를 때는 불리한 덱을 고르고 억까를 당할 수 있기는 한데, 몇 판만 하다보면 어떤 부류의 덱을 쓰는지 알 수 있기에 이에 대한 과도한 스트레스를 받지는 않았다.

게임의 신선한 덱빌딩 시스템 (정해진 카드를 사용하는 게 아니라 직접 카드를 만들어 가는 재미 + OP 카드들을 만드는 데 실질적인 제약이 없어서 스티커만 잘 뽑는다면 아무리 사기 쳐도 말리지 않음) 이 굉장히 인상적이었고, 게임의 난이도가 생각보다 쉽지 않으며 상대방을 견제하는 요소도 어느 정도 생각해야 한다는 것 때문에 아득바득 개사기 카드를 만들고 뽑아서 역전하는 맛도 있었다. 다만, 아직 게임이 얼리 엑세스라 그런가, 완벽한 게임이라고 하기에는 부족한 면모들이 있었다. 이후 업데이트에서 개선해 나갔으면 좋을 점들에 대해 적어 보자면: 

> 게임 내 컨텐츠의 분량이 아쉽다. 이벤트의 개수나 게임플레이 루프의 구조는 이미 완성된 게임처럼 나와서 정식 출시된 게임이라고 해도 믿을 정도이긴 하지만, 게임 내 전투의 다양성이 아쉽고 - 정확히 말하면, 일반 전투는 얼엑 치고는 그나마 다양성이 어느 정도 있는 편인데, 보스 전투가 고정되어 있어서 계속 같은 보스를 싸우는 게 즐거운 경험은 아니었다 - 스티커의 개수 또한 더 많았으면 좋겠다는 생각이 들었다. 스티커의 경우 밑에서 더 이야기 하겠지만, 전투의 경우 더 많은 상대를 게임에 추가한다고 보장했으니 이후 추가되는 보스들도 지금 보스들처럼 개성이 있었으면 한다.

> 스티커 종류의 경우, 객관적으로 봤을 때 약 200종류가 존재하기에 절대로 적은 편은 아닌데, 전체적으로 보자면 두 가지 면에서 스티커 시스템이 아쉬웠다. 첫 번째의 경우, 게임 내 키워드 / 대체 자원 당 확실한 "종결 카드" - 슬레이 더 스파이어로 치면 독을 2배 만드는 촉매 카드나, 독의 양만큼 폭발해서 광역 데미지로 바꾸는 시체 폭발 같은 카드 말이다 - 가 거의 없어서, 키워드에 의존하는 덱의 경우 모래성을 만들듯이 매 판이 천천히 빌드업 해 나가면서 정직하게 자원을 점수로 전환해서 벌어야 한다는 게 아쉬웠다. 물고기 덱이나 음악 덱의 경우는 승리 플랜이 꽤 명확하기는 한데 (물고기 덱의 경우 낚시로 100마리 넘는 물고기들을 점수로 일정량 바꿔먹을 수도 있고, 음악 덱의 경우 음표 키워드를 사용하기는 하지만 일시적으로 음표를 많이 만들어 점수와 카드 드로우로 바꿔 먹는 어그로성 덱이라 키워드 의존도가 크지 않다) 벌레 덱이나 판타지 덱 같은 건 점수 쌓는 속도가 그리 빠르지 않고 열심히 쌓은 자원이 날아가 버리면 복구하는 과정이 그리 쉽지 않다. 두 번째로는, 매 판마다 모든 스티커를 사용할 수 있다는 점 때문에 (다른 덱빌더 게임들과 달리 직업이라는 컨셉이 존재하지 않기 때문에) 더 많은 스티커를 추가하면 할수록 스티커 풀이 희석되어서 자신의 덱 컨셉에 맞는 스티커를 뽑는 게 힘들다는 것이다. 게임 내 시작 덱마다 처음으로 받는 스티커들이 다르기는 하지만, 막상 게임 내 얻을 수 있는 스티커의 풀이 모든 판마다 똑같아서, 다른 컨셉 관련 카드들을 많이 받지 않는 이상 양발 걸치기를 할 수 없기에 일명 쓰레기 스티커만 받게 되는 판들도 많다는 게 아쉬웠다. 개인적으로 StarVaders 가 이에 대해 잘 대응했다고 생각했는데, 중립 카드들이 매우 많지만 모든 중립 카드들을 5장씩 컨셉에 맞는 팩에 나누어서, 매 판마다 3개의 팩을 뽑아 그 중립 카드들만 이번 판에 나올 수 있게 하였다. 이와 똑같은 시스템을 도입하라는 건 아니지만, 만약 더 많은 스티커를 게임 내 넣고 싶다면 플레이어가 자신의 시작 컨셉에 맞는 스티커들을 뽑을 수 있는 가능성을 늘려야지 다양한 덱으로 플레이어가 게임을 깨는 재미를 느낄 것이다.

> 게임 내 카드를 추가하는 순간들이 너무 많다. 하루가 끝날 때마다 빈 카드 1장을 덱에 추가하는데, 한 판 기준 게임 내 시간으로 15일 동안 게임이 진행되기에 실질적으로 14장의 빈 카드들을 추가하는 것이다. 다른 덱빌딩 게임이라면 14장의 카드를 추가하는 게 페널티까지라고 생각되지는 않지만, 이 게임에서는 이미 덱이 완성되었는데 카드를 억지로 소매넣기 당하는 상황이 너무 많다. 물론 빈 카드들을 전략적으로 사용할 수는 있지만, 많아봤자 1 ~ 2 장 정도만 덱에 있으면 되어서 덱 안에 수많은 빈 카드들이 존재하는 상황이 그렇게 기분 좋은 경험은 아니었다. 덱 압축의 기회도 그리 많지 않은데, 이벤트 중 카드 제거 기회를 노리거나 재활용 센터를 방문하는 두 가지 경우밖에 없는데, 두 경우 모두 등장 확률이 희귀하다. 이 때문에 덱 압축 기회가 한 번도 없었다면 최종 보스와 거의 덱 카드 개수가 최대 10장 차이나게 되며, 당연하지만 최종 보스는 개사기 덱을 들고 오는데 플레이어는 그렇지 않다면 덱빌딩 혼모노에게 탈탈 털리게 된다. 차라리 게임 내 3주차부터는 카드를 덱에 추가하지 않는 식으로 업데이트하여, 한 판에 10장만 빈 카드를 추가하는 식으로 만들어 둔다면 덱 압축이 덜 나와도 덱이 꼬이지 않을 것이다.

> 몇몇 덱들은 너무 약하고, 반대로 특정 스티커는 너무 강하다. 
1. "판타지" 덱의 컨셉은 퀘스트를 완료해서 보석을 쌓는 컨셉이 주인데, 보석은 1개마다 별 1개를 주므로 많이 쌓으면 점수가 자동으로 쌓이게 된다. 이 덱의 문제점은 보석을 쌓는 속도가 너무 느리며, 이 때문에 토큰 제거 카드들에게 너무 취약하다는 것이다. 비슷하게 토큰을 사용하는 벌레나 물고기의 경우 토큰을 쌓는 속도 및 점수 전환률이 효율적인 카드들이 존재하는데, 판타지 덱은 정직하게 보석 한땀한땀 쌓아가며 점수를 따는 덱이라 박탈감이 너무 크게 느껴진다. 그나마 앵무새 스티커로 퀘스트 반복을 노린다면 보석을 쌓는 속도가 빨라지는데, 만약 퀘스트를 반복시킬 수 있는 스티커를 못 뽑으면 당장 컨셉을 전환해야 할 정도이다.
2. "공룡" 덱의 컨셉은 패 안에 공룡 알 스티커를 들고 있다가 이들이 깨어나면 강한 효과를 볼 수 있다는 컨셉인데, 공룡 알이 깨어나는 데 최소 3턴이 걸리다 보니 어려움 난이도로 이 덱을 하면 첫 판에 바로 패배할 수도 있다. 게다가 여기서 깨어난 공룡 또한 높은 점수를 주지 않는데, 대부분의 공룡이 유틸에 치중되어 있고 (상대방 사탕 3개 뺏어오기, 방어도 10 획득 등등) 점수를 주는 공룡은 1코 5데미지 (3턴 후 부화) 또는 1코 10데미지 (4턴 후 부화) 밖에 없어서 공룡이 깨어나도 점수 역전을 하는 데 많은 턴이 소모된다. 컨셉 자체를 갈아엎고 싶지 않으면 알이 깨어나는 턴을 1턴씩 앞당기거나, 더 파격적인 효과를 주고 공룡들의 효과를 전체적으로 상향해야 할 것이다.
3. "악어" / "용" 스티커 - 악어 스티커의 경우 화면에 보이는 모든 토큰을 제거하고, 용 스티커의 경우 모든 토큰과 모든 별을 제거한다. 솔직히 악어 카드의 경우 점수를 제거하는 게 아니라 토큰만 제거하는 것이라 매우 큰 문제로 느껴지지 않는데, 위에서 말한 판타지 덱 같은 느린 토큰 덱들을 다 차단한다는 게 불쾌하게 느껴질 수도 있다. 문제는 저 용 스티커인데, 모든 점수와 토큰을 제거하기에 본인이 토큰 덱이 아니라면 불리한 상황에서 사용해서 모든 걸 원점으로 돌릴 수 있다. (그리고 용 잠옷을 입고 다니는 "민" 이 실제로 덱에 용 2개를 넣고 다녀서 이 전략을 행한다!!!) 심지어 용 스티커는 1코스트라 (하스스톤으로 치면 1마나 데스윙이 게임 내 존재하는 것이라) 그냥 만능 스티커 그 자체여서, 어려움 난이도에서 이 스티커를 뽑지 못하면 게임의 난이도가 어려워지는 걸 급격하게 체감할 수 있다. 용 스티커의 코스트를 늘리거나, 효과와 코스트는 그대로 나두되 사용 후 즉시 턴이 종료되는 조건을 지니도록 스티커를 너프해야 한다는 생각이 들었다.

> 최종 보스 (덱빌딩 혼모노) 의 덱이 정말 양심없다. 물론 게임의 컨셉이 양심없는 카드를 만드는 것이기는 하지만, 어려움 난이도 기준 용 스티커 + 상대방의 마나와 점수를 뺏는 스티커 + 개사기 토큰을 1번에 10개씩 쌓는 스티커 + 내 토큰을 1턴에 4개씩 뺏는 스티커 등등 손목을 비틀어버리고 싶은 스티커 콤보들이 매 턴마다 나오기 때문에 애매하게 강한 덱을 들고 오면 탈탈 털리게 된다. 이 때문에 대부분의 덱 양상이 빌드업을 행하는 덱을 만들어가기 보다는 "내기만 하면 2000점을 획득해서 원턴킬을 할 수 있는 카드 만들기" 로 귀결되는데, 이렇게 대부분의 판들이 자신의 덱 컨셉을 적극적으로 활용하는 게 아니라 오프라인 대회에서 밴 당할 만한 카드 1장을 만드는 양상으로 이어진다는 게 아쉽게 느껴졌다. 개인적인 의견을 내자면, 용 스티커와 점수를 뺏는 해적선 스티커는 최종 보스 덱에서 제거를 해야 플레이어가 덜 불쾌하게 느껴질 것 같다.


결론적으로, 게임의 컨셉 자체가 신선하면서 의외로 어떤 카드를 만들 것인지 고민하는 맛이 있었고, 게임을 많이 하면 아쉬운 점들이 다소 보이지만 얼리 엑세스 게임이라 개선할 여지가 있다는 걸 감안해서 추천. 플레이타임의 경우 모든 덱을 1번씩 한다고 가정해도 거의 10개의 시작 덱이 있기에 그리 짧은 게임으로 느껴지지 않을 것이다. 이 때문에 가격 대비 플레이타임은 (대부분의 덱빌딩 게임처럼) 아쉽지 않으며, 덱빌딩 게임을 좋아한다면 한 번 해보는 걸 권장한다.

It's a neat idea, but dear lord is the balance in this game absolutely all over the place. I know that's kinda the idea, with how the game lets you mess with the cards and the effects, but at the end of the day, there is little I can do when the opponents can amass 100 damage on turn one, while others seem to still only use basic cards, even on week 3. 

I do recommend this game for the aesthetic and variation in fun build potential, but it just feels a little too unbalanced for the time being. Cards often don't do what they say, card-text overlaps with item-descriptions which causes the game to have a panic-attack and simply ignore effects, and I've seen some of the late-game bosses ignore max hand-size limits and even spawn mana out of thin air. I've even seen cases where the opponent just doesn't play a card for 4-5 turns. I suggest giving us more options to get rid of cards when it turns to mid or late game. It does get a little ridiculous how the game expects you to keep a theme to your deck, but still force you to add cards after every day. At some point, it's just not viable to expect me to fill a 15-20 card deck with synergies when I already need so much luck just to pull a sticker that fits the deck-type. 

Everything you do in this game, is at the mercy of randomness. What stickers you get, what events you get, what the opponent decides to play, if the claw-machine decides to pay out, if you get good stickers in the capsule-machine. There is genuinely no room for any amount of skill, when every aspect of the game, is dictated by RNG. When you can loose the game, on the first mandatory fight of the run, I think we need to step back and reevaluate the balance. The game also expects you to have some sort of counter cards at some point, token removals or counters. But of the game doesn't give one to you, at any point in the run, you are simply at the mercy your opponents RNG. It's just not a fun mechanic, and I hope they change up the progression, the day schedule system, and how the opponents scale, because right now, it's just not fun to roll a dice so often and realise that skill plays such a secondary role in this game. 

Most of my complaints come from the games hard-mode, where the only viable strategy is to just forfeit until you get an optimal starting scenario. And the amount of sweat and luck needed to beat even the starting opponents is genuinely discouraging. You need to break the game, you need to find infinite combos. There really is no room for experimentation, since there are 200-ish stickers in this game, and there is no way to even somewhat reliably get specific types or grades without just plain RNG, since the game pulls out of the entire pool of stickers, rather than focusing on giving something relating to the chosen deck-type. 

I'd honestly give it a little more time in the oven while everything gets ironed out. To be completely honest, it's a fine game. The art is charming. The concept is really unique and gameplay is engaging, but it's a little discouraging to get dumpstered on turn 2 on a good run because my opponent just happened to start the round with a stacked hand.

A comprehensive collection of the Swords & Sandals games you used to be able find on old flash sites back in the mid-2000's.

This collection originally added a few bugs and I had refrained from playing it when I bought it all that time ago, which have since been thankfully fixed as well as a few long-standing bugs that have been there since the flash days and that's honestly pretty refreshing. Do I think the games hold up though? Well...they're FUN, but definitely full of flaws - and each game has their upsides and downsides.

S&SI is short, and feels more like a tech demo than anything else, probably my least favourite.
S&SII, of course, is the classic I remember playing so much as a kid. The balancing is kind of insane and you really have to pull out some cheese for some of the difficulty spikes but somehow that makes it satisfying.
Gross-Out uses the same engine as I and II but is honestly just...terrible. I appreciate the preservation but man that game sucks ass.

S&SIII is probably my personal favourite, I never could find a free version online back in the day so it was nice to be able to fight all of the champions and see all the game had to offer. Now some of those champions were absolute hell and the Yeti...I'm surprised I beat it without the little fat kid's help. The game also weirdly feels grindy despite being very short, progress gets kind of slow in the later levels and it feels like a chore sometimes.
S&SIV is some weird mashup between mario party-esque board games but with a simplified version of S&SIII's combat system, lots of people like it, wasn't my thing personally. Lots of board variety and includes multiplayer via local hotseat.

Crusader was definitely interesting, it has about the balancing you come to expect from the franchise but with the presentation of an extremely simple 4X. While fun, it's not exactly gonna be a contender in the genre, and is more like a casual thing than anything else.

The music is catchy but not exactly high quality or anything. There also IS a plot throughline between the games, but it is both very understated and not at all that interesting. You fight in a gladiator arena, somehow Antares returns every game, also III has automatons which are not in the rest of the games lol, it gets a little silly at times.
Also, a new addition, is fan mods. Most of them are rebalances and kind of nice to be included in the collection.

So my recommendation...if you played these games way back when or are just a fan of older flash games? Absolutely. 100%. It's also very cheap so it's hard not to recommend it. The hurdle is mostly how much flash jank you can put up with, and that's definitely a personal preference.

The future. The universe is horrifying and dark. The Captain is a Psyker Witch Raider. She captains a stolen Imperial battlecruiser. Her crew consists of a Blood Witch, a Necromancer, two Imperial warriors, and a collection of mechanical husks, half-living half-dead. How are two Imperial warriors kept in thrall amongst this collection of of rapacious blood cultists? While there is no explicit game mechanic covering this aspect, you are free to use your imagination.

The ship encounters a trader, who does not immediately open fire. A rarity in this universe. Having no need of any missile parts, the Witch Captain calmly states "Let us drink their blood.". The crew know what to do almost instinctively, they have been through this routine many times. The Necromancer and the Blood Witch start muttering occult incantations. The two Imperial Warriors board the assault sled. The husk manning the weapons battery warms it up, but does not fire. "Weapons ready Captain." The husk croaks. Thus begins the brutal last 60 seconds that the trader crew will ever experience in this horrifying universe.

The Blood Witch completes her incantation and summons a Blood Thrall, not in the enemy ship as one would expect, but directly next to the Witch Captain. Before giving the order to fire, the Witch Captain hurls a lance of mental energy at the traders ship's shield generator. It bypasses the shield to strike the generator directly. As she is hurling the mental lance, using her battle axe she calmly slashes the throat of the Blood Thrall standing next to her. She is soaked in blood and imbued with additional occult energy, which allows her to launch a second lance immediately. The second lance completely cripples the shields.

"FIRE!" she roars, and a full broadside of energy bolts hits the shield room, crippling the shields completely and damaging the crew inside. Trader crewmen rush to the flaming room to initiate repairs. As the Witch Captain calmly makes her way to the assault sled, she casts a third spell which kills all of the already damaged traders trying to repair the shield generator. "Cease fire." she instructs the husk, as she does not want the trader ship disintegrating whilst she is on board sating her bloodlust.

The assault sled containing the Witch Captain and her two Imperial Warrior thralls launches. As it is latching on to the hull of the trader's ship, the Necromancer completes his incantations, and summons two terrifying ghouls in the trader ship engine room. The Witch Captain bursts into the enemy ship, her Imperial warrior thralls in tow, and with a blood curdling scream begins the process of finishing off the trader crew.

Esse jogo exala jogo de plataforma da época de PS2, mas aqui chegou no seu peak com gráficos de cair o queixo!!

Único ponto fraco do jogo é a história, ela começa meio do nada e termina meio do nada também, não é explicado exatamente o que a kena veio fazer naquela região, o jogo até provoca um pouco explorando o passado da kena, mas explorou BEM superficialmente, os personagens são muito interessante e carismáticos, mas não parecem acrescentar nada no desenvolvimento da protagonista.

A gameplay desse jogo é boa, ela não é tão simples, mas também não é nada muito complexo, o combate me lembra bastante de God Of War (2018) com o R1 sendo ataque leve e R2 sendo ataque forte, L1 pra defender e L2 pra usar o Arco/Bomba, é bem divertido lutar, mas meo amigo, dar parry nesse jogo é um PARTO, e a mecânica do parry é extremamente importante na dificuldade mestre + new game plus, poderiam ter dado mais frames de resposta. Gosto da exploração desse jogo, não atoa peguei todos os colecionáveis, deveriam ser mais fácil de achar, igual Tchia, tirando os rot e os centros de meditação o resto não trás muita progressão ao personagem, os amuletos por exemplo, quase não traz nenhum grande upgrade pra kena, e quando traz algo minimamente descente também traz um debuffs considerável.

A trilha sonora desse jogo é muito gostosa, há momentos que fazem você sentir vontade de chorar, acertaram muito bem nas transições de música, não é uma mudança brusca quando muda de música ambiente pra uma música de combate.

- New Game Plus -

Se você gostou desse jogo não estrague sua experiência jogando na dificuldade mestre, é EXTREMAMENTE frustrante, lutar com os bosses pra a terceira fase deles recuperar 70% da vida é sacanagem, se você não aprender a dar parry você VAI passar sufoco, principalmente no último desafio que libera depois de fechar o jogo (sério, eu devo ter passado pelo menos umas 6 horas tentando derrotas os três bosses finais ao mesmo tempo), aprenda a usar o ataque carregado, bomba Rot e Dash, vai fazer com que você sofra um pouquinho menos. 4/5.

[h2]単純操作でわちゃわちゃしたプレイは非常に楽しい[/h2]

セールしてたら購入していいと思うよ。
ただストーリーモードをEASY以外でやるとやや苦痛。
というか、ある設計に気づかないと面白くないので伝えておきたい。

[h3]一人でも複数ユニットを並べる事はできる[/h3]

まずこのゲームの CO-OP.MODE だが、自分以外全部CPUも可能。
要するにマルチプレイもどきはいつでも楽しむことが出来る。
そしてこのモードの場合は全員にある程度の経験値が手に入る。
メインストーリーで使う前に同時に育てるのも出来なくはない。

[h3]一人でも ONLINE GAME すら出来る[/h3]

オンラインでのCO-OPは6人プレイまでが可能。
オンライン協力とは？　と言いたくなる1人6キャラプレイも可能。
LOCAL GAMEと異なり複数ユニットに経験値が入ることはない。
しかしその代わりに同一ユニットを複数編成できる。

つまりLV100の強力キャラが1人育てばパワーレベリングが出来る。
一定難易度までなら、圧倒的な数の暴力を体現してやれる。
これで1人だけパワーレベリングした方がLV上げ自体は圧倒的に早い。

ここまでのことを理解していれば一人でも凄い楽しめるぞ。

[h2]さて、次は難点も書く[/h2]

実際に人とプレイしようとするとマッチングの難しさがある。
適当にASIAでやってマッチングすることはまずない。

超必殺技のカットインが前面に入り一瞬停止を挟むのでやや邪魔。
重ね方を工夫して背景の前、キャラの後ろに流すとか出来なかったのだろうか。

難易度が上がると敵に自分が埋もれて何がどこにいるかわからなくなる。
ここはゲーム性としては結構致命的なような気がする。

ストーリーが説明不足。後述。

[h3]ストーリーの説明不足についての詳細[/h3]

ストーリーモードはファントムブレイカーというゲームが前提のストーリーモード。
このゲームはあくまでその格闘ゲームの外伝作という立ち位置である。
登場人物もその関係性も何もかもがよく分からない専門用語で話が進む。

だからこのゲーム単体では割とちんぷんかんぷんである。
ざっくりと説明してくれるがそれでも人間関係の把握は全く難しい。

せめて説明みたいなページが欲しかったような気がする。

[h3]今後どうなるのかよくわからない[/h3]

個人的にはこのてのわちゃわちゃしたゲームデザインは好みなので、
今後も色々なキャラが増えてほしい。

だが、今作においての最初のDLCはコスプレイヤーモデルのオリキャラ。
こうなるとどういう基準で増えていくのかは疑問が残る。
原作キャラが増えるのか。オリジナルが増えるのか。
はたまた、何かしらコラボキャラが増えるのか？

DLC第二弾なんかでこの方向性が決定付けられるのではないだろうか…。

There's always something to do in this game, and I never feel bored. It's hard to quit, because I always want to do just one more thing before I stop. Every time I think I've seen everything, the game adds another gimmick. For example, I'm 22 hours in and I've only now found out that I can keep a pet! Yet, despite having tons of tasks and things to do, this game is relaxing and stress-free.

I thought this would be a simple farming game with a bit of crafting. Plant seeds, sell crops to buy more seeds, cook, craft, some fetch quests, things like that. And you will be doing a lot, but there's also a lot more. Explore dangerous areas to battle monsters and collect rare items with top-down shooter gameplay. Invest in trade routes to increase the number of items available in your sect's store. Manage your sect's lecture hall to recruit and listen to lecturers who can enhance your stats. I can't say it does any of things really well, but the combination of all of them together is nice.

I like the attention to detail, too. For example, you can make honey by building a beehive. But you don't just need the beehive, but also need to plant flowers near the hive that the bees can use. Not only that, but the type of flowers you plant influence the type of honey that's produced. So I naturally want to build several hives and experiment with all different types of flowering plants.

Progress is very slow, but I don't think it's a bad thing. The game is focused around Cultivation, which as I understand it is the concept of gradual self-improvement. Everything you do can contribute to your cultivation foundation: battling, fishing, planting, cooking, etc. I've only had two "breakthroughs" (basically level ups) in all my time playing the game. Character relationships also take a lot of time, and I've only managed to fill 1 of the 6 hearts for 2 of the characters so far. So I'll probably be playing this for a long time.

The characters are all interesting in their own way. Just to name a few, you have the idealistic girl who wants to be like the heroes in her novels, the genius but somewhat unwise boy who always comes up with strange inventions, the mysterious and antisocial woman who lives in the forest and can teach useful knowledge, and the lazy fisherman who is sometimes capable of deep philosophy. Side note: sometimes the game drops some legitimately interesting philosophy, like when the fisherman asks about the relationship between fish and the river, with the conversation concluding that the river isn't a prison that the fish are forced to be in but a guide for the correct direction to go, which I think covers Taoist philosophy. Most of the character art is nice, but my one complaint is that some of the characters who show up later have a different artstyle that's kind of a downgrade IMO.

I love the music, too, most of it being soothing and relaxing. I wish they would release the soundtrack for purchase.

From the very first mission, [b]Starship Troopers: Terran Command[/b] nails the [i]Starship Troopers[/i] aesthetic. The environments — dusty deserts, mining colonies, and bleak frontier outposts — evoke the movie’s satirical depiction of humanity’s expansionist future. Between missions, the game uses faux propaganda broadcasts and recruitment ads that perfectly mimic the film’s “[i]Would you like to know more?[/i]” tone, blending dark humor with militaristic fervor. This attention to atmosphere makes every campaign feel like a small episode in the endless war against the Bugs.

The story is presented through mission briefings and voiceovers rather than cinematic cutscenes, but it still conveys the harsh, hierarchical world of the [i]Terran Federation[/i]. You’re not the hero — you’re a cog in the military machine, executing orders and making sure your troopers die “for the cause.”

[b]Starship Troopers: Terran Command[/b] plays as a real-time tactics game rather than a base-building RTS. There’s no resource harvesting or building construction. Instead, you capture control points, manage limited reinforcements, and try to hold your lines against massive Bug swarms. This focus on positioning and fire discipline feels fitting for the setting: a small, disciplined human army facing a relentless alien tide.

Infantry are the backbone of your force, ranging from standard rifle squads to rocket troopers, engineers, and snipers. Each unit type serves a clear tactical purpose — riflemen suppress, rocketeers clear clusters, and engineers set up MG turrets or flamethrowers for choke points. The key to victory lies in terrain control and firing arcs: if your units are flanked or surrounded, they die quickly. The game emphasizes line-of-sight and elevation advantages, rewarding players who think defensively and anticipate where the Bugs will break through.

The mission design is one of [b]Starship Troopers: Terran Command[/b]’s strongest aspects. Scenarios vary from desperate last stands to large-scale offensives across Bug-infested colonies. Some missions require capturing specific objectives, while others challenge you to defend extraction zones or escort convoys through hostile territory. The tension builds steadily, often culminating in massive, cinematic bug assaults that test your ability to manage limited manpower under pressure.

Graphically, the game is functional rather than flashy. The environments are detailed enough to be immersive, though textures and models are modest by modern standards. What sells the atmosphere is the lighting, unit animations, and large-scale battles that fill the screen with chaos. Watching hundreds of Arachnids swarm over ridges toward your soldiers never loses its thrill.

[b]Starship Troopers: Terran Command[/b] succeeds as a faithful and atmospheric RTS that captures the essence of the film’s militarized satire. Its strategic gameplay, clever mission design, and relentless sense of pressure make it a standout title for fans of tactical combat. However, the lack of multiplayer, limited strategic depth, and repetitive combat loops keep it from achieving greatness.

A tough, engaging, and thematically spot-on RTS that will delight fans of the franchise — as long as you’re ready to serve the [i]Federation[/i] and fight the Bug menace to the bitter end.

秋霞的年齡應該是設定在26、7歲左右沒錯吧?
但她的行為舉止完全是50歲up的歐巴桑

OST가 좋은 게임.
아직 다 플레이한게 아니라서 팁만 약간 남깁니다.

(1) 자기계발(단련)
 - 능력치는 5레벨까지 성장하는 것으로 보입니다. 그 이후로는 단련해도 경험치가 오르는게 안보이니 쓸데없이 단련할 필요는 없습니다.
 - 개인적으로는 초반에는 체력을 먼저 올리는게 좋아보입니다. 지능은 논문작성, 매력은 호감도상승에 보너스지만, 체력을 올리면 행동력이 오르니 어떻게든 써먹을 수 있으니까.

(2) 상점
 - 매일 3개의 아이템을 랜덤으로 판매중입니다. 행동력을 1 사용해 리롤 가능한데 솔직히 리롤은 낭비같음.
 - 상점에서 단련효과를 늘려주는 아이템을 팝니다. 비싼편. 단련효과상승은 5단계까지 있습니다.
 - 아르바이트 효과 상승 아이템이 있는데, 마지막(4단계)에 미니게임 스킵시에도 대량의 보상을 받을 수 있다고 되어있습니다. 근데 스킵하면 직접한거 반정도 밖에 못받는걸 보면 개구라같음.

(3) 아르바이트
 - 아르바이트 미니게임은 하다보면 차선변경하는 차량이 나오기 시작합니다. 사람이 있든 없든 그냥 깜박이도 없이 밀어버리니 주의. 거기다 차선2개분량의 충돌판정있음. 안전운전의 달인의 인터뷰가 떠오르네요. "운전대를 잡은 순간부터 보이는 모든 사람은 전부 미XX이라고 생각해야합니다."

(4) 논문

Nexomon delivers a cheeky, self-aware narrative that doesn’t take itself too seriously — and that’s exactly what makes it so fun. Collecting Nexomon is pure joy. Each creature feels distinct, and the thrill of building your team never gets old. The game strikes a great balance in difficulty — challenging enough to keep battles interesting, but never punishing. Whether you’re grinding levels or exploring new areas, it always feels rewarding.

I did run into a bug on PC, likely due to my system being too high-spec. Thankfully, switching to the Steam Deck let me play past the issue and continue the adventure without a hitch. It’s a testament to how much I wanted to keep going — and I’m glad I did.

If you’re into monster-catching games, Nexomon is absolutely worth your time.

I am a long time fan of the series (since Hot Shots Golf 3 in 2001)

While there are a lot of things I like, unfortunately with the game in the current state I can’t recommend it to most people besides hardcore fans.  I feel like a lot of my complaints stem from the devs intentionally changing things for no reason, which is why it's frustrating.

The things I like

-  The physics seem to be straight out of HSG: Out of Bounds and I’m all for it.  It feels like a true hot shots golf game, and I’m 
really glad they got it right after initial worries of having a new developer 

-  The return to having actual characters and it just being a golf game only.  Sorry to the fans of EG 2017, but I wasn’t a big fan of the mii characters and having to level up clubs.  Same with like the game being bloated with things like driving around in a golf cart and fishing.  Plus the RNG custom clubs.  I’m glad this game went back from all that.
    
-  The amount of characters and courses at launch. Plenty of content and lots of new clubs/balls, even if it is a bit of a grind.

- The extra game modes such as scramble and wacky golf seem really fun, at least with real people (the world tour missions with those are a drag to be honest, mainly due to the dumb cpu and how long it takes to complete the chapter)

The Meh

-  Character stats.  The fact that every character can just eat food to get all S stats kinda defeats the purpose of having unique characters.  I get Fair Play is a thing but those stats are kinda wack (why is Kazuma hitting over 300y?  Why would you pick anyone besides Gloria?).  I just praised the game for going back to actual characters, so it sucks that this kind of defeats that purpose.

Plus driving almost 400y and having all S stats kinda makes the game boring and trivial. The power window is way too wide in this game.  S power should be like 300/310y at most, but in this game it's way too high.  Even if the character has all E other stats, just the fact that they can drive 400y more than makes up for it, so why would you pick anything else?

-  Music.  Overall not as great as previous entries, though I like the silver peaks theme 


The bad 

-  UI.  The UI is pretty rough and a lot of images are very low resolution, like the course pictures.  The characters are low res as well when selecting them.  It just looks very unpolished and cheap. 

The local multiplayer character select is god-awful, you can’t even see everything about the character until the next screen after everyone selects theirs.  Also the club selection doesn’t show how it affects the stats until you go back out to the previous screen.  I'm not sure why they just didn’t use the single player character select screen and UI, and instead spent extra dev time to make something way worse?

Why did they switch the colors of the control and spin stats, but keep the Pinhole and Turbo Spin clubs the old colors?  It's just random stuff like this that makes no sense for them to spend extra time doing.  Like just leave things the way they were.

-  Camera angles/tee off.  Every time you get Perfect Impact while teeing off, it has to do this “cinematic” up close shot of your characters face instead of you actually being able to see how your shot goes.  I’d like to see how it curves around trees for example.  There are just less and worse camera angles than the previous games

-  Controls:  why B/circle (xbox/playstation controller) for the default button?  In every other game, you took your shot with A/X.  If you change your controls to use A/X to take your shot, you can't fine tune your power down, only up with Y/Triangle.  I am actually shocked they have not fixed this yet. 

Overall it just feels very unpolished, with the glitches in world tour, the CPU opponents/teammates acting extremely dumb, and when you get chip ins, the fireworks animations only playing sometimes, the random "unplayable shots", etc...


The ugly 

- Side spins and curve.  RESOLVED, THANK YOU

-  Performance.  I can brute force FPS with my desktop, but this game should not run at 27fps on the steam deck OLED on low settings.  It looks like a PS3 game.

I was really looking forward to having this as the perfect handheld game, but it is borderline unplayable on the deck.  Like not even just FPS, but everything just takes ages to load for some reason, and the menus are really laggy.

First things first--considering the average comment about this game seems to be that it is, well, an average game, let me push violently against that.  There is nothing average about this game.  This is like the prototypical example of a well-above-average game with magnificence woven throughout.  This is particularly the case with the writing and narrative (as you would expect from an Obsidian game), but really just about every element of the game has flashes of brilliance--your companions, the art style, the design of the areas, the interplay of the simplified but still rewarding character development system with the movement and combat mechanics, sound design, and of course again the writing as a whole.  You could absolutely also find some things about the game to be not precisely to your liking, but Avowed is so profoundly up my alley that I struggle to think of what specifically someone (being intellectually honest) might dislike.  I guess there is probably too much loot; is that really a problem we need to fix though?

But yeah, honestly this is almost exactly what you might expect from a fantasy game made by the studio that produced the Outer Worlds, but even better, given the lessons they learned that first time around.  Any concerns I had about the Outer Worlds occasionally feeling a little lifeless have been addressed here, as there is so much stuffed into the areas here that you never feel disconnected from the world or the storyline--and what a storyline it is, by the way.  The story fits perfectly into the grand traditions set by some of the other best CRPGs of all time, and if there is even a single fault with Avowed it is that I did not entirely understand how good the game was at first.  I cannot put my finger on anything in particular, since the parkour feels good, the combat is fun (especially daggers basically attacking as quickly as you can hit the mouse button; excellent decision to make me use daggers in a game for the first time ever), but it was not until I had my second companion (no offense though Kai, I came to love you in time) that I really started to see and appreciate what the game was going for, and started realizing that even things I thought might not be important were going to come up again later in this beautifully-written and executed tale.

If you played and loved the Pillars of Eternity games you definitely have even more reason to check out Avowed, particularly if you are like me and went from "ugh this is so much lore about so many things I do not understand" on your first playthrough to suddenly having the world and its inhabitants and regions and factions click on your second playthrough, you might find yoruself muttering things to yourself while playing Avowed like "wait, is this an Engwithan ruin in the Living Lands?  But that doesn't make any sense!" and realize you have 100% bought into Eora as a real place and look forward to moving there whenever that becomes possible.

Now team up with InXile and do a new Wasteland in this style.  Thanks in advance!

The problem comes from the sheer amount of time gating in this game. Almost every single goal in this game is time gated beyond belief. I have played MMO's with constant FOMO events that respect your time more than this game does. I'll go bit by bit with the most important parts of the game that are time gated.

Resources are spawned every single day, up to three days of stacking. You eventually can become best friends with the main cast of characters and they'll pickup items for you, but at the start of the game you will be absolutely desperate for resources and will need to go manually collect them. There will be days where you will have to throw up your hands and be like "welp, guess I'll just logon tomorrow to be able to craft two iron bars!" 

Friendship leveling is next. You get levels by doing weekly/daily quests and gifting them items of one to three heart levels, with three hearts being best value. You will NEED to level the friendship of other characters because besides making them collect items, they have various abilities that'll make your time in the game better considerably and give you various resources needed to craft items. Later on you can even bring two friends with you, and certain combos can massively boost you. 
The problem though is this is slow, you won't have friend abilities at usable levels or at all for a long while, and best friend status genuinely can take months. There are also certain characters who can take even longer due to their three heart items taking a long time to be able even available to craft. A certain funny bunny being a particular issue, if you know you know.

Quests themselves often have time gates, forcing you to "wait until tomorrow" frequently. This wouldn't be so bad if it wasn't possible to run out of quests to do very often, leading to just multiple days of hopping on and then hopping off. You will eventually reach a state where you literally have no quests to do unless a random time gated friendship quest appears. Quest design in this game is insanely boring though, and eventually I started skipping dialogue. Even worse is that this is acknowledged ingame with your character's useless dialogue choices often having a choice of "okay I guess I'm gathering sticks again", which of course is completely ignored by the cast. There is literally one quest series where you just follow a character around for five minutes with minimal dialogue breaks.

There are constant rotating events, and they are shockingly strict with how much time you have to get enough event currency to obtain items or even just do daily rewards. In a few of the events, missing even one or two days can completely blow your chance of getting every event item. Also before a recent update, older event items had to be obtained via random chance at Tuxedosam and My Melody's shops. That has been fixed though, with event stands allowing you to just get older items easily now.

Finally the bit I hate most, the visitor system. A ton of quests, functions, etc are hidden behind the visitor system. If you are aiming to get the one hidden achievement, you will be waiting a full year as you are stopped by seasonally locked visitors, event item locked visitors, and literal months long waits for a few of the visitors. Visitors come for a "week" long period when their rotation happens. Some visitors appear anytime though. It is not a week however for rotation based visitors, it is five days from Thursday to Monday. You can "max out" their chances of appearing, but honestly it doesn't feel like it. Other people have noticed, but since a certain update visitors seem to have lower chances to appear, so realistically you will see them max twice a week. If you have many visiting at once though their quest to get stars (max five before being allowed to permanently stay) might not even appear due to the dailies having a max quest limit. On top of this sometimes they just won't give quests at all. Visitors will not appear two days in a row, and only leaving if their quest is done to hopefully visit another time in the rotation.
This leads to intense frustration, as some visitors only visit once a real time month as noted before, and those visitors often have some of the meatier content behind them including unlocking other visitors.

I understand the goal of this game is to not rush, but they have done everything in their power to make sure you don't have a choice. "Time travel" (setting your clock forward) breaks large chunks of the game, including events and multiplayer. If you want to experience the game in full, you are forced to endure the constant time gating.

Once I get my final achievement, I'll probably put down the game, as it lost its charm many hours ago and is just exhausting me now. This doesn't feel as fun anymore, it feels like a chores simulator with a Hello Kitty flavoring. 

If you do decide to get it, wait for the base game to be 20 USD (or equivalent in your local currency) or lower, and don't be afraid to quit playing if it starts to burn you out. My silly self is in too deep now.

The second half leans more into survival horror. Usually I’m not big on that, but it still worked here. The pacing stayed intense, and it added a different kind of tension that kept things fresh until the end.

For a first game from the developer, this is an easy recommendation for any horror fan. Plus, there’s free DLC on the way, which is always a bonus.

Recommended, because this game delivers what it promises: A RimWorld-like base game, overlaid with all the classic xianxia tropes: cultivation, warring sects, inner and outer disciples, manuals describing powerful techniques, and popular Daoist-inspired mysticism.

The RimWorld-like portions of the game are a bit basic. The work priority system is limited to "on" and "off", and you can't say "make timber from logs whenever I have less than 30 timber". But unlike some RimWorld knockoffs, you do need to pay attention to individual disciples, including the outer disciples who actually do the work. As a RimWorld-like game, it's a decent B-tier.

Inner disciples require significant individualized attention, because they're your major weapons, your adventurers, and your magic crafters. The game mechanics support the literary tropes here: the main job of your inner disciples is to become ever more powerful.

But xianxia is all about gaining power through esoteric knowledge. And this game really leans into "esoteric knowledge" mechanically: You will need to learn Daoist elementalist interactions. You will need to care about the feng shui of your bedrooms. You will be constantly searching for secret manuals and rare natural treasures. You will care about the cultivation potential of your recruits. You will search for advanced cultivation paths (and each path works differently). The game is full of subsystems and hidden knowledge.

There are also some things to be aware of. Several of the tutorials have been broken for years. The English-language documentation and wikis only scratch the surface. There are some occasional bugs in actual game play.

But overall, this is a positive review, because if you want a B-tier RimWorld base with xianxia tropes, and if you want to search for esoteric knowledge in order to gain ridiculous power, the game delivers. It's a very solid match between mechanics and tropes.

Add Solasta to the list of games that don't start great.

     Your 4 party members sit in a pub, waiting for a boss-type guy to show up that wants to pay them to go into the "Badlands" (guess what kind of place that is).  As your party sits drinking, 4 tutorials are doled out as each member tells about their trip to the pub.  Each short tutorial does explain different important aspects of the game but dividing it up into four parts makes it all feel much longer than it is.

     Also, meeting our characters for the first time when they're drunk isn't a great first impression.  None of them are instantly likable and there's an awful lot of vulgar, juvenile language used in the first 30 minutes.

     Gameplay wise, mechanics feel solid, the UI and HUD are modern and work well and the graphics are good to very good although the world seems a little sparse.  Holding down a key to show all items one can interact with usually results in the highlighting of a single object on screen, if that.

     The story becomes even more plodding once boss guy shows up and hires the four.  It seems you have to register with some council first, something that turns out to be as exciting as being sent to DMV to renew one's license.  Honestly, it's an awful first hour.


20+ hours in:

The Pros:
     The core gameplay is fantastic, with the actual combat being the highlight.  Huge amount of options for each class and race factor into the fights.  And the UI is so clean and well laid out that it never gets confusing what options are available to each character.  The game will even give you helpful reminders and pause mid-fight with something like "You can provide a magical shield to keep your friend from getting hit, do you want to?"

     The UI throughout the entire game is very good, with a clean, uncluttered modern feel to it all that makes doing anything in the game a pleasure.

    The environments look good enough and are usually laid out in ways that offer interesting aspects to each battle.  The game is extremely vertical, with many lands having multiple levels.  The game can take this to negative extremes, though.  Some environments just have too much going on, on too many levels and are confusing to navigate, little alone fight through.  There's an early battle that takes place almost entirely on high columns that are frankly a nightmare to deal with.


Unknowns:
     The game comes with multiplayer and what I hear is a complete dungeon and campaign editor that lets you build anything from small adventures up to complete epic adventures.  I haven't tried out either yet but I'm looking forward to trying out the workshop mods in Steam; I hear that many are even better than the vanilla campaign that comes with the game and it looks like there's a ton to choose from.


The Cons:
     Jiminy Christmas, are these player characters and NPC's the worst I've ever seen.  I understand that the team that built this game is smallish and far from the large AAA teams so many of us are used to.  I'll assume the devs did the best they could with the time and resources they had and considering how good the important parts of the game are, I'll just say the cutscenes throughout are pretty painful and leave it at that.

     Unfortunately, dialogue and story aren't great, either.  All the characters here suffer from that modern trend of making every line a smartass punchline and listening to this is painful, as well.  It's never, ever funny and never deepens the characters in any way.  So far, the story is substandard, but I can't say much about it when I'm only a quarter of the way through.

     I can, however, criticize the opening hours of the game, one of the most important aspects of any game that's supposed to impress you from the start and hook you into wanting more.  The start of this game is boring and filled with the ugly cutscenes and character models and dialogue.  It puts their worst traits forward and that's a shame because the actual core of the game has lots of enjoyable gameplay to offer.

This game can be really good. It looks good, an awesome setting, sounds nice, and the gunplay is pretty decent. There is a really good game here, and I absolutely love Remedy games, but in its current state I can't recommend it at all. I don't think the other negative reviews on this game do a very good job other than to say this game doesn't have content. So I wanted to record here all of the glaring problems my friends and I had with the game in our short time with it to help others make a more informed purchase:

There is very little content in the game. There are only 6 levels, and while they are very good, they are not very replayable because there is one scenario per level, there aren't different objectives for each level. When you run it once, you've seen everything it has to offer.

The level modifiers are neat, but there's only a handful of them and they really aren't that meaningful. They also all are dealt with in the same way, through the blackrock gun you find at any ammo station. I thought the supernatural items were gonna have a much much larger influence on this game, that was part of the draw for me buying the game! More on this later.

There are only 3 kits. They are varying levels of bad. I played the water kit mostly, and it was awful. You have a healing tank that gets destroyed instantly and is extremely onerous to even put down. And why would you put it down outside of combat, because most people just run back to the shower and ammo stand! And that's it. You get a water gun and water tank. You don't ever unlock anything else.

The buildcrafting is pretty much nonexistent. No upgrades you get are meaningful. Even good upgrades don't really buff you enough to feel like it matters. Leveling up just doesn't do anything, and any interesting perks are locked to really high levels. 

The equipment items are so weird. Why does the water gun have the left click ability at all? It's takes forever to charge and shoots a meaningless water bubble and overheats your equipment super fast. The right click and hold ability is the only usable one, and I've heard the other kits feel very similar.

My absolute biggest gripe with this game is the fact that the supernatural class items are so meaningless. Each kit gets ONE. Thats it. I thought we were going to deal with supernatural items in the levels and maybe capture them, so we could use them ourselves. Instead everyone gets one item and some are better than others. This is my biggest issue with the game. This is the coolest part of Control and it is just a sidenote in this game.

Weapon progression is bad. The only good weapons are the pump action shotgun and the smg. Every other weapon, especially the single shot weapons like the revolver and hunting rifle are just awful. There are way too many enemies and they have way too much health for these guns to be any good. Maybe if you could have two weapons at once? Every weapon feels like it should do a bit more damage to be honest.

The glacial pace you crawl when you are down is really dumb. Let you crawl faster or just remove it!

Environment effects are extremely annoying. It feels like the constant fires in the levels only exist so that the water kit can not feel useless. It is really obnoxious that the turret kit causes fires. Status effects are either useless or annoying, like when you accidentally electrocute yourself or your friends with the electric augment. Or the radiation augment, because yeah I want to irradiate enemies so that they run up to me and irradiate me and my friends with no way to get rid of it without going back to a shower!

Movement feels kinda bad. You are unreasonably slow with certain weapons. And why even have a crouch slide when it serves no purpose? Mantling isn't very consistent.

The encounter design/director is awful. Sometimes you get levels where the enemies will spawn forever. They spawn in front of you, behind you, and don't give you time to rest. Being stuck in a safe room forever is so stupid. This completely breaks the flow of a horde-like game, as you never have the point where you can relax and retool. Not to mention, you'll face infinite enemies while running around, but when you'd expect to be fighting the hordes during defense objectives, the enemies are nowhere to be found and you're left just sitting there. And this is very common we found.

The difficulty levels are also odd, as it feels like it just ups the amount of enemies substantially and that's it? Normal mode is hilariously easy, whereas hard mode is insanely swingy between easy levels vs enemies spawn infinitely levels.

Progression is annoying. The same currency used for actually improving your kit is ALSO used for buying cosmetics! So basically I never got any cosmetics during my playtime. The voice packs that the game director was super passionate about are non-existent? The characters don't really interact and when they do it's for some terrible joke like asking your boss for a raise. I thought they were going to expand the lore of the FBC??? The characters don't interact basically at all in-game, which is wild. The cosmetics also look kinda lame.

There is literally only one boss in the entire game. Sticky Ricky. And he wasn't that engaging to fight. Every other boss is just a buffed up normal guy. THEY ALSO NEVER DID THE "STICKY RICKYYYYYY" YELL IN THE LEVEL!

There should also be a lobby like in Deadlock where you can actually move around and there could be world-building elements in it.

It's way better after their big update, but it still gets boring real fast. Not enough content and variety in gameplay, still some jank they need to work out. Matchmaking is better but still mid. Would be fine for $10.

+++绝佳的能力与关卡设计
+++精致的像素艺术，灵动的电子音乐

---BOSS战有些无聊，感觉上就是小怪pro max
---徽章不少但多为简单的数值加成，战斗多样性主要来自能力组合而非徽章搭配[/b]
[h2]什么叫他拿的是瑞士军球？[/h2]
      本作的核心就是“悠悠球”，一切设计都是围绕它来展开。它是跳跳乐时的钩锁，是解谜时的钥匙，也是战斗时的利剑。多功能集于一体的设计让其简单易操作而又有着惊人的可塑性。能力的丰富自然也带来了多样的关卡，而本作的关卡设计让我想到了《帕箱》作者的一句话：
[quote=Patrick]The purpose of the system is not to make cool puzzles.
 The purpose of the puzzles is to showcase this cool system.[/quote]
      本作的一些关卡没有什么难度，但在你完成关卡时会利用视觉、听觉等方式来给予你正反馈，仿佛是玩家在与关卡共舞。没有复杂的做题，没有极限的跳跳乐，没有高难的战斗，有的只是纯粹的对系统的欣赏，对游戏的享受，就是为了告诉你我们这个系统做得能让你有多爽！（当然以上也并不是说本作设计就那么浅显，深度这方面我觉得本身就属于见仁见智）
      游戏内对悠悠球各种能力的开发十分精妙。每次获得一个新能力都又能打开一大片新的区域，又会有许多隐藏待玩家发现，又会有许多有趣的玩法供玩家体验。在整个游玩过程中，新鲜感几乎是从未褪去的。从头到尾都让我对制作组还能用这个悠悠球玩出什么花样而感到好奇。探索越多发现越多，发现越多越想探索，一玩就停不下来。:D

[h2]This is true music&pixel art[/h2]
      本作的音乐非常棒，战斗时的节奏鼓点能让人热血沸腾，探索时的悠扬旋律又恰到好处地烘托出了悬疑感。不同区域的音乐各有特色，玩法保持新鲜感的同时视听体验也让你保持新鲜感。音乐的氛围烘托、情绪引导都做得很好。
      游戏整体画风是复古的像素风，但是角色立绘精致可爱（小动物们可爱捏），动画流畅细腻，“复古”只是观感而非体验。在游戏里甚至可以调出GBA游戏机，在游戏里的老式游戏机里玩游戏，真真切切复一把古。XD

[h2]剧情老套 ≠ 体验无趣[/h2]
      本作的剧情如果概括来看属于是相当老套，但其细节方面的呈现做到了生动有趣，使得即使玩家能预测到剧情的下一步发展也不会对剧情失去期待。在剧情中讽刺一些社会现象时，制作组用轻喜剧的笔触化解了其中的严肃，不会让玩家在联想到现实时感到沉重而是能会心一笑，也不会令只想一心享受游戏的玩家感到厌烦。总的来说，整体剧情质量不错，无功也无过，最后结局落到的点我很喜欢。😌

      综上所述，本作整体素质超高，是一款超棒的类塞作品，强烈推荐！之前没有汉化也许算个缺憾，但在几位大佬的努力下汉化也已经完成，可以前往下面的指南内下载，或去B站、小黑盒搜索一下即可找到汉化发布帖。

A compelling sense of mounting dread and great use of a singular location star here, alongside the titular Skinfreak, in a game that cements Torture Star as the king of indie B-horror, and Black Eyed Priest as one of the best developers carrying that mantle.  

These games have always been small, scrappy, brutish, ugly, and proud of it, and Skinfreak continues that tradition in much the same way as previous titles.  But it's done with the flair and confidence of people who have spent years honing the art of interactive exploitation.  You already know whether or not you like these sort of games, and if you do then I'd say Skinfreak is a great showing of everything you crave.  The environments are jagged and polygonal.  Vibrant colors bleed out of light sources like Argento's own blood.  Death comes loud and violent.  And in the absence of death, there is only silence, the buzz of fluorescent lights, and a parade of vaguely farcical obstacles to your character's goal.

The atmosphere is thick, the scares are jarring, the puzzles tickle your brain, the characters turn your stomach, and the story keeps you interested enough to press on through the ever-present threat of loud jumpscares and horrifying face textures.  An absolute top-tier piece of trash, and a great way to spend an October evening.

When Oscar Wilde said imitation is the sincerest form of flattery, I believe he had Sworn in mind. Sworn is a decent game that will forever live in the shadows of a truly great game that "inspired" it -- Hades. Sworn steals pretty much every thing that was not locked and nailed down by Super Giant, so much so that it almost leaves a bad taste. It's so much of a clone, that you start to think, "Maybe Nintendo has a point", and that's something I never thought I'd be saying.

So Sworn pretty much lives and dies by how well it executes Hades formula, and the answer to that question is "It's good, but not as good".

On the plus side, it has 4 different playable characters, each with 4 unique weapons and 4 unique spells, so there is a decent amount of variety here. The game also has co-op, so if that's important to you, you may want to give this game a try. I'm a solo player, so it didn't matter.

Combat feels okay, with a slower pace than Hades. There's a small window where attacks can leave you vulnerable, and a ever so slight cool down on dodge. It's just enough of a different pacing that you never get into "flow" state. There's always a split second where you are making a conscious choice to attack, move, or dodge. It's also just enough that when you take damage, you feel like it was "cheap". The game is very stingy with health, so a more defensive play style is often needed.   You'll also find that the bosses are fairly easy, as it's easy to handle 1 single enemy. You are only really in danger when taking on multiple enemies at the same time. 

Progression is decent. Of course, you start under powered, but you quickly get access to all kinds of upgrades. It does start to feel just a bit of a grind as you get about 75% of your way through the game, as each play through starts to take 30-40 minutes to complete.  However, after after 24 hours and completing on Squire and Knight difficulty, I was ready to call it quits. Post game is just enemies being more health sponges while adding more and more environmental damage.

Story wise, there is no story. The Camelot setting is just window dressing, there's no depth to it or characterization. I disliked the idea of King Arthur "breaking bad" and the fae, who are basically demons, being the "good guys". Not everything needs to be edgy and dark, especially when there's no real story it's in service of. I would have much rather have a game where the knights of the round table are the ones giving you blessings.

This review may sound negative, but I had a good time playing Sworn. It's not a bad game to burn a weekend on, but it's never going to dethrone Hades and Hades II.

Verdict: SWORN can most accuratelly be described as Hades from Wish. It is fun for a few hours but seriously needs a lot of polish.

Gameplay's pretty solid too, coming with a Pokemon-esque Element system to encourage you to at least think about how to best approach your fights, and a surprisingly large count of party members - 32 total during the whole campaign. There's tons of side content too, the game will have you active and doing new stuff all throughout its runtime.

Highly recommended if you're and RPG fan or horror media enthusiast. There's bound to be some things you'll find charming in this worthwhile package.

I wouldn't recommend Sailing Era. I had hoped that this game might offer a similar experience to 'Uncharted Waters' on my SNES console—an experience that balanced a love of discovery with a need for more traditional 'adventure' mechanics. But that didn't happen.

In Uncharted Waters, every call to a port mattered. It felt like you were a humble captain carving out a place for your name in a huge world. The game had a measured tempo but made it worthwhile to experience it directly—you established connections, gambled away your fortune, and even cared for your ships. There had been some beauty to this simplicity that Sailing Era has not even come close to with its realistic 3D maps.

Sailing Era tries to be modern but loses the heart. The interface feels cluttered and over-engineered. Trade and exploration have been reduced to spreadsheet-level management. The storylines are disconnected, characters forgettable, and the dialogue lacks the earnest tone that made Uncharted Waters engaging despite its age. Even the sea battles, which should have been an upgrade after 30 years of progress, feel like a chore rather than an event.

I wanted that same rush that came with setting out to sea without knowing what the horizon held. Instead, I got a game that seemed to constantly remind me that I was basically playing against a to-do list. Sailing Era isn't a bad game—it’s a soulless one. If you’ve ever stayed up late nights on your SNES finding fame and fortune within Koei’s world as you knew it under their old map of the globe, this will only remind you of how much better those games were when your graphics were worse.

This is a game I've really tried to enjoy, and came back to on occasion with updates, and... well, the saying I would use is "Wide as an ocean, deep as a puddle."

There's a lot of different mechanics, but none of them feel fully fleshed out. It VERY much feels like the dev added it to say "Hey, look, we have taming/transforming/farming/etc mechanics!" and then NEVER goes back to it. If you look at the update logs, it's always, ALWAYS new things. Never fleshing old things out. Maybe some tweaks, but never making them deeper.

To expand the fleshing things out metaphor, you often have games that are the bare bones. Then the dev fleshes it out; then puts the finishing touches, and it comes to life. This feels like just a giant bone skeleton where they keep adding more and more bones until it's some bone centipede monstrosity with no flesh whatsoever. Which sounds cool at first, but you do need flesh on it to keep it going.

I would prefer a game with half of these mechanics, but each one is better and more engaging to explore that mechanic.

It's not technically a bad game though, and I bought it because I could see the potential. But unless you want a variety of shallow experiences, I wouldn't recommend it.

I just came back to this game because they announced an upcoming sequel. I just got platinum again because for some reason, they added that stupid sworn brother gimmick. Review for the game as a returnee:

The game is truly the jianghu experience that you're looking for if you're a wuxia enthusiast. So much Techniques, Characters, Alternate routes, Higher Leveled enemies, and Multiple Sects. I loved this game when I first played it as it was my gateway to wuxia type games and will forever hold a place in my dao heart.

So much build variety, enjoyable soundtrack, wide roster of characters, good world building, insane replay value, Fun Gameplay, Flashy moves, and Pets. It's especially fun navigating through the world and looking for that Legendary manual, Meeting Old Masters, Fateful Encounters, Hidden treasures, and so much more.

Now for the sad part, this game has a lot of issues. From Translation, Forced Softlocks, Breaking Immersion, Loading Screens, and Couplets that were annoying and forced me to reset a lot without a guide. There's also the fact that homestead is quite unbalanced as it makes the game really easy, I genuinely think they made a mistake on that one, it felt unfair that only your characters got the highest level martial arts because of that gimmick making the enemies weak. I also think this game is heavily favored towards solo play after you start getting the achievement bonuses. It takes so much time when playing as a team because you have to level all of them and finishing a run with solo is just so much quicker with how broken the scaling is in this game. Most of these are pretty minor and only slightly affect my rating.

Finally, this game is pretty much a roguelite as in you would need to sacrifice some runs to make your character stronger in the next playthrough (not necessary for getting the best endings if you're good enough). Overall, a 7/10, I wish I could formulate my review better but it's hard as a returnee my memories are no longer fresh :(

Странная игра. Кажется, первая за долгое время, про которую мне даже сказать нечего. Переводится название игры как «Ручной Сэм» (не путать с Крутым) — в этом и вся суть. Посмотрите трейлер и считайте, что всю игру вы уже прошли. Я вот с ней справился за полтора часа — время потрачено не впустую (я отдыхаю от других надоевших игр), но и рекомендовать тяжело.

Геймплей весь построен на ручном управлении персонажем: надо передвигать ноги (каждую отдельно), моргать, вдыхать-выдыхать воздух, а также двигать руками и головой. А, ещё и осанку держать. В большинстве случаев либо рассказчик, либо сама игра подскажут, что именно нужно сделать. Не знаю, можно ли проиграть какой-нибудь уровень — у меня всё получалось с первого раза, несмотря на фейлы. Так что необходимость следить за морганием, осанкой и дыханием были скорее препятствием, чем дополнением к сюжету и подаче истории. 

В начале игры ходить не так или случайно размахивать руками, задыхаться — прикольно. Но спустя минут 20 или пару уровней, веселье уходит. В игре остаётся только сама история и её персонажи, которых тут всего немного: Сатана, Смерть, Война, сам главный герой, отец главного героя и рассказчик. Основной замут — Сэму надо прожить целые сутки на ручном управлении, чтобы не умереть и не отправиться в ад. Ну и по пути он попадает в разные передряги как в свои, так и между выходцами из ада. История подана без грязи и лютой расчленёнки, имеет пару смешных моментов, а также заигрывание со зрителем, мол, думаешь: случилось что-то плохое, а будет всё хорошо или наоборот. Смерть, который будет сквозным персонажем в этой и ещё в двух играх от тех же авторов — мастер кринжа. Говорит с присказками «йоу», «бро» и прочим псевдопацанским сленгом. А ещё все персонажи вместо «shit», «crap» используют слово «faeces». Так же — сначала забавно, а спустя двадцать минут одного и того же — скучно.

С одной стороны, короткие уровни и сама игра — это хорошо, потому что игра не выдыхается. Ты оглянуться не успел, а уже титры. С другой стороны, контента и правда мало. В апреле этого года вышел чуть ли не ремастер игры внутри самой игры, в котором добавили достижения, в т.ч. по спидрану. Не знаю, был ли он раньше, но только соревнование на скорость и в особых условиях (например, дышать не больше пяти раз за уровень) дают игре какую-то изюминку. Я вот не любитель таких соревнований, поэтому игра для меня закончилась. 

Ситуацию могли бы исправить достижения, но их не так много и они довольно простые — половину я собрал в первое прохождение, а ради остальных нужно спидранить. Да и сами достижения скучноваты: есть лишь одно забавное. Оно сквозное — сначала надо активировать кое-что на первом уровне, а потом — на последнем. Вышло это довольно случайно и забавно, притом оно построено на косячном управлении Самуэлем — странно, что больше таких приколов не добавили. Так, многие фейлы просто встречаются сарказмом от рассказчика, притом с кучей повторений.

Ну, вот так как-то. Оцениваю игру как 50/50: за идею — лайк, за скоротечность — дизлайк, но в Steam оставлю положительный отзыв, т.к. занижать рейтинг негативным было бы грубо. Посмотрим, что авторы выдадут в [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1095120/Helheim_Hassle/]следующей игре[/url].

Шведы дали вторую жизнь прекрасной игре на NES, малоизвестной за пределами Японии, потому что очень по ней фанатели. Запустив игру, я увидел довольно простенький уровень с бесконечными жизнями и просто диким количеством чекпоинтов. И ожидал было ремейка в агуша-стиле, но уже второй уровень заставил передумать, а уж дальше какие трюки потом начались...

Эта игра, по сути, исправляет главный недостаток первой части - то, что та была экспериментальной игрой с уникальной механикой метания звезды, подчиняющейся гравитации, на которой можно было ездить. При этом тогда ещё не было выработано понимания "стандартного долгого платформера" в виде, например, поздних игр про Марио, не было, и уровни в игре были довольно простые и не давали вдоволь разгуляться. Ну то есть основной недостаток первой части - это отсутствие продолжения с учётом опыта левелдизайна за прошедшее время 🙂 Количество уровней-то тут осталось такое же, но их размеры стали гораздо больше.

И эта затея удалась: игра теперь триксовый платформер из кучи коротких, но сложных участков, на каждый из который уйдёт много попыток. А уж если секреты открывать, то там вообще будут ядрёный полосы препятствий, где надо выкладываться по полной и тщательно продумывать траектории бросков. Важен как разгон перед метанием звезды, так и из какой точки прыжка это будет сделано - если бросить перед самым приземлением, то она сильнее оттолкнётся и прыгнет ещё выше, чем в середине прыжка. Это всё было и в первой игре, с удивлением это обнаружил, но там это было просто не нужно в виду малого количества мест для исполнения таких трюков. [h1] 二向无常，无往而遇。万道无常，花开唯心。 [/h1]
对比前作再次进步，虽然仍有缺点、但已经是瑕不掩瑜到让我十分喜爱、愿意多次通关、想要推荐的一部作品了。

游戏性依旧是短板，但终于算是来到及格线了，整体可以概括为 在太空中探索收集物资、升级飞船、去到各种各样的地点场所、遇到各种人和事，再加上一些解密、一点点资源管理和随机roll点玩法。

画面虽然算不上精致，但形成了较为独特的美术风格、同时一些细节也能够到位地表达出丰富的叙事与情感，因此对我来说已经算不上缺点。

优点其实也显而易见了：世界观、剧情叙事、角色塑造、音乐。本作以东方神话为基础设计了一套较为丰富且完整的世界观，在这套宏大的时空背景下、再拉近叙事角度到男女主角相遇相识相知的冒险上时 让其中的故事变得更具感染力。而总是恰到好处响起的音乐更是对游戏叙事的情感烘托、以及关键时刻的情绪爆发起到了升华效果，可以说本作高光时刻的体验绝对离不开它们。此外，游戏后续更新的配音同样是加分项，对比日配我个人更推荐中配。

也许游戏的叙事并非完美，例如前两章叙事节奏较慢、后期部分剧情缺少一些更合理的发力点、又或是角色存在更多的可塑造空间，但龙脉常歌已经用细腻动人的情感讲述了一段足够温暖浪漫、让我百感交集回味无穷的故事。

[h1] OPUS系列——匠心叙事 [/h1]
系列风格其实很明确，独特浪漫的世界观背景、动人的叙事、细腻的情感、恰到好处动人心弦的音乐、再加上一般般的游戏性。这样的特点在游玩过程中让我想到了我最喜欢的游戏之一【去月球】，事实证明它们也确实有相似之处，而【龙脉常歌】更是同样被我列入最喜爱列表。

按发售顺序玩下来能很明显地感受到全方面的不断提升，哪怕是作为短板的游戏性也在进步。我对这类重剧情游戏的游戏性要求不高，只要不为难我 无聊一些没关系，因此对该系列的玩法部分还算能接受。

而来到十分想夸的长板剧情部分，出于剧透考量其实很多话写了又删，有很多想夸想分享，但又更想把更多的触动留给打算要玩的人去感受。这个系列有些不可思议的一点在于，每一部都是早早就能猜到结局、【龙脉常歌】更是直接采用倒叙的模式把时间线结尾放在游戏开头，但仍然能吸引我沉浸地去体验去想要了解故事。

而另一大绝对长板的音乐部分，更是同样需要亲自体验才能感受到其优秀，因此我十分建议游玩过程中佩戴耳机，尤其是【龙脉常歌】这部作品。不仅是因为本身游戏一部分玩法需要根据声音解密，更是因为如果没有音乐，游戏中多数高光时刻的体验都会大打折扣。

之前偶然看到一个捆绑包叫做“东方叙事匠心合辑”，所选游戏我并没有全部体验到，但【龙脉常歌】这部作品对我来说 绝对值得位列其中。

Uno de los mejores juegos basados en el universo de los monstruos digitales. 
A pesar de sus bajos costes de producción, se nota el cariño que le han puesto los responsables a este título. La historia empieza de forma lenta pero cuando se centra en desarrollar los misterios y el lore, se pone todo muy interesante y atrevido. Los personajes no son los más profundos, pero se les agarra aprecio.
Hay dos tramas paralelas:
-Cyber Sleuth: eres un detective digital que deberá salvar dos mundos y detener a una megacorporación, el tono es más jovial y optimista. Se tocan temas como el deber, la amistad, la manipulación, el fracaso y descubrir la verdad.
-Hacker's Memory: eres un hacker que deberá ensuciarse las manos para recuperar su identidad robada, el tono es más oscuro y psicológico. Contiene subtramas tristes y más drama en general. Se tocan temas como el ciberacoso, el robo y tráfico de cuentas, la consciencia y las enfermedades no descubiertas.
Los apartados más redondos del juego son el sistema de crianza y evolución y el combate.
La línea evolutiva de los Digimon es muy abierta y con multitud de ramificaciones a escoger, también puedes involucionar para acumular ABI, primero solo te pedirán cosas como cierto nivel, defensa o velocidad e INT, pero las evoluciones más raras requerirán fusiones con otros Digimon o equipar huevos especiales. Hay una granja digital para depositar a los Digimon y que se queden entrenando para subir estadísticas concretas.
El combate es el clásico combate por turnos, y vaya si funciona. Hay que tener en cuenta las debilidades de Tipo y Atributo. 
Sin embargo, el juego dista de ser perfecto, esto se nota en: los gráficos y animaciones simplonas, las mazmorras increíblemente sosas y pasilleras, las misiones secundarias de relleno, el no poder acelerar los diálogos (u omitirlos) y el hecho de tener que farmear mucha experiencia para que los bosses más difíciles no te machaquen.
La música es pasable, el problema es que varias veces se repiten los mismos temas.

P.D: Sin ánimo de ofender, este juego me parece mejor que prácticamente todos los Pokémon modernos. No leo lloros...

This game is something special. I don't even think it's the Kingdom Hearts vibe that sells it. The developers really nailed a unique combat style blending constant movement with attack chains that feel natural and uninhibited. Really, if you're a fan of action games, you need to at least try this out, but you probably won't go wrong with a purchase. 

Here are the only issues I've found, and these might be my own bias: 
- The linear feel of the game isn't a big deal if there were more enemies spread throughout the stages. Instead, it feels like you're just walking from one battle arena to the next, which makes the in-between sections feel meaningless and boring. Add more content variety in the levels. 
- The blocking seems off. It's manageable, but really seems to connect at random. Instead, the gameplay tends towards dodging and movement, which isn't a big deal but you can tell certain enemies were designed around the perfect blocking mechanic. 
- The voice acting, and general plot seems like all of your basic shonen anime tropes rolled into a single experience. Big bad guy who literally snaps his fingers to use instant transmission, loud-mouth protagonists who speak in "cocky" lingo, and characters that seem adjust to their godlike combat ability being thrust onto them even though they've never fought before. 

Anyways, I can look past all of that for the sheer reason that this game oozes passion and love. Really, the pros, in my opinion, WAY outweigh any of the cons. At the end of the day, it's a fantastic action game with incredibe upside given this is just early access. Way to Nukefist and I can't wait to see what you guys come up with next. :)

It keeps the formula that makes this type of 2D platformer fun and improves many aspects from the prequel. I consider it the best "Sonic-like" game available and hope to see more of the franchise in the future.

[b]Art and Sound:[/b] The art is better, more detailed, and the soundtrack is also pretty good. There's room for improvement on some bosses' animations.

[b]Level Design:[/b] This is where the game shines. The levels are unique and fun, whether you want to rush through as fast as possible or explore every nook and cranny. The Battlesphere Challenges add some unique flavour to the mix.

[b]Gameplay:[/b] The controls are responsive enough, as they should be in this type of game, but there are a few minor issues, like sporadic clipping problems or situational input lag (very noticeable when controlling the BFF 3000). Even so, there's nothing that would make the game frustrating or unfair.

[b]Character Gameplay:[/b] The four playable characters each have a unique moveset and playstyle, different enough to justify a replay with each one. The stages are always the same, but each character can explore them differently. The plot also remains mostly the same, with a few extra scenes for every character.

[b]Story:[/b] Freedom Planet is quite plot-heavy for its genre, but I'm glad to see that they reduced the amount of exposition sequences. As for the plot itself, it's ok. There's plenty of world-building, but many key points are left to the player's interpretation.

[b]Difficulty:[/b] Some things are easier; you don't need pro-gamer skills to get S-Rank or beat par time on every stage. However, there's a noticeable difficulty increase in the second half and a VERY noticeable spike near the end. While the game offers greater challenges, you also have more tools (items and potions) to even things out. Everything is doable with some practice. Prepare to die a lot in the final boss(es), though.

My favorite 2d platformer of all time. Extremely fun movement, creative and adequately long levels, a fun combat that caught be by surprise, and gorgeous visuals throughout the entire game. Fun characters in a plot that is totally not inspired by Sonic Adventure 2 in the slightest nuh uh no way. Worst parts are the seemingly pointless item system, the multiple playable characters seeming to have differing routes just to end up all playing every level, and classic mode being locked behind completion of the story, which while not a complaint for me (I walked around and talked to every NPC like a crazy person) I can see being a detractor. If you like the blue rodent's 2d outings, I am extremely confident you will also like this game.

I really wish there was something in between "yes" and "no" on Steam, because this is really the lightest "not recommended" I can manage. It looks and sounds lovely, and the tone is sweet, but there is just nothing here. The plot plods along as slowly as Harold himself shuffles through the hallways of the ship, to a disappointingly predictable outcome. Only in the end does it start to open up into something quite beautiful, but you earn it with too many chores and fetch quests. This game marked the first time in my 35 years of gaming that I literally fell asleep with a controller in my hand.

There are great walking simulators and visual novels where you do nothing in particular as far as gameplay goes--Kentucky Route Zero comes to mind--but those games had something special that this game just doesn't. It's a shame that the game gives you this incredible visual sensibility, but makes you wish it would just be over already.

Черпаем вдохновение у Уэса Андерсона, "не верим в худо" ft. Neverhood, помним о великом подводном BioShock и получаем на свет милого Гарольда - интерактивный мультсериал, в жанре "симулятор ходьбы".

Что понравилось:
+ Вся работа создана вручную (декорации, персонажи)
+ Чилловая музыка (заглавная тема в топе любимых ОСТов теперь)
+ Добрый сюжет, его посыл и душевный финал
+ Многие сцены и диалоги - прямое попадание в сердечко

Что НЕ понравилось:
- Душный геймплей. Много придётся ходить из точки А в точку Б и обратно...
- Долгая раскачка в самом начале
- Мало интерактивностей с окружением, пазлов (если и есть, то весьма примитивные)
- Многие персонажи, диалоги и ситуации выглядят нарочито аутистичными, что порой забавит, но в основном напрягает

По итогу имеем хороший мультфильм, который не всем придётся по вкусу. Сократить бы продолжительность, добавить интересных взаимодействий с миром (не в виде одних лишь диалогов) и вышло бы замечательно.
