Un metroidvania con unos gráficos hermosos, una historia épica y personajes llenos de carisma.

Dust: An Elysian Tail es un metroidvania de acción y aventura que, no solo tiene muy buenos gráficos y música, sino una jugabilidad muy frenética y espectacular con unas animaciones increíbles que hace que hasta el golpe más simple se vea de maravilla.

Además que, por supuesto, presenta una historia de fantasía llena de personajes que con solo ver sus diseños te enamoras de ellos.

Simplemente juégalo. Es un juego muy bueno y divertido que merece cada céntimo que cuesta.




Sin hacer spoilers:

La historia trata de Dust, un joven con una ropa extraña que no sabe quien es y que desea conocer su pasado.

Se despierta en mitad del bosque mediante la llamada de una espada mágica parlante llamada Ahrah la cual afirma que él le ha invocado y más adelante una criatura llamada Fidget (a la que quiero mucho por lo adorable que es) le sigue porqué es la guardiana de la espada.


Y así es como comienza la aventura:

Dust intenta averiguar quien es y en el camino ayudará a otros personajes mientras salva el mundo de una amenaza mayor.

Y durante el trayecto, Fidget le ayudará mientras nosotros disfrutamos de su ternura y divertida actitud que hará que este viaje sea muy agradable con su presencia.




Ahora: hablemos de la jugabilidad.

Como ya he dicho antes, Dust: An Elysian Tail es un metroidvania, pero también es un hack and slash con toques de RPG.

La razón es porque, aunque su diseño de niveles es claramente el de un metroidvania en el que obtendremos nuevas habilidades que mejorarán nuestro movimiento para ir a lugares inalcanzables, su sistema de combate se asemeja más a un hack and slash en el que deberemos luchar contra múltiples enemigos haciendo toda clase de combos mientras obtenemos experiencia y subimos de nivel para mejorar nuestras estadísticas.

Esto es algo que al principio se sentirá genial, aunque a largo plazo se hace repetitivo (ya explicaré luego el porqué). Pero de momento, quedaos con la idea que el combate es muy disfrutable sobre todo al luchar contra muchos enemigos.

Aunque no puedo decir lo mismo de los jefes, que solo son enemigos con barras de vida más grandes y que no se inmovilizan con nuestros ataques.

Por no decir que Fidget rompe el juego si la mejoramos al máximo. Ella solita hará el suficiente daño como para que ningún combate sea difícil.




Igualmente la jugabilidad de este juego se siente genial.

Todos los movimientos, sobre todo cuando estás luchando en el aire, son extremadamente satisfactorios. Entre que las animaciones se ven muy bien y que la variedad de ataques es buena al inicio, hace que las peleas se disfruten mucho.


Lo mismo va para la exploración:

Entre que los paisajes son hermosos y todos son lo suficientemente diferentes para que cada uno se sienta una zona completamente única, explorar el mapa en busca de sus tesoros y sus llaves es toda una delicia.

Que por cierto, igualmente este juego tiene la manía de subir el porcentaje de completado a más del 100%. El máximo es 117%.

Es una cosa que jamás he terminado de entender porque lo mismo sucede con Hollow Knight con su 112% y desde mi punto de vista esto no hace más que traer confusión.



¡Ah! ¡Y otra cosa que me encanta!

¡ME ENCANTAN LAS ÁREAS DE DESAFÍO!

Son minijuegos opcionales que, si bien al principio solo sirven para darte un objeto, lo de obtener 4 estrellas en cada una de ellas me gustó mucho hacerlo.

Yo que soy muy fan de los juegos de Sonic y de conseguir la mayor puntuación posible en base a la habilidad y la rapidez, estos minijuegos opcionales se me hicieron muy divertidos.




Ahora, no todo es bueno y el juego tiene algunos problemas pequeños (que no arruinan la experiencia pero son una molestia menor):


Primero es que el texto no está bien adaptado resoluciones altas.

Me recuerda un tiempo cuando jugué hace muchos años al League of Legends en 4k. Se veía muy bien pero al mismo tiempo el texto era demasiado pequeño y no se leía bien nada.

Desde mi punto de vista esto se podría arreglar con una actualización. Vale que este juego ya no da dinero a Microsoft, pero que mínimo para que la gente que compra ahora el juego lo pueda jugar en condiciones decentes.


Pero segundo es el tema del viaje rápido.

O sea, me parece muy bien que limiten esto y solo se puedan usar los portales con una piedra de teletransportación (que por cierto, no es muy cara).

Pero lo que no me parece bien es que solo se utilizan para salir de un nivel y no para entrar.

Es decir, solo puedes usar la piedra de teletransportación cuando estás encima de uno y quieres salir del nivel para ir a otro lugar. Pero cuando vas al nuevo lugar, solo puedes ir por las entradas y no a un teletransportador, el cual acaba haciendo el juego más aburrido cuando lo quieres completar al 100% porque tienes que pasar por todo el maldito nivel para llegar a ese sitio específico que está al lado de un teletransportador.


Y por último, están sus enemigos.

Mirad, se que he dicho que el combate se ve genial y es divertido hacer combos, pero cuando ya llevas un rato jugando se hace muy repetitivo.

Y gran parte de la culpa es que quisieron hacer enemigos muy sosos. Hay poca variedad y ninguno viene a ser una verdadera amenaza. Solo los gigantes (y solo es porque si te dan un golpe te hacen muchísimo daño).


Al final, este juego no se siente como un hack and slash, sino como un musou:

Mucha cantidad de enemigos que son más bien dianas portátiles en las que usar tus poderes, que no dan ni medio golpe, no vaya a ser que te interrumpan el combo y pierdas la bonificación de experiencia.











En resumen:

Un juego de acción y aventura precioso, con una gran historia y personajes y un sistema de combate muy disfrutable al principio pero que acaba volviéndose repetitivo al final.


Lo que está claro es una cosa:

Dust: An Elysian Tail es un juego que entra muy bien por los ojos y los oidos. Su historia es muy buena y sus personajes son mejores todavía (en especial Fidget. Amo a Fidget).

Se que hay mucha gente que no opina tan bien de este juego en la actualidad, sobre todo desde que salió Hollow Knight y marcó un estándar de calidad muy alto en el genero. Porque seamos realistas, Dust: An Elysian Tail es un juego muy bien valorado por sus aspectos técnicos como los gráficos, la música y el doblaje.

Pero como metroidvania... hay mejores.


Aún así, desde mi punto de vista sigue siendo un juego muy bueno.

No niego sus fallos. Acepto que cuando ya estaba terminando el juego me empezó a aburrir y empecé a verle más las costuras y sus aspectos positivos no me parecieron para tanto.

Pero igualmente, Dust: An Elysian Tail es un juego que he disfrutado mucho. Creo que Fidget hizo casi el 80%, pero realmente disfruté hacer las misiones, encontrar los tesoros y las llaves, completar los desafíos con 4 estrellas y ver su emocionante final.

Y por el precio que vale, creo que tú también deberías hacer lo mismo.

这游戏做的很棒，但是取自现实题材是他最讽刺的点。
无法想象这样的学校依旧在不知名的角落开着，更无法想象杨某的现实原型其实活的依旧有滋有味。这几年揭露此现象的报道数不胜数，但仍旧是烧不尽的歪风邪气。
对此我相和揭露这些的记者与热心群众表示敬意，同时也想要对还处在这种环境的学生们表达祝愿：祝愿他们早日在黑暗中破茧 ，于光明处化蝶！

玩了4个小时，打到了结局，有些遗憾，一个隐藏结局都没有打出来。游戏本身质量挺在线，难度和紧张程度很适当，不论作为电影还是互动游戏，都给予了我不错的参与感，作为一个想表达一些东西的作品，这部作品满分100可以打80分。
      但是这种剧，还是得讲讲剧情，剧情可能因为篇幅问题，主干都是围绕着“逃离”去铺垫的，主人公的设定很多过于理想化与宿命化，尤其是院长把监察的重担交接给刚犯错的主角时，简直是给了开挂般的权限，这很扯，但估计为了时长与通顺（贯穿其他成员的好感与连接），作者已经尽量表现的很自然。
     其次是教官收贿，与院长之“恶”，刘教官虽然狠毒嗜赌，但没有过多体罚学生，学生看起来还都挺生龙活虎，甚至后期主角还能沟通起来，和一出场印象完全不同，甚至后期直接成了引仇恨背锅的，院长虽然失手电死过学生，但除了电击禁闭外对学生没做过于出格的事，貌似想搞表里不一的形象，但最终没有刻画的很完全。这两个人是剧里想描绘的典型反派，但描绘的过程中又没有把坏事做绝，虽然招恨，但想造成一种穷凶极恶，以至于逮捕发疯的行为力度不足，简而言之，坏人刻画的有点太正直了，可能是因为我读书入社会时遇到过差不多的，我觉得他们的行为应该更恶劣吧。
       还有食堂，通过很多对话知道是想表达院长的极端以及恶劣的态度对学生，想表达给学生的食物越来越劣质，但最后，镜头下给犯过错的主角喝牛奶，以及精致的食物布置，完全体现不出这一层含义，让人感觉不到其想表达的“恶劣”。
        还有医生这个角色，其最后的结局比较少，跟着院长得不到好处，她以及楠楠还有死去的角色感觉都是虎头蛇尾的感觉，虽然不可或缺，但达成了结局后成为了一颗弃子，背景可以做文章的地方很多，结局之后一切却突然戛然而止，她们的结局并不完美，甚至并不完全，挖坑不埋。
       男主最后戴草帽好像离开学校半年都没回家，我不知道，这是打算如何铺垫，家里矛盾就如此之大？描绘的太仓促了，有点令人摸不着头脑。
       最后总结一下，缺点是学校的“恶”给人感觉不够“恶”，没有与严格的寄宿制学校做特别大的分割。以及人物背景想讲述很多东西，但挖坑却没填，戛然而止。但最终故事还是比较完整的讲述完了，逻辑上没有太大漏洞，演员演技也很到位，这些都是加分项，综合体验还不错，希望能更好吧。

I like this game, which might be surprising since I am not recommending it.
The reason I am not recommending it in its current state is because there are a lot of excruciatingly frustrating aspects of the game.

1) Your partner is absolutely useless. If you have control of the situation, he'll often arrest one and deprive you of the XP you worked for. If you detain one in handcuffs, and run to catch the second he will do the opposite and let the first one escape instead of arresting them. This means that in a situation where you have two fleeing suspects, one will almost always escape unless the AI was dumb enough to hide in a dumpster adjacent to where you're detaining the first. You can summon backup, but they seem to be very adept at letting people escape too as there is no way to 'direct' any allied NPCs.

2) Whenever you quit the game, you will lose all the XP you earned that shift and advance the number of shifts by one. There is no way to just restart a shift.

3) When a car chase starts, two things will eventually become apparent. First, every vehicle seems to be able to out-accelerate your cruiser (and if you use either of the first 2 vehicle unlocks, they will also have a higher top speed than you). The amount of XP you will earn is simply not large enough considering how long these chases can take.

4) There's a variety of side-objectives - races, time trials, that sort of thing. If you have any arrested suspects in your vehicle, they will vanish, so you either have to drive them all the way back to the precinct before trying one of these, or else sacrifice 80% of the booking XP by calling for an escort.

5) To interact with a vehicle, you have to be pointed at exactly the right spot. The spot to issue a parking ticket is too close to the spot where you order a tow truck and both are too close to the door.

6) Restarting a race causes time to elapse, but you can't see how much until the you're done. Making it very easy to use up an entire shift on race due to the disadvantages you have.

These design choices take away from what is otherwise, a pretty unique and fun game.

I'm going to go continue playing despite all this.

Confesso que fui surpreendido pela Dead Island Definitive Edition. Esperava um jogo datado, mas me deparei com uma experiência visceral, caótica e, acima de tudo, divertidíssima, que envelheceu muito melhor do que imaginava.

O jogo nos joga em Banoi, um paraíso tropical transformado em inferno zumbi. A premissa é simples: você é um dos poucos imunes e precisa sobreviver. A história em si é medíocre, servindo mais como pano de fundo para a carnificina. Os personagens são esquecíveis e as cutscenes, muitas vezes, são mais engraçadas do que dramáticas. Mas, sinceramente, isso pouco importa quando o combate é tão satisfatório.

A jogabilidade é o coração absoluto do jogo. O foco no combate corpo a corpo é brilhante. Não é sobre atirar, é sobre sentir o peso de um taco de beisebol, a crueldade de uma lâmina enferrujada e a criatividade macabra de modificar suas armas. A sensação de desmembrar zumbis, quebrar seus membros e vê-los reagir aos golpes é incrivelmente bem executada. O sistema de crafting, que permite adicionar eletricidade, fogo ou veneno às suas armas, adiciona uma camada deliciosa de estratégia e caos.

A progressão de RPG, com árvore de habilidades e personagens com especialidades únicas (como o Sam B com armas contundentes ou a Xian Mei com lâminas), dá uma boa motivação para rejogar. No entanto, o jogo sofre com a repetição incessante de missões. "Vá ali, pegue isso, traga aquilo" é o pão nosso de cada dia e pode cansar se jogado por longas sessões sozinho.

Falando nisso, jogar sozinho é uma experiência, mas jogar em co-op é A experiência. A campanha para até 4 jogadores transforma o jogo. Os momentos de tensão viram gargalhadas quando um amigo é arremessado por um zumbi gigante ou quando um bug esquisito faz o carro sair voando. É no multiplayer que a alma de Dead Island realmente brilha, mesmo que o matchmaking hoje esteja praticamente morto; é preciso combinar com amigos.

A versão Definitive Edition entrega no visual. Os cenários são lindos, com texturas em HD, iluminação e efeitos de sombra que revitalizaram o jogo. A ilha paradisíaca devastada cria um contraste belo e aterrorizante. No entanto, a remasterização não corrigiu e, em alguns casos, até piorou vários bugs. Personagens atravessando paredes, itens desaparecendo e problemas de áudio são quebras de imersão frequentes.

Dead Island é um jogo de contradições. Tem uma história fraca, mas uma jogabilidade viciante. É visualmente bonito, mas tecnicamente instável. Pode ser repetitivo sozinho, mas é uma das experiências co-op mais divertidas do gênero.

Se você é fã de zumbis, gosta de um combate visceral e brutal, e tem um ou dois amigos para se juntar à carnificina, este jogo é uma joia imperfeita, porém indispensável. Apenas entre sabendo que não virá para uma narrativa profunda, e sim para a pura e simples alegria de esmagar, cortar e eletrocutar hordas de mortos-vivos em um paraíso tropical que deu horrivelmente errado. É um caos lindo.

Dark Envoy is an indie Combat RPG for people who like RTwP. Rejoice!

The character creation aspects, and the RPG side in general are relatively light, but are enough to connect and justify the exploration and encounters, provide skill trees/progression, and it's more fulsome than their previous game. The setting is a mixture of standard fantasy/magic fayre with some sci-fi and gunpowder, and it works well.

The game has some bugs and some jank (the most annoying thing being sometimes having to click orders multiple times in combat) although post-release support has been strong right up to the day I'm writing this, a lot of things have been patched and a 2.0 version is coming, which is welcome.

The combat is quite good - there are some nice interesting mechanics in here, painting attacks is a favorite of mine - it isn't all just rote repetition of what's been done elsewhere.  The game allows both slow time, or fully paused for tactical mode, (you can adjust this by hitting tab when in tactical mode).

Overall, it's not perfect so be aware of that (we're looking forward to that 2.0 release, Event Horizon) but it's fun, and worth checking out for those who love pause and play RPG combat. It's great to see a smaller dev supporting RTwP play.

That is, if you can stomach '90s era edgy boi crassness, tons of gore, uncomfortable situations, and the philosophical ramblings of a teenage nihilistic stoner. This is basically to video games what Troma, at its height, was to motion pictures. The gameplay is jank af, but the bonkers, albeit nonsensical, story is entertaining as hell. Over the last while I’ve found myself getting more and more into roguelikes, and Path of Achra is easily one of the best surprises I’ve come across. It’s sharp, stylish, and confidently strange, like a game that knows exactly what it wants to be and executes on it with almost ritual precision on the Path to rogueness.

At first, Achra gives you the basics—move, strike, survive—but once you start unlocking the different cults, classes, and these wonderfully unhinged devotions to various desert spirits, the whole thing opens up. Suddenly you’re mixing thorn-eaters with stormcallers, or binding yourself to some inscrutable god of dust and decay, and the game just nods and says, “Sure, try it.” Half the fun is discovering that some bizarre combination you picked on a whim is actually devastating… at least until something ancient and irritated swats you into the sand. Loss is frequent, but it’s the good kind of loss—the kind that sends you back in for another run before you’ve even processed the last one.

The pacing is a huge win. Runs are intense but quick; you don’t need to carve out an entire Saturday to make meaningful progress. I can jump in, experiment with some weird devotion-tree interaction, and walk away feeling like I’ve uncovered a brand-new approach in under an hour. As someone who doesn’t have the same uninterrupted time I once did, that’s invaluable.

Visually, the game is minimal but striking, leaning into this mythic, sun-scorched aesthetic that suits the world perfectly. Every sprite feels intentional, every colour choice deliberate, and the whole thing radiates this low-grade mysticism without ever getting loud about it. The writing, too, carries that same energy—small pieces of lore that feel like they’ve been carved into stone rather than shouted at you.

The combat is where everything really comes together. It’s turn-based, but fast enough that it never feels like you’re waiting around. You make a choice, the world reacts, and suddenly you’re adapting in this steady rhythm that feels almost meditative. Once you start messing with devotion upgrades, aspect mutations, and all the little mechanical modifiers, the layers start stacking in a way that’s incredibly satisfying.

The OST and sound are incredibly simple but effective. The music keeps a steady atmospheric hum that backs the action without distracting from it, and the effects—your strikes, blasts of wind, the skittering of some sand-drenched horror—are clean and crisp. It’s not a cinematic score, and it doesn’t need to be. The audio sits comfortably in the background, quietly reinforcing the world’s mood while letting the gameplay take the lead.

I’ve put in a good number of hours, and every time I think I’ve got things figured out, the game throws me a new devotion path or class twist that completely changes how I will approach the game next. 

I’m entirely comfortable saying that Path of Achra has become one of my favourite modern roguelikes: deep, replayable, stylish, and full of those “okay, that was awesome” moments that make you immediately dive back in. It’s a rare game that feels both carefully crafted and joyfully unrestrained—and Achra nails that balance.

To add insult to injury, the game requires you to download free packs off of its Steam page to unlock the Labyrinth of Amala and True Demon ending, alongside Raido Kuzunoha. Pontos positivos:
1) A ambientação do jogo é excelente, eu realmente me senti em um mundo pós-apocalipse, em alguns momentos até lembra um game de terror. Por exemplo, no início do game tem que explorar um hospital vazio com alguns fantasmas, é claro que não chega a dar medo nem nada, mas fica um clima tenso.

2) Em vários aspectos é uma expansão e uma melhora dos dois primeiros SMT. Geralmente o jogo tinha três rotas e por consequência três finais, mas no 3 isso foi expandido para termos mais finais. O sistema de fusão de demônios tá bem melhor e mais instintivo, nos games anteriores não era tão fácil fazer fusão boa e eu até procurei guias de fusão, pois no 3 eu simplesmente fui jogando e fui conseguindo fusões boas, fluiu muito melhor.

3) O nível de dificuldade é bem satisfatório, com o normal sendo um pouco difícil porém perfeitamente jogável, e o hard sendo para quem quer sofrer.

4) O sistema de escolher uma build para o protagonista é excelente, além de você mesmo distribuir os stats também é você que escolhe quais skills vai aprender, e o sistema é flexível o suficiente para conseguir trocar de build mesmo estando longe no jogo, não tem aquela coisa de "oops acho que eu devia começar um new game porque fiz coisa errada".

Pontos negativos:
1) Sendo um jogo do PS2, eu tava esperando uma história mais desenvolvida, mas ele segue o padrão dos SMT de snes, ou seja, a história não é ruim, mas ela claramente não é o destaque do jogo, ela tá lá mais como pano de fundo.

2) O new game+ poderia carregar mais coisas da primeira run, seria bem mais interessante. Eu comecei um NG+ e fiquei muito decepcionado quando vi que o protagonista não carrega nada, ele começa fraco igual da primeira vez e você tem que fazer uma build do zero de novo.

Твердолобый, воспринимающий все выражения напрямую, из-за чего множество смешных моментов связаны с ним. Грут – дерево-гуманоид, последний в своем роде. Спокойный и рассудительный, за частую останавливающий взрывной нрав Ракеты.

    [u] Сюжет [/u] игры незауряден (а какой еще может быть в супергеройке), при этом отнюдь не скучный. Игра пытается поднимать важные и драматичные темы, при этом делает это легко и непринужденно. В основе стоит тема утраты и принятия. Каждый из Стражей кого-то потерял или что-то пережил. Игра делает акцент на этом. Главный посыл заключается в том, что не стоит жить в своих иллюзиях, необходимо принять все невзгоды и жить дальше.

     В первую очередь естественно мне понравилась химия между всеми членами отряда. Они постоянно пытаются стебать друг друга, шутить. За ними приятно смотреть и наблюдать, так как в них чувствуется искренность и живость. У них возникают конфликты и по ходу игры они пытаются уладить все разногласия. Персонажи очень много разговаривают, даже слишком много) Они постоянно что-то обсуждают. Игра даже стебется над этим в конце, [spoiler]ведь финального босса Стражи буквально побеждают своей болтологией [/spoiler], понимая, что у них к этому есть талант (бесить всех). По ходу игры возникают иногда очень кринжовые и абсурдные ситуации, но они не ломают повествования, благодаря абсурдному поведению персонажей, так как ты проникаешься ими. Мы можем принимать те или иные варианты развития событий, но кардинально сильно от этого сюжет не меняется (это все-таки не РПГ).
В игре множество отсылок на других супергероев, а также в целом на комиксы и фильмы Marvel.

     Что касается [u]геймплея[/u] то, как было описано выше играем мы только за Звездного лорда, все остальные стражи исполняют наши приказы по ходу боя. У каждого из стражей, включая Питера, есть 4 способности. 3 из них можно прокачать, зарабатывая очки прокачки, а четвертую можно получить по сюжету, в определенные моменты, когда каждый из стражей преодолеет свои страхи или же смириться со своей утратой. Сам же Питер вооружен дополнительно своими бластерами. У бластеров помимо основного режима стрельбы есть стихийные способности. Они помогают в бою (так как некоторые враги уязвимы к некоторым видам урона) и преодолевать препятствия, решая платформенные головоломки. Какой-то тактической глубины в способностях нет, я неоднократно нажимал их хаотично, за это игра меня не наказывала. В основном вся игра сводится к отстрелу болванчиков.
Каждый из стражей может помогать не только в бою. К примеру, Грут может сделать мост из своих веток, Дракс может перетащить тяжелые предметы, по которым можно вскарабкаться, Гамора может зацепится за стену и подбросить Питера, а Ракета в силу своего малого роста способен пролезть туда, куда другие не могут.

        Не смотря на все шутки, плюсы и положительную атмосферу, игра не без минусов. В первую очередь это удручающее техническое состояние игры, было много багов, застреваний, а моментов, когда игра вылетала просто не счесть. Бывали иногда скучные моменты, особенно когда приходилось просто долго добираться куда-то. У игры есть одновременно забавная и немного бесящая особенность, которая заключается в том, что ты думаешь, что она сейчас закончится, но нет, происходят новые события. Злодеи и босс файты, получились беззубыми, не хватает челленджа (хотя для казуалов это, наоборот, плюс).

        Если подводить итоги, то Стражи Галактики это хорошая, добрая, смешная и развлекающая игра, в ней можно хорошо отдохнуть и кайфануть. Игра, которой не нужно быть идеальной. Всем советую!

[b]Гра, яка повертає у літо - а може, навіть у те саме, з дитинства.[/b]
Вона сподобається тим, кому до вподоби Animal Crossing. Тут навіть трапляються схожі анімації, але головне - знайомий тип мешканців: милі, наївні й дуже добрі. Саме вони створюють той самий затишний вайб.

[h3]Сюжет[/h3]
Головна мета - дістатися вершини гори та подзвонити мамі, повідомивши, що ви безпечно приїхали на відпочинок до тітоньки Мей.

[h3]Світ та мешканці[/h3]
По дорозі нагору ви зустрінете безліч мешканців і туристів: хтось рибалить, хтось бігає, хтось займається альпінізмом. З кожним можна поспілкуватися, допомогти або чомусь навчитися - це приємно урізноманітнює шлях і додає грі затишного життєвого ритму.

Світ гри нагадує той час, коли тобі шість, і кожна зустріч - маленьке відкриття. Це той дивовижний період, коли всі діти справді різні: хтось збирає фантики не тому, що вони красиві, а тому що смачно пахнуть; хтось придумує небачену гру й щасливий, що ти граєш разом; хтось любить бігати й щиро радіє змаганню; а хтось просто багатий на цукерки та пригощає кожного нового друга.

У грі повно таких персонажів - ніби з дитинства. Це можна й не усвідомлювати, але дуже легко відчути. І ця атмосфера нагадує ту саму магію, якою славиться Nintendo.

[h3]Геймплей[/h3]
До речі про Nintendo. У плані геймплею гра найбільше нагадує пригодницькі моменти з The Legend of Zelda. Тут можна парити, злітати високо над островом, знаходити різні способи пересування, грати з місцевими мешканцями - загалом світ створено так, що хочеться користуватися буквально всім, до чого дотягнешся. Він живий і природно відгукується на ваші дії, як і його жителі.

[h3]Темп гри та тривалість[/h3]
Гру можна пробігти за дві години, а можна провести в ній десять - тут справді є чим зайнятися. І якщо ви зайдете лише на годинку-дві, це теж нормально: вона приймає будь-який темп, який ви оберете.

[◉°] Even though this is a threequel, it remains charming, especially for those who enjoy searching for mysticism in everyday places that change with the onset of darkness. Unfortunately, the increase in scale hasn't done the game any favors. Now it can feel more repetitive and sometimes empty. There are still some interesting new ideas, but the threequel is inferior to its predecessors. Now there are "bosses" at the end of each chapter, and honestly, this is one of the weakest aspects. They are simply uninteresting, not hard, but sometimes frustrating (especially the final one). However, the story is still consistent with the spirit of the series, there are plenty of secrets and items to collect, and now you can play as your OS, although the customization options are quite limited. It may not be the best part (gameplay-wise), but it's definitely not even close to bad. Hope for another sequel, as this is a unique series that I couldn't help but fall in love with.

Loved the setting and the visuals, enjoyed the story as well, but the gameplay was a bit of a mixed bag for me. As a huge fan of Alien: Isolation, I expected this to be a lot better after getting hyped from the demo.

The stalker is the biggest issue, really. She's almost always nearby, her hearing range is very good (so you might as well forget about your sprint button; running makes far too much noise), and is extremely fast. If she notices you, she's relentless in giving chase, and is very quick to open doors you might close behind you while trying to run away.

Finding a hiding spot is also somewhat frustrating; since the stalker is so fast, you don't really have a lot of time to search, which often results in stumbling around in the dark and getting lost while she's right behind you (so even if you do climb into a safe spot, she will see it and drag you out). It also doesn't help that the icon indicating hiding spots only appears when you're standing very close to them, and it's not immediately obvious at a glance which areas can be used for such purposes. I would often look at the interaction icons and confuse sliding doors with hiding places, or go "okay, so is this a chest I can open, or is it just a hiding place?" So again, this results in a lot of frantic searching around the house while the creature gives you no time to breathe.

The thing is, while Alien: Isolation gave you tools to rely on, either to distract or temporarily fend off your stalker, Hollow Cocoon gives you no such items, aside from maybe the limited-use warding talismans located in save rooms. Other than that, your only options are to run or hide, which makes every encounter with the stalker very frustrating. And like I said, it's always patrolling around the house; even Isolation's Xenomorph would retreat into vents temporarily and allow you to explore for a while. No such thing in Hollow Cocoon.

The puzzles are also extremely simple and only exist to give you an excuse to wander around the house and force you to play hide-and-seek with the creature. When you pick up an item, it becomes immediately obvious where it must be used; imagine finding an X and then stumbling across a door with a huge X-shaped keyhole. That's what most of the puzzles are like.

Thankfully, the game is fairly short, meaning it ends before its issues can really become a major source of frustration. And the visuals/atmosphere are genuinely well done. But if you're looking for a fantastic (and terrifying) experience like Alien: Isolation, this is not it.

As much as I would like to recommend this game, I just can't. I am only writing this review in the hopes that the devs see this as I would really like to see this game improve. In it's current state, it feels more like a demo than an actual game. That is because at some point after a lengthy play time, routes get nonsensical no matter what game mode you play. Two of the largest issues I see that make the mid game and beyond almost completely unplayable would be simply fixed by adding a priority system for the passengers. As of right now it appears to be based entirely on distance, but even then it's not solely on distance which leads to a very frustrating experience when trying to set up an optimized network that makes sense so that you can follow a strategy as you build up.

1. The competition AI can simply establish a bus route thousands of miles away and that will cause passengers in your hubs to build up. They won't use your routes to get to closer cities, like you would think if it was solely based on distance. This can lead you to either purchase hundreds of busses for each city in your domain, or you have to get the biggest and most expensive planes for EACH city. This completely breaks down the nature of transportation networks and the use of hubs to make an efficient system. Instead it eventually breaks down to where you have to establish a point to point direct route for EACH city which makes absolutely no practical sense.

2. Passengers will still choose unoptimal routes themselves. In my latest plane only discovery mode game, routes that were previously established in which were working just as intended later became unused for less optimal routes. For example, I was trying to make Baghdad a central hub as that was my starting city and Basra as a collector hub where close iraqi and iranian cities would feed into. However, at some point passengers stopped using this hub to hub connection. So passengers coming from Basra and using Baghdad as a hub to connect to, say, Ankara, stopped using my Basra to Baghdad and instead  go through a city that was in between them. So I had hundreds of passengers line up and wait for this intermediary route that would still take them to Baghdad as I was having planes from Basra to Baghdad run empty. They instead chose the longer and slower route. It makes absolutely no logical sense. And that is not the only route like that, and the illogical priority system worsens as the game advances into a complete shit show.

Imagine managing a grocery store and you have 5 registers open. Now imagine seeing 40 customers line up for one register, and the line just keeps growing and growing when the customers just refuse to use the available capacity. This is an extremely fun and addictive game, but it feels like you are restricted to only early game. So I recommend you just play the demo and have fun with that until the dev is able to tweak the algorithm for passenger priority. Pls dev.

--東風谷早苗がひたすら駆け抜ける、軽快でテンポのいい横スクロールアクション。

■ 概要
『東風谷早苗の神風とともに』は、東方Projectの人気キャラ・東風谷早苗を操作して進む横スクロールアクション。
短めのステージを駆け抜けながら、敵を撃破し、仕掛けを抜けていくシンプル構成のゲームとなっています。
手軽に遊べる“軽アクション作品”として位置づけられ、原作を深く知らなくても遊べる作りです。

■ ゲーム内容と遊び方
本作のゲーム性は、古典的なアクションゲームの流れに近い構造です。

● ステージ制横スクロールアクション
早苗を操作してゴールを目指す。
パターン化された敵やギミックが配置されており、スピード感のある操作で進む。

● 主なアクション
・吸い込みと吐き出しで遠距離攻撃、また敵の能力をコピーし、使用することが出来ます。
・ジャンプ回避
・シンプルな攻撃と回避特化の構成
・アクションはそこまで複雑ではなく、直感的な操作で遊べます。

● ゲームのテンポが良好
テンポは速く、やられてもすぐリトライ可能。
軽快さを重視した“サクッと遊ぶアクション”の設計になっています。

■ 良い点
● シンプルに遊べて分かりやすい
ステージを進みながら敵を倒すだけの直球アクションなので、迷わずプレイ可能。
原作知識ゼロでも問題なく遊べます。

● テンポの良さでプレイ中のストレスが少ない
スピーディに再挑戦できる作りは快適。
「短時間でアクションを楽しみたい」人には最適です。

● 価格に対して遊びやすい構成
シンプル設計なので、手頃なアクションゲームとして十分楽しめます。

■ 悪い点
● 難易度やギミック構成が単調になりがち
直球アクションであるぶん、後半までプレイすると敵のバリエーションや仕掛けの広がりが薄く、単調に感じる場面があります。

● 原作の深い要素は薄め
早苗のキャラ性や東方の濃い演出を期待すると、あっさり気味に感じる可能性あり。

■ 総評
本作は「東風谷早苗でサクっと遊べる横スクロールアクション」としては十分に楽しめる一作です。
内容はかなりシンプルで、凝ったギミックよりテンポの良さを重視した構成。
アクション初心者でも触りやすい反面、ゲーマー視点ではボリュームや変化に物足りなさもあります。
しかし、軽いアクションとして割り切れば快適で遊びやすいゲーム。
東方ファンはもちろん、ちょっとした息抜きにアクションを遊びたい人にも向いています。

向いている人
・サクっと遊べるアクションゲームが好き
・東方キャラ（早苗）が好き
・軽量でストレスなく進むゲームを求めている
・シンプル操作で遊べる作品が好き

向いていない人
・ギミックや戦闘に深いゲーム性を求める
・濃い原作演出やストーリーを期待している
・長時間遊べるアクションを探している

A Furi-like bossrush game. This game is definitely above average for a Touhou doujin title and comes close to greatness in several areas but lacking in some.

Things I Like:
[list]
[*] Cirno as the protagonist and Reimu as the antagonist — a rare setup.
[*]  Roguelike mode — a plus, though I didn’t play it.
[*]  The minigame — actually fun, unlike some cheap throw-ins in other games.
[*]  The depiction of Reisen
[/list]

Informative Points:
[list]
[*] The game is hard but manageable. If Clownpiece is the tutorial boss, you know what you're in for. There are challenges, extra challenges, and an assist mode. The challenges are brutal for casual players.
[*]  Controls: The dash and fly combo feels awkward at first. I only got used to it near the end.
[*]  No voice acting. A pity, but understandable for a doujin game.
[*]  Soundtrack: Doesn't match my personal taste but it's decent. Various genre including jazz and rap.
[/list]

Things I Don’t Like:
[list]
[*]  Challenges are required for the true ending. I dislike having to beat bosses again just to unlock the full story. If you don’t replay, you’re left with a half-baked narrative.
[*]  Fan service: Lewd art after beating bosses feels forced and awkward.
[*]  False sense of exploration: It’s a boss rush game, but each stage has a short walk, a cutscene, a conversation, then the fight. The walking part feels unnecessary.
[/list]

This is easily one of the best Zelda-likes in recent years!

Everything feels super polished - from UI, sprite work, animations to level design. Each major area introduces new mechanics and gameplay ideas, nothing manages to get stale over the course of the game. 

There are quite a few puzzles and they are of type "why haven't I thought of it earlier?!" and I mean this in a positive way. Game world is relatively small, but dense with secrets & charming NPCs to interact with.

The pig sidekick is not only a cute companion, but also an important asset for traversing the environments, often helping to get into places where main protagonist cannot. 

Fight is simple, but satisfying - exactly what I expect from this genre. Boss fights are perfect - not a single one of them is a damage sponge, each requires an unique strategy.

Overall, I can't recommend this game enough. This year is full of amazing releases and this game joins the lineup.

Neon Abyss 1のころからのファンです。レビューを見て、Neon Abyss 2 は爽快感がなくなったなどの記載があり、ずっと買うのを躊躇していましたが、買ってよかったと思っています。
しばらくプレイしてみて、爽快感が無くなったのではなく、戦略性が増えただけであったということがわかりました。きちんとシナジー効果を考えてアイテムを選んだり、分解したりすれば、むしろ爽快感がある旅が楽しめるようになっているという点で良い方向に進化していると思います。
自分はカジュアルゲーマーですが、前作は、正直言って簡単すぎて、すぐに爽快感は得られるものの、達成感が全くありませんでした。（強くなって当然だったので何も考えず脳●で進めればよいため）

今回は、前作に比べて次の点が戦略性が高くなった点です。
・敵が固くなった（が、組み合わせでそれを上回る火力を得ることは可能）
・二段ジャンプや羽の力を得やすいので、「高いところにアイテムがあり、取れない」ということはほぼなくなってストレス減。前作では、二段ジャンプか羽が超レアで、それが無いとそもそも取れないもの多くて身動き取れなった。
・武器を分解して、Lv UP に使えるようになった（店で売っている武器を買って、即分解して手持ち武器をLvUpするなどの戦略も取れます）
・ゴールドを得る手段がたくさんある（店で何を選ぶかによって、結果が大きく変わるためやりがいあり。繰り返しますが、本作では武器の分解をして手持ち武器をLvUpさせられるので、お買い物の選択肢と重要性は大きくなりました。）
・ハッチモンが役に立つ程度に進化できるくらいの卵の量が取れる、孵化ができる。孵化部屋もある。
・どのキャラでもアイテムの説明がすべて表示される！（戦略を練るためにアイテム説明は必須です）
・爆弾・鍵・ゴールドがそこそこ得られる。
・釣り堀+虹の鍵コンボが強力！場に落ちているアイテムを全交換するなども、わざとフィールドにコインとハートだけ残しておいて、いきなり高価値アイテムに変換できたりする。こういう突然のインフレコンボがあるのでハクスラとして面白い。

改善して欲しい点
・ハッチモンさん、もっと尖って強力になると面白いかも。現状役に立つ、レベルではあるけど、特定のハッチモンが出て嬉しい！のようなことは無いので。
・信仰の部屋が、一度出たら消えてしまうのは選択肢を少なくしているだけの気がします。信仰の部屋を見たうえで、動きを考えたい（例　鍵やコインを節約しておくかどうか、など）。
・他の方も言われていますが、キャラの個性が少ないので、結局最初のキャラを選んでいます。もっと尖って（特徴を持って）ほしい。
・Diabloみたいに、アイテムや武器にレア度をつけて、レア武器やアイテムをさらに強力にするとギャンブル性が増して面白いです。現状、スロットなどのギャンブル装置は、自爆する（ハート1つ分食らう）まで回し続ける、ということしか選択肢が無いので、あまりギャンブルっぽくない。
・フロアが変わると宝箱や残したアイテムにアクセスできなくなる割に、フロア当たりの部屋数が少ない。もっと多くすればいろいろな選択肢（楽しみ）が考えられるが、現状は開発者の「想定の範囲内」のインフレしか起こらない。

RPG Maker MZ is an incredible toolset, with the capability to create incredible RPG-based games. I've got over 6000 hours on the clock. I've used every pixel of it.

Yeah, it's 2D. But that adds to the charm, imho. 3D based games will RINSE you in assets.

The interface is simple enough that you can 'pick up and go' almost right away, and as your mind thinks of more creative things to do and you do eventually reach the limitations of the toolset, you can insert script, and write plugins to do the rest. The toolset is build and designed for it.

"Do I need to code?" No, not really. JavaScript is pretty easy to pick up and understand visually, though, and can help with advanced stuff. But the majority of what you need is a google away.

"Do I need to be capable of making art?" No. But I would advise yes. You can use the stuff that comes with, but your game isn't going to stand out against the thousands of shovel-ware out there.

Where it fails: The toolset doesn't. It's the things associated with it.

The RPGMaker Forums (english speaking)
I've been using the internet since the 90s. I have never come across a more rude, uppity, self-important, post-count-hungry shower of pricks in all of my life. And I've used 4chan, reddit, twitter AND WoW barrens chat. It doesn't matter how much you search. It doesn't matter if your problem has never existed, it doesn't matter how polite and apologetic you are... the residents of the english speaking forum will find a way to belittle you and make you feel like a prick for posting. But... there are free resources there if you can bear it.

RPG Maker MZ DLC is recycled MV stuff.
Out of ALL of the DLC for RPGMaker MZ, there are only TWO that actually match the packed-in artwork and style. The 8 Wizards, and the Dark Fantasy. 
Other tilesets/portraits/art are either MV tailored, or their own art (which is never, ever enough to build a game around) so a warning there: don't waste money on DLC. I'll pre-empt it now. Learn to draw. Learn to edit your tilesets. Just do it. The DLC is just a cash grab.

EVERY single generator pack, hero pack, etc, are re-packed MV DLCs, and even though there's file compatibility between MV and MZ, the art style, (and the facing direction of portraits, and the poses in SV battles) differ. MV's parts will make a blistering mess of your generator. Save your money.

Regarding difference to MV:
They are virtually the same in structure. The art differs slightly between the two. MZ allows map building with layer control (invaluable), MV does not (learning curve, harder to make map edits on complex maps). MZ allows the collapsing of conditionals in event editor, MV does not. MZ ships with a 64-bit compatible nw.js, MV does not*. MZ by default allows keyboard input for name input, MV uses a console-esque letter selection. MZ has better code support, MV uses older JS libraries.

What else? Oh yeah, Plugins.
MV has a metric TON of plugins to use, these add features to your game, or modify existing ones.
MZ has less, which people will tell you is 'a bad thing' but MV ones can be converted to work in MZ.
There's paid ones, tht are pretty good, but for most stuff, the free things will get you far.

Lastly... I want to add a warning. If you plan on developing a game, and you've never done it before - it will - irreversibly - change your relationship with video games. The curtain lifts.
You will see all the shortcuts. 
You will see all the lazy effort, 
...and see right through the recycled slop that's shovelled out year after year by 'Big Game'. 
...and your library of games you actually play will drop significantly.


*compiled games can be made compatible with latest OS releases, but that's extra work

Wargroove is a great turn-based strategy game. It’s very clearly inspired by Advance Wars, with even a little bit of Fire Emblem thanks to the commanders. They give the classic Advance Wars style a lot more personality, with memorable characters and fun hero abilities that really change how a battle plays out.

The game has a great campaign, which is where I put most of my time. It works both as a solid tutorial for this kind of game, letting you learn different aspects of the gameplay at a steady pace throughout, while also telling a charming, lighthearted story set in the unique world of Aurania.

All of that comes together with a beautiful pixel-art style that reminds me of old-school strategy games, and a very upbeat, catchy soundtrack that fits perfectly.

And if that’s somehow still not enough, once you finish the campaign and the free DLC, there’s a huge amount of community content in the in-game workshop. There are thousands of maps, campaigns, puzzles, and more to try out.

Censorship aside, Onimusha 2 is basically everything I want in a videogame. 
The game tells a simple and engaging story. Cutscenes are not frequent and they are quick, so you spend most of your time actually playing the game. 

The game encourages you to use every weapon you find because they all have their own magic bar. This allows you to main a weapon you prefer while strategically using others magic attacks to deliver a lot of damage to bosses or oneshot stronger enemies. The characters in the game are all unique, with different playstyles. The gift mechanic lets you choose who to be friend with, which impacts also the story. Depending on how you treat your allies, you can get different story moments, such as a character betraying you, another one oneshotting a boss or giving you a special weapon you can't find anywhere else and more. The game even lets you play as these characters in certain areas, giving you some different experience for a while.

To get 100% completion, you have to play through the story multiple times and each playthrough can be different based on your interactions with the characters as mentioned earlier. Beyond that, you can aim for achievements, play on higher difficulties or try the extra gamemodes as they offer unique experiences, like encountering an enemy not found in the main story (which I loved), a puzzle focused gamemode or a mode where you can swap character anytime. 

Unlike the first Onimusha, you explore a variety of areas, so you don't feel stuck in one giant space you have to figure out like in classic Resident Evil. The backtracking is minimal unless you get lost. There are optional puzzles throughout the game that give you extra resources or key items. While only 3 puzzles are mandatory to beat the game, solving them all is better as you get a much easier time against bosses or normal enemies due to extra resources, upgrades and new attacks you can learn.

The combat is simple but with some interesting stuff. Beyond basic attacks, you can use a kick to knock enemies down, giving you some time to focus on another enemy or perform the ground attack that deals a lot of damage and kills most low tier enemies. You can also sidestep attacks instead of relying only on blocking since you can't block all attacks. The game also has parries and the “counter” mechanic. Simply attack or block right before an enemy's attack hits you to oneshot them. Speaking of enemies, there is a good variety of them and they are introduced at the right pace.

The fixed camera angles give the game an artistic feel we lost with modern games even though sometimes it's frustating when you can't see properly enemies around you or there are sudden camera changes during combat. The game also has no DLC or microtransactions, meaning you unlock everything just by playing.

There are only two things I dislike. The first is the unnecessary censorship in the remaster, it should have been an option to turn on or off (if they had to put it). The second is the 2nd part of the final boss fight. You just run, dodge projectiles, mash the attack button over and over and heal if you get hit by the stupid masks the boss throws at you. The 1st part is way better as it requires you to use all weapons, transformation, dodging, resources etc. 

The remaster has also introduced 2 good changes to the gameplay. One of them is the ability to quickly change weapons without opening your inventory. The 2nd change is the transformation mechanic. Now you can transform at will after collecting five big souls. In the original game you were transforming automatically once you collected them all. This allows you to be more strategic. For example, you can save your transformations for bosses to gain an advantage at the beginning of the fight.

I loved this remastered and I hope we see Onimusha 3 on Steam too in the future.

A Shopping Trip to Eklan Tor by Glass Kettle Games is a simple search and find game with terrific cute graphics.

So that you don't lose the overview, a board hovers above the city, on which all searched and found things are displayed.

 A Shopping Trip to Elkan Tor is the most relaxed shopping you can experience in today's hectic times. In addition, the game is also completely family-friendly and has a fine sense of humor.

If you've made it to Trails of Cold Steel 3, then you probably don't need a review.  If, for some reason, you're new to the series and reading a review of the third entry, there's a lot to think about before you jump in.

TLDR: It's the platonic ideal of the JRPG, with every positive and negative connotation of that term.

I am not a massive fan of Japanese role-playing game series.  I enjoy a JRPG once in a while, but I'm not a fanatic about it.  I picked up Trails of Cold Steel on sale on a whim and enjoyed it.  I knew nothing about the series, but it was (mostly) full of charming characters and I liked the story.  It had all of the things that I like about JRPGs.  Then I played the sequel, and I enjoyed it much less.  It had all of the things that I dislike about JRPGs.  Then, I got to the third game, and it started throwing character after character at me that I was clearly supposed to have some preexisting connection to, so I looked up the history of the game.

Oh, good grief, The Legend of Heroes has 2 complete series of games prior to Trails of Cold Steel, and Trails of Cold Steel 3 starts to bring in a lot of crossover.  They provide only the barest backstory for most of them - enough to remind you who they are if you already knew, but not enough to make me care.  Then, those crossover characters do almost nothing in the story, making them just more noise in an already extremely cluttered narrative.  Maybe if you've played all 5 of the prior games this is a good thing.  I found it to be an endless annoyance.

The Legend of Heroes series is the most JRPG series I've ever played.  Quirky characters are everywhere.  Some are cute, some are annoying as hell.  Japanese social values abound, even when the game is trying to pretend that there are multiple societies.  If you take a drink every time someone says "We'll give it everything we've got!"  or "Don't hold back!" you'll be dead before you finish the prologue.  Player agency begins and ends at "you can choose to do this optional side quest".  You have zero ability to impact the plot of the game.  It's much more of a visual novel with combat.

Speaking of combat, it's OK, but the game has a lot of systems.  Like, a lot.  Arts, crafts, regular attacks, S-breaks... Managing your spells, er, "arts", through the use of "quartz" that you acquire constantly and need to pay careful attention to if you want to be at maximum effectiveness is practically a game unto itself.  If you like micro-management you'll love this game.  Weirdly, there were far less upgrades to the actual weapons used by the characters in this game.  Many JRPGs follow a constant cycle of "new town, new weapon", but not Trails of Cold Steel 3.

All of that is pretty much a given for the JRPG fan.  Where your enjoyment lives or dies in any JRPG probably comes from the story.  Remember, you're not helping craft the story, just discovering it as you go.  I would suggest that, even among a group of nerd enthusiasts such as gamers, there are 2 primary reactions to a JRPG story.  The first group goes, "This is so cool!" and just dives in head first.  The other goes, "Oh, you have got to be kidding me."  I am very much in the latter camp.  My experience with all Japanese stories (games, anime, manga) is that they get more and more ridiculous with time.  The Trails of Cold Steel story starts off at a relatively low key, but by game 3 we're dealing with world ending cataclysms and a curse that's lasted for more than 1000 years.  Every layer is a quantum leap more ridiculous (or awesome, if you are so inclined).

The other make or break aspect is the social relationship of the characters.  It is, once again, utterly Japanese.  For most Americans (and possibly Europeans, I don't know) the idea of a teacher romancing a high school student is fairly horrifying.  It's worth remembering that Japan raised the age of consent from 13 to 16 in 2023.  2023!  When one of the student characters is constantly hitting on the protagonist, everyone just (literally) goes "Hah hah, isn't she cute!"  Um, wow.  Or the horny grandpa, a staple of Japanese stories, talking about how sexy the students are.  Or the guy who is in a "will they/won't they" pseudo-sexual relationship with his adopted sister, another staple of Japanese stories.  The game is both extremely horny and totally chaste.  It is, again, completely Japanese.  When a close friend gives the protagonist a hug every character reacts like they're basically having sex.  But, despite the pervasive sex talk, there is no actual sexual content.  The protagonist is courted by nearly a dozen women, but it never goes further than a kiss on the cheek.  That same thirst trap character is, naturally, totally oblivious to the effect that he has on women.

The author absolutely refuses to apply any sort of negative judgment to characters that are friends of the protagonist, even if they do horrific things.  If they're your friend, that's all that matters.  I can't say more without spoilers.  It's also a big part of Trails of Cold Steel 2.

I often wished that the author would just pick a tone and stick with it.

My comments may come off as universally negative, but I generally enjoyed the game.  If you liked the first game there's very little chance that you won't enjoy this one.  This is the point where I stopped playing Trails of Cold Steel, and went back to play the earlier games.  It's obvious that I need to develop some knowledge of the dozens of preexisting characters and history to fully appreciate Trails of Cold Steel 4.

I will give it this - I think this game is better than any Final Fantasy game.  Imagine if every Final Fantasy was in the same world, took place in a 10 year time-span, and had complete internal consistent of character and world building from game to game.  That's the type of complexity you get with the Legend of Heroes series.

[h1] Great Game [/h1]
Summary: Waterpark Simulator is a refreshingly different management game that mixes humor, chaos, and real substance. For an Early Access title at just €12, you get a surprisingly solid foundation with a lot of potential for the future.

[h3] Graphics [/h3]
For a €12 game, this looks really impressive. The developer picked assets that actually fit together well, and the overall look feels cohesive. The water looks great – even if there’s no real physics behind it. The environment feels alive, and there are even proper 3D building facades. (Something Pokémon could still learn from, honestly. xD)

[h3] Gameplay [/h3]
You build and manage your own waterpark – a perfect mix of humor and seriousness. Guests have different needs you need to satisfy to keep them happy.

There are various visitor types: regular guests, vandals, stinkers, and even creeps who take photos or hit on other guests. While you’re busy selling food, cleaning puddles, and fixing equipment, you also have to deal with the troublemakers before they ruin the atmosphere.
And yes, if someone takes a forbidden photo – grab your taser and make sure they never come back. The other guests will thank you with generous tips.

At the same time, you can research new upgrades and tools to make your daily work easier or unlock new building options.

[h3] Building Options [/h3]
The customization options are surprisingly extensive. You can repaint and redesign pretty much everything. Build pools, slides, and diving boards, and decorate your park with plants, deck chairs, and umbrellas. Add vending machines or snack stands to keep guests happy.
Visual improvements even earn you extra satisfaction points from your visitors.

[h3] Technical Aspects [/h3]
Of course, there are still some bugs in this Early Access phase – but nothing game-breaking. The developer is very active with patches, and most bugs are actually more funny than annoying.
For example: sometimes guests just swim through the park instead of walking. Looks ridiculous, but honestly, it’s hilarious.
Performance is generally fine, though bigger parks with lots of visitors can drop FPS a bit.

[h3] Wishes for the Future [/h3]

- Ability to hire more staff (currently very limited).
- Fully custom-built pools and slides.
- A more engaging endgame – once you’ve unlocked everything, there’s not much left to do.
- Co-op mode (already announced).
- More textures for floors and walls.
- A merch stand you can personally manage – like in a shop simulator.
- A proper apartment you can furnish instead of sleeping in a tent by the roadside.
- A character editor for your park manager.

[h3] Final Thoughts [/h3]
A charming and technically solid game with plenty of personality and humor. Even in its Early Access state, it’s already an easy recommendation – especially for fans of management and building sims with a unique twist.

[h1] Starkes Game [/h1]
Fazit vorweg: Waterpark Simulator ist ein erfrischend anderes Aufbauspiel, das Humor, Management und Chaos auf sympathische Weise kombiniert. Für Early Access und 12 € bekommt man hier erstaunlich viel Substanz – mit Potenzial für deutlich mehr.

[h3] Grafik [/h3]
Für ein 12-Euro-Game sieht das hier richtig stark aus. Der Entwickler hat optisch passende Assets gewählt, die das Gesamtbild stimmig wirken lassen. Das Wasser sieht klasse aus – auch wenn es keine echte Physik besitzt. Die Umgebung wirkt lebendig, und es gibt sogar vollwertige 3D-Hausfassaden. (Etwas, das nicht mal Pokémon hinbekommt xD)

[h3] Gameplay [/h3]
Du baust und verwaltest deinen eigenen Wasserpark – mit einer Mischung aus Humor und Ernsthaftigkeit. Besucher haben unterschiedliche Bedürfnisse, die du erfüllen musst, um sie glücklich zu halten.

Es gibt verschiedene Besuchertypen: normale Gäste, Vandalisten, Stinker und sogar Perverslinge, die unerlaubt Fotos machen oder anderen Gästen nachstellen. Während du Essen verkaufst, Pfützen aufwischst und Geräte reparierst, musst du gleichzeitig die Problemgäste aus deinem Park entfernen – bevor sie die Stimmung versauen.
Und ja: Wenn jemand ein verbotenes Foto macht, zückst du deinen Taser und sorgst für Ordnung. Die anderen Gäste danken es dir mit fettem Trinkgeld.

Nebenbei forschst du ständig an neuen Features, die deinen Alltag erleichtern oder neue Baumöglichkeiten freischalten.

[h3] Baumöglichkeiten [/h3]
Die Gestaltungsmöglichkeiten sind überraschend umfangreich. Du kannst fast alles anpassen, bemalen und umbauen. Pools, Rutschen, Sprungbretter – alles lässt sich kombinieren. Mit Vegetation, Liegen und Sonnenschirmen schaffst du gemütliche Chill-Zonen, während Snackautomaten und Imbissstände für zufriedene Gäste sorgen.
Auch optische Anpassungen bringen dir Bonuspunkte bei den Besuchern.

[h3] Technik [/h3]
Natürlich gibt’s im Early Access noch Bugs – aber nichts, was das Spiel zerstört. Der Entwickler fixt regelmäßig, und viele Fehler sind eher amüsant als ärgerlich.
Beispiel: Manchmal schwimmen Besucher einfach quer durch den Park statt zu laufen. Sieht seltsam aus, sorgt aber für gute Lacher.
Leistungstechnisch läuft es solide, auch wenn größere Parks die FPS etwas drücken können.

[h3] Wünsche für die Zukunft [/h3]

- Mehr Personal einstellen können (aktuell stark begrenzt).
- Frei baubare Pools und Rutschen.
- Ein spannenderes Endgame – aktuell bleibt nach den letzten Erfolgen nicht mehr viel zu tun.
- Koop-Modus (bereits angekündigt).
- Mehr Texturen für Böden und Wände.
- Einen Merch-Stand, den man selbst verwalten kann – ähnlich wie in einem Shop-Simulator.
- Eine eigene Wohnung, die man einrichten kann, statt nur in einem Zelt am Straßenrand zu leben.
- Einen Charaktereditor für den eigenen Parkmanager.

[h3] Fazit [/h3]
Ein charmantes, technisch solides Spiel mit viel Humor und eigenem Stil. Trotz Early-Access-Feinschliff schon jetzt eine klare Empfehlung – vor allem für Fans von Aufbauspielen mit Charakter.

It's more of the same Cladun-- an iteration rather than a big departure from what came before, which is a bit sad considering the gap inbetween this one and the previous games, but I'm not one to complain as seeing this even exist to begin with came as a huge surprise to me. I'm happy seeing it localized as well considering a lot of NIS' output lately hasn't seen the same treatment. 

Mota's art, another amazing Yoh Ohyama OST (and a jukebox!), and the magic circle grind, it's as if nothing has changed. Although "more of the same" is something that can be viewed as criticism in equal mesasure. There are weapon types that were added to Sengoku that were removed (even with a Ninja class existing...), and at its core the gameplay is just the same as its always been with not a lot new added at all, really. It's the core gameplay, customizability, and progression that were always solid from before that carry this game.

The worst offense in regards to this lack of progress for a new title in my eyes is that the network functionality and asset-sided customization are so very horribly lacking. We're using friend codes like we're still on the DS or Wii. You would think that this part would be figured out and and iterated upon for the better, but after all these years it's still stuck in the past. Granted, the suite of tools and what you are able to customize-- whole maps with a full pixel editor, every part of your character and their appearance, the music, that's all still well and good, mind you! After all, it was that aspect of the previous games that meant so much to me, and a sort of grassroots built creative community is something that is just ignored and lacking in a lot of games lately.

But I really have no idea what they were doing with this part of the game. When it comes to the editor, it was like it was one step forward, two steps back. You used to be able to upload your own files to the game. Working with the in-game pixel art editor is enough to fry my brain with how unintuitive it is (no undo or a move button... skin color still being locked in your palette and only giving you three options, why???) The global release not being connected to the JP servers means that there's a LOT that's being missed out on and I'm not holding my breath that more JP maps will get "ported" over outside of the ones they decided to bring over on launch. At least they're still giving a bit of love with bringing over the collabs, but even still, there was something untapped here and it's always things like that which make me feel a bit sad considering what could have been. Another case of a good game that I can't help but sigh about because it could've very easily been something more. Either way, still going to play it for a good hundred hours or so like a good little Enjoyer, so... You know.

I only played the first Mega Man, almost at the end, and already I'm loving this collection.

I also appreciate the Challenge Mode as a way to keep people playing even after finishing all six games.

There's also an Art/Music Gallery in this compilation as well, from some concept art to final designs, to music from each game (Dr. Wily's Stage 1 theme in MM2 is absolute fire).

Basic border settings and aspect ratio aside, the one feature that truly won me over is the CPU Speed option. I was having second thoughts of buying this collection because the games are known for having slowdowns when there's too many sprites (I heard Mega Man 3 suffers that the most) Obviously people who want authenticity can pick Original Speed.

What I don't like is how difficult the games are to the point where I have to continuously save-scum each time I get the upper hand against the bosses (Looking at you, Yellow Devil boss). Cheating be damned.

There's also apparent input delay, but I'm not experiencing any of it, even with the CPU Speed to Turbo. Maybe it's the case with the console and handheld versions, and the fact that it's still not improved to this day really sucks.

Overall, props to Digital Eclipse for going the extra mile to put in extra features and not being like "Here's all the ROMs, that's it. Have fun." As well as Capcom for acknowledging not just this series, but all the others as well, like X, Zero, Battle Network, etc. 8/10

Plant Therapy is the game I never knew I was missing. I’ll admit I went in with a bit of bias. But I’m so glad I gave it a shot, because it turned out to be exactly what I needed.

This game offers a beautifully open-ended experience where I could decorate however I wanted, set my own goals, and spend as much (or as little) time as I pleased just being present in the space. It doesn’t demand anything from you which, honestly, is rare. So many games require constant energy, decision-making, or performance. Plant Therapy simply lets you be. It’s therapeutic, grounding, and has quickly become one of my digital safe spaces.

One small issue I ran into was with placement visibility. When I was moving items around, it was sometimes hard to tell if a space was already occupied. A few times, I accidentally nudged or picked up another object without realizing it was there. A subtle visual cue—like a slight color shift or glow to show available vs. taken spots—could make a big difference. I know the ability to lock items is there (and super helpful!), but when you're rearranging a lot, it can get a little tricky.

That said, the customization options are fantastic. I had so much fun experimenting and personalizing the space. There’s something really satisfying about creating a room that reflects your mood or aesthetic, and this game delivers that in spades.

Es gibt eine "Übergeordnete Story", Gebietsstorys und mehrere Quests -, Charakter und Einzelstorys.
Insgesamt eine tolle Mischung, die absolut passend und ineinander passt und vor allem schlüssig ist. 

Die Stadt Sun Haven ist wirklich schön gestaltet. Man lernt nach und nach alle Einwohner kennen und auch lieben. Die einzelnen Charaktere sind alle besonders und besitzen wirklich Storys und Charaktertiefe. 

Zudem spielt man im Laufe der Geschichte drei weitere Gebiete frei. Nel`vari, Brinstone Deep und Withergate.
Eine eher "Elfenartige" und eine "Horror" Stadt =D 
Das Spiel selbst ist sehr Fantasylastig, was sich in Story und auch den ganzen Charakteren zeigt. 
Dies ist für mich hier ein großer Pluspunkt, da ich dieses Genre liebe und hier wurde es super gut eingebaut. Selbst die Story insgesamt ist bisher weder langweilig noch zu wiederholend. 
Hier herrscht das richtige Maß an mitreisender Story, die hauptsächlich durch die Charaktere getragen wird. 

Die einzelnen Charaktere kann man übrigens via Herzen befreunden und später auch heiraten =) 

Auch gibt es, wie aus anderen Games bekannt, ein Schwarzes Brett, bei dem man Aufgaben annehmen und abarbeiten kann. 

Manchmal geben auch die NPCs selbst Quest aus. Dies sind manchmal verlorene Items oder auch Dates :3

Nicht nur farmen und anpflanzen gibt es, sondern auch fischen, erkunden und man kann auf Reittieren durch die Gegend reiten. Dies ist besonders toll, da man oftmals schneller ist, als zu Fuß =)

As much as I would have liked to see the game launch in this state, the Rearmament Update has finally delivered on the performance improvements and bug fixes that made the game unplayable for many. Gameplay feels and sounds so much better! This game hasn't reached its full potential yet, but this update has definitely taken it several steps in the right direction.

The Rearmament Update finally brings Killing Floor 3 closer to what it should have been at launch. While it’s hard to overlook how poorly Tripwire handled the game’s initial release—an incomplete, disappointing product—the new update demonstrates a genuine effort to repair and refine what was broken. It’s reminiscent of Fallout 76’s redemption arc: a disastrous start that, over time, evolved into one of the most enjoyable multiplayer experiences in its genre.

Performance has noticeably improved. The game now runs smoothly, gunplay feels tighter and more impactful, the Zeds are far more engaging and less predictable, and movement feels fluid rather than clunky. These enhancements make the core gameplay loop feel substantially more rewarding.

That said, the update isn’t without flaws. The damage system remains confusing and unnecessarily convoluted. Having both Armor and Zedtech as separate weak points feels redundant; simplifying it to Armor, Flesh, and Mire would make visual cues and strategy more intuitive for players. Similarly, several damage types feel superfluous—Sound Wave, for instance, could easily be merged with Force Damage, while Acidic and Biological could be consolidated without sacrificing depth.

Class passives also need reconsideration. While the introduction of toolkits is interesting, many passives feel underwhelming or situational. Instead of utility bonuses like “extra syringe capacity,” passives should directly empower players in combat, reinforcing each class’s identity and playstyle.

Lastly, certain weapon archetypes and damage types still lack balance. The Ninja class, for example, struggles on higher difficulties since Cut Damage is ineffective against armored enemies. A passive ability tailored to counter this would give the class more viability and depth.

Overall, The Rearmament Update is a significant leap forward—a clear sign that Tripwire is listening. But for the game to truly reach its potential, its systems need more cohesion, its design more purpose, and its classes more meaningful differentiation.

I have played this game a few times since it came out, and even here in 2025 it is still in my top ten. As a former U.S. Navy serviceman, I connect with this one in a way I never have with Call of Duty or Battlefield. Those games are great for spectacle, but Medal of Honor feels real.

From the moment it starts, you can tell this game was made with respect. The radio chatter, the way the team moves, the quiet professionalism, it is not about flash or kill counts. It is about brotherhood, the mission, and the cost. The developers worked with actual Tier 1 operators, and you can feel it in every firefight. Nothing feels exaggerated; it feels earned.

The campaign is short, but every mission counts. The mountain fights and night raids are some of the most immersive in any military shooter I have played. And that ending is brutal. It stays with you long after the credits roll. It is not cinematic; it is personal.

I really wish EA had kept this series going, but they stopped supporting it in favor of Battlefield. That is a shame, because there is nothing else like Medal of Honor. It is a grounded, respectful look at modern warfare, and it still holds up beautifully.

If you want a military shooter that feels authentic rather than over the top, this is the one.
Respectful, emotional, and real.

Tomb Raider, released in 2013, is a masterful reboot that transforms Lara Croft from a frightened young archaeologist into a hardened survivor after being shipwrecked on the hostile island of Yamatai. Titan Isles nails everything that makes VR gaming awesome – nonstop movement, adrenaline, and pure team energy. You can feel the love and attention to detail the moment you jump in. The four Exo-Suits all play completely differently - from a fast jetpack scout to a heavy tank-style bruiser - and each one feels fantastic in motion.

The boss fights are massive, cinematic, and seriously challenging. Every Titan has its own attack patterns that keep you on your toes, and the four difficulty levels (Easy, Normal, Heroic, Legendary) really let you choose your pain level. Legendary mode? Buckle up — it’s wild!

Playing co-op with friends is where the game truly shines. The team dynamics are insane — calling out weak spots, covering each other, and syncing attacks feels amazing. It’s chaotic, tactical, and ridiculously fun all at once.

And between the big boss runs, there are tons of fun mini-games like time trials, target challenges, and even little scavenger hunts 😄 - perfect for blowing off steam between fights.

Technically, it’s rock-solid: buttery-smooth performance, punchy sound, and gorgeous visuals that make the islands feel alive.

If you love VR and want huge battles, great co-op action, and plenty of variety - you need to play Titan Isles.

[b]Verdict: A hidden gem that delivers everything VR fans and Coop-Lovers crave - intense, fun, and totally addictive! [/b]

Windlands 2 was one of my all-time favorite VR games, and Titan Isles is a worthy successor.  The most fundamental changes from the Windlands series are an increased focus on combat and a choice of 4 different exo suit types that each have their own movement and combat mechanics.  If you want to play the game as if it were Windlands 3 you can use the Hunter suit with grappling hooks and a bow and arrow that will feel very familiar to veterans of the series.  The Storm suit has the easiest controls for newcomers and fans of standard shooters, with dual plasma pistols and a jetpack that makes you feel like Iron Man.  The Blink suit has a triple jump that was an interesting alternative to the other options, but I mainly stuck to the Hunter and Storm suits.  The game campaign has about 10 levels and can be completed either single-player or up to 4-player co-op, though I only played in single-player mode.

The gameplay loop is fairly straightforward--enter an open arena with a closed door, kill all the enemies, then proceed to the next area until you reach the boss at the end.  Depending on your suit choice, you can dive into the action with weapons blazing for chaotic bullet-hell fun, or hang back and pick off enemies one at a time with a bow or sniper rifle.  At the higher difficulty levels the number of enemies can be overwhelming as a single player so sniping at a safe-ish distance can be a key survival tactic.  I found it interesting that you can completely bypass certain combat sections in a level by simply going around them, but eventually the game throws up a barrier that sends you back to your last completed section if you skip too far ahead.

Unlike the Windlands games where you have unlimited lives, in Titan Isles you have 8 lives to complete a level before you have to restart from the beginning of the level.  At first I found this frustrating when I would make it all the way to a boss only to fail and have to run through the whole level again, but as I got better I appreciated the added pressure of having limited respawns and enjoyed the thrill of beating several bosses on my last life.  When you complete a level, you get chips you can use to upgrade any of your suits, and I liked the sense of progression and the upgrade options.  After finishing the campaign you can keep playing a small subset of the levels, but there was no way to go back and replay any level you want which I found disappointing.  There is also a New Game + option, which starts you back at the beginning of the campaign with all of your suit upgrades and makes the enemies a little more challenging, though I didn't notice a huge difference.

Overall I highly recommend the game.  The traversal across the huge open spaces feels amazing, and the combat never got stale for me.  There are also some collect-a-thon targets and relics that offer good replay value for each level.  It doesn't have the very challenging traversal sections that I loved in Windlands 2, but it includes about 10 epic boss fights that are even better than the handful in Windlands 2 which were my favorite part of that game.  It sounds like these are even more fun in co-op, so definitely go in with friends if you can.

Outstanding 2D platformer with really, really TIGHT movement and a wide variety of gameplay styles. 15 classes and 30 weapons overall - EACH of them offers a different attack style, from a basic sword swing in front of character, or narrow lunges but in 4 directions (like in Hollow Knight), to AOE attacks, boomerang attacks, and even jumping on static projectiles you place beforehand. Rogue Legacy 2 manages to combine a lot of mechanics from different platformers and blend them into one thing, where you can CHOOSE what you want to play and master. Worth mentioning, you won't be forced to play everyone or lock in to a single character/weapon, but this game does a great job of encouraging you to conquer different playstyles, since you gain bonuses for leveling them up and rare valuable traits sometimes roll on characters you don't normally play, so...
 
Yeah, traits. For anyone unfamiliar with Rogue Legacy 1, the highlight of this series - what makes it truly unique - is trait system. Every character here can have up to 2 traits that can change the gameplay DRASTICALLY or don't change it at all. For example, your character can be blue... or your damage numbers are exaggerated... or you can only see a small area around you and enemies and nothing else... or you have 75% of max health and become a Touhou player with hitbox being just a small heart inside you instead of your entire character... you get it. And some of the hardest or at least difficult traits, like being a one-hit character, provide you with gold bonus which you can spend on further meta upgrades. This makes difficulty really optional but very rewarding, making your journey as hard and engaging as you want to. 

Speaking of meta upgrades, I don't really want to go in-depth, but I just want to warn people hoping for a true roguelike - Rogue Legacy 2 leans heavily into meta upgrades and this is the main factor of you progressing. If you're stuck on a hard boss, you can easily outlevel them and beat first try, or you can come underleveled and have a bad time (still can git gud tho). 

Music, art, story and everything else aren't the main focus here imo, but they all compliment the core gameplay and... The game just looks pretty, okay? 

[b]Definitely recommend.[/b]

There's a few games that are still keyboard-mandatory, and there are a few new UX insanities involving backing out of menus.  I have come to expect this genuine insanity from D3Publisher, I think the key to getting them to promote your game is to make really weird control scheme choices.

I could go on a methodical breakdown of all the reasons I'm a bit... whelmed by this, but I can not rouse the interest in doing so.  I'm sorry, I just don't feel any urge to write a rambling essay about it.*

So let's conclude, then:  This game aspires to mediocrity.  It's weird in that some of it contains actual, technical improvements.  If I gave the original a 51%, this one gets 49.9%.  It got pity-rounded to a pass.  Buy it on a deep sale. Join me in feeling whelmed, neither over nor under.

There's a lot of games like Vampire Survivors out there. There are extremely few games that are even close to what this game has. This is as much of a game that you experience as a game you play, and the skill that is encouraged is unlike what Vampire Survivors requires. Vampire Survivors at its core is a knowledge check: how well do you know the roster of weapons and items and do you know which ones are the best? Picayune demands not only understanding of your weapons and items, but also the capacity for dodging that you see in bullet hells. It's the perfect fusion of both disciplines, and it lives up to the strange and trippy aesthetic it portrays, inspired partially by I imagine the classic Yume Nikki and the other inspired works that sprang from it. All of the characters in this game are quite lovable and interesting, especially the character you play as, Cyl, as a sort of no-nonsense dead inside warrior type who will go to any lengths to make sure Earth is safe. I love this game, and even coming back a long time later I find the gameplay loop and even the new content to be engaging and compelling, adding more to the story and the loop as a whole. Absolutely worth playing at least until you crush the final boss, but I recommend 100%ing the game, as it's not demanding of your time and focus as a lot of other games would be.

[i]Loan Shark[/i] was a complete surprise. This isn't the longest game by any means, and it does cost five bucks - but unlike nearly every other $5 indie horror game on the market right now, this game is vastly more engaging and compelling than the majority of generic "run away from the monster" games. Make no mistake, [i]Dredge[/i] this is not. The mechanics are very simple, the fishing has no real depth to it, the entire game takes place on one small fishing boat. It is tedious, it is basic, and there's nothing immediately scary to speak of whatsoever.

...And then, you catch a very strange fish, and everything begins to change.

[i]This[/i] fish can help you. This fish can make a deal. You're only out on the seas fishing in order to repay your debts as an increasingly threatening loan shark calls you up to make demands. The fish can help. Do you accept his offer? Do you take his deal? Do you trade one loan for another? An eye for an eye? This is the question this game asks, this is the conundrum. How far will you go to clear this debt? What will you give in return? The game is a spiraling descent into desperation and madness, all wrapped within a short-but-sweet package with great atmosphere, surprising humor, and a dread that ebbs and flows with the tide. 

The game also appears to have a decent amount of content to explore. I got the "main" ending, but the choices throughout the game do seem to be meaningful, with a variety of endings to unlock and pathways to follow. I plan on replaying this a few times to get more of these endings and learn more about the game, because it ultimately [i]is[/i] very charming while not being tedious or frustrating to any extent. The length in this regard is actually a positive that facilitates the exploration of this enjoyable little game. 

So crack open a beer, cast your line, and remember: Private property is sacred.
