First things first:
* This review contains minor spoilers. I've marked significant, concrete spoilers as [spoiler] such [/spoiler]
* I got this game at a discount and paid only 7.50 Euros
* I played the game in coop with a friend (Coop is built in to the game and works out of the box without major issues)
* Overall it took us around 13 hours to beat the game.


[h2] Good things [/h2]

The game starts off really strong. The first few areas give off a great atmosphere. As someone who hasn't played other souls-like games before I enjoyed the combat system. The game is funny, and doesn't take itself too seriously. This section feels short, because there's not a lot to write about the game doing good. Still, I want to reiterate: The first half of the game is nice! (first half = before you leave the [spoiler] forest [/spoiler])

[h2] Bad things [/h2]

[h3] Onboarding / World Building [/h3]

"The Last Hero of Nostalgaia" does not explain much about the world. I think the intention is for the player to discover the lore for themselves. For example, each weapon has a small piece of lore attached to it, and you can piece these together. I don' think this is in itself a bad decision! 
Unfortunately, for this game, it just doesn't work. Throughout most of the game we had little to no idea where we were going besides "Walk somewhere to defeat XYZ - somehow". At multiple points we got completely lost and did not understand what was happening. Maybe we missed some optional dialogue, but key dialogue should not be optional.

This feeling of being lost is not limited to the story. There are three different damage types in "The Last Hero of Nostalgaia", and as such each armor's stats page lists three different resistance values. But there is no way to tell what damage type an enemy's weapon will deal. Moreover, the last damage type barely appears before the last chapter of the game, so you're left with confusion at what the value even means.

[h3] Gameplay [/h3]

As I said before, I enjoyed the gameplay for the first half of the game. It's fun, you walk around slaying enemies and collect loot.
However, at some point the game stops introducing new (meaningful) content. The core gameplay loop ("kill enemies, upgrade gear, kill more enemies") was fun because you were quickly met with new, interesting areas and enemies. Take that away and you end up with a very repetitive experience.

The end of the game is [u]extremely[/u] disappointing. Usually you would expect a game to start building up tension in the later half, leading up to some big battle concluding the story. Instead the game prepares the player for what seems like the last big battle (against the [spoiler] Narrator [/spoiler]). This battle ends pretty quickly and without much fighting - making us think that there is more to be done and the game is not yet over (and it isn't). But then it just fizzles out. There is one more short and easy fight (in the [spoiler] Arena [/spoiler]), against enemies that are not new and not hard. After this we literally had to google if the game was over(it's not) or if there was more to come - no credits yet, but we had no clue where else to go. We ended up stumbling over the [u] final [/u] (for real this time) section by pure chance - I have no idea how else you're supposed to find it.
The last section ([spoiler] Tentacle Dungeon [/spoiler]) feels very rushed, hardly fits into the rest of the game and ends with (another) mechanically uninteresting boss fight. 

[h3] Difficulty [/h3]

There is no difficulty selection (at least none that I could find, maybe because I wasn't the host). Overall the game is too easy, me and my friend beat most areas and bosses without issues. We weren't even using any consumables or similar ways to get stronger. I haven't tried the singleplayer so maybe the coop version just doesn't scale well.

The bosses are extremely basic and close to being just stronger, bigger versions of the usual enemies with a health bar attached to them (The one exception is [spoiler] the dancing golden guy, which has two phases and more than one attack pattern (: [/spoiler] ). There are also [u] very [/u] few of them, four in total. The battles themselves are disappointing and boring.

[h3] Mechanics [/h3]

In the last third of the game, two new mechanics are introduced - one for movement([spoiler] Walking in 2D on walls[/spoiler]) and one for combat([spoiler] a special attack when an icon appears above an enemy [/spoiler]). I've found these to be very poorly executed.

First off, they are introduced very late in the game. The combat mechanic can only be executed when a specific icon appears on an enemy, and it only appeared twice for me throughout the entire rest of the game, so there was hardly any point to having it at all. Moreover, the icon appeared long before the mechanic itself was introduced, which was confusing.

The movement mechanic can only be used in specific places and allows players to traverse gaps that they couldn't pass before. That is the only thing that it is ever used for. It is introduced very suddenly and then nothing is done to make it interesting. There's no mechanical challenge, its just a different way of holding "W". It feels very forced, like the developers felt they had to add more features. Note that the game does already use doors in many places to lock off certain areas for the player, so I don't know why this was added at all.

[h3] Bugs / Lack of polish  [/h3]
Me and my friend experienced de-syncs multiple times while playing through the game, where one player would see an enemy and the other one would not. Maybe this is limited to the coop mode. Still, the coop mode is part of the game so it should be treated as first-class content.

The models themselves are also not particularly polished. My character constantly had the sword floating besides his hand, or stuck in an unnatural position (either on his leg or protruding to the side in a 90° angle).

At some points the levels are badly designed - enemies that attack first are positioned behind enemies that won't move, so that the moving enemies are pretty much guaranteed to get stuck when they try to get to the player ([spoiler] This happened a lot with the pickaxe-wielding rats in the gold mine and their "commanders" [/spoiler]). The later sections of the game are visually far inferior to the earlier ones and usually take place in the sky or some blank void.

[h2] Conclusion [/h2]
For the 7.50 Euros I paid the game was completely okay. But I would not recommend anyone to buy it at full price.

Teaching you behind your back, a Car Mechanic Simulator 2021 Review:

Another Hit from the Quintessential Car Mechanic Simulator Series. I have been playing the CMS series of games since the first one in 2014. Each entry into the series gets better and better, adding more detail and more customization options. But what it doesn’t tell you is that it is also teaching you behind your back.

I’ll be for real; I’m a nerd with the mechanical fascination type of autism. So, this game series tickles all the right areas of my brain to make me secrete happy chemicals. I really vibe with pulling a rust bucket from the clutches of a junkyard, and blasting music while I strip it down to the frame and rebuild it with custom parts, turning a surefire tetanus risk into a prize-winning 1960’s classic muscle car with high-performance parts running under the hood. 

CMS 2021 is the Culmination of all of the iterative improvements and new mechanics of the games. With a brand-new scrapping and upgrading mechanic, where you can take old parts that are below 100% durability, destroy them to get scrap, and then spend that scrap to upgrade parts for a boost in performance and power. CMS 2021 also did away with RNG based repair system of previous games and instead added a minigame where the repair is based on timing, which is amazing, as RNG often hates my guts.

Over all of the games in the series, I have racked up probably about 500 hours of playtime, just spent fixing cars and rocking out, but what I didn’t know is that this game is not only fun and genuinely pretty to look at, but it was even educating me behind my back. That’s right reader, this game gave me real life mechanic skills. 

I took my car, a real car, into a real-life mechanic, and was told that one of my rear brake pads had broken apart and scored the brake rotor. Not good. No one should drive a car with broken brakes. The mechanic quoted me $1000+ for replacement parts and labour. They don’t even replace only the broken part, because it causes uneven wear which will lead to even more parts failing. However, with $500 left to spend in my bank account, I couldn’t afford the fix. They even made me sign a waiver saying I new the car was unsafe to drive.

In comes CMS to save the day. I went online, found a car parts site, entered my car info, and it found me the appropriately sized parts for my make and model, for $129, Tax included. 11 days later, with parts in one hand, and tools from my late grandfather’s workshop in the other, I jacked up my real car, in real life, and changed rotors and pads for my rear wheels, using only knowledge bestowed upon me by playing Car Mechanic Simulator. My mother was sitting and watching me the whole time and told me that she couldn’t be prouder of me, for the skills I had acquired from a video game coming in handy in real life, and while I don’t think I’m quite ready to go examining the timing belts and piston rings of my engine, I definitely learned enough to save myself $871 worth of labour.

I think probably the only way they could make this game better in the next iteration, is by letting us do ridiculous engine swaps for the cars. Like I really want to cram a double turbocharged high performance V12 engine into a 1960’s coke body muscle car.

10/10 Fun and secretly educational. A must play if you like looking at pretty muscle cars.

Sniper Killer mantém a fórmula dos jogos da Torture Star Video, mas traz como diferencial uma gameplay estilo Sniper Elite versão Halloween e um jeito bem peculiar de contar sua história.

Você vive a trama por três lados: o das vítimas antes de morrerem, o do assassino antes de matá-las e o do detetive responsável por caçá-lo. É uma forma diferente de contar a história, mas que funciona muito bem.

Jogar com as vítimas e com o detetive traz a tensão e o clima bizarro dos quais já estamos acostumados em jogos desse tipo. Já jogar com o assassino dá uma nova experiência. O jogo quer que você pense como ele, pegue a melhor posição, prepare o tiro e espere o momento certo. Esse contraste entre o medo e o controle dá um ótimo equilíbrio tanto para a narrativa quanto para a gameplay.

A história em si é imersiva e prende a atenção bem rápido. Logo no começo, você já começa a criar teorias e querer as respostas para os mistérios que o enredo apresenta. Qual é a real motivação do assassino? Qual a ligação entre as vítimas? Tudo isso faz parte de um plano maior? Todas essas dúvidas e a forma como elas são implementadas ao longo da narrativa fazem, na minha opinião, Sniper Killer ter uma das histórias mais interessantes já distribuídas pela Torture Star até o momento.

Talvez o final decepcione algumas pessoas. Não vou dar spoilers, mas o jogo se mantém crível por boa parte do tempo e acaba dando uma viajada sinistra no final. Não me incomodou, mas acho que já estava bom do jeito que estava.

No geral, é um ótimo jogo e uma excelente opção para quem curte esse estilo.

it is the duty of a video game to trick its player into feeling something; to make them forget they're poking at a fancy state machine by letting the meaning shine out from between the gears.

moon is, mechanically, a very simple game. you can walk, collect items, interact with NPCs or points of interest, and, importantly, wait. most of the puzzles in the game can be solved following a flowchart that goes through those options. can you see a solution walking around? is there an item to pick up? are there any interaction points? if not, wait. you will do a lot of waiting.

but moon does its duty. was i standing still and waiting for something to happen? no, i was staking out the office of the robo mayor to gather intel. no, i was positioning to commandeer a live firework for my own ends. no, i was hearkening the signs and preparing for the return of the dark lord sadmile.

except in the desert, when it made me stand still doing nothing for the entire night four different times. but that was really funny, i had to give it to them.

moon is not an RPG, but it'll make you forget that. it's a vision of a path RPGs might follow, sometime in the distant future of the 2000s. as it turns out, RPGs would broadly follow a [i]much[/i] different path, but we got at least a few games like the ones moon was hoping for.

if i could offer a piece of advice to a prospective player, don't worry about 100%ing it or following a guide. if you've played some adventure games, nothing in moon is too outlandish to solve by yourself. the critical path will become obvious, and you should follow it once you're ready. don't scour for content. i think moon itself would agree with me on this. stop playing that game and go to bed!

besides, you'll have to do that fucking fishing competition if you don't take my advice, and no one wants that.

TL;DR : This game is good and the atmosphere is perfect but the wave of xenos are are predictable bullet sponges. There's no hiding or need to and personally, I feel an alien title like this needs more Alien Isolation and less run and gun. Slight/significant changes to the Alien's behavior is all this needs to be a top seller.

Worth It on Sale, But Flawed at the Core

It's a good game and definitely worth the price if you catch it on a sale. I actually refunded this product initially, primarily because of how the Xenomorphs would attack—it felt unnatural and much more like a simple wave of enemies. Even now, if you linger in a room for too long, one or two Xenos will randomly spawn, know your general location, and make a beeline for you. That pattern, while still present, was a huge turn-off at the beginning.

 Atmosphere / Scares

I decided to give it another shot, and it’s genuinely a 100% fun shooter packed with jump scares and an easy-to-follow story. The atmosphere of obscure corridors and constantly changing environments kept me on my toes the entire time. Seeing a Xenomorph crawl along a wall or scurry across a ceiling just to vanish always freaks me out, and combined with the overall atmosphere, this game makes for an awesome VR experience.

Predictable A.I.

This is where things start to shift. It’s as easy to love some parts of this game as it is to dislike the more obvious issues that desperately need attention. Since the entire game is built around your interaction with Xenomorphs, this is where the heaviest changes are needed.

My issues boil down to my perception of what a Xenomorph should be, so take this with a grain of salt, but the random spawning and attacking outside of scripted events absolutely drains the tension from the otherwise terrifying atmosphere. As mentioned, they path their way toward you, you shoot them, and then you get the next five minutes or so Xeno-free. Not only is this repetitive, but the A.I. makes the creatures objectively less convincing.

More Robot less Xenomorph

To me, Xenomorphs are smart, aware of their surroundings, and hunters, very smart hunters. In the game, the A.I. just paths directly toward you, usually through vents, rafters, or specific, environmentally designated spots. All pathing even through vents is mostly predictable. You can often watch them crawl along a ceiling or wall, allowing you to easily anticipate which vent they’re heading for.

The A.I. feels predictable and easy to target—not unique. They don't wait for you in corners or follow you in the shadows; instead, they path along a ceiling in a very open, highly visible style before dropping right in front of you. This is fine for an occasional maybe aggressive behaving xeno. But in the A.I.'s current state it happens almost on every encounter and it loses its novelty to routine.

Replaceable A.I.

Here's the question that made me realize why this upsets me for an Alien title: If you replaced the Xenomorphs with something like zombies (28 weeks later or some fast durable zombies) what would you have? Well, you'd pretty much have the same game (minus the ceiling crawling unless there are zombies that do that). They’re just targets that soak bullets, spawn in a small waves, and pop out of nowhere for a scare. The A.I. simply does not make you feel like you are being hunted by Xenomorphs. It’s like someone coughed the word "Xenomorph" into an A.I. program, and this is what we got. But this is also a good time to point out its strengths, the atmosphere sells it, the gun play (although limited and needs *some* work) sells it and even small features like how you save sells it its is simply the A.i. that needs work.

You never feel a genuine need to hide behind a counter or a table to escape certain doom (and there are no such features anyways). That box you just threw across the room? Doesn't matter. The Xenos only react to gunshots. If you haven't hit the end of the five-minute spawn timer, shooting will bring them to you early—but only if you shoot. Run all you like, knock over boxes, throw objects, open and close doors a thousand times, none of it matters; the Xenos won’t bother you.

One thing that was really cool to me is the Xenomorph in Alien Isolation learns about you and your weapons, realizes that certain weapons can hurt it. It would be cool if the waves of Xeno's were more cautious after realizing you can gun them down, stuck closer to the shadows and ambush techniques and maybe you had an that occasional outlier that straight up attacks you. One thing that happened later in my game was a Xeno got stuck on in corridor wall and ended up making its hissing noise in a fogged up completely dark hallway, it was terrifying at first but then I realized the audio kept playing over and over in the same spot just for it to be an alien in distress lol.

All of this to say the game is fun but the Xenomorphs are beyond predictable and easily replaced with a different fast moving creature like zombies from 28 weeks later or input whatever moves fast and is scary to you. The game needs behavioral changes in the A.I. and it should take some inspiration from one of the most popular Alien games to date. Outside of that its still fun but still needs work.

Silent Hill f is a third person survival horror game set in 1960's Japan. From the Silent Hill franchise, this game feels like a spinoff. Silent Hill f has combat similar to the Dark Souls series, atmosphere similar to the Fatal Frame series, and audio design similar to the original Silent Hill games. The game takes approximately 8-10 hours to complete your first playthrough, however the game encourages you to play for at least 3 playthoughs to fully understand the story of the game. There are a total of 5 endings and 56 achievements. The total time it takes to 100% this game is approximately 35-40 hours.

+ The story of this game is deep once you really dive into it, heavy on the psychological horror. At first face value you might think that the story is thin and stereotypical, as the game throws a bit too much in your face in the first 10 minutes. (And a few times near the end, I'm looking at you UFO ending). However if you play as long as I did, you will discover a deep engrossing story underneath it all involving drugs and demons. 
+ The cutscenes are all well made, you really get to know the 8 main characters in full detail as the game progresses. 
+ I found the combat to be quite satisfying. There are many ways to take down certain enemies and different ways to equip your character to deal with certain situations. High strategy involved, you can't just go in and swing at everything. There is weapon durability in this game, but I never found it to be too intrusive, there are extra weapons and repair kits around every corner if you search off the beaten path.
+ The art direction is jaw dropping gorgeous at times. Especially the outdoor environments and certain enemy boss designs.
+ The music is very Silent Hill, that is undeniable. Many times the game's music gave me goosebumps. Very beautiful, especially matched with certain epic visuals on screen.
+ The voice acting is professional and well done.

+/- A huge twist will happen during the middle of the game that will certainly divide players.

- Most of the puzzles in this game are extremely vague and difficult to understand. Even when looking at a guide I couldn't figure out how the developers came up with many of the solutions. I believe the game is a bit lost in translation in the puzzle department. There literally isn't one puzzle in the game that I found interesting.
- I can see how completing the game 3-5 times in a row can get a bit mundane and tiresome for some.
- The last hour of the game is very "Devil May Cry", where you fight multiple enemies over and over again in blocked off "Arenas". Feels like a cheap cop out, like they ran out of ideas.  
- For those going for 100% achievements, the collectibles are insane. Certain documents, if you miss one in a 10 minute section of the game, you literally have to play the game 2 more times to get back to the game state where you can collect it again. (The game runs in a NG, NG+, and NG++ cycle).  Also the bosses on "Lost in the Fog" difficulty will make you want to scream.

To me, the game didn't feel like Silent Hill in the slightest, and thats ok. Its a spinoff, confirmed by Konami. I've played through all Silent Hills 10x over least since the first Silent Hill 1 in 1999. Story politics aside, this game is well made in its own right. I had lots of fun with my 40 hours with it.

Overall: 8.5/10

Wow, what a great surprise! I have heard of the game, heard that it was pretty good, but I had no idea it was this fantastic. 

HAAK gives strong metroidvania, in that exploration is very-very rewarding. There are tons of secrets and collectibles to find, and apart from some dyes for your cape, they all add to the sense of progression. The story is also surprisingly intriguing, with a strong post-apocalyptic theme and some family drama. The world looks great, the pixelart is very pretty and the music is just this sort of melodic undertone, that gives the whole world a haunting ambiance. 

Progression-wise, so far, it follows the logic of the story, meaning you can't jump back and forth between levels but you rather go from location to location. Qithin the levels, there are multitudes of ways to go and backtrack. Movement is great, you have some cool traversal options right away and it extends significantly as you go along. The fighting is on the easy side, but that is not a negative at all in my book. It allows for nice progression. 

I think in a way, the design of the titular character gave this game a bit of a disservice. Looking at the funny-looking, almost cartoonish mask Haak is wearing, it planeted a guacameele-like image in my head, thinking it was going to be a more lighthearted, run-of-the-mill platformer with some gimmick. But I am very-very pleasantly surprised. The game is much better. It has grabbed me and it was fascinating to see where it was going. It's exactly the type of brooding, exploration-heavy metroidvania I've been craving. 

I encourage everyone to give it a try, it became one of my favourites.

This is a very bugy, unbalanced, glitchy, janky game I had so much fun playing. You can abuse those bugs as strategic methods to win some difficult fights against higher level enemies. 

You can become a walking, god-like warehouse where you backpack will hold the entire geological and material output of the continent. A skill tree and levels that goes on for days. Forget meticulously organizing 100 different chests in your base. In this reality, two large boxes have the storage capacity of a small dimension. The economy is even more brilliant, you might stumble upon a glittering ore mine, but you'll ignore it. Why? Because the real path to becoming a billionaire is monopolizing the local berry market. Yes 1 berry sells more then hot singles near you.

The enemies in this game have the situational awareness and intelligence of a loaf of bread and can be utterly defeated by a closed door. Enemy archers fire arrows with the velocity of a drifting tortoise, giving you ample time to check your watch, contemplate your life choices, and then casually sidestep to dodge. Conquer armies by standing on a slightly taller rock. Bully epic bosses with your sword that violates the laws of physics while dressed as a fish.

Raids are more of a unbalanced scheduled demolition that will steam roll your defense unless you funnel them into a glitchy killbox, turning a desperate siege into a hilarious parade of lemmings walking into a woodchipper.

The world map is a bit of a shallow puddle, you can explore all within 15 hours but it contains location called "The Castle," a location so vast and intricate you'll suspect the developers spent 99% of their budget on it and built the rest of the world over a single weekend.

- Нелинейность в прохождении квестов.
- Адаптация мира в зависимости от выбранных игроком статов.

[h2]纸房子——作者脱离实际的幻想[/h2]

这部作品看似是在描写操蛋的现实，但其内容并不符合现实。里面的背景以及人物画像充满了矛盾点，完全为作者所想的剧情服务，并没有考虑到这个身份，这个性格的人做出这样的事是否合理。
个人认为这部游戏只是在堆叠、消费一个个的标签，叠得够多了，那自然能有玩家在现实中所经历的人事，从而产生共情。这并不是因为游戏多好，而是情绪够糟。

在玩之前听别人的描述我就大约明白这不会是我喜欢的游戏，之所以还要打开来玩是因为一个朋友和我说ta的朋友因为这个游戏躯体化了，令我感到好奇。玩了之后确实如我所料，作者创作出这样的作品，大概率是因为自己或者身边的人或多或少地经历过。没有解决方法没关系，也许是能力不足。但她甚至没有表现出关怀，就一味地输出痛苦，再安上一些做梦般的结局，令人不适。

我觉得该有第二个无好感结局，那就是赵颖考上了211摆脱原生家庭。她不需要和家里人鱼死网破，也并不需要借助他人的力量才能离开。说到底她看似什么都没有，但已拥有了很多，有相貌有成绩，有关怀自己的老师与朋友。她只是给自己画了个圈固步自封不愿走出去，而当一个人觉得自己很悲惨时，不管现实如何她都会活得很悲惨。

不推荐有相似经历的人游玩，游戏只会令人想起不好的人和事，带来一些负面情绪，而不会起到任何疗愈，或者说抚慰的效果。

《纸房子》是一部中等的篇幅的视觉小说，一周目时长约在[spoiler]6小时，分几天玩也不错，中间有适合休息的节奏点。[/spoiler]
游戏有着黑白的美术风格，线条感强。在阅读时，玩家可以在心里填上想要的颜色。
游戏的文本大多是对话和心理活动，比较好读。作者的台词功底很好，语言流畅，其中一些精辟的对白让我怀疑过作者是否有相似的经历。
游戏的配乐调度优秀。在一些时刻，音乐的转换或停顿，让文字未出，情感已至。此外，一些同样的文字用不同的配乐演出，也很出彩。总体来说，游戏的配乐比较“后台”，作用到位，也不抢戏。
我没把ED和OP算在配乐内。我在关掉灯的房间里循环了许多遍ED《在我变成你之前》，这将成为我2025年夏末记忆里的一部分。



[b]以下的所有内容都包含剧透。[/b]


我刚开始玩《纸房子》时，被设定在2018年的县城和高中吸引。游戏里的描绘，与我青少年时生活的千禧年后的省会城市有诸多相似——电玩城，相约一起上厕所的高中同学，有着水泥花窗楼道的旧公寓等等。中学时候的一个夏夜，我去好友阿J的家。我穿过旧公寓里的楼道，在他家的窗边看到了此生难忘的夏日星空。

如果我生得晚一些，会把中学时亲密无间的友谊当作爱情吗？这是个难以回答的问题。我很喜欢王艺菡在ED2里的那句反问，“但我对这段友情的用心程度难道比恋爱更低级吗？”回望过去，是否要为每一份亲密的情感贴上标签，已不重要。
我还会想到，如果大学毕业后我留在了的国内，一个人生活着，是否会像徐敏敏一样，手插在外衣口袋里，眯着细长的眼，行走在不知名的小城，与小自己几岁的青少年成为朋友。那是我的The Road Not Taken.

《纸房子》是个悲伤的故事，但作者笔下对幸福的描写更让我难忘。
当一个人来到人世间不久，成为青少年，面对荒谬的世界与绝大多数的原生家庭，往往少有选择的余地。内心之外传来的声音会告诉ta，是ta自己要去选择高考，努力，去走向那些被众人期许的道路。但是，朋友，年少时的朋友，往往是我们人生第一次真正意义上的选择，这个选择不需要被任何声音告知和劝诫，就知道是内心所愿。

于是在我心里，这是一部关于青少年之间，朋友们的亲密感情的故事。友情也好，爱情也罢，真挚与迷惘，爱与恨，我猜测这也是作者最想写的。

这篇评测我思索了很久，在九月初的一周目玩完后，我就时不时想要写点什么。
关于作品的角色和剧情，我有一些遗憾。许多结局戛然而止，又或者像王艺菡ED1里，在17岁的夏天与过于梦幻的结局之间，我想还有许多值得书写的故事。

一直到了10月，在已经有些冷的一个秋天的早晨，我坐在麦当劳喝着咖啡，想着作者给的留白，想着我期望看到的角色们17，27，37岁的“三部曲”。我意识到，作者没写的部分，我可以自己弥补。于是我开始写一篇同人小说。

以下，便是同人故事的内容了。
故事的起点是陆婷线的ED1之后。


[h3]Ratty’s Love, After Story[/h3]

玻璃橱窗里，一只小老鼠站立着。它后肢下的短爪支撑着圆滚滚的身体，灰色的毛抖动，黑珍珠般的眼睛扑闪着。
它从覆盖着尖脑袋的绒毛里伸出粉色的小鼻子，头在玻璃窗中不停上下晃动，像闻到了什么新颖的味道。
玻璃的另一面，是一根纤细的手指。手指在玻璃上划着圆圈，逗弄着橱窗里的小鼠。
手指的主人穿着毛绒的白色卫衣，戴着兜帽，像一只大号的小鼠。

“喜欢就买了吧。”说话的是一旁的赵颖。她向橱窗微微倾斜身子，声音带着暗哑的烟嗓。
赵颖穿着灰色T恤，双手插在牛仔裤的口袋里，手腕上彩虹色的编织手链露在外面。
“不要。我说了只是看看。”陆婷直起身，用双手把自己头上的卫衣兜帽向后摘去，甩了甩露出的黑色短发，“看到就很开心了。”
她戴着黑框的大圆眼镜，镜片后一双大眼睛扑闪着，笑着看向赵颖。

几个星期后。
空荡的房间里，赵颖在床上翻了几下，而陆婷穿着卫衣，站在床边。
床边的床头柜上，是一张放有两人合照的木制相框。照片里，两人摆着V字手势，露出笑容。
赵颖又翻了几下。
“你醒了？”陆婷问到。
赵颖的头昏昏沉沉，脑子里还有成片的文字，是昨夜赶的稿子。

过了一会儿，她皱着眉，睁开眼。床边的陆婷手里提着一个像是开心乐园套餐一样的纸盒子。
“哎？你买了什么？吃的吗？”赵颖问道。
“哦！这个啊……”陆婷右手把纸盒子放在床头柜上，左手抓着卫衣的下沿。“我还是，买了……”
“啊？买了什么？”赵颖左手扶着额头，右胳膊将自己从床上撑起，将身子探向床头柜。
陆婷伸出手，打开纸盒上的卡扣。赵颖看到，里面有两只灰色的毛绒小鼠，探着鼻子四处闻着。其中一只对着盒子的角落，另一只则看向她。赵颖和看向她的那只小鼠四目相接。
“噢！很可爱啊！”赵颖笑了。
陆婷紧皱的眉头舒展开来，坐到床边。“那个，我……还会想着她们。然后店员说，她们是社会性动物，至少要两只一起，所以……”
赵颖看着陆婷手舞足蹈地“解释”着。从纸盒子的方向，她闻到了一阵暖暖的，略带一点臭臭的味道。那个味道，与小狗身上的味道有点相似。那是小生命绽放的味道。

陆婷还在向她描述店员如何和小老鼠斗智斗勇，把她们从玻璃橱窗里拿出来。
而赵颖看着她，眼里是十年前，还是高中生的陆婷和她一起逗着豆花。那时，陆婷笑着说，“有时候看着它们吐着舌头傻乐，我的心情也会变得很好……“
赵颖伸出手，抚过陆婷的短发和侧脸。
陆婷愣了一下，赵颖已经吻了她的嘴唇。


十年后。

清晨的阳光穿过窗户，照在已经摆满了家具和花花草草的房间里。房间里，一些全息投影在家具、花草和墙上闪烁着。
阳光也照在房间一角的一个木制小桌台上。
桌台最靠外边，摆着两个粉色的陶瓷小碗，里面盛满了棕色的三角形小饼干。
小碗的后面，是两个白色的小罐子。两个罐子上都画着爱心的图案，分别贴着一张小老鼠的照片。

房间的大门被推开。赵颖穿着T恤和牛仔裤，提着一个装着早餐的纸盒子走进来。
陆婷坐在餐桌边，穿着一件粉色的旧长袖。比起十年前，那长袖已经大了一号。

陆婷抬头望向赵颖，没有说话。
过了一会，她又把头低下。
赵颖把盒子放在餐桌上，坐到一旁的座椅上。

两人相对坐着，沉默了一阵子。良久，赵颖露出笑容，从桌面上伸出手。
在她的手在离陆婷的脸还有一尺距离时，一直低着头的陆婷突然抬起头。“写王艺菡写得爽吗？”
黑框眼镜后，陆婷睁大了黑色的双眼，露出似笑非笑的表情。
赵颖收回手，笑容凝固在脸上。“那只是一篇…… 给社里的小说。”
陆婷耸起依然纤瘦的肩膀，双眼直视着赵颖，没有说话。
赵颖看着她，深吸了一口气。“王艺菡和我只是朋友，而且，我们十多年都没联系了。”
说完，赵颖也低下头，两人又沉默了一会。

过了许久，赵颖抬起头，继续说，“记得我进去之后，你们两个那段时间关系还不错。”
陆婷偏过头，不再看向赵颖，耸起的双肩放下去了一些。
“那你那个上司是怎么回事？”陆婷依然偏着头，没有看向赵颖。
“我们只是工作关系…… 而且，我高中都没毕业，她对我来说就像……”赵颖还没说完，陆婷便用力把头甩回来，直盯着赵颖。赵颖吓得抖了一下，没再说下去。

陆婷停顿了一下，也深吸了一口气。“那最近和你很熟的那个同事又是什么？！”
“啊？”赵颖长大了嘴，下巴僵硬。“他，他是个……男的……”
“够了！”陆婷吼道，然后又低下了头。
赵颖看到，眼泪顺着陆婷的镜片滴落。
她呆坐在椅子上，看着陆婷抽泣。

过了一阵子，陆婷抬起头，满眼已都是泪水，“我知道你不喜欢我外婆，但她去世前，和你说过你要给我幸福，你明明答应了……”
“我……”赵颖想说话，却像被掐住了脖子。
周围的空气突然变得刺骨的寒冷。
高中时潮湿的宿舍，那天早上醒来时，陆婷掐着她的脖子。那时的陆婷也是满脸泪水。

“我讨厌你！”还在恍惚间，陆婷的吼声再次吓了她一跳。
赵颖的椅子都往后退了一点。
她下意识去摸牛仔裤的口袋。
口袋里空空的，她才想起，她已经戒烟十多年了。


天气已经炎热。赵颖和陆婷又吵了几天。
一天早晨，赵颖推开公寓的大门。门外，夏日的阳光耀眼。
二十年前一个普通的夏日，陆婷与她在宿舍相拥。
陆婷身体的触感，温度，在她耳边的呼吸。
陆婷抱着她说，“我们可以一直在一起，其他人都不用管，就我们两个……”
“原来，她真的是说，就我们两个啊。”赵颖笑了。“她与陆婷是那么的不同，终有一天，陆婷也会离她而去。”

赵颖在公寓门口驻足了一会。
她最后看了一眼屋内。视线的每一寸，都满是她们一起生活了十多年的痕迹。
卧室门的另一边里，陆婷还在床上安睡，她睡着时的表情总是有点紧张。
至少这一次，她将这间“纸房子”留给了陆婷。赵颖想着，露出了笑容。
然后关上了门。

两天前，她去了杂志社，和上司确认了今后将远程工作的事宜。
那时她还没想好要去哪里，直到徐敏敏出现在她脑子里——那个几乎已经被她遗忘在记忆深处的神秘女子。
她们曾在湖边丢水漂。敏敏姐眯着细长的双眼，和她描述东北的雪景。
就去东北吧…… 去一个湖边，租一个老房子，在里面写写画画，看看雪景。
她做了决定。

车在公路上行驶着，不久后已经快到城郊。
赵颖把车在一家店门口停下，然后下了车，走进店里。
店的自动门打开，她看到这家店除了把一些标牌和指南换成了全息投影，其它装修和十年前没什么区别。
白色的顶灯，大排的货架，透明的宠物橱窗。
她走进店里，向一个她确定要去的地方走去。

非常感谢尼妮薇和烟草，感谢两位“第一读者”对这篇同人小说的阅读和建议。

Ratty’s Love的标题来自陆婷的全ED攻略成就，“老鼠的爱” 。
游戏里，陆婷是我攻略的最后一条线。我习惯把想要选择的支线留到最后，尽管在她还是“不知道叫什么婷”的时候，就已决定了。

终于，我写完了这篇评测和同人小说，也到了要和《纸房子》，和2018年的陈水，和角色们告别的时候。

能通过游戏，在今年夏末的夜里，一瞥那时的幸福和痛苦，于我是一段珍贵的旅程。

最后，我很高兴在我的阅读过程里，有与我在截图区聊天的Steam好友们，和大家一起边玩边聊真的非常开心！
此外，还有游戏社区里想和我一起踢爆那个“男的”的蛋的陌生玩家们，我也很高兴遇见你们。

I really wanted to love this game… but it’s complicated.

On paper, it had everything to be a great experience: an emotional story, dual protagonists, and some interesting mechanics. But in practice, it struggles to deliver.

The narrative tries to be deep and moving, but the pacing is off. Long cutscenes right from the start make it hard to get invested — players barely get a chance to play before being asked to sit through lengthy dialogues. Storytelling is important, but it works better when players are already hooked.

There are good ideas here, like switching between characters, which adds variety. Unfortunately, it feels underused. Combat quickly becomes repetitive and tedious, and exploration is almost nonexistent. The world isn’t open, and movement is constantly blocked by tiny rocks or twigs — which breaks immersion. Looting is limited to a few items that don’t seem to serve much purpose since there’s no crafting system. Upgrading gear happens at campfires (à la Tomb Raider), but doing so respawns enemies, which feels more punishing than rewarding.

Gameplay mechanics — both combat and exploration — feel clunky. It’s not one specific flaw, but rather a general lack of flow and fun. It’s a shame, because the game seemed promising… maybe it gets better if you push through, but it doesn’t really make you want to.

And then there’s the graphics. For a title built on Unreal Engine 5, it’s surprisingly rough. Grass popping in, foliage effects that look like 20-year-old sprites, and outdated wave animations — all on a rig with a 3080. Older games like The Witcher 3 or A Plague Tale: Requiem look far better.

I’m still early in the game, but my motivation to continue is fading fast. Dropping this review here while another game finishes installing — not sure I’ll be coming back.

Не столь важно как вы закончите, важно как вы пройдете этот путь и как ваши решения повлияют на финал.

To clear things up — this happened because Unity discontinued the UNET service, which powered the game’s online multiplayer.

For multiplayer to work again, the developers would have to completely rebuild the game’s network system. That’s not realistic for an older title, especially when there’s already a remake with better graphics and active player support.

So, if you want to play multiplayer, get Arizona Sunshine: Remake or Arizona Sunshine 2, which also features an 8-hour campaign.

We loved you, Arizona Sunshine (2016). You’ll be missed.

I was about to post a positive review for VTM Bloodlines 2. I wrote it while playing, listing every strengths and weaknesses of this game. But then I reached the end of the game and I was baffled, and this is an understatement. 

I was enjoying the game in the beginning, even if it is indeed not really "Bloodlines 2". Well it is not at all in fact. But it is still a solid game from the World of Darkness universe and I was happy with that. I really loved some of the characters, the gameplay was basic but fun, I really enjoyed the investigation parts with Fabien, Phyre (a.k.a. the Nomad) had an interesting story, the change of rhythm when switching from Phyre to Fabien was good and prevented me from getting bored with neither of them, the story was slow paced at first with every mysteries growing thicker until everything eventually started to unveil. Geez, this game had such a good recipe here for a good thriller. Since I love detective novels, I was absolutely delighted with all this. 

But then after the two thirds of the game, just after the big climax of the story, it felt incredibly rushed and disappointing and everything started to blurs together. From a well crafted and slow paced story you jump into a messy and rushed ending. Some main quests were useless and felt like they were there to fill the gap in between, while others doomed you in the end if you didn’t choose the choice the studio wanted you to pick. So much things has been left aside or were underexploited without any reason. Everything was happening so fast that you struggled to follow each events and their repercussions. And the cherry on top was this awful and insulting "epilogue". Seeing how the game started, I think the original plan of the studio was to make this story longer than it actually is. The difference between the good beginning and the rushed ending is really contrasted in a very bad way. 

It definitely wasn’t Bloodlines 2. It wasn’t an RPG. It wasn’t even a good linear thriller. It was nothing but smokescreen and missed opportunities. And it fatally ended in bitter disappointment. You either finish your game properly, or you do not sell an unfinished product at all, period.

Hot take incoming, this game has my favourite story in the series thus far, granted this may be due to my bias of early year Batman stories but I love character driven plots and more than the others so far, this one really gives Batman time to shine and grow in this game. Granted this game is very unpolished, I didn't have most of the issues that a lot of people had with the PC port of this game but I was playing with the Community Patch so that's likely why. The game was really fun, had some fun side missions even if a fair lot of them were just copy-pasted from City (as well as a lot of this game) they were great and housed some really good boss fights. Speaking of, yeah the boss fights in this game are absolutely the best in the series so far, these characters got so much love in this game, Deathstroke was such a great first impression on how the bosses would be in this game (not counting Killer Croc as the first boss but he was pretty good for the tutorial). The open world though I probably the least memorable so far due to this game fully taking place in Winter (literally Christmas Eve) and the top half of the map literally being Arkham City's map but covered in snow and not partially submerged. The voice acting of this game is stellar, special Highlights to Batman (Roger Craig Smith), Joker (Troy Baker) and Alfred (Martin Javis) especially with the former two replacing Kevin Conroy as Batman and Mark Hamill as Joker in order to portray younger versions of these characters and they, as mentioned before, killed it in their roles, they need to be cast as those characters more often. Highly recommended but get the Community Patch for it.

i LOVE this game, i just found it yesterday and i had to have it after i spent lots of time in the demo

story: the plot is your basic "we gotta get the mcguffin and challenge our rival" etc fantasy stuff but it doesnt need to be more because the way it's told is so funny, these characters you meet will stick with you! also i love seeing the notes people left along the way in chests and stuff, there is a world being built here, this game is funny and intrigiuing for even a basic story, if you choose lore to prioritize you won't regret it

gameplay: this is really cool, random dungeons but it also seems to be following somewhat of a linear story which is cool for me. You have 3 choices of playstyle too, prioritizing lore, puzzles or combat (i went with lore). Theres crafting and mining elements too and it never gets in the way of the core gameplay, its fun to keep diving to the bottom of the dungeon and seeing what characters you might meet or what new traps lie before you! when you get into combat, its a system of clicking when the cursor hits a certain area, kinda like a golf game. it sounds weird but it absolutely works, it's addicting as hell especially when you get powerups that help you either slow it down or give you more hit areas.

A basic mechanical bite-sized experience lasting just under seven hours.
Right when I launched the game, I got flashbacks to Blade Runner 2049 — the holographic love scene between Joi and Mariette, where their unforgettable faces and bodies overlapped.
In this game, the overlap was more like local, limping peasants sitting on chairs because they had nowhere else to rest before the movie started, munching warm popcorn through two merged faces.
It felt like a cheap Lidl-style interlude that sent a tingle straight to my cerebral cortex.

And yet, the charm, the potential, the rough edges, the bugs, selecting movies and the somewhat dragging process of upgrading my business actually captivated me.
Even if the developers stopped updating the game, I still enjoyed the monotony — the graphical glitches of a promising simulation experience, where I, as a manager, just named my cinema Rotten Greya. A place where all film lovers and enthusiasts happily rot in their musty seats, light up cigarettes, record movies on their cheap cameras, or make phone calls.
My opinion wouldn’t change even if the game’s development stopped, but I surely wouldn’t pay real-life technicians who only turn on the movies but never fix broken machines, and whose staff don’t even restock supplies from storage. They all stood there as if whipped — which, ironically, reminded me of reality, and I agreed with it. Not everyone is hardworking, after all.
The game isn’t perfectly thought-out, but it gave me a pleasantly tuned evening.
🍿 solid 7/10🥤

As far as I can tell, this game genuinely does have the makings of a Black and White spiritual successor. It has a lot of the feel. Unfortunately, I can't honestly recommend it, after only an hour of playtime. There are two main reasons for this.

1. The tutorials.

they're not good. They make reference to game systems you're unfamiliar with, like belief, mana and faith, like you're expected to know them and what they do and where to see them in the UI. There was one tutorial, I think about one-shot wonders, that mentions using them in front of villagers gives you belief points. 

Okay. Fine. What are those, where do I see them, what are they for, and how do I tell when and how much more I've gotten? I've never heard of Belief as an in-game system before. Or maybe I have, but all the tutorial is is a guy talking to me - no making sure I've learned the concepts, no highlighting relevant UI elements to point them out to me, nothing. A better tutorial would be to give me a free wonder to play around with for tutorial purposes and requiring me to use it near the village, and pointing out the increase in belief by highlighting the relevant part of the UI (as well as a previous tutorial talking about what belief is, how to identify it, and how to build and spend it). 

If this was my only gripe with the game, I'd probably power through. But I can't, because of...

2. The bugs.

villagers don't move around believably. Their renders don't match where the game expects them to be. In the God Hand tutorial, I used God Hand on a villager, and punched the ground half a mile away from where the villager actually was. Was that good? Did I do the right thing? Moja recenzja oparta jest na odczuciach z punktu widzenia laika, gracza niedoświadczonego w soulsy.
Po pierwsze postać jest irytująco drewniana.
Wybrałam do walki lekką broń - kusarigamę, żeby być szybka, zwinna i sprawna. Okazuje się, że podczas walki postać zanim wyprowadzi atak, zanim cała sekwencja ataku się skończy a ataku nie da się przerwać i zrobić unik przed atakiem wroga, mijają nieskończone 2 sekundy, w tym czasie wróg, unika i wyprowadza serię kilku ataków i wąchasz kwiatki od spodu:/ Na początku gry, kiedy jeszcze nie jesteś wyekspiony rzucanie czaru w bossa trwa również nieskończone 2 sekundy i nie da się przerwać tego rzucania w momencie kiedy on naciera na twoją postać, no i znowu zdychasz. Najbardziej to czuć przy szybkich bossach, spamujących seriami ataków. Można odblokować umiejętność izoteryczną, żeby rzucać zaklęcia natychmiast ale żeby ją wylewelować to trzeba przejść całą grę, a po co mi ona po ukończeniu gry? Do ogrania DLC, owszem ale nie każdy ma na to ochotę. Spodziewałam się, że w tej grze z tak wysokim poziomem trudności jaki oferuje i silnymi przeciwnikami, relacja pomiędzy siłą i zwinnością postaci a siłą i szybkością wrogów, będzie lepsza a jest piorunująco słaba i niesprawiedliwa. Ktoś by powiedział, bo soulsy takie są, że wrogowie mają gracza na jednego "hita" ale po co, w takim razie, lewelujemy postać? Po to, żeby przeciwnicy mieli nas na dwa "hity"? Ale o tym w dalszej części.

W czasie misji zbiera się mnóstwo zbroi, broni i innych przedmiotów z różnymi statystykami, stylami gry, które zaśmiecają ekwipunek, celowo piszę zaśmiecają bo w obliczu większych przeciwników lub bossa nie dają spodziewanej obrony czy odporności na żywioły. Po przejściu gry, po wielu irytujących walkach, krwawych porażkach, frustrującej straty amrity (potrzebnej do lewelowania), nadal masz takie wyposażenie, że przeciwnicy mają cię na jeden cios. Po przejściu podstawki odblokowuje się nowy tryb, trudniejszy - "Droga Siły". Tu znajdujesz lepsze pancerze, broń i akcesoria ale poziom trudności jest o wiele wyższy niż twój poziom postaci, także dalej jesteś "na jeden cios", co prawda możesz wrócić na poprzedni tryb czyli na "Drogę Samuraja" - jest łatwiej ale tam niewiele zarobisz doświadczenia i pieniędzy. Na dalszych trybach gry, a jest ich 4, schemat obowiązuje ten sam. W ten sposób grę trzeba przejść 4 razy, a wszystko to w celu zdobycia kilku osiągnięć.

Menu jest bardzo nieintuicyjne i niezrozumiałe i gdyby nie wyjaśnienia przyjaciela, to nie wiem ile musiałabym nagrzebać się w internecie, żeby zrozumieć cały interfejs. Co gorsze, nie ma możliwości ustawienia klawiszy akcji pod wygodny dla nas przycisk bo gra nie rozpoznaje bocznych przycisków myszy, powodem jest nieprawidłowe przeniesienie interfejsu z konsoli na PC, nawet opisy przycisków akcji (klawiatury i myszy) są pod pada.

Różnorodne misje często rozgrywane są w tych samych lokacjach, autorzy nie postarali się o inną lokację dla każdej misji, a lokacje mnie kompletnie nie urzekły, często są ciemne, pokręcone, specjalnie utrudnione jakimiś dziurami w podłodze,wodą, ogniem, przepaściami a upadek=śmierć :/ Jednym zdaniem, lokacje w tej grze nie należą do najciekawszych. Rzuca to cień na odbiór klimatyczno-krajobrazowy. Spodziewałam się wielkiej przygody z piękną scenerią japońską a zastałam ciasne, powtarzające się klitki z mnóstwem potworów lub bossów do zabicia i ciężko zrozumiałą fabułą, a można było zrobić przepiękne scenerie japońskie, wtedy gra zyskałaby na odbiorze. Do tego grafika jest na średnim poziomie, taka no... do przyjęcia.
Fabuła hmmm jest ale przez japońskie nazwy postaci, trudno się w niej połapać ponieważ ciężko zapamiętać kto jest kim. To może ja Wam skrócę tą fabułę: dobro/zło przy trudnych wyborach moralno-etycznych walczy ze złem/dobrem a nasz protagonista to irlandzki żeglarz, który stał się samurajem i został wciągnięty w tą walkę, jak myślicie kto i co wygra? Hyhy, to tak z przymrużeniem oka;)

A tak nawiasem mówiąc, prawdziwa rozgrywka zaczyna się po ukończeniu podstawki bo dopiero wtedy zdobywa się boskie przedmioty, dające żenująco "większą" obronę i zadawane mierne obrażenia, a przy posiadaniu wszystkich DLC można zdobyć wszystkie osiągnięcia.
No i sobie gram... wyposażona w boskie ulepszone u kowala opancerzenie i boską ulepszoną również u kowala broń i co? I też mają mnie na jednego hita... to po co to lewelowanie i zdobywanie tych wszystkich pancerzy, broni, umiejętności? Po 200 godz. gry, przeciwnicy mają mnie na jednego hita! Pełna frustracja!

Kolejny minus tej gry jest następujący: żeby trafiać swoimi atakami przeciwnika trzeba go zaznaczyć ale jeśli jest ich kilku, kamera sama się przełącza z jednego na drugiego na trzeciego przez co ataki nie trafiają w ani jednego. Jest to tak irytujące i utrudniające walkę, że odechciewa się grać. Dodatkowo jeśli znajdziesz się w ciasnym pomieszczeniu z 10 silnymi wrogami, a twórcy z rozmiłowaniem robią to na każdym kroku, to w pole widzenia wchodzą ściany, drzwi, sufit i inne elementy scenerii. I jeszcze taki mały szczegół ale też bardzo irytujący, jeśli nasza postać lub wróg znajduje się na jakimś przewyższeniu terenu, to niestety ataki są niecelne, ech.

Następny feler dotyczy gry w kooperacji. Zapraszamy znajomego i możemy razem grać ale chramy (kapliczki zapisu) nie odnawiają eliksirów leczniczych ani zaklęć, przywracają jedynie część paska życia, bowiem można grać razem ale z ograniczoną ilością zgonów (ok. 7 zgonów na misję). Jest też możliwość zaproszenia znajomego ofiarowując kubeczki ochoko ale przy każdym zgonie trzeba ponownie je ofiarować i zacząć misję od nowa. W grze solo natomiast przy każdym zgonie, odradzamy się przy kapliczce i odnawiamy czary i eliksiry. A w otchłani przyzywasz znajomego, żeby było łatwiej ale łatwiej nie jest bo zamiast jednego bossa pojawia się dwóch bossów.... a poziom otchłani rośnieeee ee ale żeby wyekspić się dość dobrze, to trzeba spędzić w tej grze 500 godz. ... albo pół życia... no trochę przegięcie ze strony twórców.

Podsumowując, postać drewniana i powolna, lewelowanie postaci i przekuwanie najlepszego opancerzenia i broni nie dają satysfakcji, niejasny interfejs, te same nieklimatyczne i nieatrakcyjne lokacje dla różnych misji, fabuła ciężka do połapania się, przełączająca się kamera między przeciwnikami, nieskuteczne ataki na podwyższeniu terenu, gra multi ma ograniczone możliwości. Zapomniałam o plusach... yyy chyba tylko ogrywanie tej gry ze znajomym. W mojej ocenie 4/10.

The general mood in the air, backed up by a lot of big-brain YouTubers, always told me that System Shock 2 is some unforgiving, demanding monstrosity that you basically need a PhD or something to play. In reality, it is fairly easy to get into if you don't fall asleep during the tutorial and use some common sense. Basically, leave the weird builds for the second playthrough, remember that fix and maintain are two different things, and always have at least 100 nanites on you in the second half of the game. Do this and you're golden. This game is way, WAY more approachable than System Shock 1 ever was, despite being way more complex.

The game aged way better than expected in general. The story is really gripping; something deliciously bleak is happening all the time, and The Many is as much of a great antagonist as SHODAN is. Exploration is fairly great too - Von Braun is way less of a same-y maze than Citadel, but it still demands you to pay attention. It is pretty much a happy medium between "oh god, how do I navigate this mess" of System Shock 1 and the almighty GPS navigator of Bioshock. The action part is nothing to write home about, but it is like that basically throughout the genre.

Hilariously enough, the curse of underwhelming ~shock endings starts here, but thank god here it is just kinda abrupt and goofy and not the game running out of steam but still agonizingly going on for a few more hours (looking at you, Bioshock and Prey).

All in all - this is an all-time favorite, despite the age and all.

System Shock 2 is a First Person Shooter where the player is a soldier on board the starship Von Braun, which has been taken over by a rogue Artificial Intelligence called Shodan, and an insect hive mind called The Many.

I never played the original version which released in 1999, so I’m just reviewing this like any new release. It doesn’t feel as good to play as the System Shock 1 remake, but if I understand correctly, SS1 remake featured gameplay improvements over its original version, whereas SS2 remaster is just a graphical improvement.

As the player explores the Von Braun, you’ll have to fight against various enemies including mutants, cyborgs, security robots, defence turrets, giant spiders, and monkeys (who can fire psychic projectiles at you). Security cameras, which can be destroyed, will summon lengthy waves of reinforcements if they spot you, however some enemies seem to slowly respawn over time anyway.

Available weapons include a wrench and alien crystal for melee attacks, pistol, shotgun, assault rifle, grenade launcher, various laser pistols/rifles, and some other alien weapons which I didn’t use. To equip a weapon, the player must upgrade the relevant weapon category (standard, energy, heavy, exotic) to a high enough level, by spending cybernetic modules. You can also find different ammunition types for some weapons, for example standard bullets, anti-personnel which deals more damage against flesh based enemies, anti-armour which deals more damage against robotic enemies, and different types of grenades.

Weapons will wear down over time and can break during combat, which can be annoying, so you’ll have to keep repairing and maintaining them, which requires putting upgrade points in two separate skills. Some items must be researched before you can use them, while things like turrets, cameras, and vending machines can be hacked, both of which require skills to be upgraded to the appropriate level.

Inventory management is a constant challenge. Even after upgrading to maximum capacity, you can’t simultaneously carry all weapons and ammo, plus healing items, and quest items. Thankfully you can leave things on the floor and they’ll still be there if you want them later.

I played on normal difficulty, which wasn’t too tough, especially because the player can respawn if you’ve activated the relevant machine on each deck. This is useful because there’s not many healing items to be found. You can buy more from vending machines, but dying and respawning is actually cheaper and restores more health. However, if you can find and repair a surgical bed, you can get a cheap full heal.

I found the biggest difficulty to be navigating the maze like map design which is typical of ‘90s games. It was sometimes unclear where I needed to go, or how exactly to get there, to complete mission objectives. Also one quest update in my journal wasn’t very helpful. It told me to go to the engine core, but then didn’t tell me what I had to do when I was there. It didn’t help that enemies seemed to be respawning quickly in that room, so I couldn’t have a proper look around to figure out what to do. After consulting a walkthrough, I could see that I was given a door code in an audio log. Would have saved me some confusion if that code was displayed in the journal, which does happen with codes for other quests.

It took me 16 hours to complete the story. I didn’t have any problems with bugs, crashes, framerate or stuttering. Controls are rebindable and work well with mouse and keyboard.

System Shock 2 feels a bit janky by modern standards, but I’d say its still worth playing if you pick it up on a sale, especially for fans of single player First Person Shooters.

You play as Mia. Her father has recently gone missing on a mission and Mia is going after him with her dog Lupi. Along with her allies: Samuel and Agatha, Mia must explore an area known as the Perimeter to find him. During her search, she discovers what happened to the team her father brought with him 20 years earlier and the Cult of Fear that they were researching.

From a technical pov, the game is set in the world of “Paranormal Order” – a paper RPG created by Brazilian streamer Rafael Lange (Cellbit). Unfortunately, this is both an advantage and a disadvantage. Advantage, because for some players it is an entry into a world they have already explored during classic sessions; disadvantage, because the rest are thrown in at the deep end without any explanation of what and how.


Would I recommend it? No.
It’s a decent survival-horror and good detective game, that tries to innovate in both genres instead of following old, pre-defined paths. Unfortunately, the game has a lot of serious flaws; from unpatched bugs to strange and ill-considered gameplay solutions. 
Honestly, I don't understand why this game has an "overwhelmingly positive" rating on Steam. I assume we're dealing with the fandom of the classic system, and unfortunately, this leads to them overlooking obvious flaws so as not to criticize what they love.

✅[list]
[*] Pixelart 2D mixed with semi-realistic 3D graphics. 

[*] Very creative and original maps of individual locations. Each of them feels distinct, has its own rules, which you need to learn and understand in order to achieve anything on a given map.

[*] Soundtrack and sounds. It's rare for it to creep me out in any game, but here they managed to do it.

[*] Complex and interesting story.

[*] Creative and complex puzzles and use of in-game mechanics. 

[*] Nice mechanic of direct interaction with puzzles instead of simply providing part.

[*] Available tools really complement the gameplay and allows us to discover hidden hints, dialogues and other mysteries.

[*] Not direct, "hidden in plain sight" hints.

[*] Most boss battles are unique in their execution and well-thought-out. They utilize the environment and lore to achieve a goal rather than direct combat.

[*] original character selection mechanic.

[*] Secret ending needs thinking “outside the box” + often breaks the 4th wall.

[*] In-game secrets. Some puzzles are really complicated and require lot of research: ciphers, mathematical equations, plotting graphs etc.

😐
K&M controls could be better. Game was obviously done with controller in mind.
Windows pointer instead of something more in-line with game design.

"Se eu quisesse resolver mistério, eu era da gang do scooby doo".

Brincadeiras a parte: o jogo tem uma proposta muito interessante e talvez para o público dele, faça sentido e seja bacana, mas em nenhum momento esse jogo tem um disclaimer falando que é somente para o público que já gosta dos conteúdos do Cellbit, ou seja, puzzles que envolvem coisas externas ao jogo (tem enigma que você precisa ir até na pasta do jogo pra resolver!!!) falta de explicações de certas mecânicas (sério que no labirinto o cachorro latir é um jeito de resolver? não foi nem explicado que o cachorro latia), ausência de explicação de botões (descobri em 70% do game que existia um mapa borocoxo chamado mapa mental).

Primeiro que o jogo não tem nenhuma função de jornal que é presente em qualquer outro jogo do gênero, quer se lembrar de alguma pista ou anotação? Boa sorte. Se tiver no modo mais fácil, vai precisar acessar o mapa mental e se lembrar onde a anotação está, se estiver no mais difícil, que você tenha paciência de se lembrar onde está pra ir lá andando. Tudo isso poderia ser resolvido de outra forma: modo fácil você ter um jornal com anotações e o modo dificil você ter o mapa mental e se lembrar onde estão, evitando o backtracking infernal.

Backtracking infernal, sabe por que é infernal? porque a personagem é lenta pra ir, e navegar de um lado pro outro é maçante, mesmo com os atalhos do subsolo, ainda se torna um caos ir do ponto A ao ponto B. Em conjunto com isso tem o problema da gameplay toda travada do jogo especialmente em combates, eu sinceramente me questiono se o combate desse jogo devia existir, mecânicas completamente clunky, uma boss fight final incluindo quase um parry/defend em um jogo que claramente não está pronto para receber essas mecânicas.

Eu sei que o nome do jogo é "Enigma" do Medo, mas o jogo literalmente tem um enigma pra qualquer coisa existente a se fazer, é enigma em cima de enigma, e as direções são nulas e totalmente dependentes de você explorar cada anotação em cada lugar. Em vários outros jogos do gênero você não precisa ler literalmente TODAS as anotações disponíveis do lugar pra resolver 1 puzzle, nesse você precisa, e vai precisar se lembrar de onde elas estão pra você checar várias vezes se necessário. Da metade pro final eu desisti e procurei as respostas porque queria descobrir mais sobre a história e não perder a cabeça com os puzzles.

A história no final tem seu momento alto de revelação, mas ficou rasa, não me senti tão conectado com as coisas da lore e situações num geral, talvez seja porque não acompanho o universo, mas mesmo jogos que derivam de universos maiores não são totalmente dependentes de você precisar estar imerso neles previamente pra desfrutar da história do jogo atual (como baldurs gate e witcher por exemplo).

A otimização desse jogo é pavorosa, um jogo simples em pixel art não devia ser tão custoso pra rodar em qualquer PC que seja.

Meu resumo é: assistir alguém jogando isso deve ser um prazer incrível, mas a experiência de jogar, lidar com os puzzles necessitando explorar cada canto, se lembrar de onde está cada anotação, combate pavoroso, história confusa, otimização extremamente zoada torna-se uma experiência frustrante.

Não recomendo, existem jogos melhores, com propostas melhores e que entregam um resultado melhor. Orçamento de mais de 4 milhões, tem muito jogo indie que com muito menos entregou coisa MUITO melhor.

This game is an anomaly, I've tried to start writing this review and have started over about three times because of how hard it is to put into words. So my thoughts won't flow as smoothly as I'd like but bear with me. (Tldr at bottom but gimme a shot)

The game is easily the most influential a piece of media has ever been on my life. The only discernible time I have opened a game, movie, book, song, or anything else and left it permanently altered in some way. - (I'll follow up on this x1)

I also do not recommend it to you, more than likely, and that's not a matter of me guessing your taste but rather the majority of people who just want to play a game would not find this unenjoyable. Myself included, I picked it up in a state of severe disillusionment with games, which I've loved my whole life. I wasn't looking for a game, and if you came here looking for that, I suggest you write this game down and buy it another time. Or don't, it's really not for everyone. I don't know anybody I'd recommend it to.

I'd recommend it if you feel like you can push yourself and commit, muster the willpower to stare at a glorified painting for hours and hours over the course of a long time. The game begins quiet and ends quiet and never screams.

(following up from before)- The game's strength lies in one great thing. It does not need you to be here, and will not encourage you to stay. Even in the game mechanics you can just boot it up once and not think about it for a year. But the process of staying is what I am writing this review for, because calling it rewarding is an understatement. The game with masterful subtlety lulls you into contentment if you let it. If you're not looking for a large battle or showy displays of intense emotional climaxes after a few hours commitment, but instead you just stick around and let it happen, it can happen. 

The slow, easing reward is you becoming okay with there not being very much. The lull it puts you in is recontextualized as just simple contentment as soon as you see a pretty piece of art in the game that makes you feel satisfied. There is no stimulation other then the presence of your surroundings and the music, until short bursts hours and hours apart that may seem like absolutely nothing to someone else, but everything to the player. If you 'worked' in a triple A game for ten hours and your reward getting to see a spider, you'd be pretty ticked off. But in this game it works perfectly.

And for more context, even though I said it before, I did pick up the game while not playing games. A phase where the mass stimulation of action and explosion filled games did nothing for me. And when I was playing this game I realized it wasn't trying to do that for me. It wasn't trying to stimulate my mind so badly I'd need to chase highs like that in gaming forever. It was simply nothing. Almost nothing. Nothing but the bare minimum for my mind to process until getting to process anything became the reward.

After playing this game it's changed how I look at that kinda mental stimulation. I don't need high octane adrenaline movies or games or anything. I can sit for hours on end and just stare at a wall if I please. (not that I have a reason to, but I could) And honestly, I don't expect these words to impact anybody in the slightest. The game shows this all to you in a way I simply cannot, or even just words in general cannot.

Tldr, Don't play this game, more than likely, if you came here to check out potential fun video games. Because it's not what you want
Play it when you'd like to get lost in thought, and have an artful program masterfully subtly guide a mind already lost in thought in a way that will cause a thinking that some guy on steam found very useful

NavalArt is an incredible ship design game, it is easily one of the best out there. It takes a bit of time to get used to, but once you do, the creative possibilities are almost endless. You can build practically anything, though the main focus is on ships. Compared to Ultimate Admiral: Dreadnoughts, NavalArt absolutely outclasses it when it comes to design freedom. (and with far fewer bugs, too)

It’s the perfect game if you love naval warfare but don’t want to be limited to a single era. You can jump between 19th-century ironclads, World War II battleships, or even modern stealth ships.

That said, NavalArt feels less like a traditional “game” and more like a simplified 3D design tool. Think of it as a mix between Juno: New Origins 
rather than Kerbal Space Program. Most parts, like turrets and guns, are finished assets, but hulls, superstructures, most mast will need to be building by hand. This isn’t a flaw, though; it’s just something to be aware of. If that level of creative control appeals to you, you’ll love it. If not, you can always download incredible hulls and ships made by the community on the Steam Workshop. And if you’re unsure, try it out — you can always refund it if it’s not your thing.

Graphics are good and it runs smoothly for me. Only thing that sometimes bugs me personally are the loading times on bigger builds, but that's to be expected.


Now, onto some quality-of-life improvements I’d love to see or I just haven't found yet (these aren’t really bugs, just small fixes and conveniences):

Persistent settings: Movement and rotation increments reset after testing a ship. For example, if I set movement to 0.1 m for fine adjustments, test my ship, and return to the dock, it resets to 3 m.

Universal scaling: Let players scale all parts by default, not just basic hull pieces. Developer mode already allows it, so why not make it standard?

Part identification: Add an option to see the name of a part after it’s been placed. It’s easy to lose track of what’s what in complex builds. (This also includes seeing the specifications of a ship in the dock and not having to move to the main menu)

Alignment issues: Sometimes parts refuse to align properly, even when they should. A small snapping fix would go a long way.

World vs. part-relative controls: It would be great to switch between moving or rotating something relative to the world or the part itself. This is especially true for the rotate tool, as it is very hard to make proper changes that involve more than 1 axis.

Overall, Great Game, would recommend, 19€ is a Lil but heavy but just buy in a Sale (as you probably always should)

Decaying Logic gelingt es auf einfache Art und Weise das beste Jigsaw-Puzzle-Game auf Steam zu betreiben. Ich sage bewusst betreiben, denn die Zahl der Erweiterungen steigt stetig und die monatlichen Challenges können durchaus als Community orientiertes Weiterentwicklen betrachtet werden. Es ersetzt natürlich kein echtes Puzzle, das Aufräumen entfällt aber und so viel Platz nimmt es auch nicht weg. Das Basisspiel bietet derweil nicht all zu viele Puzzle, lässt einen aber einen kostenlosen Einblick in die Mechanik gewinnen. Dabei wird von Seiten der Entwickler eigentlich alles richtig gemacht. Übersichtliches Menü, einfache Bedienung, attraktive Features.

[b]Features[/b]

Für das abschließen von Puzzles gibt es neben den Errungenschaften auch "goldene Puzzleteile" und während dem puzzlen kann man "Hints" finden. Mit den Hints lassen sich beim puzzlen Hilfestellungen anfordern (richtige Rotation eines Puzzleteils, genauer Ort eines Puzzleteils & kurzer Blick auf das Gesamtbild) oder 50 Stück können in ein goldenes Teil umgewandelt werden. Mit goldenen Puzzleteilen lassen sich Items im Kiosk freischalten. Von Zeit zu Zeit gibt es auch Events, wo für das Abschließen eines Puzzles doppelt so viele goldene Teile vergeben werden.

Decaying Logic hat mit dem erwähnten Kiosk ein Feature implementiert, welches als Langzeitmotivation angesehen werden kann. Neben kosmetischen Items zur Individualisierung des Spiels (Cursor, Musik, Themes), lassen sich auch sogenannte "Uniques", d.h. besonders schwere oder aufwendige Puzzle freischalten. Dazu können die bereits angesprochenen goldenen Puzzleteile verwendet werden. Auch alte Challenges lassen sich auf diesem Weg noch spielen.

Die monatlichen Challenges sind ein weiterer Pluspunkt bei der Entwicklung. Kostenlos und äußerst anspruchsvoll, lassen sie den Puzzle-Fan schon die ein oder andere Stunde vor dem PC verbringen. Die Motivwahl ist dafür auch sehr unterschiedlich, wobei die Farbnuancen und die Puzzle-Form der Einzelteile einen zuweilen zur Weißglut treiben. Bei erfolgreichem Abschluss erhält man ein sogenanntes "Ultimate Piece", welches auch im Kiosk eingelöst werden kann. 

[b]Die DLCs[/b]

Ohne Packs wirkt das Spiel recht leer. Wer bereits die anderen Spiele der Pixel Puzzles-Serie erwerben konnte oder sie bei einer der etlichen Promotionsaktionen kostenlos erhielt, der kann sie bei der Ultimate-Version nochmals spielen. Auch das ein oder andere DLC kann noch kostenlos im Netz gefunden werden, wie bspw. DaVinci oder Beach Volleyball, sodass man eine doch schon recht große Auswahl an Puzzlen (ca. 100) von Beginn an haben kann. Es bedarf aber etwas Arbeit im Vorfeld!

Die DLCs scheinen auf den ersten Blick natürlich überteuert, jedoch erhält man für die Preise i.d.R. guten Content. Für 0,99€ kann man dann, je nach Erfahrung, mehrere Stunden mit puzzlen verbringen. Wartet man auf einen Sale, rentiert es sich erst recht. Bewertet habe ich jedoch nur all jene DLCs, welche regulär mehr als 4,99 Euro kosten. Dies wären "[i][url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Xeeran/recommended/591508/]Spanien[/url][/i]", "[i][url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Xeeran/recommended/591502/]China[/url][/i]" und "[i][url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Xeeran/recommended/589651/]Pin-Ups[/url][/i]".

[b]Fazit[/b]

Das Spiel bietet jedem Puzzle-Fan eine platzsparende und gute Alternative zu herkömmlichen Puzzlen. Wer in Pixel Puzzles Ultimate nur einen teuren Jigsaw-Puzzler sieht, den er auch kostenlos im Netz haben könnte, der verkennt die Vorzüge. Ein Test kann nicht schaden, weshalb ich auch nichts zur Mechanik sagte und sollte die meisten Interessierten überzeugen können. Denn dort gibt es keine Beanstandung. Einzig die Musik nervt, doch mute und Radio schaffen abhilfe!

A great spin on a ghost game! Finally one that isn't mainly about finding out about the ghost, and only finding out how to survive it while you rob people broke! 

The tasks given to you for each round is to hack data, find secret messages or specific paintings to steal/destroy, find ID cards, safe codes, hack servers, or even destroy a ghost orb. The tasks, which actually are somewhat simple once you get the hang of things, are made more difficult by the ghost that haunts the location you choose. Once the bells ring for midnight, it's on! Each randomly chosen ghost has their own specials, behaviors, and interactions, which can make some jobs even tougher. Keeping track of the closest hiding spot to you at all times is deadly important, otherwise you'll end up in the spirit world trying to help your teammates from the other side. Finish the job successfully and escape unharmed so you can gain favor with the boss and earn money, intel, perks, etc. 

Hacking:
The hacking tasks are fairly mundane and easy, but when the risk of a random hunt looms in the background of your mind, they can get stressful. Some hacks are done by clicking circles, finding the odd man out, translating numbers and letters, and even basic math. They've added new ones in as well, such as navigating a maze and tracing wires, which are fun to figure out, but the added time can make them risky. Work fast and accurately, every second counts!

Side/Secondary Missions:
When they added these, my friends and I completely became obsessed! Instead of just finding the photos, cameras, data, and black market items that were originally included, now there's extras to work on to help gain more XP and money! Finding paintings by scanning them with cameras or using a UV light, finding secret messages, spray painting locations, or even trying to find an ID badge hidden somewhere in a room where UV footprints led you definitely adds on a ton more gameplay and excitement. While not all of them are necessary to complete the heist, they are definitely worth the extra time!

Maps:
They're still adding more, and they're great! Originally there were just a few medium to large maps, which were somewhat hard to manage if playing solo. But since then, they've added a few small maps as well as a couple more medium and large, which is super nice for fearless solo players. Plus the new Police Station map added with the 1.0 update is great! The atmosphere on the maps are great, layouts are awesome, and even the decor (or lack thereof in some) make them spooky yet manageable.  Hopefully more will come out in time! The maps are set though, and not procedurally generated, so while certain locations of items to find or hack change, the maps themselves are easy to memorize. Circuit breakers, server rooms, and depending on the Black Market Mission Modifiers, hiding spots don't change. (Find the bathrooms, trust me! Safest hiding spots around!)

Ghosts:
The ghost models and abilities are extremely unique and wonderful! Each ghost type has their own strengths and weaknesses, which make each round challenging in different ways. One round you can get the hulking mass that shakes the entire building when it walks around, so you know when it's hunting, and the next you can get the completely silent floater that can creep up behind you before you know it. Learning behaviors is fun and challenging, but once you get it, you can manage each round easily once you get the first hunt and find out the ghost. Each challenging spirit makes their own sounds too, so learning those can make it easier to differentiate before the first hunt hits. (I love the crying woman!!!)

Round Modifiers:
The Black Market Missions that they added in a while back definitely makes the round a heck of a lot more interesting. Each one, ranging from the easiest one at 1 star and maxing out at the most difficult 5 star, adds both pros and cons. For example, you can get a percentage more XP or money, more safes, more black market items, and such, but the ghost can change, or you can get 2 ghosts, or less hiding spots, etc. There's both free ones to choose from, or you can pay data to generate your own based on difficulty level, so go crazy!  If you want to add more difficulty to the game, this is the way to do it. 

Gear:
Originally we were only given the standard gear of a phone, tablet, flashlight, and lockpick. The phone also had a camera and the flashlight also had a UV. When the new missions, modifiers, and side quests were added, they also added more gear. A separate camera, UV light, USB stick, bat, spray paint, etc. Each one is upgradeable for added benefits, including adding the UV back to the standard flashlight and the camera back to the phone (they were originally removed with the new update, but were added back due to player request). Learning what each does and how they work is key for staying alive and completing everything as quickly as possible. The upgrades are worth it!

Modules:
You can print modules by using money, which can add buffs to your character. They come in different levels, all random, and have different additions to your buffs, which are also random. You can spend a lot of money getting those epic ones, but again, well worth it! (Get the entity detection one as quick as possible! It may take some rolls of it to get it, but it can save your life.)

Characters/Customization:
The characters to choose from don't themselves come with anything special, other than the clothing you can buy for them. I will say that they all look kind of like dirty plastic dolls, but I love that about them. (My go-to girl I lovingly call MaGaga, since she looks like a mix of Madonna and Lady Gaga.) With the 1.0 update they added in new clothes, so now I have to save up to buy the new stuff, after finally saving up enough to get the paper bag (that I haven't even used yet, lol). I love that they're adding more, though I think some extra customization would be nice. Maybe throwing in the ability to change color on the super special and super expensive gear, or even some secret buffs on the high end stuff? Anything is possible, and the devs are great, so you never know!

In general, I love this game, and have loved following the development of it throughout the time I've been playing. I recommend it to anyone that loves the spooky stuff, but doesn't want to have to worry about finding out what the ghost is and how to banish it and instead just wants to survive it while stealing or destroying stuff. It's extremely replayable, has great atmosphere, performs well, looks great, and is tons of fun! Just get it already!!!
