Rise of the Tomb Raider foi sem dúvidas o melhor jogo de exploração que tive a oportunidade de jogar até agora, não somente pela gameplay insana e cinematografia extraordinária, mas também pela complexidade e arco da personagem principal e de todos os outros personagens.
Lara Croft é uma personagem incrível: forte, destemida, ambiciosa, empática, em certos momentos até parece ser indestrutível - porém nas vezes em que ela fica sozinha, se mostra uma garota vulnerável, que sente medo e saudades do pai.
A construção da sua personalidade, desde a sua ambição por honrar o nome do seu falecido pai até a busca e encontro pela sua própria subjetividade, fez dela a minha personagem fictícia favorita do mundo dos jogos (junto com a Ellie :p).

Os demais personagens, como Jonah, Jacob, Konstantin Ana e Sofia foram marcados e explorados com profundidade (suas histórias, emoções, arcos, finitude) e isso deu ao jogo uma imersão maior, somado as cartas e pergaminhos que contam a origem de Kitej, da vila por onde passamos e dos antigos moradores e serventes do profeta - perfeito para quem curte histórias profundas e bem polidas.

Quanto ao jogo em si, ele melhorou muitas das mecânicas que eram um tanto precárias no primeiro, apesar de ainda precisar polir algumas funções de agarrar que encontram-se bugadas. 
Tiveram puzzles desafiadores que me fizeram parar para refletir e lutas épicas que me fizeram dar alguns rages aqui e ali kkkkkk. 

Sei que nem todo mundo liga para isso, mas, para os que ligam, as conquistas são possíveis e, ao mesmo tempo, desafiadoras. Existem colecionáveis espalhados por todos os mapas e desafios realmente complexos, o que dá uma vontade a mais para se continuar jogando mesmo depois de zerar a história principal.

Estou com expectativas altas para o Shadow of the Tomb Raider. 
Espero não me decepcionar, visto que o gancho que tivemos no final do segundo foi muito promissor para se fechar a trilogia com chave de ouro.

В дверях нет смысла потому что они больше замедляют ваших миньонов, а не врагов. Да и врагов замедлять смысла нет, потому что у них нет никакого таймера на пребывание. Они либо живы и бьют ваших, либо мертвы.

Ловушки, особенно сплэшовые, больше дамажат ваших юнитов, чем врага, потому что обысно врагов приходит 3-5, а ваш муравейник окружает их скопом в 20-30 человек. Это крайне неприятно, учитывая что хп ваших миньенов раза в три-четыре меньше чем у эндгейм врагов, и даже самые безобидные враги по типу Воров или Дознавателей будут класть ваших пачками и без помощи ловушек которые этим самым миньонам снесут 30-50% хп.

Роботы вообще ужас - да, не едят, но также ходят заряжаться, так и ещё постоянно пытаются в бой первыми ворваться. В чем проблема? А они взрываются после смерти. Нет, они не супер-танковые ребята, они ложаться ровно также как и остальные миньоны соответствующего класса, но в отличии от них - взрываются, дамажа не только ваши постройки и всех окружающих (А как вы помните - ваших в зоне поражения в разы больше чем врагов), так ещё и пожар вызывают, что при затяжной драке может очень быстро эскалировать в тотальный ужас по всей базе.

Ваше оружие судного дня тоже бесполезно. Да, оно снижает внимание от властей, но с тем количеством врагов что на вас идет - можно просто из каждой пачки по 1-2 типа захватывать, допрашивать у вас будут просто бесконечные разведданные для ровно такого-же моментального снижения внимания.

Геймплей затянут невероятно. После первого часа игры вы вообще никогда не выключите Х2 ускорение, и она всё равно будет утомительно долгой. Когда вы построите более-менее хорошую базу (А происходит это примерно часу к 3-4) - ваш основной геймплей будет простым втыканием в ожидании пока натренируются юниты для Квестовых Миссий. Вам быстро надоест делать сайдквесты кроме добычи новых миньонов, потому что это (кто-бы мог подумать) бесполезно. Приспешники не настолько мощные (хотя можно всё-же собрать полный отряд) что-бы из кожи вон лезть и добывать их, а добыча - вообще просто украшение.

Короче, писал сразу после 32ч. прохождения, минусы лезут в глаза больше чем плюсы. Возможно просто не моё. Делайте выводы сами.

As you can probably see, I have played this game quite a bit and believe myself to be familiar enough with the base game, DLC, mods, and community to really give a review for those of you who may be considering this game in 2025 or later.

First and foremost, the base game is pretty...bad. The guns are inaccurate, as in when you aim down the sites, you can literally see the bullets hitting AROUND your site, not on it. The AI is bad, the voice acting is bad, the dialogue is bad, the story is bad, just a dumpster-fire overall of a campaign. The campaign was so bad that I actually haven't played the 'Stasis Interrupted' DLC campaign because I'm not a masochist and didn't want to subject myself to anymore torture. 

The multiplayer is supposedly fun, or at least that's what I'm told as I have never been able to play a single online game since purchasing in 2018. And this is an utter crime as there are so many movie maps from locations in the franchise that are absolutely beautiful in their level design. There's even a "Processor" map of the hive where the Marines get ambushed in "Aliens". It is such an awesome and eerie feeling walking around and seeing all of the locations from that scene in the film. But unfortunately, the map is useless because it is only available in the dead multiplayer modes. There are several other movie maps like this (Nostromo from 'Alien'/Fury 161 from 'Alien 3') that are completely unplayable because of them being locked behind multiplayer game modes only. The only thing you can do on these maps is explore them in offline mode by yourself. 

Now, if there were one reason why you should consider purchasing this game, it would be for BUG HUNT.

Without a doubt the best game mode and the only thing worth it in this game. Bug Hunt is the games "Horde" mode, like CoD Zombies, where you just fight waves of Aliens and survive for as long as you can. Oddly though, there are also Weyland-Yutani Mercenaries in this mode which is silly. Supposedly Gearbox wanted the game to be more "CoD" like, which is the exact opposite purpose of the game. But still fun. Though there are only three maps in Bug Hunt mode, unfortunately, and I think only one of them is of any interest being "Tribute" which is Hadley's Hope. 

Although, luckily, you can improve the game greatly through mods from moddb. First and foremost, the one that everyone has to have with this game is Templar_GFX's Overhaul Mod. This mod drastically improves almost everything about the gameplay such as fixing the enemy AI, fixing the aim accuracy, the colors/atmosphere and overall look of the game. This is a must have. But there are also a bunch of mods out there, and with a little bit of effort, you can actually learn how to mod this game quite easily yourself once you have the right tools and know how to use them. For example, in the Hadley's Hope map for Bug Hunt, there are several locations that are inaccessible unless you pay for them, and a lot of the prices are quite steep so there was a lot of the map I had never even seen due to the fact that I was unable to purchase their respected gates. I was able to mod the game to where all of the doors are free so I could use the full Hadley's Hope map from the beginning of a game. I was also able to remove the Mercenaries and replaced them with Xeno's, then I also changed all Xeno's to the 'Warrior' class to make it much more accurate to the 'Aliens' movie as that was the only Xeno type in the film.  

The online community? There is none. I'm in several A:CM discords and no one ever plays it anymore so chances are you'll never get to experience the full game, which is understandable as it is a 12 year old, mediocre game.

But the most frustrating thing about this game, though, is the potential it has to be great. There are so many things that have drastically improved the experience, but there's also so many things that are RIGHT THERE out of reach to make it even better. All Gearbox needs to do is give the community the tools to do so. For example, theoretically, it's possible to add bots to the offline multiplayer game modes using the games fixed AI system which would enable the multiplayer maps useful again. There is also the possibility of turning these maps into "Bug Hunt" Maps if Gearbox gave the Original Unity Map Projects to the community which would allow modders to customize the maps and use them more liberally. The only reason why this game has any sort of following is because of the modding community, so I am begging Gearbox to release the original projects for them. Underneath this awful game is an amazing one just dying to come out like a chestburster. 

So, would I recommend this game? If you're a big fan of the franchise and would love the hunt Xeno's on Hadley's Hope, then sure. Although I do think the price is steep at $15 considering the only useful mode being Bug Hunt, it's still worth it as a fan. For everyone else? No. Not unless Gearbox releases the base projects for the modding community. If you're not a GIANT Alien franchise fan, this game would be a complete waste of money at its base model.

Do you like to play bad games as a guilty pleasure? Go for it. Is the game dirt cheap? Sure. Do you like Alien? Well, at this point you might as well play it. But seriously, only play this if you answer yes to these questions. Otherwise, there are way better games out there. I just happen to play bad games as a guilty pleasure. Please take this into account, as this is a very conditioned recommended review.

First off, you should really consider if a game like this is right for you. If you really enjoy liminal spaces and walking simulators, in addition to a more "art gallery" style of game, then you'll love this title.

This game does have very valid criticisms, most notably the performance being worse than the demo and the lack of an FOV slider. These issues 100% need addressing. That said, the people criticizing the game for being "mindless wandering", or for sprinting not being the default movement strike me as laughably goofy. What did you expect? Is your entire drive simply to see how fast you can reach the credits? Why not ask for a mini-map and compass, too?

If you've wanted a liminal/backrooms experience that doesn't involve running from monsters/jumpscares, this game and Pools are the best available. The level designs are extremely high quality, and I found it fun to simply wander through them. The levels are also [b] enormous [/b], meaning you will inevitably get lost along the way. Despite that, there are often subtle hints that nudge the player in the appropriate direction and there are also fairly frequent checkpoints, so having to leave mid level isn't an issue.

You're not running from anything in this game. There's no danger, no threat. There's no urgency. There isn't even an objective beyond "find the exit". This game has no fail-state. It's pure atmosphere, and it does it exceptionally well. Wandering is [i] precisely [/i] what you're meant to do!
It has a very good atmosphere and ambience that brings out the backrooms and a touch of nostalgia. Great game BTW

[h2] Um passeio pela infância [/h2]

Little Misfortune é um jogo indie curto e no estilo point and click, onde acompanhamos a querida Misfortune Ramirez Hernandez em sua jornada na busca pela Felicidade Eterna. A arte do jogo é uma evolução evidente perante os demais jogos da Killmonday Games, onde sua história é comicamente bizarra. Lembra muito algo entre "Coraline e o Mundo Secreto" e "O Labirinto do Fauno".

Apesar de não possuir quaisquer desafios em seu gameplay e jogabilidade simples, o jogo brilha é na interação de Misfortune e do Sr. Voz, com diálogos muito bem escritos e interpretados. A trilha sonora também não fica atrás, com músicas ambiente e que combinam bem com os cenários caricatos.

Acompanhar Misfortune nessa desventura é um passeio e tanto pelos altos e baixos da infância. O jogo trabalha bem na forma como uma criança vê o mundo, num misto de inocência e melancolia, onde a imaginação coloca beleza até mesmo nas situações mais sombrias. Numa promoção é recomendação certa para quem gosta de Little Nightmares, Limbo, Inside ou os próprios Fran Bow e Sally Face do mesmo estúdio.

If dopamine had claws, it would look exactly like *Crab Champions*. I went in expecting a goofy crustacean meme game and came out with a deep spiritual connection to my inner crab. Ten minutes in, I wasn’t just playing — I was scuttling. I was dodging bullets sideways like a seafood Neo. I was crab.

The gameplay? Chef’s kiss with claws. Every run feels like an ADHD fever dream powered by a synthwave soundtrack and pure serotonin. One moment you’re blasting hordes of demonic coconuts, the next you’re dual-wielding rocket launchers while doing a backflip off a coral cliff. It’s like *Doom Eternal* and *Finding Nemo* had a radioactive baby.

And the polish — my god, it shines harder than a crab shell under a full moon. Movement feels buttery smooth, the gunplay is tighter than a crab’s grip on a french fry, and the loot system constantly tickles your reward centers. “Just one more run” turns into “Oops, it’s 4 a.m. and I’ve transcended humanity.”

Also, let’s talk about the vibes. This game radiates pure positivity. Even when you die, you don’t feel mad — you feel enlightened, like the crab gods have gently tapped you on the shell and whispered, “You did good, little buddy.”

In conclusion: 10/10. Peak crustacean excellence. *Dark Souls* walked so *Crab Champions* could scuttle at light speed. I didn’t just buy a game — I adopted a lifestyle.

Its "missions" with different lighting and weather conditions change the mood in cool ways, but the game doesn't apply those to the freeform shredding you'll spend the majority of your time with, so the experience can get very samey. The proximity based multiplayer is occasionally a great time, but can prove erratic with connections dropping in the middle of score based runs, suddenly making the guy you compete with disappear from the leaderboard.

Basically, three years of updates later it still can't quite fully capitalise on its strong core mechanics, nor shake its early access, proof-of-concepty feel. And yet, it feels great to play, and I do return to it often.

"I'm going to give it the thumbs up." What starts as a simple endorsement quickly unpacks into a complex, yet enthusiastic, take on a very nice game that offers a fantastic core experience but struggles with some deeply frustrating quality-of-life (QOL) issues. At its heart, this game has a lot going for it. The learning curve is surprisingly easy to get your head around once you wrap your mind around the core mechanics. It’s accessible, which is a huge win in a market filled with overly complex simulators and management games. You can jump in, understand the basics, and start building your little empire without needing a 400-page manual. The progression system feels well-tuned; farming and levelling up isn't a soul-crushing, endless grind. It manages to balance progress with the 'fun' side of the game, ensuring that every session feels rewarding rather than a chore.
However, the warm fuzzy feelings of a gentle grind and easy learning curve are quickly doused by a bucket of cold water – a bucket that is far too small, incidentally. The game’s biggest, most glaring flaw is its absolute impossibility to play solo, or even in a small group. This is a game that feels fundamentally balanced for a full party, and that's a real shame for those of us who might want to enjoy a quiet evening running their virtual tavern alone or with just one friend.
The so-called "added servant" is less a servant and more a decorative house guest who occasionally does some light dusting. They handle some of the basic chores, sure, but the critical, time-consuming "serving" tasks? Nope. You're still on the hook for all the real work: cooking full meals, carefully dressing plates, pouring and serving drinks, running back and forth, and generally spinning plates faster than a circus performer. This creates an immediate and frustrating dilemma: you must make a choice to either run your tavern business effectively or go out and do the quests that the game provides as part of the main progression. You simply cannot do both.
This issue is painfully amplified by the water system, which is arguably the single most infuriating part of the entire experience. The water is gone in a flash, and the capacity is ridiculously low. You are forced to spend a comical amount of time running back and forth every 30 seconds for a single bucket of water that is then consumed in about 5 seconds of actual gameplay. It's a momentum killer, a flow-breaker, and a constant, aggravating reminder that the game is demanding more hands than you have.
The struggle bus is real, and it has room for two. We initially tried playing with my brother as a two-player team, and honestly? We struggled significantly. We were constantly overwhelmed, constantly behind on orders, and the entire experience felt more like a frantic battle against the clock and cumbersome mechanics than a fun co-op session. Everything felt like a bottleneck.
Then, we introduced another friend into the mix, bringing our total to three players. It was better, for sure. The workload was distributed slightly more evenly, and we could actually achieve a semblance of order in the chaos. But even then, the game felt like it was straining under the burden of being "almost" but not quite fully staffed. It really feels like the game has been meticulously balanced to run smoothly and be genuinely enjoyable only once you are actually at a full count of four players. This is a significant design flaw that severely limits the game's appeal and accessibility for smaller groups or solo players. The potential is there, but the execution in this regard is lacking. It shouldn't require four people to be fun.
Looking ahead, we're eagerly anticipating future patches. The core game has so much promise, and a few key quality-of-life mechanics could elevate it from a frustrating, niche experience to a truly great co-op game. The most requested feature from our group would be a smarter, more capable workforce. Maybe, just maybe, in a future update, the employed staff could actually pour drinks and, crucially, find the food in the storage chests automatically, like in some other, more polished games of the genre.
We're all looking forward to future patches that will hopefully add mechanics and QOL changes that would make the game more manageable and genuinely fun for smaller groups. This game has a ton of heart and potential, but right now, its rigid requirements for group size are holding it back from being a true masterpiece. Fix the servant problem, sort out that ridiculous water system, and you’ve got a real winner on your hands. Until then, it's a qualified "thumbs up" with a side of frustration.

The setting of the game is genius and the small stories and dialogues are really fun. The game also plays with stereotypes in Pen and Paper and RPG games. Have you ever seen a traffic wizard? Hilarious :)

Why the negative review then?

Because it is NOT a tactical game. Basically its a puzzle game with some chess-like elements. There is THE solution for many levels that require exact steps each turn. Yes, you have some freedom, but most time freedom leads to subpar results. So you basically solve puzzles the devs created for you, wrapped as a tactical game. And that's simply not what I wanted and how its advertised. For me a tactical game is a game that gives me the freedom to choose my team, my weapons, stealth or not, kills or not. It's definitely not "In Turn 1, you have to position char 1 here and shoot there, char 2 must move exactly here and push that enemy so that in Turn 2 you can....". That's a puzzle. Solving it means to play each move as intended. The little freedom you get are mostly sub variants of exact these moves. The rating of each mission reflects exactly this: how well did you solve the puzzle at it was intended to be played?

Compare this with the complete freedom for Jagged Alliance, XCOM or Shadow Gambit. These are great tactical games that make you think about how YOU want to solve a level/fight. There are no best ways or preferred tactics in these games and thats what make them a tactical game.

A very respectable effort at bringing the joy of building Lego into a video game: it's more construction-based than Lego Builder's Journey, and its sumptuous dioramas look almost as good. With some admittedly awkward-at-first controls (at least on mouse and keyboard), you explore various Lego builds in isometric view, where you come across points where you are placed in a blank slate for building certain structures, like bridges, ramps, vehicles, or cranes. It's absolutely great that once you finish building them, using special bricks you purchase as you progress if you wish, you then see your creations come to life in the actual game world. So for instance, the crane you built rotates and lifts things, or you can watch other minifigures ride the rollercoaster cabin you made. Before you can do this, you need to run a simulation with a test robot to see if your structure holds up under weight, and sometimes the physics seem rather picky, which can be a problem in the puzzles where you aren't given a generous number of bricks to play with. It is fun to see the test robot fall off a faulty bridge though.

The first two worlds (Jungle and Desert) really brought back fond memories for me of playing with the old-school Adventurers sets, especially so since I've been collecting classic Desert sets from ebay lately. The Medieval Castle world was also fantastic. The only real let down is the overall story, which is completely unremarkable, and the ending, which feels undercooked and not fully thought out. If any more expansions or updates come out from this point in time, I would like to suggest some kind of Space level - perhaps Rock Raiders or Ice Planet 2002 anyone?

As far as the key bindings for the building parts go, they are OK in general, although it's very common to accidentally place a brick one or two studs out from where you want, and fine-tuning is a necessity. I'd also like to point out that the traditional mechanical puzzles outside of the construction scenes are very fun, using a number of skills you learn as the game goes on. The amount of content in this game is very admirable, making its price a tempting one.

The economy is broken... complex, time-consuming crafts sell for barely more than basic ones, and the late game is extremely grindy with little incentive to continue.

Despite years in Early Access, progress is slow, quests and NPC interactions are minimal, and key features are still missing.

Cute art aside, there’s just not enough depth or content to justify the price. Do yourself a favour and stick with Stardew Valley (or the many other clones that do it better, and cheaper, than this one).

I do love this game, because I like the part of running a tavern. However it quickly becomes obvious the game doesn't want you to run a tavern. The game wants you to mine resources and grind while automated employees run the tavern for you. So the first few hours are fun but as you start to unlock new things the game gets worse and worse, and it seems the devs are only more thoroughly following along this path, turning it into a sort of stardew valley clone rather than a tavern simulator. The devs are very confused about the nature of their own game and it's very disappointing that they've lost the plot entirely.

As of now the game is still not at all finished or ready in my opinion. 

Just for clarification this is not a negative review but a Neutral with a slightly more negative lean. 

Presented UI is kind of all over the place and I've seen some improvements from the updates made by the devs so it seems like those issues will be ironed out soon. 
My advice is to really narrow it down as it honestly kind of overwhelmed me trying to understand some of the basic UI elements in the game.

The actual game play out side of the repair section is quite good but there are some teething issues and some pet peeves of mine. The tank ballistics are quite accurate and good but there are some strange behaviors that I can't quite understand. Major one being a T-34-76 not taking any damage from a frontal plate shot from an 88mm from a tiger. I make no claims on my expertise on the manner of ballistics such as Over matching and Shell Interaction with armor itself but as far as I'm aware the t-34-76 would be toast in every manner if it found itself on the receiving end of a 88mm shell at pretty much all reasonable combat ranges besides the outrageous. Yes the sloped armor is a great addition to its ballistic profile and encourages deflection of rounds, but the 88 would cut through it rather easily especially at the close ranges I was some how getting no damage shots from on level ground. Even using the provided shaped charge rounds which ignore angle's did nothing. I don't quite under stand how a close range shot at level ground with the deadliest cannon available would simply not do anything. Judging by this game seemingly wanting to be a simulator I'm more surprised the affected T-34 could even return fire after having their bell rung by a high velocity shell slamming into them.

Besides the ballistic issue's the product presented is rough but promising, AI still needs some work and the aforementioned UI elements need some ironing out but I do see promise in this game. Keep it up devs.

Edit 11-15-25- After the 1.1.7 patch a LOT of the random no damage and ricochet shots have been handled. However, there are still some issues with ballistics that I will chalk to the system just not being mature enough in development. For now Ballistics are "OKAY". Issues with UI elements, AI having eyes in the back of their head or being absolute neanderthals in uniform still stand. The improvements are showing some results but the game still has a LONG way to go before I recommend it.

[h2]相比原版[/h2]
《地铁2033》的原版在2010年推出，续作于2013年推出后，制作组在2014年把两部作品全部用新版本的4A引擎重置/复刻了。这也就是《地铁：归来》（Metro Redux）捆绑合集，包含《地铁2033》和《地铁：最后的曙光》的重置版，同年制作组把两部原作都下架了。《地铁：最后的曙光》的重置版相比于原版仅间隔一年，引擎新增加的内容并不多。本作虽还不至于达到称为「重制版」的地步，但相比于原作间隔四年，引擎变化大，新内容多了不少。最明显的是笔记收集和保险箱，与之伴随的是多了些隐藏的区域用来找钥匙或保险箱。相当多的细节也不同了，比如开场动画不再是从红场照片拉远开始，部分人物建模更换，删除了一些固定机枪，多了可以携带的喷火枪等。一些关卡流程也有改动，之前的数个短关卡被合并，在图书馆门前多了一场防守战。到达D6基地前，独自行动时遭遇的敌人类型也有改动。当然，画面和音质都有不小的提升，亮度和生物多样性提高，蜘蛛和昆虫变得随处可见。

打完原版之后，紧接着我就开始重温这个版本，把更接近原版的「生存模式」，以及更接近续作的「斯巴达模式」都在高难度下打通了。由于本作的成就和原版有点不同，总体更容易达成，我还专门解开了全部成就，没用SAM。两个版本虽然都没有官方汉化，但民间汉化的质量已经很高了，测评区还有很多人发下载链接。这款Redux确实在很多方面改进了体验，战斗和潜行都相对更容易了，但原版也有其独特的魅力。原版的场景更黑，更压抑恐怖；敌人听力敏锐，更加强悍，潜行难度大。我不在两者之中做选择，而是全都要！

[h2]另一种核战末世风格[/h2]
我之前所看所玩的核战末世题材大都是美式风格，比如《废土》和《辐射》，这种俄式风格倒并不多见。虽然叫俄式，但要知道制作组4A Games于2006年成立于乌克兰的首都基辅，创始人是从GSC Game World离开的，当然GSC也是家乌克兰的游戏开发公司。两个国家现在打了好几年仗，还是得搞清楚的。游戏的发生地是俄罗斯的莫斯科，有很多地标建筑和真实的地铁站点出现。在本作中绝大多数时候都是在阴暗的地铁隧道中，出去的机会并不多，让我想起了曾经钻《辐射3》地铁迷路的日子。其风格相比于《辐射3》里的戏谑荒诞、黑色幽默和人性光辉，《地铁2033》里的末世更加冷峻压抑和现实主义。这里面的很多人终生生活在黑漆漆的地铁里，挣扎在生死线的边缘，还得时时担心里面的怪物和更加难以名状的东西。受制于空间限制，人类的生存空间狭小，大部分人的房子只有几平米，甚至只有一张床，还得分上下铺。质量上乘的战前军用子弹作为货币使用，每个站点就像一个村子，俄罗斯人民似乎回到了曾经那个穷苦农奴制下的痛苦时代。

我没看过原版小说，但有人给我讲过里面的一小段内容：主角阿尔乔姆看见一对母子很穷，只能吃地铁里的苔藓。随后他从弹匣里退出一些子弹，追上女人。“给……这是给你的，这是给你儿子的。”女人难以置信地盯着他，然后鄙夷的撇了撇嘴。“你想什么呢，五个子弹就想换我孩子？”起初阿尔乔姆没明白她的意思，等反应过来时，他本想张嘴解释，却什么都说不出，只眨巴眼傻站在那里。女人对自己一番话的效果感到满意，便将表情由愤怒转为宽恕。“那好吧，半小时二十个子弹。”阿尔乔姆惊骇的说不出话来，他摇了摇头，转身大步流星地往回走。“吝啬鬼，算了，那就十五个子弹吧！”女人在后面喊。

[h2]射击游戏里的人文关怀[/h2]
本作背后有畅销小说《地铁2033》作为支撑，甚至原作者德米特里·格卢霍夫斯基也在一定程度上参与了游戏的制作。原作中的战斗很少，而游戏以FPS作为基底的同时，居然也没有完全丧失原作的文学性，在其中加入了相当多的独白、对话、站点人文和探索等。以主角阿尔乔姆一开始所在的展览馆站为例，我们可以看到制作组细致展示了地铁居民的居住条件、家居装饰、中央厨房、市场店面、医院诊所、防守前线、轨道交通等一系列的场景，当然更主要的是里面居住的人。他们或履行自己的职责，或在酒馆和篝火旁攀谈，或待在家里不想被打扰，或挤在房间里听音乐，或可怜的四处求援……

制作组为每个站点制作了这么多的人文内容，怎么让玩家慢慢去体会，而不是直接走开呢？4A Games为此内置了一个道德系统，与结局相关，道德值累计的够高就可以开启隐藏的好结局。当然，已经玩过续作的我们已经知道官方接续的结局就是消灭黑怪巢穴的坏结局。不过，这个系统还是能很好的增强游戏的人文性。如果给予乞丐施舍，帮助他人不要求回报，救下所能见到的人，完成别人的临终嘱托就会获得。当然该点数是不可见的，仅会在完成时听到滴水声。借助于这套道德系统，制作组在你和碰到的人聊聊，倾听完他人的交谈（哪怕是敌人之间的对话），按照同伴的要求倾听管道里的声音，不去打扰那些未知的事物等方面也提供了点数。这就使得很多玩家养成了不断停下来观察环境人文的习惯，同时发现了敲门时不同人的反应，单亲爸爸和孩子的对话，女人在厨房谈论男人，汉莎的盘剥、瘟疫的流行、战争的爆发等相当多有趣的文本。该设计正好也与东斯拉夫文学作品里那股子悲天悯人，关注人性复杂和现实矛盾的劲相合。

和《辐射3》和《潜行者》系列的开放世界所不同，本作是类似于《半衰期2》的线性流程，主要在各个不同的地铁站点和有限的地上区域活动。正因如此，游戏的规模可控，场景容易设计的十分精细，同时其氛围刻画也是一流的。地铁内的派系颇多，有新纳粹第四帝国、苏联共产党红线、资本主义汉萨同盟三大势力最为强盛，彷佛二战又来了一遍。前两者在交汇的站点里大打出手，能看出纳粹的装备先进，以及红线一边人数众多。不同地铁站点的境况差距十分巨大，波利斯站点的强盛繁华彷佛让人感觉回到了战前，有些站点里是温馨火堆旁欢笑的人群，有的则岌岌可危，正面临大量怪物围攻，甚至亲眼见识了一个站点的沦陷。地表上的冰天雪地、遍城废墟和毒气辐射，与地铁站形成了鲜明的对比，独自行走其中带给人强烈的孤独感。图书馆更是阴森可怖，带给人很强的沉浸感。如此压抑、悲凉和孤独氛围中，游骑兵的存在让人安心，乌尔曼那张的贱嘴甚至能不时让人笑出声。

[h2]颇有压力的生存之旅[/h2]
在一般游戏中，照明是件非常平常的事情，只要注意别在潜行时开启就行了。到了本作，黑漆漆的地铁里十分依赖手电筒，但其亮度会逐渐衰减，需要时时注意用手捏发电机充电。不光手电筒，夜视仪、电磁武器，甚至气枪，也是一样的原理，需要时时注意电量/气量，不断加以补充。如果这一切已经开始让你这个强迫症有压力了，那么呼吸面罩系统会直接让人压力骤升。一旦我们进入地表或不适宜呼吸的地下区域，就必须戴上呼吸面罩，与其搭配使用的滤芯是个消耗品，需要每5分钟换一次，最后1分钟还会滴滴响着提醒你。近距离战斗时，所带的面罩会溅上血，需要手动擦拭来恢复视线。如果长时间在室外探索或潜行，滤芯就会不够用，逼迫你赶紧找路离开。如果你不潜行，而是选择直接战斗，就得注意别被子弹打到。因为面罩也会破损，严重的话就不能用了，直接憋死。那么在必须戴面罩的关卡里，无论潜行还是战斗，都有风险，令人颇有压力。如果你在进入地表前带了个坏的面罩，或者没有滤芯了，得，整个关卡直接都无法进行下去了，死档了！我就碰到过这个问题，怎么也无法到达图书馆，还得重开之前的关卡。要不就得用邪道方法，不断戴上摘下，麻烦的很。

本作中的FPS部分中规中矩，有枪械、子弹和难度三个方面可以讲。前期的枪械大都是些土制武器，冲锋枪威力小，霰弹枪弹容少，手枪两样缺点都占，面对成群的敌人非常吃力。气枪和电磁武器的子弹少，还得时时注意气量/电量。中期拿到AK和标准霰弹枪，压力稍微减弱，后期则有20发霰弹和好一点的步枪。游戏支持给枪械加装配件，但不论怎么用，在和人类与怪物的正面冲突中始终难以游刃有余。大部分武器的子弹威力小，而且弹容少，很容易在防守战中打光。步枪可用军用子弹，但除了最后的关卡，估计没人舍得用。游戏的难度设计和大部分游戏不一样，越简单敌我就越肉，越难的话两方就越脆皮，个人感觉中高难度反而更容易点。我非常喜欢里面的潜行，手枪加装消音器和瞄准镜后简直是人类克星，一枪一个，配合飞刀轻松穿越敌阵。潜行能观察敌人和各种路线的情况下，同时需要留意吹灯，发出噪音的玻璃碎片和罐头铃铛，以及致命陷阱，通过后成就感很强。面对成群怪物则难上不少，加上怪物的受击反馈不咋好，自我血量又低，个人不太喜欢。

[h2]末日里的噩梦[/h2]
本作表面看起来是个末世求生的题材，对抗人类和辐射变异怪物，但在那之下却有着很多超自然的元素。游戏里不可名状之物不少，特别是和可汗相处的那段，有可以被看到的灵魂阴影，能听到死去人的声音，重温他们的死亡时刻。蹲在地铁的管子旁边能听到小孩的声音，听久了还会受伤害。里面还有种类似球形闪电的东西，似乎有自我思维。主角自己在某些场景中能看到过去的画面，听到过去的声音，甚至直接置身核战前的公园，摘下面罩畅快呼吸。有个场景里能在公寓废墟里看到亮起来的电视，直接化身恐怖游戏。

游戏里的各种怪物也十分可怖，超大超多，比狼还大的Nosalis，善于钻洞潜伏的Lurker，会发干扰声波的Winged Nosalis，会飞的「恶魔」，以及图书馆里大量的「图书管理员」，有很多甚至都难以说出来是什么动物变的。其中最为神秘的则是「黑怪」，也称黑暗族/黑暗裔，作为游戏中最重要的一条线索，整个故事因他们而起，也因他们而结束。不过，不知他们是如何产生出来的，神秘的仿佛外星来客，而且似乎是专门对标人类而出现的。比人类更强大，比人类更加适应目前的环境，也难怪阿尔乔姆的养父悲观地认为人类要被替代了。他们用脑电波沟通，但常人无法承受，要么死掉，要么发疯，导致人类对其敌意非常深。主角阿尔乔姆勉强可以承受，会被拖入精神世界，但仍然无法完全理解对方，直到结局才大致得知对方并无敌意。

这些超自然内容可能跟俄国著名的科幻小说《路边野餐》有关系，该书和被改编的电影《潜行者》里都充斥着超乎想象的奇观。本系列的灵感主要来源是《地铁2033》小说，可能也受到上述两部作品和俄国文脉的影响。作者自己还说他受到《辐射》系列游戏的启发才开始写的小说，游戏里面本身也有不少说不清，道不明的神秘之事，传承到这里面也不奇怪。4A Games跟《潜行者》系列游戏创作者GSC Game World渊源不浅，后者受《路边野餐》和《潜行者》电影的影响更大。这些元素为游戏增添了神秘气息，不只是个冷峻的末日生存故事，而更像是一次事关人类命运的噩梦挣扎。不得不说，游戏在绝大部分方面都十分优秀，而且提供了整个系列多部作品，成为我最爱的末世题材之一。

[h1] Call of Duty - an unpolished diamond [/h1]

[b]Prelude[/b]
The first Call of Duty is undoubtedly an FPS classic which, along with the Medal of Honor series, gave rise to the subgenre of games with more cinematic campaigns, grounded stories about war or special ops – rarely going beyond the modern era, nearby future or WWII, only occasionally stepping into sci-fi territory.

Speaking of the gameplay aspects of this subgenre, these shooters share some usual traits: usually 2-3 weapon types instead of a full arsenal; a small variety of enemies, typically limited to different types of soldiers; linear levels where exploration ends with a couple of tiny side alleys; HP regeneration or lots of medkits; checkpoints, etc. The list could go on. I’m not insisting on this categorisation as final – as in any art form, genres blend, and CoD-like FPS games may borrow something from retro shooters (hello F.E.A.R., RAGE).

Long story short: compared to what came before it, Call of Duty revolutionised the genre – whether for better or worse is a matter of taste, but as the fact it must be acknowledged. Now all that’s left is to examine the game itself: did it manage to pull this off on the first try?

[b]Review[/b]
Short answer: yes, it succeeded, but with some rough edges

The first thing that catches the eye is the graphics. Unfortunately, even at its 2003 release, the graphics didn’t produce much of a wow effect. Enemy models, by the standards of the time, look somewhat more detailed in comparison to RTCW: characters actually have polygonal pockets, folds and little bumps on their uniforms, but the textures drag down the overall impression. The weapon models are quite decent, though the iron sights are too thick and not really comfortable to use.

The levels range from «wow, that’s impressive», like the unique german battleship or the dam, to generic villages with identical house interiors that often repeat themselves (some locations are reused for two missions, day/night). The soviet campaign with its gray ruined walls and snowy forests ending can make you feel upset too.

As for gameplay, the gunplay is very pleasant and not very realistic, but reasonably accessible. It’s hard to say there’s a great variety of guns: most missions are completed either with your standard issued kit or the MP-40 & Kar98k combo. Still, it’s always exciting to pick up an FG-42 or StG-44 though you’ll rarely find much ammo for them.

As already mentioned, the game’s key feature is its cinematic nature. Every mission feels like «Saving Private Ryan», where you feel your involvement, your role in the operation. The levels are full of military bravado – there’s no room for deep reflection here, but that is Call of Duty, and that is why we do love it. There are chases on car, stealth infiltrations, dangerous landings, assaults. And the defence of Pavlov’s House alone is worth mentioning – the best and the hardest level in the game. Overall, it’s a real thrill-ride.

However, there are a few things that personally disappoint me. Some levels are repeated and it’s understandable that reusing a map with different lighting is easier than building a new one, so this isn’t a critical issue. The biggest drawback for me are the stationary weapon sections, where you don't have an opportunity to hide, and the first enemy can shoot your entire face off with a couple of accurate hits – leaving you stuck like that unless you restart the level. I understand it probably has to do with AI behaviour and the lack of health regeneration. The developers just threw in a few medkits, but once you use them up, the enemies can just blast you again in the same way.

Speaking of AI: the machine gunners are extremely annoying. They instantly switch focus to you and suppress you with heavy fire. If you’ve run out of health and medkits, you’re forced into pure save-scum process and boring peeking from a cover, waiting for enemies to “forget” you. And sometimes friendly fire happens – but that’s a minor issue :D

The absence of health regeneration. The developers added it only in the second game, and it was a great change, it made the gameplay much smoother and eliminated the need for save-scumming when medkits were gone.

And one more minor drawback about the graphics: this is the only FPS where I genuinely struggle to distinguish enemy silhouettes. I don’t know why, but the camouflage here blends with the environment a little too well.

[b]Epilogue[/b]
The first Call of Duty is definitely a good, though not perfect, game, and many of its rough edges can be forgiven, considering it was an experiment. Is it worth playing at least once? Definitely yes. I’ve replayed it many times, and every time, the game delivers enjoyment. This is one of those cases where an old game can truly be called a classic – not outdated junk.

Let me start this review by saying that I am [b]not[/b] calling [i]Bears in Space[/i] a bad game. It's not that I have issues with the game; it's that I am clearly not aligned with this game's target audience.

The core shooting gameplay, with the running and gunning, the weapon upgrades, and the open combat that emphasizes movement instead of seeking cover, that's all perfectly fun. Where [i]BiS[/i] and I don't get along, though, is pretty much everything else.

The humor pretty much entirely flies right past me. [b]One[/b] side character, I understood the reference(Vin Botsil, referring to actor Vin Diesel); but the reference is to a franchise that I actively dislike([i]The Fast & the Furious[/i], where I much prefer Vin's other franchise [i]The Chronicles of Riddick[/i]).

The platforming and puzzles in general aren't enjoyable to me; but that's entirely due to the fact that I'm not much for puzzles and/or platforming in [b]any[/b] game, with the minor exception of the [i]Sonic the Hedgehog[/i] franchise.

And the random gimmick moments that move away from the main shooting gameplay(not including the platforming and puzzles), oh sweet holy [b]crap[/b] do they rub me the wrong way. The [i]Time Crisis[/i]-inspired sequences are genuinely frustrating at times, mainly because I'm playing on a controller, but still. And the "Radium in the Stadium" boxing match was just beyond unwelcome. But, again, I'm not going to describe them as poorly made or poorly executed; it's entirely my fault for wanting something that [i]Bears in Space[/i] clearly isn't.

At the end of the day, I'm left wishing that the game leaned harder into the core shooting gameplay; but, at the same time, I feel like cutting out everything outside of that would destroy the identity of [i]Bears in Space[/i].

Call me an unhappy, unfunny lout that needs to go back to the 1990s, but I simply cannot find enough of what I enjoy from [i]Bears in Space[/i] to say that it's worth my time. [i]Bears in Space[/i] has left me crashed and burned with a 4 out of 10.

This is not the cute little wolf family simulator that you think it is. It is an endless story of struggle, grief, loss, and death. It is a loop entrapped within the confines of the brutality of nature, one fraught with peril and the constant looming threat of something always out to get you. You either live with constant vigilance or you perish and become lost to the never-ending cycle.

You carve out your life through the grit of your canine teeth and the spill of your blood, scratching and biting and clawing for every square inch of territory in hopes your pups will survive that much longer. You raise them from nothing, bringing them every scrap of meat you can find in this unforgiving landscape, until they become a reflection of yourself. You watch them carve out their own lives, scratching and biting and clawing alongside you, and for a moment, you have hope that you have something that could last in this desolate, lonely landscape. A fleeting vision of your descendants carrying out the very same life you experienced. But then comes the inevitable - the bears, the cougars, the eagles, the coyotes, the rival wolves, the flea infestations, the sickness, the famine, the wounds, the blood and the murder - and you watch as the once small creatures you shed blood for for so very, very, long sheds its own for the last time.

You move on. You keep biting and scratching and clawing. But you never forget. And you carry those you bled for with you forever.

Anyways, the game is pretty good 👍

[b]Pacific Drive[/b] стала для мене приємною несподіванкою. Спочатку я не очікував від гри чогось особливого, але перші дві години геймплею буквально затягнули мене, наче [i]гравітаційна аномалія[/i].

[h2]Геймплей[/h2]
Гра пропонує унікальне поєднання виживання, досліджень і управління автомобілем. [b]Система ремонту та апгрейду машини[/b] додає глибини та змушує планувати кожну поїздку. Кожна поїздка у пустку сповнена ризику, але це лише додає драйву.

[h2]Атмосфера та графіка[/h2]
[i]Pacific Drive[/i] вражає атмосферою. Похмурі пейзажі, таємничі зони і несподівані небезпеки створюють постійне відчуття напруги. Графіка деталізована, а звук занурює у світ гри настільки, що важко відірватися.

[h2]Саундтрек та радіо[/h2]
Одним з найбільших бонусів гри є [b]саундтрек[/b]. Радіо в машині – це справжнє музичне відкриття. Кожна поїздка стає емоційною пригодою завдяки чудовому підбору треків. Музика ідеально доповнює напружені моменти та спокійні поїздки пусткою, створюючи відчуття повного занурення у світ Pacific Drive.

[h2]Враження[/h2]
Ця гра – справжній [u]шедевр для тих, хто любить виживання та дослідження[/u]. Вона змушує думати, планувати і реагувати на непередбачуване. Навіть після кількох годин гри я не хотів виходити з цього світу.

[b]Висновок:[/b] Pacific Drive – це гра, яка захоплює і не відпускає. Саундтрек та радіо роблять поїздки неповторними, а атмосфера та геймплей тримають у напрузі від початку до кінця. Якщо ви шукаєте щось нове та атмосферне, вона точно варта вашої уваги!
[i]P.S. Особлива подяка розробникам за українську локалізацію.[/i]

[h2][b]The Gyst[/b][/h2]
This is a great remake of a fantastic game. There are a few things I prefer about the original version, but for anyone new to the series, this remake is absolutely the way to go. If you like puzzle games, adventure games, and everything in between, you owe it to yourself to play this incredibly well-preserved piece of gaming history. (Consider checking out the Myst remake first, if you want the best experience of being eased into the story and puzzle design philosophy of the series.) That's all you need to know, but I'm going to keep yapping about this game because it's iconic to me. I played the original when I was a little kid and then again in high school, but having now played it as a fully grown adult, I am happy to say it deserves all the love I've always had for it.

[h2][b]Riven is an All-Timer[/b][/h2]
While the individual puzzles themselves may not be the most challenging or thought-provoking in gaming when viewed through the lens of mechanical game design, the truly special thing about Riven's puzzles is also what I'd consider to be the game's crowning achievement: how the puzzles are intertwined with the story and worldbuilding. To solve many of the puzzles, you need to pay attention to certain things in the world and think about them based on bits of sometimes fantastical logic in terms of how the world works. It's a bit hard to explain without spoiling, but you'll know what I'm talking about once you play it.

From a story perspective, the act of finding the information required to solve many puzzles often reveals details about the characters, factions, and historical events of the Age of Riven. Every new nugget of information is like a mental puzzle piece, and the more of them you find, the more they fit together and form a cohesive overarching story. Though the immediate narrative is just "the player wanders around the islands solving puzzles to power up devices with the goals of freeing Catherine and trapping Gehn," there is much more to it than that. Additionally, beyond the scope of the puzzles, there are [i]loads[/i] of excellent visual designs and musical tracks that contribute to the game's environmental storytelling. (I was so scared of certain areas as a kid, and I now realize it was mainly due to the sound design.)

While Riven's archipelago is initially intimidating and sprawling, it all falls into place in your mind at a surprisingly fast pace. By the time you complete the game, everything about it will have [i]clicked[/i]. I'm not the first to say this, but it's true that playing the game kind of makes you feel like an anthropologist studying a new culture. Several games have taken lessons from Riven in this sense; where the logic of the puzzles [b]is[/b] the logic of the world and those who inhabit it. But the mystical (pun not intended) qualities of Riven elevate it above the rest, as far as I'm concerned.

[h2][b]The Remake is Almost Universally Better[/b][/h2]
The older style of the Myst games made them essentially glorified point-and-click slideshows. There's really no way to say it clearer than: walking around the world like you would in any other 3D exploration game is just a better, more immersive experience than constantly being locked to specific locations and perspectives. Also, you don't have to worry about swapping out CD-ROMs when traveling to different islands!

The most important point I want to touch on in this section, though, is regarding the changes that were made to many of the puzzles. You see, Cyan Worlds didn't just remake Riven - they changed a lot of the game's puzzles in order to make sure the experience could still be fresh for veterans and more welcoming for newbies. Some of the changes are basically quality-of-life updates, such as adding windows to certain walls that let you get a better sense of the environment or cutting down the minutiae of certain challenges that would more often lead to frustration than fun. The primary puzzle of the game is simplified, but the spirit of the puzzle remains. And while I know there are many oldheads out there who would bemoan this approach, I think it's a good change. It's rarely considered good puzzle design when the player knows what needs to be done but is constantly at risk of tripping over the tiniest of details where there are so many opportunities for something to go wrong along the way. ([url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=42SDc2Fhkm8]This episode of Design Delve[/url] talks about how the best puzzles usually take a small amount of time to complete once you have that a-ha moment. Ironically, this video is largely focused on a bad puzzle in another one of Cyan Worlds' games!)

As for the VR support that this remake includes, I would recommend not playing the game this way for one key reason: there's no way to take notes without taking off your headset. Compounding this issue is the fact that some things in the game require you to be looking at them while note-taking for the most accurate notes, and that just isn't possible with a VR headset. I really wish there were an in-game system of taking notes while in VR, because this could have made it the definitive way to experience Riven. Still, I can't deny that stepping into the Fifth Age while fully immersed in my Meta Quest 3 brought a smile to my face. Having the chance to "really" stand inside the village on Jungle Island, look over the lake, climb down into the bathysphere, and so forth... Young me never would have thought this possible back in the day.

[h2][b]What I Miss About the Original[/b][/h2]
I have to open this last section with a caveat that it's mainly rooted in my own nostalgia, aside from one thing. 

Pointing and clicking to navigate a glorified slideshow? Loading up a different CD-ROM each time you go to a different island? THAT'S how people used to play this?!?

Yes. And you know what? As a kid, I thought it was [i]cool[/i]. It was unlike any other game I had played. It made the whole experience feel grander, more interesting, and I'd argue...even more immersive. While I'm sure Cyan Worlds would have preferred to not ship the game on five separate discs that the player had to consistently swap out, I think this quirk actually lent the game a fascinating layer to the overall experience. Handling the physical discs in real life makes the "you are kind of an anthropologist" angle feel all the more valid. I liken it to listening to all the music ever made anywhere you go with your little black rectangle vs. putting on a vinyl record in your living room. That physicality adds [i]something special[/i]. We remember things that involve more doing, like handwriting instead of typing notes. I will always love Riven and if I ever get the desire to play it yet again in the future, I'll definitely stick to the remake. But I will always treasure the memories I made with the old-fashioned way of playing it.

There's also a major puzzle that got a total overhaul between versions. I won't get into spoilers, but I slightly prefer how it was handled in the original, mainly because of a few areas of logical failing. It's one of the few instances in the remake where video game logic totally dictates a certain part of the puzzle and couldn't realistically happen in the game world. (Again, I won't explicitly reveal it, but it involves the behavior of a certain type of animal.) I totally understand why this puzzle needed to be changed for the remake, though. And I had a lot of fun getting the new a-ha moments that this revamped puzzle delivers.

To end this long review, do not let this last section distract you from buying and playing Riven, in whichever form you prefer! It's such an inherently great game regardless of the nitpicky complaints I've rambled about.

Odyssey will forever be one of my favorite AC games. I have finished the main game twice non-steam and finally decided to get that platinum. While it may not be a traditional AC game and strays further from previous titles' gameplay, Ubisoft has tried something new with Odyssey and absolutely cooked.

While I enjoyed playing Origins, this game hits different. For me, Origins felt kinda empty at times (especially in the endgame) but I never had that feeling playing Odyssey. The game is huge, the world is beautiful and while there are many fantasy elements, the world stays true to Ancient Greece and it's culture.

The world of Odyssey is massive and I don't think people realize just how huge this game actually is. I'm talking about 120+ hours of gameplay for a platinum, easily 180+  if you want to collect literally everything. I'm 80 hours in and I'm still not done with the first DLC (I do collect everything though). A lot of these hours consist of repetitive quests but to be honest I don't really mind them that much - at the end of a day, I'm just happy I could stab some malakas.

Nevertheless, Odyssey has everything you'd want from a game situated in the middle of Peloponnesian War. Even though the story itself is in my opinion one of the weaker points of the game, it's still pretty solid. What I absolutely do love though is the scenery. You can turn on the photo mode literally anywhere on the map and I guarantee you it's going to look stunning - and no I'm not talking just about Kassandra.

Знаете, порой хочется простого человеческого уюта. Ну, знаете: налить горячего чая, открыть любимое печенье и, лениво залипая в экран, просто наслаждаться историей без каких-либо интенсивных сражений с мобами или бесчисленных открытых миров. Таких проектов немного, но этот точно входит в их число.

Не могу утверждать наверняка, но есть ощущение, что авторы вдохновлялись «Firewatch». Это прослеживается как в стилистическом, так и в идейном плане. Да чего греха таить, у них даже схож некий вайб загадочности происходящего. Не хочется слишком долго расписывать, что тут да как, но если кратко: история, диалоги, лёгкий детектив — всё это вовлекает, и ты не можешь оторваться. Основная идея этой истории — принятие себя, принятие прошлого, осознание своих ошибок — осмыслить все это поможет нашему герою его приключение по красивым зимним пейзажам. Диалоги не просто не дают заскучать во время долгой ходьбы, но и постепенно раскрывают характеры героев, их прошлое. Наблюдать за происходящим — одно удовольствие.

Единственное, финал игры чуть-чуть может подкачать: не совсем понятно, что же всё-таки происходило в этом месте, некоторые вопросы остаются. Да и последняя сцена будто намекает, что это вовсе не конец, открытый ли это финал или нет, непонятно, может быть я это не так понял. Но если все-таки да, то я считаю, что это неудачное решение. Но да ладно.

Касаемо игрового процесса, геймплей не напрягает. По сути, это простая бродилка — ходить порой приходится долго, и при этом подолгу ничего не происходит, в отличие от той же «Firewatch». Сгладить эти углы могли бы какие-нибудь интерактивные сценки или объекты на пути, да даже те же записки и дневники. В общем, в целом не хватило побольше интерактивных предметов, при взаимодействии с которыми герои могли бы поделиться своим мнением или мыслью. Причём такие в игре уже имеются, но их крайне мало. Ещё я считаю, что стоило бы отказаться от механики с голодом: умереть от голода уж очень надо постараться (если вообще есть такая опция, лично я не проверял), так как еда валяется буквально повсюду и в больших количествах.

Если подводить итоги, игра мне очень понравилась. Хотелось бы, чтобы таких проектов у нас все-таки было побольше. Разработчикам желаю дальнейших успехов и надеюсь, они учтут всю критику и ошибки, и их следующая игра будет ещё лучше.

O jogo não é extremamente horrível igual quem tá nos comentários fica dizendo, até porque certamente não jogaram Sonic 4 ou Advance 2.

Esse é na minha opinião uma enorme evolução dos jogos clássicos do Sonic, e fico feliz que tenha vendido bem. O problema é que as pessoas vão ficar irritadas por não ser o Mania 2 e por não ter o mesmo design de gameplay dos outros jogos clássicos.

Pra começar, o jogo É BEM DESAFIADOR. Você não vai mais ver bosses que demoram 20 segundos pra morrer e não vai ver um level design piedoso com o jogador. Aqui os bosses são genuinamente difíceis e levam um certo tempo pra matar, além do design das fases ser especialmente focado em exploração, no qual dá pra entender a descontentação. É um level design que não estão acostumados.

O jogo mantém a mesma historinha feita com animações de sprite que tinham nos jogos anteriores, e as partes mais cinemáticas são mostradas em animações curtas. Nesse jogo, as Esmeraldas do Caos conseguiram finalmente ter um uso decente: cada esmeralda libera um poder individual que você pode usar em cada fase pra acessar áreas novas ou coletar certos itens. Assim, você não precisa ficar caçando todas as esmeraldas pra ter algum poder que facilite sua jogatina.

Os special stages do jogo também são muito bem feitos. Tem o special stage de checkpoint, que tem inspiração no que tinha no Sonic 1, só que dessa vez com mecânicas novas e um controle que presta e não te irrita absurdamente. E também tem os anéis gigantes, que te dão warp pro special stage principal, onde você tem que fazer um minigame de grappling hook coletando anéis pra manter tempo, e indo mais veloz atrás da esmeralda.

Pra alguns defeitos mínimos, a música do jogo foi feita por diversos artistas, e fica bem nítido quais músicas foram compostas por qual pessoa, o que acaba deixando a soundtrack bem inconsistente e não sendo muito do teu agrado pra certas fases do jogo. Não é HORRÍVEL igual no Sonic 4, mas também não é na magnificência da OST do Mania. O background das fases também peca bastante em trazer um gráfico consistente, principalmente na Golden Capital, que provavelmente é a fase mais feia do jogo.

O level design das fases introduz mecânicas novas  pra cada uma delas, e deixa o jogo cheio de conteúdo, principalmente na Cyber Station. O multiplayer que você viu nos trailers não funciona direito, se você correr um tiquinho, todos os seus amigos morrem em segundos, é impossível jogar o co-op.

O multiplayer real do jogo é o maior foco dele, mas infelizmente é completamente morto, você nunca vai conseguir ver como é o conteúdo dele, considerando que o jogo base te pede muito pra coletar medalhas, nas quais liberam personalizações de personagem nesse modo. É uma ideia legal, mas não deu certo.

Enfim, eu não acho justo o jogo ser tratado como um dos piores jogos 2D do Sonic, mas entendo que ele não é perfeito em certas coisas. As pessoas da fanbase não costumam se conformar com diferenças em cada um dos jogos, então ficam procurando agulha no feno só pra tirar o desgosto de uma gameplay que você não experimentou antes. Esse não é um jogo ruim de forma alguma, eu diria que é muito bom e é quase tão bom quanto o Mania.

Fable isn’t just one of my favorite games — it’s a nostalgic masterpiece that still holds up today with the remastered graphics. Replaying it instantly transported me back, and once again, I found myself completely drawn into Albion. The charm, the addictive soundtrack, the immersive atmosphere.

For me, Fable represents the gold standard of the franchise and a blueprint for modern RPGs. Every time I dive in, I start as a Holy Paladin-type, embracing that righteous path, but the beauty of the game is in how flexible and personal your journey can become.

If you're into fantasy RPGs and want a rich, story-driven campaign, Fable is a must. Take your time — don’t rush because it isn't the largest game. Complete every side quest, explore every path, and really soak it all in. The endgame is light, but it’s the journey that makes it worth every minute. And when you're done? Start fresh, try a darker playstyle, and see how different the world reacts.

Nostalgia definitely adds to the magic for me but even without that lens, Fable still delivers an unforgettable experience.

I've been following Dreamed Away since its Kickstarter  launched roughly two years ago, so when I saw that it finally launched, I knew that I had to buy it. Now before I say anything, I want to note that I played the entire game up till the final boss on Switch 2, for roughly 8 hours. However, I felt that a review was needed for this game, so I bought it on Steam for precisely that reason.

First and foremost, the game is not fun. The battle system is your standard 'totally not Undertale' system that every indie RPG tends to follow these days, but while Undertale understood the bullet hell genre, Dreamed Away does not. You're basically stuck at the bottom of the screen moving left and right exclusively, immediately kneecapping what made Undertale's system good, and the patterns that enemies hit you at are entirely random, making some bosses' moves literally impossible to dodge. What doesn't help in this aspect is that leveling up does pretty much nothing for your stats. No matter how many levels I gained or how many weapons I equipped (which weren't many, I was stuck with a stick for 80% of the game), I found myself consistently dealing out 8-13 damage all the way through to the final boss. Also, did I mention that you need to cast a power spell at the start of every fight--wasting your first turn every time--if you want to deal any significant damage to the enemy?? Without it, you'll hit with a whopping 4 damage most of the time, and this is on bosses who have 40+ health. Combine these terrible stats with an unfun battle system and I found myself actively avoiding fights as much as I possibly could. I was actually crossing my fingers when the game was nearing its end, hoping that the final boss would just be a cutscene. There's also this strange DDR-esque system that the battles also use, which is admittedly better than the other form of combat, but these two switch off at random.

My second major issue with the game is its pacing. Have you ever wanted to play a game that's 80% dialogue/flashbacks and 20% "game"? No? Well then this game is not for you! For nearly hours at a time, Dreamed Away would have no enemies to fight, just boring fetch quests. This happened several times throughout the game, the most egregious of which was near the end when your character is in an underwater hospital. The only actual gameplay you're given here is running errands for the director, and by errands, I mean slowly running back and forth through giant, long corridors to deliver mail to doctors whose names you don't know yet. The only distinction you're given on who to give the letters to are their names, mind you. After this, there's a confusing color-coordinated code that the game gives you no hints or clues at to solve, which took me over an hour and ultimately led me to just look up the answer. That's a lot of what this game is in the later parts, by the way. Utter nonsense where the only way to continue is to run around through the entire game's map and press the A button on literally everything, hoping a cutscene is triggered. And again, the game gives no indication that you're supposed to do this. I also forgot to note this earlier, but the pacing is so bad because after an hour+ of no enemy encounters, the game will throw 15 enemies at you all at once. They all fight the exact same way too, with maybe very slight deviations. Though when the battle system is this shallow, you can't really blame anyone for repetitive battles. Like I mentioned earlier by the way, I actively avoided these fights as much as I could because they weren't fun and never made me substantially stronger. After killing 15 bats, you'd think that your character would be strong enough to one or two-shot them, but no, unless you do frame-perfect presses of the A button, they're pretty much always a four or five-shot.

My third issue with the game is its story. It's all over the place. The plot follows a little boy who needs to find his missing sister, and for the first four hours or so, he travels through a few "whimsical" lands to get to her. I say whimsical in quotes because it's all very generic, but it's better than what follows. Eventually there's a part where you're in a submarine with a pirate captain, and then you find yourself stuck in the dreaded underwater hospital I mentioned earlier. The issue here is that this is where the game's plot ends. The sister is barely mentioned after this, and the missing pirate captain just never returns. I don't know if he died or something though because that's not revealed either! In fact, until the literal last scene of the game, not a single one of the game's mysteries is ever revealed! Normally a good mystery gives the audience a clue or two to gnaw on as they continue on, but not Dreamed Away. You'll be stuck in this foe-Ghibli nonsense world that carries none of the Ghibli charm for 8 hours until you reach the very underwhelming answer to the game's mystery at the end--which I won't spoil, but man, I was expecting something with a lot more impact.

My fourth big issue will just be other miscellaneous problems I had with the game. For one, towards the end of the game, there's basically nowhere to buy good health items, which are kinda needed for the ridiculously unfair late-game bosses. Another thing about said bosses is that the late-game ones (and maybe even the earlier ones, I don't remember) don't have audio triggers for any of their moves. They'll just hit you with a 3-frame attack with no tell and you're expected to somehow dodge it. Another issue I have are the characters. RPGs thrive off of good stories and interesting characters, and this game has neither. No one's funny, no one's interesting. They all essentially speak in riddles since no one wants to let the player in on the big (underwhelming) mystery, and that alone makes them all boring. They also just don't have fun personalities. I feel like I should bring up Undertale again because someone like Papyrus just oozes personality. The closest Dreamed Away has are these elf goblin guys who're basically just a general nuisance, and after finishing the game and realizing what was going on the whole time, they also don't really make sense?? Like I still don't know what the purpose of them even was aside from artificial comedy (which for me, fell flat every time). There were also characters like the Storyteller who felt like they should be important but barely did anything the whole game and were never fully explained, which felt convoluted at best and like a waste of time at worst. There were also other small issues I had, such as every character saying "A-gain" spelled exactly like that, as well as characters like the 5-year-old sister speaking like an adult. For the first 2/3 of the game, mirrors play a big role (which doesn't make a whole lot of sense when you learn the meaning of the game at the end), but for some reason the devs chose to take this major plot piece and use it as an Undertale reference?? I know I talked that game up on this review already, but isn't it just kinda lame to take the "It's you." and "It's still you." lines from Undertale when looking in a mirror, especially when mirrors aren't just a set piece and are an actual big part of your game?? Like I said, it's a pet peeve, but there's a time and place for references; major set pieces aren't it.

Ultimately, my issues with this game boil down to it not being fun. There isn't much too say that other reviews have not. As a Final Fantasy fan, everything about this game is amazing except for the actual "game". 

The characters' 3D designs, full voice acting, music, player icons, level designs, etc, are all amazing. It's amazing to see all of the characters in full 3D and interacting with each other between franchises.

The actual Dissidia NT game is not fun. It is a bland and boring 3D fighter where everyone flies around like DBZ characters in a chaotic mess. The UI is a total incomprehensible mess. The stamina feature is jarringly annoying when you dash around for a few seconds and then have to stand completely still for 2 seconds to regenerate it. Combat is largely consistent of hitting enemies that can't see you or being hit by enemies from offscreen that you can't see, due largely in part to the absolutely indescribably awful camera and lock-on system.

You have very limited control over the camera because you are forced to always "lock on" to a target. You cannot de-target, only switch to a different target, which swings your camera around wildly. Even with the minimap, this leads to scenarios of being hit by enemies or attacks that are very difficult to see.

The game has no real respect for player agency or you time in general. Both small and large annoyances. Moving around the maps can be frustrating because of the constant starting/stopping from the above-mentioned stamina. It's common to get hit by chains of attacks that pancake you into walls and cause your character to take over 10+ seconds to recover, meaning you can just set down the controller when this happens and watch your character get dribbled like a basketball. You can frame-cancel your attacks to block (or possibly dodge), but this interrupt takes so long in your animation that it rarely works. It's more economical to simply not attack and wait for the enemy to attack in order to block/dodge/counter. 

One of the biggest mechanics in the game is the "summon" mechanic. Once per match, each side will basically get to call down their summon. You are treated with a jarring complete stop in the battle (even if you were in the middle of attacking, etc) and get to watch an unskippable 10 second cutscene. The summon attacks are easily dodged, but because they are so quick and persistent, you basically have to spend 100% of your time dodging them for an entire minute. If you are on the offensive side of the summon it really isn't any more fun, because your opponents are just going to run away the entire time due to dodging the summon's massive AoE effects. So basically 2 minutes of every match will be all of the players zipping around avoiding each other. It's such a weird halt to all of the action and isn't fun.

You will not be able to be auto-matched to any real players due to zero player count, so unless you join an online (Discord) community dedicated to setting up matches, you will have to play against bots. The only way to play against bots in ranked mode is to sit at the matchmaking screen for exactly 4 minutes before the game fills in the slots with bots.

Playing against bots is boring and awful and I do not recommend it. They are the worst-of-the-worst AI and do nothing but 1) input reading and 2) break the rules of the game themselves. I have  consistently seen them use abilities that are supposed to be locked out for the first 30 seconds of the match within the first few seconds. They have a very set script of attacks they do, very consistently. For example, if you try to use your dash attack they always immediately counter with Poisonga. If you block they immediately detarget you and run away. Beating them isn't difficult, it's just boring and frustrating and involves figuring out which of your moves and attacks manipulate their very limited AI.

I have never played a Dissidia game before, so I know a lot of the complaints I have read are that players are only comparing this to the past games, which are a different format. I can say that this game is just terrible on it's own merit, as a video game. The gameplay is boring and frustrating, even when you are winning. The UI is one of the worst messes I have every seen.

There is a very short single player mode that is basically a few cutscenes and then the same boring fighting against bots as the multiplayer mode. There are zero RPG or progression mechanics in the game. It's just a pure arena battler where every fight is exactly like the last fight, over and over again.

Even for free this game is a hard "do not recommend". You will be a better person for having never played this game.

Spells & Secrets, developed by Alchemist Interactive and rokaplay, and published by rokaplay, is a vibrant magical roguelite that captures the feeling of being a student in a living, breathing school of wizardry. The game begins with a simple premise: you’ve just arrived at the prestigious Greifenstein Academy, a sprawling castle full of mysteries, but before you can settle into your first year, chaos erupts. A magical incident traps the school in disarray, and it’s up to you—and any friends joining you in local co-op—to restore order using your growing mastery of spells and arcane knowledge. What unfolds is a lighthearted yet challenging adventure that blends the charm of a magical academy setting with the replayability and unpredictability of a roguelite.

The core gameplay loop revolves around exploration, experimentation, and combat inside Greifenstein’s ever-changing halls. Each run through the academy’s procedurally generated rooms introduces new layouts, enemies, and combinations of spells. You begin with basic magic and a small handful of abilities, but as you defeat creatures, solve puzzles, and unlock new professors, your repertoire grows. The joy of Spells & Secrets lies in its flexibility—spells can be combined, upgraded, and altered through artifacts to create unexpected results. For example, what begins as a simple levitation spell can become a powerful tool for manipulating enemies or accessing hidden areas once enhanced. Every run is an opportunity to try new builds, experiment with synergistic items, and approach encounters from fresh angles.

The sense of discovery extends beyond combat. The game encourages you to explore each environment thoroughly, rewarding curiosity with hidden lore, collectible artifacts, and secret puzzles. Many of these side activities feel like they belong in a proper school of magic, blending education with danger in a way that feels authentic to the setting. Some rooms serve as classrooms, others as libraries or laboratories, all filled with interactive objects that add personality and encourage experimentation. Even outside of combat, magic feels like the center of everything, from moving objects with telekinesis to creating makeshift bridges or dousing fires. The result is a world that feels alive, playful, and reactive.

The combat itself is brisk and satisfying, balancing accessibility with enough challenge to keep players on their toes. You can equip up to three main spells at a time, with an additional slot for swapping in others mid-run. This limitation forces strategic thinking—choosing which spells to keep active at any given time becomes crucial as the difficulty ramps up. Enemies range from mischievous magical creatures to corrupted students and rogue spirits, each requiring different tactics. Boss battles punctuate each floor of the academy, offering intense showdowns that test your ability to adapt and make smart use of your spell combinations. Though some of these bosses are a bit simplistic in design and behavior, they still deliver moments of excitement and reward experimentation.

Visually, Spells & Secrets shines with its colorful, stylized presentation. The world is rendered in a warm, cartoon-like art style that evokes both whimsy and nostalgia, reminiscent of classic fantasy adventures. The castle itself is detailed and dynamic, with moving staircases, floating books, and shimmering portals adding to the sense of magic. The soundtrack complements this with light orchestral tones that shift smoothly between peaceful exploration and energetic battle themes. These aesthetic choices combine to create an experience that feels inviting and enchanting without ever losing its sense of mystery. It’s a game that encourages players to get lost in its world and enjoy the thrill of discovery.

While Spells & Secrets succeeds in charm and atmosphere, it does have some mechanical and structural shortcomings. The restriction of only three active spells can feel limiting when you’ve unlocked a wide arsenal of creative abilities. The variety of enemies and environments, though visually pleasing, doesn’t always evolve as much as you might hope across repeated runs. The roguelite elements also lean more toward accessibility than depth—death doesn’t carry much weight beyond restarting your run, and long-term progression systems are modest compared to more complex titles in the genre. For some players, this simplicity may be a strength; for others, it may feel like a missed opportunity for greater depth.

Despite these flaws, the game’s replayability and cooperative potential keep it engaging. Local co-op allows two players to work together, combining spells and coordinating tactics in chaotic, often hilarious ways. It’s one of the features that gives the game real staying power, transforming it from a solo adventure into a shared magical romp. The developers clearly wanted to make a roguelite that anyone could enjoy—one that captures the sense of wonder and experimentation that defines good fantasy storytelling. Whether you’re a genre veteran or a newcomer, it’s easy to appreciate how approachable and inviting the game feels.

Spells & Secrets ultimately stands as a delightful, if not groundbreaking, entry in the roguelite landscape. It thrives on creativity, atmosphere, and the joy of magical experimentation, offering players an accessible gateway into the genre’s appeal. The school setting, interactive world, and whimsical tone give it a distinct personality that sets it apart from darker or more demanding roguelites. While it doesn’t reach the mechanical or narrative complexity of the genre’s heavyweights, it more than compensates with charm, energy, and heart. For players who love the idea of conjuring spells, solving puzzles, and saving a magical academy one chaotic run at a time, this is a game well worth stepping into.

Trans-Siberian Railway ist ein sehr guter Simulator, der aber nicht nur das simple geradeaus fahren hat, wir müssen Aufträge der Mafia erledigen, wo es auch mal Schusswaffen zur Sache geht. Aber die meiste Zeit sitzen wir im Zug und starren die ganze Zeit nach vorne und fahren von A nach B nach C nach D nach E ... Viel gibt es im Zug nicht zu tun, außer auf die Strecke aufzupassen, da wir öfters mal nur 40km/h fahren dürfen oder wir die Stromabnehmer herunternehmen müssen. Die ganze Strecke soll über 800 Kilometer haben - aber ob es ein Ende gibt, weiß ich nicht. Die Story ist leider bei ca. 300 Kilometer Strecke vorbei. Dann kann man nur noch selbst fahren und/oder Waggon-Aufträge erfüllen. Aber ich denke, da kommt noch einiges, weil man derzeit eine Errungenschaft nicht bekommt, wo man alle Missionen der Mafia erledigen muss.

Das Spiel spielt sich gut und der Zug fährt auch echt teils realistisch. Das heißt, wenn wir Bremsen, müssen wir das genau abschätzen, da der Zug nicht nach 30 Meter zum Stehen kommt. Man muss halt je nach Geschwindigkeit, Zustand der Bauteile, wo der Bremshebel steht und ob man Waggons hinten dran an, mit bis zu 1000 Meter Bremsweg rechnen. Zudem läuft es sehr flüssig, es gibt nur hin und wieder mal kleine Laderuckler. Ich hatte auch kein einzigen Absturz.

Leider sieht die Strecke zu 95% gleich aus... Überall Schnee und Links/Rechts paar Bäume. Natürlich befinden wir uns halt an einem Ort, wo es nun mal quasi Winter ist bzw. so aussieht. Aber ETWAS Abwechslung wäre echt gut, es ist immer noch ein Spiel, nicht die Realität. Weil es ansonsten echt schnell öde wird. Es gibt z.B. keine Gebirge, keine Stadtdurchfahrt oder Strecke neben Flüsse oder so. Ohne die Ortsnamen würde man denken, man fährt nur im Kreis.

Die Gegner in den Missionen sind leider auch Strohdumm... die meisten bleiben einfach wie Schießbudenfiguren stehen. Als Beispiel die Lagerhalle mit den vergifteten Alkohol. Da gibt es ca. 20-25 Gegner. Die sind auch ALLE durch die Wände in Rot markiert. Und 95% der Gegner rühren sich kein Stück, 3 kamen um die Ecke gerannt, die waren auch nicht markiert, keine Ahnung warum. Die anderen suchen keine Deckung, sie stürmen nicht auf einem zu. Ausnahme, wenn man z.B. an Bahnhöfen herum schießt, dann kommt schon mal die Polizei hinter euch her. Aber 1-2 Bahnhöfe weiter und niemand weiß von deiner Aktion. 

Zudem kann man mit dem Zug jederzeit stehen bleiben. Wer sein Zug kaum bis gar nicht Wartet und auch nichts macht, um Geld zu verdienen, der hat irgendwann die A-Karte gezogen. Weil dann kannst du dir keine Ersatzteile kaufen und dein Zug reparieren.

Was ich besonders gut finde, ist das System beim Essen/Trinken etc. diese Balken füllen sich echt sehr langsam. В мире шумных экшенов и сложных стратегий Farming Simulator 22 занимает свою, особую нишу. Это не просто игра про фермерство. Это цифровое убежище, где время замедляется, а тревоги уступают место ритмичному гулу трактора.

Как и в ETS 2, здесь ваш главный соперник — не другие игроки, а вы сами. Ваша цель — не победить босса, а построить свое идеальное, процветающее хозяйство. И это невероятно умиротворяет.

Почему это "ламповая" игра и релакс-симулятор:

🌾 Медитативный геймплей. Процессы здесь цикличны и предсказуемы: вспахать, засеять, собрать, продать. В этом есть что-то первобытное и успокаивающее. Можно часами кататься на тракторе по полю, слушая подкаст или любимую музыку, и полностью отключать голову от внешних проблем.

🌾 Ощущение прогресса и порядка. Вы начинаете с маленького участка и старенького трактора, а благодаря своему труду постепенно превращаетесь в владельца огромной агроимперии. Чувство удовлетворения, когда видишь результат своего труда — аккуратные поля, полные ангары и растущий банковский счет — бесценно.

🌾 Уютная атмосфера. Игра красива по-своему. Восходы и закаты над полями, смена времен года (которая здесь реализована просто великолепно), тишина зимнего утра — все это создает невероятно "теплую" и комфортную среду.

🌾 Огромная свобода. Хотите — занимайтесь только растениеводством. Хотите — разводите коров и овец. Или, может, вас манит виноделие или производство одежды? Здесь нет правильного пути, есть только ваш путь.

Какие "косяки" стоит иметь в виду:

⚠ Некоторая монотонность. Если вас не цепляет сам цикл "посадил-вырастил-продал", игра может показаться рутинной. Это специфика жанра.

⚠ Технические шероховатости. Физика иногда подкидывает забавные сюрпризы (например, прицеп может решить жить своей жизнью), AI помощников не всегда идеален, а графика, хоть и приятная, не является топовой.

⚠ Сложность входа. Симуляция довольно глубокая. Новичку может быть непросто разобраться во всех тонкостях удобрений, севооборотов и логистики. Но это та сложность, которая доставляет удовольствие при её преодолении.

Итог:

Farming Simulator 22 — это не про драйв. Это про спокойствие. Это про порядок, который вы создаете в виртуальном мире, пока в реальном царит хаос.

Рекомендую ли я ее? Однозначно ДА, если вы:

Ищете игру для релаксации после тяжелого дня.

Любите "песочницы", где можно строить и развивать что-то свое.

Наслаждаетесь процессом, а не только результатом.

Ищете игру "на подольше", в которую можно возвращаться месяцами.

Это та самая игра, которая стоит на страже вашего спокойствия. Просто садитесь в свой трактор и катитесь к горизонту. Все остальное подождет.
