Games like this are why reviews being either "recommend" or "not recommend" is an imperfect situation at times.
The story is lacking, but coming from MW5: Mercs, it feels like a refreshing improvement. 
The cutscenes... actually exist this time, rather than... not.
The graphics are a solid step up.
The gameplay is more challenging, though that may be because 1. I was running mods for Mercs and 2. the missions seem to be noticeably longer in most cases, so more chances to get shot up.

The problem is that the difficulty comes from a vast majority of missions being long, winding hallways filled with 20x the tonnage of mechs vs what you can bring. Later on, you will go entire missions without seeing a single light-mech. You will often have armor in the red, be begging for a repair bay or just for the mission to end, only to have someone hop on the radio and inform you more enemies are inbound and then multiple assault mechs come out of a dropship. Sometimes that dropship is also shooting at you. Meanwhile you are out of ammo in one of your weapons.

But, you probably bought the game because you want to pilot big, stompy mechs and shoot other mechs to pieces. This game delivers you a preponderance of enemy mechs to shoot at.

As for the other big draw, mech customization, it is... OK. You are definitely more limited than I like, especially after running modded Mercs, but it also in a way turns it into a puzzle for you to figure out, so there is SOME benefit from the limitations, as it makes you think. That said, I agree with the complaints that the constraints are annoying because almost every mech variant has just... wasted weapon slots. There are scarce few mechs that can be highly specialized to a certain weapon type. Many have a full mix of ballistic/missile/energy, that leaves you coming up a little short in every category. 

There are variants that avoid this shortcoming, just not as many as I would like.

So I would call customization either a wash, or a slight let-down depending on how much you appreciate the "puzzle" aspect of figuring out how to make things work within those tight constraints.

The combat is solid, but like I said, it is usually just a grueling death-march for 90% of missions that often leaves you exhausted by the end, so can become a bit tedious. However, I realized far too late how valuable pulling up the tactical map and issuing orders through it can be. It saved me big time on the last two missions. It is not generally necessary to succeed, but does add a nice layer to the combat sometimes which might help ease the monotony of the missions for some.

Lastly, the story. It is... not great. It is a very slow burn with not a great payoff. Most missions are just focused on the objective of that mission and can feel divorced from any overarching plot. Many times I would pause and ask myself "wait, what IS the overarching plot, here? Where is this all going?"

Well where it was going was a surprise, and not a great one. I will not spoil it, but the "overarching plot" is very small in scale compared to what you might expect and leaves you feeling like nothing was really accomplished in the end. To be fair, from what I have learned over time, this is... kinda a very Battletech way for things to go. It seems a lot of conflicts in the universe just result in everyone being battered back to square one, but... in this case, it was done in a pretty unsatisfying way for me. Every single arc of the story ends with almost nothing having been truly accomplished.

In terms of gameplay and visuals, this is currently the pinnacle of what is available for stompy mechs. Yes there's also Armored Core, which I love, but that is a very different style of mech compared to Battletech. In terms of story and mission design... well I am glad I brought up Armored Core, because that is a much better example doing both well. You don't even see the faces of the characters in AC6... or... any of the games, perhaps(?), and yet it at least feels a bit more cohesive with a clearer direction of where things are headed.

Speaking of the characters, we really did not get enough of them. You cannot even interact with them outside of missions and cutscenes, so your ability to bond with and care about them is going to be very hit or miss, and I can see why some people find most of them boring if not outright unlikable. It is actually hilarious how each character in your "Star" (squad) literally gets like a single one-on-one conversation with the main character, like they were checking off boxes to say "OK, now it is this one's turn for a bit of character development." Aside from that, they rarely get more than generic mission chatter during gameplay though I guess you might notice SOME patterns with what they say in that chatter over time.

I say get it on sale. It still delivers solid mech gameplay with great visuals, it is just everything surrounding that is a huge mixed bag. And while we cannot give the game too many points for mods, it IS nice that there is official mod support via official mod tools, and with what Mercs got, I have some hope for Clans getting cool stuff going forward.

I heard a lot of mixed things when this came out, as a huge battletech fan I was disappointed to hear bad news but eventually picked this game up on sale and while I'm enjoying it somewhat, the cut-scenes are nice and the battelgrid is a solid addition overall I agree with many of the negative sentiments I read. 

Namely the gameplay is very poorly tuned, Normal difficulty is a grueling slog, most of the missions I've played so far well into the Turtle Bay arc I have finished with a single functioning mech barely still standing and I finally gave up and switched to Easy after a mission where I had to clear multiple caches, fighting the whole way and then faced three assault mechs as enemy reinforcements and was ordered to flee, the escape route is littered with vehicles and a mixture of light mechs and my Lance/Star was already badly mauled and down a mech at this point, fighting through left me with just 2 mechs and 1 medium laser between them only to then find I had to destroy six light and medium mechs before extraction, needless to say that did not happen and I just wasted half an hour of my time. I was at max tonnage for the mission, the early engagements went well, I utilized positioning and the star-mates as much as I could and it was still nowhere near enough, I have no idea who playtested this mess but that is just ridiculous. At no time playing MW5:Mercenaries did I struggle that much in any mission ever. 

Then playing on Easy is just... mindless, far, far too easy. The jump from easy to normal is absurd and I can't imagine playing on a harder difficulty than that. Mech chassis and pilot-skill upgrades might make for an easier time replaying those missions but I can't see those things swinging the results all that much. The biggest advantage clan mechs have is range and speed and few of the missions ever give you the chance to really utilize either of those things. The one good thing I'll give is that AI Teammates actually use Jump Jets at times and their AI does seem to be somewhat improved over MW5:Mercs. 

Graphics are slightly better overall with the switch to Unreal Engine but not so much so that it makes up for the deficits in other areas. I've had a lot of spotty textures, pop in is rough on higher settings even for my solid rig and aside from much better machine gun animations and sounds the visuals and feedback of most of the weapons is grossly inferior. LRMS in particular look pretty bad here compared to mercs. 

At this point I honestly hope MW5:Mercs continues to get more expansions and we see the remaining clan mechs and omnimechs already present in MW5:Clans get ported to Mercs. The Ebon Jaguar, Huntsman, Hunchback IIC and a few others would be nice additions to Mercs but other than that I just cannot recommend this game except to the most die-hard battletech/mech combat fans.

The combat is fun - not too hard, not too easy - with plenty of abilities and enemy variety to keep it dynamic. Bosses are on the easy side, but still satisfying enough to make you feel like you’ve accomplished something. Where the game truly shines, though, is in its puzzles and exploration. Each one actually feels handcrafted (crazy, right?), mixing logic, physics, and curiosity in a way that never gets dull. The Tartarus vaults in particular are brilliant.

Graphically, it’s not a technical powerhouse, but the cartoon art style works surprisingly well. It's colorful, full of personality, and refreshingly un-Ubisoft-like. Performance is excellent overall, aside from the occasional hiccup courtesy of their beloved launcher.

The soundtrack is great, with a few standout tracks, and the lighthearted tone of the story gives it real charm. It doesn’t take itself too seriously, which is probably why it succeeds where so many of their “epic” games don’t.

It’s been a long time since I’ve had this much fun with a Ubisoft game. Highly recommended.

I wish I could recommend this game, I truly do. It still has a slightly decent population of players actively playing it, even if most of them have basically been spending most of their times just hanging out or leveling brand new characters. The community is certainly not dead, but the game is definitely in maintenance mode. 

Maintenance mode is defined as the point of an online game's life cycle where there is minimal to no expectation of a game being updated with new content, with a token development team just making sure the servers are still running for its players. Arc Games/Cryptic has long since moved on from Champions Online to their other properties--Star Trek Online and Neverwinter. 

The game is still somewhat fun to play even if there's no expectation of running group content outside of the game's most active hours. It's amazing how completely [i]customizable[/i] the game's controls can be. Run it like a normal MMO? Run it like an action game? Run it like an FPS? You can change around the bindings and the way targeting works to suit your desired playstyle. It's surprisingly modern in that regard. 

But beyond that, roleplaying has basically devolved to people e-boning each other. There's very little RP to be had and the community for it has basically gone dormant. 

The game no longer has a subscription to get unlimited freeform slots. Now you have to pay around $25 for a Freeform Slot token. The only good thing about this (beyond the obvious cash-grab nature of it) is that the token is applied per-slot, not per-character--so you can create and delete as many times as you want and you'll never lose the token. Playing this game freeform is basically the way to go as it allows you to create the superhero of your dreams. 

This game has so many great ideas but it all gets cobbled together into one giant mess that isn't even being regarded by its developers. I would personally recommend moving on to something else--the game this is essentially a spiritual successor to, City of Heroes, is back online now thanks to the volunteer efforts of its community.

What The Golf? est une petite pépite qui se dévore à une vitesse impressionnante. J'ai terminé le jeu à 100% en l'espace d'un seul weekend, soit un peu moins de 10 heures, et je n'ai pas vu le temps passer.

Ce jeu est un festival d'inventivité et de surprise. Il est bourré de "juicy" – ce feedback de game design si satisfaisant qui rend chaque interaction addictive et amusante. Le principe reste simple, mais le jeu ne cesse de renouveler son concept.

Chaque niveau est un mini-jeu, une idée folle où l'on doit propulser tout sauf une balle de golf, du cheval à la maison, en passant par... le jeu lui-même ! Les développeurs ont fait preuve d'un talent monstrueux pour maintenir l'effet de surprise du début à la fin.

Le jeu est également plein de clins d'œil et de blagues, notamment des jeux de mots très pertinents et des niveaux entiers transformés en hommages à d'autres licences vidéoludiques. Les segments inspirés de Superhot, Among Us, ou encore Portal sont des réussites hilarantes et surprenantes.

L'expérience est extrêmement addictive et surprenante, tout en restant agréable et accessible. Il est difficile de se lasser quand le jeu réinvente ses mécaniques toutes les deux minutes.

Verdict : Une bouffée d'air frais, un titre idéal pour un weekend de jeu intense. Si vous cherchez un jeu court, intelligent, et incroyablement drôle qui fait travailler vos zygomatiques autant que vos méninges, What The Golf? est un must-have absolu. Je fais une pause avant d'attaquer What The Car? par peur de l'overdose, mais ce genre de jeu m'a énormément plu !

Twelve years on, Papers Please serves as both the pinnacle and progenitor of its own genre of narrative-driven simulator, and despite a long list of replicators and imitators, has only been (maybe) superceded by Lucas Popes follow up.

The sheer ingenuity and creativity behind this game is staggering. The fact that somebody (Pope) thought ‘You know what would make a good game? What if you were a guard at a border crossing and you had to cross reference paper-work.’
Like, ‘ V I D E O G A M E S ‘ are where you are a hot person with a gun or a sword and you kill people and do kickflips, not a monotonous, stressful work simulator where your concerns are about sick family members, and the omnipresent conflict between your own totalitarian dystopia and the nations surrounding it. On paper, a game where you deal with a bunch of paperwork and have to pay your rent and worry about the state of the nation isn’t very fun… and it also isn’t very fun in practise either, and I say that with utmost respect.

I think ‘Papers, Please’ proves that video games don’t have to be fun (or atleast, kinetically exhilarating) to be good, which seems insane to think, but it is true. The real metric for a good video game is not ‘fun’ but rather ‘engagement.’ It doesn’t actually matter if you are having fun, if you are enthralled and engaged - this game delivers that in droves. It realizes the casual horror of living in a Soviet-era regime, and is able to tell stories from the smallest scale to the greatest of consequences, all from this one screen. From small character narratives of love and fear, to the global conflicts and wars, it all filters through your little booth. The moral choices this game places on you are so rarely seen in any form of art, and in general dystopias are not depicted in such a realistic way.

You are not in the high offices of government, you are not a soldier on the front lines, you are an immigration inspector at a border crossing, yet you have power over people lives, life and death are controlled by your stamps. Trying to walk the balance between being empathetic towards people, while not making too many mistakes, and trying to not get so many fines as to starve your family is a tense tightrope you have to walk. 

Do you let in this grieving mother, despite her papers being outdated? They are only expired by a few days. This man is moving with his wife, but his passport is obviously forged, but he is fleeing from a warzone. Another has wrong papers, yet hasn’t committed any real crime, but you get bribes for each person you detain, and your family is starving and freezing to death at home. Should you detain them for a minor transgression? Even the people the game ASKS you to detain - they are in the wanted criminals bulletin - we are never told what they have done, and they seem shocked and surprised at being detained. Are they really criminals, or have they just spoke out against Arstotska? 

Papers, Please is an example of sheer focus and execution on a single vision, and the power of video game story telling. It is also an example of choice. You could be empathetic, you could engage with everything, and read the newspapers, and help to thwart the government. Or you could keep your head down, ignore anybody who talks to you, and just do your job and keep your family safe. A timeless game which should be studied and put in museums.

下面说几个吐槽点：
1、剧情模式太简单，哪怕是英雄模式，都随随便便通关。所以最后还是只能玩无尽模式..
2、无尽模式就很蛋疼，腐化格这个设定很恶心，没有有效的应对手段，21关后怪物血量十几万，炮塔依旧是5点8点伤害，超过100点伤害的攻击速度很慢，感觉是为了难而难非常不合理。
建议：
1、无尽模式前可以向剧情模式一样，搞个几小关，然后就可以工坊强化搞一些强化格，不然强化格的获取太少只能靠宝箱。
2、每日每周你可以照常搞，但是多出一个自定义让玩家可以选择自己想玩的图，类似杀戮之塔那样玩家自定义一些参数。
3、巨大化的锤子应该变成基础设定，不然无尽不选那个胖子其他角色没法玩。
4、出一个技能，比如全塔加攻速，全图眩晕之类的，可以用多余的技能点出一个商店，玩家可以购买一些道具和强化一些技能之类的，这样多以的技能点也有了去处。
总结：总体来说，这个价格对于这个内容还是偏贵，可玩性不是太高，还是期待制作组多听取玩家意见，多更新一些后续内容。

There has now been an endless mode added, but upgrade costs in general have been increased in an effort to lengthen total gameplay i assume, between this and the fact endless mode is only post game the core gameplay loop has been slowed down and arguably become more boring youll have to repeat maps in the exact same way to grind for even more resources than before. Makes things more interesting at the end game however, but its still a very short title to complete overall, no new maps or modes added or even challenges. Pretty short and very repetitive, already completed 100% all content and i dont even have 3h played. Theres some cool ideas here but it feels more like a demo than a fully fledged game.

Theres only like 4-5 basic enemy types as well, gimmick is they just scale hp and so you repeat to grind resources to out scale the scaling. You dont really see maps with different wave varieties either, it will always be a mix of the same standard enemies so the strategy you gravitate towards will work on mostly any map provided you have the meta progression to get through the scaled enemy hp.
 
Theres also only 15 maps total then youre done. Between the small map pool and the limited enemy variety game started to lose my interest rather quickly.... but it was also over quickly to 100% the game. Both not great points to have in your game.

[strike] Theres also no endless mode of any kind on any of the maps in order to grind for resources faster or max out your defences, [/strike]  

I found myself simply repeating a map several times in the exact same way to grind resources to complete the next map. Not exactly exciting gameplay just going through the motions to unlock the next thing to beat the next map. 

Skill tree could do with some restructuring as well, many perks are very boring % bonus to x, and skill tree also wants you to go down one path focusing on one tower to maximize benefits. with minimal enemy wave variety you can just beat the game by choosing a tower and upgrading its meta till you win. You dont really need to use multiple towers. Skill tree also a bit confusing at times, you dont know what you need to unlock in order to unlock the upgrade so you can start collecting the next tier of resource, you just stumble across it and kinda go "oh, now i can upgrade all this stuff i wanted to but couldnt until now" a sense of direction to the skill tree to at least point you to areas you should look for the next tier of upgrade currency would be nice instead of it being a bit of a mess.

Game also lacking some basic features youd expect to see in a TD like hotkeys in general (game is entirely mouse only) or change default tower attack preference (most towers default to closest which isnt the greatest option often)

Overall i think if this game was priced more in the $2-3 range it would be a charming little indie title, but as it stands the content just isnt there for the asking price, even on the 40% off sale. 

Will revisit this  if more content is added along with QoL but in its current state its certainly quite lackluster for what i expected. Happy to see dev working on it a bit though

I’ve been never a big turn-based strategy gamer - XCOM never interested me even though I received one of their games for free (never downloaded). Civ 5 really did capture me but no other turn-based game has since. Instead, I immersed myself in RTS and grand strategy games. Those RTSs included Eugene System's Steel Division and Wargame franchises, and the Total War games like Warhammer 2. In terms of grand strategy, I clocked up hundreds of hours on Paradox titles including Imperator: Rome and Europa Universalis IV (see my previous reviews for evidence).

This is all to say turn-based strategy games aren't my traditional stomping ground. Yet I'm pleased to confirm the Troop is one of the best strategy games I've ever played. The AI is competent, perfect for those who like a challenge. It punishes the reckless placement of your troops and makes an active effort to probe and flank. This is not a game for Total War players who want to marvel at AI swarms getting mowed down by fire and brimstone at the click of a mouse (Total War arty spammers where you at??). It’s also important to know that the AI doesn’t feel unfair - it didn’t act like it had an all-seeing eye, falling to my ambushes and ambushing me in return for good measure.

The Troop rewards patience. For example, the accuracy and fog of war mechanics mean you often don’t order your troops to fire on first sight of the enemy. Your troops WILL be spotted and the return fire could be devastating especially when you're outnumbered (I just completed my first campaign, playing as the 1944 Germans). So you hold fire until the enemy are close before ordering the MG42s and Pak40s to say "Guten morgen!" to those Allied troops.

Your units’ attacks are determined on a dice roll, with lower probabilities to hit the further the target is and the less action points the attacker has (e.g. they just moved to a new position/they’re tired). This is a big oversimplication but the context enables me to say this: no other game made me clap my adult hands together like I won a small lottery whenever my tanks made the shots they needed to.

If you like WW2 settings, get immense satisfaction from making clever plays (fellow RTS players who like PvP - I'm thinking of you <3), and appreciate the difference between a Panzer IV and a Panzer V Panther, I implore you to try this game. I wouldn't have written this review unless I had something to recommend. I believe the developers are an indie studio and so it's even more impressive they made a game that gave me delusions of being in the German High Command. There's no multiplayer but that's no biggie for me, there's lots of strategic content here over 2 German and 2 Allied campaigns among other features including one-off scenarios.

1944/10, would have commanded 21st Panzer better than that profligate Feuchtinger.

Idol Manager is a simulation game where you recruit girls to be Idols, create a group for them and manage their success with the help of a staff. The staff is also hired by you, in fact the amount of responsibility and management in this game should be overwhelming but its displayed in such a way and fed to a piece at a time, so its not.

The UI and menus are intuitive easy to navigate, and understand. The music while redundant, is pleasant and fits the game well.

While this title barely qualifies as an "Ecchi" game in my opinion, I'm reviewing it cause I feel it manages to eek across the line... only barely. With the R18/NFSW patch (found in the Steam Workshop or on the developer's website) you can add spicy content (not much but some) that organically fit into the story and your relationships with the various idols.

The workshop also has a plethora of wonderful mods to tailor the experience to you and what you want out of it. Sexier idols, famous anime characters as idols, new outfits as well as a mod (that requires a tiny bit of legwork offsite) that will add entire NFSW capabilities and game play elements.

Even without mods though, whats here will keep anyone into sims busy for hours.

You can manage everything from salaries to if the girls are allowed to date. You have them perform (don't see any actual performances), build facilities for them to use, "style" them, chat with them, create hit singles and compete in award shows... and much more.

There are light visual novel elements mixed in, a pretty good story that progresses over the long campaign and you can even make more than one idol group once your a big enough company.

I highly recommend this even though I would of appreciated more spicy content and more actual artwork during events and scenes. [h1]思ったより酷くはないが、皆の言いたいことは分かる[/h1]

[h2]◇はじめに[/h2]
筆者は三國志11、14のみプレイ済みでリメイク前の8はプレイしたことがない。
結論を先に言うと、第一印象(steamレビュー評価：賛否両論)よりは面白いがフルプライスで買うにはかなり厳しいのでセール価格で買うべし。

[h2]◇良かった点[/h2]

[h3]責任がなくて気楽[/h3]
君主プレイの三國志や信長の野望はその勢力が滅亡してしまうとそこでゲームオーバーだが、武将個人プレイの今作は[b]むしろそこからが始まり[/b]まである。
君主ではない一般武将は評定でできることが少なく(軍師や太守は4回～5回に対して一般武将は1回のみ)、せいぜい敵拠点の諜報や前線への輸送の提案だけで、あとは決められた開発ノルマさえこなしていれば旅行に行ったりほかの武将と交流するだけでいい。戦になっても軍師や太守でなければ自分の部隊しか操作できず、[strike]コーエー特有のアホアホAIなのもあって[/strike]負けても自分の責任にはならない。

[h3]シナリオがわりとすぐ終わる[/h3]
自分が君主や太守・都督といった軍権がある立場であれば、行軍の概念がない分11や14に比べてあっさりとクリアできる。加えて中間エンドが豊富で、1地方を制覇すればクリアの地方制覇エンドであったり、武名や文名、悪名がMaxになればクリアできたり、名品をコンプするとクリアであったりと色々な終わらせ方がある。
また、日常フェーズ1ターンが1か月なのですぐ1年が終わる。だらだらやってると一瞬で月日が経って武将が死んでしまうので好きな武将と戦場を駆けたいなら意外と急いだほうが良かったりする。

[h3]交流がとても重要[/h3]
今作はほかの武将たちと交流して信頼度を上げることで戦場で連携しやすくなったり能力経験値をもらえたり彼らに特技の心得を教えてもらえたりする。交流を重ねていくうちに能力はみるみる上がり、最初は貧弱だった能力もいずれはムキムキになっていることだろう。加えて一緒に交流した武将にも経験値が入っていて能力がアップしたり、定期的に起こる交流イベントで特技を覚えたりするので交流そのものが勢力そのものの強化につながることになる。

[h3]子供が作れる[/h3]
結婚用の演義伝を進めるか独身の異性武将と交流し仲良くなると結婚できるのだが、結婚した後その配偶者の元に何度か交流しに行くと、[b]いかにもな演出があって[/b]子供を授かることがある。子供が生まれると自分で名前を付けることができて、1年に1回子育てイベントが発生し15年後に成人する。[strike]正直15年もあれば元服するよりも早くクリアしてしまうのでアレなのだが、[/strike]子供には愛着がわくし、史実武将でプレイして架空子供を作って、その架空子供をオリジナル武将で制作して別のシナリオを遊ぶという二毛作プレイが非常にはかどる(たとえば筆者は反董卓連合軍シナリオの張遼で一度クリアして、その架空子供で合肥の戦いシナリオを遊んだ)。

[h3]戦闘が面白い[/h3]
三國志11のような完全ターン制の戦闘であり、じっくり考えながらのプレイができてとても面白い。BGMも良く、特に中原の合戦BGMがお気に入り。
今作は部隊の兵数がその部隊の戦闘力に直結しているため、そこそこ以上の能力を持った敵将が1万を越える大兵力を率いていると物理攻撃に対する反撃ダメージだけで1/3くらい削られてしまう。そのため軍略戦法を中心とした反撃を受けない戦法が非常に重要で、こちらの武将の質や兵力が劣っている場合でも軍略戦法を連打するだけで安全に攻撃できる。
11も14も設置物の火罠や火球は強かったが計略としての火計は正直言って弱く、周瑜や陸遜といった火関連の個性を持っている武将でもない限り使い道はほとんどなかったが、今作の火計(烈火)はとんでもないほど強いのでその武将が烈火を覚えているかいないかでだいぶ変わってくる。
また、軍略戦法は強力な代わり発動できる地形に制限があるのだが、そういう点でも烈火は非常に強力で、岩山や砂地・湿地以外のほとんどの地形で着火可能かつ雨の日でも関係なく使えるし火もなかなか消えない。毎ターン炎上ダメージと気力減少効果があり、加えて燃えている地形にはZOCが発生するのでマップを火の海にして制圧する動きが非常に強い。
敵側に軍略戦法を使われず自分は使えるような地形に位置取ることが重要であり、そこも面白い点だと思った。


[h2]◇よくない点[/h2]

[h3]在野・放浪軍プレイが結局のところ一般武将・君主プレイの大幅劣化でしかない[/h3]
放浪軍は滅ぼされず自由に拠点を移せる代わりに収入やコマンドに大幅な制限のある君主プレイでしかないし、在野に至ってはその町々にいる適当な武将に一騎打ちや舌戦を吹っ掛けるしか本当にやることがない。放浪軍は[b]自発的に[/b]勢力同士の戦争に介入する義勇軍プレイや金銭で雇われて援軍に行く傭兵プレイ、街で略奪したりする盗賊団プレイ、在野は太閤立志伝の様に商人や医者・暗殺者のようないろいろなロールプレイができるようになればもっと遊びの幅が広がると思う。

[h3]都市コマンドが空気[/h3]
街で見聞すると民心が上昇し、民心の合計値がトリガーとなるイベントがあったり、内政コマンドの効果が上昇したり在野や旅人の情報を教えてくれたり100になると友好の証をもらえたりするのだが、任務ノルマのある一般武将だったり在野の多い序盤はともかく、中盤以降や太守や君主だと見聞コマンドを実行するメリットがほとんどない。在野プレイだと本当に意味がない。たしかに100になった時に貰える友好の証は貴重品で有用なアイテムだが、チュートリアルで5個くらい貰えるしたまに店に売ってたりするのでわざわざ行動力200も使うくらいなら[b]その行動力で他の武将に10回稽古を挑んだ方が良い[/b]。
せめて民心を上げる過程や上げ切ったあとにお金や兵糧・特技の心得・名品などを定期的にもらえたり、兵糧収入や徴兵時に色々メリットがあるなどがあれば上げる意味も出てくると思う。
同様に酒屋での請負も消費する行動力(50か100)に対して得られる金や名声が少なすぎる。チュートリアルで「名声を上げるためにはまずは酒屋で請負をするのがおすすめ！」と言われるが適当な武将に一騎打ち・舌戦をした方が経験値も貰えるし一石二鳥である。

[h3]プレイヤーの所属している拠点だけ保守的すぎる[/h3]
同じ勢力内でもNPCのみで管理されている拠点は積極的に攻撃を仕掛けるようになったが、プレイヤーが一般武将や軍師で所属してる拠点だけ異常に保守的で一切攻撃を仕掛けようとしない。
結局プレイヤーが特権を使って侵攻を提案するまで動かないことがほとんどなので「今回こそは一般武将プレイに徹するぞ」と思ってプレイしていても毎回同じ展開になってしまう。
また、NPCはしょっちゅう異動を行うのにもかかわらず、プレイヤーがいくら優秀な武将であってもNPC君主は異動をしてくれない。そのため自分が後方都市にいる場合、自分から異動を申し出ない限り一生前線に呼ばれないのもマイナスポイント。

[h3]部隊編成がめんどくさい[/h3]
部隊編成がめんどくさく、合戦より時間がかかることも。
一応一括設定機能もあることにはあるが、兵科に関しては個別に設定することが多く、毎回最大10部隊をそれぞれ個別に設定して副将も特技や相性を見ながら個別に設定して援軍も個別に設定して～を繰り返していると非常にかったるくて仕方がない。メンバーや兵科、兵器や艦船の種類はプリセットとして保存できるようにして欲しい。

[h3]人間ドラマが希薄[/h3]
武将と仲良くなって発生する友好イベントはせいぜい5種類程度しかなく、関羽や諸葛亮といった超有名武将相手でもそれらの汎用イベントしか起きないため、酒を飲まないかと誘ってくる諸葛亮や狩りに行かないかと誘ってくる貂蝉などキャラ崩壊のような状況になる。せめて三国志の主役級の武将にはそれぞれオリジナルのイベントがあっても良いのではないかと思った。
友好イベントは毎月のように発生するため、めんどくさくてスキップしようとしても妙な暗転硬直がありそれもプレイの快適度を下げている。
また史実や演義には派閥争いや跡目争い、功績に対する妬み嫉みや宴会などでの些細な諍いからの讒言・暗殺・降格・左遷などがあったが今作にはそういう人間ドラマが一切ない。演義伝でどちらの派閥につくかとか、負けた派閥が反乱を起こして独立勢力になるとかそういうのがあればもっと深みが増したと思う。
また、敵勢力の武将とも交流できるのだがその恩恵は引き抜きの際に有利になったり後述する相克予防程度に恩恵しかなく、例えば合戦後や勢力を滅ぼした後に仲の良い武将に対する助命嘆願ができたり、13にもあった外交時の口添えなどもう少しその辺りを作り込んでも良かったのではないかと思った。(そもそも敵対勢力の武将や君主が敵の都市にすんなり入り込めるのもおかしな話なのだが)

[h3]相克がめんどくさすぎる[/h3]
戦場においてプレイヤーと能力が近しく、好感度が好意未満の武将に対して攻撃すると相克関係になることがある。相克になるとこちら側は相手を一切捕縛できず、合戦開始時に相手だけ気力がいきなりMaxになる。この、[b]いきなり問答無用で相克関係になること[/b]、[b]捕縛が一切できないこと[/b]がとてつもなくダルい。相克の解除手段がほとんどないのも問題。
先述した人間ドラマが希薄というところにも関連するが、戦場で相見えただけで嫌われるのが本当に意味が分からないし、この仕様にOKを出した人を小一時間問い詰めたい。せめて相生関係が4つの段階を踏むように相克関係も4段階を踏むようにして、同一武将に複数回撃破されたり、戦場において一騎打ちで負けたり、相克とは別にある仇敵関係と統合して相生関係の武将や親族を撃破されたり討ち取られたりしたときに発生するなどすればドラマがあって良いと思った。また、相克の相手との個別イベントなどあればまだ許せたかもしれないがそういうのも一切ない。せめて所属勢力が滅亡した時にだけは捕縛できるようにして斬首するか選べるようにするべきだ。

[h3]複数の子供が作りづらい[/h3]
今作は11や14と異なり、男性武将は重婚して3人まで妻を持てる。そこは当時の価値観らしくて大変結構なのだが、一方で子供は1人目を作るとその子供が15歳になって元服するまで2人目を作ることができない。つまり1人目を作ると2人目を作るためには15～6年待たなければならないし、3人目は約30年後になる。女性側は51歳になると子供が産めなくなってしまうこともあり、現実的に見て作れる子供は2人が限界。
配偶者が3人いればそれぞれに1人ずつ産ませて3人は作れるが、1人しか愛さない純愛プレイだとひとりっ子になってしまいがち。曹操や司馬懿のような子だくさん家庭にはどうあがいてもなれないのは非常に寂しい。

[h3]NPC側は人間関係を新たに構築しない[/h3]
プレイヤーは交流しまくることでいろんな人間関係を構築することができるが、NPC側は新たに人間関係を構築することはない。11や14の親愛は今作の相生に比べて軽率に設定されていたためNPC同士でも容易に連携が発生したが、今作はかなり数が絞られているため戦場においてNPC同士はほぼ連携しない。
プレイヤー側がNPCに対して交流や義兄弟や婚姻の仲介をできるようにして欲しい。たとえば今のところ空気な宴会コマンドを使うとそこに呼ばれた武将同士で仲良くなったり喧嘩したりするようになれば面白いと思う。

[h2]◇結論[/h2]
史実武将でプレイした初回とその架空娘息子でプレイした2回目までは結構楽しめたのだが、在野プレイや放浪軍プレイに手を出した途端急に飽きが来た。太閤立志伝のようなプレイ体験を求めていたのだが、結局どの遊び方をしても君主プレイの劣化でしかないというのが良くない。
合戦はめちゃくちゃ面白いが、そもそも軍権がない立場だと保守的なAIのせいでその合戦にたどり着けないし、かといって合戦以外の部分は作り込まれていないしでどっちに重きを置きたいのかよくわからないどっちつかずの印象。セール価格6,500円だと許せるが、これを10,800円で買おうとはとても思わない。

Drawful 2 is a chaotic, hilarious, and deeply social experience that embodies the unpredictable charm that Jackbox Games has become known for. Building upon the concept introduced in the original Drawful, it takes the simple act of doodling and guessing and turns it into a fast-paced showcase of creativity, confusion, and comedy. The core idea is beautifully straightforward: each player, using their phone or tablet, receives a strange or absurd prompt and must attempt to draw it. The rest of the group then tries to guess what the original phrase was, crafting their own fake answers to mislead others. What unfolds is a wild blend of unintentional artistry and shared laughter, where every terrible sketch and ridiculous guess becomes part of the fun. The brilliance of Drawful 2 lies in how it uses simplicity as its foundation—anyone can play, regardless of drawing skill—and transforms it into an endlessly entertaining social event.

Jackbox Games refined several aspects of the original formula in this sequel without overcomplicating the experience. One of the most noticeable improvements is the addition of a second color, which might sound minor but adds a new layer of expressiveness to the chaotic sketches. There’s also a significantly larger pool of prompts, helping to keep rounds fresh even after multiple play sessions. Perhaps the most impactful new feature is the custom prompt creator, which allows players to invent their own inside jokes and absurd phrases. This feature elevates Drawful 2 from being just another party game to becoming a creative canvas for personalized humor. It makes the game infinitely replayable since players can adapt it to any crowd or occasion, from family gatherings to online streams filled with viewers submitting their own bizarre ideas.

Technically, Drawful 2 remains accessible and user-friendly, with the familiar Jackbox setup that allows players to connect via a web browser without needing additional hardware or controllers. Its presentation retains the studio’s quirky hand-drawn art style and lighthearted music, both of which contribute to a relaxed, inviting atmosphere. The interface is intuitive, and rounds move briskly enough to keep energy levels high. However, like most Jackbox titles, the experience depends heavily on context. Drawful 2 thrives in social settings—either in person or online with a streaming audience—and loses much of its appeal when played alone or with a very small group. The joy doesn’t come from competition but from the absurd situations that emerge organically as players misinterpret drawings and embrace the game’s lack of precision. In fact, the more terrible the art, the better the laughs.

Despite its comedic strengths, Drawful 2 isn’t immune to repetition. After several sessions, even the expanded prompt list can start to feel familiar, and the novelty relies heavily on player creativity. While the custom prompts help offset this, they also demand active participation and a playful mood from the group to maintain momentum. Technically, the drawing tools are serviceable but intentionally limited, maintaining the clumsy charm that defines the series. Still, some players may find the small color palette and lack of precision a bit frustrating, especially if they expect more polished drawing options. Yet this design choice is deliberate—it ensures that everyone, regardless of skill, operates on the same comedic level. In Drawful 2, perfection isn’t the goal; hilarity is.

In terms of value, Drawful 2 occupies a unique space in the Jackbox catalog. It’s sold as a standalone title rather than as part of a larger party pack, which makes it a low-cost, high-reward option for players who want quick and easy fun. However, those who already own the original Drawful or any of the Jackbox Party Packs that include it may find the improvements relatively incremental. The core gameplay hasn’t evolved dramatically, and the sequel functions more as a refined version than a full reinvention. That said, its affordable price point, customizable content, and universal accessibility make it an appealing choice for newcomers and party hosts looking for a guaranteed crowd-pleaser.

Ultimately, Drawful 2 succeeds not because of technological innovation or deep gameplay mechanics, but because it celebrates human imperfection and group humor. It captures the spontaneous joy of friends laughing together at their own bad drawings and terrible guesses, creating moments that linger long after the game ends. Few digital experiences replicate the same level of communal absurdity and shared creativity. It’s a reminder that games don’t need to be complex to be unforgettable—they just need to bring people together in the right spirit. Drawful 2 stands as one of Jackbox’s purest and most enduring examples of that philosophy: a messy, unpredictable, and endlessly enjoyable party game that thrives on laughter above all else.

[h1]Sh*t Souls II – O Pior L1xo Já Criado[/h1]

Primeiramente, se você é fã disso aqui, talvez precise de um psiquiatra. Isso não é amor pelo jogo, é síndrome de Estocolmo disfarçada de nostalgia. Agora, vamos falar sobre essa aberração. Se você pensa em jogar essa coisa esperando um teste de habilidade, paciência e diversão, parabéns: vai encontrar exatamente o oposto. O jogo é inimigo do lazer, nêmesis da criatividade e campeão em ser o pior Souls que já joguei. Tudo aqui parece feito com preguiça, e o resultado é uma experiência que confunde dificuldade com caos, transformando-se em uma completa tortura.

[h3]Design de mapa[/h3]

A ambientação é um mosaico de ideias jogadas no liquidificador. Cada área parece feita por uma equipe diferente que nunca conversou entre si: conexões geográficas sem sentido, elevadores que desafiam a gravidade e castelos vazios, com mais eco do que mobília, mesmo sendo habitados (aparentemente, a rainha da COBIÇA e o rei vivem de bolsa família). Os atalhos são mal planejados e as bonfires ficam em lugares sem sentido. O level design é um desastre monumental, com corredores infinitos, salas genéricas, becos sem saída em excesso e backtracking forçado só para inflar horas de jogo.

[h3]Combate[/h3]

O combate, que deveria ser o ponto alto, aqui é um festival de inconsistências. Animações quebrando, golpes que às vezes acertam e às vezes não, i-frames que transformam rolamentos em sorteios. Inimigos entram em super armor aleatoriamente, dano às vezes chega antes da animação e combos que deveriam matar mas que, milagrosamente deixam o mob com 1 de vida. É impossível lutar com confiança quando o próprio jogo parece conspirar contra as leis do próprio mundo.

[h3]Bosses medíocres[/h3]

Os chefes são versões recicladas de inimigos comuns, as arenas são minúsculas, cheias de mobs e uma hitbox mentirosa. Muitos têm mais HP do que mecânica, e as batalhas se resumem a repetir três ataques previsíveis. O verdadeiro desafio aqui é o tédio, e ele sempre vence. A sensação de vitória é substituída por alívio de nunca mais precisar ver aquela desgr4ça.

[h3]Inimigos e IA[/h3]

Sh*t Souls II acredita que dificuldade = quantidade. Cada zona é um zoológico lotado de mobs que te atacam em bando, flanqueiam em corredores minúsculos e te detectam através das paredes. Outros disparam flechas e magias que fazem curva para te acertar atrás de coberturas e, às vezes, até atravessam paredes. Mas, caso você tente enfrentá-los juntos, vai virar alvo de um exército: se tentar bater em um, outro irá te interromper; se correr para curar, eles pulam na sua cabeça; se tentar atacar enquanto estão parados te olhando, eles aceleram o golpe. O mesmo vale para os arqueiros, que disparam muito mais rápido que você. Aqui, você só sobrevive por sorte, nunca por habilidade. Ah, e ainda há o alcance do aggro: você pode atravessar o mapa correndo e ainda terá um filho da put# te perseguindo. Mas, o melhor de tudo é quando você tenta fugir e os inimigos viram o flash. Se você tiver um mínimo de QI, vai perceber que é muito mais conveniente ignorar tudo e rushar até os bosses, que, ironicamente, costumam ser ridiculamente fáceis.

[h3]Sistema de Combate[/h3]

Já vamos começar pelo pior: a stamina, que consome mais rápido do que paciência em fila de banco e se regenera na velocidade de um idoso subindo escada. É algo tão ridículo que, se um mob decidir te combar com pelo menos quatro ataques, você não vai conseguir revidar. Outro ponto terrível é a adaptability: é praticamente obrigatório se não quiser um jogo lento e frustrante, seja pela quantidade miserável de frames no dodge ou pela velocidade patética ao usar o Estus. E também tem o status de poison, que é ridiculamente forte, chegando ao ponto de permitir que você infecte o boss e passe a luta correndo enquanto ele morre de c4ncer.

[h3]Itens, cura e durabilidade[/h3]

O Estus é MUITO lento, mesmo com agility alta, o personagem bebe mais devagar que um monge em retiro espiritual. Nem faz sentido usá-lo, já que há uma infinidade de itens de cura em abundância e muito mais eficientes. As armas quebram com uma frequência irritante, especialmente quando há múltiplos inimigos, e o dano de queda é completamente aleatório. Às vezes você morre caindo de um degrau, outras vezes pula de um penhasco e sai ileso.

[h3]Hitboxes e colisões[/h3]

As hitboxes daqui são tão largas que parecem incluir o ar ao redor do personagem. Bosses como Fume Knight e Lud & Zallen transformam cada golpe em uma ameaça de proporções cósmicas: você apanha mesmo estando em outro CEP. E, frequentemente, as armas colidem nas paredes, ou melhor, as SUAS armas colidem nas paredes, porque as dos inimigos parecem atravessar a matéria.

[h3]NPCs e quests[/h3]

As quests continuam sem sentido como sempre, mas há o bônus de algumas terem requisitos chatinhos, como o fato de você não conseguir certas roupas herdadas apenas porque não invocou o queridão para um combate três vezes. Em outras palavras, você é obrigado a chamar um NPC para te ajudar se quiser platinar o jogo. Nada disso é explicado em lugar algum; não há pistas nem detalhes sobre isso. Parece até que foi feito para forçar o jogador a pesquisar guias externos. Orçamento, aparentemente, estava em falta.

[h3]Polimento e trilha sonora[/h3]

O jogo dá claros sinais de pressa no desenvolvimento: quedas de FPS do nada, texturas piscando, mapa de lava parecendo um benchmark de CPU. Também há microtravamentos após trocar de janela, inimigos aparecendo com atraso e bugs por todos os lados. O som é outro desastre; várias áreas simplesmente não têm trilha alguma, e quando têm, são faixas recicladas de DS 1.

[h3]Ideias boas, execução desastrosa[/h3]

O jogo tenta enfiar dezenas de mecânicas como counter damage, back attack, power stance, weapon scaling, sweet spots, entre várias outras, mas sem qualquer integração ou explicação decente, e quase não há momentos apropriados para usar a maioria, ou as vezes apenas não funcionam de forma consistente. No fim, é mais fácil ficar parado spammando ataque em um ponto cego dos mobs.

[h3]Problemas diversos[/h3]

Falta orientação e lógica nas mecânicas. Um ótimo exemplo é o moinho, que não dá o menor indício de que precisa ser incendiado para desativar o veneno da Mytha; as portas que você encontra no começo, mas que só serão abertas muito tempo depois; a falta de avisos sobre como melhorar a cura; entre vários outros detalhes jogados ao acaso. Há itens que podem ser perdidos caso caiam na lava, runbacks absurdamente longos, ausência de i-frame nas fog walls, e spam de emboscadas que seriam toleráveis em pequenas doses, mas que aparecem a cada cinco metros. E o farm de covenants continua sendo uma tortura para quem quer platinar, feito apenas para inflar tempo de jogo.

[h3]Conclusão[/h3]

Já deu pra entender que o game é falho em praticamente tudo o que faz, né? Ele apresenta vislumbres de algo que poderia ter sido incrível, mas tudo se perdeu em um mar de falhas técnicas, mecânicas desastrosas e escolhas de design que preferem inflar conteúdo e criar dificuldades artificiais, em vez de construir desafios memoráveis. O resultado é uma paródia do próprio gênero que ajudou a consagrar: um jogo que pune o jogador não por falta de habilidade, mas por suas próprias inconsistências, bugs e decisões preguiçosas. Se pensa em comprar esperando algo à altura dos outros Souls, esqueça. Isso aqui não é difícil; é chato, tedioso, inconsistente, desrespeitoso e entorpecente. Um jogo que suga a alma e o prazer. Mas, se quiser experimentar o abismo da frustração e entender o verdadeiro significado de sofrimento, bem-vindo a Sh*t Souls II.

Tragiczna gra, optymalizacji NIE MA, pomimo mocnego sprzętu gra nie działa mi w przynajmniej 60 FPS na ustawieniach niskich, sam gameplay również do kitu, nic się nie dzieje, jedyne co to jakieś beznadziejnie zrobione akcje typu napad w nocy które po prostu są jednym zdjęciem i opisem, nie da się tego ,,obronić", zresztą gdzie jest jakiś poziom trudności? powinien być jakiś łatwy (brak napadów, klienci wpłacają dużo, kredyty są duże i bardziej opłacalne) i trudny, w którym są napady na bank (ale jakieś ciekawe, nie jak te aktualne), klienci wbłacają mało i wypłacają dużo, a kredyty są mniejsze. [quote=Giant Sparrow] В конечном счете, это игра о том, насколько мал и незначителен человек в сравнении с окружающим его бескрайним и непостижимым миром.[/quote]
Если вы, как и я, цените в играх не столько сложность геймплея, сколько хорошую режиссуру и глубокую историю, то What Remains of Edith Finch - это тот проект, который нельзя пропускать. Это не просто игра, а настоящее интерактивное кино, которое оставляет после себя долгое и светлое послевкусие.
В своей жизни я не раз оказывался в шаге от того, чтобы стать калекой или вовсе умереть. Я как сейчас помню тот день, когда гулял внизу, а мои друзья с балкона многоэтажки решили, что кинуть огромный булыжник - это отличная идея. Он упал в сантиметрах от меня.
И я прекрасно знаю, что сказал бы на это тот самый прагматик, мудрец из безопасного кресла: "Сам виноват. Не надо было там стоять. Техника безопасности написана кровью". Именно такие люди пишут потом рецензии, где вся трагедия семьи сводится к "Премии Дарвина", а человеческая драма - к вердикту "сами виноваты".
Слышите? Холодно, просто и абсолютно бессмысленно перед лицом реальной, чудовищной случайности. Это мог быть булыжник. Или черепаха, упавшая с неба. Или качели, улетевшие за горизонт.
Легко быть мудрецом постфактум, сидя в безопасном кресле и выстраивая логические цепочки, которые привели к трагедии. Человеческий разум жаждет порядка; в конце концов, величайшие умы вроде Эйнштейна посвящали жизнь поиску закономерностей в хаосе вселенной. Но делает ли наша способность к ретроспективному анализу нас умнее или мудрее тех "дурачков", что пренебрегли правилами техники безопасности? Даёт ли она нам самим гарантию, что завтра мы не погибнем от другого, не менее "глупого" поступка?
И что самое поразительное, игра показывает, что самый суровый мудрец сидит не в нашем кресле, а в головах самих выживших Финчей. Мы постоянно слышим это мучительное "если бы...". [spoiler]"Если бы я тогда не подзадорил Кельвина с качелями, он был бы жив". "Если бы я не отвлеклась на тот телефонный звонок...".[/spoiler] Это отчаянная попытка найти в хаосе трагедии тот самый переключатель, который можно было бы щелкнуть иначе. Признать, что смерть была чистой, бессмысленной случайностью, - невыносимо. Гораздо "проще" взвалить на себя бремя вины, ведь вина, в отличие от хаоса, предполагает причину и следствие. Она создает иллюзию, что миром можно было управлять.
Мне могут возразить: "Нужно просто свести риски к минимуму!". Безусловно. Но до какого предела? Правил техники безопасности можно написать бесконечное множество. "Не гуляй под балконами, с которых могут кинуть камень". "Не стой под орлами, если у тебя лысая голова". Каждый новый пункт этого бесконечного списка лишь подтверждает, что ты не стал умнее тех, кто погиб, - ты просто знаешь на одну историю больше. Так где же та грань, за которой осторожность превращается в паранойю, а оправданный риск - в "смерть по глупости"?". Почему падение булыжника - это "трагическая случайность", а полет на качелях - "детское безрассудство"?
Именно здесь вся логика рушится, потому что она основана на ложной предпосылке, будто существует некий "безопасный" режим по умолчанию, от которого Финчи по своей глупости отклонялись. Но такого режима нет. Жить - в принципе опасно. Каждый шаг - это риск.
[spoiler]Может, нужно было поступить как Уолтер, один из самих Финчей? Запереться в подвале на десятилетия, чтобы спрятаться от мира и его опасностей. Он попытался включить тот самый "безопасный режим". Там, вроде бы, сложнее умереть. Но разве это была жизнь? И разве это его спасло?[/spoiler] Сама игра наглядно демонстрирует, что путь тотального избегания риска - это просто другая форма смерти. Так где же он, этот мифический гайд о том, как умереть "не нелепо"?
История знает и другие примеры. Взять хотя бы Эсхила - великого древнегреческого драматурга, отца трагедии, мудреца своего времени. По легенде, он погиб, когда орёл, приняв его лысую голову за камень, сбросил на неё черепаху, чтобы расколоть панцирь.
Была ли смерть человека, подарившего миру "Прометея Прикованного", глупой? Нелепой? Или она лишь подчёркивает, что перед лицом рока, случая и абсурдности бытия мы все равны - и великий поэт, [spoiler]и мальчик на качелях?[/spoiler] Если уж мудрость и величие не могут защитить от падающей с неба черепахи, то какое право мы имеем судить Финчей за их мечты и порывы?
Именно здесь мне могут возразить: "Постойте! Смерть Эсхила - это уникальная, абсурдная случайность, а [spoiler]гибель младенца Грегори в ванной[/spoiler] - это предсказуемый результат безрассудства! Из истории Эсхила мы вынесли лишь забавный урок о том, что не стоит гулять под орлами с лысой головой. А правило [spoiler]'не оставляй младенца в воде без присмотра'[/spoiler] известно всем".
Легко повесить холодный ярлык: "преступная халатность". Но давайте доведем эту логику до абсурда. [spoiler]Наверное, мать специально хотела, чтобы её ребёнок утонул? Конечно же, нет.[/spoiler] За этим ярлыком стоит обычная человеческая ошибка, секундная потеря концентрации, [spoiler]тот самый роковой телефонный звонок, который мог случиться с каждым.[/spoiler] И что в итоге случайнее: черепаха, брошенная орлом, [spoiler]или этот звонок, раздавшийся в одну-единственную, фатальную минуту?[/spoiler] Разница лишь в том, что во втором случае нам проще найти "виноватого" и успокоить себя мыслью: "Уж я бы так не поступил". Эта иллюзия контроля и превосходства защищает нас от страшной правды: мы так же уязвимы. Она позволяет нам жить внутри уютного афоризма Бродского, повторяя про себя: "Смерть - это то, что бывает с другими".
Гениальность What Remains of Edith Finch в том, что она не позволяет нам быть сторонними судьями. Она помещает нас прямо в сознание своих героев. Мы не смотрим, как они умирают, - мы переживаем их последние мгновения. Мы чувствуем восторг, страх, уход в фантазию. И в этот момент вопрос о "технике безопасности" становится бессмысленным и даже кощунственным. [spoiler]Мы не просто видим качели над обрывом - мы чувствуем восторг полета. Мы не просто видим ребенка в ванне - мы погружаемся в его мир, где игрушки оживают.[/spoiler] Игра заменяет осуждение сопереживанием.
Игра не рассказывает о семейном проклятии. Она говорит о "проклятии" самой жизни - её хрупкости, её непредсказуемости. О том, что каждый наш шаг, каждая мечта несет в себе долю риска. Финчи не были глупцами. Они просто жили, и жили на полную катушку, не прячась от мира в стерильный кокон. Их дом - нелепый, растущий вверх, нарушающий все правила - это и есть метафора их жизни: опасной, непрактичной, но невероятно живой и полной историй.
Для меня эта игра стала не просто историей, а утверждением. Утверждением того, что нет "правильных" и "неправильных" жизней и смертей. Есть только истории, каждая из которых заслуживает того, чтобы её рассказали с сочувствием и уважением. Это игра, которая не судит, а обнимает, утверждая фундаментальную правду о нашем собственном хрупком, прекрасном и, возможно, нелепом - в самом высоком смысле этого слова - существовании.

This is... this is Rimworld. I don't mean "this reminds me of Rimworld" or "this is a similar sort of experience to Rimworld", it's the same game with nicer graphics and some features left off. It feels weird to give a thumbs down to a game I've put over 100 hours into, but my honest review is "Go play Rimworld instead." If you love that game, you sadly won't find anything new here. If you've never played it, you're better off experiencing the original.
I guess if Rimworld's low-fi graphics were bugging you, or maybe you thought its gameplay was a bit too detailed, this game is probably for you. For my money, I find myself missing a number of Rimworld's features and in-depth management, and my NES-era brain stopped being impressed by shiny graphics upgrades a long time ago.

I don’t think this game is abandoned — it’s finished! Maybe in the future this hidden gem will shine, but right now it’s not the next RimWorld. I mean, it has a community and some great mods, but it’s not on the Minecraft level of popularity.

I think anyone who likes survival and management games will love this game. This game is like another flavor of the same recipe — and I don’t mean that everything is just like RimWorld but in 3D; it has its own charm! Saying that this game is just a RimWorld clone is like saying every game with crafting is a Minecraft clone.

I don’t think the game is abandoned; I think it’s finished. Maybe it will shine in the future, but as with everything in capitalism, what dictates what happens next is money. This game wasn’t made by one passionate guy — it was made by a small passionate studio. Still, it’s a studio; everyone needs money to pay their bills.

If you like this genre — colony-sim, survival, sandbox — you’ll like this game. Give it a chance!

I've had over 1,000 hours on this game, and it's safe to say that I'm pretty done with this game. At first, the game is a dream for bus nerds and those that want to recreate the routes in their city. However, this quickly changes with the significant game performance drops that take hold very quickly after you've made a couple routes. I have 32GB of RAM, even opting to utilise my SSD instead of my HDD drive to boost game performance. Yet just calculating making a route takes about half my day. Lag spikes are constant for no apparent reason, and I've constantly having 95%+ of my RAM and 90%+ of my disk space being used up from this one game alone. This is one of the most ridiculous I've ever witnessed in my entire life. Not even triple A games on highest graphic settings can turn my setup into a potato. 

The cherry on top? The painstaking, heart-breaking, blood pressure inducing crashes that has ultimately drove me to the very end of this game. I've seriously considered giving this game a pause in the past, considering how long everything takes to load, from the save itself, to making routes or changing schedules. I have given this game every ounce of patience and time, yet nothing significant is made regarding the performance issues. The latest crash, and a loss of over 2 days of progress has really put the end to this. The auto-save feature? Useless. It makes the game even more unplayable with the long pauses and "CBM.exe has stopped responding" messages that pops up every time it conducts one. Had it not taken so long to save/load, I wouldn't really mind much, but the fact that it does renders every bit of joy off the table for game. 

Normally, I never rant or write reviews like this, but this game has seriously taken a toll on me. Don't get me wrong, I love every aspect behind this game. The concept itself is amazing, one of the first on the market, but the performance issues that comes with it is atrocious. Developers if you ever see or acknowledge this, please for the love of God focus on solely making this game more playable, instead of adding new features or DLCs for the sake of profit. There is no point to add those to the game, when the game itself is not even playable (see crashes, lag spikes, long loading times, and specs being pushed to the max !) 

Until then, I think it's time for me to put this aside. 1,400 hours on this has been a true test of resilience on my end, and I'm afraid that I cannot continue any further like this.

Le cinquième épisode ne m'ayant pas pleinement convaincu, il me fallait une nouvelle dose de Gears of War. Par chance, j'avais choppé Gears Tactics en même temps que l'autre épisode.
Toutefois, je dois bien avouer que je n'ai moi-même pas trop compris pourquoi j'ai aussi acquis le titre dont il est question ici tant le genre tactique, celui avec des probas, m'a été rédhibitoire jusque-là. Je déteste XCOM 2, pourtant considéré par beaucoup comme le modèle du genre, le trouvant beaucoup trop aléatoire, punitif pour rien. Bref, tout ça pour dire deux choses : que les rares jeux tactiques que j'apprécie sont ceux qui nous laissent avec toutes les cartes en main, qui ne nous prennent pas bêtement en traitre d'une part, et que je ne pourrais pas rédiger cette critique sans comparer Gears Tactics à XCOM 2, vu que c'est le titre dont il se rapproche le plus, qu'il s'agit du modèle du genre, et qu'il s'agit du seul que j'ai sous la main de toute façon.
Malgré tout, et quitte à commencer la comparaison de suite, je trouve Gears Tactics bien plus intelligent que son concurrent sur bien des aspects. Outre le fait qu'il n'emploie pas de vils stratagèmes en minant ses arènes de « dalles piégées » qui alertent aussitôt l'ennemi, il se montre aussi bien plus souple avec le joueur. Outre le nombre de points d'action qui passe de 2 à 3, la possibilité de se mouvoir après avoir tiré, le titre de Splash Damage inclut surtout une idée géniale en plus d'être totalement raccord avec la philosophie de la licence : celle de faire regagner un point d'action à tous les membres de notre escouade pour chaque exécution effectuée. Sah quel plaisir de se retrouver acculé, mais d'arriver à grappiller mètre après mètre, exécution après exécution, du terrain, et d'arriver à éliminer la totalité des locustes qui étaient sur le point de mettre fin à nos jours à la fin du tour précédent. Moins limité qu'un XCOM, Gears Tactics arrive à présenter au joueur des séquences grisantes grâce à une ouverture que son concurrent ne possède pas. Le jeu n'a pas à être joué d'une façon bien précise et, contrairement au titre de Firaxis, il faut parfois utiliser son cerveau.
Le titre excelle dans son équilibre défense/attaque, entre les exécutions d'une part, certes, mais aussi grâce aux vigilances, capacités disponibles par défaut qui pousseront nos unités à tirer automatiquement sur les ennemis passant dans leur cône de vision lors du tour suivant. Chacune des cinq classes du titre possède quatre arbres de compétences différents, quatre sous-classes, tous plus ou moins orientés vers un style de jeu particulier. La classe unité lourde peut par exemple s'orienter défense, avec des compétences passives pour le mode vigilance et la possibilité d'entraver l'ennemi ; s'orienter démolition, en privilégiant les dégâts de zone ; s'orienter artillerie pour maraver un ennemi spécifique avec des coups critiques ou vider le chargeur sur lui ; ou encore privilégier le mouvement en s'orientant vers la sous-classe spécialiste. Encore une fois, le titre se veut plus ouvert qu'un XCOM qui ne proposait qu'un simple choix binaire par niveau acquis : on peut très bien choper quelques compétences qui nous intéressent sur un arbre donné, puis partir dans une autre direction.
Enfin, Gears Tactics ne jurent pas avec les autres épisodes de la licence malgré le genre diamétralement opposé. On retrouve une direction artistique proche des deux premiers épisodes de la série, un Unreal Engine 4 qui a très bien vieilli, ainsi que des cartes qui pourraient limite être intégrés dans un format TPS. Force est de constater que tout a été fait pour se montrer le plus respectueux possible des deux premiers épisodes de la série, de l'univers conçu par Epic Games.

Malheureusement, en termes de structure, Gears Tactics enchaîne les erreurs, les mauvais choix. Le premier truc con qu'on remarquera sera que la mort de l'un des personnages principaux équivaut à une défaite, et ce quelle que soit la mission, mais que nous pouvons engager à côté des recrues qui peuvent très bien crever à tout moment. Le problème, forcément, c'est que les héros seront indispensables lors de certaines missions, ce qui nous pousse à augmenter leur niveau en priorité. On se retrouve donc confronté à deux game design hétérogènes, l'un hérité de XCOM, l'autre de Gears of War, deux game design qui ne peuvent être miscibles. Autre détail con, de nouvelles recrues s'offriront très régulièrement à nous, mais avec le même niveau que nos unités avec le plus d'expériences. On se retrouvera donc régulièrement à faire le tri, à virer celles avec lesquelles nous n'avons jamais joué pour en recruter d'autres… avec lesquels nous ne jouerons pas non plus certes, mais vu qu'elles ont un meilleur niveau, autant ne pas se priver. Sans déconner, il n'y a qu'une seule unité « sacrifiable » que j'ai gardé tout le long du jeu : quand je le pouvais, je sélectionnais les héros. Gears Tactics aurait gagné à ne pas inclure de recrues pour nous proposer un nombre limité de héros, mais tous caractérisés et différents les uns des autres. Ç'aurait pu le différencier encore un peu plus d'un XCOM et ancrer davantage ce Tactics dans l'esprit de la licence, avec ses personnages identifiables.
Quoique je dise ça, mais les héros de ce Gears Tactics ne possèdent aucun charisme. C'est le vide, le néant. Gabe Diaz arrive à être encore moins mémorable que Kait, sa fille, héroïne du cinquième opus, alors qu'elle était déjà très oubliable. Sid se démarque un peu niveau apparence et c'est probablement le personnage dont on se souviendra le plus une fois le titre terminé, mais ça ne fera pas de lui un personnage mémorable pour autant. À cela, il faut ajouter la façon dont les différents héros nous rejoignent, c'est de pire en pire à chaque fois. On force le premier à rejoindre notre équipe en une minute chrono ; la deuxième passe en l'espace de deux lignes de dialogues de « Fachos ! » à « Ok, je vous rejoins » ; enfin, pour la dernière, ils ne se sont même plus faits chier puisqu'elle nous rejoint comme n'importe quel autre personnage secondaire nous rejoint lors des missions secondaires de sauvetage. Je serais limite tenté de croire que les développeurs ont abandonné leur jeu une fois arrivé à l'acte 3 tant il n'y a plus rien à découvrir une fois cette étape atteinte.
Pour revenir sur les problèmes de structure, il faut ajouter à ce que j'ai déjà évoqué plus haut des missions secondaires de remplissage qui reviendront régulièrement. La plupart du temps, ce sera effectuer deux missions secondaires sur trois proposées, et les Gears sélectionnés pour la première mission ne seront plus disponibles pour la seconde. Autant sur le papier ç'aurait pu apporter une certaine stratégie quant à l'utilisation de nos unités, autant concrètement ça n'a aucun intérêt vu qu'encore une fois on peut débloquer fréquemment de nouvelles recrues à niveau. De surcroit, les objectifs, ainsi que le level design des maps en question, sentiront très vite la redite. Bref, aucun intérêt si ce n'est grappiller de la durée de vie inutilement (déjà que la campagne principale le fait assez bien). Pourquoi ne pas avoir rendu ces missions secondaires optionnelles afin que le joueur se mette à niveau ou obtienne de l'équipement seulement si besoin est ?

This is a nifty little game. It's nothing amazing, the replayability is pretty low since it has no base building, no unique traits for soldiers, and limited random elements. It took me about 40 hours to complete the game and do a few achievements.

The story is pretty good, with the exception of a few cutscenes where the main characters suddenly become absolute dimwits in order for the plot to advance. The primary character is likeable, mostly competent, and I did get invested in his success as the world and our dear leaders kept screwing him over.

The mechanics are pretty good, with the exception of the fact that there are five classes and you are locked into the four main characters during the final battle, meaning that the Heavy class is entirely pointless, as learning how to use it well is a complete waste, which is sad because it’s one of the most interesting classes. There's also no reason to get attached to your soldiers, as you can just hire new and better ones.

If you liked Chaos Gate: Demonhunters, XCOM2, and other games of its genre this is a nice little 40 hour palette cleanser, but it could easily have been much more with minimal effort from the game designers. There’s an unlimited grind-fest-mode after you complete the campaign, but there’s no story, no choices, just the option to keep playing and grinding up characters for no reason except achievements.

Developers. I’d buy a DLC with a simple update to the Veteran mode, where you add a simple text based story to the missions. You don’t need voice actors, the frankly amazing cutscenes or anything like that. Just give me a story-reason to keep playing.

You could also simply create a New Game+ so I can actually use my already established characters, AND in this new campaign, I can actually use the damn Heavy in the final mission.

Now THIS is the peak point and click horror experience I've been wanting for so long. The pacing was slow while not being too grueling, the puzzles while convoluted at first glance make a lot of sense once you use your brain, and the story was really well put together, connecting both the trilogy and this game very nicely (while also sprinkling in some references to other scriptwelder works too).
I played this the first few hours it was out, and I will admit, the combat system was a bit jarring to add to a game like this, especially how it was at release. Not only that, but some of the abilities enemies have later in the game made some fights straight up impossible without grinding for an absurd amount of time. Fortunately, as any good game dev should, this was later fixed to not only be balanced, but also a new mode that puts WAY less emphasis on the combat and lets you take in the intended point and click nature of previous titles.
I haven't really taken my time to write out fully fleshed reviews for games before, but this one really outdid itself and I feel this should be standard for how games like this should be made.
I've been playing scriptwelder's games since middle school in the computer lab, and to see something that not only holds up to the quality of his previous games, but also giving off nostalgia to those glory days is honestly quite an experience that I heartily enjoyed!

In short, peak game. You should buy it if point and click horror is your thing. You won't regret it.

作为一位参与了playtest的玩家，我强烈推荐这款游戏；
优点：
1.唯一有联机功能的火车模拟游戏，可以当调度或者司机
2.真实度高，按照真实线路和列车打造，基本还原驾驶或调度
3.性价比比TSW高，打折100就可以买到400km路线
4.列车种类丰富，客运、货运、回送、工务......，可以体验3-4小时连续驾驶的火车，也有不到一小时的短途
5.随机事件多样，每一次驾驶都可能有不同的体验
缺点：
1.教程严重不足，每个车的教程时间基本都在半小时以上，真正有效的时间很短，而且教程只会教你最基础的操作，如何精准制动，撒沙......都没有（就像你学会了踩油门刹车打方向，现在你可以去跑WRC拉力赛了）
2.本地能玩的车次较少，大部分都在联机，同一种车次，有时想跑一趟完整的还要掐好时间或者碰运气
3.联机AI小概率会抽风，有一点小问题就会卡死，造成列车挤压；AI放行逻辑抽象，经常让货车压在客车前面，造成晚点，还有的时侯无缘无故把你放到侧线。
4.大部分玩的人都是波兰的，国人一般比较少，他们有不少人不会英文，语言沟通需要自备翻译器
5.游戏无存档功能，想要完整开一趟长途车需要你坐在电脑前面一个下午
6.官方更新慢，一年一大更，半年一小更
      总之，simrail虽然有许多缺点，但是瑕不掩瑜；从playtest到现在，这款游戏已经进步许多（更新太慢了！！），增加了许多功能，我从一开始对驾驶一窍不通到现在熟练驾驶各种列车，变成资深火车迷，中间经历了很长时间摸索，其中还有许多外国朋友的帮助，他们会对你说thanks，也会在会车时友好鸣笛。如果你想买这款游戏，可以先看看下面这个游戏wiki网站，里面有对游戏里铁路知识的详细讲解，希望对你有所帮助！
https://www.wiki.simrail.cz/%E4%B8%93%E9%A2%98%EF%BC%9A%E4%BB%8E%E9%9B%B6%E5%BC%80%E5%A7%8B%E7%90%86%E8%A7%A3SimRail#

不难看出本作并不是一款纯粹的弹幕躲避类游戏，本质上是花费点数点击技能树提升数值的割草游戏，游戏固然存在着不去升级数值就会卡关的问题，但是好在这一关要是过不了的话就回上一关刷几把随便点点技能树就能过关了，就像是咖啡因能给大脑带来兴奋一样，本作体量小且劲儿来的快，4个小时的流程恰到好处，在这4个小时里有着上瘾的快感循环。
本作主要的问题体现在游戏中后期也就是流程2个小时以后，敌人的数量和数值陡增，经常出现满屏都是敌人的弹幕，再加上各种地图机制限制玩家的走位空间让玩家的生存压力一下子大了很多，光是这一点的话还可以接受，主要问题是在上述敌人数量数量和弹幕很多的情况下，玩家控制的飞船本身很小并且不会显示受到伤害的判定点，实际判定点要比飞船小，点了移动技能以后经常一头撞到墙上撞死或者是因为满屏都是眼花缭乱的敌人玩家看不清自己控制的飞船在哪里，死都不知道怎么死的。
总的来说咖啡星矿工是一款爽感来得快散得也快的游戏，电子ED的时候拿来玩玩还是很不错的。

I have read some comments about play-ability, especially where it relates to movement with the keyboard and character speed. I cannot speak to the use of a keyboard, but I can confirm there is ZERO issue with movement or player speed/controls using a hand-held game controller. As an aside, character speed can be increased using the LT on the controller. Player stamina will increase if you eat cooked food.

In terms of overall play-ability of the game, I find it works fine, does not crash. There is a weird alpha layer glitching that occurs with the grass and water graphics most notable during the night, but that is strictly aesthetic and does not affect play.

My only real complaint with the game, and this is strictly a 'me' preference, is that I HATE all the mini-games. They wouldn't be so bad if they were optional and you could skip them, but they are not in many cases and are required to further the story often. I would rather these 'mini-games' were just incorporated into the storyline and the items they unlock were hidden in world or attached to a quest. Which ultimately they are, but the mini-games are required to trigger them. This one feature is so incredibly annoying as you move further into the game, that it is almost reason enough "for me" to just call it quits. But I am stubborn, so probably won't. 

Another feature I simply HATE is when you sleep at night. If you get a dream that is great as it is just an info dump and it will unlock a quest for a new object or animal; usually. However, when you do the dream lottery, which you're locked into playing, the wheel often lands on wolf and this tears up the farm every single time. If you change the dream to skip the wolf, you get a different annoying dream mini-game. No matter the case, you will wake up in the morning to find animals out of pens, and a ton of fencing broke, even if you didn't dream the wolf. It gets extremely annoying and tedious to have to constantly rebuild features, recapture animals, and then all the farm chores, which must be done daily. Sometimes by the time I finish it is night again already. I believe the developers probably thought these dream features would be cute and interesting, but they're not. Ultimately they're just annoying and frustrating, without adding any interesting game play to the game. 

Some people have commented on bugs. There are a few. The majority of bugs I encountered seemed to stem from save files for whatever reason. But sometimes I just couldn't finish a quest because the item would not trigger and/or appear. I have had to start the game over from the beginning over 4 times. This last restart has so far been pretty good. And I discovered some of the "bugs" turned out to my misunderstanding some game mechanic. For instance, I too was having an issue with stamina, but soon realized that you can increase it, and keep it high by cooking food and eating it everyday. 

Ultimately I think it is a good game but needs some further development, bug fixes, and some general housekeeping. If they would get rid of all the mini-game BS and incorporate that into the game, thereby fleshing out the base game further, I think that would be a real win. I doubt that will be the case, just saying.

Succubus is a first person action game set in a dark fantasy setting. You play Vydija, a demonic entity fighting through hostile zones. The tone is violent and explicit. The game focuses on aggressive combat and fast movement.

Combat uses melee weapons, claws, and powers. Encounters push constant offense and mobility. Enemy types vary and fights stay direct. Finishers and execution mechanics add impact but repeat often. Difficulty depends on gear and skill use rather than deep tactics.

Progression includes skill upgrades, weapons, and cosmetic customization. The path is linear with hub sections. Upgrades provide clear power increases. Exploration offers secrets and collectibles, but levels guide you forward.

The story is secondary. Dialogues serve to move you to the next zone. Writing leans on shock value. Worldbuilding exists through environmental design rather than detailed narrative. Cutscenes are brief.

Visuals use detailed, gruesome art. Performance is generally stable. Sound design supports the intensity. Content is targeted at adults due to violence and sexual themes.

Overall, Succubus is a focused action title built around fast combat and provocative presentation. It suits players seeking a short, aggressive experience with high intensity rather than depth or narrative complexity.

So, at the end of 2025, here is one of my favorite discoveries of 2024.

It's a trip into a strange, unsettling version of the industrial American South. It’s one of those games where the visuals don’t just go along with the story - they [i]are[/i] the story. They build a world that feels dirty and real, but also slightly unreal, like a fever dream somewhere in Southern Gothic lands.

The pixel art is honestly fantastic. It’s not “retro for the sake of the retro”, but rich and detailed, showing a world that’s both alive and falling apart. Abandoned refineries, flooded streets, swamps where time feels frozen - all of this turns into a visual language about loss, industrial decay, and the quiet frustration of people forgotten by “progress”.

The story starts with Kay coming back to her hometown after her mother’s death. From there it slowly becomes a story about memory, family, technology, surrealism, and how big corporations slowly grind down who you are. You don’t know what’s going to happen next, the world is still unfolding, and the line between reality and mysticism stays blurry. Later on, the plot becomes more linear and direct, and some players might not like that. The game chooses a clear path instead of keeping every option open. But I don’t really see that as a problem - if anything, it shows how strong and focused this world and story are.

If you enjoy games like Disco Elysium (my personal GOTY), Kentucky Route Zero, or the first season of True Detective - or anything where visuals and style are part of the storytelling and not just a backdrop - NORCO is a must-play. It stays with you long after the credits roll, not just because it looks great, but because it actually makes you think, and, you know, [i]feel[/i] things.

Alright, so here’s my honest take after jumping back into The Front 1.0 — and I want to be straight with you all.

I played this game two years ago in early access, and I was really hoping the 1.0 release would tighten things up. But after all this time, it feels like they’ve barely touched the optimization.

I’m running this on a Ryzen 9 5900X, RTX 3070 Ti, and 128 gigs of RAM, and I’m still getting wild FPS swings — anywhere from 40 to 200 FPS — even with everything tuned and optimized. I’ve got DLSS on, shadows low, view distance low, and OBS recording with NVENC, but the frame pacing is all over the place.

After digging into it with MSI Afterburner, I can tell you exactly why: the game is main-thread bottlenecked.
One CPU core is maxing out while the other 23 sit nearly idle. My GPU usage hovers around 35–40%, meaning the game isn’t using my hardware — it’s just choking itself.

And that’s the frustrating part.
After two years of early access, this should not still be an issue. It’s running on Unreal Engine 4, and like a lot of survival games built on that engine, it’s still single-thread heavy and poorly optimized.

The end result? You can have a top-tier rig, and it still feels inconsistent — like your system’s waiting on the game to catch up.

Visually, yeah, it looks decent. The gameplay loop is still there. But performance-wise, this feels less like a 1.0 release and more like an unfinished beta.

If you’re thinking about buying this game now that it’s officially “released,” I’d hold off until they push a serious performance patch.
Because right now, The Front 1.0 still runs like The Front Early Access.

I love this game conceptually, but the tutorial for Launch & Rendezvous - the only one that really matters - does not work. Following the instruction places you in a highly eccentric orbit with a pretty sizeable RV to the station.

I think this is because the game makes assumptions about the pitch angle you will maintain during ascent, but because the parameters like the actual size of the planet aren't given - it's not possible to determine other than by "eyeballing" it, which isn't very fun honestly - especially considering there is no time compression in-flight.

In general I feel like this game fundamentally isn't very fun to play because it withholds a lot of information from you, the orbital MFD on the right is hardly good enough - for one it doesn't even indicate the direction of motion.

Yes technically I can look at my FPA, my altitude, my apoapsis/periapsis altitude and make a determination as to whether I'm going up/down and eyeball roughly where along my flight path I am (e.g. if my FPA is going up, and my altitude is increasing towards my apoapsis, that means I'm somewhere before my apoapsis, and how close to it I am is the difference between current and apoapsis altitude)

But I don't understand why this can't be represented a bit more clearly on the orbital display, because otherwise it's frankly pretty useless other than just showing a circle.

One thing it would be useful for is showing layers of the atmosphere to make sure you're at the altitude where air resistance isn't going to send you to your doom, because the orbital prediction doesn't take that into account.

It shouldn't necessarily do that - KSP doesn't really do this either for instance, but it also gives you the information you need because the altimeter has sections that showcase where the atmosphere begins.

I'm nowhere near smart enough to know much of anything about space - but as far as I understand, generally speaking predicting these things and this information being available to the pilot (and IRL - mission control) is paramount to actually successfully orbital mechanic-ing. 

Technically you can almost disregard orbital mechanics in that tutorial and simply burn towards the target - but that's not how docking is meant to really work, you synchronize your orbits first (though keeping the alterations to the orbit resulting from the following in mind if the launch window didn't already take this into account), then you burn towards what you're trying to reach, then you dock.

If the tutorial about the rendezvous isn't going to actually tell you how to synchronize the orbits and expect you to just burn away towards the goal, and following it's instructions leads you to your doom, then prior to docking, information about your orbit and the orbit of your target should be front and centre, both in numbers (inclination, apogee, perigee) and ideally as a visualization.

This is also on top of bugs like the fact that without fail - audio cuts out after ~5 minutes of playtime. 

Or the fact there's an unskippable intro cinematic. Or the fact there's an unskippable picking up cargo cinematic. Or the fact that the tutorial for the launch and rendezvous is locked by a bunch of completely unrelated other tutorials - even if you've played the game before.

Which kinda just sucks.

This game is way better than a few of the other zombie survival games out there. The one I'm thinking of in particular is 'Vein'. This game has a lot more depth and potential than Vein. Yet Vein's recent reviews are more positive than this game's recent reviews.

This game has variety. For one, in the types of enemies you face. There's different types of zombies, bandits, and even wild animals in Mist Survival. I died to a bear attack right before writing this review. Vein doesn't have the same variety. Plus the Vein Zombies are stupid easy to kill. And their physics are super buggy. In contrast, you have to be one your toes playing Mist Survival. I was building a basic campfire right in front of my base when a bear surprised my from my right.

The amount of tasks you can do in this game will keep you busy for awhile. Building a base. Crafting all sorts of needed items. Hunting for food. Growing food. Exploring. Scavenging. Don't get too wrapped up in looting though. The Mist can show up out of nowhere. Do you get home in time to hunker down and wait for the Mist to dissipate? Or stay put and hunker down away from home? Or tackle the Mist head on, and whatever it brings. There more I could add

The recent mixed reviews for Mist Survival don't do it justice, in my opinion. Yes, it's a work in progress. Yes, there are some issues that need tweaking. But you're playing an Early Access game. It's to be expected. Knocking the lack of completeness of an Early Access game is silliness, and borderline insulting to the process. It's more ambitious than some of the better-rated Early Access zombie survival games on Steam. It's just going to take time for them to polish all the variety that's here.
