Se você esperava uma revolução em relação ao primeiro Dead Island, pode ir ajustando suas expectativas. O Riptide é, em essência, "mais do mesmo". A sensação geral é a de jogar uma DLC expansiva, e isso não é necessariamente ruim, mas também está longe de ser brilhante.

A história continua exatamente de onde o primeiro jogo parou: nosso grupo de sobreviventes, após escapar de Banoi, acaba naufragando em outra ilha tropical igualmente infestada de zumbis. A narrativa serve mais como uma desculpa para nos colocar em cenários novos do que como um elemento cativante por si só. É funcional, tem algumas reviravoltas, mas é simples e dificilmente você se lembrará dos nomes dos personagens depois de desligar o jogo.

O coração do jogo, como sempre, está na jogabilidade. A premissa continua sendo extremamente satisfatória: pegar qualquer objeto pontudo ou contundente e despedaçar zumbis de maneiras criativas. O combate corpo a corpo é visceral e divertido. Eles adicionaram algumas coisinhas novas, como a possibilidade de escalar certas superfícies e realizar ataques aéreos (que, por sinal, podem bugar e te prender no cenário), novos tipos de zumbis especializados, como os que ficam à espreita na água, os que cospem veneno e os "gritadores" que atordoam, e um sistema de defesa de base, onde você coloca barricadas e segura hordas, que é um dos acréscimos mais bem-vindos.

No entanto, Riptide herda todos os problemas do seu antecessor e, em alguns casos, parece piorá-los. A inteligência artificial dos inimigos humanos continua sendo um insulto à lógica, o minimapa é notoriamente inútil para traçar rotas, e as missões secundárias são incrivelmente repetitivas, envolvendo sempre "salve meus amigos" ou "encontre meu companheiro desaparecido". A locomoção de barco, uma novidade, é lenta e frustrante, com zumbis conseguindo parar a embarcação com um simples toque.

E então, temos os bugs. Ah, os bugs... Eles são tão frequentes quanto zumbis em um shopping center. Armas ficando invisíveis, personagens flutuando, inimigos spawnando dentro do chão ou simplesmente desaparecendo durante uma missão. A experiência é pontuada por pequenas e grandes falhas técnicas que, embora raramente quebrem o jogo por completo, quebram a imersão constantemente.

O maior divisor de águas aqui, sem sombra de dúvidas, é o modo cooperativo. Jogar Riptide sozinho pode ser uma experiência mediana, repetitiva e, em alguns momentos, solitária. Mas com um grupo de amigos, o jogo se transforma. A bagunça caótica de desmembrar zumbis juntos, rir dos bugs e superar os desafios faz com que as deficiências se tornem parte do charme. Sozinho, é um passatempo; com amigos, é uma festa no apocalipse.

Riptide é um jogo difícil de defender com unhas e dentes, mas também é difícil de odiar completamente. Ele é a definição de "mediano". Se você adorou a fórmula do primeiro jogo e quer simplesmente mais do mesmo em um novo mapa, ele entrega exatamente isso. A diversão visceral de combate está lá, mas vem embalada com todos os problemas de sempre e uma dose generosa de bugs. Compre apenas se estiver com vontade de um "brain dead game" para desligar a mente e esmagar caveiras, de preferência, com uma companhia garantida para dividir a ficha. Sozinho, a jornada pode ser bem cansativa.

Я пропустил эту часть во время ее выхода и всегда хотел наконец ее пройти, к этому времени уже вышел ремастер и оригинал удалили из магазина, так что первое(и последнее) прохождение было именно в ремастере. 
Это отвратительный ремастер спорной игры. Первое что бросается в глаза - ужасные "новые" эффекты, которые делают освещение и картинку убогой, я посмотрел несколько видео в оригинале и пусть текстуры там местами были не очень(игра всё таки вышла 13 лет назад) в остальном картинка была хорошая и приятная глазу. Благо частично их можно отключить в настройках, но сломанный и жутко яркий свет останется на протяжении всей игры.
Далее был очень странный и не интуитивный интерфейс, особенно производства и караванов, только к концу игры я обнаружил, что оказывается можно отправлять караваны не только в Бостон. Возможно это только моя проблема, возможно я не привык к интерфейсу для геймпада(это мой первый ассассин пройденный на геймпаде). Но то, что отображение доп.задач и сайдов сломано - явно проблема игры. Доп задачи появляются на секунду и сразу пропадают или наоборот висят уже после прохождения задания из-за чего приходится заходить в меню или карту, проверять всё ли сделано. К слову о доп заданиях, в этой части впервые появилось больше одной доп задачи на миссию и это неплохой способ добавить челленджа, но тот, кто придумывал эти задачи явно ненавидел людей. Приведу пример: несколько раз за игру нужно гнаться за персонажем не убивая его и каждый раз доп задачей для этого является "не толкать прохожих" и ладно бы если бы они сохранили механику из частей про Эцио, где есть быстрый бег, но при столкновении с кем-то ты замедляешься и более медленный бег, при котором ты расталкиваешь всех, но нет, теперь есть только один бег при котором Коннор автоматически толкает всех из-за чего нужно переходить на шаг в местах с людьми, чтобы он случайно не задел кого-нибудь. Да и в целом у конкретно этой задачи мало логики, ведь изначально доп задачи появились в качестве "повышения синхронизации" в миссиях, т.е. выполняя их ты делаешь задачу более приближенно к тому, как делал ее предок. И в чем логика Коннора, который бежит за очередным тамплиером, которому нужно отомстить? "блииииин, не хочу толкать прохожих........."и плевать, что чел может убежать, пока он будет аккуратно обходить всех, бред. Есть еще несколько бредовых и даже сломанных доп задач, но эта вызвала у меня самое сильное жопогорение.
Далее скажу немного про управление лошадью, в предыдущих частях оно было довольно простым и отзывчивым, практически повторяло мувсет персонажа. В этой же части они что-то сломали, лошади медленные даже в "верхней стойке", ускорение теперь не постоянно, а прожимается, что добавляет немного реализма, но ощущается как насмешка "Ты можешь ехать быстро, но только в течении 5 секунд, потом едь 5-10 секунд в медленном режиме", отзывчивость в управлении тоже куда-то пропала. Мною лошадь использовалась только зимой, так как Коннор утопал в сугробах и двигался очень медленно.
Пистолеты тоже ощущаются странно, это можно простить конечно, ведь это первая игра с полноценным огнестрелом, плюс я сначала прошел блек флаг, в котором одно удовольствие стрелять из них.(мушкеты, к слову, норм)

Review after playing through the game, which took about 7 hours. This is a remaster of a game from the NES in 1990.  It is certainly the best of the FF NES games and stands up as a pretty good game on its own.  I can recommend this to folks who are into indie JRPG's in general.  I have started and stopped different versions of this game since it came out, and this is the best version of it that's available today.

So in Q&A form:
- Does this game hold up? Yep, this one is the first of the numbered final fantasy's that is just a good game on its own.  It has a decent story and could hang with indie JRPG's from today.  
- Would you recommend this instead of the other Pixel Remasters?  No.  FF6 is (imo) the best of those.  And mechanically if you are looking for something similar, FF5 has an objectively better done job system than this one.  I see this as something to play in addition to those, not instead of them.
- It has all of the quality of life features that the other pixel remasters have, such as:
-- Graphics are greatly improved
-- Audio has a modern arranged score that sounds really good
-- You can turn off encounters so that you can get around faster
-- You can 4x your xp, job growth, and gold gain if you want to
-- You can run
-- There is an in-game map of every zone and the overworld that is great. That map keeps up with what chests you have opened where.
-- Quicksaves
- If you use that stuff isn't that cheating? IMO, if they put it in the game it is there to be used.  That said, the biggest hack in this one is the map; it is amazing.  The boost is a time-saver for sure as well.  
- Why is this worth playing?  The story is actually pretty good, and definitely better than 1 & 2.  Mechanically, it does feature a 'jobs' class change system which is interesting to explore (though again, done better in FF5).  It does still use spell slots instead of mana so can be interesting to check out.  It is pretty short if you run with the boosts on, so if you get it on sale it isn't a big commitment.

Before buying the bundle I hadn't played FF3 since the DS remake was new, and I'm so glad I ended up treating myself to some classics. Onion Knight is the chadliest of gigas! (Can't wait to get my Onion gear!)

This remaster captures the old school feel, polished graphics while staying 2D. Music is catchy, the class system is pretty great, and it's about as NES era Final Fantasy as you can get! FF3 walked so 5 and Tactics could run... going through this game again makes me appreciate how much the game added to the series, and it helps that the game itself is super fun & addictive!

You unlock new classes for every Crystal you are blessed by, and the diversity of classes makes not just for fun strategy, but adds some great replay value!

The story is pretty basic and the nameless party members are whoever you want them to be (it's an RPG, they should be whoever you want them to be!) but including class mechanics to progress through dungeons? Seems primitive in 2025 but back then it was pretty innovative; you never had cool stuff like this in what was then a pretty fresh genre!

3 Crystals in, just got the Invincible, looking forward to beating this game again after so many years. If you're into classic games and enjoy a fun class system? Give it a try!

First, I will start by saying that I don't often write reviews, but I'm going to for this one. I spent a total of 92 hours playing this game. Tl;dr I wanted to love this game, but I just couldn't.

For this first point, I will speak as diplomatically as possible. If you're looking for LGBTQ representation, especially T, this game is for you. This is good for some, but not for others. If you like using pronouns, every single NPC has their preferred. Again, good for some, not for others.

Secondly, the part that drove me the craziest is that every single NPC like, talks like exactly like the next Cheddar! It's like totally Spicy and Bright? OMG it's like my favorite person ever (insert player name here). Basically, every NPC character speaks like a not-very-smart valley girl from the 90s. It made me want to rip my hair out, and I actually asked many critters to leave me island because of it. There are about three profile types that all 40 or so NPCs share, and they all speak the same. It was very aggravating.

Next, there is very little instruction in many areas of the game, and I found myself googling many different aspects to save myself hours and hours of trial and error. I did not appreciate this. There are only a few businesses, and there are many NPCs, but only certain critters like certain jobs. Good luck finding out which ones without googling, and further good luck on having the right critters wash up on shore. The recipes for many food items are not readily available either, leading again to a trial and error which wastes materials.

I spend approximately 25-30 game hours to get to the point I was bringing in enough revenue to do anything substantial, then I had too much money. It did not seem very well balanced. This aspect should have been more gradual, instead of so sudden.

I really liked designing my character. I made a pretty BA dragon creature. The animation and character movement were pretty nice. It was fun to explore, but it all gets pretty redundant after a while. Another sunken city with more randomly generated materials. It's like there was plenty to explore but nothing to look at or do. 

I would have also like to see more of buy/sell option to make money instead of relying solely on tourists. That's more of personal request, but I think that it would have brought another element to the game, such as motivation to explore deeper and further to gather valuable materials. As it was, everything was better stacked in storage because of some future project.

All in all, I think this game could have been something really great and special, but it missed the mark. It's too bad, because there aren't many games exactly like this one, if any.

🔧 Gunsmith Simulator

I spent some time with Gunsmith Simulator, and overall I had a positive experience. It’s not perfect, but it’s definitely an interesting and satisfying simulation for anyone curious about how firearms work.

First of all — no one in real life disassembles guns this easily. It’s clearly an arcade-style interpretation, with screws that unscrew instantly and perfectly clean parts snapping into place without resistance. But that’s part of the fun — it’s light, fast, and oddly relaxing.

There are even leaderboards for gun disassembly and reassembly times, which adds a bit of friendly competition. The gun selection isn’t massive, but it includes plenty of iconic and recognizable models. There’s even some old flintlock stuff — a bit of a joke addition, but amusing nonetheless.

It’s the kind of simulator where you “finish work and go do more work.” You take orders, clean, repair, assemble — and it’s strangely meditative. But eventually, repetition starts to creep in.

✅ Pros:
✔ Extremely detailed disassembly mechanics down to the smallest parts.
✔ You can test your guns at a shooting range — a very cool touch.
✔ Simple, intuitive economy and progression system.
✔ Cozy workshop atmosphere — calm and mechanical.
✔ You can create your own collection bunker for display.
✔ Educational value — you start realizing how complex real firearms truly are.

❌ Cons:
➖ Repetition — eventually, it all becomes a cycle of similar tasks.
➖ Limited number of gun models so far.
➖ The trailers and store page make it look more expansive than it really is.
➖ Some content (like antique weapons) feels filler or gimmicky.
➖ No real storyline or motivation beyond upgrading your workshop.
➖ Can start to feel more like routine than discovery.

📝 Conclusion
Gunsmith Simulator isn’t a blockbuster, but it’s a relaxing and technical experience — something between a puzzle and a workshop meditation.
It’s satisfying to understand how guns actually function, and for a few hours, you really do feel like a craftsman surrounded by precision and metal.

👉 Rating: 7/10. Enjoyable, educational, and relaxing — though it can wear thin after a while.

🎮 Fun Facts:
• Several weapon models are recreated from real technical blueprints.
• The disassembly system is detailed enough to appeal to real engineers and gunsmiths.
• Includes leaderboards for competitive assembly times.
• Some interface elements are inspired by actual repair shop layouts.
• The developers have announced future updates adding more weapons and customization.

死んだら進行状況がリセットされ、セーブポイントから再開。
ダッシュやローリングによる無敵回避やパリィはない。

■基本操作
小攻撃、大攻撃、ジャンプ、バックダッシュ、クマちゃん。
・小攻撃はボタン連打でコンボ。押しっぱで溜め攻撃。
・ジャンプはダブルジャンプ&急降下キック可。
・バックダッシュは無敵時間がない。硬直時間もあるので使い勝手は良くない。
・クマちゃんはライフゲージがある時に光弾発射。
光弾でしか倒せない敵、一部の扉を破壊したりスイッチを起動させる事が出来る。
ライフゲージが0の時はクマちゃんを抱きしめてライフを8割回復。

■聖闘士星矢ソックリな聖衣を装着する鎧システム
5つの鎧があり、それぞれ雷、水、火、地、光の属性がある。
敵には属性があり、弱点属性で攻撃すると大ダメージを与える。
各鎧には専用のスキルや必殺技があるが、長くなるので割愛。

■アップグレード
主人公は残機数増加とライフゲージの延長のみ。
鎧のアップグレードは1回のみで攻撃力アップと必殺技の追加。
どちらも専用アイテム複数個と多額のお金が必要。
しっかり探索してアイテム回収や金策をしないとアップグレード出来ないので注意！

90年代のメトロイドヴァニア感があって懐かしさを感じた。
不便さが目立つが普通に遊べる佳作。
ストアページのレビューに書かれている問題点の殆どは、2025年の大型アップデートで改善されている。
昔（90～2000年代）のメトロイドヴァニア好きにオススメ！
余談だが、Blasphemousの主人公の悔悟者がゲスト出演している。

9 Years of Shadows es prodigioso

Trataré de exponerlo de una manera más concisa:

ARTE

La primera impresión por supuesto es el arte, maravilloso y detallado pixel art, lleno de color y estética. Ningún escenario está descuidado, lo cual es importante ya que en un “metroidvania” constantemente tienes que regresar a varios puntos del mapa. Cada cuarto y cada momento es agradable a la vista, acompañado por envolvente música que es una combinación entre lo-fi moderno y JRPG de los 90’s (siendo el tema del “Teatro” un gran ejemplo de esta combinación).  

Los personajes son otro acierto. Teniendo un estilo combinado entre ánime, cómic americano y arte europeo. La protagonista  tiene un diseño y apariencia fabuloso, con un carácter de rudeza y determinación, sin perder una personalidad amable y femenina. Los “NPC”  (que en esencia representan músicos), son de estilos muy exóticos y estrafalarios, lo cual hace a cada uno muy identificables, y sus diálogos sencillos y concisos amenizan la tensión.

Los “Jefes”, son tal vez lo más destacado, ya que a pesar de sus cortas apariciones (sólo en las batallas) tienen unos diseños y personalidades dignas de tener sus propios “spin-offs”. 
Los monstruos rivales, desde los “fáciles de derrotar” hasta los jefes gigantes, son criaturas extraordinarias e insólitas, parecen salidas de un sueño.   

La belleza de los escenarios, los personajes  y la música me hizo soltar el control más de una vez, para disfrutar la atmósfera.

GAMEPLAY

La comodidad de un control es difícil de explicar, simplemente se siente bien;  la fluidez de los saltos y ataques son evidentes desde el inicio, cuando adquieres un nuevo movimiento se vuelve inmediatamente intuitivo y responsivo al estilo del juego, el diseño de nivel está pensado de tal manera que al obtener una habilidad el juego te presenta una situación sencilla en la que puedes usar el nuevo movimiento (y las combinaciones con otros movimientos) para que estés listo en los momentos más retadores del juego.

En el trascurso de la aventura estos “upgrades” serán diferentes armaduras, claramente basado en “Caballeros del Zodiaco”, no lo mencioné en el apartado de arte, pero son preciosas (sin spoilers diré que la armadura final emocionará a cualquier fan de “Saint Seiya”). 

Dichas armaduras proveen diferentes poderes que son necesarios para avanzar en los cuartos y derrotar enemigos (como un buen metroidvania). Estos poderes están basados en elementos como agua, fuego, tierra etc. Y puedes causar más daño a los enemigos que tengan debilidad a esos elementos (tipo Pokémon si se quiere ver de esa forma), lo cual le da más dinámica.

Y todavía no he mencionado al oso. El coprotagonista es un mágico oso de peluche flotante que lanza poderosos rayos (suena excéntrico, pero tiene más sentido visualmente que por escrito); dichos rayos son fundamentales para abrir puertas y derrotar enemigos específicos, el oso lo puedes mover y manipular a criterio, siendo muy cómodo de usar. Lo peculiar es que sus rayos te bajan barra de vida, te causan daño. Sin embargo, recuperas barra de vida al golpear a los rivales, lo cual provoca un interesante balance que te mantiene expectante en todo momento. Al perder toda la barra puedes hacer una acción que abraza al oso y te recupera vida (lo cual me parece de simpática ternura).  

La dificultad es precisa, me pareció el balance perfecto entre retador y justo. El mapa es fantástico, muy bien planeado y diseñado, cada piso y cada cuarto es entretenido por diferentes razones y es cautivante explorarlo todo. Agregaré que adquirí todos los trofeos y no fue algo previsto que buscara hacer, simplemente me encantaba indagar en los escenarios y terminé encontrando todos los “secretos” y coleccionables.

HISTORIA

Toda la fantasía creada en “9 Years of Shadows” te envuelve instantáneamente, eres absorbido a una atmósfera, a una ilusión. Similar a “Castlevania” te adentras a un castillo para terminar con una bestia que inició una maldición que ha durado 9 años; entre sus varias calamidades destaca la ausencia de color (el juego empieza en blanco y negro). La heroína “Europa”, se ha entrenado para destruir la maldición (motivada principalmente para vengar la muerte de sus padres), sin embargo fracasa rotundamente, hasta que aparece el mágico oso de peluche flotante que lanza poderosos rayos (sigue siendo raro escribir esa descripción), el cual la salva y le ayuda, recuperando el color en el proceso (e insisto, el color en este juego es hermoso).

Los diálogos son pocos, la mayoría viniendo de “Europa”, especialmente me gusta sus reflexiones que aparecen cuando se sube a los elevadores. Como mencioné antes, sus interacciones con los “NPC” son muy agradables, y sus discusiones con los enemigos son memorables. Con poco, hay mucho, pues deja llenar lo que no se cuenta a nosotros (como la relación de “Europa” con su maestro). Naturalmente no daré “spoilers” pero estoy muy satisfecho con la historia, es una fábula preciosa y de buen gusto.

CONCLUSIÓN

9 Years of Shadows es prodigioso. Si tú, estimado lector, jugaste y disfrutaste “Symphony of the Night” y “Super Metroid”, no hay más que decir, este juego es para ti. Si no jugaste “metroidvanias” clásicos, o incluso no eres muy afín del género, diré únicamente esto:
El juego es divertido y es una obra de arte en movimiento.

Mis felicitaciones a Halberd Studios de México, por crear un juego de esta magnitud y belleza.
Actualmente lo considero uno de mis videojuegos favoritos.

This game just hits on every level

At its heart its a dungeon crawler, you go on runs, get loot and repeat. 

Sounds familiar right? But it has to be said how each of Sulfurs influences are so well implemented and to the right level that makes everything so engaging. 

I could glaze about the sound, the enemies, the customisation, how this game has made me realise why loot has been boring in other games and that's deterministic crafting. You have real purpose with what you find and RNG is fun in having them drop, plus you usually have multiply ways to get what you want. 

The constant risk of loosing your gear keeps it tense, though the amulet to teleport back to town is always within reach and provides a great checkpoint for having quick runs. 

The areas give you an expectation on what you will come across, with enough variations on how you find stuff and sometimes if you will. 

Cooking being the main way to get high health returns, while also being linked to how fast it replenishes, it's just a fantastic way to make you feel like your scavenging and surviving. It always keeps you careful and on edge, but not too much. 

All of this layering, has this become something that's fun to think about and indulge in.

 I really could go on, like how each enemy has it's own sound cue to help with distinction, when there are details like that, you know it's a wonderful game. So well thought-out and insanely fun.

Randomly generated upgrades sometimes fail to provide meaningful advantages, leading to moments where progress feels out of the player’s control. This, combined with uneven unit balance and abrupt difficulty spikes, can make certain stages disproportionately punishing. Over time, the experience risks slipping into repetition, especially once you’ve seen most of the available unit and upgrade combinations.

Recuos gigantes, bazucas são toscas, lança granadas são toscos, e se você usa sniper que mata em 1 hit você é tosco. [h1]MISSÕES[/h1]
Não fazem muito sentido,[i]vai lá e arromba tal porta, entrega em tal lugar, agora bota uma bomba ali na loja, agora pega esse carro e leva para x local[/i](?). Tem 2 distritos para guerriar, Waterfront e Financial, uns que não sei oque é, é tipo minigame, e tem um distrito para lazer, que é o Social, onde você pode customizar suas coisas, trocar de roupa, fazer tatuagem, mexer no leilão, ouvir o funk dos brs (sim, tem chat de voz, mas só quando ta perto da pessoa).

Como posso falar disso sendo que não tem? Sério... [b]É A PIOR COISA DO JOGO[/b]. Isso é o motivo de todo sofrimento. Ah, e sobre ser [b]Pay2Win[/b] como falam. As pessoas podem depositar grana e comprar a arma mais tunada, e os carros mais bizarros. E se for premiun, mesmo perdendo a partida a recompensa é mais recompensadora do que quem ganhou e ta sem premiun lol.

Jogue sempre com um amigo, é bem melhor, você faz estrategias e no final você acaba se divertindo.

Assassin’s Creed® Liberation™

Liberation nos apresenta Aveline de Grandpré, uma jovem assassina que viveu no final do século XVIII e que busca libertar da escravidão a população negra de Nova Orleans, assim como a própria cidade do domínio dos Espanhóis e Templários.

Em termos de mecânicas e jogabilidade o game segue a cartilha estabelecida pela franquia na época, com missões que envolvem investigações, exploração, furtividade e logicamente assassinatos, com um combate pouco desafiador, mas com uma boa dose de violência e brutalidade característicos da franquia. O grande diferencial de Liberation é que a protagonista pode assumir três identidades distintas, cada uma com desvantagens e atributos especiais, primeiro temos a identidade de Assassina, que conta com maior proteção e maior arsenal, segundo temos a identidade de Escrava, que é mais fraca e tem um numero menor de armas disponíveis, mas permite que a protagonista se misture de forma mais fácil entre a multidão e por ultimo temos a identidade de Dama, que tem movimentos limitados devido as suas vestimentas, mas consegue acessar locais restritos, além de conseguir seduzir guardas. Tais identidades, mesmo que aproveitada de forma limitada durante a campanha, dão um ar de novidade e dinamismo ao gameplay.

A ambientação é bastante competente, com uma Nova Orleans bem detalhada e movimentada, porém é inegável que o game tem um escopo limitado se comparado com os outros games da franquia e isso fica evidente ao se notar que o mapa dos pântanos a fauna é quase que inexistente se comparado com o mapa fronteira de Assassin's Creed III, além do mapa da cidade de Chichen Itza, localizada no México, ser extremamente pequeno, não oferecendo muito conteúdo além das missões principais do local. A própria Nova Orleans, apesar de densa, se demonstra pequena e de fácil exploração.


Assassin's Creed: Liberation é um bom jogo, que apresenta uma protagonista carismática, mas com uma trama pouco desenvolvida e com uma jogabilidade que segue a cartilha estabelecida pela franquia. Um game indicado principalmente para os fãs da serie Assassin's Creed.

La conclusion approche à grands pas et l'histoire prend de belles envolées, y a toujours beaucoup à se mettre sous la dent !
Minagoroshi est, pour résumer, une réussite de synthétisation des 6 premiers chapitres, un buildup particulièrement efficace pour le dernier chapitre, et se paye le luxe de mêler à son intrigue un message puissant, pertinent et très subtil à ses lecteurices.
Je tiens à rendre une chose bien claire : même si vous êtes habitué.e à ce genre d'histoire progressivement complexe, qui parlent de cycle, de volonté humaine et utilisent la méta-narration (comme NieR Automata ou DokiDoki Literature Club pour citer les premiers qui me viennent en tête), je pense que vous ressortirez impressionné.e de Higurashi. Déjà parce que BON SANG ça a été écrit entre 2002 et 2006, c'est fou ! Mais aussi et surtout car la proposition tient encore la route 20 ans plus tard, et a sa propre identité vis-à-vis de toutes ces thématiques profondes. C'est le plus grand compliment que je puisse faire à cette série.

Attention ça va spoiler.
J'avoue avoir été un peu déçue de ne pas voir la vente aux enchères développée comme les autres moments de jeux entre l'équipe, mais bon. Quelques variations de sprites supplémentaires pour les personnages principaux auraient été la bienvenue. Garder leur même allure tout du long, même dans les moments plus violents, ne cause pas nécessairement de problèmes à la mise en scène, mais ç'aurait tout de même apporté un p'tit truc en plus.
J'ai juste deux points négatifs à relever : le premier sont les "hau, hau, hauuuu" constants de Hanyuu, quel que soit le contexte ; ça enlève à l'ambiance et j'aurais aimé un changement de voix qui reflète les enjeux extrêmes, comme quand Rika passe de "mignonne" à "désabusée". Le second, plus chiant, est une poignée de crashs qui m'ont fait perdre une demie-heure de lecture.

Bref, l'histoire a beau dévoiler lentement son final, même si ce n'est pas exactement celui que j'espérais voir je dois bien avouer qu'il reste excessivement bien mené et fun à lire !

Comparado aos capítulos 5 e 6, Minagoroshi é, de certa forma, menos caótico, ao menos até o epílogo. Ele nos apresenta uma nova personagem (não tão “nova” assim) e foca bastante na relação entre Rika e Satoko. Se você joga ativamente tentando desvendar o mistério, recomendo reunir suas teorias mais sólidas, pois, segundo o próprio autor, este é um “gabarito” no qual é possível comparar as conclusões a que você chegou com a verdade por trás de tudo. Naturalmente, muitas questões ainda ficam em aberto para serem resolvidas no capítulo 8, que encerra a história.

Em especial, este capítulo é fantástico por aprofundar a Rika e certos personagens. Talvez você até se sinta revoltado com alguns problemas muito reais retratados aqui, como a ineficiência de certos órgãos públicos. Em suma, é mais uma escrita fantástica do Ryukishi07. Tudo culmina e tudo termina aqui.

作为一款僵尸求生题材类型的独立游戏，他最新颖的地方在于：有着其他同款类型游戏没有的丰富的异常状态系统，被僵尸攻击以后，如果你没有药物或血清的话，在穷途末路的即将变异那一刻是选择死亡还是成为黑暗势力的一员的那种纠结感是这个游戏的一大特点;在流血时如果没有绷带止血的话，到了最后你会因为失血过多而痛苦的死去的那种绝望感同样是这个游戏的一个独特的地方；在你受伤严重的情况下你的视觉会变成黑白色，此时的没有救助的你会感到世界更加的危险，那孤立无援的绝望感比流血过多而死的绝望感还要恐怖，那是一种生不如死的绝望感。种种感觉仿佛给人一种电影班的感觉。其次是弹药检查系统，大家都知道：在尸如潮水的情况下，作为一个平民，手里有一把枪是最令人安心的事，而因为你是一个平民而不是军队的士兵，所以你没有大把大把的弹药挥霍，所以你要合理分配你手中的枪弹才能保证生存，然而面对一堆(我是说一堆)僵尸开了几枪后，你不知道你还有多少子弹而又无法检查的话，可能在面临下一波僵尸的袭来的时候就无法全身而退了，所以你需要时刻看好你的子弹以保证你还有能力自保。然后便是我最喜欢的近战系统：大到斧头锤子，小到手电拳头，无一不能对僵尸造成实际伤害，而且按住右键蓄力可以打出高于普通攻击数倍的伤害，每种武器的攻击轴都各有不同，这就决定了你能够扫一大片还是对单独的某个僵尸（好吧我并没有看到能扫一大片的那种场面）来一下子，尤其是使用大型武器的时候，对着僵尸脑袋来一下子看着他飞出去的感觉无疑是最爽快的,但是如果沉迷这种状况的话，僵尸就有可能从周围蜂拥而至（我是过来人）。再一个就是僵尸的种类：有遍地都是的“乌龟”，也有少数变异不完全的“奇行种”，还有由于变异丧失走动能力的爬行者,和全副武装的军人僵尸，甚至还有孩子。是的，这个游戏里的僵尸的种类还包括了孩子，我所认识的僵尸类的游戏，都没有看到其中有孩子类型的僵尸的身影。但是在我看到两眼发白，不断呻吟的孩子的时候，不禁感叹这款游戏的真实性。在这个游戏里，你要保证自己完全健康的情况下，还要和黑暗势力斗智斗勇,最终逃出生天.我觉得这款游戏如果有个好剧本，拍成电影绝对能门庭若市。

This game has all the ingredients to be a truly great game, but unfortunately stumbles frequently and badly enough to end up only a pretty good one.

First off, if you've heard about this game there's a good chance it's because someone said the words "Obra Dinn" or "Golden Idol" or "Outer Wilds" and you started magically floating over to the Steam page. 

Unfortunately those comparisons are a bit misleading. It has all the trappings of a true deductive investigation game, but at its core Blake Manor is an Ace Attorney game. There is no real risk of failure, and any thinking you might have to do is automated for you by the game. The time system that would ostensibly create a fail pressure is a total macguffin; you can do every possible thing in the game with time to spare.

This handholding is also unfortunately integral because the puzzle pieces are not carefully crafted enough to stand on their own. The game occasionally depends on the PC massively jumping to conclusions and some deus ex machina reveals to jam its image into focus, necessitating the system be automatic.

This is all further dampened by a litany of bugs, ranging from mildly annoying to progression breaking. I personally encountered a bug that locked out the ability to complete 2 characters storylines, and the trigger of the bug occurred so early in the save that by the time I'd realized, there was no way I was going to redo it all and hope it worked next time.

Blurring the line between bug and jank is the general lack of polish around contextual awareness. I have a lot of sympathy for what a gargantuan task presenting information that can be discovered in so many different orders is, but sympathy doesn't change that the final result can be extremely rough around the edges. Characters will semi-frequently reference conversations you haven't yet had, or tell you things as if they're brand new when they're something you've already discussed at length. You'll often think "wait, what am I missing?" and the answer is nothing, the game just messed up.

This has been an extremely harsh review, but you may notice that I still recommend the game. Ultimately, despite the bitter taste much of the above left in my mouth, I enjoyed my time in Blake Manor and don't regret playing it. When it's at its best, the rails you're on seem to melt away and you feel those sparks of Obra Dinn-esque brilliance. The work put into the setting is exceptional; Blake Manor feels every bit the late 19th century Irish mansion it claims to be, and pays that off incredibly well thematically.

If you go in with your notebook down (you won't be needing it) and prepare for a slightly headier take on an Ace Detective game that's a bit unpolished in places, I think you'll have a very worthwhile experience.

My recommendation for this game comes with a lot of ifs and buts. It's ultimately a pretty good experience, but I have to do some expectation managing here. Other reviews are comparing this game to Outer Wilds, Obra Dinn or the Golden Idol games. This is actually what led me to buy the game and to be disappointed even if I did end up enjoying it for what it is. This game is simply not up to those standards, because it's barely even a puzzle game. Yes, it has puzzles, but I can only think of one instance in the whole game where I actually had to stop for a minute and figure out what I had to do. So, if you're looking for a good puzzle game, this is not it.

I don't want to linger in that negativity too long, so I'll start talking about what IS good about this game and make my way into the more flawed aspects.

[h3] The lore [/h3]

This game was clearly made with love, and about 90% of that love goes into one thing, which is Irish folklore, mythology and history. If you are Irish or are interested in these subjects, then I definitely recommend this game. I myself wasn't particularly interested in them, but the game honestly got me hooked on most of what it told me. It was so interesting to learn about the aspects of modern western culture that are influenced by Irish mythology and its clash with catholicism. While there's obviously a lot of focus in all of this, the game also touches on other cultures (from which many of the characters originate), always with a focus on the occult, and it overall feels very respectful of these cultures (emphasis on "felt", because, to be honest, I'm not knowledgeable enough to be sure about this). If this paragraph doesn't make you interested in the game, it might be a sign to skip it entirely, because I think it's the only thing that the game does well in a unique way.

[h3] The plot [/h3]

Apart from the lore that the game exposes, the plot itself centers around a disappearance that you, as a detective, must solve. The plot itself is pretty good, with some nice few twists here and there. However, the actual "detective" aspect of the gameplay is not that satisfying, mainly because of what I already said about almost never having to actually figure stuff yourself as the player. Adding to this, the game lets you keep track of each character and mark them as to rule them out as possible culprits. This sounded like a great idea at first. However, about the time you enter the endgame, you realize it is barely necessary to do such a thing.

Regarding the dialogue... it's kind of hit or miss. There is a lot of it and a lot of characters too. Each character has its own little story and its own resolution. Some are better than others. Some had very unsatisfying resolutions. As a whole, though, I'd say it's okay.

[h3] The limited time mechanic [/h3]

The game has a time mechanic. You have a limited amount of time to do your investigation. However, time does not actually behave as time. It's rather like a currency you spend to do certain actions (mainly looking at things of asking people questions, each action taking one minute). At first, I wasn't sure if I liked this mechanic. Now, I think it's kind of genius, but with a few flaws that honestly might be worth it.
Basically, the game forces you to be economic with your actions. There's lots of things to look at and lots of questions to ask. I think it's great because, in most games where you go around talking to people and have like ten things to talk about with each one, I always feel like I have to exhaust every option or otherwise I will miss content. In this game, you can't do that. You have to be mindful about what you spend your time on. Even so, the game gives you more than enough time to do everything important, even if you stumble a bit. It is a nice balance, where you don't feel rushed, but you also can't go around looking at every piece of silverware in the manor or asking each character about every other character in the game (which the game lets you do, by the way).
It still has its flaws. For example, there was a certain kind of thing that I quickly learned not to waste my time inspecting because it never yielded any useful information, but I eventually found one that I did have to inspect, even though it looked like any other (if you're curious, I'm talking about [spoiler] libraries [/spoiler])
Also, the game has certain events at certain hours that you can attend to and will take a considerable chunk of your time. These events can give you interesting tidbits about lore or the characters, but I don't recall any of them actually aiding my investigation, so it kind of felt like wasting a lot of time with nothing to show for it.

[h3] The puzzles... [/h3]

Time to expand upon why I think the puzzles are so bad. There are two types of situations where it seems the game is trying to challenge your brains.
One is simple, classic puzzles. That would be, having to arrange something, be it a code, password, combination or whatever. These are all pretty easy, to the point that it kind of ruins the immersion of you being this big time detective. For example (very minor spoiler here), at some point, a character asks you to translate a word for them. For this, they give you the notes they have about the language you have to translate, hoping you can fill in the gaps. Well, the "notes" are a literal one to one mapping between the English alphabet and that language's alphabet. All you have to do is match the symbols. You don't even get to write the letters yourself, you just click on the symbols it shows you in the right order. A baby could do it, and it is very jarring that this character seemed to need your help with it, because this character is supposed to be quite knowledgeable in the matter.
The other situation would be when you actually have to follow the threads of your investigation, to know who to talk to, what questions to ask, and where to go exploring. However, the game holds your hand way too much on all of this, to the point you barely even have to think. You can simply go to your mystery board and, most of the time, it will outright tell you what to do. The problem is that the game just keeps track of way too much in this board. Sometimes it feels like you do anything and suddenly the game gives you five different notifications of evidence and threads being added to your board. You can mindlessly brute force your way through this game by just following the board.

[h3] Some technical aspects [/h3]

For a game of this caliber, none of what I'm about to say really matters that much, but I will say it for sake of completeness. The game lacks some polish. There are some errors in the text, some errors in the map, some issues with the interfaces, sometimes things you can't interact with will light up in detective sight (idk if it's called that, I've just made it up). That being said, the only bug I had that was actually annoying was that at one point the camera didn't zoom into a safe when I went to input the code, so I just had to count the number of turns I made.

Also... why does everything take so long to load? It's not like it drives me mad, but it's odd that a game like this, that I have in an SSD, takes three to four seconds to load every room and every cinematic. It doesn't sound like much, but this game has to load a new room at EVERY door. I don't know why. I don't know much about making games, but I don't see why the whole manor couldn't be seamless, especially considering that everything except the player in this game is stationary. If you're in the drawing room and want to get to the telegraph room, it's a short walking distance, but you have to go through four doors, which means you will spend roughly the same time walking as in a loading screen.
All of this isn't a big deal obviously. I just wanted to rant about it.

[h1] "Such is our calling.” [/h1]

Cronos: The New Dawn (2025) represents a third-person action-horror game, developed by the company Bloober Team and published by the company Bloober Team SA. Both organizations are based in Poland.

[i] Pros & cons: [/i]

++ Upon your arrival in the socialists’ wet dream of New Dawn, you will experience the oppressive atmosphere of a decaying city within a time field as you try to find your own meaning in this beautifully desolate world.

+ Fight your way through hordes of meta-bionts, accumulations of flesh eager to devour any biomass, including yours. Fortunately, you can find some excellent tools for individual and mass destruction that you can modify to your heart's content. My personal favourite is to make as many incendiary grenades as possible and enjoy the erupting barbecue around me. Even for the few female gamers among us, the game offers a special gift: You can pet cats, and they shall gather in your own room. By the gods, the irony!

o Here are some things that need dire improvement: 1. You cannot drop items, only destroy them. 2. Enemies who are lying on the ground should be able to be destroyed by the player and not suddenly awakened from stasis just because I triggered an event. 3. Despite the appearance of walking around in heavy armour – I am looking at you, my massive metal dome – and the feeling of controlling a female Big Daddy, I still possess the fragile constitution of an asthmatic woman. 4. The artificial reduction of inventory space to create a certain similarity to a survival horror game seems completely out of place when the protagonist is a walking workbench. I could throw my entire Christmas decoration on her and still have space for some power tools from my car mechanic shop and neighbouring construction site.

- Two beings with speech impairments musing about the meaninglessness of their existence in a dystopian future with more logic gaps surrounding the paradox of time travel than Swiss cheese, while simultaneously pointing out the perfect and sublime nature of cats, do not constitute an intellectual debate that a normal player would understand or be interested in.

-- The constantly monotonous voice acting drives me up the wall. Basically, her charisma and empathy equal an iceberg. During the entire playthrough I felt no connection with this human refrigerator.

[i] Summary: [/i]

This is not your long-awaited solution to your Dead Space addiction. It remains something unique with a different atmosphere, but a similar gameplay principle. Overpriced for what it offers, but competent in what it achieves. 

“But great MK, I crave for some action! What should I do?”, I hear you inquire my dear reader. Well, my little junkie, wait for the first sale. Such is your calling.

On a personal note: I was born in Poland during the era of socialism behind the Iron Curtain, as depicted here. And I appreciate the developers' efforts to capture this atmosphere; they succeeded admirably.

Ai Limit is a hidden gem that deserves more attention, I easily and highly recommend this game.

Ai Limit takes all the good pieces from Dark Souls, Bloodborne, and Code Vein and blends it together in a really nice highly polished package. If you like any of the games I just mention you'll also love Ai Limit.

From Bloodborne, the game has quick dashes, no weight system, and a weapon swap attack akin to transformation attacks. From Code Vein, you have a sync meter that you expend to use abilities and you replenish by attacking enemies. From Dark souls, you have the atmosphere and the level design of areas looping back on themselves and unlocking shortcuts.

I would say the difficulty of this game is on the same level as Dark Souls 1. It is slower and more methodical compared to modern souls-likes; enemies have telegraphed attacks and are predictable, parrying isn't too hard to master but punishing if you fail, you'll never die to an enemy and think your death was BS nor will you get killed by one-shot attacks (not until NG+, anyway). In the modern souls-like gaming landscape many would call this game easy, but I personally would describe the game as very fair.

My first playthough of the game took about 30 hours. I took my time exploring, experimenting, reading item descriptions, and I even missed a few areas. My second playthough I did on NG+ and aimed for 100% completion, which took me about 16 hours. How long this game will take you to beat I think depends on what type of player you are. If you don't dally and keep pushing through you can complete the game in less than 20 hours on a blind first playthrough. While this game is shorter than a traditional souls-like, it is of high quality and when I beat it I still felt like I wanted more so I did a second playthrough right after.

This game doesn't have character creation, but the devs make up for it by giving us something even better: The protag has tiddie physics and a really nice butt.


If you end up getting the game here's a quick tip:

Level your Strength, Technique, and Spirit to 12, then start leveling your health to 50. You can rely on weapon upgrades for increased damage. This will meet the requirements for a lot of the toys, letting you experiment to see what you like best. Eventually you will get an item that allows you to respec freely and as often as you want with no cost at all, allowing you to experiment and specialize as much as you want. My advice will hold you over until you get that item.

... act 2 really "[b]ruins[/b]" the experience of this game. 
You need to know what you are looking for, where to find it, and how to get there, and you're probably not going to put all the clues in the main chamber together, so you'll hit the 3 crystals and jump down the well.

Welcome to Well Hell, motherf*cker!

The hub well sends you to a random puzzle room. It probably won't be the room you need, but in order to leave, you need to over come the challenge of the room. Ok. 
You complete that challenge, rinse and repeat for a while until you find yourself back in a challenge room you already did, but now you have to repeat the challenge, and [b]that's[/b] where everything starts to fall apart.

Just moving between rooms is a puzzle, and the punishment for failing to know how to use the well is completing the same challenges over and over and over. I'd say each challenge is interesting exactly once, when you're first figuring it out. After that it become a chore, the price of admission for another go on the Welly-Go-Round.

I'd say I gave it about as much time as I spent on all of Act 1 trying to figure it out, but I was getting bored of the time wasted redoing a challenge AGAIN. So I tried looking up a guide. Even with a guide putting what's going on in plain english, it's a puzzle, but at least the sense of progress made it fun. Then, one room had a crystal randomly spawn in a hazard, and in trying to reach it I died, losing all my progress.

I might have been willing to push through if there was more Act 1 type gameplay after Act 2... but I'm pretty sure it's just a boss fight, and since I wasn't given any story motivations to move forward... I don't imagine fighting a boss for reasons beyond my comprehension will make up for the suffering of Act 2.

All in all, I will recommend this cause Act 1 is fun, but seriously, just get Gutter World, you really don't need to play this to get into that and it's way better in nearly every regard.

嗯，又是inti的游戏，画风真的可爱，但游戏就做的很残念了。

回忆起来我最早对这个游戏感兴趣是因为看到有人说这个游戏的“魔女”职业有横版中最像法师的操作体验，实际情况是法师通过对应按键顺序组合输入咏唱魔法，具体操作就是R1（打开魔导书）→BBBB（咒语咏唱，理论上手速够快的话这个阶段可以做到瞬发）→X（释放魔法），而这还只是法师最低级的属性攻击方式之一，只是丢一个小火球...想认真打输出则需要R1→YYYY接R1→XAYABA接R1→AYAYAYAY→X来换取一次强力攻击，而这还是省略的，愿意的话中间可以再加一段R1→AYAYAYAY的咏唱开头再加一个B来接强化。
先不说魔女这个操作逻辑是腱鞘炎真神，更大的问题是她在咏唱期间是纯站桩没有任何自保能力。正常来说这种角色会有其他补偿来提供一些防御性能...比如隔壁的同社游戏《苍蓝雷霆 爪》中虽然都在吐槽双主角角色性能不平衡，但一样是需要锁定敌人输出那边的弱势角色GV在和敌人保持安全距离输出这点更占优。但《龙之死印》这边就没有这种情况，单人特定职业对上一些头目就会因为上述的没有其他角色基础的机动性直接坐大牢，而原因就在于本作是多人游戏要做职业分化，所以缺的性能就直接交给其他角色了~于是魔女就成为了一个在激烈的横版战斗中没有闪避没有二段跳没有防御，攻击前还需要罚站的角色。
这个游戏还有很多设计就像魔女这个角色一样，也许出发点是有趣的，但制作力完全没能跟上想一出是一出的设计思路，最终端上来的就是半成品感满满的四不像。

直觉上我觉得这种玩着不会快乐的游戏我不想推荐，但另辟蹊径一想在坐牢这一块这游戏给了我很多独特的体验，这么想的话本作确实给人带来了快乐[strike]被气笑了[/strike]，出于不能只有我被这个游戏折磨的想法这里还是给个推荐吧。

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3532289712]The Alters[/url] для малышей — две космические [i]подруги[/i], ищущие где что плохо лежит на разных планетах, (на примерно последние деньги) прилетают в очередное место, поражённое странной слизью (тем самым "ганком") и находят там руины неизвестной инопланетной цивилизации, а также какой-то трубопровод по типу нефтяного. Есть надежда, что и до остатков планетарных ресурсов тоже можно добраться, но у планеты обнаруживается другой секрет. 

Преамбула в моём описании получилась достаточно интригующей, но в самой игре первая треть сделана крайне вяло — ты ходишь туда-сюда, учишься засасывать слизь механической рукой, есть самая капелька пространственных головоломок (позже авторы эту компоненту разовьют примерно до уровня "Томб райдеров"), собираешь растущие тут и там ресурсы для (скромных) апгрейдов руки и слушаешь сварливые переругивания главных героинь, которые винят друг друга в своей бедности и безответственности. 

Дело становится чуть интереснее посреди игры, когда мы доходим до собственно руин, и меня умилило, как дальше сюжет развивается по классическому западному сценарию "отважные идеалисты смело и агрессивно вмешиваются в конфликт, о причинах и контексте которого им ровным счётом ничего не известно", но игра была написана явно такими же точно идеалистами, так что в конце, конечно же, побеждает [i]добро[/i] (а сюжет удобно останавливается в точке самой победы, после чего храбрые героини улетают домой, а местная флора и фауна снова остаётся одна на один со своими экологическими и прочими проблемами). 

Главная моя претензия к этой семичасовой игре сводится к тому, что она [i]никакая[/i] — студия, сделавшая SteamWorld, нацеливалась на милое лайтовое космическое приключение, а получилась безликая скукотища. Ну не прям ужас-ужас, но на мой взгляд не стоит своего времени, особенно если вы искушённый игрок. Технически игра сделана нормально, и на деке идёт хорошо, разве что в последней локации местами чуть подтормаживает, когда на экране появляется слишком много всего, ну и один раз я провалился в неудачный закуток, откуда не смог выпрыгнуть, пришлось загружать автосейв минутной давности.

Why do I play Cursebreaker?
It is a question I'm asking myself after 1h of play, again 4h later and now after 20h asking this the third time I realize that I should have never played, let alone buy this game.

So, why did it take me 20h? The game did scratches an old itch of playing old school games that experimented with leveling up skills by using them, such as Dungeon Siege, Ultima Underworld and the Elder Scrolls games. At the time I could ignore the lack of QoL features and accepted improvement as a simple bonus point without opening up new gameplay. And to be honest, I was fully immersed into most of those older titles. Today, games have evolved. The better ones bring interesting stories, will draw you into their world and you don't even realize how chockfull of QoL features they are. Today there are so many good/great ones that I cannot find time for all of them. Today, I can skip the filler ones, the mediocre and throw away the awful ones. Cursebreaker borders awful...

Some argue that not being able to play a woman is outrages. Long before having that discussion, I'm already disconnected by not being able to name my character... in an RPG?! Rothar... is that a name for a dog? Is it an easter egg to the second problem with this "RPG"? The second problem is that Rothar is a slave to a necromancer. Meaning you have no free will. You must play Rothar. Despite it is obvious that the necromancer Rothar serves is pure evil, all Rothar does is running around doing "goody two-shoes" fetch quests for imbecils: "Please can you harvest 5 barley, because my arm hurts!",  "Can you find my son a suitable wife?", "Can you cook 4 chickens and 2 fish for these poor lots?". The worst part is that Rothar has 200 uncooked chicken and 400 fresh fish, but there is NO stove to be found in the entire capital of this world?! Rothar needs to travel miles to get to some outskirt to cook the damn food. Oh yes, there is a "nearby" fireplace, but for some reason the raft to get there is on the other side of the river. Nowhere in the history of mankind has there ever been someone that took the time to make a raft for bridging a river and forgot to add a rope to use it in both directions, has there?

Anyway, the immersion of Cursebreaker really breaks when fighting mobs. While Rothar is killing a bandit inside its own camp, another bandit stands no more than 5 yards away idling, not being aware his friend is fighting for his life. Once Rothar finds an enemy too strong and flees, the enemy will stop the chase and runs back, start regenerating as a troll and suddenly zooms out and pops back where it started, completely void of any awareness of the previous fight. While looting a corpse, it is not uncommon that a new copy spawns back, because the respawn timer is extremely short, and immediately resumes the fight. Rothar can even make use of this to farm a unique boss that drops a lot of gold. Simply bind a key to "respawn nearby enemies" and Rothar doesn't need to wait or walk back like in Diablo. Another immersion breaker is how Rothar obtains crafting materials, in particular skins. While a farmer was trying to calm down Bessie, an old cow. Rothar was ranshaking the field. Killing all the other cows for a 50% of obtaining a cowhide, of which Rothar needed 4 to have himself crafted a set of "critterhunting gloves". There was one person that complained about the killing of crabs. Yes, crabs! But after butchering many of them for a few coins, she had no problem talking to Rothar without even the mentioning the crabs again. Did I mention that pathfinding is broken?

Coming to the improvement of Rothar. He possesses 12 skills. They start at level 1 and can be upgraded via use to level 100. After 20h I have a couple at 20-22 and most around level 15. And this is broken. I do not really care that it may take a long time, but leveling up does not bring new things, or rather new gameplay. As an example, basic woodcutting allows to cut down spruces (needle-leaved trees). With the wood Rothar can make a level 1 spruce bow (+3 accuracy, +1 damage). Rothar needs to get to level 20 woodcutting to cut down an oak. With level 20 crafting Rothar can make an oak bow (+60 accuracy, +3 damage) and Rothar needs level 20 archery to use that bow. But wait, leveling up woodcutting goes at a pace of 10 exp per chopped wood (Rothar gets nothing when a cut yields no wood). To get to level 20 Rothar needs exponentially more exp per level, already 1744 to go from level 15 to 16. How much wood does Rothar need for the spruce bow? That is right, 4! So after crafting hundreds of bows Rothar basically has leveled up. Rothar can also try to loot an oak bow from an enemy, but enemies that do are too strong (basically Rothar misses every shot) with a spruce bow. How does "accuracy" even work in this game? Is it an effective method to gate more difficult sections of the world? Leveling up attack skills (archery, melee, sorcery) is actually very silly and extremely boring. Rothar gains exp by the amount of damage he does. Hence, Rothar finds a training dummy (such as an archery target) and start hitting it for a couple of hours. Not a lot of fun, but at least it allows Rothar to equip that new bow. Hurrah!

All in all, Cursebreaker does not immerse. It is a time sink that does not reward you with anything interesting. The game lacks many QoL features (don't even start about storage and item management...), making it a tedious effort to make any progress. Better to not waste your time as Rothar.

Cursebreaker is a weird game to review. While playing it, I recognized that there were glaring flaws that could easily be deal breakers for many, but, still, I came back time and again to put more hours into it. Why? I think the answer is that I thought that if I dug deep enough into it, I would find a rough, overlooked, gem of a game that just took time discover. Well, after pouring more time into it than I probably should have, I can safely say that it's not what I had hoped.

Cursebreaker plays like an old school MMO, but it's single-player, for the most part. You can see other players around, but I don't think you can do much with them other than chat with and inspect them. No trading. I don't know if you can go out in the world together as I set it so that I would only see others in towns. Regardless, you get quests of varying difficulty and importance from NPCs and you level up a variety of skills that allow you access to new equipment, abilities, spells, crafting recipes, etc. Unfortunately, grinding these skills up can be quite a pain, and I found it difficult to have my non-combat skills keep pace with my combat skills.

Which brings me to combat. There are three main avenues of dealing damage; melee, ranged, and magic. I focused on magic, but also got my melee skills into good shape, as well. Given the rudimentary nature of the game, I'd say combat is fine, if a little boring. Melee is actually much more engaging, allowing players to actively hit buttons to do special moves like blocking any incoming attack with their shield or delivering a powerful kick that pushes both yourself and the enemy away from each other. The enemies you fight are quite varied across the game, though some enemy models are reused. One thing I noticed is that they don't really care about their friends all that much, so it's easy to hit one in a group with a ranged attack to pull it out and kill it on its own. I'd say this is actually a positive, as engaging more than one enemy at once is dangerous. There are some attacks/spells that hit more than one target, but I didn't find them to be very useful as using them often resulted in my death.

I turned off the music pretty quick so I could have either other music or a YT video playing on my other monitor. Sound effects were fine, though when you enter into or exit out of a cave the sound of a door opening is heard, so that's a little funny. 

I think the writing and the quests were fairly good, especially the longer, multi-stage quests. I found myself engaged in what was happening and wondering what going to happen in the story. However, some of the quests require you to have leveled a certain skill, which wasn't very fun if that was a skill I had neglected. That said, there were several times when the game would surprise me (in a good way) by doing something unexpected, which were usually related to a quest. 

There are some other mechanics in the game I didn't explore too deeply, such as buying and furnishing houses. There are several houses to purchase, but I only ended up buying one (apart from the starter home you're given) and putting in a few pieces of furniture. Likewise, I didn't do any ranged combat (with a bow), even though it's available.

As other reviewers have stated, the main story in this game is unfinished, so that's a real bummer. Additionally, there are areas later in the game that feel less fleshed out, with fewer quests, both large and small, compared to earlier sections. Unfortunately, it seems unlikely that any real development will be put back into this game, at least in the near future. 

Ultimately, I can't recommend this game, but not because I don't think it's good, but mostly because I don't think a majority of people would like it. I wouldn't have put so much time into it if I didn't have fun with it, but I think I had fun mostly because it scratched a very specific itch that I had. However, if you're looking for a game with skills to grind, old school graphics, and a sizable, yet digestible, world to explore, then you might like Cursebreaker if you can get it at a discount.

Rating: ★★★★★★★★☆☆ (8/10)

Watch Dogs is one of those games that got way more hate than it deserved. After fully completing the game and unlocking every achievement, I can confidently say it’s a serious, grounded, and underrated open world experience that aged surprisingly well. It might not have the variety or freedom of other Ubisoft titles, but it nails its atmosphere, story tone, and characters better than most newer Ubisoft titles.

Story Mode

You play as Aiden Pearce, a hacker driven by revenge after a tragedy that changed his life. While some people found him too cold or emotionless, I actually think he’s one of the most believable and serious protagonists Ubisoft ever made. His personality fits perfectly with the game’s darker tone quiet, determined, and haunted by guilt.
The story might not be revolutionary, but it’s tight and consistent. There’s a real sense of purpose in Aiden’s actions, and the game doesn’t try to make him a hero he’s flawed, but relatable like a Batman but without a costume. The tone of the narrative is mature and grounded, something that later sequels kind of lost unfortunately.

Open World

Chicago is beautifully recreated with a realistic, urban feel that fits the hacker theme perfectly. Hacking into traffic lights, cameras, and bank accounts still feels satisfying and clever even years later.
The problem comes with the side activities there are a lot of them, but most are too repetitive. Criminal convoys, gang hideouts, fixer contracts... after a while, it all starts feeling the same. Still, the city atmosphere and dynamic weather make exploration enjoyable.

Gameplay

The gameplay loop is fun, stealth mixed with hacking, shooting, and driving. Combat is satisfying, and using the environment to your advantage exploding traps or disabling enemies through cameras never gets old.
The driving can feel a bit floaty, but it’s manageable once you get used to it. The variety of weapons and gadgets keeps missions interesting, and you can approach most situations your own way guns blazing or silently through hacks.

DLC Bad Blood

The Bad Blood DLC is a great addition and easily one of the best post launch expansions Ubisoft has done for the series. You play as Raymond “T-Bone” Kenney, one of my favorite characters from the serie, a character with a strong personality and more humor compared to Aiden. His story is engaging and adds depth to the overall Watch Dogs universe.
Sadly, the same problem from the main game returns side missions get repetitive fast. Still, the new gadgets, missions, and co-op opportunities make it worth playing along with its story short but good.

Soundtrack & Atmosphere

The electronic soundtrack fits the tone perfectly, mixing tension and modern beats that match Chicago’s tech driven setting. Ambient city sounds, police radios, and rain on pavement make the world feel alive.

Achievements 100%

Going for 100% was a bit of a grind. Between collecting all audio logs, QR codes, and completing the side content it was really boring and too much, it can feel repetitive, but it’s rewarding once you see that final trophy pop up. The online invasions and multiplayer challenges add an extra layer of fun but nowadays it's rare to find people besides hack invasion, but they’re chaotic sometimes.

Conclusion

Watch Dogs is an underrated gem from Ubisoft’s library a serious, story-driven open-world game that doesn’t rely on over the top humor or endless filler. Aiden Pearce might not be the most charismatic hero, but he’s one of the most human and grounded ones.
Despite its repetitive side content, the strong story, hacking gameplay, and solid DLC (Bad Blood) make it a worthwhile experience, especially if you appreciate mature storytelling and tech thriller vibes.
It’s not perfect, but it’s one of those games that deserved better surely.

Thomasina’s complete obliviousness to the danger she’s bringing upon herself and everyone else builds up this slow, inevitable sense of doom. Watching the train crash in slow motion feels very typical of a Lovecraftian story.

My only real gripe is that Hob’s Barrow is labeled a horror game, but it doesn’t feel like one, creating a disconnect in the final act. Thomasina fears nothing, dismisses every supernatural warning, and stays firmly rooted in logic. How can you feel unease when the protagonist doesn't? Even trapped in the barrow, she’s unfazed. Slightly startled by hallucinated cats, then casually picks up a severed hand like it’s nothing. Girl. Fine. Summon the eldritch horror, then. So it ends up feeling more like a jaunty lil romp than true horror - which I kind of dig, but I don’t think that was the intention.

This is the best minimalistic city builder on the market. Low to the ground, high skill ceiling. It's worth your time and money. But hey, if that doesn't convince you (why would it?) let me explain:

If you are looking for a cozy experience read the upcoming comment;
If you are looking for a game to optimize the review starts from the line of asterisks ******

~For the Vibes~

Soundtrack: This game has a 10/10 soundtrack with over 90 minutes of runtime and they have additional island ambiance like bird calls or waves crashing. The soundscape has not gotten old, and that's coming from a player with over 200 hours in the game! Its up there with classics like Hardspace Shipbreaker, Poly Bridge 3, or Shapez 2.

Art Style: I mean, c'mon, you can see the game for yourself. Everything looks gorgeous on its own, and after a city starts to take shape the buildings start coalescing into districts that look absolutely wonderful. So much so that the devs have added a sandbox mode for you to create the city of your dreams, regardless of the points it produces.

UI: While this game might have you clicking and pointing at everything to make your decisions, there isn't a need for high-APM so it doesn't matter much. Granted, there are hotkeys for some things but they are hidden behind menus. This is good so as not to clutter the screen with senseless information, but newer or more casual players may never use the hotkeys. Its functionality is not perfect, but the aesthetic MY GOD THE LOOK OF THE UI. Each biome has a color palette it uses for the islands - which will also update the color palette of the UI - which will also update the color palette of your buildings, such a nice touch! And you can really notice all the light touches (from mouse-over sound effects) to little blips when new buildings get added to the bar. And don't even get me started on all of the animations for scoring points. Every point feels like it matters because each point is represented by a coin going into your score meter in the bottom right. It's bright and flashy, while somehow never getting old or in the way of things.

****************************
For the people who like to score chase:
It will take me too long to explain the intricacies of this game, either take a look at one of my videos (https://youtu.be/56vroBwZ91w), or take my 200 hours (with many more to come) as a testament to the depth and replayability of this game. For anyone that NEEDS a comparison to a different game to validate their purchase of this game, well I won't give it actually. Judge this game on its own merit, not the merit of others.

The game also has a plethora of novel challenges to try in case the base game isn't your style. Trust me, you will find a game-mode you adore, and there will be plenty of competition in it on the leaderboards. I hope to see you guys there >:)

Никогда не мог себе представить, что найдется игра, которая затмит для меня серию «Arkham» от “Rocksteady”. Конечно, это два разных проекта, с разными целями и задачами под аудиторию, и их не имеет никакого смысла сравнивать, но я сейчас имею ввиду не жанр, а эмоциональное наполнение после прохождения. Сейчас я попробую объяснить вам, почему я в таком восторге, и почему для меня этот проект по вселенной «Бэтса», становится отныне на первое место. 
Итак, внимание:
- Неповторимый, непредсказуемый сюжет, который вобрал в себя все лучшее от предыстории всех героев и злодеев, преподнеся это нам таким образом, что мы уже никогда не забудем первые встречи Бэтмена со своими врагами. Узнаем, на какой почве появились их конфликты, а так же, их становление от обычных чиновников или психопатов, до главарей преступного мира, их цели и мотивы, фактически с нуля.
- Я не знаю, кто писал эти диалоги, кто озвучивал персонажей, но фильмы Кристофера Нолана в чем-то даже проигрывают игре, от маленькой и скромной студии “Telltale”, которая лишний раз доказывает нам, что дело не в бюджетах и заголовках, а в любви к своему делу, бескорыстной идее донести свою мысль и свое видение вселенной через творчество, через свой собственный эксперимент.
Вспомните, какими были фильмы про «Бэтса» до Нолана, это была клоунада и позор. Мне видно лишь одно, что авторы слушали свой внутренний голос, когда делали игру, и не старались никому подражать, поэтому этот проект - бриллиант, в каждом своем аспекте, в каждой детали и тонкости.
- Первые появления персонажей здесь - это отдельный вид искусства. Ваше знакомство с Джоном Доу (фанаты и так знают кто это), Карменом Фальконе, Освальдом Кобблпотом, и конечно - Харви Дентом, врежутся вам в память навсегда. То, как разработчик меняет характеры персонажей в процессе игры, отталкиваясь от наших выборов, просто сводит с ума и не дает насытится эпизодом, как он уже заканчивается.
- Сама стилистика и атмосфера игры не так мрачна, как например в “Wolf among Us”, что для меня удивительно, ведь это прогнивший Готэм. Но и в этом есть что-то особенное, мрачной атмосферу делают именно поступки злодеев, и происходящие вокруг события, а не световой фильтр и текстуры. Особенно тучи сгущаются к концу игры, когда мы узнаем все о прошлом «Леди Аркхем».
- «QTE» эвенты сделаны здесь на самом высшем уровне. Они конкретно уничтожили все боевики, слэшеры, аркады, что были на моей памяти, где эта механика только бесила своим присутствием. Разработчики молодцы, они показали всем, в каком жанре, при каком повествовании нужно грамотно поименять эту механику, с какой периодичностью, чтобы она не выглядела глупо и не нужно, а наоборот, предстала основной фишкой и преимуществом. Такое чувство, что “QTE” создавалось специально для серии игр «Telltale», потому как лучше них это никто не научился делать, а на дворе уже 2025..
В общем и целом, минусов у проекта просто нет! Я даю вам гарантию, что вы не оторветесь, если начнете прохождение. Пройдя первую часть,  можно сразу перенести последствия своих выборов во вторую, делается это за 10-секунд, и невероятно увеличивает вайб от прохождения сиквела.
Мою оценку этой игре нельзя отразить в цифрах, мой восторг нельзя передать словами. Это просто то - что вы обязаны попробовать, пока у вас есть такой шанс!

Decided to take a journey through the Sumo Digital Sonic racing game series. I remember owning this for the Wii 10+ years ago, but didn't remember much about it going in initially.

To start, there are 3 main game modes

Grand Prix is pretty straight forward, race through 4 tracks in a cup and have the most points at the end to win. Three difficulties in Beginner Advanced and Expert, all affecting how aggressive the bots are. Regardless of difficulty I never had issues with the bots as even on the highest difficulty they could almost never catch me. If you know the lines for the maps, you'll have an easy time maintaining a lead. Only 6 cups with 4 courses each, you can breeze through all the cups on each difficulty in a couple hours.

Time Attack is also pretty straight forward, a mode to test how fast you can complete each course. In this game the Time Attack mode only times for a single lap as opposed to all 3 laps. There are staff ghosts you can race, and beating them is required for completion, but they were not difficult at all. I was able to beat all of them first try with Shadow.

Mission mode is arguably the most interesting game mode All Stars Racing has to offer, providing different challenges on each of the stages with different scenarios (EX: Drift as much as possible, hit the rival racer a certain amount of times, defeat a boss on the map, etc). You're graded on your performance from D - AAA, with A being the passing rank. Getting AAA on every mission is required for challenge completion, however most of them were pretty easy. There are over 60 missions to do so this is probably where you'll get the most of the challenge this game has to offer, and also probably have the most fun.

Characters and Tracks: There are 24 playable characters in total alongside 24 tracks. Out of the whole roster 7/24 characters are from Sonic the Hedgehog while 9/24 tracks are from Sonic the Hedgehog. While it's not too surprising to see Sonic highly represented in characters and tracks, it would've been nice to have a little more variety. The tracks are also a bit disappointing regarding variety. While there are technically 24 tracks in the game, there are only 8 distinct level themes, meaning the same 8 level themes are used 3 times throughout the game (3 Seaside Hill maps, 3 Super Monkey Ball maps, 3 Jet Set Radio maps, etc). This leads to a lot of the tracks blending together visually. If you showed me 2 maps from the House of the Dead series I could maybe tell which track was which, but i couldn't put a name to them. The tracks themselves are also pretty straightforward and a tad boring. While some have hidden routes that reward players who are on the lookout for shortcuts, they are pretty few and far between and most of the time everyone will be on one path. for the whole race. Some of the later maps are a bit trickier and reward players for mastering the game's handling (looking at you Monkey Target), and the track design shines the most with these tougher tracks.

Gameplay: All races are 3 laps with 8 players per race. It's a kart racer, you can grab items and use them to attack your opponents. All of your archetypes are covered with trap items, bouncing projectiles, tracking projectiles, etc. The items themselves are pretty bland, mostly just being generic things like boxing gloves and traffic cones, I think it would've been much cooler if these items were references to the SEGA properties in the game. The most unique item is the All Star item. This item is the super flashy powerful attack, and every racer has their own special attack catered to them (Sonic turns in Super Sonic, Billy Hatcher gets on a giant egg to run people over, Ryo gets forklift certified, etc). I really like that each All Star as a specialized icon in the item roulette as well, very nice touch. As cool as these sound on paper you are almost never going to find them as they are exclusively available to players stuck in the back of the pack. If you know what you're doing you will almost always be in the front and will never have access to these items unless you go out of your way to drive poorly and roll for them. 
The driving controls feel really good. It's very different from other kart racers, using the triggers for acceleration and drifting, which makes the game feel more like an arcade racer. Your primary way of maintaining high speeds is by building mini turbos with drift as well all doing tricks in the air. Bikes characters can also wheelie for free boosts making them much better than those driving normal cars. The main technique you'll need to know for some of the more challenging maps (again, looking at you Monkey Target) is releasing your accelerate to take tighter turns. There is no separate brake button, as your drift and brake button are tied to the same input. This control setup might take a bit to get used to but once it clicks the game feels incredibly satisfying to navigate.

Presentation: The game looks fine, about what I would expect from a game designed with the WII in mind. Environments look pretty even if the details are very simplified, I don't really any map being too hard to read save for some parts of the Final Fortress tracks being a bit dark. 
The music (and character voice clips) is pulled from each series' catalog of music, and you can choose which track plays during your race based on the level theme and what music is associated with it. This is a nice touch, as SEGA has a lot of nice music they pulled from, and changing the music can help break up the samey feeling some of the maps have with shared visuals. The announcer is very fun to have, though some people might find him grating. There is an option to disable him specifically if you don't want to hear his commentary but it adds so much character to the game despite being super corny.
The UI is fine, pretty simple but it gets the job done. My biggest issue with the UI is the mini map, or rather the lack of a mini map. Instead of a mini map showing where everyone is on the track, All Stars Racing thought it would be fun to have all race progress be tracked on a straight line, and icons would move closer or further to yours based on how close they are. This *works* but I would really rather have a map on screen to more easily keep tabs on where everyone is.

Multiplayer: Local or bust. There is no online option for the Steam version. I don't have anyone who would want to play this game locally, so I couldn't tell you how it is. 

Other things: Completion is pretty straightforward, I managed to finish every challenge in the game after about 16 hours of playtime, but there were a couple of challenges that were just filler. One of the secret challenges requires you to defeat 100 enemies on a specific type of map with a specific character, something you will almost never do naturally, I had to go out of my way to run multiple 9 lap races going out of my way to kill enemies on the map, this wasn't hard it was just time consuming. The other major slog challenge is the final SEGA miles challenge. By the time i finished every other challenge in the game, including the 100 enemies one I talked about before, i had only gotten 2/3 of the way done with the final SEGA miles milestone. Since I had literally nothing to work towards I had to run a bunch of 30 second long races for over 2 hours just to get enough miles to hit the last threshold. This didn't add anything to the game for me, only extending my playtime by a couple of hours. I assume this was supposed to be supplemented with multiplayer, however as mentioned before this version does not have online play, so you're not getting that unless you have someone to play with locally. 
I also wish there were options to change input bindings. You are stuck with the defaults whether on KBM or controller. The glyphs in-game also don't update if you're using a controller, so you'll just have to figure out the buttons on controller.
