This game is an insult to the Dead Space franchise but it is a great game by itself. I have listed the pro's and con's that I have found with this game.

[+] The gameplay is almost identical to Dead Space 2. The biggest difference is that you also shoot people which I do not have a problem with because I would imagine someone like Isaac Clarke would eventually have to kill actual people along the way to achieve his objectives. Plus, Isaac killing people is nothing new, he also killed people in Dead Space 2 who tried to kill him. Also you can crouch and roll which is great. Other than that, the controls and feeling of the game are almost identical to Dead Space.

[+] The game is actually very fun to play. I really enjoyed playing the game and shooting Necromorphs and solving puzzles which is consistent with the last two Dead Space games.

[+] I actually like the weapon crafting system. It does bring out the engineer within Isaac's character and it makes the game more interesting.

[+] Dead Space 3 has the longest campaign out of the two previous Dead Space games. I believe the campaign is around 12 hours long if you do the side missions which is another plus I like about this game, it gives the player feeling that they have more freedom and are more in control of Isaac.

[+] The added Necromorph lore was extremely important to this game and I'm glad we managed to get some more insight behind the Necromorphs and the Markers. 

Now for the negatives, and there are plenty.

[-] The biggest negative about this game is that there is too much action themed elements in this game and not enough horror. Dead Space is a survival HORROR franchise, not an action survival franchise. EA really took this amazing franchise and tried to spin it off as an action themed game to make it appeal to a larger audience for larger profit. The game does not take out the horror element entirely, there are still a good amount of horror themed moments scattered across the game, but overall it still feels like a more generally action-oriented game and this kills the vibe of Dead Space 3 compared to the previous Dead Space games.

[-] The action-themed music in the game does not belong in Dead Space at all. Dead Space is supposed to have purely horror driven music. I don't understand why I am playing a survival "horror" game and I'm hearing Marvel-themed music. It just doesn't fit with Dead Space at all.

[-] The developers decided to remove the shop and instead replace it with a resource type mechanic. Taking out the shop is already a massive L on its own because we are so used to having a shop in the previous Dead Space games. I like the new weapon crafting system, but taking out the shop is something that didn't sit right with me.

[-] The characters are absolutely unlikable. I don't want to talk too much in-depth about them because I do not want to spoil the game, but the majority of the characters who are supposed to be your allies are actually very hard to like. Even Carver was very hard for me to like.

[-] I don't mind the themes of romance in Dead Space 3 because there was already a theme of romance in Dead Space 1. But Dead Space 3 tries to put it all up in your face throughout the game, trying to navigate through the tiring love triangle between Isaac, Ellie, and Norton and it gets extremely exhausting because it distracts from the main premise of the game and makes you completely forget that you are supposed to be playing a survival "horror" game.

[-] EA decided that you have to pay to finish the actual ending of Dead Space 3. I think that speaks enough on its own.

Overall, this was a fun game to play. The actual gameplay and the Necromorph lore are probably the only two things that actually saved this game from being a commercial failure entirely. This hardly felt like a Dead Space game because it is the least scariest of the three games and I would agree with the statement that Dead Space 3 is the black sheep of the Dead Space games. Hopefully Visceral games wont have to keep pouring their effort into a company like EA and can actually make another Dead Space game like how they want to. So if you are looking for a fun survival horror shooter to play, I definitely recommend this game. But if you are a die-hard Dead Space fan, well I got bad news for you.

Bulwark: Falconeer Chronicles is an unusual and atmospheric take on the city-building genre, shifting its focus away from rigid optimization and instead embracing an almost meditative style of construction. Set in the flooded, windswept world of the Ursee—introduced previously in The Falconeer—the game trades aerial combat for architectural experimentation. You begin with nearly nothing: a surveyor ship, a lonely outpost, and a horizon filled with mist and towering fragments of rock. From these sparse beginnings, you slowly stitch together a sprawling network of walkways, platforms, towers, and settlements suspended above the ocean. The overarching narrative is one of rebuilding and reclamation, but the game is less concerned with storytelling and more interested in giving you space to shape the world at your own pace.

At the heart of the experience is a freeform construction system that encourages experimentation over precision. Instead of snapping neatly into a rigid grid or forcing you into strict resource bottlenecks, the building tools allow you to organically extend your fortress outward—bridges curve gracefully, towers sprout at uneven angles, and platforms stack in irregular shapes that give your settlement a unique silhouette. Resources like stone, iron, and wood are gathered automatically once you’ve connected your outpost to extractor sites, and from there the game becomes a gentle exercise in expanding your reach and maintaining a steady supply flow. The emphasis is on creativity rather than efficiency, and this relaxed approach makes the act of building feel fluid and expressive rather than mechanical.

Atmosphere is one of the game’s greatest strengths. The Ursee is rendered with a painterly sense of scale, with harsh skies, shifting seas, and distant ruins emerging from fog. The visual style is distinctive—clean, sharp, and heavily stylized—giving each structure a striking contrast against the ocean. The soundscape reinforces this contemplative mood: distant thunder, the low hum of machinery, and subdued ambient music contribute to the feeling of quiet resilience. As your fortress grows, there’s a strong sense of carving something monumental out of an empty and dangerous world, and that emotional texture is one of the most memorable aspects of Bulwark.

However, the tranquility of the experience also highlights its limitations. Because the focus is so firmly placed on creative construction, the strategic depth is relatively shallow. Combat exists, but only lightly; encounters lack the tension or tactical challenge found in more traditional strategy titles. Exploration is present but not especially dynamic, and much of the game’s progression follows a soft, self-directed arc rather than a structured campaign. This makes Bulwark ideal for players who enjoy open-ended creativity but less appealing for those who want clear goals, demanding resource management, or layered systems.

Despite these constraints, the game carves out a distinctive niche. It offers something few city-builders attempt: a calm, unhurried sandbox where the pleasure lies in shaping a world rather than conquering it. The interface is intuitive once mastered, and the game plays smoothly whether you use a mouse or a controller. It runs well on a variety of hardware, including handheld PCs, and its simple logic systems make it approachable even for genre newcomers. For players who enjoy designing elaborate fortresses, creating visually striking settlements, or losing themselves in a world that moves at a soothing pace, Bulwark provides a compelling and memorable experience. Those seeking challenge or complexity may drift away sooner, but for anyone drawn to creativity, exploration, and atmosphere, this is a uniquely satisfying journey across the endless Ursee.

Well, I’m going to start this off by saying this wasn’t my first playthrough of I Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream. I first played it back in the early 2000s on my oldest cousin’s Dell laptop, so for me, this was a nostalgic experience. Let’s begin.

I Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream began as a short story written in 1967 by Harlan Ellison and was later adapted into a video game in 1995. I see this game as a haunting and unique experience that blends psychological horror, moral philosophy, and ethical boundaries. It’s a vintage point-and-click masterpiece that becomes unforgettable. The story dives deep into the darkest parts of humanity—confronting guilt, cruelty, and raw survival. Each character’s arc gives a chilling glimpse into their suffering and redemption.

The point-and-click gameplay adds nostalgic charm, reminding me of my childhood with my cousins. Sitting there, clicking through this desolate world, never feels boring or repetitive like other games in the genre. The puzzles are challenging yet grounded, offering just enough complexity without overdoing it.

The soundtrack deserves special praise—it’s eerie, immersive, and perfectly atmospheric. It captures every emotional shift, enhancing tension and reflection alike. Every sound, from the music to the ambient noises, pulls you deeper into this world. Huge credit to John Ottman for composing such a hauntingly effective score.

What surprised me most is how replayable it is. Each run can unfold differently, and chasing achievements or exploring alternate paths keeps it engaging. Even decades after its release, I Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream remains a timeless masterclass in storytelling, mood, and moral tension.

I hope anyone who plays this game enjoys it as much as I did.

Многие игроки обходят такие проекты стороной, а некоторые и вовсе не считают их играми, наивно полагая, что это всего лишь детские книжки с картинками. Эти люди даже не подозревают, от чего отказываются. А ведь данную визуальную новеллу пропускать никак нельзя, если, конечно, вы не боитесь столкнуться со скримерами и по-настоящему жуткими сценами.

Чем же игра подкупает в первую очередь?
— [b]Великолепный арт[/b], который идеально передаёт как ностальгическую теплоту 90-х годов, так и нарастающее ощущение ужаса.
— [b]Цепляющая история[/b], где загадка исчезновения детей переплетается со славянским фольклором и личными драмами персонажей.
— [b]Хоррор-элементы[/b], которые не просто добавлены для галочки, они пронизывают каждый эпизод, вызывая постоянное, щемящее чувство тревоги.

Отдельный плюс за [b]озвученные диалоги на русском языке[/b], что является большой редкостью среди визуальных новелл. Озвучка выполнена профессионалами, голоса настолько живые и эмоциональные, что полностью раскрывают характеры персонажей.

Некоторые проходят данную игру на ютубе, что лучше не делать, ведь чтобы по-настоящему проникнуться игрой, нужно самому погрузиться в процесс, читая текст и принимая самостоятельные решения для развития сюжета. Именно ваши, зачастую неочевидные, выборы влияют на ход событий, что добавляет игре реиграбельности. А если играть ночью, в полной тишине, можно испытать непередаваемую атмосферу детских страшилок из 90-х. Признаюсь, игра местами пугала до мурашек, а порой удивляла настолько, что хотелось аплодировать разработчикам.

Strange Horticulture is an interesting game. I played it in English, which is not my native language, so sometimes I had to translate letters and notes on my phone. It was a nice way to practice my language skills.
After finishing the game once, I saw that Steam didn't show 100% completion, so I played it again to see why. In total, I played twice, but it still didn't reach 100%. Later, I found out that the game has different endings based on a few key choices, but the main story and puzzles stay the same. I guess you need to finish the game around eight times to get full completion.
Because most things stay the same, replaying it many times can feel repetitive.

[h2]Sinopsis[/h2]
Strange Horticulture es un ingenioso juego de investigación y rompecabezas, donde tendremos que cultivar e identificar una gran variedad de plantas, todo bajo unas mecánicas Point & Click. Tras el fallecimiento de nuestro tío, recibimos como herencia una herboristería llamada “Strange Horticulture”, situada en el peculiar municipio de Undermere. El negocio consiste en cultivar plantas con diversas propiedades y atender a los clientes que buscan ayuda y consejo en nuestros remedios botánicos. El problema es que las plantas que disponemos no se encuentran etiquetadas y carecemos de los amplios conocimientos de nuestro tío, por lo que tendremos que investigar en nuestros ratos libres la forma de conseguir nuevos ejemplares y catalogar los ya existentes con su nombre correcto. Sin embargo, no tardaremos en vernos envueltos en un peligroso y antiguo misterio que asola estas tierras, donde los secretos, la magia y el misticismo se mueven entre sectas y hechiceros.

[h2]Jugabilidad / Apartado técnico[/h2]
En Strange Horticulture nuestro principal cometido será regentar nuestra herboristería. Por un lado, tendremos las estanterías donde iremos colocando todas nuestras plantas y por otro, nuestro escritorio, donde podremos consultar un detallado mapa de la región, la enciclopedia botánica o todas las notas y cartas que vayamos recibiendo. A lo largo de varios días, iremos recibiendo clientes en busca de alguna planta particular. Como ya he comentado, las plantas de las que disponemos no están identificadas, por lo que tendremos que acudir a la enciclopedia o estudiarlas individualmente, extrayendo pistas o detalles de sus hojas, flores y propiedades, de forma que podamos identificarlas y etiquetarlas. 
De forma paralela al negocio, iremos recibiendo visitas de personajes relevantes en la historia, cartas o mensajes secretos, los cuales nos irán aportando pistas de lugares que visitar gracias a nuestro detallado mapa de la región. En estos lugares encontraremos misiones secundarias, revelaremos secretos y conseguiremos nuevas plantas para proseguir en la trama. En momentos puntuales podremos decidir si ayudar o perjudicar a algún personaje (según la planta que le entreguemos), influyendo en el desarrollo y desenlace de la trama, que cuenta con varios finales alternativos.

[h2]Valoración[/h2]
Strange Horticulture es un juego que se muestra la mar de interesante, porque detrás de su aparente simpleza se esconde un juego lleno de secretos y variadas mecánicas. Por un lado, la identificación de plantas responde a nuestra capacidad de observación y deducción a partir de escasas notas o dibujos, algo que al principio parece complejo, pero que está perfectamente equilibrado para no ser frustrante o injusto. Por otro lado, las ubicaciones que tenemos que encontrar en el mapa no se dan a la ligera, sino que tendremos que deducirlas a partir de mensajes encriptados, adivinanzas, acrósticos, etc., o empleando objetos sobre el mapa, como un monóculo especial, una rueda con símbolos, cartas con recortes que coinciden con elementos del mapa, etc. Todo esto, sumado a su interesante historia, sencilla jugabilidad, variedad/diseño de plantas y la posibilidad de encontrar distintos finales, hacen que Strange Horticulture sea una obra maestra para los amantes de los juegos de investigación, el misterio y los rompecabezas. Personalmente reconozco que me lo he pasado en dos largas sesiones de vicio, me ha enganchado mucho, algo muy de agradecer, ya que últimamente es difícil que un juego sorprenda.

✔️ [b]Positivo[/b]:[list]
[*]Mecánicas muy interesantes y variopintas, donde se mezcla el cultivo e identificación de plantas con la resolución de puzzles y acertijos de forma muy original y entretenida. 
[*]Historia atractiva, llena de secretos que se van revelando progresivamente. El juego cuenta con 8 finales diferentes según las decisiones que tomemos y a quien ayudemos o perjudiquemos.
[*]Diseño gráfico muy llamativo en general, tanto del escenario como de los personajes, pero en especial, de las más de 70 especies de plantas que nos encontraremos, cada una con características morfológicas que necesitaremos observar para identificarlas con la enciclopedia. [/list]
❌ [b]Negativo[/b]:[list]
[*]Se echa en falta que quede un registro de las ubicaciones que visitamos sobre el mapa (yo lo he llevado con un Excel). Además, convendría que ciertas palabras clave de la enciclopedia pudiesen resaltarse o subrayarse, ya que de cara al final del juego tendremos que buscar ciertas características entre más de 70 páginas de texto.
[*]Para poder investigar una región del mapa necesitamos energía, la cual se consigue con el paso del tiempo o regando plantas, una tarea algo lenta y tediosa en ocasiones. Al igual que tener que etiquetar manualmente cada planta.
[*]A pesar de tener 8 finales, varios de ellos se parecen mucho entre sí. Algunos de ellos están ligados a decisiones al comienzo de la aventura, por lo que en caso de querer ver todos los finales tendremos que repetir el juego casi de cero. [/list]

📢 [b]Idioma[/b]: Interfaz y subtítulos en español.
⌛ [b]Duración[/b]: 6-7 horas juego base/ 8-10 horas para 100%.
🎮 [b]Steam Deck[/b]: Verificado, funciona perfectamente.

[H1]Sadly more trolleys than dilemmas. Still funny, but not at all what I expected[/H1]

Let’s be clear: The Trolley Solution is not the philosophical crisis simulator I signed up for. I came for moral dilemmas mixed with cute random mini-games, not a plethora of mini-games that occasionally throw in a choice like “Who gets splashed? You or a random stranger?” and call it a day. It’s funny and quirky, yes, but don’t expect to debate about life while pressing the right click button at high speed.

That being said, the mini-games themselves are entertaining (at first). They’re varied, occasionally absurd, and really original. You can also customize the color palette, which gives the game some accessibility perks and a fun touch, especially if you put everything in black and red like in that one evil mode guide. I genuinely laughed a few times (“Trolley-san” is going to haunt my brain forever) and the collection of philosopher trading cards is a clever touch. There’s also an “after-ending” update system that adds new twists and mini-concepts over time, which is limited, but enjoyable.

There is one main issue though: the fun burns out fast. The mini-games keep getting longer, the actual trolley dilemmas stay scarce, and what once felt chaotic and witty becomes a bit of a slog. And don’t even get me started on achievements: if you’re a completionist, brace yourself for 3 full playthroughs of identical content, unless you specifically plan 2 whole playthroughs around the achievements (which kind of defeats the whole purpose of the game). It’s not difficult, it’s just…tedious. The replay value is nonexistent, and by the time I hit my third run, I was basically controlling the trolley out of spite.

Overall, The Trolley Solution isn’t a bad game. It just doesn’t deliver what its title or premise promise. The disclaimer at the bottom of the description is commendable, but not enough. If you’re in for mindless fun, absurd humor, and cute mini-games, go for it. If you were expecting ethical brain-benders and true moral torment accompanying said mini-games, well…the track doesn’t lead there.

I will preface this review with three questions, and if the answer is "Yes" to any of these questions then I suggest you give Mortal Online a long hard look; if you say "Yes" to all of these questions then stop reading this start downloading Mortal Online! 

--------------------

Questions: 

1.  Are you tired and/or burnt out on all the MMORPGs out, or coming out, on the market?

2.  Do you want to play a game where EVERYTHING you do is an accomplishment and reinvigorates that sense of discovery you had when you played your first MMORPG?

3.  Does the idea of an open loot system (you lose everything you are carrying when you die) fill you with a sense of excitement and adventure?

--------------------

Overview

Mortal Online is a Fantasy Sandbox MMORPG that takes familiar elements from games like Ultima Online and Runescape, and takes them to a whole new level.  The entire game is played in first-person, and there is no functionality to change the view to third-person.  All combat and actions within the game are based off of targeting with your reticle, so if you want to hit a boar in the head then you need to aim for it's head.  Character progression is based on skill points rather than levels, and you only have so many skill points to use.  You aren't safe anywhere, not even in cities, so always be on your guard, but don't turn into a jerk, just be wary.

--------------------

Skills

Skills are broken down into a ton of different categories that are based on Parent and Child relationships, so a player would need to learn Armor Crafting (to a certain skill level) before he/she can learn Soft Armor Crafting.  Many skills you can begin learning just by attempting to do them, such as chopping down a tree or mining for ore, but other skills will need to be learned by reading skill books.  Skill books can be obtained from Libraries (for a price) or from the Auction House, players can begin reading these (some can take 8 hours or more) and the reading timer will continue to countdown when the player logs off.  

I mentioned that you have a finite number of skill points to use, and in the beginning, you will burn through over half of these pretty quickly.  Don't panic!  You can lock skills that you don't want to increase anymore and you can even decrease skills you aren't going to use to get the skill points back to use on something else.  This can be confusing at first, but this really allows the player total freedom in choosing what their character does without letting characters become masters of everything at once.

--------------------

Combat

Combat is based on using your aiming reticle and blocking or dodging the attacks of your enemies.  I haven't done much of this yet, besides slaughtering herds of innocent pigs, but I think it is very engaging, sort of a melding between Skyrim and Mount & Blade combat, but better.

--------------------

Magic

No comment at all on this, but it is very in depth, with required components for spells.  Healing magic, for instance, can require water.

--------------------

Crafting

The crafting in this game is intense.  I repeat: the crafting in this game is INTENSE.  There are spreadsheets and emulators online that help players calculate the required components to create other components to finally (maybe) create the item they want to create.  There is more than one way to make a particular piece of armor, and some components will make the end item heavier or cooler etc.  I think this is an amazing part of the game, but it is not for the faint of heart.

--------------------

PvP

Mortal Online works on a flagging system.  Here is the breakdown:

Fledgling: Yellow
Innocent: Blue
Criminal: Grey
Murderer: Red
Hidden Criminal: Grey with Blue Stripe

Basically, if you do something negative to someone then you will be flagged Grey, unless that person was already Grey.  The flagging system is one of the most important parts of MO to understand, so check out this Beginner's Guide for more information : http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=519329793.

--------------------

Conclusion

Mortal Online is a really in-depth game, but it is most certainly not for the casual player, and I don't mean the time-casual player, but the player that is more instant gratification.  If you want your cake and eat it too then this game is not for you, but if you want to bake your cake, eat some of your cake, then sneak around to hide your cake in the bank until you can share it with your guild mates then this game is for you!  

You can try the game for free, and all F2P Accounts can use skills up to skill level 60.  What that means is that you can raise your skills above skill level 60, but you can only use the skill at skill level 60.  I highly recommend subscribing to the game if you are 8 hours in and enjoying it.  The subscription costs less than other MMORPGs, and it is well worth it to support such an awesome game.

--------------------

Grimstein's Personal Tips

1.  Buy the Reading Skill Book (yes, that's an actual skill book) and begin reading that right away.  That will allow you to read other skill books more efficiently.

2.  Find a Guild on the official MO forums.

3.  Get out of the starting city.

4.  Turn up your graphics and other options as high as you can.

5.  Only keep what you immediately need on you.  Bank your money until you need to buy something, and keep your skill books in the bank until you want to start reading them.

6.  If you are going on a long journey, such as to join up with your new guild, bring along some food and bring everything you can with you.  Banks are localized, and if you store something in Tindrem, you will have to go back to Tindrem to get it.

--------------------

I hope my review helped you make an informed decision.  There is so much more to Mortal Online than I touched upon in this review, but I hope it gives you a taste of what's in store if you play.  Good luck, and I hope to see you in Nave!

Evris Grimstein

Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name é uma carta de amor ao nosso amado Kazuma Kiryu. Além de ser um excelente jogo, foi o primeiro que eu tive o prazer (e me dispus a isso) de fazer todas as conquistas e faria novamente. 

O jogo é chamado de Spin-off, mas ele basicamente faz parte da jornada de Kiryu como um todo. Mesmo o jogo funcionando como uma DLC standalone, ele entrega tudo que precisamos para um jogo completo. Porém, é importante ter em mente de que ele é uma péssima porta de entrada para a franquia, então evite começar por ele. (Você vai ficar boiando legal)

A história acontece logo após os acontecimentos o sexto título, onde Kiryu decide desaparecer por um tempo e seguir a sua vida protegendo quem ama. . Agora, Kiryu é um agente da facção Daidoji sob o nome de Joryu. Sim, eu sei, para alguém que não quer ser identificado, o nome não ajuda. A Daidoji é uma organização secreta que atua principalmente na política e economia do Japão, então Kiryu é uma peça-chave para eles. Nisso, ele terá que fazer de tudo para que não seja descoberto e possa viver a vida em paz (em algum momento isso tem que acontecer, porque Jesus amado).

O jogo traz dois estilos de luta: o estilo agente, focado em usar apetrechos como o sapato a jato e o cigarro explosivo, além de ser muito útil em combate com vários inimigos. E o estilo Yakuza, que é uma mistura de tudo que já vimos do Dragão de Dojima até agora, focado principalmente no combate mano a mano. Os estilos de luta são bem característicos e funcionam muito bem. Tudo é muito plástico e bem fluído, mesmo o jogo tendo apenas 6 meses para ser desenvolvido, já que foi feito entre o Ishin e o Infinite Wealth. 

Teremos apenas 2 lugares principais na nossa jornada em Gaiden: a clássica Sotenbori em Osaka e o Castle, um castelo enorme no meio de um navio. Sotenbori é a mesma de sempre e eu adoro revisitá-la. Já o Castle, é um lugar totalmente novo onde temos vários minigames, como cassinos e cabarés e teremos o coliseu. Aqui, o coliseu recebeu uma atenção maior e temos bem mais variedade de lutas dentro desse sistema, além de ele estar atrelado ao enredo também. 

Quanto aos seus gráficos, o jogo brilha em trazer a Dragon Engine em uma de suas melhores formas. O jogo é tão bonito quanto Yakuza Kiwami 2 e Yakuza 6. Ele sofre com um pouco de serrilhado em alguns momentos bem específicos, mesmo eu tendo jogado com o DLAA ativado. Isso provavelmente acontece devido a falta de polimento do jogo em certas partes, mas nada que tire seu brilho como um todo. 

Já na performance e otimização temos um jogo digno da franquia. A RGG nunca decepciona em trazer um jogo devidamente otimizado no PC e rodando com poucos bugs significativos. Eu não enfrentei nenhum problema relevante durante toda a minha gameplay com o jogo, então provavelmente você também não enfrentará. 

No geral, o jogo é um excelente título para a franquia e nos oferece um enredo emocionante e digno de nos tirar uma lágrima ou outra no final. Se voCê nunca jogou nenhum jogo da franquia, passe longe desse por enquanto, mas se já é fã de carteirinha, esse é um título obrigatório para todos. 

Ele está custando R$ 250,00 no preço cheio e R$ 270,00 na versão Deluxe. Se possível, pegue-o em promoção na versão Deluxe, já que os personagens extras vão ser úteis durante o jogo (se você focar no Coliseu, claro. E eles são jogáveis)

Jogue Like a Dragon Gaiden e seja uma pessoa feliz. Logo mais trarei uma análise completa em vídeo aqui e você poderá aproveitar também.

Для меня «The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe»  — шедевр игрового искусства, который поднимает важные философские вопросы (свобода воли vs предопределенность, значение выбора) и дарит незабываемый опыт.   

Самое необычное в игре — свобода выбора. Можно следовать инструкциям  или пойти против них, создавая свою собственную версию сюжета. 

Игра начинается с простого офисного работника Стэнли, чья жизнь внезапно превращается в интерактивную историю, управляемую рассказчиком. Чем дальше погружаешься в сюжет, тем больше понимаешь, насколько важен выбор игрока и насколько непредсказуем финал - каждый поворот ведет к новым открытиям и неожиданностям (и, как следствие, к новым концовкам).
Да, иногда приходится делать выбор, который ни на что не влияет - это создает ощущение бессмысленности действий, подчеркивая абсурдность ситуации, но абсурд - это неотъемлемая часть всей истории.

Чем зацепила меня игра с первой же секунды? Ответ очевиден - рассказчиком. Он добавляет игре особый шарм и заставляет улыбнуться даже в самые напряженные моменты; он постоянно комментирует ваши действия, иногда даже вмешиваясь в процесс и меняя ход событий. Это нарушает традиционную структуру повествования и определенно создает комичный эффект.

Резюмируя, скажу, что «The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe» — это уникальная игра-путешествие. Если вам надоели линейные сюжеты и предсказуемые истории, то эта игра точно для вас!

[h1]他のシミュレーター系を一つのゲームにまとめた作品[/h1]

～～シミュレーターというショップ経営系のシミュレーターが数多く存在する。

本作はショッピングモールを舞台にし、「中にある店舗を複数経営」というこれまでのシミュレーター系にあった様々な店舗を経営できるといういいとこどりになっている。

最初はアパレルショップから始まるが、その先はどの店をオープンさせるかプレイヤーの自由になっているのが嬉しい。

店の種類は
　・アパレルショップ
　・スポーツ用品店
　・おもちゃ屋
　・スーパーマーケット
　・ゲーム屋
　・PC/スマホ屋
　・化粧品屋
　・カフェ
　・インテリアショップ
　・ゲーセン
　・映画館
　・ハンバーガーショップ
　・宝石屋
　・花屋
　・寿司屋
と大半は既にシミュレーターとして販売されている。

ゲームの進め方も
　・アパレルショップでとことん稼いでから他の店をオープンさせる
　・アパレルショップで他の店の開店資金が貯まったらオープンさせる
という[u]プレイヤーの好きなタイミングで進められる[/u]のが変な縛りがなくて良い。

また
　・自販機
　・ATM
　・プライズゲーム
　・フォトマシーン
　・TCG販売機
などの小物も序盤からどんどん設置可能。

さらに嬉しいのがスタッフ雇用だ。

販売スタッフ、在庫補充スタッフの2種類存在するが[u]ゲーム序盤から安価で雇用可能[/u]である。

なので[u]「アパレルショップをとっととスタッフに任せて自分は新しい店を開ける」[/u]という遊び方もスタッフ雇用の条件が易しいからこそできるというわけだ。

あと細かいところで言うとショッピングモールそのものと店舗ひとつひとつに命名可能なのも地味にありがたい。

値段設定については競合同様に行えるようになっていて、確認した範囲だと「2割増し」までは文句なしで買ってくれるが「3割増し」にすると買ってくれる客はいるが、文句が出始める。

商品の品揃えについては「高額商品のみ」で問題ないバランスとなっている。バリエーションが少ないことに不満を言う客はいるが、誤差レベルで少ないので利益率の高い商品に統一してしまって問題なさげである。

[h1]翻訳[/h1]

中華フォントを使用しているが翻訳そのものは自然。

[h1]操作・UI・UX[/h1]

競合とほぼ同じ操作だがレジ操作でカード払いに対して確定操作でSpaceは適用されていない。

一方で現金払いに対しては最後の1枚のコインを選択した段階で支払いが確定するので少し楽。

商品の購入時の送料は存在しない。

購入した商品はそれぞれの店舗の出入り口に配置されているのでアクセスは良好。

段ボールからの補充も動きがスムーズで、なんと段ボールの在庫が0になった瞬間に段ボールが自動消滅するので便利。

補充スタッフは出入り口に置かれた段ボールから勝手に持って行ってくれるのでわざわざ在庫棚に段ボールを置く必要はない。

ショッピングモールは広いこともあり、プレイヤーの移動速度は早め。

開店はショッピングモールに入って左手のスイッチで開店。閉店も同様の操作。

時間は開店前と22時以降は時間が止まっているので、そこで色々行うことになる。

[h1]問題点[/h1]

・3時間もプレイするとプレイヤーは「商品の発注」と「機械の補充」という単調な作業がメインとなるので同ジャンルに慣れていると早い段階で飽きが来る

・他の作品でもあるが、新しいライセンスに金を払ってもアンロックされる商品が必ずしも現在より利益の出る商品であるとは限らないこと（バリエーションを揃える必要のないゲームデザインなので「ただのリソース損」となっていてリソースを無駄にしたストレスを感じる）

・PC屋のような高額商品の店をオープンしても差額による利益が他の店と変わらない割に全般的に購入費用が高いため、早期で開店させるメリットが皆無となっており、自由度の高さの割に順当に安い店からオープンさせていく保守的なプレイのほうが効率がいいという面白みのなさ

・プレイを重ねるほど同じ商品を発注し続けることになるが、その繰り返しに対する利便さが用意されていない

・最適化が足りておらず、ゲームを進めれば進めるほど処理が重くなっていき、最初は日を跨ぐ処理で10秒、２０秒、30秒かかるようになって最終的には「応答なし」が表示されるようになり、通常のプレイ時においてもコマ落ちが頻繁に発生してゲームとしてまともに遊べなくなる（重くなり始めるタイミングとしては全体の1/3店舗を運営するあたりからで全体の2/3へ到達するあたりでまともにプレイできなくなる）

[h1]まとめ[/h1]

People have been talking about this game for a while as sort of a successor to Obra Dinn. It's not an adventure game, it's a detective type game where you're just filling in the blanks (literally) as to who everyone is and what transpired in the scene you are viewing. There are 11 main game scenes and 6 DLC scenes. Base game took me about 4 hours and the DLCs took about the same amount of time despite being half the number of levels.

The core story is entertaining and would make a good novel (DLCs as well, which are a prequel). However, I think it hits better if you don't figure out the twist early; I think the seed is planted too soon in the plot. The sounds are fine but nothing to write home about. Scenes are very slightly animated so they are not completely static, and the art style is kind of uniquely unpleasant, so at least it stands out.

The core issues I have with the game are twofold: First, the difficulty of the base game is lacking. Over the course of 11 levels only a handful really used the mechanics beyond an extremely surface level implementation. The DLC missions fix this somewhat. Secondly, the implementation itself has core flaws related to grammar. Verb words (typically blue) will have tense endings attached to them which practically reduces the number of valid choices by 50% or more in many cases. In some rare cases (one particularly nasty one in the second DLC), there are additional articles before where a word should go which makes the correct answer grammatically incorrect. I understand the difficulties of implementing this kind of system, especially if you are translating into multiple languages, but the end result in this case is a huge disservice to the game's premise.

Ultimately though, while I think the game doesn't quite deserve the level of praise and attention it's gotten, it's still quite good, and the DLCs are a welcome increase in challenge if you enjoy the base experience.

I knew this game wasn’t gonna be super good when I bought it, purely judging from the reviews. What I didn’t know though was that the reason for it being bad is that once you pass the tutorial segment it is just an empty shell of nothingness.

First and foremost, I wasn’t super happy when I first launched this game and found out that they force you to sign up to WB in order to play. So, after giving them money for a copy of their game, they still demand things from you in exchange to let you play. A bad start already.

After finally getting in, I played through the training levels, which do a good job teaching you all the different roles, I actually did enjoy the training a lot. Though I don’t understand why they recommend playing this with a controller. I tried both controller and mouse and keyboard and I found mouse and keyboard superior in every way. It is so much easier to control when you turn with your mouse. I also found it quite annoying that the game constantly returns to the character editor after every single match in the tutorial stage, like why?

After finishing the tutorial segment though, I realized why this game never really succeeded. Lets start with the fact that there is no story mode. There is a career mode however, but it is nothing but a few generic matches bundled into 3 or 4  tournaments and boom, it’s over (I looked this up on YouTube). Like, I don’t give a fuck about multiplayer, and even if I did, it is totally dead anyway, so without a proper story mode, there is nothing for me to do in this game. It would have been so cool if you could actually have made a meaningful character with a real story mode attached to it and where you chose what position on the team you wanted to play. I imagine one where your character starts off in small leagues but through hard practice and dedication makes it into the big league by the end. Maybe you start as a first year at the wizard school and would have to juggle between schoolwork and quidditch practice and balance it all to become the best, and eventually end up being signed to one of those world champion teams by the end of it all. But there is none of that. Maybe my vision is unrealistic, but it would need all of that for me to pay 30 bucks for it.

The quidditch itself is actually pretty fun and I think they made it quite well, like the mechanics of it all. It is just all the rest that is missing. It feels like a long demo. I am lucky that I realized this when I was still under the 2 hour mark so I could refund it. I know a lot of people weren’t that lucky.

I loved Carrier Command back in the day, and even had a good time with Gaea Mission. This game is not really either of those games.

This game does what the basics of that of Commanding a Carrier force from a bridge and moves it towards the VR realm. A nice idea in principal where all of the controls are part of the environment rather than mapped to buttons. To interact with a system push a button in the game space. A lovely Idea for immersion But....

The OG Carrier Command and Gaea Mission you could play single player as you could set a load out, and task a launch and a destination from the bridge of a carrier, but you were just moving between screens, so you could toggle to something that required your attention in the game space relatively seamlessly.

In this game you need go from sitting down at one console to load out a Tank / Helicopter / Plane, move to another console to launch it, interact with another console to task it or control it directly, all the while taking your boat to somewhere on an island without crashing into anything expensive.

The busy work can be great for immersion and to keep you occupied (You can turn on spotlight and aim them and change the intensity of displays) has no tangible effect on the actual game play tasks but clearly included for the people think that those features are really really important.

But as a single player experience it is too akin to needlessly spinning plates to be absorbing.

If you have a selection of friends who loves the minutia of a process and nautical themed battle simulations, congratulations on finding each other, you guy and gals will probably have a blast delegating tasks within this game.

If you and your friends can commit to what is probably a solid few hours of gaming together.

If you (Like me) are the sort of person who loves the minutia of a process and nautical themed battle simulations an plays video games to escape people like me, this is not the single player experience for you.

Якщо б я описав DOOM Eternal одним словом — це шаленство. Гра створена не для того, щоб “сидіти і чекати”, вона створена для того, щоб кидатися в бій, рухатись безупинно, використовувати все, що маєш, домінувати. Коли ви берете кермо за Doom Slayer — це не просто “герой стріляє”, це “герой, що розтрощує, розриває, літає, рве і крутиться”. Ви відчуваєте силу, але й відповідальність: не зупинятись, слідкувати за ammo/броню/здоров’ям, обирати правильну зброю, вчасно перемикатись.

Візуально гра вражає: величезні арени, багаті локації, демонські простори, технологічні комплекси, міста під кроком апокаліпсису. Саундтрек б’є прямо в серце фанатів екшену — це “метал + пекло + рух”.

Але… є “але”. Якщо у вас очікування типові: “просто увімкнув, побіг, стріляю, насолоджуюсь” — DOOM Eternal це дає, але ще й дає додатково: платформінг, хитромудрі арени, слабкості ворогів, зміни темпу. І деколи це може вимагати більше, ніж просто “розважитись”. Деякі рецензії справедливо зазначають, що це може знизити “чистоту” досвіду.

Отже, рекомендую DOOM Eternal тим, хто:

- Любить FPS, де не просто стріляти, а чуватись вправним, рухатись, думати на ходу.
- Має терпіння до того, що гра може мати “платформінг” чи “бути складною” в окремих моментах.
- Хоче масштаб, “епікшн”, показову силу героя‑Слєєра.

Менш рекомендую, якщо:

- Ви більше цінуєте чисту простоту, атмосферу, де “відпочиваю і граю” без великих механік.
- Не хочете відчувати, що гра “вимагає” від вас постійної концентрації.
- Вам більше імпонує темна, сувора, менш “аркадна” атмосфера.

Висновок:

DOOM Eternal — це не просто продовження, це апгрейд формули, який піднімає планку, але й вводить нові вимоги до гравця. Він не ідеальний, але він вражає. І якщо вам хочеться “вибухового” шутера, який не соромиться бути складним, коли треба, і величезним — це один із кращих виборів. У порівнянні з DOOM (2016) — він цікавіший боєво, але можливо менш “чистий” у відчутті.

Якщо б я мав підсумувати: „Візьми рушницю, бігай як скажений, розтрощуй демонів — і не зупиняйся“)). Це DOOM Eternal у своїй суті.

9 Dragons is a game that has gone through many changes and publishers since 2006. I have followed it from the early days from when it was published by Acclaim to present day where it is now published by RedFox Games. What a journey it has been. I’ve played it off and on since 2007 until I finally quit in early 2014.

Do I recommend this game to new players? No. Stay far away from this.

Not only is this game a grind fest, it also is heavily pay to win. If you look at the item mall, you will quickly see that you need to spend at least a few hundred dollars just to be mildly competitive. I put at least 5,000 hours into this game and I regret a lot of them. It was a fun game back in 2007-08, but it has gone nowhere but downhill since then.

The mechanics in place are designed so that players are compelled to spend money in the item mall if they want to stand a chance against other players or even be strong enough to complete higher level content. This is even further enforced by the strong gambling mechanics built into the game. If you want to refine your clothing or weapons (gives a nice stat boost), then you must risk losing them after refining them to a certain level. The crafting in this game is generally focused on success rate percentages. Some items have a 100% chance to make them. Other items have less than a 1% chance to make.  You can purchase things in the item mall that mitigates the risk of losing your precious gear.

This brings up a pay to win element. Being able to sell item mall items in the game severely disrupts the game economy and favors those who are willing to spend hundreds in the item mall. You would think that the item mall would at least be fairly cheap if the game requires it right? Prepare to spend hundreds of dollars just to have a chance at decent gear. Even the item mall is built around gambling with things like boxes which give you random items when you open them. They aren’t cheap either and you could literally spend thousands and not get anything worthwhile from them.

Even if you look past all of those negatives and see what the game has to offer, you won’t find much. Besides endless grinding; there are a bunch of fetch quests that don’t really give you much for your time. The combat is hot bar based and uses a unique active skill system where your character performs a set of animations depending on the active skill being used.

The story itself is mildly interesting the first time you play through it, but it isn’t much different for each clan in the game. The maps themselves are small and the graphics are extremely dated. The game does has a sort of charm to it though. Something about the whole package is appealing at a first glance. It will be fun and interesting at first, but it quickly grows tiring and you’ll find yourself playing for the next level instead of having fun. 

TL;DR? It's just another grind focused Korean MMORPG that reached its peak about 8 years ago. Only play if you are a grind junkie and like old school MMOs.

I can't express my love for Rabbit and Steel more clearly than writing a glowing review for it. This game seems scientifically engineered to target several things that I enjoy and find addicting.

I have a secret love for a certain series of bullet hell doujin games (you probably know what I'm talking about) that Rabbit and Steel calls upon for inspiration. In addition to that, it also lends elements from rogue-lites and coop raiding mechanics similar to FFXIV, and it merges these mechanics together seamlessly.

From a mechanics overview, it's structured like a rogue-lite. You pick a cute character with a specific loadout, you hop into a run, and you gain ability upgrades and items that subtly change how you approach your rotation as you become more powerful. There's even a little DPS notification that flies over your head after a boss just so you can brag to your friends about how well you've optimized your kit. There are a few "routes" you can take to the final boss, the first of which is determined when you start. Everything after that is random until the final section. There's also a cute little story that unfolds with added dialogue and illustrated stills as you go through repeat playthroughs.

This game also really shines with coop as some of the boss mechanics are entirely different between a 1, 2, 3, or 4-person playthrough. You'll have to think hard about what that random tether you have does in the split second you have to decide where to stand. The layers of mechanics will give you a feeling of multitasking akin to patting your head and rubbing your belly as you try to survive with your limited health pool while dps'ing. This is especially pronounced at harder difficulties.

There are also hidden characters/loadouts to unlock and alternate color palettes, most of which can be unlocked simply by beating more bosses, though some are locked behind hard mode achievements. Shout outs to the shockingly few people with the adept skins for beating hard mode, apparently.

My only gripe with this game is that I have to bully my friends into buying a copy to play coop, and that also requires having 2-3 friends who also enjoy getting their teeth kicked in playing an admittedly niche genre. I look forward to the renewed interest in this game once the DLC releases additional characters, bosses, and rewards.

Oh, and don't forget to pat the shopkeeper's head. She's doing her best out there.

tl;dr:
Cute girls doing rogue-lite things with bullet hell and pseudo-mmo raid mechanics. A fun solo or coop romp if you like those things, and a dastardly way to torture your friends if they don't.

If you’ve ever spent hours wiping on FF14 raid mechanics and called it “fun,” this game will feel like home. Rabbit & Steel mixes raid-style boss mechanics with a top-down bullet hell shooter, and sprinkles in light roguelike progression and RPG-style upgrades. Controls are simple — keyboard and mouse work great — but the depth comes from learning mechanics rather than aiming.

The characters are adorable: stylized, anime-like bunny warriors that look like a mix between Viera and paper-cut mascots. In single-player, there are charming story scenarios centered around their little rabbit clans, which gives the game some personality beyond pure gameplay.

Normal mode co-op is very beginner friendly. Runs last around 10 minutes, and up to four players can party together. No friends available? Just create a public lobby and random bunny girls will hop in. It's surprisingly active.

If bullet hell games scare you, try the lower difficulty — it’s cute, forgiving, and your HP fully regenerates between stages. Despite the “bullet hell” label, most dodging is based on reading telegraphed shapes: sweeping bars, expanding circles, rotating blocks… basically FF14 mechanics translated into a shmup. Each class has a brief invulnerability skill to avoid damage, so even newcomers can survive dangerous attacks. Anyone familiar with FF14’s advanced raid mechanics will adapt quickly: spread mechanics, stack markers, safe zones after knockbacks, etc.

The level count isn't huge, but the character roster makes up for it. Each bunny has its own class identity — DPS, support, utility — with unique playstyles and skill loadouts. New characters unlock as you progress, so there’s motivation to keep playing.

Examples include:

A spell-slinging rabbit (Black Mage vibes)

A greatsword berserker (Black Knight energy)

A dancer buffing teammates with rhythms

A druid-like healer rabbit with support abilities

The soundtrack gives off a definite FF14 influence — energetic, orchestral, and surprisingly catchy for such a cute game.

Bonus points: it supports Steam Workshop, so there’s space for community content.

Whether you're a raider looking for that dopamine hit of perfect mechanics, or just want chaotic co-op fun with adorable rabbits, Rabbit & Steel is a gem.

Flesh Made Fear is a retro styled survival horror game complete with fixed cameras and tank controls. The game has you explore the outskirts of a town, sewers, and inside various buildings throughout. There are 2 characters you can play as, each with a different game route. I would say each character explores about 85% of the same area, with 15% being original with different bosses to fight. The game took me approximately 5 hours to complete my first playthrough with one character. It took me exactly 15 hours to 100% the whole game and all of its achievements.

*HIGHLY recommend using a controller for this game. There are a few quick time events that are a breeze when using a controller. Also due to the tank controls, a controller really helps dodging zombies with ease.
The controls are second nature if you grew up playing RE(1-3) on Playstation.

+ From the opening menu screen, the synthwave music just smashes throughout and sounds amazing. 
+ The atmosphere is gorgeous, creepy, with many interesting buildings and places to explore. The neon aesthetic is beautiful.
+ The voice acting is well done in a cheesy way. Also most of the collectible notes are read through by voice actors, a nice touch of immersion.
+ There is a secret infinite weapon to unlock if you find all the plushies hidden in the game and beat the game on hardcore mode. This weapon is hilarious and lots of fun to use while mopping up post game achievements.
+ The story at first sounds simple and cliche, but there are many notes to discover for those who want to deep dive into it if they so choose. This leaves it up to the player to choose how much they want to learn the backstory, which is perfect.
+ The puzzles are well balanced, not too difficult or obscure, no guide needed.
+ Several bosses are disgustingly hilarious, and well designed.

I was actually going to add a positive review with a recommendation. This game looks a bit like a mix of BDO and New World, but it looked like the devs were doing everything right, that New World was doing wrong. This game did have the potential to be what New World promised; a modern MMO for everybody who enjoys a good MMORPG. And, it appeared that the devs followed the success formula of Black Desert Online and Albion Online and offer so many things to do, that you must pick a few to get good at or suck at everything.

It is early access, but after the latest couple of updates it is becoming apparent that the devs have lost focus on what made this project very promising for everybody who enjoys a good MMORPG to begin with. 

The devs listen too much to the very vocal minority of the gear-vs-gear end-game crowd and I am afraid that Quinfall is on the same path down the toilet as New World. 

Just like New World, the concept of Quinfall was sold as being a sandbox for everybody. Right now, the focus is exclusively on the corner with the gear-vs-gear players, who cry if there are not enough plastic shovels, sieves, and buckets for them to be constantly entertained (read new dungeons, better gear drops, more trinkets and glitter, higher level ceilings, expansions, and more, more, more).

The game has been in early access for 8 months and the tables with profession rankings show that there should be plenty of skilled crafters for a healthy supply of both mid and high level gear on the auction house. Yet, there is not. Either those who reached level 70 (before the patch) did so as a means to their gear-vs-gear end-game or they burned out and left the game. Those of us life-skillers grinding away at the crafting skills did not provide that gear, because we were not yet able to. The solution? Drops of high level gear to satisfy the gear-vs-gear players, which was a slap in the face for those of us who wasted our time on crafting professions. So, the devs fixed the wrong hole and created another to bleed players.

In addition to making crafting pointless, the gear drops can be recycled and you get high-level materials, so no point in being a gatherer either. The game is still early access and they have already increased the max character level! Pretty soon, you will be able to start a new character at level 100; then you just have to grind a few levels before you can start spending money on enhancing your end-game gear drops.

Such a sad waste of potential.

I love hidden object games, and have played enough of them to know what a good one is like. While this game has some potential, there is a lot of room for improvement.

Pros: Story line is pretty decent. 

Cons: Each time you explore an area, you use energy, and a large amount of it. You either have to wait several hours for it to replenish or spend money to buy more. The amount of time you are given to explore an area is only 1 minute. This is not enough time to find hidden objects, especially if the graphics aren't that great. If you are zoomed out of a picture, they graphics are nice, but when you zoom in to locate a hard to find object, the graphics become pixelated and somewhat distorted. Also, when you find a chest, you only have a very limited amount of time to solve a puzzle to open it. 

Overall: Game play time is limited and you almost feel rushed to complete puzzles and hidden object areas.

Don't let that Izuna Drop in the trailer fool you. If you're looking for something with the depth of a AAA 3D action game like Ninja Gaiden, you're not gonna get that here. The relatively low content offering (as of release) and the lack of real depth to any of the systems apart from the rogue-like randomizations make it hard to justify going back to it after so many playthroughs - an issue which a great deal of games in the rogue-like genre tend to fall into.

That doesn't mean you won't get any enjoyment out of it, because you definitely will. The game has a decent amount of polish and hitting things can be VERY satisfying (Flan or Mokou being the best examples imo). Just know what you're getting yourself into, and temper your expectations going in. You're getting a great game for the price.

全成就达成，整体给我的感觉是优缺点都很明显。比起一般的休闲种田游戏这游戏一点都不休闲，基本是从头肝到尾。对于游戏整体我个人是倾向于体验不好的。
本来是奔着种田来的，实际上和种田没什么关系，而是作为一个工坊主搞城市基建的故事。游戏的玩法就是收集素材制作物品过剧情搞城市基建，各种材料都是不合理的缺，前中期的肝度个人感觉很不合理，科技树也很不合理，等到了实现资源自由和自动化的时候已经可以准备结坑了。前期特别缺资源，体力又少，又没有很性价比补充体力的手段。导致资源空缺这块一直在拖累主线进度，体验感很不好。
游戏是老游戏了，建模粗糙和游戏操作手感比较生硬这些就不说了。游戏里的各种小游戏手感也很怪。比较有创意的是各种特殊节日的小游戏和活动，这方面做得还行。可角色攻略这块设计得还不错，都有攻略后的特殊剧情（我只攻略了有成就的几个其他的没攻略也不知道有没有特殊剧情），约会等玩法就挺中规中矩了。
地图探索这方面还算能接受，随着主线推进逐渐扩大可探索范围和传送点（传送点的分布密度也还算好）加上后面解锁了坐骑跑图也还算轻松。
个人感觉设计得最糟糕的是战斗系统，操作手感生硬和不合理的数值带来的是堪称灾难般的体验，就我个人来说，深层的遗迹基本都是靠嗑药硬过的，最好的武器是主线完结才给，手感更是用过的武器最怪的。所幸的是游戏需要的战斗面还算少。
最后是游戏的剧情，我个人觉得很难崩，主角一个人从收集素材到制作零件组装工具到安装，城市的基建从头到尾都是玩家手搓的，这市长不如主角来当，老爸离开莫名回归又离开，从头到尾都是谜语人。要我说这剧情不如不做）。不过这游戏的卖点也不是剧情。
最后就是这种玩法不能联机还是太可惜了，感觉这肝度就是设计给联机一起玩的。
整体不是很推荐，不过折后史低的价格确实很不错，尽管体验感不是很好但是量大管饱，能接受上述缺点和喜欢肝的玩家可以入手。

首先，我喜欢这款游戏。喜欢的理由归于以下几点：
1、共同回合的机制。对战双方同时执行自己的回合，然后统一结算。富有战略性，能体验运筹帷幄的快乐。
2、对战区域的划分。包括进攻区域、防守区域、支援区域、指挥官区域，以及由它们组成的概念：被部署区域、战场。区域的划分和不同区域特定的功能大大扩展了对战策略的可能性。
3、卡组机制。组成套牌前对势力的选择决定了你整个套牌的风格和可利用的资源，要求玩家不断取舍，最终完成自己喜欢的战术。
4、比较轻松的游戏体验。不需要大量的时间、精力和金钱投入。
当你在了解了整个游戏从确立思路、组建套牌到最终随机应变取得胜利之后，游戏的体验会相当不错。然而这款游戏的诸多缺点也就来源于玩家这个熟悉过程之前。
1、中文翻译不完整，概念解释缺失。游戏初期有诸多不加解释的概念，严重影响玩家融入游戏。包括组建套牌时的规则不明确，会让新手玩家摸不着头脑。
2、糟糕的网络连接。较差的网络环境甚至不能让你完整体验一场游戏。
3、UI（交互界面元素）设计不合理，拥有较多生物时会拥挤，难以精确操作。画面特效单一。
当玩家熟悉了这些之后，我仍然认为这款游戏值得喜爱卡牌游戏的玩家尝试一下。同时也希望官方能加紧改正上述缺点（如果可能的话）
希望我的体验能帮到大家，祝大家游戏愉快。

Em toda minha longa jornada recente jogando vários títulos de automobilismo, sinto que finalmente encontrei minha parada final. Assetto Corsa é definitivamente o MELHOR jogo de corrida já feito.

Isso se dá por motivos de que Assetto Corsa não é necessariamente um jogo, mas sim uma plataforma.

Com uma física robusta e um script aberto para modders, Assetto Corsa possuí toneladas e toneladas de conteúdo feito por comunidade na qual qualquer defeito que se possa apontar no jogo base, é simples concertar ele com alguma MOD. Não por menos é o simulador no qual muitos pilotos reais usam para se preparar para suas corridas.

Você achou os gráficos ruins ? Baixe o mod Pure.
Você não tem um simulador ? Baixe um script para jogar com o controle.
Você não gostou da HUD do game ? Baixe um mod que deixa com o HUD do GT7

O jogo pesa originalmente 15gb, em meio aos meus mais de 250gb de mods instalados eu tenho todo o calendário de pistas de temporadas clássicas da F1; tenho o campeonato inteiro de GT3 para jogar; corridas clássicas que antecedem a criação da fórmula 1; tenho diversos carros da HotWheels; tenho um chevette blocado; um rx7 com nitro; carros da temporada de 88, 92, 93, 01, 05, 08, 13, 16 da F1; uma pista que é a Dust 2... e mais uma infinidade de coisas. Tudo isso decorrente da facilidade que é instalar MODs e a cultura incrivel que existe envolta desse game.

Existe sim alguns problemas no qual eu não consegui resolver ainda, talvez por não correr atrás o suficiente, como a IA dos bots e a dificuldade de criar partidas online, no entanto, nada disso tira o quão maravilhoso é Assetto Corsa.

Eis aqui o final de minha jornada, o fim do meu bombardeamento de reviews de jogos de corrida e a morte de algumas centenas de horas. Assetto Corsa virou um vicio, virou um hobby e virou uma paixão.

One of the best sim racing experiences you can get, even years later.

Assetto Corsa might be getting old, but it’s aged like fine wine - especially once you dive into the modding scene. The base game alone is solid but a bit barebones by today’s standards. The real magic happens once you install Content Manager and Custom Shaders Patch (CSP). Those two completely transform the game -better lighting, weather, physics tweaks, smoother performance, and tons of quality-of-life features. It honestly feels like a new title after that.

Then you’ve got the mods - cars, tracks, visuals, sound packs, everything you can imagine. The community support is insane, and there’s something for every kind of driver, from casual track day enthusiasts to full-on sim racers. You can go from drifting in Japan to racing GT3s at Spa, or even just cruising through city maps at sunset.

If you’re playing on a controller, don’t worry - there are some amazing Gamepad FX scripts that completely change how Assetto Corsa feels without a wheel.

For grip racing, there’s Advanced Gamepad Assist, which smooths out steering, reduces twitchiness, and gives you way more precision when braking and cornering. It makes racing with a controller feel natural and consistent.

For drifting, there’s a different script called A7 Assist, designed specifically for smoother countersteering. It makes it much easier to catch slides and hold long drifts without the car snapping or feeling unpredictable.

Both are absolute game-changers depending on your driving style.

Performance-wise, it runs great on most modern PCs, and the visuals can look stunning once you tune everything with CSP and a good graphics preset (would definitely check out Pure if I were you)

All in all, Assetto Corsa is one of those games that grows with you - the deeper you go, the better it gets. It’s not perfect out of the box, but with the right setup, it’s easily one of the best and most flexible sim racing platforms ever made.

[i]Without Within[/i] is more of a short introduction rather than a full visual novel, to Vinty's story; and it is the first of InvertMouse's VNs that I've enjoyed. It has a charming narrative, and lets you decide whether you'd be interested in Vinty's journey in following games for yourself; since it is free.

Well, here in this 20-minute narrative, you'll take a glimpse to Miss Vinty's life. One would like to say she is a calligrapher extraordinaire, but nope, she really is not. She is simply a young woman who tries to keep her dreams of becoming a world renown calligraphy artist alive, while she struggles to make ends meet. Her reality is full of responsibilities, harsh comments and random trolls, so she starts questioning what might be wrong about her luck. Is her work that awful, or is she doing something wrong?

The game mostly consists of cartoony anime artwork and uplifting midi music as display. The narrative mainly relies on humor, pop culture references and a series of smart remarks as Vinty's own impressions; and before you can count to three, you finish the game. You are given choice options 5 time throughout the game, yet the right option is always more than obvious. The wrong choice will immediately roll the game to a bad end where you'll be explained that being a jerk never bear rewards; and the right option will make progress with the story. Oh, and the actual ending is another joke on poor Vinty's life.

Is it extraordinary? Not really. Is it funny? Somewhat it is since it brings a smile or two on your face. Is it sincere? Yeah, and that is the charm of [i]Without Within[/i]. Vinty's aspirations and her journey to become a famous calligrapher mirrors on the developer mostly. The game autocritiques on itself and its creator, revealing hardships of any kind of creative career in 21st century. It serves to be an honest, even self-mocking open letter about personal experience, a struggle between dreams and reality. Not for fabulous artworks or imaginative story, but for that, for the simple honesty of it, I loved [i]Without Within[/i].

[h1][i][b]A very short Visual Novel about an ambitious girl called Vinty who has a dream to realize – to become a rich and famous public figure specialized in art calligraphy![/b][/i][/h1]

[h1]Game’s premise:[/h1]
[i][b]You play as Vinty, a young lady bearing a dream since she was a child – to become a calligraphy artist. While living in a very tiny and deteriorated apartment barely affording to pay her rent, the heroine keeps fantasizing about being rich, to the point this fantasy sometimes gets a hold of her reality thinking of herself as superior while trying to sell her works – that appear to not even reach an average level of decency in calligraphy field.[/b][/i]

[h1]About Vinty:[/h1]
Our hardworking main character who does not give up to her dreams at all! In fact, she does dream a lot and often does not realize when it is time to fall back when responding to rude customers. Often ending up in embarrassing situations, she is still the typical kind-hearted girl who would help a person in need right away.
Works as part-timer at a restaurant where she often gets scolded given her awkward attitude and personality, looks forward to finding a better job and pursuing a career of her own.
She is also passionated about videogames; Visual Novels in particular.

[h1]Featurings:[/h1]
This is a very short Visual Novel that you should be able to complete in ~30 minutes.
The story is choice-based, therefore depending on how you choose to act you will either be reaching a bad ending or the continuation of a story. While there are few bad endings, there is only one true end.
The story is really fun, particularly appreciated the humour behind Vinty’s situation and the hardworking part of her personality. The character might be found relatable due to her awkwardness as well as ambitiousness and I believe the message that this story is trying to convey us is to not give up on our dreams and keep working hard, which is really wholesome.
The art is simple, yet well done and the background music fits the story well movimentating the setting when necessary.

[h1]Overall:[/h1]
This game is recommended if you’re looking for a short and cute Visual Novel with an awkward heroine.
Not recommended if you’re looking for a serious Visual Novel featuring average length and expanded narration.

O problema está na versão para PC, que infelizmente é muito mal feita. O analógico direito simplesmente não funciona corretamente em vários momentos, o que compromete completamente a jogabilidade com controle — algo essencial em um jogo baseado em movimentos e decisões rápidas.

Como resultado, o jogo acaba sendo muito mais jogável no teclado e mouse, o que tira boa parte da imersão e da naturalidade da experiência. Para um título que depende tanto da fluidez dos comandos (principalmente do analógico direito), isso é um grande problema.

Então, por mais que eu admire o jogo em si, não recomendo essa versão. Ele merecia um port melhor e mais cuidado.

This isn’t a welcoming game. It doesn’t hold your hand, offer adaptive difficulty, or ease you into its systems. But for players who crave a challenge, it delivers a battlefield where every victory feels earned.

I came in with a strategic mindset, experimenting with civilizations, map types, and AI allies to simulate a learning mode. I studied resource placement, refined build orders, and adapted to enemy advances. The enemy AI punished me relentlessly. Even on the easiest difficulty, it floods the map with units while I’m still stabilizing my economy. Ally AI often stands idle as my town center is razed within sight.

There’s no in-game guidance on civilization bonuses, no pause-and-queue system, and no scaffolding for solo learners. It’s emotionally exhausting. But wins give you the most rewarding feelings ever.

This game doesn’t respect your time, but it does respect persistent effort. If you’re new to the series and want a fair solo experience, this version may not be for you. But if you’re here to be tested, to earn your victories through grit and adaptation, "Age of Empires I" will reward you.

非常欣慰，结尾又落回到具体的人。的确是日本游戏的传统，不同的是，它除了对亲密关系有些执念外，并没有太多其他固守的价值，而捕捉到的，是价值在现代性中的流动。不幸的人更能体会其他不幸，并且愿意做点什么。其实是挺朴素的道理，一种另类生存的可能，不能被情与法、东西方这种二元对立所概括，却极少被发觉。这是缝隙之中的洞见，也是最短兵相接的源于生活而高于生活，相比之下《谓何》那种文艺结构就显得外在许多。文本在尖锐和敏感、制度的现实和人的灵活之间，把大的政治惊悚故事进一步缩小、收束在集体内部的斡旋，无论是合作还是破裂，信息的不断流转交换，进而互相利用垫脚，从来都是这种权力关系中的一部分。不太喜欢尽心竭力去说教的片段，虽然这更符合东亚的叙事形式。而它最大的问题，是自以为能在现代法与私仇之间找到一种折衷，这种文本上的确凿，让极端的个人经验变得可以被玩家理解和代入，但现代性的困境被柔化了。结尾那句“如果再早一点伸出援手就好了”让我想起了《嘉年华》。从某种意义上来说，后者是一部真正意义上“现代”的作品，因为它拒绝一切的抚慰和修复，暴露出系统性失语的同时，也让裂缝成为叙事的终点。它有一种连愤怒都无法指向对象的无力。大多数玩家所诟病的主线支线无法统一的问题，并非是叙事技巧的疏漏，而是现代游戏叙事的结构性困境。当一部作品要同时成为文学与游乐，它必然在伦理与娱乐的轴线上产生断裂。这类文学想要获得胜利，必须通过填满所有细节的整体性才能实现。

[i]Batman: Arkham City[/i] is an action-adventure game developed by Rocksteady Studios and published by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment.

[b]Story[/b]
I suggest playing through Arkham Asylum first, as events from that game are used as a setup to setting of this one.

Arkham City takes place 18 months after Arkham Asylum events. Taking credit for stopping Joker's siege, director Sharp becomes a Mayor of Gotham City. Declaring Asylum no longer suitable, he creates immense prison enclosure known as Arkham City inside Gotham's slums, taken care of by mysterious Hugo Strange while monitored by private military firm TYGER Security. Our protagonist, Bruce Wayne, opposes that idea and ends up in a titular prison himself. Here as Batman he wants to find out more about mysterious Protocol 10 and real intentions behind the prison.

[b]Gameplay[/b]
If you played Arkham Asylum, you already know what to expect as City builds up upon gameplay from previous game, providing third person open world venture where you will investigate, explore, stealth and brawl through the prison as our favourite Caped Crusader, searching for truth (and few faces to soak your fists in).
First thing you will experience is the main dish of the game- combat. Punch, kick, smack thugs before they smack you to avoid a dreadful fate of watching villians laugh in your face as you lose and reload a checkpoint. Counter or dodge incoming attacks, chain up combinations to gain speed and power, utilize plenty of gadgets to surprise your opponents. Game provides improved version of the "Freeflow" combat system, meaning you can now perform more moves, such as option to counter multiple attacks at once or being able to chain combinations for long enough to unleash deadly special attacks. Enemies can be armed with different armor and weapons, forcing you to adjust your moves accordingly.

Sometimes you get a chance to resolve encounters silently. Similar scenario as with first game, utilize vantage points, environment, detective vision and your gadgets to eliminate enemies without them noticing you. Watch as fear strikes their minds and heartpulse keeps rising with each performed takedown on their buddies, but just like in combat, thugs are a bit more Bat-proof this time so they come with more firearms, jammers and extra tools that will make your life harder, as tides can quickly shift back and forth. Know when to strike and when to wait for opportunity, or just create your own!

Arkham City opens up the area, providing way more space to explore. Glide, grapple and sprint around looking for collectibles that expand the narrative and lore, side activities, or just seek out local thugs waiting for a fight! (Or to be knocked out silently by a sneaky Bat.) Fans favourite Riddler returns with his trophies and riddles, while other villians make an appearance in side quests spread all over the prison, unlockable as you progress through the story. Same applies to gadgets, so you might have to wait a bit to obtain a tool or two before you can enter certain buildings or collect specific trophies. No pressure, you can always return to every area you visited.

Combat and exploration grant you experience points, earn enough to level Batman up and unlock new skills, moves, or improve gadgets.

[b]Playtime, other modes[/b]
It took me roughly 13 hours to complete everything in Arkham City. After beating the story you unlock New Game Plus where you can utilize everything you have unlocked with increased overall difficulty to balance it out. Additionally there is "Riddler's Revenge" mode, where you tackle on different challenge maps and campaigns for medals! Fair to say you can spend a bit more time in City than you might think at first glance, if interested. Especially as this version comes with extra DLC, Catwoman content, and extra characters in RR mode.

[b]Impressions[/b]
Out of the gate I will go out with a very bold claim- Arkham City is probably the best sequel I ever had a pleasure to play. A textbook definition of how they should be made. It's not a revolution, but an evolution. If you played Asylum you feel right at home almost instantly as game keeps same great controls and fantastic core gameplay allowing you to quickly get into action, increasing and opening up the location where game takes place, addition of side quests and expanded lore make it feel like an entirely new experience. Already great combat is now reaching superb levels, it's smooth, it's intuitive, with very tight controls and top notch precision when it comes to inputs as if game knows which thug you want to hit before you even do. Some annoying moments from Asylum where Batman in the middle of combination would decide to punch ghosts are gone, combined with new moves and gadgets it practically makes you beg for as many enemies on screen as possible to go wild.

But game knows when to slow down, when to give you a stealth section to showcase pretty solid enemy AI, allowing you to fully lean into Batman's strategic side with various gadgets, careful planning and utilization of environment to his advantage. Quite frankly it's a shame that because game is no longer as linear as first title, plus complete change of area where game takes place so it's almost impossible to just give you a stealth section in the middle of the city, it doesn't actually have that many of those section. But when you get them, it's an absolute treat to play.

Asylum no doubt had it's own unique atmosphere, but City is no slouch in that department either. Prison filled with crime in the middle of gang wars, with secrets on top of secrets, the mash of destroyed slums with iconic locations, freedom you get to explore it and encounter many more and lesser known villians across short yet satisfying side quests, it hits right. Fortunately game never feels too long, it doesn't drag on, even if you decide to dive into the madness that is collecting those forsaken trophies.
Fantastic audiovisual side, strong art direction, top of the game performance from voice actors and animators, game even today looks fairly impressive. Forgot to even mention expanded extra side mode of the game in which you can spend plenty hours, if running around Arkham City gets boring for you.

If there something...mixed, I can say about this game, it would probably be about the story. In my book the main villian in this one was a bit..disappointing? Especially as he was pretty much a "main face" when it came to promoting the game. I expected a better conclusion of certain arcs and felt like it could have focus on just one story, instead of jumping around and trying to have two main storylines branching out and at least for me, that never really worked. So yeah, story is enjoyable but I would like it to go into a different direction.

Nonetheless, Arkham City is simply superb. Easy recommendation. Combat feels great, explorating feels enjoyable, still holds up visually and it's a treat for fans of DC/Batman.

[b]Final words and conclusion[/b]
Said it before, gonna say it again, GOTY Edition comes with everything released so you get all the fun stuff- alternative costumes, post-main game DLC and extra characters- in one pack!

Batman: Arkham City improves pretty much everything from first game while still focusing on core strenghts- fantastic combat, great audiovisuals and intriguing exploration. Buy it, play it, enjoy it.

[b]Its a 5 dollar horror game.[/b]

If you're one of the few out here having an existential crisis over the minor imperfections a game of this size & caliber can provide, then perhaps you should reconsider your entire evaluation process.

Panicore is a simplistic survival horror game where you and up to 4 other players are given the task to survive and escape a handful of levels varying in sizes. Some of these levels include a School, a Hospital, and as of the recent update, a Military base. Within these levels its the players jobs to collect materials and solve puzzles to plan an escape, all the while avoiding the big baddie of the mission whom can also hear your every move. The sound aspect of the game is this titles "big gimmick", and to be frank, its flawed. However in my experience while playing with others, the sound aspect doesn't really seem to even effect gameplay all that much. These monsters are aggressive regardless of whether or not they hear you fart into your microphone. So with a little bit of patience and an equal amount of perseverance, each of this games levels can be conquered with a tiny bit of luck.

Look, is the game ironed out to perfection? No, absolutely not. You [b]will[/b] run into bull$%^# during your play session, mostly the NPC monster being an overpowered, spastic, sometimes random-af, ass$%^*. However, isn't that what you want in your "horrifying monster chase down" game...? The level of difficulty, while undoubtedly challenging and even unfair at times, does lead to genuinely spooky instances and laughs amongst your friends. Its an experience where you and your pals are completely screwed and at the whim of said monsters mercy. Whether or not that was originally the intended take of the devs, its certainly the one you end up with. And more times than not, its fun because of it!

[b]No[/b], this isn't a masterpiece. [b]No[/b], this isn't a flawless experience, And [b]no[/b], this isn't going to last you weeks upon weeks of playtime. Panicore is a [b]very simple[/b], [b]very rudimentary[/b], and sometimes [b]very difficult[/b], [b]budget[/b] survival horror game, whos time is more enjoyable spent with friends over a headset. If you got a couple of pals who are into spooky games and have a good sense of humor, then for 5 bucks, its not a bad way to spend an evening for some laughs and scares.

This game is so much fun with friends, but it has a few downsides:

- I'd say the monsters are a bit too basic — jsut don’t talk, and you just run away if they chase you.
- The hospital map is a pain when it comes to finding items.
- The submarine map is too small, and there are a lot of one-way paths that can just kill you if you’re unlucky.

BUT we really loved the military camp map !

The objectives were clear, there weren’t a thousand things to check for items, and the monster was fun and quite scary to play against. We were three players, and we always had to keep one person on watch duty so the others could stay “safe.” Even then, we still had some terrifying moments when things went downhill. 

And the most important part: we could speak freely. I know it sounds weird to say, but being able to communicate with friends about the objectives is such a relief — it really prevents that feeling where one person is doing everything while the others just run around looking for things to do.

So please, devs — keep adding fun mechanics and great maps to your game. We really love playing PANICORE !

If you've played any of the 100 Cozy Games series before and liked it, you'll probably enjoy this one too.  It's a simple hidden object game with very low stakes making it a good way to just de-stress and relax.

As usual I find the hand drawn line art to be whimsical and fun.  It's fairly calm images this time depicting cats in a Cyprus setting.  You are given two scenes to look through and as usual for me, there were two cats that were bit elusive.  You can at any time use their their hint without penalty to find cats, but they are fairly easy to find as long as you look for anything remotely cat shaped or anything that looks out of place. 

Compared to other games in their 100 Cats series this did seem a little different. The cats felt easier to find but my playtime wasn't too different than other games even accounting for the 5 minutes that I left it idle before actually starting.  But it still felt easier to find everything.  The other thing I noticed was that it felt as if the graphics were not quite up to their usual standard.  Part of the image had crisp clean lines while others were a little fuzzy.  It wasn't as noticeable zoomed out, but was the more you zoomed in.  I don't recall noticing that on any of their other games.  In addition to that, when you find a cat they disappear from the image but usually a clean background image remained.  Instead, in this one, the background after the cat disappears often leaves a messy, unfinished looking background.  Missing outlines, smudged looking colors.  It looks like it was a mistake deleted from a Photoshop work in progress.  I felt a little dissatisfied whenever finding a cat because of that.  I don't know if production was rushed or what, but that little bit of final polish would have made it a better game.  I'd still recommend it for its low price point and relatively relaxing play, just be aware if that type of thing will bother you, it might not be as satisfying or relaxing as other entries in the 100 cats series.
