[h1] A spiritual successor that lacks spirit [/h1]

The original Majesty was one of my most played games as a kid. I easily sank hundreds of hours into it, and over a hundred more as an adult with the Steam remaster. It was a game full of charm and quirks and just the right amount of challenge, and to this day I still never get bored of playing it.

I've long wished for a spiritual successor to the Majesty series. The sequel, Majesty 2, didn't hit quite the same mark as the original. A few games here and there have come close in their own ways, but none have captured the entirety of the Majesty spirit.

I'm sorry to say that though Lessaria has most of the form of Majesty (and even the same Advisor voice actor as the original - the inimitable George Ledoux), it is lacking the spirit that made the original so compelling. Including demo time I'm 7 hours in and about halfway through the campaign missions, but I've already lost interest in continuing.

My interest is surely not helped by a lack of sandbox mode; DESPITE what the store page claims, there is no sandbox mode - just a single endless survival mode set on one static map layout. If you, like me, derived most of your playtime in Majesty's sandbox mode, you will be immensely disappointed.

Mechanically, Lessaria is an indirect control RTS like the original Majesty. You have control over building placement (in this case on a visible grid) and upgrades, and hero recruitment, but your heroes act on their own volition - choosing to explore, or fight, or shop, or flee, with some classes tending toward certain behaviors (e.g. Rangers like to explore, and Rogues are more easily motivated by coin). Like in Majesty 2's expanded flag system, you can entice heroes toward certain actions with bounties to Explore, Attack, Defend, and Avoid, and Lessaria is very transparent about which heroes find your price suitable, eliminating the guesswork of how large of a bounty is sufficient.

As mentioned, kingdom building takes place on a grid, so you can more easily see where a building can be placed. However, Lessaria limits your building area to a relatively small portion of the overall map, beyond which you can never expand - with the exception of trading posts, which must be placed on specific (sometimes hard to spot) pre-set locations, like in Majesty 2. This means your ability to exert map control with defensive structures is much more limited, and your heroes will be wandering far afield from the relative safety of your base.

Lessaria addresses this distance problem with a portal system - for a small sum of gold, you can build a portal structure in your city and permanently link it to several pre-placed portal sites across the map (once you've scouted them), allowing your heroes to instantaneously travel to and from far-flung locations. It's a good solution, and generally the portal sites are well-placed on Lessaria's hand-crafted (not randomized) maps.

Beyond the hard limit of space constraints, Lessaria imposes a softer limit on what you're able to accomplish through a new resource: population. As your city expands, you will need to (manually, as opposed to automatically in the Majesty series) build peasant homes. These contribute population (and tax income), which are spent to recruit heroes (refunded when the hero dies) and to build certain economic structures. At certain thresholds of population your overall gold income gets reduced, making it harder to expand beyond a certain point. You won't be able to build a grand kingdom here as you delay pursuing your objective to let gold accumulate, and you won't be able to recruit more than perhaps two dozen heroes total.

Speaking of delays, Lessaria adds one other mechanic to ensure the player can't take things easy. Waves of monsters will attack your kingdom on a set timer, with a wave strength rating of 1-5. Each successive wave will increase in strength, with the upper end being strong existential threats that can quickly wipe out your kingdom. The wave strength is reduced every time you destroy a monster den - but these dens are limited in number, and the waves are not. If your heroes are overzealous and destroy the dens too quickly, you will have no way to mitigate the strength of the assaults for the rest of your mission. And a lack of dens will not affect the strength of the assault - assault waves spawn out of thin air, with no regard for how many (if any) monster dens remain. This effectively imposes a timer on every scenario in the game, and encourages the player to counter-intuitively preserve monster dens until they are needed to reduce the strength of the assault wave, in order to buy enough time to accomplish the scenario objectives to win.

Finally, and perhaps most disappointingly, your units just lack personality. There's no cries when a unit dies ("I'm mellllllltinnnnnng!"), and in fact death happens so quietly I often don't notice until I click a guild and see an opening. Units have very few voice quips, which you only hear when selecting them, or when zoomed in far enough to hear them during a fight (the sound mixing on the game needs some polish). There's no jaunty cries of "tax collector!", or building animations when, say, the tavern or blacksmith are being visited by a hero. All those little audio and visual details that gave the original Majesty its charm and humor are missing here.

In summary, Lessaria is a spiritual successor that lacks the spirit that made the original Majesty so good. It tries some mechanical tweaks to the formula with mixed success. It bears evidence of systems that were tried and either abandoned or never expanded on (resource gathering, random hero personality traits that affect their stats but can't be interacted with). There are several places lacking polish (audio mixing, mismatched written and spoken dialogue, typos). And it completely lacks the sandbox the store page claims it has, and which gave the original Majesty such longevity (for me at least).

If you're a fan of the original Majesty and craving something to scratch that itch, I can't say Lessaria will do so. It didn't for me. Maybe come back after a few more patches, for additional polish, balancing, and hopefully an actual sandbox mode.

First of all, I do recommend this game because I love Majesty. The developers wrote that they were inspired by this game, but more of a copycat with minor changes. Nevertheless, it captivated me, but there's no way I'll give it a positive review on Steam, considering we, the players, are beta testers. The game is playable in its current state, but it's riddled with bugs, as if no developer had even launched this game for their own testing before release.

Examples:
1. The price of each upgrade or character creation is listed, but many are unpriced, clearly an unintentional error. How can you programmatically create a Class in OOP and make it work for one character and not for another? And how can you release a game without seeing such a basic thing? Some prices are different than they actually are...

2. The game offers the ability to increase the gameplay speed, but this clearly causes problems in some missions, and the flow of events on the map is buggy. It looks like a problem with the game engine. In one of the missions at x3 speed, a series of triggered events instantly occur, while at x1 speed, even the simplest one doesn't have time to trigger. Some might say I didn't get it, but the game also has a pause function, and using it, you can still manage effectively at x3 speed....

3... but on another map, it doesn't change anything, because the events are adapted to the player's actions, so without leaving the starting location, you can level up to the max and go make coffee; the map will practically navigate itself. Because the heroes move on their own...

4... of course, the fact that they move on their own is inherent in this game, it's just a shame that on some maps it doesn't work at all.

5. Highly developed heroes don't listen to our commands, regardless of the reward.

6. The last mission is a joke. We play through the entire game according to the usual pattern, but at the very end, the city is complete, the buildings are scattered, there's no income, and now we have to manage a completely different type of gameplay. Who came up with such a stupid idea?

7. Caravans/porters/merchants, whatever you call them, sometimes get bugged and don't reach the castle.

8. Almost half of the achievements on Steam don't work!

9. In general, the progression of triggered events on maps is poorly designed. This causes unbalanced missions. The game doesn't get more difficult with each map. Furthermore, a child could guess these triggers and beat the game.

10. There are no keyboard shortcuts, and if there are any, they're hidden and you have to guess.

11. After setting the game speed to, for example, x3, pressing the spacebar pauses the game. Pressing the spacebar again doesn't return the game to x3, but x1.

12. Regardless of the game speed you set, you still have to wait for the narrator/advisor to finish talking before you can move on with the map. And the game continues. This is especially problematic in timed missions; it's better to pause the game and wait for the guy to talk. Meine Review zu Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot:

CHA-LA HEAD-CHA-LA!! - So liebe Dragon Ball-Freunde, nach ca. 52 Spielstunden will ich mich nun endlich an eine Review zum wahrscheinlich besten STORY-Dragon Ball-Game überhaupt wagen!

Vorne weg: Ich bin ein großer Fan des kompletten Dragon Ball/Z/GT/Super/Daima-Franchise, egal ob Manga, Anime oder Games, in vielen davon bin ich bewandert oder habe zumindest hineingeschaut.

Dragon Ball-Videospiele habe ich so einige in meiner Sammlung und auch auf Steam habe ich bereits einige gezockt und/oder zocke diese immer noch Regelmäßig.

Aber kommen wir nun zum Spiel an sich:

"Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot" habe ich am 24.06.2020 begonnen und habe jetzt knapp 5 Jahre später am 25.10.2025(!) die Hauptstory abgeschlossen...diese zog sich somit für mich über 1949(!!!) Tage...WAS ZUM SHENLONG ist da denn passiert!?!?

Das ist ja ein echt Irres Ding! O: Irgendwie schon krass wie sich das hingezogen hat und ich bin mir nichtmal ganz Sicher wieso überhaupt? Naja, zum einen vielleicht weil eine sehr lange Zeit mit dem Kampfsystem an sich nicht richtig klar gekommen bin, bzw. dieses erst jetzt zu beginn der Boo-Saga voll Verstanden hatte---also nach knapp 40h Spielzeit...au Backe! ^^' Im Grunde hatte ich mir das Spiel zuvor schwerer gemacht wie es eigentlich hätte sein müssen, da ich meine Gegner nur mit Ki-Attacken und ein paar Special-Moves eingedeckt habe, statt auch starke Schlag-Kombos zu verwenden.
Nun gut, wie dem auch sei, hatte ich dennoch viel Spaß mit dem Game, da es außerordentlich gut versteht die bekannte Serie der Manga und vor allem der Anime-Vorlage samt passender Musik zu präsentieren! Einfach Wunderbar! Das freie Bewegen in den unterschiedlichen großen Arealen hat mir sehr große Freude bereitet , genauso wie das absolvieren vieler größerer und kleinerer Sidequests, die immer wieder zum Schmunzeln anregten oder toll Fillerfolgen aus dem Anime adaptierten, z.B. die grandiose Fahrschul-Folge mit Son-Goku und Piccolo! :D

Von beginn an bis zu einen bestimmten Punkt der Boo-Saga habe ich sehr viele Sidequests angenommen und absolviert, circa ab dem Punkt als das Weltturnier relativ zu beginn in Kraft tritt, habe ich mich nahezu ausschließlich auf die Hauptstory konzentriert um mit dieser endlich mal abschließen zu können und das hat auch sehr gut funktioniert! Zwischendrin habe ich mich wirklich fast wie in der Anime-Vorlage gefühlt, nur dass ich gelegentlich den A-Knopf betätigen musste um die Gespräche voranzubringen oder eben in den klasse inszenierten Kämpfen den Xbox360-Controller bearbeiten durfte um meinen Gegnern die Visage zu zerbeulen und mit heftigen Energiestrahlen um mich zu ballern! - Das machte unglaublich Laune und machte das Kampfsystem nun durchaus etwas taktischer und Sinniger, als ich es zuvor immer wahrgenommen hatte!

Vor ein paar Wochen hatte ich mir "Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot" + A.P. DLC nochmal für die Nintendo Switch gekauft (für unschlagbare 2,79€ im eShop, dies dort nicht zu kaufen wäre schon kriminell gewesen) und freue mich eigentlich jetzt schon darauf das Game da nochmal Story-fokussiert durchzuspielen! 

Puhh. Das war jetzt ein ganz schöner Schwung an Hintergrundgeschichte meinerseits zum Spiel, vielleicht hier nochmal ein paar Aspekte die speziell auf's Spiel gerichtet sind:
Man beginnt an sich sogar noch etwas vor dem Start des DBZ-Animes und die Hauptgeschichte endet im Spiel nach dem Sieg gegen Kid Boo -  danach scheint das Spiel an sich aber noch weiter Spielbar zu sein, zumindest ließ eine direkte Sequenz darauf schließen, da man von einen Charakter angerufen wurde, den ich da so nicht erwartet hatte aber das sind Dinge mit denen ich mich erst noch auseinander setzen werde...ach ja und den "Power Awakening"-DLC zum Spiel habe ich ja auch noch, der auf mich wartet, ich freu' mich drauf! Achso, ja, die Spielaspekte:
Man hat keinen festen Hauptcharakter - klar Son-Goku - aber man wechsel Story-bedingt immer mal wieder durch verschiedene Figuren durch, wie halt Son-Goku, Son-Gohan, Piccolo, Vegeta usw. und das macht schon Sinn und lockert das Geschehen immer wieder auf. Vom reinen Gameplay her bleibt das Movement und das Kampfsystem in den Auseinandertsetzungen aber ziemlich gleich, es ändern sich halt immer mal wieder ein paar Angriffe. Man hat die Möglichkeit allerlei Dinge in der Spielwelt einzusammeln - was zugegebenermaßen unglaublich motivierend und befriedigend ist! Es macht einfach Spaß zu sehen wie die Zahlen der verschiedenen Sammelgegenstände nach oben gehen, aus den meisten Sachen kann man halt auch andere Dinge herstellen, wie Heil-Items usw., auch kann man im Spiel Angeln und Kochen.
Technisch lief das Spiel bei mir absolut Rund...bis auf eine Ausnahme:
Denn vor einiger Zeit bekam das Spiel ein umfangreiches (kostenloses) Update auf dem PC (was auch schon z.B. auf der PS5 vorhanden war), das heißt: Man hat jetzt ein überarbeitetes Grafikgerüst, bzw. Beleuchtung, Texturen usw. wurden überarbeitet und wirken jetzt genereller moderner und detailiertet...ob die nun immer Stimmiger aussehen...das ist eine andere Sache. Das Problem war aber nun das durch dieses Update die alte Standard-Version des Spiels mir in einer Session bestimmt 5x hintereinander ohne ersichtlichen Grund abgestürzt ist...was sehr ärgerlich war. Demzufolge wurde ich etwas genötigt den Spielstand auf die neue Version zu importieren um dort weiterspielen zu können. Jetzt wäre es ja mal interessant zu wissen ob das nur ein Problem bei mir war oder andere Spieler auch damit zu kämpfen haben/hatten??

Lassen wir mal dieses spezielle Technikproblems bei Seite und erfreuen wir uns noch ein wenig an die gelungene Spielepräsentation! Ich habe das Game mit der originalen japanischen Synchronisation und deutschen Untertiteln gespielt...mit den englischen Stimmen kann ich nicht all zuviel anfangen aber das gilt generell für das komplette Anime-Genre, entweder japanischer O-Ton oder eine gute deutsche Synchro! Und die deutsche Synchro bei DBZ ist halt einfach Legendär, sehr schade dass es diese nicht ins Spiel geschafft hatte...das wäre dann wohl das BESTE Dragon Ball-Spiel aller Zeiten gewesen, so ist es "nur" das beste Dragon Ball Spiel das die Story am besten wiedergibt! 
Denn auch musikalisch wird man verwöhnt, vor allem wenn man in den Optionen die passende "Feld-Musik" auswählt und unbeschwert durch die Gegend fliegt - da kickt die Nostalgie mit einen deftigen Magengrubenschlag rein - im besten Sinne! ;)

Generell verbinde ich viel Gutes und natürlich auch meine Kinder/Jugendzeit mit Dragon Ball (Z) und ganz im ernst, zum Ende hin, als man im finalen Kampf war, der Opening-Song mit "CHA-LA HEAD-CHA-LA" einsetzte und man den bösen Boo endlich die Lebenslichter ausgeknipst hatte, da hatte ich schon ein kleines Tränchen in den Augen und etwas Gänsehaut! Also besser geht's nun wirklich nicht! Demzufolge: Wenn ich die DBZ-Geschichte noch einmal erleben will, dann doch bitte mit diesen Spiel hier! "Dragon Ball: Sparking! Zero" hatte das ja gewissermaßen ziemlich in den Sand gesetzt und "Dragon Ball Xenoverse" hatte die Story ja eher geremixt und auf links gedreht, statt diese chronologisch durch zu erzählen und "Dragon Ball FighterZ" hatte ja seine eigene Geschichte, die allerdings auch sehr cool erzählt wurde.

So. Bevor ich jetzt aber noch weiter abschweife will ich diese Review zu einem schlüssigen Ende bringen und bedanke mich ganz herzlich bei jeden der, sich mein geschreibsel bis hier hin durchgelesen hat. Vielen lieben Dank! :)

Ansonsten melde ich mich dann hier nochmal zurück, wenn ich im Late/After-Game noch etwas ausgetobt  habe oder den "Power Awakening"-DLC unter die Lupe genommen habe.

The Game Kitchen are aptly named because they are cooking with every game they drop.  Ragebound is a gorgeous 2D gauntlet of a game that manages to slot just below the classic NES trilogy in terms of difficulty (due to its honestly forgiving modernisms) that instead of trying to make the classic games more complex, decided to simplify its complexities and bring a fairer and more well rounded experience. With a simple story with likeable characters and the building of a relationship between our dual protagonists I think we have a very strong base for a secondary franchise to build upon and improve further, but make no mistake, this game feels complete in what it wants to be and is an absolute joy to play.  I want to see more of the black spider clan in future in tandem with the Hayabusa squad (maybe Ayane too pls). 

Worth a purchase for the best pixel art The Game Kitchen have produced but even more worth playing for the tight gameplay.  9/10.

Итак, после много-много часов игры я подвожу итог и раскладываю по полочкам, почему вам не нужно играть в эту игру, если вы не готовы потратить 100+ часов. 

[h2] Кратко: [/h2]

Физика - гaвно. Кооператив или за счёт потери сюжетного контента, либо только с рабами, которые будут строить дороги и возить ресурсы. ИИ - гaвно. Основная цель игры - строительство дорог, по факту скучная рутина. Смысл играть в игру - достижения и пасхалочки, а также повалять большие машинки в грязи. Нормальных машин немного, используешь по итогу штук 5-7 из всего автопарка. Лесозаготовка - гaвно. 

[h2] Длинно: [/h2]

Касательно физики: 

Физика в игре отвратительная. Любое столкновение обрабатывается словно столкновение резинового попрыгунчика о батут. А касание, наоборот, словно все поверхности в игре и транспорт в том числе обёрнуты наждачной бумагой, это относиться и к езде. Ощущается она как раз таки как езда по наждачной бумаге на колесах, политых клеем. Такое ощущение, что каждой точке на карте искусственно прописана максимальная скорость движения и как только транспорт касается зоны этой точки, скорость мгновенно меняется без учёта какой-либо инерции. Точнее вся инерция будет уходить в полную остановку на месте, иногда сопровождаемую переворачиванием на крышу, разворотом на 180 градусов или катапультированием вертикально вверх. Центр тяжести почти всей техники находиться где-то на три метра выше крыши. Особенно это заметно на бульдозере, в походном режиме у которого этот центр тяжести где-то в пяти метрах выше и впереди ковша, и от любой кочки или наклона он просто заваливается набок. Отдельная “боль моя дырка задница” это физика железных дорог, когда техника гигантских размеров не в состоянии преодолеть железнодорожный рельс. 

Касательно кооператива: 

Контента в виде заданий в игре не очень много. Фактически приглашая случайного игрока, вы теряете этот контент. Большинство заданий не требуют присутствие более одного игрока, их почти всегда можно выполнить одному на одном виде техники. По сути, у вас два варианта кооператива: либо у вас будет бесплатный раб (или несколько), который будет прокладывать ровные дороги, строить мосты, собирать мусор для переработки, перевозить ресурсы на склад и валить лес, либо вы будете в большинстве случаев вдвоём делать то, что быстрее и интереснее сделать одному. 

Касательно строительства дорог: 

Строительство дорог с помощью ИИ. 
Данная функция доступна почему-то только через задания. Нет возможности задать произвольный маршрут, хотя такая функция очень бы упростила и ускорила игру в одиночном режиме, да и в кооперативном. Можно было бы определить зоны, где можно задавать ИИ прокладывать дороги. Хоть и основной геймплей игры именно в строительстве дорог, но рутину можно было бы дать на откуп ИИ, а уже сам игрок бы прокладывал дороги через какие-нибудь дебри. Кроме того, ИИ умеет пользоваться только маленькой техникой в этих целях. Большой асфальтоукладчик и каток просто сваливаются с песчаной насыпи, если ими управляет ИИ. Односторонняя дорога, построенная ИИ, имеет очень крутые песчаные обочины, если на них заехать хотя бы одним колесом, то с вероятностью 90% ты либо перевернёшь технику на крышу, либо просто застрянешь в грязи. Есть буквально пару заданий на строительство дорог, где есть две полосы и дорога достаточно широкая и комфортная для использования. Однопутную дорогу приходиться всегда корректировать, расширяя песком обочины, чтобы не падать с дороги. 

Самостоятельное строительство дорог. 
Основная претензия к радиусу карьеров. Если вы всё-таки решите купить игру, то ставьте максимальный радиус при запуске первой сессии. Возить туда-сюда песок вне радиуса карьера просто невыносимо. Это превращается в постоянную возню в грязи с разворотом грузовика и прыжки из бульдозера в грузовик и обратно, чтобы сразу разравнивать кучу. Можно было бы сделать радиус покрытия карьеров на всю карту, но возможность их использовать сделать через задания или за большую цену в служебных жетонах. Переносной просеиватель песка откроется примерно после прохождения 2/3 игры, нужно полностью закрыть на 100% примерно 5-6 карт, что бы хватило опыта открыть просеиватель. Можно было бы дать просеиватель в начале игры и завязать его на карьерах, например с помощью него расширять радиус карьера, если просеиватель находиться в карьере. 

Касательно мостов: 

Из полезных в игре только бетонные мосты и широкий деревянный. С узких деревянных и мостов для “скаутов” вы будете просто падать на любой технике, так как управление транспортом и физика в игре не очень комфортные. Такой же бесполезный мост из металлических балок, в котором запросто можно наглухо застрять, зацепившись за опоры. Через этот мост нельзя нормально проехать даже на бульдозере в походном режиме, если ты не попал в миллиметраж по габаритам. На лесных картах стройте только деревянные широкие мосты из рядом расположенных деревьев. На пустынных бетонные, желательно широкие, если там будут прокладываться маршруты.  

Касательно лесозаготовки: 

Сбор и погрузка брёвен особая “боль в моя дырка задница”. Лично я просто спиливаю дерево, везу его до точки сбора или точки строительства моста и там уже обрабатываю. Погрузить нормально бревно в лесовоз на грани подвига. Физика брёвен отвратительная, ровно в лесовозы брёвна уложить просто невозможно. Во внедорожные грузовики-самогрузы брёвна в длину не помещаются, а грузовики длинномеры вне дорог вязнут в грязи. Ещё вариант просто покупать брёвна и грузить их в длинномер, а потом везти туда, где он сможет проехать, либо куда была проложена вами дорога. А лучший вариант, просто строить бетонные мосты. Плиты единственный ресурс, который комфортно можно грузить и перевозить. 

Касательно грузовиков длинномеров: 

Нулевое сцепление и проходимость. Катается эта срань только по идеально ровной горизонтальной асфальтированной поверхности. Просто не покупайте и не используйте эту технику вообще. Задания с доставкой выполняйте с помощью крана - цепляете длинномер за бампер, разворачиваете стрелу крана назад и тащите его волоком за краном до точки назначения. Альтернативный способ только один - проложить идеально ровную асфальтовую дорогу с максимальными уклонами/поворотами в пять градусов и молиться что бы его не стащило на обочину, потому что даже на песке он обязательно забуксует и завалиться на бок в грязь.  

 Касательно прокладки маршрутов: 

Ещё одна “боль в моя дырка задница”. Боты ИИ забивают на следование точкам маршрута, разлёт в пять метров влево-вправо совершенно нормальное для них поведение. Большинство машинок проезжают почти везде, кроме вязкой грязи, где можно подсыпать песочка, но вот длинномерам нужны только горизонтальные асфальтовые автобаны. Если самостоятельно почти невозможно, где любо проехать на этой срани, то ИИ тем более постоянно загоняет их то в грязь, то стаскивает с дороги. 

Но всё-таки в игре есть и положительные моменты: 
 
Красивая графика и проработка окружения. Листики это прям листики, а не текстура. Всякие мелочи в дизайне карт. Пасхалочки. Всё выглядит очень симпатично, особенно лесные карты. Каждая карта с душой прям сделана. 

Пару забавных заданий и достижений. Достижения можно сказать составляют чуть ли не половину интереса в игре. Без них просто не было бы смысла играть больше пару десятка часов и изучать карты подробно. По факту только из-за них мною и была пройдена игра. DLC без достижений даже трогать не стал.

记得小时候，我伏在舅舅的椅背上，看着一个个文明在眼前展开。舅舅的手指在键盘与鼠标间忙碌地起落，哒哒的声响，混和着游戏中战马的嘶鸣、火枪的齐射，便是我童年里最奇特的交响乐。我其实看不大懂那地图上的纷争，只觉得那建造房屋的动画好看，那一队队行进的士兵威风，还有那奇异的“卡片”，能从故乡源源不断地送来援军与牛羊，像是一个永远也拆不完的礼物包裹。
现在我上班了把《帝国时代III：决定版》放入了购物车。下载，安装，点击那个熟悉的图标，铛铛铛，铛铛铛当那浑厚而充满历史感的主题音乐再度响起时，我仿佛听见了童年那扇紧闭的门，吱呀一声，为我重新敞开了。
我拥有了自己的堡垒，自己的村民，自己的军队，上网看教程学习船运的卡片，我像一个迟到的学生，终于坐进了本该属于我的课堂。我沉迷于调配经济发展的节奏，我享受着一支骑兵队冲垮敌人阵线的快意，我更会精心挑选那些从主城驶来的“卡片”，每一次选择，都像是完成了一场与过去的、心照不宣的对话。
说来也怪，当童年的憧憬被亲手实现，那份由距离产生的神秘美感并未消散，反而沉淀为一种更为醇厚、更为私密的温暖。它不再是叔叔屏幕上那个遥不可及的世界，而是我的书房里，一盏台灯下，独属于我的一方天地。在这里，时间仿佛是可折叠的。屏幕里是十九世纪的殖民拓荒，屏幕外是我现代的办公桌，而我的神思，却可以轻易地飘回那个伏在椅背上的、闷热的下午。
这不仅仅是一款游戏。它是一个时间的胶囊，一封我写给童年自己的回信。如果你也曾有过那样一个伏在长辈椅背上的下午，如果你的记忆里也封存着一段来自过去的、模糊而温暖的光影，那么，我真心地将它推荐给你。来建起你的第一座城镇中心，训练你的第一队民兵，接收你的第一张来自故乡的支援吧。你会发现，那个你以为早已远去的孩子，其实一直安静地等在屏幕的那一端，等着与你，重逢在这场跨越了岁月的远征里。
Decades later and I still enjoy it like the first time. If only the devs put more work into the title.

After 100%ing everything, I can say most of my playtime was pretty boring. After clearing the game once by taking down the 13 bosses (which really only takes one prestige), the rest of your game time is going to be taken up by grinding. You need at least 600-700 kills on each boss to guarantee max rarity, and more to get the materials to max them out. 

This is 90% of the content in the game. Builds range from "one-two shotting the final bosses" to "potentially taking half an hour per kill", meaning that not optimizing just feels like a giant waste of time. At the top end, there's really only two viable builds. There used to be more, but they snapped the game in half too much and were nerfed. So the main selling point of theorycrafting builds is pointless because there's no incentives for anything other than speed kills.

The power spikes that you get in incremental games that give you dopamine are very rare, with them coming only from item rarity upgrades and progressing in the skill tree. Progressing in the skill tree is odd, as the most effective way of doing so is to stockpile a bunch of resources and then getting the funds as quick as possible to purchase the buildings that let you buy more skill points. This means that  it both incentivizes speed kills and also doesn't really let you toy around with builds.

I didn't even bother doing that, so it took me 76 hours to get everything done. However, I was paying attention for only 5 of those hours tops.

Tldr:  just no

Long version: I finished the game start to finish in update 1.1, completed 100% of acievements and then continued the grind to get all pets and all items maxed. There are a lot of problems I see with the game.

I played a click freeze-; a burn-; a poison-; a "mid budget" troll-; a physical damage- and a Light Spear build. The difference in their power is astonomical. With one build of them you one shot every boss (insanely low investment), one with higher investment and with others despite higher investment you sit there for 20 minutes to kill a mid-tier boss. Due to the way the game is build there is nothing you can do about this other than playing "the best" build.

We all know idle games, you one shot everything, get to a wall, use a ascension mechanic of some sort and get stronger. Not here. You fight these Bosses, most of their abilitys are not at all impactful and for like 2 or 3 of them they can litterally break your build. But thats fine for me. What is not is the pacing. You dont get to a wall, reset and then get stronger - no. You earn skill points [b] once [/b] when defeating a boss for the first time and then you spend them in a limited skilltree (with limited I mean there is a predifined number of passives to take). So when you got everything for a archtype you cant get stronger through that when hitting a wall. Instead you have to grind the items you need by killing the bosses which drop them. You need 1000 items to level an item to its highest rarity. On the highest difficulty you drop 2 loot chests with the item garanteed. So ~500 kills - not to bad you might think. Well that depends on the kill time. The last boss of the game needs to be killed 100 times for its hardest archievement - the second last one 400 times. You will probably not do them on max difficulty but even if you did you still did not finish the item.

You basically come to a point where you get a build together just to farm items which not requires you to actively click anything and leave it running on low level bosses to get the item to max rank you need for a build. Its just so boring! Killing the final boss with the right build is pretty easy, but then the game is basically over. There is no point to farm the items or farm skill points (you can get more every 20 minute as an exchange for ingame materials) because you most likely cant spend them. And when you see a 200+ passive points build guide dont let yourself be fooled. Two builds that I played could one shot the last boss in their highest difficulty and when I stopped I "only" had 147 passive points.

Is it perfect, no. It's got heart. It's got soul. It's got an insanely detailed world to explore. 

Is it janky? Yes. 

Are  a lot of the gripes in other reviews here spot on? Yes. 

It doesn't matter, this game is AMAZING despite all those flaws. 

We need more games like this. Ever since Bethesda screwed up Arkane Austin, Rebellion is our only chance of getting anything remotely as good as Prey. 

Anyways, back to the game. It reminds me of Farcry 3 in terms of just wonder of exploration. Lots of points of interest and caves and bunkers and Manors and on and on. 

It is interconnected like the worlds in Dark Souls. Has some elements of Fallout sure, but not really. You're not wandering a wasteland. You are in a HIGHLY detailed world. 

I'm guessing no procedural generation was used here. It feels hand crafted. It's a joy to walk around in. 

I do wish there was more puzzles and actual secrets. I only found 1 'puzzle' so far and I'm 22 hours in. Most secrets are kinda ruined because there's always another way in so I rarely ever felt like I solved something. Hopefully they can improve on that in the next game. The enemies could have better AI but they aren't horrible. 

The medical center is truly terrifying. The different zones are so unique. From a town to the woods to a military zone, all felt different and kept me intrigued to keep playing. All the ingredients are here for a great first entry into what hopefully is long line of games. 

I love how it's not open world but the zones are huge and there are very few if any pointless areas. Contrast that with Breath of the Wild or GTA where there's so much space but everything is so spread out and not much going on in most areas. Open world games are 1 inch deep and 20 miles wide, this game is 20 feet deep and 1 mile wide. More my style. 

And the Cherry on top??? 

I'm running this at 60+FPS solid on a 7 year old computer. It's a GTX 1080 folks. It looks amazing. Butter smooth. No stupid stuttering from shader compilation Unreal Engine bullcrap. f5 and f9 works. It's a dream. FOV slider. All games should start at this technical level and build from there. Really a masterpiece of a game. I can't stop writing about it lol. 

Oh and the story and dialogue. Most games I just get impatient and skip as quickly as possible to get back to... ya know... gameplay.... but this game I actually paid attention to what was happening. I'm not done yet, but there are multiple people asking for loyalty so I'm guessing there are multiple endings. Wow. Imagine that. All choice in a game. Since it's a game and we can do that. A developer that understands what GAMERS want. That this is a GAME not a MOVIE. Seriously people. Throw money at this company. We need more games like this.

I really can't say enough about it. It's a GAMERS game. Oh and I also get a little bit of a S.T.A.L.K.E.R. vibe as well in terms of aesthetics and quest design. Not a ton but a little. 

So to recap, you have the wonderment of exploration of hand crafted, intricate environments ala Dark Souls, Tomb Raider, Farcry 3. You have the shooting and quest designs more like Fallout/S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Throw in some crafting, some MYST, and multiple endings and the absolute rock solid tech...  Come on now. This is a MUST BUY.

I do not work for or know anyone from Rebellion. I'm just a 44 year old dude who enjoys GOOD games and I want to see this company make more games.

[i]Atomfall[/i] fait partie de ces bonnes surprises que l'on n'avait pas forcément vues venir.

Comme l'excellent [i]Generation Zero®[/i] auquel il me fait un peu penser, [i]Atomfall[/i] offre une ambiance et un environnement incroyablement réussis. Que ce soit dans le soin apporté aux décors, les détails ou l'architecture des lieux traversés, [i]Atomfall[/i] offre un magnifique voyage dans le Royaume-Uni des années 1950 avec ses maisons typiques et paysages typiques. On prend vraiment énormément de plaisir à parcourir cette campagne anglaise recréée par les développeurs. Qui plus est, les développeurs ont su varier les environnements traversés, alternant entre un pittoresque village, des installations militaires plus ou moins secrètes, l'inquiétant Échangeur, une sombre forêt, etc. Le dépaysement est toujours garanti, et la maîtrise artistique se retrouve également dans le [i]design[/i] des personnages croisés. Même si les jeux en vue subjective à l'univers post-apocayptiques sont nombreux, [i]Atomfall[/i] se détache de la masse par son ambiance et son identité uniques. 

L'ambiance du jeu est également très réussie et nous plonge dans la catastrophe nucléaire de Windscale, qui ici a connu une évolution complètement différente. On croisera au cours de notre quête un grand nombre de personnages haut-en-couleur qui ont chacun leurs propres objectifs, pas toujours avouables, et qui ne manqueront pas d'essayer de nous manipuler pour les aider. Ainsi, entre la quête principale et les très nombreuses missions secondaires confiées par les personnages ou découvertes au fil des événements, on ne manque jamais d'occupations, bien au contraire. Il faudra d'ailleurs un petit temps d'habitude pour gérer les différentes tâches et les nombreux éléments qui se multiplient rapidement. Il en va de même pour les mécaniques du jeu qui demandent un peu d'expérience : on ramasse de très nombreux éléments que l'on peut transformer, modifier ou améliorer. L'inventaire devient vite pléthorique et une bonne gestion est nécessaire pour ne pas s'encombrer d'éléments inutiles et ne pas passer à côtés d'objets indispensables. 

Pour moi, [i]Atomfall[/i]  est clairement l'une des plus grandes réussites du genre depuis [i]Generation Zero®[/i] et mérite clairement de figurer dans la bibliothèque des joueuses et joueurs qui ont le goût des bons jeux de survie.

1. There is no real progression in the game besides unlocking the tools and side quests to upgrade the crafting table on your train. I resorted to just having a pile of coal in the room with me because even using the storage next to the furnace I would have to go back and forth grabbing one piece at a time.

2. It would be nice if I had a separate tool wheel from my inventory so that exploring a new area I didn't lose half my inventory space to taking a pickax, shovel and axe. Going along with that there is the oversight that material nodes drop 3 items but your inventory stacks to 4 making it frustrating when gathering materials.

I am a bit conflicted on this game. On one hand, I enjoyed my 40 hours spend with it and I definitely got my money's worth. So it's hard for me not to recommend it on just that basis. But at the same time I see tons of wasted potential with weird design choices and ultimately not that much to actually do, culminating in a game that fundamentally is very solid, but is deeply flawed. And because of this I don't see myself ever coming back to it to grind for the rest of the achievements or to 100% all of it's "content". And I am sure there are some people out there who would not like this game because of those things, so let me talk about them in this review so you can make up your minds.

The first big problem this game has is that it pretends (purposefully or not) to have way, and I mean WAY more things to do than it actually does. The game assaults you with lots of characters, stages, multiple game modes, and a massive list of unlockable things and progression systems. But in reality it is all VERY inflated by re-using content over and over. Some examples: 

-Different stages have next to no differences between one another and no relevant gimmicks to make them stand out or play different 
- Differences between characters are largely just based on different stats and a couple character specific skills, even the character specific mechanics you unlock as you level them up are the same thing across all character (just repackaged with different visuals and stat variations). But every character plays 99% the same way.
- Same skills are repeated multiple times with just their elements or other arbitrary characteristics altered. So the hundreds of skill this game has practically boild down to a few dozen distinctly feeling ones
-Different enemies are just reskins that use the same few attack types. If it was just stage enemies I would not even list it as an issue... but it goes for bosses too.

You get it, this is the patter through the whole game. Everything is stretched so thin, one unique thing is split into a couple more things that are almost the same, just to make the game feel larger than it is. The first time you open this game you might be overwhelmed by just how much stuff there is in front of you, but as you play it is starts feeling very, very small. Ultimately this isn't really a deal breaker, because the amount of unique things here is... alright, it's not too much but not too little. It just feels cheap and lame, the game would've been much better if it had 25% of the "content", but it all felt more unique. And while this is definitely this game's biggest weakness, it ultimately would not detract from it's replayability if it pulled off it's own satisfying gameplay loop.

... Which is where we arrive at the game's the second big problem: balance. The problem here is twofold, and it compounds on itself:

1. The way this game does it's damage formula is just... bad. The way they made the math work forces you into the exact same build path if you ever want to make a good build, and it's not the first game that made this mistake either. This game has both additive and multiplicative damage multipliers. Meaning, a 50% damage boost can either be a 50% increase to all the damage that you do, or just a +50% bonus added to all the other bonuses you already have. On it's own that is not a problem, many games do this and it works well if it's done properly and the devs make both play nice together. Here unfortunately the developers completely dropped the ball. Long story short: the game features many debuffs that stack multiplicatively with your total damage dealt. That alone is immensely powerful, but then they also made those debuffs multiply on top of EACH OTHER. That's right, we are no longer just multiplying things, we are doing FACTORIALS now!! And the worst part of all of this, this is THE ONLY way to increase your damage like this. There is no other way in the game to scale your damage in such an absurd way, which means that if you ever wish to get a "god run", you need these debuffs, and you need to be able to stack them as best as you can.

2. There is an archetype of damage skill that is just... superior. It's the skills that multiply their damage based on either the number of debuff/status stacks on the enemy, or ones that consume said stacks and multiply their damage. Basically: the skills taht scale their damage based on debuff number one way or another. It's not even funny how much better these skills are than all the others. And it's sad to see, because there are other skills in the game that clearly try to be good damage skills too, scaling of different things or having other gimmicks to raise their damage. But the difference in strength between the good ones and the bad ones are so massive, we are talking multiple zeroes at the end of the number differences, you HAVE to use these skills if you want the best results.

And if you add those two problems together, you end up with a game that puts extreme emphasis on skills that either directly apply the debuffs I mentioned earlier or are good at applying them in other ways once you get supporting skills, and then it makes you take the scaling damage skills that scale off either the 3 DOT effects, or the status effects, of which there aren't that many. Suddenly, the hundreds of skills this game has boil down to MAYBE a few dozen actually good ones. And since every character is basically the same and can use the same things, you will end up making the variation of the same build every single time... the only way to enjoy some variety here is to unfortunately play on lower difficulties and intentionally ignore the objectively correct way to build your character. Basically: playing the weak, off-meta build in a hack and slash game. And let's be honest, almost nobody enjoys intentionally gimping themselves in a game like this.


So, all of that sounds pretty bad, right? And yeah, it is. And that's why I will probably never come back to it. But that doesn't change the fact that before I arrived at this point, I got 40 hours of good fun out of it and finished the game, and for those 40 hours the problems I mentioned didn't really surface and were not that big of a part of the game. It was really only after I beat the game's final boss for the first time that I started to think "yeah, I think I'm done, there isn't that much here to enjoy afterwards". So, a careful recommendation for people who enjoy this genre of video games.

Getriebe unserer Kriegsmaschinerie und will ganz bestimmt nicht auf Sekunde und Pixel 
genau manövriert werden.

zum Triumph nach oben.

Solange wir mehr pro Sekunde fördern, als unsere aktiven Bauprojekte vom Konto saugen, 
lassen wir einen endlosen Raumschiffstrom vom Stapel.

Hours Played: Too many that I’ll never get back.

Destiny 2 is a game that could have been legendary, but instead chose to be a live-service treadmill where every season resets your progress and makes last month’s loot worthless. You don’t progress here— you rerun the same chores forever just to stay level with everyone else.

Weapons and builds get replaced or nerfed constantly, not for balance, but to push you into the next paid season, the next expansion, the next cosmetic bundle. It feels less like a game and more like a subscription to disappointment.

PvP? Don’t expect skill or mastery to matter. It’s all about who brought the correct flavor-of-the-month weapon or exotic combo Bungie hasn’t nerfed yet. It’s not competitive. It’s rock-paper-scissors, except sometimes Bungie temporarily removes rock and charges you for scissors.

The story has been wandering in circles for years, characters appear and vanish, plot threads get dropped, and entire campaigns you paid for have been deleted from the game. Imagine paying for a product that gets removed later. That’s Destiny 2.

At this point, the strongest enemy in Destiny isn’t a raid boss — it’s the realization that Bungie wants your time, your money, and your patience, but gives very little back.

If you’re considering starting this game now: Don’t.
If you’re still here out of habit: Walk away.

Cabernet is not that. It's an arguably smaller pool, but it goes incredibly deep. The art style is gorgeous, the VA and music is astounding, and the story genuinely pulls you in at every moment. It has a few hiccups, and admittedly I'm coming in to the game late, so I imagine they fixed some bugs prior. There's still a few issues in that department; but unlike VTM:Bloodlines 2, where I'm struggling to want to continue the story through what feels like chore after chore - Cabernet is like a book I couldn't put down until I was finished.

The story is yours, it draws you in, and the game is clever and funny at times, and at other times, the characters and their stories make you want to cry. The relationships Liza forms are genuinely touching, and the romance is done incredibly well.

My biggest issue with Cabernet? That it ended. I didn't want to say good bye to Liza, and naturally, I'm already on another playthrough to try a different path and style.

This game is worth every rose it is given.

Path of Exile (POE) não é um MMORPG, como a maioria o classifica. POE é, na verdade, um action-RPG online. Você não tem necessariamente que interagir com outros jogadores se não o quiser, e mesmo que o queira, sua interação é limitada apenas a um chat global e a alguns poucos (5) jogadores que você, por ventura, permita que entrem em sua equipe (party).

Considerado o sucessor verdadeiro do Diablo II pelos mais saudosistas, Path of Exile é um jogo bastante interessante para quem gosta de RPGs hack-and-slash com uma grande gama de possibilidades em suas builds. Com uma árvore de habilidades de mais de 1300 pontos diferentes além de um complexo sistema de crafting, cada personagem torna-se único em seu potencial, apesar de, no momento, não ter tantas possibilidades de customização visual.

Após mais de 4000 horas jogadas, sinto-me confiante que posso dar o verdadeiro valor ao jogo nessa análise sem, no entanto, deixar de considerar seus pontos fracos. Por isso, vamos por partes:

[h1]Conceito e Existência[/h1]
Path of Exile é um jogo que foi desenvolvido desde seu início para dar aos saudosistas jogadores de Diablo II um ar de renovação. Chris Wilson, o líder do projeto, e seus companheiros fundaram uma empresa chamada Grinding Gear Games, a atual responsável pelo gerenciamento do jogo, e decidiram dedicar-se exclusivamente ao desenvolvimento de POE.

Seguindo o modelo original de Diablo II, o Path of Exile tem point-of-view semelhante, embora com gráficos melhores e atualizados para uma nova geração (inclusive, recentemente, recebendo suporte a DirectX 11 e algumas funcionalidades exclusivas deste), além de conter o mesmo 'feeling' de grinding que tanto tornou Diablo II famoso.

[h1]Jogabilidade[/h1]
Com uma árvore de habilidades de mais de 1300 opções, além de 6 raças iniciais, POE tem uma jogabilidade altamente imersível e de grande liberdade aos jogadores. Ao criar um personagem, você tem uma série de quests que devem ser seguidas sob uma história modelo, dividida em dez atos e em duas partes. Ao finalizar a primeira parte da história, você parte para a segunda, com uma dificuldade maior, já que você recebe algumas penalidades.

Terminada a parte da história e com seu personagem por volta do level 60 (level 100 sendo o máximo), você parte então para o conteúdo end-game do jogo, que consiste, na maior parte do tempo, 'rodar' mapas (mais de 100 tipos diferentes) em dificuldades diferentes em busca de mais level e/ou itens raros e ajudar Zana, uma NPC, na guerra do atlas. É aí que o grinding se torna interessante para pessoas que gostam (como eu). Para as que não gostam, você pode simplesmente começar de novo se quiser e tentar novas e divertidas builds.

Para se ter uma ideia dos níveis de grinding do jogo, estima-se que a possibilidade de dropar um dos itens mais raros do jogo (Espelho de Kalandra) seja de uma vez a cada dez anos se você jogar cerca de 4 horas por dia. É bastante, de fato, mas seu alto valor no jogo faz com que todos sonhem com a possibilidade de tornarem-se ricos da noite pro dia.

Os servidores são divididos em ligas. Há a liga permanente softcore e a permanente hardcore. A diferença entre uma e outra consiste no fato de que, se você morrer com seu personagem na liga hardcore, ele será automaticamente transferido para a liga softcore (ao contrário de Diablo, onde você perde o personagem).

Há também as ligas temporárias, normalmente lançadas a cada 2 ou 3 meses. Elas oferecem um "fresh start", ou seja, um início fresco para aqueles que não querem se submeter à inflacionada economia das ligas permanentes ou simplesmente desejam tentar se perpetuarem como ricos comerciantes ou crafters de itens nas novas ligas. Note que, ao final de cada liga, seus personagens lá localizados, bem como o baú da sua conta, serão transferidos para as ligas permanentes.

[h1]Gráficos[/h1]
Além do que pode se ver nas próprias imagens, Path of Exile não é um jogo que possa se dizer ser muito voltado ao desenvolvimento de belos gráficos. Os gráficos são sim medianos, mas mantém-se sempre atualizados com o que há de moderno no mundo dos jogos. Há cerca de um ano, como já mencionado, o jogo recebeu suporte a DirectX 11, além de alguns efeitos especiais a mais (como o movimento responsivo de capas e asas de personagens a skills ou até mesmo o vento). Na mesma época o jogo também recebeu portabilidade para o Xbox.

Sua customização visual também não é muito rica (por enquanto), sendo você, na maior parte do tempo, obrigado a ficar preso ao visual de seus itens e de sua raça (não há diferença de sexos, por exemplo - se você escolher raça X onde o personagem é, por padrão, feminino, ele continuará sendo feminino). Toda e qualquer customização visual não padrão, ou seja, que não é próprio do item que você esteja usando, é paga. A única exceção são as recompensas fornecidas no final de cada liga. Apesar disso, no último ano, a GGG tem investido bastante nesse quesito, com uma notável melhora.

O jogo tem atenção exclusiva da Grinding Gear Games, sua empresa gerenciadora. Com um início difícil de 5 funcionários, ela hoje conta com mais de 150 pessoas em dedicação exclusiva, fazendo com que seu suporte seja um dos mais efetivos que eu já tenha visto (enviei cerca de 10 a 15 tickets e a média de tempo para resposta deles foi de 5 minutos - é incrível).

[h1]Comunidade[/h1]
Você pode escolher interagir com a comunidade ou não. Esse é o principal fator que faz com que Path of Exile não seja, per-se, um MMORPG, onde, por definição, você é obrigado a interagir com um universo de jogadores. No geral, a comunidade de Path of Exile é bastante amigável e disposta a ajudar, mas, como em todo jogo, há bastantes trolls e, principalmente, scammers.

O [i]scam[/i] é legalizado no jogo desde que não seja através de transações da vida real (ou RMT - do inglês, [i]real money trading[/i]). De acordo com o próprio Chris Wilson, a empresa tenta não realizar nenhum tipo de regulação do mercado dentro do jogo, logo cabe a cada jogador tomar conta de seus itens e analisar seu devido valor antes de se desfazer dele para outro jogador. Ainda segundo ele, no jogo, [i]'knowledge is power, and power is everything'[/i] (conhecimento é poder, e poder é tudo).

No começo, não foram poucas as vezes que fui enganado por jogadores mais experientes, comprando a preço de banana mercadorias que poderiam valer bem mais caso eu soubesse seu devido valor, por isso recomendo cautela a jogadores novatos.

[h1]Pay-to-win?[/h1]
[b]Não.[/b] Não há sequer um fator que possa ser considerado pay-to-win em todo o jogo. Tudo que é adquirido por dinheiro real é por mero conceito de embelezamento e/ou [i]status quo[/i]. O único fator que possa ser considerado pay-to-win para alguns jogadores (eu não considero, no entanto) é o fato de que, ao criar uma nova conta, você recebe gratuitamente 3 abas no baú e para adquirir mais abas você deve dispor de dinheiro real.

No entanto, é bem comum o conceito de [i]mules[/i] no jogo, onde você cria vários personagens (você pode criar mais de 20 ao todo) para guardar itens dentro de seus inventários, o que não faz com que seja um fator limitante aos jogadores que não desejam pagar por conteúdo dentro do jogo.

[h1]Conclusão[/h1]
Path of Exile é uma obra-prima dos action-RPGs onlines. Sem dúvida o melhor do gênero, com a melhor companhia de jogos existente da atualidade em sua direção, mas eu, obviamente, sou suspeito a falar, já que "desperdicei" (e com orgulho) mais de 3000 horas da minha vida no jogo. Se você gosta de jogos com bastante [i]grinding[/i] e com uma grande gama de possibilidades de ações, sugiro que teste Path of Exile.

[h1]Nota: 9.5/10[/h1]
Pontos positivos:
[+] Grinding complexo
[+] Grande gama de possibilidades
[+] Árvore de habilidades com mais de 1300 opções
[+] Ligas que oferecem um começo igual a todos

Pontos negativos:
[-] Baixa gama de customização visual (mas que tem melhorado no último ano)

本作究竟讲了一个什么样的故事呢，我的朋友们，我不知道我该用什么样的表述来总结这一路上的颠簸流离，这都要从故事的开头说起。

Phew, this game took me a long time to finish. It wasn't because it's really long or because I had no time to play; it was just a combination of things that made me stop playing for two months. I'm mostly talking about the optimization and the open-world. Don't get me wrong, I really like this game, but I can't ignore those issues.

Rebirth runs decently, but honestly, I couldn't deal with the constant stutters and freezes. No matter how many tweaks and mods I used, it was still almost the same. That was my first complaint.

My second complaint is the open-world activities, which feel kind of repetitive, to be honest. I'm not talking about the Protorelic quest line — it's the only interesting and diverse activity — but the others feel so monotonous in every region. I know I could skip all these things and not torture myself, but my inner perfectionist won't let me. I agree that's somewhat my problem, but I can't deny that the activities are uninteresting. Sometimes it's really annoying. For example, I've completed 100% of the optional activities in a region, and after 30–60 minutes of story gameplay, the game gives me the next region with the same activities. These two complaints bother me the most.

FF7 is amazing: an interesting story and characters with hilarious and sad moments; cool, varied mini-games, especially in the story; an outstanding OST, even in optional quests; deep gameplay that forces you to think rather than just smash buttons like in any other action-slasher; stunning landscapes (with max graphics settings, of course); and other little things that make the game even better.

Overall, I loved this game, but a few things stopped me from enjoying it to the fullest. Subjectively, it was my desire to complete all locations 100%. Objectively, it was due to optimization issues and repetitive activities in the open world. Otherwise, the game is amazing and I love everything about it, especially the characters and their relationships with each other. I would describe it as a cool road movie with the colourful characters we fell in love with in the first part.

It's the only game in which I've taken more than 500 screenshots, by the way.

An enticing visual story of the imperial West's role in Iran during the 1950s.

In The Cat and the Coup, you play as the cat of Mohammad Mosaddegh, the first democratically elected Prime Minister of Iran, and go through back in time his story as Prime Minister, starting with his death under house arrest, and ending with his defense of the nationalization of the oil in Iran. The Cat and the Coup is a must for anyone interested in Iranian history, and especially for anyone who hasn't heard of Anglo-American intelligence operations that led to Operation Ajax, and the outing of Dr.Mosaddegh.

A short visual novel, the few minutes you'll spend in The Cat and the Coup will detail to you the events that led up to Operation Ajax, and will, with subtle jabs, the imperialist ambitions of the West whose espionage led to Mossadegh's overthrow.

[h2]TLDR:[/h2] Strange and haunting, Final Fantasy IX is a well-written game loaded with content and things to do.

[h2]GAMEPLAY OVERVIEW:[/h2] FF9 opens with the game's arguable protagonist, a monkey-boy named Zidane, and his acting / swashbuckling troupe on their way to kidnap Princess Garnet of Alexandria. As it turns out, Garnet wants to be spirited out of the city. Unfortunately, their airship is shot down during the escape, and things get much more complicated. Over the course of the game, Zidane and Garnet are joined by six other permanent characters (who come and go at various story points) and several temporary ones. Up to four characters can be in the party at a given time.

FF9 offers multi-layered gameplay, with real-time movement in the overworld and "interior" locations (cities, dungeons, etc.). There are many hidden surprises scattered through cities and dungeons. Poking into every corner of the interior locations will reward the diligent player with money, collectibles, or gear.

The relationship between character gear and abilities is one of the most interesting and dynamic facets of the game. Each piece of equipment provides a character with abilities (passive or player-activated) that the character can activate as long as they wear that gear. Each ability shows a "learning bar" while equipped. After each combat, the character gains "ability points" that automatically fill in the ability's learning bar. When the bar is filled, the character will retain the ability once the gear is removed. Older, less effective gear (such as weapons that do less damage) may carry an important skill and must be worn through enough combat to teach the character—at the cost of the character having impaired combat ability for that duration.

This aspect requires some hard choices for the player, such as balancing between decreased stats and teaching the skill, and whether or not to spend time to go back and grind against smaller (but less dangerous monsters) to safely learn the skill. It can even be a matter of which character to equip as some gear pieces give different skills to different characters. All of this requires planning and tough decisions for the player.

The equipment question can become even more daunting as certain pieces of gear can be combined to make far more effective weapons and armor, though the combination points (synthesis shops) are not available at every point of the story and certain pieces of early armor and weapons may not be seen again until much later in the game. So the player will have to decide whether to upgrade their gear and lose access to some skills for part of the game. All of this gear decision-making makes an already-deep game even more so.

When encountering a foe, the game shifts to turn-based combat, where characters can attack, use items, cast spells, and so on. It's not a strict attack-and-effect system; there are delays between selecting an action and it actually occurring, and there is no meter of where the enemy attacks fall in relation to the characters. It often makes sense to keep a healer or defender in reserve (by delaying their turn) to deal with unexpected or severely damaging enemy attacks. There are numerous status effects—positive and negative—that the player can either inflict or be affected by, such as darkness (makes physical attacks more likely to miss), silence (cannot cast spells), haste (faster attacks), auto-life (automatically resurrect a character that is knocked out) and so on. 

General world encounters are usually not too difficult, though status effects can make them more challenging. I rarely had trouble with these, save wandering into areas at too low a level. On the other hand, some of the boss fights are very imbalanced, essentially requiring the correct strategy / equipment / character build just to survive the absurd amounts of damage or crippling status effects—and even then, too many rely on stupid amounts of raw damage as "challenge." It simply feels like lazy game design—especially since this applies to certain mandatory story bosses, not just optional encounters. The second-to-final fight of the game was the perfect example of this, where that boss cast mass AOE damage over and over again, faster than my characters had turns, and quickly outpaced even my overleved healers. This type of thing happened several times and soured me on what was otherwise a fantastic experience.

Aside from the main quest, there is a metric ton of side content and optional quests available. Much of it centers around seeking treasure while riding the ostrich-like chocobos (as is standard across FF entries) and the entire chocobo storyline is a lot of fun. A series of friendly monsters hide out across the world and finding them all is a challenge.  A specific monster roaming the forests will ask riddle questions in exchange for rewards. A variety of minigames—including jumping rope with local kids, fighting monsters for a shopkeeper, and racing a local youngster—can be played at various points. Some of the minigames are available only for a limited window, so if you're enjoying one, get your fill before moving on. There is also the card game Tetra Master, which can be played with dozens of NPCs across the world, but it's moderately horrendous and frustrating.

This game is a journey, not a destination, and I think the best experience comes from treating it as such. There's so much to see and do, and very little reason to rush through it. 

[h2]STORY / WORLDBUILDING:[/h2] One of the most endearing aspects of FF9 is the degree to which each of the main eight characters has an interesting backstory and unique personality. All eight struggle with some form of uncertainty or inadequacy and watching them grow over the course of the game was a great experience. I ended up liking them all to some degree.

Like other entries in the series, the overarching story is simple enough on the surface but hidden layers peel back as the game progresses and things get much more engrossing, if moderately predictable. Overall, I found the writing consistent, clever, and gripping.

The world of Gaia is clearly a product of its era. It's decently large but also largely empty, with few obvious points of interest. None of the interior locations are very large and inside, load screens are annoyingly frequent, sometimes coming every few steps. On the plus side, the locations themselves are loaded with content. Almost every NPC can be addressed for a line or two of flavor dialogue, which was a pleasant surprise. Some offer story advancement, items, or Tetra matches.

[h2]TECHNICAL ASPECTS:[/h2] This port of FF9 ran flawlessly for me. Graphics and sound are acceptable for a twenty-five year old game, and as per the norm for the FF franchise, the music is excellent, shifting from more mellow tones when exploring to a faster, more urgent tune during combat. The (English language) dialogue is basic—even cheesy in places—but I wonder how much of that is the product of inexact translation. Some of the cut scenes are rendered in the game engine, while others have a more cinematic format, which I found to be an odd choice. The UI is adequate and very typical of PS1-era games.

I think this is a great game. However its usually advertised as a really realistic medieval battle simulator. It is not. It is a arcadey sword fighting game with really realistic graphics. Allow me to explain. In Mordhau,  there are certain mechanics that are completely different to how they are in real life. Blocks only last for a short period of time, and have a cooldown. Naturally this is to prevent block spamming, but it creates a meta that revolves around circumventing blocks through abuse of the non speed based damage system. (The feint isn't abuse as its meant to interact with the block mechanic naturally) Also shields are weirdly not physical objects unless activated to block or if something is thrown at them. Naturally the game actracts people who like the wacky nature of arcade fighting games. It's good at being a game but not at being a realistic medieval game.

As a longtime Jackbox fan who wasn't super enamored with the last 2 packs, 11 is just what I'm looking for. If you've fallen off the Jackbox bandwagon, definitely give this one a shot!
A brief overview of the games:

Doominate - Going to be honest, I wasn't expecting this one to be as funny as it was, but it really had my friends laughing! I'm a Quiplash fan and I thought this wasn't going to be as good, but even people who usually struggle with Quiplash liked this one because the prompts made it a bit more structured.

Cookie Haus - Loads of great moments with this one too. The googly eyes, sprinkles, and depth you can get with the frosting made for some great creations. Only problem we had with this one was that some of our phones really struggled to keep up with the cookie decorating--not sure if it's because the cookie decorating technology is more sophisticated than something like Drawful, or a launch-day server issue. But the game itself was loads of fun.

Hearsay - The absolute star of the pack for us. Our friend group loves to make dumb noises and do silly voices, so this one was nonstop laughs.

Legends of Trivia - A great concept that was also a lot of fun. My only criticism is that at times it seemed pretty slow-paced, but a lot of the slowness was because of the tutorial elements (which were necessary and helpful). I'm excited to revisit this one and see if that speeds it up. There might be settings that help make it a bit faster, too, that I've missed. But it was a nice twist that the trivia was co-op, and I definitely see myself revisiting this with my more trivia-focused friends.

Suspectives - Another big standout from this pack. Truth be told, I'm a big fan of hidden role games, but I haven't always loved the ones Jackbox has put out--except this one! The survey format makes it easy to understand and also turns it into a game of how well your friends know you in real life, not just your tells, while being friendly for remote groups (unlike the somewhat similar Fakin' It).

Overall, a really excellent pack. Looking forward to playing more of it!

As I write this review, the next title (EU5) is slated to release tomorrow and I felt compelled to write a review and pay homage to the greatest strategy game of all time before I must say goodbye. 

This game is so much more than just a map painter, it's a an escape to a different world, a glimpse from a time long gone, a strategy sandbox where you can write history in so many different ways. For many of us, the year 1444 has become as familiar as our own birthdays, the borders and rulers of that frozen moment etched into memory like a second language. This game has taught me more about history and geography than any college class or textbook ever could. 

There’s such a simple joy in choosing a nation and immersing yourself in its story, roleplaying its triumphs and disasters, navigating diplomacy, warfare, and economics in a living, reactive world. 

Sure, it has a significant learning curve, but it incorporates the best systems and ideas about economics, warfare, and diplomacy from similar games into one massive sandbox. Even after 4000+ hours, every campaign is different, a unique story told through the lens of ambition, power, and chance.  A single decision can ripple through centuries. Truly a game with a unlimited replayability. 

The multiplayer is another aspect entirely. I could write pages more on that, but to keep brief, they were the fondest gaming memories I'll have. 

No other game has continued to captivate me 10 years later.

It's truly a masterpiece in its genre. 

10/10

Палинур - короткая, кинетическая (без выборов в диалогах) визуальная новелла в жанре научной-фантастики, с грустным, философским и чертовски хорошим сюжетом.

[i]Справка: Палинур - персонаж Энеиды и античных мифов. Опытный навигатор, работал кормчим у Энея, героя Троянской войны. Когда узнал что боги пропустят корабль троянцев из Сицилии в Италию только получив жертвоприношение, решил пожертвовать собой и прыгнул в море. Был выброшен на берег, где был убит местными жителями. Боги получили свою жертву, троянцы добрались до Италии.[/i]

1) [u]Сюжет[/u]: новелла поведает нам историю путешественика, отправившегося в путь с космической станции, на шаттле под управлением искусственного интеллекта, по направлению к нужной ему колонии на Альфа Центавре. Но корабль попал в астероидный шторм в результате чего был сильно поврежден. В результате наш герой оказался заперт в дрейфующем корабле, один на один с бескрайним космосом и искусственным интелектом с уничтоженным модулем блокирующим эмоции. 

В сюжете поднимаются много философских вопросов - о войне, искусстве, жизни и смерти, смысле бытия и многом другом. Главная тема которая пронизывает сюжет - когда искусственный разум остается машиной и когда он уже переходит грань осознания себя настолько, что его можно уже считать живым существом? Кто помнит книги вроде -  "Снятся ли андроидам электроовцы?" Филиппа Дика, тот проникнется сюжетом еще больше. Есть много отсылок к классическим произведениям искусства, будь то музыка, фильмы или мифы. История в игре пронизана светлой грустью, концовка же запомнится надолго. Сюжетно это имхо одна из лучших НФ новелл что мне встречались.

2) [u]Графика и звуки[/u]: новелла сия больше про сюжет, поэтому артов мало. Задники в основном представлены темным и звездным космосом, за исключением начальной станции. Большая часть артов это наш прекрасный ИИ. Музыка мягкая, мелодичная и приятная, часть трэков - обработка классики.

3) [u]Язык[/u]: новелла сия только на английском. Язык здесь имхо не слишком сложный, но при этом есть довольно много культурных сносок, плюс поэтические обороты речи, поэтому стоит это иметь ввиду, если есть сомнения касательно своего уровня владения языком.

[u]Как итог[/u]: одна из лучших в сюжетном плане научно-фантастических новелл, с хорошей историей и философским наполнением. Любителям жанра, рекомендую категорически!

If you are well-versed in the genre of visual novels (VNs), you will find Palinurus to be a well-written, tight little story that was made as a NaNoRenO 2015 submission by Watercress Studios. If you are a casual VNer, or new to the genre entirely, say perhaps a fan of anime and anime styled art, then you will find Palinurus to be a surprisingly deep and introspective story with great music and very cool storyline. Keep in mind that the studio is all volunteer, and NaNoRenO is a game jam where developers are challenged to make a visual novel from start to finish - in just one month! Palinurus is noteably impressive for being such a rapidly developed story. The strength is in the synergy between the poignant message, the character interaction and the amazing music composition. This VN is great. It is absolutely worth the experience of reading through.

Very early days, but there's already a lot to love here. Many people have already made the comparisons to 7 Days to Die and Project Zomboid, and those are entirely accurate. The pace is exceptionally and intentionally slow - this seems like a game that's less about surviving the zombie apocalypse and more about the rebuilding society while incidentally dealing with zombies. There's a massive amount of details in the crafting and world interaction options - if you can see it, you can affect it, and it's a lot of fun to pull working parts out of one car to install in another to make a working option. Or lowering the blinds all through your safehouse so that you can turn the lights on, from time to time.

It's the development direction that bears watching, because that's sort of where the Fun Pimps went wrong - by making a game that was more accessible to more people, they stripped out most of the really good, crunchy parts of the game. And by contract, PZ is a masterpiece, but is hard to pull people into, graphically, and has a depth of detail so overwhelming that the learning curve bucks a lot of folks off. Right now, Vein is riding the line between those two really well - you're willing to learn the deep functioning because the world is vibrant and interactive. I keep finding fun surprises that keep me playing, and I'm excited to get a chance to play with my friends. 

Don't lose sight of the fact that this is still very much in dev, and only has a team of two working on it. Even if that changes, this has a ways to go before launch, so if you're picky about 100 percent complete games, keep it on your wishlist for now. But don't forget about it.

After spending some time with Expeditions: A MudRunner Game, I can’t help but feel disappointed. Compared to SnowRunner, this one leans heavily toward an arcade experience rather than a proper simulator. The core feeling of weight, traction, and realistic vehicle physics that made the earlier titles so immersive is largely gone.
Vehicle control and steering feel strangely artificial — almost like the trucks are gliding on rails rather than interacting with the terrain. There’s a lack of that gritty, tactile feedback that fans of the series have come to expect.
For players like me who enjoy open-world driving and realistic exploration, the gameplay suffers from an overload of unnecessary “fancy gadgets” and tech gimmicks that pull you out of the raw off-road experience. It’s as if the developers tried to modernize the game but ended up stripping away what made it truly special.
Honestly, this time I should have listened to the many negative reviews on YouTube. They were right — Expeditions feels like a step backward for the series.

8.boss设计稀烂，钟楼boss给人一种东方的感觉，混合双打外加全屏AOE，互动性差只能灌伤害。无尽祈祷者限制了空中平台输出，且掉落即死，在二阶段会有个拆平台的动作但是在满屏光污染的情况下十分容易忽略，导致有时候拆的正好是站的平台完全无法避免掉落即死。盐之圣体会的奥东，一坨，数值高的一笔，有肉有输出，范围大出手快还能招小弟，虽然每招都能拆且偷刀但是因为其超高的血量导致打起来十分便秘和恶心，常规战斗时长得在5-7min，且没有大输出窗口，全靠偷刀和法术，导致互动性非常差，如果没有招小弟环节可以把评分提一提，但是搞群殴就算了吧，就是一坨大的，而且招小弟是没规律的，可能连续拉好几波。
在推荐和不推荐之间摇摆，还是觉得从引起兴趣的角度来说，是可以玩一下的。除此之外确实没办法再夸什么了，是个中评2.5-3/5，但凡吃过细糠或者玩过同一品类游戏的，都能感觉到游戏的受众是不同的，也可能是我对真人电影实在不感冒，大多都显得廉价。让人动容的部分也是有的，但是来自于历史，而非游戏本身。谁非过客？花是主人。

[h1]Я — украинец, и да, я купил эту игру[/h1]
Сколько же много срача было связано с этой игрой! Я сам в неё поиграл… и не пойму причин.
В игре нет пропаганды СССР, о которой трубит большая часть украинских ютуберов. Наоборот, совки — зло, пытающееся захватить весь мир. Mundfish это, конечно, не оправдывает: они максимально на «отъебись» ответили на события в моей стране, и я уверен, что у них есть люди, поддерживающие войну. Но русские разработчики поступили более правильно, чем наши, — не добавив настоящих намёков на действительность. Я про радио в S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 с руссофобской песней.
[b]Да, я могу понять поступок наших людей, но факт есть фактом — и он уходит в пользу Mundfish.[/b]
[hr]
[h2]Геймплей[/h2]
Как я уже говорил, я прошёл игру на плохую концовку. Вторую давно проспойлерил на YouTube, поэтому не вижу смысла возвращаться к основному сюжету.
Геймплей — чистая духота: врагов всегда много, нападают толпой, патронов мало, а бьют больно. Я быстро устал и взял один большой перерыв — может быть, на несколько месяцев. Вернулся, остановился на боссе [b]Роса[/b]. Оказалось, она немощная, если всё время держаться рядом.
После неё изучил арсенал в Элеоноре и понял: у меня была самая гавняная милишка. Если бы увидел это раньше, проблем бы не было. Близняшки дались легче, но всё равно не всегда понятно, когда уворачиваться: боссы быстро двигаются, а у некоторых куча спецэффектов.
[hr]
[h2]А теперь чистый позитив[/h2]
[h3]Озвучка[/h3]
Русская озвучка — нечто! П-3 — грёбаный гопник-матершинник и сильнейший тугодум, мне это жутко нравится. Теку от голоса Кати, остальные тоже хороши, но Катя — маст-хэв.
Кстати, в бою с близняшками мне показалось, что они плачут и кричат (не уверен, планировали ли это, или просто звук получения урона).
Ещё очень понравилась химия между Сергеем (П-3) и Захаровым (ХРАЗом) — их диалоги огонь! Не пойму, почему другим не заходит.
[h3]Графика, музыка и сеттинг[/h3]
Графика, музыка и сеттинг — реальный кайф, особенно в боях с боссами. Я не фанат СССР, но сеттинг этой игры и её визуал мне жутко нравятся.
