Hello everyone!

Review: Starcom: Unknown Space – An Average Space Trip

Starcom: Unknown Space is advertised on Steam as an action RPG of space exploration. After completing the game, I'm left with a solid, but unfortunately only average, impression. The game is by no means bad, but it never sparked that "Wow, that's awesome!" feeling.

Positive Aspects

The core systems of the game deserve special mention:
Ship Crafting: The ability to build and optimize your own spaceship in detail is excellently implemented and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Research and Crew Skills: The research trees and crew skill development are also very appealing and meaningfully integrated into the gameplay. Criticisms of Exploration and Map: This is where the game unfortunately showed its weaknesses:

Dreary Space: While exploration was fun at times, it was disappointing in many places. There's a lack of diverse objects like giant space stations, space factories, or other exciting things that would bring some life to the otherwise very dreary universe.

Empty Map: I was disappointed by the map. There was really nothing to discover only in the core area. I took the time to explore the outer regions, but found almost nothing there.

Functionality and Frustration

Trading: Trading with the factions is functional, but unimaginative – it primarily serves to acquire necessary resources for shipbuilding.

Enemy AI: A major annoyance was the behavior of the computer-controlled enemies. In some parts of the game, they seem to simply keep building new bases and spawning ships without needing any resources. It just doesn't feel right.

Story: While the plot is quite nice, I personally found it somewhat minimalist and it didn't really captivate me.

Conclusion and Rating

Starcom: Unknown Space leaves me with a solid, but unremarkable impression. It's a fair game that masters the basics well, but doesn't offer any real highlights.

Therefore, my personal rating is:

6 out of 10

Please note: This is my personal experience. Everyone should keep in mind that other players may have a completely different opinion of Starcom: Unknown Space.

I like the premise of the game and I like most of the mechanics of it. But why would you not include a basic storage buffer? Yes, the individual buildings have some small local storage, but it's not sufficient for scaled industry and resource transport like trains don't work with the local storage. This is the only production/factory game I've encountered that doesn't have one.

You do get a storage for construction materials (because somehow those are different???), and there are tanks for liquids/gases. but everything else... nothing. The closest you get is a collector/distributor system.

The collector can only accept 1 thing in the radius you specify. And it disables the normal output of facilities that end up in the radius that you want to keep on a different "network". This gets problematic with large resource nodes with lots of mines on them. The collector also cannot output to anything other than a distributor.

The distributor, like the collector, only holds 1 resource and only exports to facilities in it's radius. This causes similar issues with facilities that are close to resource nodes they use.

An additional unnecessary complication for these buildings is that you cannot change the direction of their input/output roads.

In summary, I think the core mechanics of the game are good overall, but without something as fundamental as a basic storage system that just acts as a buffer, the game isn't fun and I'm pretty much considering it dead.

Hopefully a future update will change the logistics and add a consistent, basic storage facility for normal resources and get rid of the collector/distributor setup.

I will say upfront that the game isn't TERRIBLE or completely unenjoyable, just exceptionally mediocre as far as a game like this goes. It is probably a bottom 10 or even bottom 5 short incremental game. For this mediocrity the game is overpriced too, probably being more in line with 2 dollars instead of 5. The comparison between this game and Astro Prospector, both in the same bundle and pricerange, is a night and day difference. Astro Prospector blows it out of the water in just about every metric.

Starting with the main flaw of this game, its uncreative and extremely linear skill tree. As others will rightfully point out, this is the most restrictive skill tree you will find in the genre, it is so linear that it often feels like it is a skill tree in name only. Progression in the skill tree is effectively gated behind a currency only dropped by bosses. These bosses are tough enough that you generally have to buy most, if not all of the basic stat upgrades in order to beat them. 

And this leads to the other half of the skill tree issue; its just basic upgrades. Every level of the skill tree comes with a damage upgrade and a life upgrade, usually a virus spawnrate upgrade too. As the levels go up the upgrade variety decreases as well. Attack speed was given out too early, and maxes out quickly, but what I think really exemplifies the lack of thought and care with the gameplay is how armor upgrades just completely disappear after the early game. The game almost never goes beyond the absolute basics. There are critrate and double resource drop upgrades that max out at 35%, a better game would have had them max out at 100% and worked that into the progression (no unique synergy with either critrate or resource collection either) . There are no lifesteal upgrades at all, bare minimum quality of life, even most of the upgrades that require the boss currency are very basic.

The game also has very subpar ability progression. You unlock the minigun almost instantly, but it is effectively the only permanent weapon you unlock until the last few levels at the end of the game. For a strange reason the game keeps on trying to push temporary (5 seconds at best) powerups as your main form of damage progression beyond the basic stat increases. These powerups are not super reliable, and not as satisfying as a dedicated weapon unlock. In particular the game keeps trying to push the "Shock" powerup on you, which sucks as a powerup when you get it and will never get better. You would think that this would become a basic weapon later on, but it doesn't. 

The gameplay is also very basic with no redeeming qualities. The normal red viruses don't do any contact damage or have any unique features. Occasionally a chasing suicide virus will spawn, which is probably the highlight of gameplay. It is reasonably fun to get the hang of dodging it since it moves quite quickly. The green viruses on the other hand are just annoying. They have significantly more health than standard viruses and charge you VERY quickly at close range. The problem is that all your weapons are close range, so you are forced to get close. If they manage to hit you, not only do they deal damage but they also don't drop their special resource. This is particularly annoying early on when you first unlock them and don't know what they are capable of yet. The other enemies are no better. Boss is effectively just a big red virus, white virus is just a rare red virus, blue virus shoots basic and annoying screenwide lasers... 

The only area of the game it does a decent job in is with the music and visual design, both of which are more than adequate for the standards of short incrementals. The pixelated CRT artstyle is used so often for good reason, although it certainly isn't helping this game beat the "bland and uncreative" allegations. 

Overall, this is certainly a short incremental game of all time. If you just wanna relax for a couple hours and not have to think deeply about anything, it might fit the bill. Otherwise, definitely look elsewhere for your incremental fix. There are enough of them out there these days that it will take quite a while before you run out of games better than this one. This review has been a bit harsh on it when it is still just "mid" but the standards of the genre have long outpaced games of subpar quality like this.

Ultimately, I will say that Shadowed does a wonderful job being a traditional roguelike with stealth elements.

A quick summary of pros and cons

Pros
- A balance of stealth and combat that doesn't overshadow each other
- Classes have diverse playstyles
- Classes play very different from each other, the only two classes that really have overlap is shinobi and iga, and even then they're pretty different
- Information being cleanly displayed, you won't need a wiki for this game comparing to other roguelikes
- Fast combat (in terms of turn count) and tactical combat that doesn't feel cheap when you die. If it feels cheap, that's because you didn't read what the enemies do
- Diverse enemies with diverse strengths and weaknesses
- May not be relevant when you're reading this review, but while this game had support, the dev has listened greatly to community feedback


Neutral
- Classes aren't balanced comparing to other classes, a class might excel at the same while another might fail
- Fatigue system. You have to be careful on how you explore levels and how you use your stronger attacks, because everything, that isn't sitting still doing nothing, makes you tired.
- Thresholds. Perks require you to have certain a certain amount of a stat, and the perks are more impactful then the stats. So this typically makes you focus on getting stats to a certain threshold to get perks, and also strength for carry weight.


Cons
- Each class mostly focuses on one playstyle, diversity exists in the classes but the other playstyles are typically noticeably weaker
- It's a trad roguelike, if you aren't aware of what a trad roguelike is, this is your warning
- Requires reading, certain enemies have 100% armor, 200% dodge, inflict you with a status that makes you unable to attack them
- Game was made by a solo dev, he tried his best but there are bugs/glitches/oversights you'll have to expect from a game made by a solo dev

Characters: 9/10 The MC changes a lot throughout the course of the story, a growth that felt natural and made me smile. Each of the characters she came to trust were well written and fun. I think this was a very well written cast that felt natural in the world of the game.

Story: 8/10 This is a story focused game, and while not everything flowed perfectly I found myself hooked from start to finish. My reasons for caring grew alongside the MC's reasons for caring and this is one of the rare games that has ending gameplay after the final boss instead of just an abrupt end. The story was unique and thought provoking, but also well written and fun, and it's clear the devs knew the world very well.

Combat: 7/10 Okay, this one is a difficult rating. On the one hand, stealth is one of my favorite combat elements in games, though it quickly devolves into I've been spotted and now need to fight. And combat was sorely lacking in the beginning, all the way up to just past the first boss fight. Gradually, as the game progresses, more tools are added to your arsenal that made combat outside of stealth incredible, an absolute must in a game that only allowed stealth combat about 50% of the time and otherwise forces you into physical combat. Once I gained all potential fighting abilities, I no longer cared if stealth broke because of how much I could do to get back into stealth or to use powers to beat up a whole camp of enemies and feel awesome (except for when I didn't). Combat feels incredible UNLESS you're fighting a boss. Inevitably, the bosses have varying degrees of abilities that nullify yours, which makes it a very difficult battle of attrition in which they do more damage and have far more attacks.

World: 7/10 This is a linear game, which may turn some people off, but it suited me. I was just along for the ride. And the world is stunning and well designed. I felt like each area was beautiful and unique. Sometimes traversal wasn't obvious (always took me a few tries to recognize when there was a thin ledge to creep along to get to the next area), but I found it well balanced with other aspects of gameplay.

This game initially received a bad reputation for being an unpolished AAA game, but it's actually an AA game published by an AAA studio. There are areas that aren't wholly polished, but I had a lot of fun and would definitely recommend.

有些评论提到“老一套”，这些确实是经典议题，但游戏的表达我认为是中立的。例如，关于药物阴谋的指控，“我”是无法独立查证的，只能做出有限的选择（可能通过多周目可以验证），这些黑衣人有无可能是外国特工？在游戏里“我”是无法判断的；是国有医保还是私有化医疗？显然对不同阶层影响是迥异的，而在特定时期一国的总资源必然是有限的，感兴趣的可以了解最近的医改；是全球化可能低价但冲击本土产业？还是本土保护主义但国民无法买到便宜的商品?如果20年前这个问题还不太清晰，那这几年应该会更有体会。再包括国家统治方式的情况，事实上“我”所能做的只是是否支持现总理沃尔夫，但沃尔夫下台就会民主化吗？还是会更加政治混乱，抑或是迎来下一个强人？这是没有被揭示的。
但人总要做出选择，也总会做出选择，当然这么个小小主编能做出影响如此巨大的选择，大概是另一个世界

If you're looking for a difficult Roguelike experience then EX mode is the way to go, it has all the classic hallmarks like choices and rewards after each stage. Story mode has rogue elements too and comes with permanent upgrades between runs, secret dungeons and crafting. The only downside to the story is that it is short but it does come with seemingly infinite NG+.

The gameplay is a little similar to Neon Abyss and at first I felt a lot of the items were derivatives from each other... And they are, BUT, once I got near the end of the game the highest tier of weapons and abilities get wild. I believe the derivation comes from the progression system. It's ALL items and weapons. You get a small amount of stats from your upgrades and then the rest is through items. Some of the crazier builds I've managed includes spamming ungodly amounts of projectiles and permanent invincibility.

EX Mode changes the rules a bit and is why I'm re-writing my review... It's an absolute banger. For context when you synthesize items in story you're simply re-rolling them for an item of equal or greater rarity. In EX Mode you're mixing stats and effects together. If you have a sword and find a grenade, instead of equipping your grenade in your usable item slot you can synth it with the sword and it will throw grenades on hit while freeing up the item slot for something else. So yes, if you find a nuke and have an SMG... You get the picture.

All in all a solid roguelike. The credits at the end of the game is one of the shortest I've ever seen, if you like investing into indie devs I think these guys deserve a purchase. The code was thought out ahead of time to allow a dynamic weapon and effect system which is something I really appreciate. There's also workshop/mod support and cheats available from the start for those who struggle with roguelites.

very very fun. but if you play it you will become insufferable to everyone around you because you will be constantly thinking of new words you can use in the game and shouting them out at inappropriate times.

This game lacks actual substance. It's fun for a bit if you like words, but drops off if you want anything more than words. The actual items and pickups all feel extremely low-impact. There are so many "upgrades" that say something like "Gives 1 bonus point every play, increases by 1 every time you use like 5 vowels in a single word" or something. It's just not interesting at all.

This lackluster set of items forces you to continue using longer and longer words as you move up in difficulty. The items that are supposed to shape the run end up enforcing constraints, but even when I find myself playing to these constraints, I find myself bored of looking through my limited lexicon for any possible words I could play. Often, nothing comes to me (you try finding a word that has more vowels than consonants and ends in a "D" that is longer than 6 letters, with no "E" in it... Yeah, just kinda screwed).

This sort of thing would be fine if that were a one-off run, where other runs were spent dialing into builds and playing to the strengths of your letter bag or perks, but it's almost every single run where every reward screen you get 3 boring options which will do absolutely nothing to help you on the harder levels. The problem is that on a normal length run, you only get like 10-14 rewards screens. If you sell them, you get "refreshes," which barely help if you're going for any sort of letter-bag build (as you may end up refreshing away a key special letter). There's no counterplay for the limited rewards options. That is, I can't sell a perk for a different perk later on. Once I sell it, it's gone (into refreshes). Therefore, you either get extremely lucky with a good perk choice at some point in the run, or your run just grinds to a halt at the higher levels, with absolutely nothing you can do about it.

Other roguelikes are fun, in my opinion, because the randomness throws you into a unique run every time. Issues that come up and screw your build can be played around, and you can always counterplay the randomness in some way. This game is not like that. If you strike out early, you'll almost certainly fail the run. And that's just not fun. This could be resolved by putting more diverse and powerful items into the game. More specialized, but more impactful. For example: one of the best items I've gotten was a "x2 word score for dot tiles, increases by 0.2 for every dot tile successfully played." -- insanely good if you're running dot tiles. However, for the rest of the entire run, I never got another dot tile related item. Just stupid bonus point items, or some variation of "replace 1 letter with a consonant" active item. If there were more of these specialized items, you'd have the ability to pair them together in interesting and unique ways, or if there were some way to obtain more chances at perks, or some way to pivot your build later on, there would be less of a chance you simply get unavoidably screwed on the later levels.

If you're good at coming up with words, and you're looking for a game where you do nothing but come up with words given increasingly difficult constraints, this could be for you. Personally, though, I was hoping for that PLUS an interesting "build-driven" roguelike, and I unfortunately did not find that here.

По первому впечатлению, при просмотре на ютюбе, игра казалось казуальной и простой. В одном порту требуется зерно, в другом оно производится, привези и получи прибыль на пустом месте. Потом открой 2-ой лвл порта и тебе доступен новый товар.
 Но на деле, при кажущей сначала простоте, игра не так проста, как могло бы показаться. Существует 3 типа ресурсов: 
1) Требуемых порту (читай городу); 2) Требуемых производству для переработки в другой ресурс (не все производство требует ресурс, но большинство все же требует); 3) Ресурсы на продажу, которые производит город (а следовательно их нужно вывести из порта).
 Чем выше уровень порта, тем больше нужно на вход ресурсов, но и тем больше произведенных ресурсов. Казалось бы тоже все просто, но маршруты поставки разной длины, производство производит в разном объеме, город и производство требуют ресурсы все больше и больше по мере роста  и все более новых. Чтобы прокачать порт который основной для нас по сценарию, нужно арендовать и прокачивать другие порты. Кроме того в игре случаются события, которые могут осложнить выполнение целей сценария (забастовка докеров, эмбарго на экспорт товара и т.д.), а так же события могут вам повысить заработок (Олимпийские игры, субсидия города или государства и т.д.). Часть событий в сценариях заскриптована, часть случайные. Помимо всего прочего вы исследуете и строите все более мощные и экономичные суда разных типов, боретесь на аукционе за право купить какое-то производство, соперничаете с ИИ компаниями за долю в рынке. Боюсь все описывать очень долго.
 Резюме: Играть интересно, игрок постоянно вовлечен в процесс создания новых маршрутов, удовлетворения портов, выполнения испытаний. Скучать на х3 перемотке придется лишь в самом начале, когда у вас мало денег, вы создали маршруты, построили суда и поставили на маршруты и у вас денег нет, ждете прибыли. Но это не долго, потом времени на х3 нет, разве что в эндгейме придется мотать время при ожидании постройки судна (узнал об этом переведя китайские комментарии под новостью о игре).
 Рекомендую, игра захватывает!

Indie game studios continue to be the real heroes of the games industry, producing all the really enjoyable games at a fraction of the price of AAA. Deck of Haunts is a great example. It's simple enough of a core concept to understand, and gets elaborate enough that you have to think about what you want to do as the game progresses. 

If I had any complaints, I find the names in the intruder's little avatars too small to read well, but that doesn't really matter much in the game. The other thing is challenge, in that the game feels a little too easy at times, but that's fixed with the community made scenarios being a thing now.

Overall, it's an excellent deck-building/puzzle horror game with a cool premise and great design, and I highly recommend it to anyone who likes the genre or the setting.

Gato Roboto é aquele tipo de jogo que conquista logo de cara pela sua simplicidade e charme. Um metroidvania em preto e branco, com uma pegada retrô e um humor leve, ele coloca você no controle de um gato  sim, um gato!  dentro de uma armadura robótica, explorando um planeta misterioso.

A gameplay é rápida, responsiva e muito divertida. Tudo é bem dosado: as áreas são pequenas o suficiente pra não cansar, mas cheias de segredos que recompensam a curiosidade. A trilha sonora é ótima e combina perfeitamente com o clima de exploração e descoberta.

A história é simples, mas cheia de personalidade, com diálogos engraçados e um tom descontraído que deixa a jornada leve do começo ao fim. É um jogo curto, direto ao ponto e incrivelmente satisfatório daqueles que você termina com um sorriso no rosto.

No fim, Gato Roboto mostra que não é preciso muito pra ser memorável: basta uma boa ideia, uma execução bem feita e, claro, um gato pilotando um robô.

[h1] Обрубок потенциально великой игры [/h1] [i] и вот почему:[/i]

[h3]Первые часы это ад для новичка[/h3]
Первые часы Tyranny - самые душные. Пока начинаешь понимать, кто есть кто, как работает мир, и что вообще от тебя хочет игра, хочется просто дропнуть.
Именно из-за этого я не мог осилить её несколько лет назад. Но главное потерпеть и вникнуть. Дальше становится значительно лучше, и постепенно игра раскрывает свои сильные стороны.

[h3]Система репутации - гениальная идея, реализованная явно не так как надо[/h3]
Система репутации сначала кажется глубокой: ты можешь накапливать страх и уважение у каждой фракции, получая разные бонусы и реакции.
Но чем дальше, тем сильнее понимаешь - она обманывает.
Ты можешь прокачать и дружбу, и страх одновременно, и никто этому не удивится. Хотя казалось бы, это взаимоисключающие факты цельного представления о твоем персонаже.
Никаких реальных последствий до самого конца нет — всё влияние репутации проявляется только в последнем часу игры, когда начинается выбор концовки, в зависимости от выбраных действий и наличия той или иной репы.
Геймплейно это работает странно: игра дает тебе перки, но наказывает только финалом.
В итоге весь смысл системы растворяется, и чувствуешь, будто зря вникал в её механику.

[h3]Компаньоны - крепкие, но без откровений[/h3]
Спутники здесь стандартные для Obsidian: каждый представляет свою фракцию, комментирует происходящее, иногда встревает в диалоги.
Химия между ними есть, но не сказать, что она яркая.
С другой стороны, их характеры и идеология хорошо вписываются в сеттинг, а некоторые личные квесты действительно интересны. Просто хочется больше и персонажей, и личных линий.

[h3]Разнообразие[/h3]
Главное разнообразие Tyranny кроется в выборе стороны, за кого ты будешь топить.
Большая часть игры строится вокруг этого, и под конец действительно появляются разные пути. Но по факту — этого преступно мало. Все сводиться к тому с кем ты будешь в конце 1 акта или попробуешь свергнуть весь режим.
Я пытался отыгрывать дипломата, который ищет мир и порядок, старается примирить враждующие фракции.
Но игра на это плевала с высокой башни — все дороги ведут к поножовщине.
Как бы ты ни выкручивался, почти каждый диалог заканчивается битвой, будто сценаристы просто не предусмотрели, что кто-то может быть разумным.
После нескольких попыток я перестал искать «мирные исходы» и просто вступал в бой — зачем тратить время, если результат всё равно один?

[h3]Заскриптованность и отсутствие гибкости[/h3]
Tyranny не позволяет нам быть настоящим манипулятором.
Хочешь сыграть в словоблуда - уговорить одну сторону, потом прийти к другой и договориться о новом раскладе?
Забудь. Если квест не предусмотрел такой вариант - игра автоматически всё знает и сразу делает другую фракцию враждебной.
Для изометрической RPG это выглядит максимально странно.
В других проектах жанра такие трюки были нормой (вспомнить хотя бы Arcanum или Fallout 2).
Здесь же всё заскриптовано, всё по рельсам.
Свобода игрока - иллюзия.

[h3]Но за что игру всё-таки можно уважать[/h3]
• Крутой лор и диалоги.
• Концепция мира, где зло уже победило, и ты часть этой новой власти, подана гениально.
• Магическая система одно из лучших, что Obsidian когда-либо писали.
• Вариативность концовок.
Она действительно есть. Не столько в сюжете, сколько в контексте и идеологии твоих решений.
Концовка зависит от того, как ты трактовал власть и порядок — это редкость для жанра.

[h3]Где игра сломалась[/h3]
Tyranny ощущается как демо-версия великого проекта, которому просто не хватило бюджета и времени.
Из этого вытекают все проблемы:
• мало спутников (всего пара по-настоящему интересных);
• мало необязательных боссов и локаций;
• почти нет побочных квестов;
• слабые анимации (иногда персонажи просто «телепортируются» вместо движений);
• и главное - ощущение, что всё закончилось слишком рано.
После прохождения я читал статьи о разработке — Obsidian вынашивали идею Tyranny десятилетие.
И в этом свете особенно больно: потенциал огромный, идея — редкая, но результат получился недосказанным.
Как будто перед тобой черновик шедевра.

[h3]Немного о вдохновении[/h3]
Забавно, но я буквально в этом году прочитал цикл Глена Кука «Хроники Черного Отряда».
И теперь уверен - Obsidian отлично уловили ту самую атмосферу, где зло не разрушает мир, а пытается установить порядок через страх и железо.
Tyranny чувствуется духовным продолжением этих книг - только без второго тома.

[h3]Итог[/h3]
Tyranny - это великолепная идея, застрявшая в черновике.
Игра, которая могла стать новым словом в жанре RPG, но осталась эскизом, наброском того, что могло бы быть.
Тем не менее - рекомендую.
Потому что даже в усечённом виде это уникальный опыт, который дарит редкое чувство власти и моральной серости.
Просто будь готов к тому, что история оборвётся на полуслове.

P5S's novelty as both a genre-swap and a post-credits reunion of the original game's characters makes it difficult to ignore after having really enjoyed P5. Sadly, P5S fails to deliver a captivating story or sustainable gameplay. Having a one-hundred-hour-RPG's worth of prior gameplay, narrative context, and character growth by which to judge a canon spin-off means that discrepancies in the quality of the writing, voice acting, and animation are going to stand out even more. 

Story-wise, things are pretty rough. These villains aren't nearly as intricate and the new friends don't offer much emotional depth. There's no meaningful conflict for any of the main cast since they've all had their toughest problems solved already in P5, so very little of interest occurs with them. Having fully-voiced characters is always appreciated, but the from-home pandemic voice acting is rather noticeable with there being inconsistent mic quality between characters. Dialogue sequences take up large portions of P5S's runtime and a majority of them accomplish very little and are simply archetypal banter.

Translating Persona 5's iconic UI and turn-based battle mechanics into an action game is done cleverly and with ample respect for the source material. The Dynasty Warriors gameplay has its highlights and flows well, but it never gets any deeper as the game advances. That unchanging foundation is far from enough to sustain a game of this length. Every main character is playable right out of the gate, which is slightly overwhelming and a tad lazy since no one gets any sort of spotlight and everyone gets a few pop-up text boxes as their only tutorials. Staggering their introductions would’ve supplied some sense of mechanical progression to a rather stagnating experience.

It's not an entirely bad time. For one thing, the music is top-notch. Maybe if each dungeon didn’t share the same structure or somehow contained unique gameplay situations/objectives it'd feel like there's more of a reason to keep playing to see what’s next. P5S is something I've been chipping away at for months and I never felt invested enough to play it for more than tiny chunks. Because of that, I'm not particularly keen on recommending the game, even to those who might be similarly enticed by the premise of more adventures with the Phantom Thieves.

Soy una apasionada de los city builders desde que tengo uso de razón. Llevo años buscando un buen sustituto de mis favoritos (Pharaoh y Zeus), y este la verdad que se ha acercado bastante. Los gráficos están bien y, aunque me gustaría que fuesen de un poco mejor calidad y más llamativos, entiendo que han basado su estética en hacerlo lo más fiel posible a la verdad, dentro de lo que cabe. La jugabilidad está bastante bien: un puntazo eso de que aparezcan los dioses en el mapa como en Zeus (¡lo echaba mucho de menos!), el tema organización/distribución bastante acertado también y la variedad de objetos, recursos, etc, magnífica. Sin embargo, cojea aún en ciertas cosas: 
1- Ya desde las primeras misiones avanzas muy rápido de nivel y la verdad que la magia va perdiendo sentido a medida que avanzas, siempre es lo mismo.
2- Desde las primeras misiones también desbloqueas casi todas las mercancías, todos los dioses... por lo que al final pasa como en el punto uno: siempre es lo mismo y acaba aburriendo. No hay novedad, no hay una escala y nuevas cosas de una misión a otra.
3- La dificultad del juego se basa especialmente en lo difícil que es conseguir que suba la población. De lo cual explican bastante poco o nada (añado que les envié un mail porque llegó a parecerme un bug o algo porque no era normal lo que costaba y no me contestaron nunca, mal también), y hace que la mecánica del juego sea bastante simple. Hay que lograr conseguir un equilibro entre población-empleos y entre gastos-ingresos.
4- El tema de los Dioses está bien pero falta más interacción. El botón que hay para visitar el olimpo no sirve para nada. Los dioses no hablan nunca, no puedes pedirles favores o algo así. Eso sería un añadido.

Podría seguir pero bueno, ahí van unos cuantos puntos fuertes. En resumen: el juego está bastante bien y con unas mejoras podría ser fantástico pero, en mi opinión, se queda bastante corto. Me quedaban dos misiones para terminar la campaña principal y pasar a los DLCs pero la monotonía y la poca novedad (en su mayoría) han hecho que me acabe aburriendo. Ojalá hagan algunas actualizaciones que mejoren la cosa porque no me importaría volver, el juego tiene potencial, le falta un pulido.

Variations of the animal's coats, maybe even rare coats.
The ground being paintable so you could have some variation in the appearance of forests and plains

Do you hate fun? Do you hate knowing what to do in games? Do you want to waste hours upon hours looking for needles in haystacks? Do you hate quest logs? Then get ready to question your life choices in Skopje 83. You are a person in a place at a time, (The game hardly explains anything, why should I?) and something is happening. The literal only objective you are given in game is to destroy the towers and save the city; the real objective of the game seems to involve some kind of sphere you get pieces of by killing the bosses with secret quests.

The entire game is basically just a bunch of hidden content. All of the guns are hidden behind bizarre puzzles, the bosses as well as their secret quests are entirely secret, and you never quite feel like you know what is going on. As far as I can tell the game only spoonfeeds you one weapon, and that's the one you get for clearing all of the towers the first time. Otherwise you can potentially be running around for entire days playing this game and never find a single weapon! 

For example, you have to tamper with boilers in order to kill the first boss. The game fails to explain how this works, does not reveal that the handles can be rotated left/right, and the needle on the pressure gauge only moves once the puzzle is completed. Your only hint that you get is that you have to listen to the boiler, when knowing the very freaking basics of how the "puzzle" worked would of helped. 

The quest to enter the second bosses area is even worse! You have to drive from temple to temple starving yourself and filling the donation boxes, using a special hammer to fight infinitely spawning enemies. If you screw this up, you have to start all over again. I want to punch whoever came up with this in the nose. 

The heavy shotgun is even freaking worse. To get the shotgun you have to find a single specific police station in the game world, pick up the key there, find the bunker it opens nearby, find a whiteboard there with locations, and then traverse a junkyard maze at night while timed in order to pick up phones to get the numbers you need. Or if you are anybody not playing the game on release, you enter 2580 to get the shotgun because that puzzle is beyond stupid and pointless. 

Map design is your typical open world copy/paste garbage where you can run in a direction for minutes without finding anything. The majority of loot is hidden in apartment buildings, the rest of the game world is pretty much barren and empty. Ironically, hidden among this barren world are blueprints, items, and puzzles. Because the map is a real city that has been re-made in a video game, it's not very hard to get around so that's nice. 

The looter/shooter aspect of the game is bad. Loot can only be reliably gained in apartments. Enemies never drop any items of any type. There are blueprints and special items all over the map, but only singular copies of them. So you can spend entire weeks playing this game and never be able to find the blueprints you need because there's only one single hidden copy of it in the game world. 

This is Macedonian Redfall. There's pretty much no content besides the quests, and the quests are all super hidden/obscure. You spend hours upon hours looking for needles in a haystack because it will make you play the game longer; 99% of the runtime of this game is the time spent figuring out what you have to to before the game allows you to progress.

A somewhat niche genre of games I call "make your own ugly contraption game", using the game's system of simple pulleys, pretty much allowing you to transfer the momentum to create anything with wheels or rotation, such as cars, catapults, forklifts, detachable objects, and all kind of other abominations. It reminds me a little of the Gish's level editor, it feels closer to a creative tool than a video game. Dude, is that a Walker in the trailer, looks a little complicated, no?

It's a hard game lol, may look simple, but even making a line with 2 wheels is not as easy as it looks, let alone have things that detach and grab objects while you move around, it's actually a physics game with a lot of trial and error, you need to know how to create your own fun here, otherwise I think you may find it pretty frustrating. You can technically skip any level, but what is the point of buying the game then if you not gona play it, with that said, I wish the game was more rewarding for solving those hard stages, perhaps more achievements or at least better visual progression, the game sadly looks the same the entire way.

You can attach various behaviors to the objects which sort of allows you to make transformers, like you could make a car with a detachable hook, emphasis on you "could make", not saying you will be able to. There is definitely a bit of a learning curve to it, don't expect things to work as you expect them to.

[h1] Pros: [/h1]

(+) It's a game that does a good job allowing you to express your creativity to solve puzzles in unique ways, however, I don't think it's an easy game to pick up, and it's more for people that can create their own fun, I think.

(+) I think you did a good job creating unique challenges, I kind of like that game is not going easy on you, you actually have to brainstorm some of the puzzles, potentially for multiple hours.

[h1] Feedback: [/h1]

For the jumping momentum, try to give the player more mid-air control, you made the momentum conservation a bit too heavy.

It's a good idea to give the game some visual progression, while I like the puzzles, it's not very satisfying if the entire game looks the same and you don't feel rewarded moving forward. I personally would have preferred an achievement for each stage after tutorial, just because so many of them are hard and don't reward you for putting in the time.

[b] Overall Thoughts: 7/10 [/b]

I think it's an awesome puzzle game for the right person. I use to love game editors like the one that came with the GISH, it's very much a physics tool that allows you to create basic machines, and it's not an easy game you can pick up and expect fast results. Like I said, you have to make your own fun with it, it's a game for creative people, not so much a chill puzzle game for the average player. A gioco, praticamente finito e quasi platinato, salvo futuri aggiornamenti, posso dire che ho apprezzato molto la veste grafica, sia degli oggetti che degli npc. Belli anche gli effetti in cielo nel passaggio dal mattino al tardo pomeriggio, con la formazione e dissolvimento costante delle nuvole che simula il movimento del vento ed il movimento stesso del sole che segue il passare delle ore.
Dal punto di vista ludico è un gioco molto rilassante che non presenta alcun tipo di sfida nella gestione delle finanze, in quanto fin dall'inizio ti permette di guadagnare quanto basta per progredire in modo costante e regolare, ma che proprio per questo risulta appagante e mai frustrante o lento.
Molto carina l'idea dei "gingilli", oggetti estetici ma che fungono anche e soprattutto da power up. Una volta sbloccati in game apportano sostanziali migliorie al gioco come ad esempio la velocità di movimento tua e degli npc.
Piccole migliorie che si potrebbero implementare sono legate alla produzione nelle serre, che se sfruttata interamente per gli spazi che offre risulta di molto eccedente rispetto a quanto viene effettivamente acquistato dai clienti, portando in breve tempo al caos in quanto i giardinieri depositano a terra una quantità tale di frutta e verdura che non trova assolutamente posto per gli spazi offerti dal magazzino, decisamente troppo piccolo anche una volta raggiunta la sua massima espansione. 
Anche se è possibile smaltire tutto in una speciale cassetta che ti offre il 90% del valore della merce, anch'essa sbloccabile tra i gingilli, la meccanica di dover portare una quantità enorme di cassette avanti e indietro verso di essa alla lunga può stufare.
Aggiungerei quindi nelle opzioni la possibilità di farlo fare di default direttamente agli npc.

Alla voce bug, a parte quello di finire raramente bloccati (ma già risolto tramite menù di gioco) ho da segnalare solo quello relativo al carrello porta casse, che spesso, se richiamato tramite il tablet, perde il contatto col terreno e non permette di raccogliere o depositare correttamente le casse o se stesso dove si vuole.
A volte per risolvere il problema e ripristinarlo è necessario concludere la giornata in game.

In generale, viste le tante ore di relax che mi ha regalato mi sento di consigliare assolutamente questo gioco a tutti gli amanti del genere. Voto: 8/10

This game is an open-story sandbox MMO RPG, so the "fun factor" lies more in the social and political aspects of the game than in the actual game play. Still, there are some in-game tasks that require proper planning, quick thinking and excellent dexterity. The main goal of the game is to help your Corporation become the most powerful in the game by aligning itself with up to 7 additional corporations.

There is also the daily Hardcore XP contest where you are always at the edge of your seat, knowing that the next sector could be stacked with hostile players from enemy alliances. Die once and lose everything. Climb to the top of the leaderboard and earn spiffy high-level gear, all in a day's work!

Getting started can be tedious, but outgoing social players will enjoy the camaraderie. The best groups will join up with new players and help them explore the map. The deeper you get in the game, the more possibilities that are open to you. Players can switch "classes" quickly by equipping different sets of gear to handle the task at hand. There is no getting stuck as a particular class of character only to realize that you want a different gameplay experience.

Red Matter is an OK game. 

For the asking price of 25 bucks, I don't believe it is worth it. Buy on sale. 
I took my time going through the game and only got 3.6h out of it, and I even got all the achievements. 

That being said, let's shift the analysis from quantity to quality. Was that 3.6h good? I would say "yes with some caveats". 
The story is pretty good. It could have done with some more fleshing out, but it was good. 
The voice acting and writing was very well done, and so was the sound design. The game play mechanics  are generally good - even if I have to admit, that the control system could have been done much better. 

Basically, your left hand has 4 tools attached to it, of which one is: "Show mission objective" - *Thumb Stick button*.
For the sake of brevity, this is the last I will say of that.  

The other tools are: A translator, a grabber and a torch. Most of the game you are constantly having to switch between these, each time having the transition take a second or two. You press A or B to cycle through them and if you do it too fast and skip the right one, or go the wrong direction, you spend a good bit of time just getting to the right tool. It get's old REAL fast. 

I'm not saying that if it was done better, that I could have probably finished the game in 2h sans achievements. 
I'm not saying that. I really am not. 
I am just *heavily* implying that. 

Here is what I believe would have worked better:
Button A: "Action A" (Example -  Translate)
Button B: "Action B" (Example - Torch)
Trigger: "Action C" (Example - Grabber)

Petit Game Collection vol.1, developed and published by WSS Playground, is a charming and eccentric anthology that distills the whimsical spirit of the Needy Streamer Overload universe into a bite-sized package. Rather than a traditional sequel or expansion, it serves as a companion piece—a lighthearted celebration of the game’s world, characters, and aesthetics. Comprised of three small, self-contained mini-games and an additional commentary room, the collection feels like an experimental arcade cabinet meant for fans to revisit familiar faces in new, nostalgic forms. It’s a curious mixture of parody, homage, and fan service, and while its scope is undeniably limited, it embraces that limitation with confidence and humor.

Each mini-game included in Petit Game Collection vol.1 offers a distinct genre homage. The first, Ame’s Happy Happy Dating Game, is a tongue-in-cheek visual novel inspired by classic romantic simulators of the 1990s. It presents players with colorful, pixelated artwork and branching choices, channeling the exaggerated melodrama and charm of retro dating sims. It’s deliberately simple and self-aware, poking fun at genre tropes while giving fans of Needy Streamer Overload’s protagonist a chance to interact with her in a completely different tone. The second, Don’t Die, Kangel!, takes a completely different approach—a frantic shoot-’em-up that plays like a cross between old-school arcade space shooters and modern bullet-hell challenges. Players guide Kangel through waves of enemies in a convention hall setting, firing continuously while dodging chaotic patterns of projectiles. It’s intense, fast-paced, and infused with the same eccentric energy that defined the original game’s stream segments. The third, Break Out Kangel, is a reinterpretation of the classic block-breaking formula, simple but satisfying, though only available in Japanese—a small but noticeable barrier for some players.

Together, these games form a playful mosaic of nostalgia. The art direction across all of them leans heavily into retro aesthetics—pixel art, chunky sprites, and vivid color palettes reminiscent of late ’90s arcade machines or handheld consoles. Each title has its own flavor while remaining tied together through consistent character design and humor. The soundtrack complements this perfectly, offering catchy loops that mirror the chip-tune charm of classic video games. The result is a collection that feels like a digital time capsule, reimagining Kangel’s chaotic persona within the framework of genres that once defined gaming’s formative decades. It’s less about challenge or innovation and more about celebrating the medium’s roots while maintaining the self-aware irony that defines WSS Playground’s creative voice.

The most distinctive element of the package, however, may be the “Kangel’s Room” feature—a bonus area that functions as a commentary space for developers and staff. This segment breaks the fourth wall, offering fans a glimpse behind the curtain of how the mini-games came to be and why they were designed in such a specific, nostalgic style. It adds an intimate quality to the collection, as though the developers are inviting the player into their creative process. For those invested in WSS Playground’s eccentric approach to storytelling, this inclusion adds depth to what could otherwise be seen as a novelty product. It reinforces the collection’s role not as a full-fledged game, but as a reflection of creative affection for both retro gaming and the Needy Streamer universe.

That said, Petit Game Collection vol.1 is a niche project, and it shows. Each of the mini-games can be completed in minutes, and while the variety is refreshing, the simplicity may leave some players wanting more. There’s little in the way of mechanical depth or replayability; the focus is entirely on presentation and nostalgia rather than longevity. The limited localization—especially the fact that Break Out Kangel is only available in Japanese—further narrows its accessibility. The experience works best as a short, self-contained piece of fan content rather than a standalone product, and players unfamiliar with Needy Streamer Overload may struggle to connect with its tone or references. It’s a title designed primarily for those who already understand and appreciate its source material.

Despite its brevity, there’s an undeniable charm in Petit Game Collection vol.1’s sincerity. It captures the carefree joy of small-scale creative projects that don’t try to overextend themselves. It’s a love letter to retro gaming, to the quirky nature of internet fandom, and to the cult success of Needy Streamer Overload itself. The care in the art, the energy in the music, and the humor woven through each mini-game show that this was made not to impress through scope, but to delight through personality. For fans, it’s a warm reunion with a familiar character in a collection that feels handcrafted and intimate. For newcomers, it’s an odd but endearing curiosity—a peek into the eccentric sensibilities of WSS Playground.

In the end, Petit Game Collection vol.1 is less a traditional game and more a creative side project dressed as one. It’s brief, self-contained, and unapologetically specific in its appeal, but that focus gives it a sense of authenticity. It evokes the feeling of flipping through a forgotten cartridge collection, rediscovering the weird and wonderful experiments of another era. While it may not offer much depth or longevity, it succeeds on its own modest terms: a short, nostalgic, and lovingly crafted diversion for those who want to spend a little more time in the chaotic, charming world of Kangel.

There's a lot to like here, but perhaps what I want to commend most is that you can quit the game at any time and your run will be saved to pick up exactly where you left off. This is a feature missing in too many roguelikes, and makes Into the Grid a game I'm much more likely to pick up for quick sessions.

On a more substantial note, the theme is strong here. The cyberpunk netrunner aesthetic is baked into every system and mechanic, the flavor could not be more on point. The 2D card art is striking, and the 3D combat models look great. The enemy designs are all very slick. The visual and sound effects of attacks and blocks could use a little more flair and oomph to really increase the impact, but this a minor nitpick. The soundtrack is pretty chill so far, perhaps a little too chill in the early stages. I haven't gotten too deep into the game yet, so perhaps there's more excitement ahead. I hope we get some real pulse-pounders further in.

In terms of gameplay, the Trace mechanic that gradually increases the difficulty is very neat. It creates a really compelling sense of tension, and makes you really think about how much you want to explore, versus gunning for the end. The environments can be a little labyrinthine, making it hard to find the right path even if you're looking for it, so I hope we see some improvements in navigation. Some more ways to know what lies ahead and map out a layer would be appreciated.

I've only just scratched the surface of the card and driver options, but already I feel like I have plenty of playstyles to choose from, with more opening up as I keep playing. I'm looking forward to experimenting more as I go.

A very strong start for an Early Access title, and I'm excited to see it expand even further!

Finished the game in around 80 hours, great gem among factory games, with its own unique flavor and design approach in the genre.

Pros:
-Interesting and robust horizontal progression instead of very long and deep research trees
-Rebuilding 6 times across 6 elemental planes might sound repetitive but it comes with 1 elemental restrictions and new tools (element) that would give you an incentive to design a bit differently instead of redoing the same thing over and over
-Spells that are well within the design aesthetics, yet still practical for factory expansion purposes
-Hexagons for a change instead of the usual squares for the top-down factory genre
-Great pacing with introduction to new (and progressively powerful) tools

Cons:
-FPS issues as more stuff are placed down, looking forward to optimizations when the full release hits
-UI could still use a bit of polishing

Looking forward to the full release, definitely would go for another round.

Here are the things I love about this game
1) Visuals. The stuff you see in the screenshots is really how your base ends up looking because of the gameplay mechanics that push you to do that. And each of the 6 planes has a unique feel because the structures you build from the corresponding elements are different both visually and mechanically.
2) When stings start to get stale, you can just progress by powering a portal to a different plane and effectively start over with a new element from the six available. Things are familiar but also fresh.
3) The game is not grindy at all. Even late game research moves pretty fast and the resource requirements are very reasonable. 
For a $30 game, I expect 30 hrs of fun gameplay and there is definitely more here (but not hundreds for sure).

In terms of what is missing: 

The opening sequence was pretty cool and wish there was more to the story as you enter new planes. 

It's possible to have 2 streams of elements on a streamway (left and right) but it's pretty much a trap at the moment as it's really awkward to split and combine. I would stick to a single element per belt

Не верьте положительным отзывам на эту игру. Я искренне не понимаю, кто их пишет и в какие игры они вообще играют. Это одна из тех игр, что 100% должна была попасть к Зулину в 2010 году или в современный "Разбор полетов", как ретро. Вот только игра вышла в 2025. Это абсолютно абсурдный треш, но не прикольный, а именно отвратительный. Игра встречает нас не самым плохим сегментом под водой, где мы ОЧЕНЬ медленно идем по рельсам. Это самый приятный и симпатичный сегмент во всей игре (вероятно потому, что мы в полной темноте и отсутствие интерактивности кажется оправданным). После мы поднимемся наверх и первое, что бросается в глаза - это отвратительная графика. Я серьезно, она тут хуже, чем в старичке Doom 3. Не только с точки зрения технологического уровня, но и с точки зрения артдизайна. Локации, к слову, как под копирку оттуда. Только станция не космическая, а подводная, но сути дела это не меняет. Серые коридоры, огромное количество совершенно пустых комнат (ни сторителлинга, ни ресурсов, ни противников), очень странный кислотный свет и по-плохому непроглядная (вырвиглазная) тьма. Дальше клишейные скримеры и "страшные звуки". Только это звуки Хищника из одноименного фильма, поэтому как-то вообще не страшно, а скорее смешно. Побродив по коридорам, застряв пару раз в текстурах/моделях, я смог обзавестись оружием (которое давали еще в "прологе", но там не успеваешь осознать насколько плохо здесь оно реализовано) и мне рассказали про стелс. Вот знаете этот стелс, который в первой же сцене не работает? Так это буквально он. Я зашел за спину противнику и его коллега заметил меня сквозь этого противника. Открыл огонь. Искры полетели от первого персонажа, но он даже не повел бровью. Так мы вдвоем смотрели на этого поехавшего НПС, который всадил уже всю обойму в своего напарника и не планировал останавливаться. Пришлось помочь ему и я узрел ганплей в этой игре. Лучше бы его не было. Враги очень плохо реагируют на попадания, это, без шуток, прям "польский шутер", где попадание сигнализируется одинаковой анимацией и красным "всполохом" в исполнении противника. А потом он падает в смешную олдскульную physics позу. В это время его напарники бегают кругами вокруг и орут что-то, даже не думая занимать укрытие. Просто носятся, как угарелые в стиле ситкома. Тут я уже точно понял, какая это будет игра. Короче, не буду спойлерить дальше, но буквально все тут - это как машина времени в ту эпоху, когда шутеры делали на коленке за копейки, а идеи добавляли по типу "почему бы и нет", без оглядки на уместность оных. Сейчас даже в инди сегменте проекты более качественные и продуманные и встретить такое в 2025 - это буквально какая-то шутка. Хотите лютого, некачественного треша - возьмите, ведь мой пример лишь один кусочек из прохождения, а в ней все на таком уровне. А если вы поверили в хвалебные отзывы - лучше пройдите мимо. Это то ли боты, то ли люди, которых только выпустили из криокамер/подвала. Серьезно, тут ниже сравнивают с Fear и Doom - это несусветная чушь и ложь. Это скорее Rogue Warrior, Pirate Hunter или одна из фейк-хоррор-игр на Unity.

After years of building on what I learned from the first game, this sequel is finally out in Early Access. It’s bigger, smarter, and built to grow with the community.

What’s different from BGVR1?

New battle system: Combat now fully embraces 3D maneuvering with six shield arcs instead of four, making positioning and tactics matter more than ever.

More ships: Twice as many ship classes and a cleaner, more modular codebase for future updates.

Better UI: Everything’s standardized for smoother control from the bridge.

The Gauntlet: A combat-focused mode with randomized missions, rewards, and escalating challenges — risk and reward with permanent gains and losses.

Open World: A procedurally generated galaxy filled with missions, factions, pirates, mining, and trading. Play and grow however you choose.

Reworked Conquest: Build and supply stations, lay down or destroy warp lanes, and coordinate with others to push your faction’s borders. Player factions are coming.

Co-op and Multiplayer: Planned for later in Early Access.

It’s not finished, but it’s already fully playable — and I’ll be expanding it constantly with your feedback. If you liked the first game please check it out!

Don't be scared off by the age, it's still worth experiencing for yourself if you haven't.

This game took a cherished, beloved IP—one that’s been long overdue for a new release—and turned it into nothing more than a blatant cash grab. Easily one of the biggest disappointments I’ve ever endured in gaming. Thanks for absolutely nothing, Starbreeze.

Оригинальная Payday разработана/издана Overkill/Daybreak. Потом студию Overkill выкупает Starbreeze, выпускают практически ту же игру, но с названием Payday 2, которая за много лет обрастает кучей DLC и улучшений. В какой-то момент большинство основателей и ключевых разработчиков из Overkill уходят, остатки команды Overkill присоединяются к Starbreeze Studios и занимаются поддержкой Payday 2. Потом Starbreeze решает получить немного денежной подпитки и находит издателя, готового профинансировать разработку Payday 3. Но, как я понимаю, руководство Starbreeze решило не вести полноценную разработку с нуля, ибо это слишком затратно по времени и ресурсам, а просто взять модный движок Unreal и попытаться перенести на него игровой процесс Payday 2. В итоге имеем то, что имеем: это тот же Payday 2 на новом движке (и с новыми багами), несколько новых механик и видов копов, но намного меньше разных ограблений, нет интеграции с торговой площадкой Steam, нет модов (того же любимого многими Silent Assassin), нет видео-вставок с актерами, не такой яркий саундтрек (главный композитор Payday 2 Саймон Виклунд участия в работе над этой игрой не принимал). 
Возможно, когда-нибудь эта игра обрастет мяском и получит какое-то признание, если в Starbreeze есть желание и возможности её развивать, но сейчас она просто не конкурент Payday 2 по наполнению. Тем не менее, если вам нравилась/нравится Payday 2, но вы уже по несколько раз прошли все ограбления - наверное, будет любопытно побегать и в этой игре.

『Melty Blood Actress Again Current Code』は、空中機動、緊密なプレッシャー構築、対戦相性の理解を軸とした2D対戦格闘ゲームです。地上戦の間合い管理も重要ですが、ジャンプ軌道、エアダッシュ、シールドオプションが中立状況を大きく左右します。機動力は強力で、多くの攻防が空中で発生するため、精密な間合い調整と迅速な反応が求められます。

本作の中心的システムは「ムーンスタイル」です。各キャラクターはクレセント、ハーフ、フルの3種を持ち、通常技、必殺技、ゲージ循環、防御オプションが変化します。対戦相性の複雑性は大幅に増加し、事実上一つのキャラクターが三通りの性能を持つ構造となります。同一キャラクターでもスタイル差により操作感が変化し、競技シーンでは表面的理解ではなく深い知識が求められます。

攻めのシステムは多層的です。リバースビートにより柔軟なキャンセルルートが可能となり、連係の延長やフレームトラップの秘匿に寄与します。シールドはリスクを伴う防御選択肢で、的確な読みは攻め側を処罰し、誤れば大きな損害を受けます。これらにより攻防テンポが形成され、攻めは強力ですが、防御も爆発力を有します。プレイヤー判断が成果を左右します。

コンボルートは多様で表現力があります。打ち上げから空中コンボ、締め技による起き攻め展開が基本です。ダメージは高めですが、ドロップは展開をリセットします。キャラクターごとに難度は異なり、研究の成果が顕著に現れます。ゲージはEX締めやガードキャンセルに使用され、ラウンド全体の主導権に影響します。リソース運用が勝敗に直結します。

オンライン対戦環境はコミュニティによるロールバック実装に依存しており、公式サポートは限定的です。そのためオフライン対戦が標準となっています。大会シーンでは対戦相性、セットプレイルート、対策の応酬が重視されます。ムーンスタイルの存在によりキャラクター多様性は維持されます。階層差は存在しますが、プレイヤーの技量が数値差を上回りやすい設計です。

There’s a special kind of danger in Satisfactory. It’s not the giant spiders or falling off a cliff while placing a conveyor. It’s that little voice that says “just five more minutes.” Then the sun is coming up, your coffee is cold, and your factory hums like a cathedral of steel and motion.

This game nails the dopamine loop better than almost anything out there. Every time you fix one bottleneck, two more appear, but it never feels punishing. It’s addictive in the best way, full of small victories wrapped in the steady hum of machines and glowing lines of progress.

The gameplay loop is deceptively simple but endlessly deep. You start by mining iron and crafting parts by hand. Before long, you have automated the basics, then you are scaling up, building new tiers, unlocking trains and drones, and chasing efficiency that always feels just out of reach. Every upgrade feeds into a bigger idea, and every “temporary” setup somehow becomes permanent. It’s the kind of game that quietly trains you to think like an engineer, even if you never meant to.

One of the most satisfying parts is deciding how your factory will grow. Some players build tall, vertical complexes with layers upon layers of machines stacked into the sky. Others prefer wide, sprawling layouts that stretch across entire biomes, a maze of conveyors winding through forests and cliffs. There is no single right way to do it, which makes every player’s world feel personal, a reflection of their own version of order and chaos.

The visuals carry so much charm. Watching your factory come alive is a reward on its own. Conveyors glide like arteries, feeding into splitters and constructors that pulse with quiet precision. When everything works together, it’s oddly beautiful. And when it doesn’t, it’s still beautiful in its own way. A giant spaghetti mess of belts looping in every direction, machines somehow still running. Chaos that functions.

That said, there are a couple of things that can test your patience. The early game can feel slow, especially when you’re stuck handcrafting parts before automation kicks in. It’s satisfying once things get rolling, but that first stretch can feel like pushing a cart with square wheels. Later on, when your factory grows massive, performance and organization start to fight back. Belts pile up, power demands spike, and it can all become a bit of a balancing act that pulls you out of the calm rhythm the game builds so well.

That’s the magic of Satisfactory. It’s both a meditation and a madness. A game where perfection and disaster exist side by side, and either way you’ll tell yourself, “just one more fix.”

„Steampunk‑Überleben mit Riesenschraube – ein solides Erlebnis!“
Wertung: 8 / 10

Als Fan von Survival‑ und Aufbau‑Spielen hat mich Volcanoids von Anfang an neugierig gemacht – die Idee, nicht einfach eine Basis zu bauen, sondern auf einer gigantischen Bohrmaschine („Drillship“) zu sitzen, die durch Inseln und Vulkane fährt, ist frisch und spannend. Die Mischung aus Erkunden, Bau, Technik und Action trifft hier überraschend gut. 


Was mir besonders gut gefallen hat:

Die Atmosphäre: Eine Insel, die von Vulkanausbrüchen bedroht wird, kombiniert mit steampunkiger Bohrtechnik – ergibt ein stimmiges, eigenständiges Setting. 

Die Bohrmaschine als Basis: Ich liebe es, wie sich das Drillship nach und nach erweitert, neue Module bekommt und man sich eine mobile Festung baut. Das gibt dem Aufbau‑Aspekt richtig Gewicht.

Fortschritt spürbar: Man merkt, wie man wächst – bessere Ausrüstung, stärkere Gegner, größere Räume im Drillship – das motiviert zum Weiterspielen.

Ein paar Punkte, wo ich Luft nach oben sehe:

Teilweise fühlte sich das Gameplay etwas repetitiv an – nach einigen Durchgängen ähnelt sich die Routine etwas, Rohstoffe sammeln, Module bauen, Gegner bekämpfen.

Technisch gibt’s noch Macken – wie bei vielen Indie‑Survivalgames: UI könnte klarer sein, Tutorials an manchen Stellen besser, den Einstieg einfacher.

Story bzw. Tiefe: Wenn man ein Spiel mit starker narrativer Ausrichtung sucht, wird man hier eher weniger finden. Der Fokus liegt klar auf Spielmechanik und Erkundung.

Fazit:
Volcanoids liefert ein sehr solides Survival‑Aufbau‑Erlebnis mit eigenem Charme. Wer Lust hat auf Technikbasteln, auf eine mobile Basis und eine etwas andere Spielmechanik als „nur Haus und Festung“, wird hier definitiv Spaß haben. Es könnte etwas raffinierter sein und ein paar Wiederholungen stören, aber insgesamt stimmt das Paket. Für mich eine klare Empfehlung – 8/10.

I feel kind of bad giving this a negative review, and to be fair, it's not like I regret purchasing it. This is a game with a very clear large amount of effort poured into it - it has a lot of heart and soul. I don't think this is a terrible game - just a disappointing one. 
The original release, with the demo, I found electrifying. It was weird, interesting, as well as being really freaky. It was genuinely, a scary game. It leveraged its mystery through that scariness.
This game opens with just a complete copy of that original game - which unfortunately only adds to the whiplash. I'm not going to spoil this game, but all I'll say is not only is this game not scary, it's not a horror game. After that opening bit, there is only one moment (shortly after) where I felt mildly creeped out. But otherwise, the game veers completely into a kind of sappy drama. By the end, the sapfest had reached its height, while the gameplay had also gotten way more basic. It was just a lose-lose. By the end, I can't really call this anything more than a wet fart. The original was so interesting BECAUSE it was scary - to remove that is to remove the feeling and identity of what made the original game so compelling, and what made the idea of a full game so exciting. I feel very disappointed - I was hoping for a game where it would feel like I was digging through a computer and uncovering a mystery that felt more and more haunting as I went on. Instead, I got this weird glorified sci-fi romance drama walking simulator. I feel bad for not liking this, because so much effort was put into it. But I just really didn't like it.
If any of you felt similarly to me, I would say that a game that felt like what I wanted No Players Online to be was Shipwrecked 64 - that game had the same idea, same concept, but taken to far more terrifying of an execution. No Players Online feels like high quality, but in all the wrong ways.

I have some of the rarer achievements in this after one playthrough, and found a few different ways to achieve the same goals. There are areas I haven't accessed yet (the docks, noble quarter, and other parts of the capital) but I feel like I have experienced enough of the game to leave an honest review. 

The honest review is this - I've been gaming for more than 35 years. If this game had been out in the SNES era, it would have been a MAJOR player, and a complete game changer. In 2025 it stands out as doing several things that I really enjoy in this genre (RPG, my favourite) very well. 

These things are: 

1. Loot - lots, varied, and it seems there is always something new or an upgrade to chase. Chests always feel exciting, and unique/epic drops are... well, unique and epic. 

2. Combat - The combat is as smooth as can be for a top down 3rd person isometric RPG. Feels very polished and responsive. Don't forget your potions and resource management!

3. Customising your character - Not the appearance, although that is also here (albeit in a minimalistic sense). I mean customizing your playthrough with a different approach to combat. The game takes the old classics and does them well - Warrior, Ranger, Mage. You can mix and match as you see fit, once you get to a high enough level. 

4. Power fantasy - Leveling up doesn't feel super impactful at first, but if you stick with it you will be rewarded. By the end of my first playthrough I was 4-5 hitting the hidden end bosses. Making important choices meaningful means you can unlock better gear at the sacrifice of other things (I chose to use a giant 2h Unique Zweihander which required a 50 str point investment, but this meant that at level 35 I didn't have much else, a few points into luck and vitality). Don't worry if you mess up, there will be a "respec" unlocked at a certain point in the story. 

I highly recommend this game, especially at it's price point.

I've twice had game-breaking bugs preventing me from progressing in two respective attempts at playthroughs. 我一直自认为是个萝莉控与妹控，因此在玩GAL时，这两类角色始终有着最高的攻略优先级，妹系更甚，如富婆妹、纸魔、RJ天使嚣嚣、近月（少女理论）等，但在玩拔作岛时却没有太多攻略妹妹的欲望（即使二代有妹妹线路），同样的情况出现在了天选庶民、醋意乱流等作品上。合上电脑我不禁反思，我所执着的“妹妹”或“萝莉”，作为一种属性，究竟为何吸引着我。要解构妹妹这个属性的意义，不妨找一些二次元中妹妹的代表人物，如轻小说中的五河琴里、高坂桐乃、和泉纱雾等，春日野穹、谷风天音、和泉妃爱等Gal中的经典形象，我对漫画的涉猎不多，只能用星野露比和部分非女主的角色作为样本分析。可以发现，即使他们在各自的行业、或是作为学生在学业上成就斐然，但在与“哥哥”的关系中，总不约而同地呈现出某种依赖与脆弱。这种依赖未必是能力上的欠缺，而更像一种情感上的“弱势表演”，其功能在于唤起“哥哥”——亦即玩家的保护欲与主体认同。同样，萝莉属性也往往作为“被保护欲”的符号化载体而成立，可以说萝莉就是保护欲的代名词，当然萝莉老太婆和萝莉先辈也赛高，且不提其中隐喻的保护性，稚嫩的外表和成熟的内在（当然渡酱这种只有年龄是先辈的也有）的对比性真的超级渋。那么，我对妹妹与萝莉的情感投入，究竟是源于角色本身的脆弱性，还是“妹妹”或“萝莉”这类属性所预设的情感结构？如果深究就陷入了先有鸡还是先有蛋的悖论中，或许问题本身就需要被重新理解：属性从来不是孤立存在的标签，不能和具体的角色割裂。它必须被置于具体的叙事语境与角色关系中才能生效。当我无法对麻沙音这一妹妹形象产生共鸣，并不是因为角色属性的失效，而是在拔作岛的叙事中未能建立起那种唤起我情感认同的保护关系，尽管妹妹也在各种桥段中表现出了需要哥哥保护的脆弱感，但诙谐的剧本主基调使麻沙音这一形象更类似于一个光屁股长大的好兄弟形象。因此，我认为渡酱是毋庸置疑的夯中夯，不推的只能度过一个相对失败的人生。
当然，或许没有什么萝莉控和妹控，只有一类希望获得在虚拟关系中得以实现的、被需要与被肯定的心理体验的平凡人罢了。
q社能写出这种东西也是gal界的一个奇葩了，我上哪里给你找段子又多剧情还好的王道热血佳作去啊

This game has a fantastic core concept and a [b]really strong visual style[/b].
However, in its current state, it still feels quite rough around the edges. I’m definitely planning to come back in a few months to see how it’s improved — and hopefully update this to a positive review! 

For now, though, here’s my feedback:


[*]Visuals & Art Direction

The models, environments, and character designs are absolutely the best part of the game — they’re striking and full of personality. That said, some of the animations feel noticeably unpolished in comparison, which creates a bit of a contrast with the otherwise beautiful visuals.



[*]Gameplay & Core Loop

The gameplay loop could feel smoother. The potion crafting system, in particular, doesn’t feel as satisfying or intuitive as it could be.

You can’t easily see how many potions or materials you have unless you open the inventory (Tab).

Drinking potions rarely feels worthwhile compared to just using them on your weapon.

The game creates that classic “I could use this now... but what if I need it later?” feeling common in consumable-heavy systems. I often found myself either hoarding too much or running out entirely.

Some attacks also feel off, where the animations don’t quite match the hitboxes. A clear example is the lizard enemy with the cauldron in the second area — its attack timing feels out of sync. This issue happens with several enemies, but that one stands out the most.

When I try to play “as intended,” using potions regularly and crafting constantly, boss fights end up dragging because I run out of resources. If I save enough potions for the boss, the fight feels smoother — but the journey to get there becomes significantly slower.
It feels like the balance and AI design encourage resource hoarding, even though the theme of being an alchemist suggests you should be using potions strategically to gain power.



[*]Animation & Polish

As a professional gameplay animator, this was actually what drew me to the game — and unfortunately, it’s also where I’m most disappointed.

The animations frequently clip and bug out, especially during dialogue scenes. The decision to have characters snap abruptly between loop animations feels jarring. Games like Potionomics make this work, but here it just feels unnatural; a smoother transition between poses would go a long way.
I know this might sound minor, but since the game revolves around combat and returning to see new character interactions, poor animation flow really hurts the experience. It makes those moments — which should be charming and engaging — feel awkward instead.

Enemy animations aren’t bad, but they lack anticipation and clarity. Many boss attacks don’t properly telegraph what’s coming, which makes combat feel unfair rather than challenging.

I feel that the animations lack the appeal that the models bring. Which negatively creates a contrast that hinders the overall experience.
The main char animations feel somewhat disconnected to the world he lives in. The gameplay animation also feels a little rough as well.



[*]Sound Design

The sound mix needs a lot of polish.

Volumes are inconsistent — some weapons are extremely loud while enemies are nearly silent.

Certain potion effects have uneven volume levels (some too loud, others barely audible).

I understand that audio often gets finalized late in development, but as it stands, I actually found myself muting the entire game rather than risk a jumpscare from the wind weapon’s sound, for example.



[*]Final Thoughts

This game is not bad — it genuinely pains me to leave a negative review because there’s so much potential here. The art direction, ideas, and core systems all show promise. But right now, the rough edges in animation, balancing, and sound make it hard to recommend in its current form.
I’ll definitely revisit it in a few months and hope to update this review to a positive one.

Ein „nie“ abgeschickter Brief an seine Mutter

Story:
Eine junge Frau dankt in einer Erzählung ihrer verstorbenen Mutter. Nach dem Tod ihrer Mutter wird der jungen Frau bewusst, dass es im Leben leider kein „zurück“ gibt. Viele Dinge die sie ihrer Mutter gesagt oder an den Kopf geworfen hat, die sie nie mehr zurücknehmen kann. Und so viele Dinge die sie ihr noch hätte sagen wollen!

Die Vergangenheit erzählt:
Wir gehen durch das Elternhaus und erkunden den Ort der Kindheit. Währenddessen werden uns kleine Episoden aus der Vergangenheit mit ihrer Mutter erzählt. Ansprüche und Vorhaltungen, Mahnungen der Mutter, die wir erst Jahre später richtig verstehen. Viele verpasste Chancen der Mutter zu sagen, was man fühlt. Und Dankbarkeit, die nie zum Ausdruck gebracht wurde.

Steuerung:
Es ist ein Walkingsimulator. Die Steuerung gibt mir keinen Anlass zur Kritik. Ich habe nur mit Maus/Tastatur gespielt, ohne Probleme.

Grafik:
Dear Mom nutzt die Unity Engine, welche eine schöne Umgebung zaubert. Ich finde z.B. den rosa Himmel schön (ja mag Geschmackssache sein), auch die Blumen und Bäume sehen gut aus. Allerdings kam es an zwei Stellen es zu Tearing und die Grafik hat an mehreren Stellen stark geflimmert und sah ein wenig unscharf aus.

Synchronisierung/Sound:
Die Erzählerin ist hervorragend, sie erzählt die Geschichte wirklich überzeugend und mit sanfter Stimme.
Es wird Englisch gesprochen ohne deutsche Übersetzung, auch keine Untertitel.
Die Musik ist gut, dezent, nie aufdringlich und passt gut zum Spiel. Auch wenn ich das Gefühlt hatte, die Musik kommt nur aus einer einzigen Richtung.

Meine eigenen Gedanken:
Als ich dies schrieb und ich darüber nachdachte, wurde mir schmerzlich bewusst, dass es mir auch so geht. Ja ich, und viele andere sicher auch, habe meiner Mutter viele Dinge gesagt. Böse Wörter, die besser ungesagt geblieben wären, die ich nicht sagen wollte oder sollte. Ich habe diese Dinge in Ärger oder Wut gesagt und werde sie nie mehr zurücknehmen können. Und das macht mich traurig.
Aber ich habe noch Zeit und kann meiner Mutter noch viele schöne Sachen sagen. Oder einfach Danke!

Fazit:
Es ist kein perfektes Spiel, die Grafik ist gut, aber sie hätte besser sein können. Die Erzählung der Story ist stimmig und passt gut zum gewählten Setting. Ob die Geschichte einen berührt, hängt natürlich von jedem persönlich und von der eigenen Beziehung zur Mutter ab. Trotzdem ist es ein gutes Spiel mit einer berührend schönen Geschichte.

Pros:
+ A fun, interesting story with twists that will keep you hooked until the end.
+ Will take you about 5-6 hours to beat if you talk with everyone you can and interact with everything you can. Not bad for under a buck.
+ A lot of interactables, and they usually change as the story progresses.
+ You get choices, and sometimes those choices are simply inactions, that slightly change dialogue and things that happen.
+ An ending that no matter what you do is not "happy". Rare to see in any game.
+ Combat is challenging and forces you to take advantage of stuns, and to know the basics of turn based combat. There's even ship combat.
+ Free DLC that is short but fun.
+ can get paid to let a guy stroke your tail.

Cons:
- The story isn't as fleshed out as it should be. There are various plot happenings that you have to infer yourself why they happened. Other plot points aren't explained at all with nothing to help you with an answer.
- A lot of grammatical and spelling errors, but this is the norm for RPG-M games.
- Once you understand it, combat is rather simple. It stops becoming challenging once you get stun bomb. The only ailment you can inflict is stun or defense down (besides ship combat). The game is worth it, and I really hope we see a sequel.

[h1] 서로 얼굴만 봐도 흥겨운 보물찾기 삼인방 [/h1]

전사와 도적, 마법사를 번갈아 조종하며 보물을 획득해야 하는 창고지기 스타일의 퍼즐 게임이다. 적당한 퀄리티의 픽셀 그래픽은 특유의 귀엽고 아기자기한 분위기를 잘 드러낸다. 그리고 각기 특성이 다른 세 캐릭터를 적절히 움직여야 하는 게임 디자인이 나름 인상적으로 다가온다. 한편으로는 공식 유튜브에 올라온 쇼츠 영상들이 연이어 수백만의 조회수를 기록하고 있다는 특이한 이력을 보유하고 있는 게임이기도 하다.

세 캐릭터는 각자 성격이 다르다. 전사는 용감하고, 도적은 약삭빠르며, 마법사는 겁이 많다. 우선 전사는 무거운 상자나 몬스터를 때려부술 수 있다. 그리고 도적은 가시 바닥을 지나다닐 수 있고 괴물들에게 감지되지 않는다. 마지막으로 마법사는 자기 스스로나 다른 캐릭터를 2칸 범위 안에서 순간이동 시킬 수 있다. 세 캐릭터의 직업과 성격에 부합하는 특성 배분이 돋보인다. 여기에 세 캐릭터의 특성을 감안해 짜여진 퍼즐 디자인도 완성도가 제법 괜찮다.

총 10개의 챕터와 각 챕터 당 20개의 스테이지가 준비돼있다. 그리고 각 챕터마다 장소에 어울리는 특별한 기믹이 몇 가지 존재한다. 이를테면 화산 구역의 용암 바닥이나 바다 구역의 문어 촉수 함정, 궁전 구역의 포탈같은 장치 등이 그런 기믹에 해당한다. 이런 다양한 기믹이 세 캐릭터의 특성과 잘 어우러져 다양한 양상의 퍼즐 디자인을 선보인다. 따라서 챕터가 바뀔 때마다 게임의 양상이 전환되니 완전히 새로운 발상으로 접근해야 한다. 그만큼 퍼즐 게임으로써의 신선도가 오래 유지되는 효과가 있어 퍼즐을 풀어나가는 재미가 상당하다.

한 챕터 안에서도 스테이지의 양상이 다양하게 나뉜다. 초반부 스테이지에서는 새로운 기믹이 처음 나타나는 쉬운 스테이지로 플레이어에게 기믹을 숙지시킨다. 그리고 기믹을 다방면으로 응용하거나 점차 특정 캐릭터의 사용을 제한하거는 스테이지를 내세우며 난이도를 서서히 올린다. 점진적인 난이도 상승을 통한 완급 조절도 제법 괜찮은 편이다. 여기에 모든 스테이지를 해결하고 나면 각 스테이지마다 사이드 퀘스트가 추가되고, 40종의 추가 챌린지 레벨이 추가로 해금된다. 덕분에 게임을 한 차례 마친 이후에도 플레이할 것들이 여전히 많다. 이런 풍부한 컨텐츠 역시 이 게임의 강점으로 꼽을 만하다.

다만 아쉬운 점도 없진 않다. 일단 힌트 제공이 조금 부실하다. 정말 어려운 구조의 스테이지라 하더라도 힌트는 단 한 줄 뿐이고, 이마저도 정말 복합적인 스테이지가 아니라면 힌트가 아예 제공되지 않는다. 힌트의 내용이 나름 결정적인 내용을 담고 있긴 하나 퍼즐을 직접 푸는 입장에선 여전히 모호하게 다가올 수 있다. 그리고 개인적으로는 각 챕터간의 연계성이 크지 않다는 점도 아쉽다. 앞선 챕터에 등장한 기믹이 이후에도 간간히 나와 이전 챕터를 떠올리게 만들었더라면 더 괜찮았을 듯하다.

그래도 기대 이상의 재미와 완성도를 자랑하는 퍼즐 게임임에는 분명하다. 각기 특성이 다른 세 캐릭터와 다양한 기믹을 보유한 10종의 챕터, 그리고 기본에 충실하면서도 절묘한 구석이 있는 난이도 배분 등, 긍정적으로 평가할 만한 요소가 많다. 단순히 유튜브 쇼츠를 통해 알려진 게임으로 넘어가기엔 너무나도 아깝게 느껴지는 게임이다. 가벼운 디자인에 꽤 머리를 써야하는 퍼즐 게임을 선호하는 이들이라면 이 게임이 꽤나 만족스럽게 다가올 것이다.

P.S! 게임의 출시 이후 몇몇 스테이지의 디자인을 다듬은 것 같다. 이 때문에 누군가 유튜브에 올린 공략을 참조하더라도 그걸로 해결이 안 되는 퍼즐이 몇 가지 있다. 주의할 것.
