This is a very charming little game, and I think most fans of adventure games will find something to like here. Some of the chapters in this game are real bangers up there with some of the classic LucasArts games and the soundtrack is excellent and atmospheric. I would say the characters are memorable, and I enjoyed the recurrence of several of them between chapters, making the world feel cohesive and alive

I say all of this, of course, with a few caveats - because this game is still far from perfect and contains a number of truly bizarre choices.

You play as Detective McQueen, working alongside your partner Officer Dooley with the Twin Lakes P.D.'s "Darkside Division", to investigate paranormal occurrences occasionally related to the eponymous parallel realm known as the "Darkside" and its spectral inhabitants. This premise takes you to all sorts of locations ranging from a haunted library, to a summer camp beset by a lake monster, to the mysterious Darkside itself - each with its own puzzles, mystery, and cast of characters. The puzzles in question are, despite what some of the reviews here would say, far [i]less[/i] moon-logic than a lot of retro adventure games, being more on-par on average with the LucasArts games than some of the ludicrously obtuse showings from Sierra. While some of them can be particularly tough, even if one was to use a guide they would likely find that a lot of the answers they are stuck on are things they actually did know or suspect were the solution, but were simply implementing it wrong.

These cases are just, woefully unbalanced though. A few of them, the aforementioned "bangers", feature complex and multilayered environments with plenty to do and see. Puzzles that require multiple objects from multiple rooms and the completion of other puzzles, item combinations that one would expect from the genre, etc. Several others are distinctly [i]not[/i] like this, and are extremely short and simplistic. Others are somewhere in the middle in terms of length, but are still notably easy compared to earlier cases. This isn't the biggest deal, but it's strange. There's not really a great sense of progression overall, though the variety may actually serve to entice some. Similarly hit-or-miss is the humor. This game is a comedy more than it is a mystery or horror title, and while I personally enjoyed it and got some laughs every now and again, be warned that it does think it's much funnier than it actually is and several moments that appear to be leading to something unnerving instead deflate themselves with comedic bits. Again, I was fine with it, but it might tick you off if you're expecting something more aligned with a paranomal-noir adventure.

The strangest decision made by this game though, is the inclusion of the "bonus chapters". Well, the inclusion isn't the problem necessarily, but unlike the story chapters they're accessible from the very start of the game and the name implies they are optional. This is a complete lie and their categorization as such is nonsensical - these should have just been shuffled into the existing chapters or unlocked once you beat the game. 

The first of these bonus chapters is [i]extremely[/i] long and complex, featuring characters you have met in other chapters before and in at least one case, requiring some degree of knowledge of what a particular character is like in order to solve a puzzle. The second is extremely short - almost as short as the tutorial, and almost as easy too. This one requires no knowledge of anything in the game and honestly could have been the second level. The final one is the most confusing of all because while it lies somewhere in the middle in terms of difficulty and length, it [b]contains the canonical ending to the game that sets up the sequel[/b].  Why is this a bonus chapter? Why are any of these? It would perhaps make sense if there was some plot throughline through the main chapters, but there really isn't for about 2/3rds of them. The actual "final chapter" also does not serve to conclude any ongoing plotline, which makes it unclear as to why it's considered the finale when the actual ending that the sequel follows up on is contained in an optional bonus episode. 

Well, either way. This game is fun and I enjoyed my time with it quite a bit. Flaws are present, but not to the extent where they actually hinder the experience if you're already vibing with it and plan to play the entire game. Seriously, play the bonus episodes. I've heard the sequel is better, and I already thought this one was pretty good - so I look forward to playing that and seeing where the improvements lie. I've heard that one has bonus chapters too, as well as more of an overarching plot, so I'm curious to see if there's actually a difference between story and bonus chapters, and whether the bonuses inexplicably contain the canon ending again.

This is a solid first take on a Brotato-style arena shooter.

There are a bunch of frustrating things that make it less fun than Brotato:

- It's a wave-based arena shooter in a small square, but the mobs never reset between waves, so you never get to breathe. Brotato works so well because of the pacing of getting to the end of those last waves, having everything reset, and going in again. That doesn't happen here. If you have 40 mobs on you and 10 hp, it will be the same when you come out of the shop phase. Good luck.
- Related to the above, the difficulty curve is out of whack to where it feels like you're in the endgame 3 or 4 waves in. The first few waves and games shouldn't feel like the player is getting their teeth kicked in.
- There is no way to freeze or banish items in the shop, which is terrible for these games, which are so build-dependent.
- Related to the above, The meta progression feels boring and a little too specific, buffing specific spells you're unlikely to get unless the stars align. 20 damage to a spell isn't something to get excited about.
- This is similar with the relics you get during the runs. If I'm a fire build, getting a relic with a cool effect unrelated to the damage I'm investing in feels bad. It's better if the trees and relics are more general so any build can use them.
- Some bosses and mechanics feel overly punishing.
- Fire is far ahead of the other two elements right now.

All things that can be easily tweaked and balanced as time goes on.

Would love to see this dev continue to cook and add more spells, skills, characters, and levels.

I'd also love to see a pass on the UI and HUD so they're as beautiful as the pixel art in the game.

Keep it up!

Overview: This game allows people of any skill to play a lot of mini games together to find out who is the best overall. This game plays well for people that have 0 first person skills like my wife and expert skills like the primary developer of the game.

Game Play: Since each game offers a different set a rules and skills needed the game seems fresh each time you play. Some game require quick aim and fire while others require you to think quick and dodge in coming objects. The game does support controller and keyboard. This will allow each person to use their favored device. There will be games that you may not like and as the host you can choose what games to include.

Graphics: The game does not have cutting edge like COD, Hell Let Loose, or high cost games. The game utilizes the Unreal engine, so has a fun and efficient graphic engine. This also allows for more people to play due to the lower graphic requirements.

Sound: A lot of fun tracks to hear as you play the game. Biggest issue here is that they due repeat and can get repetitive if you play a lot or end up being stuck in the lobby.

End Thoughts: With me and my gaming group getting this originally to help test the near release version of this game we got to experience a fun quick game. Our group of 8 enjoyed seeing the game develop overtime and to have a lot of fun playing many of the games. Overall allowed for our many different skilled players to play the many different games together. If you like games like Fall Guys or Among Us you will enjoy this game.

Incredible, a pretty hardcore roguelike that combines well the need for skills, patience and luck to win.
The combat feels a bit simple at first but the focus is more on timing. The variety of weapons, spells and armor is cool, all of them are useful with a skill ceiling and even secondary actions. It also adds the different types of enemies with their own way to deal with them, and wow the bosses are the coolest, even with limited attacks they still need a lot of effort to not die, and the soundtrack is a banger after banger.
Obviously, the exploration is a big part of it, full of secrets and dark setting, no map and a lot of blind corners, so caution and stealth are necessary, and the upgrades you can get are very game-changing, really good rewards overall.
Sadly, there are thing I don't like or are annoying (they might be change given this is actually early access, idk), the first one is that there are a lot of enemies who can just straight up stunlock you to death, the good thing is that you can do it too, but still doesn't feel good to fight them. The UI takes a bit to get used to and is entirely on top of the character, which is fine, but the camera moves a lot when you try to zoom out by moving the cursor to the border, and most of the times this makes your character be totally out of focus, this is horrible as you don't know how much health you have or which thing you have equipped, on bosses is even worse.
The last thing, which is a bit more personal (and spoiler I guess) is [spoiler] I reaaaally dislike having enemies be straight up inmune to types of damage, I get the reasoning but this, on a roguelike where you don't have that much room to experiment with builds due to rng, is just run ending. It just make you not wanting to do certain fun builds (like the fire one) because of knowing one boss will be imposible for you to damage it, really dislike that. [/spoiler]

I love it, you will die a lot and start over but the fun never ends, a lot of potencial for future patches and a lot to things to find even when you finish it once. Totally recommended.


Esp: Increíble, un roguelike hardcore que combina bien la necesidad de habilidad, paciencia y suerte para ganar.

La variedad de armas, hechizos y armaduras es genial, todos ellos útiles con espacio para dominar e incluso acciones secundarias. También tiene diferentes tipos de enemigos con su propia forma de enfrentarse a ellos, y los jefes son tremendos, incluso con ataques limitados, hay que esforzarse mucho para no morir, y el soundtrack es una delicia.
Obviamente, la exploración es la parte importante, llena de secretos y ambientación oscura, sin mapa y con muchos rincones ciegos, por lo que es necesario ir con cuidado y sigiloso, y las mejoras que puedes conseguir cambian mucho el juego, muy buenas recompensas en general.
Lamentablemente, hay cosas que no me gustan o que me molestan (puede que cambien, ya que se trata de un early access, no sé), la primera es que hay muchos enemigos que pueden hacerte stunlock hasta matarte, lo bueno es que tú también puedes hacerlo, pero sigue sin ser divertido lucharles. La interfaz cuesta un poco acostumbrarse y está completamente encima del personaje, lo cual está bien, pero la cámara se mueve mucho cuando intentas alejar moviendo el cursor hacia el borde, y la mayoría de las veces esto hace que tu personaje quede totalmente fuera de lo visible, lo cual es horrible ya que no sabes cuánta salud tienes ni qué equipo tenes seleccionado, y con los bosses es aún peor.
Lo último, que es un poco más personal (y supongo que un spoiler), es [spoiler] la verdad no me gusta pero nada de nada que haya enemigos que sean inmunes a ciertos tipos de daño. Entiendo el razonamiento, pero siendo un roguelike en el que no hay mucho margen para experimentar con la build debido al RNG, esto directamente arruina runs. Me encanta, morirás muchas veces y tendrás que volver a empezar, pero la diversión nunca termina, tiene mucho potencial para futuros parches y muchas cosas que descubrir incluso cuando lo terminas una vez. Totalmente recomendado.

Capybara Spa is a wholesome and soothing management game that embraces simplicity and charm over complexity, inviting players into a world where relaxation is the only rule that matters. Developed and published by Cozy Bee Games, it places you in charge of a tiny mountaintop retreat dedicated to pampering capybaras and other gentle animal guests. From the moment the first capybara waddles into a warm bath, the game sets a tranquil tone that never wavers. Everything—its soft visual style, gentle animations, and easygoing mechanics—works together to create an experience designed not to challenge you, but to lift your mood and offer a peaceful escape.

The core loop of Capybara Spa revolves around expanding your spa facilities and tending to the needs of the animals that visit. You begin with a small patch of land and a single wooden tub, but as you earn coins and level up, your spa becomes more colorful and lively. You’ll place new baths, plant fruit trees to grow ingredients for treats, craft soaps and towels to delight your guests, and unlock additional animal species like turtles, ducks, otters, and frogs. Each new creature adds a small wrinkle to the flow of tasks, but the game stays intentionally light and approachable. Even at its busiest moments, the pace remains forgiving—animals patiently wait their turn, rewards come steadily, and every action feels like part of an inviting, stress-free routine.

Aesthetically, the game excels in creating a cheerful and cozy atmosphere. The artwork is bright and clean, the animals are extremely expressive despite their simple designs, and the spa itself gradually becomes a delightful blend of wood, water, and greenery. Watching capybaras sink into steaming baths, stack together in adorable piles, or nibble on freshly harvested fruit is inherently relaxing. The sound design reinforces this mood perfectly: soft musical loops, gentle splashes, and occasional animal chirps form an audio landscape that makes the act of tending the spa feel comforting and almost meditative. The game doesn’t pressure you to rush or optimize—it invites you to slow down and enjoy the gentle rhythm of taking care of happy creatures.

Progression is steady and rewarding, even if it leans heavily on simplicity. As you gain experience, you unlock new decorations, upgraded baths, cosmetic add-ons, and expansions that let you extend your spa across increasingly spacious platforms. Each level milestone arrives quickly enough to keep you motivated, adding a small sense of momentum while preserving the overall calm. The crafting system for soaps and treatments offers another light layer of engagement, and while it never becomes deep or intricate, it enhances the feeling that you’re running a quirky but beloved retreat. The joy of watching your spa grow—not through demanding micromanagement, but through gradual, cozy accumulation—is at the core of what makes the game appealing.

Yet it is this same focus on comfort and simplicity that reveals the game’s limitations. Capybara Spa is designed for tranquillity, but players looking for more robust management systems or strategic depth may find it lacking. Tasks repeat often, with little variation as the hours go by, and once all major expansions and unlocks are in place, the sense of progression naturally slows. The loop becomes more about maintaining the spa than evolving it, which can lead to a feeling of repetition for those hoping for more complexity. Some aspects of the interface can be mildly unwieldy, and the game occasionally lacks clarity in certain prompts or building interactions, though none of these issues seriously undermine the experience.

Ultimately, Capybara Spa succeeds in delivering exactly what it promises: a soft, adorable, easygoing simulation where your main goal is to make cute animals comfortable and content. It is a game best suited for players seeking a breather—something to unwind with at the end of the day, or a cozy title to accompany podcasts and quiet evenings. Its charm comes not from challenge but from atmosphere, gentle pacing, and the undeniable appeal of watching capybaras enjoy a warm soak. For fans of wholesome, low-pressure simulation games, Capybara Spa is a delightful retreat worth visiting, even if it doesn’t offer the deepest mechanics or longest lifespan.

It must take some guts making a new minigolf VR game, as this genre is heavily dominated by Walkabout Minigolf. But Walkabout Minigolf is phoneVR, designed for incredibly slow phone gpus (Adreno 650 phone gpu in the Quest 2's XR2 SoC), while Mini Golf Aeons is designed for high-end VR. This you can easily see in some of the great textures, but it's still behind Walkabout Minigolf in the design of courses and the lighting. Of course Walkabout Minigolf has many devs spending years milking the ultraslow Adreno 650 to perfection, while the devs behind Mini Golf Aeons probably has much more limited ressources.

The water quality and refelctions are much better than Walkabout Minigolf:

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3003845619
The courses would look much better adding dynamic shadows and sunlight. Maybe some 3D grass here and there? Also would be nice with more courses and more obstacles on the courses - the present courses are a bit too plain and too easy for my taste. 

The dinos look pretty good though - check out the highly detailed skin textures:

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3004824206
Note that "Knuckles" is the old word for the Index controllers, and is used in the game nenu. 

Both left and right hand is supported for holding the golf club. Snap turn but not smooth is currently supported. You'll hear a tone with the ball is still, and then have to hold the trigger to hit the ball. I would prefer if we did not have to hold the trigger to hit the ball - and if we could be able to move across the courses to take in and enjoy the nice environments, right now you cannot move much away from the ball. 

I got solid 90 fps with Index res 400% and using Ultra graphics with my RTX 3090, you do not need a RTX 2070 for this game - I'm sure a GTX 1060 will work too.

The game supports both native SteamVR and Oculus/Meta drivers, so users of Meta hmds will get optimal performance. The game works perfectly with both Valve Index and my Rift CV1.

For now this game is 7/10 to me, also considering the low price. 8/10 if we get some dynamic shadows to add more life and realism to the surroundings. And 9/10 if we can get 2 - 4 new awesome courses :-)

在写这篇评测前，我一直犹豫该给到sprb佳作还是神作。这无疑是一部非常优秀的作品，但在我心中离神作还有一些距离。
当我打完最后两条线之后，我坚定了自己的想法：sprb是一部毫无疑问的神作。
首先，尽量客观地、不剧透地说一下在我看来sprb的优缺点。
缺点：1.相较于其他galgame，选项极多，初见可能会不适应。这点对我来说无伤大雅，因为影响剧情的关键选项不多而且很明显。
2.由第一点导致的一个问题：游戏里有record，很多是由不同选项搭配达成的。record有250条，如果没有刻意收集的话直到通关完成度可能也不到一半，对追求gal全收集的人不是很友好。
3.价格有点高了……如果不是非常喜欢gal的玩家，建议等到打折时入手。只能说原价不亏，打折血赚。
优点：1.叙事节奏顺畅，对于日常的描写让人很舒服。个人感觉不太存在日常描写过于冗长无趣的问题。
2.音乐非常优秀！！！游戏里音乐出现的时机和场景都非常巧妙，让人很好代入，能更沉浸地体验这个夏日的故事。
3.角色塑造优秀，一共八条角色线，大部分线的文案都非常优秀，能很好地体现出角色的独特魅力。
4.除了gal常见的游戏模式，sprb增加了一些小游戏，并为小游戏专门做了岛乒线和岛可梦线，还是很有意思的（建议不要在推完全部女主线之前玩岛乒对决，可能会被剧透）
一些很难评的点？？？
1.剧情流程很长，据说sprb全部文本有200万字，如果完全不跳过对话的话，通关时长可以到70多小时。我只能说，对于自己真正喜欢的故事线，无论多长都会有玩下去的动力。
2.sprb名义上是sp的增强版，其实可以说就是同一款游戏了。前者相较于后者增加了四条故事线，只能说，见仁见智。
3.sprb的背景设定是日常，但在角色线中有时会有一些超自然的剧情，如果刚玩的话很容易一头雾水，直到玩完大部分剧情才能理解游戏里的一些伏笔与情节。
4.steam版本对于一些cg图进行了和谐，建议去网上找修复补丁。
关于我的感受（涉及剧透）
[spoiler]在真正打完sprb之前，我也以为夏日口袋的故事永远不会结束。真正打完之后，有一种怅然若失的感觉。游戏里前半程都是与大家嬉戏打闹的日常，平凡但温馨，而后半段才开始慢慢加刀子。key社的公式套的确实不错，大部分故事线都会给人不一样的感觉。但前面八条线几乎都遵循这些公式，玩到后面的那些自己不太喜欢的那些故事线就会感觉无聊。
但ALKA线和Pockets线改变了我的看法。（推完全部女主线之后，主页追加ALKA线；推完ALKA线后，主页追加Pockets线）
a线着重于羽未和白羽的日常，描写了一个平凡而温馨的故事。a线末尾的转折真的让我心头一颤，羽未做的一切仿佛都变成了徒劳，诅咒仍在继续。抱着一定要打出完美结局的信念，我一口气通关了p线。刚开始感觉主角不是羽依里有点不习惯，但到p线后期，一切顺利结束，所有人都有了自己的好结局，羽未也被识救到了一个父母相爱并且没有诅咒的时空，这样的结局真的让我非常满足。有人说sprb把sp的开放结局强行变成好结局了，少了很多意蕴。对我来说，过程中有多少刀子我都可以扛下去，但一个完美的he对我真的非常重要。[/spoiler]
最后，再说一句：
“唯有那份炫目，未曾忘却。”

Assassin's Creed Revelations es uno de los juegos más importantes de mi vida y es un producto que he disfrutado hasta en tres plataformas diferentes durante cientos de horas.

Aquí se concluye la historia de no solamente el mejor personaje de la franquicia, sino uno de los mejores de los videojuegos: Ezio Auditore. Tendremos la oportunidad de controlar a un Ezio que aunque envejecido, aún es tan letal como cuando era joven, pero con la diferencia de que ahora goza de la sabiduría que le ha brindado el tiempo. Además, de también poder controlar a otro mítico personaje de la franquicia, Altair y de esta manera podremos conocer un poco más de la trágica vida que tuvo el primer protagonista de Assassin's Creed. 

Revelations goza de una gran cantidad de aspectos positivos que lo diferencian bastante de las anteriores entregas de nuestro querido italiano, algunas de estas son: un interesante sistema de fabricación de bombas, un gancho que nos permitirá movernos mucho más rápido, un muy entretenido minijuego en donde debemos proteger nuestras bases de los ataques de los templarios, múltiples segmentos en donde debemos hacer cosas fuera de los habitual como luchar en carrozas, disfrazarnos y cantar en fiestas y tener encuentros románticos con nuestro futuro amor. Además, cabe resaltar que el juego contaba con un maravilloso modo multijugador que fue desataviado en 2022, como curiosidad: fui top 100 del mundo en el multijugador de PS3. 

Para finalizar puedo decir que Revelations es un videojuego que cuenta con un gran gameplay, una excelente historia, una espectacular banda sonora, un buen parkour y un gran desenlace para un épico personaje.

Se lo recomiendo a todos los que quieran conocer como era la verdadera esencia que tanto caracterizaba a Assassin's Creed.

[b]''How Not To Write a *Narrative*'' The Game[/b]
This game could serve as a case study in how Spec Ops: The Line would fail if it were written poorly. Both games try to tell a redemption story; one succeeds, the other completely misses the point.

You play as Nara, a former cult warrior who slaughtered innocents believing she was doing the right thing, just like Captain Walker. But unlike Spec Ops, Chorus starts after the regret. Nara already feels sorry, already seeks redemption, and stays in that same emotional state for the entire game. There’s no development, no transformation. She starts at “I regret everything” and ends at “I regret everything.”. That’s not a character arc; that’s emotional stasis.

What makes Spec Ops: The Line powerful isn’t that it’s some genius piece of writing, it’s not (it's genius on how it gamifies it). It simply does what any competent redemption story should: it shows the before and the after. It lets you experience the tragedy instead of just hearing about it. It follows the simplest form of the hero’s journey, nothing revolutionary.

Chorus, on the other hand, mistakes *explanation* for *storytelling*. Everything is fixed from the very first minute: Nara’s guilt, her motivation, even her redemption; all neatly stated, never earned. Nothing rises or falls in story; no event reshapes her or the world around her. The game just circles around the same confession over and over until the end.

[b]That’s why there’s no real narrative here, because a narrative moves. Chorus only describes. ''Nara did something wrong, and is regretting.''[/b]

Le jeu a un rythme un peu bizarre, la première moitié il y a beaucoup de phases avec du dialogues avec les PNJ des villes, et la deuxième moitié il y a beaucoup plus d'enchaînement de combats contre les robots. La direction artistique est magnifique, rappelant des films en stop-motion Tim Burton même si je pense il y a d'autres inspirations mais j'ai aucune référence. La boucle de gameplay en combat est addictive, même si j'avais l'impression que le résultat du dé est déjà décidé même avant le lancé. 
Il y a quelques trucs qui me chifonnent un peu : les hit box des décors et les murs invisibles absurdes. Des fois Paire se met à rester bloquer sur des bouts de planché car c'est un ou deux centimètres trop haut du coup je dois contourner d'un mètre pour descendre ? Ou sinon des fois quand je tire avec le lance-pierre pour casser les pots de pièces, le cailloux touche un mur invisible alors qu'il y en avait pas besoin ? Enfin bref pleins de trucs comme ça, aussi des artefacts visuels de combats qui restent même après la fin. 
L'écriture des dialogues, et le scénario en général et très basique, l'âge maximal du public visé ne doit pas être si élevé. Enfin, c'est surtout le ton des dialogues que je critique, surtout Pair la personnage principale qui fait des remarques un peu niaises avec l'humour médiocre des millenials. 
Le jeu parle beaucoup trop, et l'équilibre mal géré des phases avec les PNJ et des phases en combat nous le fait ressentir encore plus. Je ne vais pas parler de la musique car je n'y faisais pas si attention, elle ne se démarque pas trop.
Bref c'est un bon petit jeu sympa, mais il est loin d'être parfait. Et surtout, SURTOUT, devoir être connecté en ligne pour jouer à un jeu solo à cause du launcher EA app, il faut vraiment se remettre en question les mecs de chez EA.

[b]Knock On The Window[/b] - это весьма лайтовый хоррор с неплохой сюжетной линией и несколькими атмосферными моментами, которые, к сожалению, почти не развиваются. Из-за этого игре не удаётся удерживать напряжение и по-настоящему пугать. [u]Тем не менее, если вы любите простые бродилки без скримеров и "нервозных" эпизодов (лайт-хорроры)[/u], проект может зайти - тем более ценник у него вполне скромный.

История повествует о сотруднике фирмы, который получает предложение от босса: нужно выполнить кое-какую работу у него дома, а взамен - долгожданное повышение зарплаты. Герой приезжает в дом начальника, неторопливо осматривается и приступает к делу. Вскоре начинают происходить странности: то кто-то разобьёт стекло, то погаснет свет. В итоге протагонист решает убираться восвояси - но его похищают, и события внезапно сворачивают в неожиданную сторону.

Сюжет сам по себе не то чтобы оригинален, но я ценю [i]"второе дно"[/i]: это не просто игра про "проклятый дом". Вас водят по разным локациям, и пару раз история действительно делает приятные развороты (вряд ли шокирующие, но всё же). [i]Визуальный стиль симпатичный[/i]: да, модели персонажей иногда выглядят забавно, но в этом есть свой шарм.

Старт задаёт неплохой темп и чуть-чуть нагнетает саспенс: сначала рабочая рутина, потом дом с "непонятными событиями", затем - ещё более опасное место. В доме есть попытки напугать (пара скримеров), но в главном акте игра быстро "сдувается" и превращается в обычную, местами скучную бродилку.

[b]К чему я клоню - здесь попросту не страшно.[/b] Нет погонь, стелса, запоминающихся пазлов. Без спойлеров: учитывая сеттинг основного акта, тут прямо напрашиваются динамичные сцены - а их нет. Вы будете идти по локациям, находить ключи, открывать двери - и так до финала. Попадаются удачные шутки, но это лишь усиливает ощущение, что перед нами скорее триллер с лёгкой иронией и приятной подачей, чем хоррор.

[quote]Тем не менее, важно воспринимать игру такой, какая она есть. Если вы ищете мрачную атмосферу с крепкими скримерами - мимо. А вот если хочется ненапряжного триллера с необычной историей, симпатичным стилем и мягкой, но не страшной атмосферой - можно смело пробовать. Я бы сказал так: добавь разработчики больше динамики и хотя бы базовых "пугалок" - вышел бы вполне достойный ужастик (тематика располагает). В текущем виде - проект на любителя, но за небольшую цену и благодаря стилю шанс он определённо заслуживает.[/quote]

I originally bought this because it seemed fun from youtube videos, but there's so many little things that become annoying and suck the joy out of the game for me.

1. The optimization is awful. I know it's in early access, but how is this running worse than most of my other 3D games despite having way less in it? Even at the lowest settings it runs terribly and constantly drops frames.

2. The controls leave much to be desired. I feel like they're unintuitive and difficult to grasp, especially the constant switching between keyboard/mouse even in the same menu?? The whole "stack the loot" idea is fine and the way the items freeze if you get in your car fast enough regardless of if they're actively falling off is charming, but it's incredibly annoying to waste minutes fighting against the physics after I've done everything in my power to stack things neatly, only for a trophy or chest or any other random item to send the whole pile rocketing off at mach 5.

3. The visuals, I'm sorry to say, are unappealing. Making a visually pleasing character isn't even possible with the current editor, the lighting/hair models make the characters look like they have bald spots or are actively balding, actually the whole lighting engine needs some serious work, and the developer's insistence on adding more cosmetics instead of fixing the underlying issues doesn't bode well.

And finally:

4. The game play. This isn't a storage simulator, this is a driving simulator that happens to have storage hunting as a side objective. I don't know whether this is some ill-advised attempt at realism, but it takes SO LONG to get from one end of the map to the other, especially since the game more or less expects you to do that from the start! There's even a "scenic" aspect to the driving, but again, the visuals really aren't appealing enough for that to score points for me.

Seriously, the game play loot is just Drive - Sign up for an auction - Drive - Attempt to win the auction - Drive to the next one if lost but if you win, struggle with physics - Drive to the pawnshop - Sell everything in under 10s - Drive AGAIN.

It gets even worse with the lockpicking and rare/unique/expertise mechanics, because driving the whole map for 1 item isn't appealing in the least.

In short, it's a mess. It'd at least be tolerable if it ran well, but it really, really doesn't.

Loading the vehicle, Tetris-style, is an essential part of the game. Time-wise, it's actually the longest part, so I expect this part to work well.

Unfortunately, this is the most buggy and worst part of the game.

For example, if you lay a carpet flat on the floor of the truck and place other objects on top of it, you'd think this wouldn't be a problem. But instead, the objects placed on it bounce and wobble around because they glitch into the carpet's texture and are pushed away.

Another example: If you carefully place an object in a gap between two cabinets or other objects, the box or ball or whatever glitch into the cabinets and kick them apart, the objects you placed on top of the cabinet also start to bounce and may even glitch into other objects, and in the end, everything is catapulted out of the truck.

Every time you put something in the truck, you run the risk of provoking illogical reactions, and all your work will have been in vain.

Something that was initially absolutely fun, namely storing things efficiently and maybe even paying some attention to aesthetics, turns into frustration.

Buying the expensive 45k truck, something I've been looking forward to for a long time, but which requires an enormous amount of work. Being able to earn 45k and spare it for the truck, and reach reputation level 30 in the western part of the city, turns into a disappointment. Because of the problems mentioned, the flatbad with the walls, which would normally be a pro for storage, is now more of a con. Where previously objects could protrude from the sides of the truck, there are now walls. This doesn't only have disadvantages, but without glitches, it would have been a huge relief.

The game has even more problems, but they're not that serious. However, until the glitchy problem is resolved so that I can rely on my common sense and the laws of physics when loading items into my truck, I cannot give the game a positive rating, EA or not.

[h2]Предисловие[/h2]

We Were Here Too — не просто кооперативная головоломка, а настоящий тест на взаимопонимание и доверие. Здесь нет привычных подсказок, карты или «режима помощи». Есть только ты, твой напарник и рация, через которую вы должны понимать друг друга почти без слов. Это игра не про реакцию, а про коммуникацию — и именно в этом её уникальность.

[h2]Графика и звук[/h2]

• Графика. Несмотря на то, что проект небольшой и не претендует на уровень AAA, визуальная составляющая отлично передаёт атмосферу заброшенного замка. Холодные каменные стены, тусклое освещение, снег за окнами — всё работает на создание чувства изоляции и лёгкой тревоги.
• Звук. Звуковое оформление — ключ к погружению. Скрип полов, гулкие шаги и отдалённые шорохи создают ощущение присутствия «чего-то рядом». Музыки почти нет — и именно это усиливает напряжение. Рация звучит с лёгкими помехами, что добавляет реализма и заставляет вслушиваться в каждое слово партнёра.

[h2]Механики[/h2]

• Кооперативная связь. Вся суть игры — в диалоге. Один игрок оказывается в одной части замка, другой — в другой. Каждый видит свою часть головоломки, и решить её можно только вместе, делясь информацией.
• Пазлы. Головоломки разнообразные: символы, механизмы, рычаги, лабиринты и даже сцены с лёгким таймингом. Некоторые требуют логики, другие — хорошего описания и терпения.
• Коммуникация. Это не просто инструмент — это основная механика. Если вы не умеете слушать и объяснять, игра быстро напомнит об этом :)
• Темп. Игра движется неспешно, но именно в этом её шарм: не спешишь, а разбираешься, рассуждаешь, споришь, смеёшься и радуешься каждой разгадке.

[h2]Сюжетка[/h2]

• История здесь скорее фоном, но интересным. Вы — исследователи, оказавшиеся в замке, полном загадок. Постепенно из фрагментов дневников и деталей окружения складывается мрачная история о жертве и доверии.
• Она не подаётся в лоб — её нужно замечать: надписи на стенах, странные символы, архитектура — всё намекает, что замок хранит не просто тайну, а последствия чьего-то выбора.
• В итоге сюжет не даёт прямых ответов, но оставляет приятное послевкусие загадки.

[h2]Атмосфера[/h2]

• Атмосфера — главная сила игры. Замок будто живёт своей жизнью: ты не видишь врагов, но чувствуешь, что кто-то наблюдает.
• Постоянная отдалённость от напарника рождает интересное чувство одиночества и тревоги. Иногда даже простое «слышишь меня?» через рацию звучит как спасение.
• После прохождения остаётся ощущение, будто вы с другом действительно пережили нечто вместе — не просто поиграли, а прошли испытание на взаимопонимание.

[h2]Плюсы и минусы[/h2]

[b]Плюсы:[/b]
• Уникальная кооперативная концепция — решать загадки через слова.
• Отличная атмосфера и саунддизайн.
• Приятные визуальные детали и продуманные головоломки.
• Отличный способ укрепить дружбу или... проверить её :)

[b]Минусы:[/b]
• Игра короткая (2–3 часа).
• Без напарника играть невозможно — строго кооператив.
• Некоторые загадки требуют слишком точного описания и могут вызывать лёгкое раздражение, если вы не на одной волне.

[h2]Так а что по итогу?[/h2]

We Were Here Too — это не просто набор головоломок, а опыт общения и доверия. Она идеально подходит для тех, кто любит совместно решать задачи и ценит атмосферу загадочности.
Не для тех, кто ищет экшен — но для тех, кто хочет вдумчивого приключения вдвоём.

Оценка: твёрдая 8/10.

I played my first Dragon Quest game on an emulator in Class 6. I never finished it, but I never forgot it either. Dragon Quest XI felt like finally returning to a story I left incomplete a long time ago, and surprisingly, it still felt warm and familiar.

Some things stand out clearly:

• The world is peaceful, colourful and alive. It does not rush you. It lets you explore and breathe.
• The turn based combat is simple and satisfying. Boss fights can be frustrating at times, but every win feels earned.
• The story starts small and slowly grows into something emotional, heartfelt and surprisingly heavy.
• Characters feel genuine and stay with you long after the game ends.
• Yuji Horii’s design feels timeless. It proves that a JRPG can be traditional and still feel magical.
• Akira Toriyama’s art direction gives everything a comforting charm that modern games rarely try to capture.

For players who enjoyed Expedition 33 or anyone curious about the roots of the JRPG genre, this is a perfect place to start. Dragon Quest XI is not just a reminder of classic gaming, it is a reminder of childhood and the kind of stories that stay with you quietly for years.

Finishing this game felt like closing a chapter I abandoned as a kid. It was worth it.

I see a fair number of negative reviews where people were initially frustrated by the controls and gave up even though they liked the nature of the game. Retired competitive street fighter player and fighting game fanatic here; I've played almost every fighting game out there at some point in my life and it's rare that I find a fighter that I enjoy enough to play more than 3-4 hours. The first thing I do whenever I try a new fighting game is immediately go into training mode and try out all the characters, if I find one I like I'll learn a couple of combos and then jump online and play a few games casually. That's usually where it ends for me, except for on those rare occasions where I had so much fun that I'm laying in bed and replaying the matches in my head while thinking to myself "I really should've done this when he did that, I really want to see if I can get this to connect to that, or I wonder if I can dodge that and do this." Well, Rebirth of souls was like for me. 

The audio, the visuals, and the game play are overflowing with style; Every fight feels like an episode of the anime as flashy transformations and cinematic supers are an integral part of the game play loop - which brings me to my next point, the game play. Each game has 2-3 "acts" depending on the characters you choose and how you play. 
Act 1: Both characters are in base form, the pacing is casual, you're playing footsies, building special meter, and patiently awaiting your evolution.
Act 2: Your evolution is ready and you activate bankai, after a brief cinematic transformation you're now in a powered up state with most characters gaining access to a completely different move set, ability, or gimmick to utilize during the remainder of the battle. The pacing is faster now and the stakes are higher.
Act 3: If the battle goes on long enough both players will eventually enter into sublimation, which is the final act. In sublimation each character gains access to their most powerful cinematic super (kikon move), able to take more lives from the opponent than usual. it essentially turns the game into a winner takes all scenario where the next player to land their kikon wins.

One of the really unique mechanics at play in Rebirth of souls is that the goal is to reduce the number of your opponents lives to 0 by landing kikon moves, every character has 2-3 kikon moves that change depending on what state they are in (base, transformed, or sublimation) and each subsequent move takes more lives if you land it. For the characters that only have 2 moves they are usually able to power up their second move to take more lives with an in battle gimmick. Kikon moves can be blocked or dodged if the intended target is above 15% health. After 15 percent the kikon move is guaranteed to hit if you land it; However, you can take 1 extra life from your opponent if you decide reduce their health bar to 0. So it becomes an extra layer of strategy, do you want to take what you can now or hold out for the possibility of more later.

While there are so many things I can praise this game for, There is one glaring issue that seems to be the fate of every anime fighter, and that is this: That some characters are simply better than others. Seriously, Over 30 characters on the roster at launch and in over 80 hours of game play I've only ever consistently played against the same 6 characters. Ichigo, Aizen, Unohana, Yoruichi, Ulquiorra, and more recently Ichibe. Why? Because they have better gimmicks, stronger attack power, greater combo potential, a more diverse variety of tools utilize, an insta-kill move, the ability to take extra lives when using kikon moves, the ability to regenerate health, and even the ability to resurrect after defeat (Aizen can ressurrect twice in one match). If your goal is to win games then these characters are no brainers. If you decide to play a character other than the big 6 then be prepared to be at a significant disadvantage and be prepared to have to work much harder to secure wins. 

I'm an above average player but I lose 70 percent of my matches because I play lower tier characters, none the less, I enjoy the challenge of overcoming adversity - clearly I'm having fun so I'm going to recommend this game, it's a total gem and I pray it doesn't slip into obscurity after the first round of dlc (as is also the fate of every anime fighter.)

[b]🔍概要[/b]
このゲームでは、千年に一度の純陽霊根をもつ男修・林凡になって、宗門の小姐姐たちとの“千千劫”を乗り越えつつ、修仙の頂を目指すという設定や。RPG・シミュレーション・アドベンチャー要素をミックスしてて、日常＋選択のある物語を進めるタイプの作品や。

[b]👍良かったところ[/b]
*世界観とキャラクター設定が「中華風修仙＋エロティック」っていう強めの個性を持っとる。
*日本語インターフェース・字幕対応など、多言語サポートもちゃんと入っとるのは評価できるで。 
*値段もそこそこ手が出しやすく、“軽く遊びたい”ユーザーには選びやすい。

[b]👎気になるところ[/b]
-ボリュームとしては「本格的な作り込み」ってより“短め／ライト”な体験という印象。がっつり遊びたい人には物足りない可能性あり。
-プレイヤー数や人気の推移を見てると、発売直後のピークからかなり落ちてきとる。長く遊びたいならその点も気にしたほうがええ。 
-内容が好みに強く左右されるタイプ。エロ要素とか修仙ファンタジーが苦手な人には合わんかもしれへん。

[b]🔮総合まとめ[/b]
「ちょっと変わったテーマで遊びたい」「キャラクターの掛け合いやシナリオ重視したい」という人にはおすすめや。

This is the best game in the FlatOut series. It brings improved graphics, additional characters, tougher racing, a more active community workshop, and Steam achievements. All welcome upgrades.

I'd been meaning to get around to playing this one, and I was itching for some racing, so I finally bought it. I didn't realize it was more or less an enhanced version of FlatOut 2—and honestly, that's fine by me. It's just the better version of that game. I don't have high expectations for any FlatOut title after this one based on reviews alone, so I can say with confidence: this is the best one.

The campaign (FlatOut) mode has been revamped and feels more interesting right away. I'm enjoying it so far, and the interface is a lot cleaner. That said, I'm still not a fan of derby mode. In fact, I like it even less here. It's more about dealing damage than staying alive, which is frustrating when AI opponents seem to single you out and chase you around the map sometimes. The derby maps are nice, but I would probably play the first FlatOut for the ideal derby experience.

I'm about three derby cups in, and most of the cars are still locked. I wish all cars were available for purchase from the start, so you could buy them once you'd earned enough credits. My starter car is falling behind the pack, and while I'd like to upgrade to a different car, the one I want is locked. That progression system feels a bit restrictive.

After seeing there were new characters, I looked them up on the wiki to learn more. This led to me also reading about the original characters. Turns out their driving styles actually reflect their personalities and backstories. No wonder Ray Carter and Frank Malcov are such terrible drivers. One's carefree, the other's recovering from an injury. Knowing that made me appreciate the thought that went into these characters a lot more than I did previously. The character art is great too.

FlatOut has always been my favorite racing series since I was kid, and if you're looking to try it, this is the one to get.

After getting bored of Dwarf Fortress, and RimWorld, I decided this might be a fun stop-gap while building up the encouragement to jump back into either. Unfortunately after mastering bronze armor/weapon production this game is nothing but a snooze fest. The raids are easy to beat and the most infuriating aspect is seeing a skilled worker die and having to wait hours until someone else is semi-competent to be able to accomplish something in the first try. 

Things I wish it had:
Some way to interact with the world map or do something once you've built a self-sufficient colony. send raiders, build ships to cross oceans, start new settlments, etc.

Focus on difficulty to actually encourage arcane/iron armor exploitation, less pointless micro-management more fun, whether it's a 4X approach, dungeon crawler, or tower defense, find something that is an expansive and far-reaching goal for people to want to achieve. Take advantage of the current art style and incorporate the difficulty from Hero's Hour or Rise to Ruins... do something. In it's current state it's nothing more than dwarf fortress knock-off with an identity crisis. 

Things that are bad:
It took me about 8 hours to figure out that clicking on the object name in the room management takes you to the auto-complete rules. While the system works almost exactly like Dwarf Fortress, its somewhat pointless to micro-manage. The game seems to be focusing on combat/arcane/exploration, why have to micro-manage farming, cooking, armor production when the end result is no different? Just let us plop down a room and let it automatically make anything we need if the resources exist... set a global stockpile limit and priority and just let them figure it out. 

Animal husbandry is useless. Wool sucks more than plant fibers anyways, just kill everything and move on. Fishing and farming is more than adequate to sustain at least 30 people throughout the year. 

Things that are boring:
World exploration is abysmally slow and serves zero challenge. It took 90% of my playthrough to tunnel down to the bottom of the world while watching builders walk up and down the 100 or so ladders for a single piece of wood to build the next ladders. There is nothing stopping you from just noob tubing straight to the core and letting your dudes scale the walls back up. At least I tried to build ladders.... Still, once the treasures beneath are un-earthed, there is literally nothing left to do.

Things that I liked:
You have complete freedom to terraform to your heart's content, (Dwarf Fortress is utterly infuriating in this regard)

...Though that last point is a bit of a nitpick.

9.5/10

If you liked the first iteration of Hylics, then you'll love this sequel. Hylics 2 is the perfect improvement: better combat, more exploration and a wonderful soundtrack, with the same exact themes, characters and atmosphere.

The clay and stopmotion usage is impeccable, I have no complaints visually, the designs are surreal, nightmare-ish and very memorable. It's a colorful game, yet it does not feel joyful nor bright, it feels eerie and mischievous, not scary, sometimes even lovely, but always in a very unusual way.

Straightforward progression, a few fun puzzles but mostly easy to navigate, even in its most confusing segments. Albeit the world building is interesting enough, everything is too abstract to extract a profound meaning. Of course you can interpret it if you want to, and I perceive some elements as symbolism, eg the use of technology, but the approach here doesn't seem to create a meaningful narrative.

100% recommended.

Maybe it’s because I’m more into story-driven or psychological horror, and this one leans more toward “run or die between guts and worms.”

The atmosphere is well done, I’ll give it that: dark, oppressive, with sound design that makes you look over your shoulder even when you know you’re alone. But after a while, I felt more uncomfortable than entertained. It didn’t hook me, didn’t make me want to keep going — and that’s coming from someone who usually gives weird indie games a fair shot.
Visually, it has its style: minimalist, sickly, with an atmosphere that gets under your skin — literally. But honestly, after a few hallways and worms, I thought, “okay, I get the idea.”

In short, it’s not a bad game, it’s just not for me. If you enjoy suffering and feeling like you’ve got a larva in your arm while trying to survive with three bullets, this one’s for you. As for me, I’m out.

I give it a 4/10 for originality, plus a symbolic bonus for making me say, “well, that was weird,” while uninstalling.

BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend, developed by Arc System Works and published by H2 Interactive Co., Ltd., stands as one of the most polished and content-rich entries in the acclaimed BlazBlue franchise. As a refined version of the original Chronophantasma, it brings together everything the series is known for—complex mechanics, dazzling anime-style presentation, and an ambitious narrative that blends science fiction, fantasy, and existential drama. This entry continues Arc System Works’ tradition of pushing the boundaries of 2D fighting games, offering a gameplay experience that is as mechanically demanding as it is visually striking. It’s a title that caters primarily to dedicated fans of the genre, but its depth and style make it one of the most distinctive fighting games on Steam.

At its core, Chronophantasma Extend maintains the intricate combat system that defines the BlazBlue series while introducing refinements that make it more dynamic and rewarding. The game’s mechanics revolve around a delicate balance of offense, defense, and resource management. Each character possesses a unique Drive ability—a personal mechanic that sets them apart from the rest of the roster—and mastering these Drives is essential to success. The introduction of new systems such as Overdrive and Crush Trigger gives battles even greater strategic variety. Overdrive temporarily enhances a character’s abilities, allowing for devastating combos and comeback opportunities, while the Crush Trigger mechanic enables guard-breaking attacks that punish overly defensive play. Together, these additions make combat feel more fluid, aggressive, and unpredictable. The result is a fighting experience that rewards not just execution but also tactical awareness and adaptability.

The roster in Chronophantasma Extend is impressively large, offering over twenty-eight playable characters, each with distinct fighting styles, aesthetics, and mechanics. This diversity ensures that players can find a character that fits their preferred playstyle, whether it be the balanced offense of Ragna, the zoner precision of Nu-13, or the technical command of Kokonoe. Returning fighters have been fine-tuned for better balance, while newcomers such as Celica A. Mercury and Lambda-11 bring fresh options to the meta. The variety extends beyond simple aesthetics—every character feels like a new learning experience, with combo structures and timing windows that differ dramatically from one another. The game’s robust training and tutorial modes provide an excellent introduction to its layered mechanics, easing newcomers into its complexity while offering advanced challenges for veterans to refine their skills.

Visually, the game continues to uphold Arc System Works’ reputation for stunning 2D artistry. The hand-drawn character sprites are vibrant and fluid, animated with incredible detail and personality. Each movement, from basic attacks to elaborate super moves, is accompanied by dynamic camera shifts and explosive particle effects that make battles feel cinematic without losing clarity. The stages are equally detailed, ranging from futuristic cityscapes to mythical battlefields, all rendered with rich backgrounds that breathe life into the world. The musical score, composed by Daisuke Ishiwatari, is a highlight—an energetic fusion of rock, orchestral, and electronic elements that perfectly matches the intensity of combat. The English and Japanese voice acting are equally strong, lending emotional weight to both the story and the in-battle dialogue.

Where the game truly differentiates itself from other fighters is in its story mode. BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend delivers a massive narrative experience, one that could easily rival a full-fledged visual novel in length and complexity. It continues the saga of the Azure Grimoire and the ongoing struggle between Ragna the Bloodedge, the Librarium, and a host of intertwined characters, each with their own motives and secrets. The narrative is filled with dramatic twists, philosophical undertones, and an impressive amount of world-building. However, the storytelling can be dense and overwhelming, especially for newcomers who haven’t followed the series since its inception. The plot references past events and characters frequently, and without prior context, it’s easy to get lost in its labyrinthine structure. Still, for those invested in BlazBlue’s lore, the story mode is a rewarding continuation, offering new revelations and emotional payoffs for long-time fans.

In terms of content, Chronophantasma Extend excels at giving players value. Beyond the extensive story mode, there are multiple single-player and multiplayer options, including Arcade, Versus, Score Attack, and Challenge modes. The game’s online play remains solid, with relatively stable netcode that allows for competitive matches without excessive lag. The customization options, unlockable artwork, and alternate costumes give players more incentive to continue playing beyond the main modes. For those who enjoy testing their limits, the Challenge mode offers intricate combo trials that demand precision and creativity, further deepening the game’s replayability.

That said, the game isn’t without its weaknesses. The complexity that makes Chronophantasma Extend so satisfying for hardcore players can be intimidating for newcomers. Even with tutorials, the game’s layered systems, resource meters, and combo timings take considerable time to master. The steep learning curve might discourage casual players looking for quick gratification. The story, while ambitious, can feel overly verbose and convoluted, often bogged down by long stretches of dialogue that disrupt the pacing. Additionally, while the PC version runs smoothly for most players, it lacks some of the optimization polish and modern features found in more recent Arc System Works titles.

Despite these minor flaws, BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend stands as a superbly crafted fighting game that perfectly captures the essence of what makes the genre exciting. It combines technical precision with dramatic flair, balancing intense mechanical depth with a bold, stylized presentation. The game’s visual artistry, expansive content, and finely tuned combat system make it one of the most complete and rewarding 2D fighters available on Steam. For veterans of the BlazBlue series, it represents a high point in the saga; for newcomers willing to invest the time to learn its intricacies, it offers one of the most satisfying and visually stunning experiences the genre has to offer. It’s a game that celebrates both artistry and mastery, standing as a testament to Arc System Works’ dedication to elevating the craft of fighting games.

Rating: 9/10

[h1] 苍翼默示录：刻之幻影—扩展版 [/h1]
[h1] ——四部曲之第三部 [/h1]
[b] （别称：蔚蓝光辉/BBCP EX） [/b]

[h3] 特点总结 [/h3]
+世界观全面铺开，更成熟的POV群像叙事
+剧情长度量大管饱
+华丽的战斗画面
+玩法迥异的角色再度增加

[h3] 游玩时长 [/h3]
·故事模式+街机模式超30小时剧情流程
·多种单人/多人对战模式

[h3] 介绍 [/h3]
《苍翼默示录》是老牌FTG制作组Arc System Works开发的日本超人气格斗游戏系列，本作《刻之幻影》（简称BBCP）是正传四部曲的第三部作品，故事紧接前两作，想要理清剧情至少还要入手系列第二作《连续变换》（即BBCS）。

本作作为系列第三部，可选角色再次扩充，达到了二十多人，对战系统改进主要是采用了『OverDrive』系统，类似《拳皇》的爆气，能够使用更加炫酷的强化招式。

众所周知作为“Galgame才是本体”的《苍翼》系列，本作《BBCP》在剧情上的执念更加疯狂，即使改掉解锁剧情需反复游玩的繁琐设定，单纯阅读主线+扩展板各种分支情节就达到了恐怖的15小时！

本作《刻之幻影》剧本承接前两作，此次不再围绕抽象的概念展开叙述，而是更骗常规的日漫热血战斗番既视感，用大量故弄玄虚的名词堆设定的臭毛病有所收敛，更本分地把事情讲明白，叙事不再装逼观感立即提升。

本作《BBCP》由三条故事线交错推进剧情：
『六英雄篇』终于将整个故事开篇之前的历史背景设定进行了补完…
『第七机关篇』讲述了重要角色『九重』及其所在组织『第七机关』的相关情节…
『刻之幻影篇』作为主线则是主角团与大BOSS『帝』分属的正邪阵营全面开战的故事…

三代众多新角色闪亮登场，超级可爱的新女主老婆们萌爆了，一定又双叒叕会成为玩家们永远喜欢的唯一真爱！
爆多的角色使游戏放弃了逐个演绎剧情线的单向叙述手法，转而以POV视角聚焦整体群像，格局更显宏大，最终决战阶段主角团各展不同威风，游戏甚至给1V1的格斗玩法加了一段特殊机制的BOSS战！剧本收尾高潮迭起、燃出天际！

可惜故事又没讲完，给下一作留了坑～

此外，本作搞笑剧场也保持着令人捧腹的一罐水准，毕竟那可是“银桑”的吐槽哇。

除了『故事模式』外，『街机模式』也有剧情，二者相加会超过30小时流程，不过街机剧情中一部分是对本篇的简略总结，一部分是前作剧情的介绍，只有小部分是主线剧情的补充以及对后续发展的关联。

Tormented Souls 2 is a step up from its predecessor in every way for me. Tormented Souls 1 was a love letter from passionate fans of the survival horror genre. This game takes that love and refines it. As a sequel, Tormented Souls 2 doesn't change the formula that is in no need of fixing. It takes what the already good first game did—namely, the atmosphere, the feeling of isolation, and the fun loop of a survival horror game—and makes it even better.

The gameplay feels smoother than ever, dare I say even better than some of the other G.O.A.T.s of the genre. Tank controls have never felt more natural to me than in this game. It achieves this by letting you move more often, which you usually couldn't do in these kinds of games. Want to move while reloading? You can. Want to dodge before you get hit? Yes, you can. It blends tank controls with modern, expected responsiveness almost perfectly.

The music is so haunting yet beautiful. You know what to expect from the music in a survival horror game: from tracks of anxiety to beautiful atmospheric music you could even imagine yourself listening to while falling asleep. Music is subjective, but I dare say calling this music objectively well-performed is a fair thing to say.

I have not been far in the story yet, as you can see in my hours, but the story so far has been good enough to get me into it. I'm immersed enough that I don’t need a second tab of videos open to keep my brain on dopamine. The game itself keeps me more entertained than many games have this year. The voice acting has been improved by quite a lot. The first game had voice acting, but it had both the charming "bad" voice acting and probably little direction. From the first cutscene, you'll know this game has voice actors who know what they are doing, with direction given by a team that has more experience. In return, they deliver us a better video game.

The game is very, very fairly priced. In a modern world where games make you feel like you robbed yourself after buying them, this game makes me feel like I got it from a friend for half the original price, in my opinion.

In summary: If you like this genre or are even curious to explore it, this game is certainly worth both your time and money.

Tribal Hunter is an above-average metroidvania that uses a unique weight gain/loss mechanic to both change character gameplay and add risks (e.g., fail conditions). The player must help the main character, Munch, to manage his weight in order to progress through the game and avoid game overs. Gaining weight enables certain moves and increases per-hit damage, but also reduces hit rate (punch speed) and makes him more vulnerable to damage from specific enemy attacks. He can also become too big to pass through some tunnels. Munch has an upper limit for how hefty he can get before he pops and it's game over. Naturally, there are many enemies trying to make him gain weight. It's up to the player to choose what weight is appropriate and safe for the situation. There are also talent trees to make Munch stronger and enhance his abilities.

I think the game really opens up after the slime caves (level 2 IIRC) and the player has more of Munch's abilities at hand, so stick with it! There are many different mini-bosses to conquer and a wide variety of enemies. Sometimes feeding enemies will lead to good things. It's also worth exploring off the beaten path to find items to increase Munch's weight gain limit. You might just discover a helpful NPC in some far off place, too.

The setting is pretty fun, being an island paradise with a variety of biomes to explore. Enjoying food alone or with friends is a big theme. It really celebrates food and eating. I must also compliment the art style because it fits the game perfectly. And the sense of humor—I love it! There's great dialogue and visual gags galore. Be sure to talk to every NPC you can. There are NPCs that help Munch with traveling around the island; try it when he's really fat!

My only criticism about the game is that when you reach some of the final levels, it becomes necessary to stop and digest food (losing weight) so often that it slows down the gameplay. The player can perform this in a fast or slow way, but even choosing to sacrifice extra exp by using the quick way will find you essentially stopping everything over and over to meditate several seconds before proceeding to the next room. It's not a deal breaker by any means, just something I noticed.

At a glance, it would be easy for someone to dismiss this as an inflation/weight gain fetish game and move on, but you would really be missing out on a good time. The way I see it, the developer took their interest and made it into a great game that everybody can enjoy. Some just might enjoy it on another level, and I'm happy for them too ;)

Give it a chance!

Before I start this review, I want to make this clear: World of Final Fantasy Maxima is a fantastic game. The game itself is wonderful. If you’re into monster‑taming games (like Pokémon or Digimon) and you’ve got a long history with Final Fantasy, then this is a game for you. It oozes charm. The stacking system is clever, and the callbacks are fun. The Maxima upgrade fixes a lot of issues from the original release and adds strong post‑game content. And even though the Steam store page doesn't show it, the game does have full online functionality with PvP and trading still available. I haven't tested those since the game has an extremely low player base, but overall, I think it's a very good game.

Why am I giving it a negative review? Well, to put it simply: the port is atrocious. The port has so many issues that I’m honestly surprised this game is still allowed to be sold here on Steam. The performance is terrible across the board. The game is completely locked at 30 FPS, and if you try to unlock the framerate, the game’s logic collapses. But that’s not even the biggest issue here. The BIGGEST issue is that it literally won’t launch... like, at all!!!! You have to go out of your way to find fan fixes, patch the game’s files manually, go to the folder, and then run it directly as admin. Out of my entire Steam library, this is the only title that does that. And that’s just scratching the surface. The whole port feels super neglected.

Then there’s the missing content issue. To be fair, you do get the full main game, the Maxima post‑game, the Creature Pack DLC, Day One/pre‑order bonuses, and even the limited Balthier Champion Medal. So, about 99% of the content is here. But we’re missing a few things that should’ve been here in the first place:
[list]
[*] Sora’s Champion Medal: completely gone, not even in the files. No explanation why.  
[*] Cactuar Johnny and Crimson Armor Mirages: these ones are odd. They exist in the game’s files, and they’re available on every other platform... but not on Steam? My guess is that because it was upgraded directly from the original to Maxima, the tickets that let you fight them were accidentally left out. And since the data is already in the game’s files, it feels more like an oversight than an intentional choice. I’m surprised no one talks about it, and it’s surprising that after all these years it still hasn’t been fixed.
[/list]
On top of all that, progress tracking in this port is weirdly inconsistent, and it seems this issue doesn’t exist in any other version. Example: the cutscene “[i]Maduin, Is That You?[/i]” never appeared in Theater Mode for me, even though I’d already seen the cutscene and unlocked the Maduin Memento. Another example is that my [i]Who’s Who[/i] journal sat at 99% for a while until I backed out and re‑entered the menu, at which point it magically flipped to 100%. I know this is small stuff, but it makes the whole system feel janky and unpolished.

Despite all of these issues, I genuinely love this game. I just can’t recommend this version with good conscience. If you want to play it, grab it on literally any other platform (just not PSVita).
[h3]Summary[/h3]
The port is just terrible (needs fan fixes just to boot) and some content is missing (Sora, Cactuar Johnny, Crimson Armor). Two of those omissions seem accidental, but they’ve been ignored for years. Plus, this version has bugs that don’t show up in any other version.

I’d happily flip this to “Recommended” if Square Enix ever patched it. A small update to fix the launch issues and re‑enable the missing content would make it much better. Doing so would also make the game fully playable on Steam Deck (which honestly feels like the perfect home for a game like this), and would almost certainly bring in new players.

[h1] Introdução [/h1]
Inacreditável. Impostor Factory conseguiu ser tão incrível quanto os jogos antecessores, mantendo a essência da série, enriquecendo ainda mais, dando mais sentido, mais vida e mais história a To The Moon Series.

Assim como os jogos anteriores, Impostor Factory traz uma vasta gama de sentimentos durante a gameplay, e acho que é isso que torna esses jogos da Freebird tão especiais, trazem muitos sentimentos a tona, não é exagero chamar esse jogo de obra de arte.

[h1] História [/h1]
Assim como os outros jogos da série, o foco do jogo é na narrativa da história, e que história...

É difícil não zerar em um dia, porque você fica muito imerso na história do game. Os personagens são muito carismáticos, muito bem desenvolvidos. Cada ambiente da história é muito bem construído, cada detalhe é bem polido.

Você ri, fica aflito, sente tristeza, estranheza, fica apreensivo, sente alegria, acha momentos fofos.

Impostor Factory te deixa em um mar vasto de sentimentos, e enquanto você navega nesse mesmo mar, você começa a refletir até mesmo sobre situações, momentos e memórias da sua própria vida.

A história desse jogo é um prato bem cheio de vários nutrientes bonitos!

Nesse jogo em específico, tem um ponto de vista diferente, não quero dar spoiler, mas é algo mais diferente dos anteriores, e isso torna a franquia mais especial, porque sai daquela mesma forma, eles apostaram em um ponto de vista diferente no jogo e ficou incrível.

Na gameplay é um pouco mais simples, mas não é enjoativo.

Nesse não tem puzzles igual os outros da franquia(Tirando A Bird Story), então é mais andar e fazer os diálogos.

Aqui é onde tem boa parte da beleza que engloba Finding Paradise.

A trilha sonora é arte pura, é lindo como as musicas se comunicam com as cenas, dão mais vida aos locais e transmitem o sentimento certo para cada momento do jogo.

This is a really great game for those who like intricate and complex turn based games. The main problem is that it starts slow, and I think a lot of people might get through a few missions and think "this is it? just shoot, wait for cooldown, repeat?" it's a slog at first, but it absolutely blossoms out about a third of the way through and remains on an upward trajectory from then on. If you like turn based games or WH40k games, this is absolutely a must, it's one of the actually good ones, as opposed to all the crap out there.
     The only problem I have with it, beyond the obnoxious 'tomb awakening' percentage mechanic, where the entire tomb awakens a little with each mission and you're forced to contend with the dumbass mechanic which causes you to rush and miss a lot of stuff, is that certain characters are not believable as Adeptus Mechanicus. Mainly Khepra, the leader of your skitarii, who constantly and incessantly complains about the loss of her soldiers. This is not how the AM works, if the goal is achieved and has been valued as helpful, then the soldiers are willingly spent, with no thought toward their wellbeing beyond the fact that they should not simply be wasted. I think the devs felt they needed a more 'human' character to be the voice of empathy for whatever reason, despite this being absolutely NOT what the AM act like in WH40K. To the devs: remember, this is a universe that has already been made, and people enjoy it for what it is, we don't need you adding this stuff. She would have long ago been lobotomized and servitorized, rather than becoming the leader of soldiers. But this aside, and ignoring the awful tomb awakening mechanic (Which can be fixed by altering your save game file), there really isnt much out there at this game's level, in terms of WH40k games.

Cute and interesting system for a puzzle game, which also presents a nice challenge. LOK Digital is an adaptation of LOK, a puzzle book that follows the same ruleset.

What's interesting about these two games is that they live in very different mediums (paper- and video-), and they know this perfectly well. LOK's main mechanics work fine in both mediums, but some of them wouldn't translate well to one or the other, so rather than being a direct adaptation of the book's puzzles and mechanics, the game reinvents parts of itself for the screen, showing some new elements you hadn't seen before, dropping a couple that maybe wouldn't have made as much sense. Secrets (yes, secrets!) are reexamined and reworked. This really isn't a case of "the book is better/worse than the movie"; they're both their own engaging thing, and if you enjoy one, I would encourage you to experience both. But more importantly, I think it speaks to the designer's understanding of, and respect for the mediums they're working with.

Also I'm hijacking this video game review to let you know that Letibus Design have a few more (paper) games to wow you with, like Abdec or Workworkwork. I've always been a video game player first and foremost, but these were some of the gems that opened my eyes to what incredible stuff paper puzzles can provide, which can't quite be translated to the instant-feedback medium of video games. If you like puzzle games of all kinds you seriously owe it to yourself to look into those.

(Okay I realize I hijacked this video a little too much and have mostly been talking about videogames vs papergames, but to stay on-topic: the game is really good!!! I love these mechanics, there are some very interesting eureka moments, I wanna pinch the lokites' little cheeks. All around good stuff)

The Game and the Heist
The dimly lit room was a stark contrast to the vibrant chaos that flickered across the screen. Danny’s obsession with “Heist Master 3D” had started as a harmless diversion. The game was celebrated for its meticulous attention to detail, offering players an exhilarating simulation of bank robberies complete with blueprints, guard routines, and escape routes. Danny had spent countless hours perfecting his strategy, basking in the simulated glory of a flawlessly executed job. But what had once been a harmless pastime had begun to morph into something more sinister.

In the dingy apartment that served as his command center, Danny’s fingers danced over the keyboard, mimicking the exact sequences needed to bypass security systems and evade patrols. The game’s scenarios had become his blueprint, and his mind, once preoccupied with high scores and leaderboards, was now consumed by the idea of testing his skills in the real world. The thrill of the game had fueled a dangerous ambition.

On the fateful night of the heist, Danny had meticulously planned every detail, drawing from his virtual expertise. The bank, a nondescript brick building nestled in the heart of downtown, was chosen for its unremarkable security. The plan was simple: enter through a maintenance door, disable the alarm system, and make a clean getaway. He had even crafted a mask and gloves to ensure he remained incognito.

As Danny crouched behind a cluster of bushes, his pulse raced with a mixture of exhilaration and dread. The heist had become more than a game; it was an escape from the monotony of his life. With a deep breath, he approached the bank's side entrance, the keycard from his previous night’s practice sliding effortlessly into place. The door creaked open, and he slipped inside.

The sterile silence of the bank’s interior was unsettling. Danny’s footsteps echoed as he navigated through the dimly lit hallways, his heart pounding in sync with the game’s soundtrack in his mind. He reached the control room, his hands trembling slightly as he accessed the alarm system. The interface on his laptop mirrored the one from the game, making the task eerily familiar.

Just as he was about to complete the final sequence, the distant sound of footsteps snapped him back to reality. Danny's breath caught in his throat. Panic surged through him as he realized that his meticulous planning had overlooked one crucial detail: the presence of a night security guard.

The guard, a burly man with a flashlight, appeared around the corner, his eyes widening in shock. Danny’s hands fumbled as he pulled out his weapon, a replica designed for the game but now a stark symbol of his escalating desperation. The guard’s shouts pierced the air, and Danny’s mind raced through the escape plan he had practiced so many times.

In a frenzy, Danny sprinted towards the exit, the sounds of alarms blaring in his ears. The virtual precision he had relied on faltered as reality’s chaos enveloped him. He burst through the maintenance door, the night air cold against his sweat-soaked face. The sound of sirens grew louder, and Danny’s heart sank as he realized the game’s promise of a flawless escape was slipping away.

Within moments, police lights flashed in the distance. Danny’s heart pounded with the crushing realization that his adventure had devolved into a real-life nightmare. The escape route he had so confidently navigated in the game now seemed like a cruel illusion.

As the police closed in, Danny’s thoughts were a whirlwind of regret and disbelief. The game that had once been his escape had turned into a harrowing reality, a testament to the dangerous allure of living out fantasies beyond the screen. His ambitions had become his undoing, and as the handcuffs clicked shut, he understood the true cost of blurring the line between virtual thrill and real-life consequences.

[h2] Графика, звук, и геймплей [/h2]

Очень атмосферная игра. 
Невероятный саунд. 
Я рекомендовал бы проходить её в наушниках, чтобы порой, в тот самый момент когда твой сосед начнёт долбить стену перфоратором, ты с криком: "йоптаааа!", срывал их с головы, чтобы окончательно не долбануться, и понять что вообще вокруг происходит (у меня так сегодня утром было). 

Повествование затягивает, легенды оживают, а интерпретация скандинавских мифов выглядит крайне свежо и аутентично. Известные баллады об Асгарде, Рагнароке, Фенрире и Хелле здесь заиграли новыми красками. 
Каждое действующее лицо данной саги полностью переработано, и максимально демонизировано. 
Такого чудесного Фенрира и Хель я еще не видел ни в одной игре о скандинавских богах. 
Хель здесь такая, какая она на самом деле: безобразная великанша, с половиной сгнившего тела. 
И чёрт возьми, это прекрасно.

Боёвка.
Играть можно, практически одной рукой. 
Управление примитивное, простое, и его осилит даже маленький ребенок.
Только в локации "Море мертвецов" мобы стали какие-то чересчур активные, пришлось снизить уровень сложности, после 3-го подряд слива. Но играть на самой большой сложности вас никто не призывает. Боссов выносить на ней не самая простая задача. Особенно тяжко было с Фенриром.
А финальная битва в покоях Хель - это какая-то невероятная слэш-мясорубка была (выиграть в ней нельзя, можете просто глянуть сколько волн вы там продержитесь. Я смог девять)

J'ai beaucoup aimé ce jeu où vous incarnez Senua, une jeune femme guerrière Celte brisée qui part en direction des Enfers vikings, Helheim, afin de sauver l'âme de son amant, Dillion, tué par des Vikings. Elle doit surmonter les ténèbres pour parvenir à ces fins. 

Le jeu est magnifique, l'immersion est profonde et émotionnelle (on ressent toute la haine et la tristesse de Senua), les effets sonores sont incroyables, l'atmosphère est oppressante et fascinante dans cet univers celtique et nordique que j'affectionne beaucoup. J'ai vraiment aimé qu'ils mettent en lumière les maladies mentales/psychiques, qu'ils les fassent connaître et comprendre. Beaucoup de personnes à travers le monde en souffrent (dépression, schizophrénie, trouble de la personnalité multiple,  bipolarité, paranoïa, etc....

Les bémols pour moi sont les énigmes répétitives et peu instinctives parfois, le ciblage automatique qui peut entraîner de se prendre des murs invisibles ou de se coincer avec des obstacles, la corruption sur le bras de senua qui peut être frustrante (si tu fais trop d'échecs, tu meurs et tu recommences tout depuis le début). Pour les personnes sensibles aux bruits, je préfère vous dire qu'il y aura des murmures du début à la fin ( peut-être très dur pour se concentrer ou à supporter).

Je le recommande fortement. Une pépite.

Elite, c’est comme n’importe quelle addiction. Tu sais que c’est “trop”, trop d’heures, trop d’outils tiers, etc. Et pourtant, ce moment de quiétude en super-croisière, la découverte d'un nouveau système qu'aucune personne n'avait pénétré, un lever d’étoile sur une planète glacée… ça vaut l’investissement quand tu as le temps.

Soyons clairs : 2–3 h par semaine ne suffisent pas. Pour être un minimum compétitif, compte 200–300 h. Le jeu prend toute sa dimension quand tu acceptes son écosystème : Inara, EDDB, Coriolis, Edsy… Oui, tu vas “céder” un second écran ( voir un troisième ) à ces pages. Oui, tu vas optimisé, comparer, tracer des routes, tenir "un" ( en vrai "des" ) tableur(s). Force ou faiblesse ? Les deux. Et c’est précisément cette couche qui rend l’expérience à la fois exigeante et magnétique.

Tu seras qui ? Pirate, assassin façon Dangerous.com ( Ne suivez pas cet exemple svp ) ? Ou un grinder méthodique qui monte son premier cargo, puis le deuxième, troisième…  avant de découvrir qu'il y a des dizaines de moyens different de faire des sous. 
Frustrant ? Parfois. 
Grisant ? En Permanence.

Accessible pour voler “à la cool”, impitoyable si tu vises l’optimisation et les améliorations optimales . 
Tu y projettes tes obsessions autant que tes qualités : patience, rigueur, curiosité.

Verdict : si tu as du temps, que l’idée de passer autant de temps sur le jeu que sur des outils externes, ne te fait pas peur, Elite t’offrira des centaines d’heures immersives et sereines. Sinon, passe ton tour : ce n’est pas ton “petit jeu de la semaine”, c’est une habitude de vie.
