If you have buddies to play this with you'll have a good time. It's worth it when the game is on sale. The special weapons are very well done and I love getting them every time. My main gripes are with the objectives and lack of a player base to queue with when you play solo. I don't believe you should invest in this game if you're looking for a rich solo experience.

Playing by yourself can be fun if you know exactly what you're doing, but chances are you won't. Solving puzzles while fending off hordes doesn't work when you only have one set of hands. I find myself constantly frustrated with little things like having to put items into their respective places one at a time - which takes a hot 30 seconds of sitting still in some cases. Some puzzles seem unnecessarily obtuse as well, and I looked up guides for some of them because I was genuinely stumped. Things will be so spread out across the map that you'll struggle to get a run done in under an hour or two. 

There is a lot to love here, and I think that with some time and directed effort things could get better, but in its current state I would only pick this one up if you have friends to play with and a love for fetch quests.

What I write for this review is the experience I had with the game, everybody will experience things differently. This is my honest review if you don't like it well tough. Also no game is safe from a review whether its early access or full release, now onto the review.

Sker Ritual is a fps zombie round base game where you play through different locations trying to find out what is going on & who you are.

Maps: there are 6 maps in total in the game. These maps are great locations & are pretty big. Every map has puzzles you figure out to progress the story. A casual player will get these done in about 2hrs with each map. Only thing I find weird is that the first 4 maps have cut-scenes  & the last 2 maps do not have a cut-scenes which makes me thing the first 4 maps are base game maps & the last 2 are dlc.

Perks: there are 7 perks in the game that you can upgrade. There is health increase, faster reloading, faster fire-rate, movement speed increase, sprint speed increase ect ect. Only thing I hate is that to get the blood orbs to upgrade you need to do the story & survive 25+ rounds to get the advance blood orbs. 

Miracles: these are power up cards that have different affects like fire damage, faster melee speed, ability cool-down ect ect. There 8 different variations with each have 11 cards plus 3 rarities of each card. So you have 88 base miracles 

Weapons: there are 23 weapons from a few pistols to shotguns, a cross bow, rifles, melee ect ect. Each weapon looks really cool even when you pack-a-punch it that changes the look of the weapon. The weapon can be pack-a-punched 5x which is crazy that you can even do that in this game. However you can only pack-a-punch the weapon up to 3x on beginner difficulty & pack-a-punch it 5x on the higher difficulty levels (easy, normal, hard & nightmare).

Character Customization: you can customize your character with different mask's & different voice lines that can be obtained by the sker pass that are dlc cosmetics. I am not sure if the game had default stuff since I bought a bundle pack that was on sale.

Small issues: I do not like that players who want to play on beginner are limited to the pack-a-punch system, I think there should be no limit on the beginner difficulty. Also with the movement system I would get stuck on edge corners a lot to where I couldn't move sometimes. Lastly I dont know if the online matchmaking is player host or server host but from what I gathered its player host since a few players left & it said host left the game. This is a bad online system since it relies on players to host & that can cause progress lost or just toxic players just leaving on purpose. 

I really like this game since it is zombie round base game & takes a unique take on zombies. The story was great, the locations are awesome & the weapons are fun to use. If Wales Interactive fixes the small issues this game could be near perfect but with everything the game feels like a 7/10 score & I really recommend this to players who want a good zombie game to play.

Thats the Pony review for Sker Ritual

[spoiler]I was recommended this by a friend, which I believe I've only heard of this game by name prior. It really captures that lost media/ARG/creepypasta essence beautifully, making you feel like you're actually participating in one. The designs are very well done, with the characters seeming "bland" or innocent like a low budget N64 game to start, and the later designs being quite unsettling. Also, the imagery in the game is horrifying. It's a perfect balance of not being too pretentious of horror ("WE'RE SO SCARY AND MYSTERIOUS") but also not too campy ("AND THEN A SKELETON CAME OUT OF THE CLOSET!"). It has some over the top moments, but it's definitely self-aware enough to not break your immersion.

The back-and-forth between browser and game also deepened my immersion, as it felt you were slowly piecing together the truth behind the game.

Now for my spoiler-y complaints:
1. The only thing I wasn't too fond of involving the browser was that it requires you to download some files, which might off-put some people. I was willing, but one of the required "decoders" is an .exe program that ran my GPU up to 100% usage, which I not only couldn't find a solution to, but also one of my friends had the same issue. Luckily, I was able to use a guide to continue, so it wasn't a hard blockade, but it did break immersion and interest by that point in the game.

2. The later puzzles relied heavily on random bits of knowledge from prior in the game, while canning any recent or other info you gathered, BUT YOU STILL NEED SOME INFO YOU PUSHED ASIDE. It's okay when you don't have so many moving parts, but later in the game it got quite frustrating. Just be sure to use notes and label them for what you encounter.

3. The dreaded computer run, and all the Starlings. Initially they are quite horrifying, and the first serious horror gameplay you encounter, but it quickly wanes and they become a nuisance to deal with. They constantly hover any area you are in, and will rarely leave if you hide in a barrel. It made the computer run require an incredibly lucky setup, and a good set of balls for jumpscares. It gets even worse later in the game, once you make it to the sewers. It's a bit dumb that sometimes the best strategy is to be caught just to be done with them for a little. Rex was the only one who I could tolerate, because at least there was a way to prevent his spawn, so long as you were paying attention.

Although these complaints seem quite full, do not take it as a hatred of the game. I really did enjoy it, and highly recommend it to anyone who grew up watching or listening to creepypastas or lost media. This game should be more popular than it is. [/spoiler]

Luckyest takes a simple idea—the thrill of scratching a hidden panel to see what you’ve won or lost—and turns it into an surprisingly engaging little loop built around risk, reward, and long-term progression. At first glance, the game seems almost barebones: a clean pixel-art interface, a set of themed investment decks, and a grid of concealed results waiting for you to reveal them. Yet that visual simplicity works to its advantage. The focus remains squarely on decision-making rather than flashy effects, and the minimalist presentation makes it easy to fall into a rhythm of quick sessions that always tempt you into playing “just one more round.”

The core gameplay revolves around selecting a stake, choosing a deck such as stocks, cryptocurrency, or other tongue-in-cheek investment themes, and scratching your way through a field of potential multipliers and losses. Every reveal is a small gamble, and the tension between cashing out early or pushing for a bigger payout drives the experience. The randomness is always present, but it never feels completely chaotic, because the game gradually shifts from pure luck into a balancing act shaped by your own playstyle. You begin to feel out the personality of each deck, the risk levels you’re comfortable with, and the patterns of your own impulses—making bigger wins and losses feel personal rather than arbitrary.

What elevates Luckyest beyond a simple scratcher simulation is its permanent upgrade tree. After each run, whatever profits you manage to extract can be spent on abilities that expand your control: increased earnings, reduced penalties, improved odds, or more strategic tools that let you influence or mitigate risk. The branching layout of the upgrades encourages experimentation, and over time you begin to see entire strategies emerge around the paths you prioritize. Investing heavily in risk-oriented upgrades creates an aggressive, high-stakes playstyle, while focusing on planning or economy encourages a steadier, more methodical approach. The feeling of gradual improvement gives weight to each short session, transforming a luck-driven loop into a surprisingly thoughtful system of long-term progression.

The game’s audiovisual style reinforces its laid-back appeal. The pixel art is crisp, bright, and thematically varied depending on the deck you select, while the sound design uses small cues—gentle scratches, cheerful pings, and subtle effects—to make each reveal satisfying. It isn’t a game that chases spectacle; instead, its presentation is designed to be inviting, consistent, and unobtrusively stylish. That restraint keeps the experience relaxing even when the stakes are high, lending Luckyest an almost meditative quality when you’re fully immersed in its rhythms.

Even with its strengths, the game has limitations rooted in its simplicity. The core interaction never changes: stake, scratch, decide. While the permanent upgrades add variety, the basic loop can start to feel repetitive during extended sessions. The randomness that defines the game’s identity can also limit its appeal for players who prefer deterministic or deeply strategic systems. And although multiple decks help mix things up, the structure of each round remains fairly uniform across the entire game. As a result, Luckyest is best experienced in shorter bursts rather than long sit-down marathons.

Despite these constraints, Luckyest works remarkably well at what it wants to offer: a compact, clever blend of luck-based quickplay and long-term incremental growth. It understands exactly how to hook the player without overwhelming them, and its upgrade paths give each return visit a sense of purpose. If you enjoy games built around short decision loops, high replay value, and a light but engaging strategic layer, Luckyest delivers a satisfying and relaxing experience. It’s modest in scope but well-executed, providing an addictive little cycle of risk and reward that’s easy to pick up and surprisingly hard to put down.

Ignore the flood of under 2 hour steam renters who thought this game was made to be a sim. It was always going to be a simcade, an evolution of the heat games, and console based Nascar games in general. In that regard it does not disappoint.
Feel of the car on a controller with all the assists off, feels fantastic. Nothing like the heat games where you felt almost not in control of the car. You have to manage throttle input to prevent spinning and work the wheel to correct. Driving the car around the track feels the most realistic for this type of Nascar simcade we have gotten in a very very long time.
I haven't tried it on my rig, because I know it would just be a disappointment after using it for iRacing for hundreds of hours. That is not why I bought this game, nor do I think it was intended to be. I would expect the FFB, haptics, and hardware support to be very limited in that regard and the game to focus on controllers. It might get better with updates. Aside, from that, the controller feels great.
There is still a lot of the carry over issues from previous titles such as not having the option to control your car under caution or when on pit lane. The damage even when on full is still really forgiving. If these types of things didn't bother you on Heat it shouldn't bother you here.
Track scans, and car models are top notch. Sound track is fairly good if that is something you leave on. Sounds in car are a step up from past games but still has room to improve.
Menus and interfaces are pretty standard but do offer more options than past entries. Don't expect anything special but certainly better than the F1 games UI.
It's a great Nascar 'game', which is what it was always meant to be. I would imagine the peripheral woes will get sorted in time and future installments will continue to build on the foundation this game is laying.
As someone that has all the Nascar content on iRacing, and a 10k rig, I had no delusions when this game was announced that it was going to be anything close to a simulation, or offer incredible FFB and support all the features my rig is capable of doing. This is a console based, controller focused, officially licensed Nascar video game. The best one we have gotten in a very long time.

Именно с неё, вместе с [i]Arx Fatalis[/i], у меня началось знакомство с миром ролевых игр.
Первый опыт оказался запоминающимся и трудным: сразу после установки игры мне не удавалось убить скриба по пути в Кальдеру поскольку он побеждал меня снова и снова. Не было понятно, почему не попадаешь по нему, ведь удары наносились точно в цель, и в итоге пришлось искать совет у друга, с которым часто обменивались [url=steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3141447241] диском[/url] чтобы поиграть — один днём, другой вечером. Всё это, вместе с множеством других воспоминаний, уже стершихся с годами, и стало моим первым, сложным, но невероятно захватывающим знакомством с Morrowind.
С тех пор проведено бесчисленное количество часов в игре, сначала с официальными дополнениями, а затем и с множеством сторонних модов, исследуя каждый уголок Вварденфелла и открывая новые тайны. Среди особенно запомнившихся выделяется мод [i]«Имени Скального Наездника»[/i].

[b]В Morrowind вам никто не объяснит, куда именно идти[/b], поскольку здесь [i][u]нет стрелочек или маркеров[/u][/i], как в большинстве игр. Вам просто [i][u]нужно действовать и разбираться самому[/u][/i], постепенно [i]учась на своих ошибках и находя решение через внимательное чтение больших диалогов персонажей, книг и других деталей мира[/i]. NPC дают лишь устные указания, а всё остальное зависит от вашей [i][u]наблюдательности, любопытства и смелости исследовать мир[/u][/i].
Приходилось искать путь по описаниям, сверяя направления и приметы, в том числе первая проблема у меня возникла уже после поручения найти загадочный кубик-рубик в двемерских руинах или Кая Касадеса: тогда пришлось обойти всю Балмору и заглянуть в каждый дом, обыскать каждую корзину в городе, потому что ориентироваться по устным указаниям в то время было действительно непросто, к тому же некуда было посмотреть, ведь интернета тогда просто не было. Именно такие моменты делали каждое путешествие [i][u]настоящим приключением[/u][/i].

[b]Morrowind стал основой, на которой выросли Oblivion и Skyrim, но именно здесь родилась душа серии The Elder Scrolls[/b] — глубокий лор, неповторимая атмосфера, свобода и [i][u]редкое для игр уважение к игроку[/u][/i].
Кастомизация здесь особенная: можно было собрать доспех по частям, подобрать свой стиль и выглядеть действительно уникально, такого больше не было ни в одной последующей части. А свобода действий доходила до того, что вы могли убить любого, даже главного персонажа, и игра просто предупреждала, что теперь [i]«Со смертью этого персонажа нить вашей судьбы обрывается»[/i] и позволяла тебе жить с этим выбором.
Это не просто игра — это живой мир, который продолжает существовать без персонажа, где каждая мелочь имеет значение.

Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus, developed by Tamsoft and published by XSEED Games and Marvelous, is an unapologetically over-the-top brawler that combines fast-paced, anime-inspired combat with an unmistakably provocative aesthetic. Originally released on the PlayStation Vita before making its way to PC, it stands as one of the most defining entries in the Senran Kagura franchise—an eccentric series that embraces absurdity, charm, and chaos in equal measure. The game doesn’t shy away from its identity; it’s a mixture of genuine mechanical fun and tongue-in-cheek fanservice, offering something both playful and self-aware. Beneath the skimpy outfits and comical exaggerations lies a surprisingly robust beat-’em-up that succeeds at being entertaining, even if it’s not particularly deep.

The narrative framework of Shinovi Versus revolves around four rival shinobi academies, each with its own roster of female warriors. Every school has its ideology and backstory, creating a web of rivalries that drive the game’s campaign. The structure is segmented into four main storylines, one for each faction, and each tells its own version of events through a blend of visual novel-style dialogue sequences and explosive battles. While the story often dips into melodrama and comedy, it also carries moments of genuine character development, exploring the girls’ aspirations, rivalries, and loyalties. The writing is lighthearted, with a heavy dose of self-awareness, and though it never takes itself too seriously, it manages to make each character memorable through humor and exaggerated emotion.

Combat is the centerpiece, and it captures the essence of a fast, fluid, and accessible brawler. Each character has a distinct fighting style, weapon type, and set of combos, ensuring variety across the 20-plus playable fighters. Battles unfold in open 3D arenas where players string together light and heavy attacks, air juggles, and special moves to overwhelm waves of enemies or duel against rival shinobi. The controls are smooth and responsive, making it easy for newcomers to enjoy while offering enough depth for more experienced players to experiment with different characters. Transformations—activated mid-battle through a burst of energy—grant temporary stat boosts and new moves, while the “clothing destruction” system doubles as both a gameplay indicator and a trademark feature of the series. As the fight progresses, characters’ outfits tear away with each hit, serving as a mix of comedy and spectacle that defines the series’ irreverent tone.

Visually, Shinovi Versus benefits from its transition to PC. The higher resolution, stable frame rate, and cleaner textures make the colorful character models stand out far better than on its handheld origins. Each fighter is meticulously detailed, with fluid animations that highlight the game’s kinetic energy. The environments, while limited in variety, are bright and serve as fitting backdrops for the action. The camera occasionally struggles to keep up with the chaos, especially during crowded fights, but it rarely detracts from the overall flow. The soundtrack reinforces the game’s personality—a mix of upbeat electronic battle themes and traditional Japanese motifs that perfectly match the mixture of comedy and intensity that defines the experience.

While Shinovi Versus offers a satisfying burst of fun in short sessions, it’s not without repetition. The mission design, though energetic, often follows the same pattern: fight groups of enemies, face a rival shinobi, watch a cutscene, and repeat. The variety lies primarily in the characters rather than in the objectives or level design. However, the large cast and their individualized move sets help to keep things fresh for players who enjoy experimenting. The game also includes multiplayer, allowing up to four players to battle online or locally, though the online community has dwindled over time. When active, multiplayer matches add an exciting layer of unpredictability, as players clash in frantic free-for-alls filled with special attacks and comedic chaos.

Tonally, Shinovi Versus is as polarizing as it is distinctive. Its unabashed embrace of fanservice—complete with exaggerated character designs, suggestive humor, and playful innuendo—sets it apart from more conventional action games. This aspect is central to its appeal but also the reason it alienates some players. For those who approach it with an understanding of its over-the-top intent, it becomes clear that the game isn’t trying to shock but to celebrate its absurdity. The developers lean into the humor, balancing the sexualized imagery with genuine warmth and camaraderie among the characters. It’s a game that thrives on contradiction—equal parts silly and sincere, ridiculous and surprisingly heartfelt.

Despite its flaws, Shinovi Versus succeeds because it knows exactly what it wants to be. It’s not a technical masterpiece or a deeply strategic fighter, but it’s fast, flashy, and unashamedly fun. The blend of anime aesthetics, accessible combat, and playful tone creates a distinct experience that’s hard to find elsewhere. For fans of the Senran Kagura series, it represents a high point in terms of both content and personality. For newcomers, it serves as an entry point into a world that doesn’t take itself too seriously but still offers genuine entertainment.

In the end, Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus is a game of excess—of action, energy, and attitude. It celebrates style over subtlety, and in doing so, crafts a uniquely enjoyable, if divisive, experience. It’s a title that revels in its absurdity while still delivering a satisfying combat system that rewards fast reactions and experimentation. For those willing to embrace its eccentricity, it provides a surprisingly polished and enjoyable action romp filled with humor, charm, and relentless energy. It may not appeal to everyone, but it remains a confident, unapologetic entry in the anime brawler genre, defined as much by its outrageous personality as by the fun at its core.

Rating: 9/10

动作砍杀游戏。核心主题为忍者学院之间的竞争。剧情以关卡任务和简短对话呈现。整体语气兼具戏剧和轻喜。冲突围绕训练、荣誉与隐性动机展开。

玩法以高速战斗为主。每位女主角拥有独特连招与远程技能。上手门槛低。难度在后期任务才明显上升。内容重复较为突出。

成长系统可解锁新技能与外观。养成路径线性。刷取需求较低。主要目标为清除敌人潮或进行一对一对决。

人物通过短场景塑造。性格偏夸张。互动基于学院对立。分支剧情提供浅层动机展现。

美术表现鲜明。打击特效突出。角色动画流畅。场景样式简单且重复。多数平台运行稳定。

音频节奏感强。音乐富动能。配音强调角色特质。目标用户倾向快速街机式战斗与内容收集。游戏不侧重深度机制或严肃剧情。

目前不太推荐，后续看优化修改评测吧。总体挺休闲的，可以玩下去，但是有些问题玩久了就会很烦躁，比如：1.ui不太好，已经不是一般的字体小了，27的屏幕看得我眼睛疼2.占位网格为什么不弄明显一点啊，吸附很难受，我本来想一组同一类的摆齐，结果史一样的吸附要我反复调整3.一级和二级种植园能不能在要吸附上去的时候增加个作物类型选择，或者默认种植新解锁的作物呢？4.加个提醒吧，由于我一直在弄高层，后面才发现最下面的那一大层二级住所在一级住所之间反复横跳，难怪我说士气怎么在蹦迪，我检查了下才发现有些建筑需要供能提供buff，以及需要特定的条件才能稳住，本身这个塔身就要建造很高，难免注意不到，所以在出现异常的时候能不能弹出一些附加问题和对策建议的框呢？5.目前的话只能旋转固定角度，是否考虑在同样的水平方向上增加一个类似按住鼠标滚轮就能自由旋转塔身的功能呢？这样就可以观察建筑与建筑之间是否对齐了6.啥时候增加手柄

很好玩！目标感很足，一步步建立奇观，最后平息天灾。垂直建造很新颖，或者说打磨得这么好的实在不多见。不过每层操作稍微有点同质化，由于流程不长所以掩盖的不错。

操作方面气球的链接要缓缓移动屏幕实在有点累，居民心愿也有点繁琐。

我看到有人说物流有问题，确实有问题，但在这类游戏中算可以了，物流出问题很大概率是塔规模太大了，这个游戏的目标是建造奇观，流程比较短，不像一般的流水线建设游戏那样追求生产效率。

英雄传说玩的第一部作品空之轨迹1ST，作为重置版作品系列老粉是可以放心去玩的，但是本评测不会提及系列相关作品，只单独评测空之轨迹1ST在JRPG类型游戏里面表现如何，是否值得入手体验游玩。
ST作为系列的故事起点并且重置以后无疑是十分吸引人入坑的，但这不代表着玩完ST以后就马不停蹄的去玩其它的轨迹系列，只推荐先等等，等到了以后去玩接下来法老控重置的作品。
说回空之轨迹1ST本身，游戏一周目流程在50个小时左右，一个流程下来基本上能体验完本作的全部内容，新周目主要是做做成就挑战一下高难度以及收集一些新的皮肤，随着难度的增加能够感觉到明显的生存压力，在简单模式下不经常用的技能在高难度下是必备的，还是相当有挑战性的。
角色养成最为核心的是名为导力器的系统，说简单点就是类似于怪物猎人“拼好刀”，每一名角色除了自身的武器装备以外都有一套各自的导力器系统，女主角的导力器是从一个核心槽位里出两条线，这两条线一条长一条短，可以理解为长的那条线槽位很多可以安装很多水晶，短的那条线很短槽位很少能装的水晶数目有限，这里面说到的核心槽位是所有线的起点，安装在核心槽位的水晶所带来的属性值是所有分支共享的，女主角的导力器核心是没有属性要求的想怎么配怎么配，男主角的导力器和女主角的结构一样，不同点在于男主角的核心是只能安装特定属性的水晶，其余角色的导力器的机制都是这个意思，有的角色导力器只有一条线好处是能够很容易的配出目标技能取点是持有此机制的角色很偏科基本上走的是法师路线，另外一个比较特殊的角色的导力器是一个核心插槽上引出了5条线，每条线只能安装一个水晶。
简而言之，每个角色都有自己的核心定位，男女主角可以打物理也可以打法师，其余角色要不就是纯物理路线，要不就是纯辅助或者法师路线。
不得不说的是空之轨迹1st的地图功能是在很多游戏中地图功能最好有最有实用性的地图功能了，大道至简的风格没有花里胡哨的要素，很多游戏中在战斗结束后打开地图有一种茫然的感觉不知道从哪里来要到哪里去，本作的地图能够一目了然的判断出从哪个口出来的并且只要通过简单的旋转地图就能看出高低层的位置，很直接地解决了在高低地形下地图要素交错重叠导致的目标不知道是在高处还是在低处的问题，暴杀一些游戏里面中看不中用的实景3D地图。地图道路虽然没什么岔路，基本上都是大直道很少有迷路的情况但是地图道路纵深很长，要跑很长的路，不过你的高速模式有很好的弥补了这一点，不过需要注意的一点是部分收集品不会在地图直接标注需要到达特定屋子里面才会有提示，例如终章的男女主究极武器需要在王都咖啡厅获取，城镇大地图不会有提示，一定得进到屋子里后才能看到提示。
以JRPG游戏的角度来看本作确确实实存在着一些一眼就能看明白并且实打实影响玩家体验的问题，例如游戏不是全语音，在一段剧情中经常会出现语言播着播着突然变成文本播放，这种情况经常发生，甚至还会出现在一段剧情中NPC角色的文本有语言，轮到男女主角的文本后又没有语言了的这种诡异现象，如果玩家游玩过程中遇见这种没有语言的情况，我想这并不是什么BUG而是部分文本本来就没有语音。另外一点是剧情上有着熊孩子的经典雷点，这一点也许不应该特意去提出来因为大部分角色扮演游戏尤其是日厂游戏熊孩子桥段真的是层出不绝，但是作为一名爱好角色扮演类游戏的玩家来说，我真的不喜欢熊孩子桥段，本作空之轨迹1ST主线剧情中存在着熊孩子突然出现找事儿膈应人，完事儿后哭哭啼啼地道歉大喊着红豆泥私密马塞以后再也不敢了知道错了请你原谅我最后主角团真的就无事发生的环节，光这一点还不用特意提出来，但是如果结合刚才提到的NPC角色文本有语音主角团角色没有语言的情况呢，熊孩子在玩家的耳机里叫的比哭还难听并且熊孩子的语音文本是全的！主角团在这个场景里全员哑巴，屏幕外的玩家是无能狂怒的，这让本就对熊孩子桥段不满的我更是火上浇油。
虽然剧情上个人认为存在着熊孩子的雷点，但是法老控同时也给了一个怎么解决玩家遇见熊孩子不满的问题，虽然不是同一个熊孩子但是是熊孩子干的事儿，熊孩子天真冒失的行为让主角团错失良机并让主角团成员陷入了危险，事后熊孩子无力的坐下流出了无能的眼泪，怎么样？血压是不是已经上来了？那要怎么解决呢？很简单，直接一巴掌扇过去教做人，这一巴掌简直是扇到了我的心里面，很爽，这一巴掌过后熊孩子真正意义上获得了成长，屏幕外的玩家也是缓缓地舒了一口气，可喜可贺，可喜可贺。虽然个人不喜欢熊孩子的角色设定但是不可否认的是在空轨中每一个角色都不是可有可无的存在，剧情很严谨，因果关系并不生硬，并不存在工具人的要素。
没有动画演出真的是有点可惜了，这也许是法老控自身技术力的问题，作为空轨的第一部重置版作品基本上没有任何的动画演出这一点十分的残念，这实在是有点“经典”过头了，部分剧情画面中感觉是比较重要的桥段是一个剧情高潮但是演出只有角色特定的动作和声优的语音，剩下的只有镜头的不断切换，这种行为在部分剧情中显得十分生硬，类似的问题BGM也是一样的，虽然空轨出了很多出圈的音乐但是本作BGM重复利用率相当之高，在部分气氛紧张严肃的剧情中BGM用的却是原野探索中的BGM，BGM和角色语音的语气完全不搭，就连BOSS战也是这样的，打BOSS的时候BGM一响不知道的还以为我在打奖励关。
以上便是空之轨迹1ST比较明显存在的问题，但这并不影响我给它一个好评，因为作为我的第一款轨迹系列作品也是玩的第一部法老控出的游戏，在玩空之轨迹1ST的过程中它给我的感觉是让我玩的很舒服的，空轨1ST就像是去饭店吃饭，上菜的时候先是上了点开胃菜，然后上凉菜，再倒上一杯酒，然后上主菜，最后上点汤和水果，环节一环扣一环。虽然存在着技术力不高的硬伤但是却很明显能感觉到制作组想着怎么能让我玩好，就好比是去找一个混的不怎么好的哥们家里玩，哥们家里可能真的没啥好玩的但是哥们是真的愿意陪你玩想让你觉得和哥们玩挺开心的而不是去一家高级饭店吃饭，觉得饭店里的菜做的有问题，饭店经理听了之后急眼了，跳出来告诉你说他们家所有的东西全是最高级的，厨师也是最高级的，做出来的东西不爱吃那是客人的问题，完全没有意识到就算用的是最好的食材如果往里面加屎那就是在给人喂屎。
综上所述空之轨迹1ST是十分值得入坑的一部作品，这是一场漫长的旅途，在旅途中不断的相遇与告别，直到星之所在之处，何不把告别的眼泪留到重新相逢的时候再留？
原来不需要复杂的战斗系统也能做好一款rpg，原来不需要优秀的画面也能吸引玩家去尝试。越来越多大厂选择平庸、不暴雷的剧本为了稳定的销量，小厂选择充满争议性的剧本引发争论炒作，我都快忘记一个好的剧本，恰到好处的音乐能给玩家带来什么了。

Oh, KOTOR II. We've all know that the sequel is somewhat subpar to the original game due to all what happened during development, the cut content, and the game being rushed for a holiday release just because they wanted that holiday cash.

Even with all that, I think this game is amazing. As a massive KOTOR fan, I decided to play this just when the modern patch (which has the restored contend mod) was released and this is a whole new game, which made my experience so much better than playing the first one on modern systems. You can't go wrong with this game, you have a great Star Wars world to explore, with new planets not featured on the first game, new characters, and while the ending might not be everyone's cup of tea, I still enjoyed this amazing journey. Same with the first one, you have the power of choice, which can impact outcomes, the ending, and your relationship statuses with your companions.

This game "feels" much more modern than KOTOR. The maps have less traversing to get from quest to quest, the graphics are quite a bit better, and gameplay overall is just a lot smoother. The voice acting and soundtrack is as good as most modern games, if not better. The story is good, and offers a LOT of individual choices.

Hard to find a con for this game other than dated graphics and some QOL stuff that could be better. I think if you can get past that, you'll find one of the best RPGs ever.

Hrot is a perfect example of a boomer shooter done right, and it's one with a very unique setting and vibe at that. When I first played the demo, I was a bit taken aback by how odd the whole thing felt, but already towards the end of the demo level, I was hooked. Hrot doesn't just imitate 90's FPS's--it actually has that unmistakable visceral feel of those games.

There is a lot to like in Hrot: the game is perfect in length (13 hours on Hard difficulty), has a proper multi-slot saving system with quicksave and quickload functions (seriously, these days I'm almost giving bonus points for just that), features a decent, simple arsenal with no confusing mods or upgrades, as well as tons of really neat easter eggs and inside jokes (good luck finding most of the secrets, however) and a creepy, unsettling atmosphere of a post-apocalyptic socialist Czechoslovakia. Unlike games such as Doom, Quake and Dusk, Hrot is pretty conservative with giving you ammo, so you will be running out a lot--at least on higher difficulties. Thankfully, the game is well-balanced: with enough skill, you will never get stuck or be forced to run with empty guns past all the monsters, hoping for the best.

If I had to make a couple of criticisms, it would first be that last few levels of the game seem shorter and feel a bit rushed compared to the rest. It didn't feel like there was a buildup to meeting the final boss--I was surprised upon the realization that I've reached him.

The other thing that left me underwhelmed was the secret levels (I didn't bother to actually look for them, just checked the walkthrough online). They are too short, too simple, and "meme-y" with little substance. They're not bad per se, but had I actually spent the time to find them on my own, I'd be quite disappointed. As a side note, I think that a perfect secret level is one that is reasonably challenging, introduces some twist to the gameplay not seen in any other level (e.g., solving some puzzle in what is primarily a shooter game), and rewards you with some special collectible, power-up, or piece of information that you wouldn't see otherwise.

There is no question that Hrot's unique, intentionally ugly presentation is not for everyone. However, if you are looking at the trailer and thinking that you may at least somewhat enjoy it, then give it a try. I really doubt you'll regret it.

Simplesmente a melhor campanha de um Call of Duty já criada.
Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare foi deixado de lado com o passar dos anos, e poucas pessoas lembram dele com carinho. Algumas recordam de momentos da infância em certos mapas… mas eu não. Eu lembro desse jogo como a melhor campanha que já joguei em toda a franquia.
E digo isso não por nostalgia. Quando joguei pela primeira vez, lá em meados de 2015, eu era garoto, e sinceramente achei a campanha chata. Eu não tinha maturidade pra entender o que estava sendo contado ali. Mas, anos depois, rejogando, percebi o quão grandiosa, complexa e ousada essa campanha realmente é.

 A Campanha: Política e poder.
A campanha de Advanced Warfare é perfeita. Nunca vi um Call of Duty tão bem elaborado e tão bem pensado, principalmente nas questões políticas que apresenta.
Esse jogo não tenta escolher um lado. Ele mostra que, no fim das contas, não importa se você é de esquerda ou de direita, o que realmente vence é o poder militar.
A frase "ideias não determinam quem está certo, o poder determina quem está certo. E eu tenho o poder, então eu estou certo." martela na minha mente até hoje...
Posso dizer sem medo: esse jogo moldou a forma como eu penso sobre poder, política e humanidade.

 O vilão, que pra mim nem deveria ser chamado assim, é o melhor que a franquia já teve. Muita gente vai dizer “e o Menéndez do Black Ops 2?”.
Com todo respeito, Menéndez é ótimo, mas eu fico com a profundidade do antagonista de Advanced Warfare. A verdade é que o que move eles, o que os transformam no “vilão”, é algo humano, compreensível e ao mesmo tempo assustador. E é aí que mora a genialidade na criação de ambos. Mas eu ainda fico com o "vilão" de AW.
Essa é uma campanha que exige maturidade pra ser entendida. Você precisa olhar e pensar:
“O que esse cara tá dizendo… não tá errado. Talvez os meios sejam, mas a ideia não.”
Isso é raro. E é algo que só esse jogo conseguiu fazer.

 O multiplayer de Advanced Warfare não é ruim, tive ótimas lembranças jogando, especialmente naquele mapa que lembra um pequeno bairro, bem similar ao mapa do navio do Black Ops 2.
O sistema de pulo duplo funcionou bem, claro, o do BO3 é mais refinado, mas o de Advanced ainda assim é divertido e dá dinamismo às partidas. Muita gente critica essa mecânica, mas eu achei que foi uma boa inovação pra época.

 O Modo Zombies... kkkkkkk
Sinceramente, o modo Zombies aqui parece mais um enfeite do que uma proposta real. Entrei uma vez, vi o básico, e deixei de lado.
Não é ruim, mas também não tem brilho. É um extra, nada mais. Prefiro não alongar para não perder o carinho que tenho por esse jogo KKKKKKKKKKKKKKKKK

 Conclusão:
No fim das contas, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare é o único COD em que o multiplayer é o complemento da campanha, e não o contrário.
Hoje, as campanhas parecem existir apenas pra acompanhar o modo online.
Mas aqui não. Aqui a campanha é o coração do jogo.
E digo mais, se esse jogo tivesse sido lançado só com a campanha, sem multiplayer nenhum, ainda assim seria um sucesso absoluto.
É um jogo que envelheceu bem, e que merece ser lembrado não pela nostalgia, mas pela mensagem madura e ousada que entrega.
É O CALL OF DUTY MAIS SUBESTIMADO DE TODOS!

用未来感与大场面，翻盘前作的沉闷

IMO, this should be marked as BETA. It has a lot of bugs. It's not beginner friendly, either. If you know nothing of programming, you would probably find it hard to follow and learn. It doesn't really have an audience: It's too buggy for professional development, yet too complicated for beginners, IMO. 

"Programming Without Coding" sounds like a misnomer, too. It's not like SCRATCH, for instance. You can't just build the code like building blocks, per se. You need to understand the semantics of RING to program with it. For instance, you need to know the syntax of conditionals, strings, etc. 

It says I used it for 12.5 hours, but that's a lie, lol. I left the program open overnight :) I used it for maybe a couple of hours, exploring what it was about, but I keep running into bugs. 

For example, it will crash out of no where, then you lose all your unsaved code. If I run into it again, I will describe what happened.

There are other areas that don't make sense, like you can't move blocks of code through drag and drop or between branches. Let's say you want to enclose an area into a loop that you already created... Well, you have to copy, cut, paste it into the new area. You can't just relocate it. 

Another annoying area is how the console popup works: When you run code for console mode, a CMD prompt pops up, which is fine, but you can't reuse that popup and put it into a split screen. The popup takes forever to come up on my computer, then each debugging requires a new popup, which isn't on top of the screen, so you have to navigate to it through the task bar. 

If you try to use the program in split screen, the program crashes for some strange reason. Like if I put the CMD prompt on one side and this on the other, it will crash and freeze. 

There is no way to put the CMD prompt into the development area, either, so it's aggravating. When I was looking online, I came across RING Notepad, which does have input in the development, too. 

Some of the decisions seem weird, like the Switch statement: It has cases for the individual cases, yet in the RING Notepad, a lot of examples uses ON, so that's a weird change. I noticed that you could use multiple things for the same thing, like PRINT versus SEE versus PUT. I don't know the language enough, but the documentation uses SEE a lot, so it's weird that this uses PRINT everywhere. It's just confusing if you are following the RING documentation. 

I could see the developer is passionate, and I support that, but I can't recommend it outside BETA. Thus, I will go with not recommended for that reason. If it was in BETA, I would recommend it.

PWCT is a refreshing entry into the field of easier to use products for conceptualizing an idea into an actual working application. PWCT should be considered an easier transition into the world of understanding what it is to develop an application. With its visual approach to programming it makes the understanding of what is required and how to apply it less of a burden on people who want to create applications. 
How does it do this? It provides a list of many of the building pieces called components in PWCT that allow you to apply everything from declaring variables to interfacing with files or databases. Does this require you to understand the concepts of developing applications? Yes, it does but the learning curve to gain this knowledge is made easier by PWCT’s visual approach to putting the application together. 
It closely resembles the idea put forth by Legos the popular toys that provide a way to build anything you can imagine. Although Legos will allow you to build complex building structures it does require you to understand building principles to accomplish that goal. However, like Legos there is little, or no knowledge required to get started and begin to build something that works and bring you satisfaction that it is indeed possible to take an idea from concept to reality with the right tools. 
PWCT is supported by a team of dedicated professionals who are very responsive to the questions and needs of their community. Each  day a new tutorial is being created to help new users of this product to create something that works while learning programming concepts at the same time. The community is strong as well for a new product with some of its members providing tutorials based on the learning they are doing of PWCT to assist others who might be helped by a different perspective; that of someone learning the product as they are. 
The price point to dive into this development environment is very inexpensive currently compared to other integrated development environments or tools. What can you develop with it, really anything you can imagine. A personal application, something that would be sold commercially, or even a game as it supports many gaming libraries as well. As you progress your knowledge of the development process will improve. That learning process is required to have an understanding of the pieces needed to create a larger more complex application. 
Achieving this though is made easier by PWCT’s approach to it. I as an owner of the tool and end-user still learning, encourage others to jump into this environment. What do you have to lose, a few dollars and a little time if it doesn’t work for you. What do you have to gain, a broader world where you now can create applications that serve your needs and allow you to gain some important skills in the world of development.

Blasphemous es un tremendo juegazo, pero con matices:

Para empezar, creo que no tardas más de dos horas en darte cuenta de que fue el primer trabajo del estilo por parte de TheGameKitchen. Algunas zonas tienen claros fallos de diseño y la movilidad es más bien un poco tosca.

También tardas poco en darte cuenta de que tiene más bien poquito de Metroidvania aunque como Soulslike 2D es una maravilla. Dicho esto, agradezco que los "power-ups" que complementan el plataformeo, sean algo más originales que el doble salto clásico. 

Una vez sabes donde están las reliquias, la exploración y las primeras horas se hacen mucho más amenas en comparación a la primera run, y bueno, recalco, agradezco que la solución a los obstáculos no sea un doble salto o un super dash por ejemplo, porque a mí personalmente me parecen soluciones pobres y fáciles a la hora de diseñar un mapa.

Ahora bien, por otro lado:

La banda sonora no es buena, es que va genial con la ambientación. La guitarra y el piano...sobre todo en las zonas de nieve...una delicia de tracks.

El pixel art es muy bonito y está bastante on point, aunque creo que lo disfrutaría más en una Steamdeck, por ejemplo.

De la historia no sé muy bien qué decir porque es la clásica historia a lo Souls en la que todo es excesivamente críptico y al final descifras el lore a raíz de leer todos los ítems y forjar tu propia interpretación. Más o menos intuyo por donde quiere ir, como mínimo es interesante.

Los bosses no tienen término medio: o son muy difíciles o sacos de boxeo. Esto en el NG+ se aprecia más todavía. Quitando eso, los bosses que son difíciles son MUY buenos. Isidora (mi favorita), Crisanta, Esdras, Laudes...en overall son bastante decentes todos.

Quitando la dificultad que para mí es lo de menos en los bosses. Los diseños...damn, van duros de cojones. Además creo que con Blasphemous han hecho una tarea de absoluto 10 plasmando figuras y leyendas del folclore español y del cristianismo, cosa que para mí tiene mucho mérito porque es innovador y algo por lo que sentirse orgulloso. Dentro de lo que es una atmósfera soulslike, usar y moldear el universo alrededor de la religión y su historia junto a una ambientación íbero-medieval me parece brillante, valiente y digno de aplaudir por lo que supone.

Además, el doblaje es una delicia (jugadlo en español, por el amor de Dios) y cuenta con unos actores de doblaje de absoluta locura, se nota muchísimo que Baxa aprecia y respeta el mundillo.

Independientemente de su relevancia en el género (que no es poca, porque ya hemos podido ver bastantes títulos a lo largo de los años cuya inspiración artística viene directamente de Blasphemous), solo como producto español y por lo que supone para la industria a nivel nacional y cultural, me parece un producto muy digno en varios aspectos. En conclusión:

Creo que Blasphemous es un producto muy interesante para diversas personas y jugadores y estoy seguro de que no dejará indiferente a nadie que sea un apasionado del mundo de los videojuegos.

9/10 – Painful, Beautiful, Worth It

Blasphemous is brutal, but it never feels unfair. Every death teaches you something, every victory feels earned. The world is dark, detailed, and full of meaning.

It’s not just a game — it’s a journey through guilt and redemption.

[h1]🧐 Rick's Opinion 🧐[/h1]

Hi. Rick Sanchez here. Yeah, that Rick Sanchez. If you don’t know who I am, congratulations, your IQ is probably below the recommended minimum to operate a toaster. I just finished High on Life, and I’m here to tell you that this game is a beautiful, stupid, chaotic masterpiece created by people who clearly haven’t slept since 2018.

Let’s get this out of the way: this game is an absolute clown fiesta. A rainbow vomit carnival. A multicolored fever dream produced by a team of overcaffeinated raccoons with access to Unreal Engine and emotional trauma. And I loved it. I loved every second of it. I hate that I loved it. I hate myself for loving it. I hate you for reading this.

The intro tricks you with a knockoff retro FPS tutorial featuring a guy who sounds like me if I had a sinus infection and a misdemeanor record in another universe. Then the game throws you into bright alien worlds filled with creatures that look like rejected Pokémon designs drawn by a hungover intern. And I’m sitting there thinking, “This is trash. This is absolute trash.” But like, the gourmet kind. The trash you dig out of the bin at 3 a.m. because it still smells good.

And speaking of trash, Morty is a gun now. Let’s not gloss over that little nugget of cosmic horror. I pick up this gun and it talks like Morty but calls itself Kenny. Like, buddy, if you’re going to reinvent yourself, at least choose a name with some dignity. Kenny is the name of a guy who sells fake AirPods on Facebook Marketplace. Anyway, he won’t shut up. None of the guns shut up. The entire world won’t shut up. It’s like playing inside a podcast recorded in a padded room.

Combat? Look, the regular enemies are basically cardboard cutouts with guns, but the Bosses slap you around like you owe them rent money. First one killed me a few times, and I thought the game was broken. Turns out it’s just expecting you to, you know, get good.

The weapons are fun, varied, and absolutely unstable. Some of their best upgrades are hidden away in chests, because apparently the developers thought “Hey, what if we put essential character progression behind scavenger hunts designed by an eldritch prankster?” I found most of them anyway, because I’m smarter than the average player. So if you miss them, that’s on you. Or on the level designer. Or on Morty. Let’s blame Morty.

The level design is incredible. No joke. That part is genuinely impressive. It’s like navigating through a psychedelic interplanetary theme park built by someone who both understands game design and deeply resents the player. I scoured these planets like a space raccoon hopped up on plutonium. Still more satisfying than anything I’ve done with Morty this week.

The story is simple, the pacing is solid, and every gun has its own running commentary, which is brilliant because I get bored easily. I swapped guns mid-dialogue just to watch them bicker. It’s like Thanksgiving dinner but with more murder and fewer emotional consequences.

Visually, the game looks like what would happen if a rainbow had a baby with a hallucination. It’s gorgeous. It’s loud. It’s excessive. It’s perfect. The alien designs could use more variety, but whatever, it’s still more original than 90% of modern sci-fi.

Technically, the game ran flawlessly on my rig (AMD 5950X with NVidia 5070). Smooth framerate @1440p (~120fps), no crashes, only a few tiny bugs like falling off the map, which honestly feels like a friendly reminder that gravity still works.

Look, I could insult this game all day, but the truth is: it’s great. It’s a mess, but it’s a fun mess. Like Morty’s life. Or your search history. Or my garage.

Would I recommend it? Absolutely. Would I insult you for enjoying it? Also absolutely. Would I play a sequel? Only if Morty stays a gun.

IT'S EARLY. A lot of y'all are a bit too harsh on such a new game. The roadmap looks very promising and so far the update frequency shows a very active dev team. So here are my thoughts.

1. My biggest issue is the waves/physics. They certainly are not bad, however, the ships all seem way too light as if they did not have much mass to them. Even smaller waves rock them back and forth much more than they should. Even with the biggest ships in the game. They should pitch roll and yaw a bit slower and manage the water better. So far, there are not any splashing visuals for when a ship rolls over a breaking wave and crashes back into the water either. Instead, a strange looking void opens up in the water and it passes around the ship smoothly. If they can get rid of that and make some nice, large detailed splashes, and have water spray all over the boat and rush across the decks, it would be amazing. Also, in certain harbors like Rost, the waves should be minimal in there considering how isolated it is from the main sea. So localized wave quantities and strength should also be addressed. Lastly, the wake behind your boat, especially larger ones, needs to last for way longer, like several hundred feet behind the ship. Wakes should also have detrimental affects to docked ships when a jerk wants to go full speed through Rost Harbor and crunch everyone else's hulls alongside the dock walls lol.

2. Still related to the waves a lot, is the sound. When I go through a storm, and large waves, I want to hear immensely loud, violent slamming sounds of metal hulls crashing back into water and splashing out sprays of water all over the front of the ship and onto the windows. Inside the ship in first person should be some creaking and stretching of wood and metal, maybe items being shifted around the interior as the boats are tossed around, etc. Sound is everything. Things like the thunder already sound great. But the ocean is terrifyingly loud in a storm. The water doesn't feel scary when it lacks it's horrifying noises.

3. Lighting. Even on max graphics, spotlights and nav lights, work lights etc do not illuminate the water. I imagine this is already being fixed, but until then, its very hard to see anything at night around you. Interior lights look oddly dull when you look at them while they are on. They light up the cabin well but don't really look like they are turned on. Lighting is probably the biggest and most overlooked aspect of what people consider "amazing graphics", and so, if the devs can hit the nail on the head with the lighting, it will be incredible. They need to be much brighter and more rich in color. The navigation lights should have a nice red and green glow along the water at night and be very visible from far away. (If weather allows of course)

4. The map is not perfectly 1:1 with the actual world. There are some areas of land or shallow water, reefs, etc not marked visually on the map that you will run into on occasion when doing things like using autopilot. So the map simply needs an accurizing update. Speaking of auto pilot, being able to save routs would be GREAT. Set it and forget it and you can switch between routs for whatever you need, like port to port trips, restocking fish farms, etc. 

5. Water hoses are wayyyy way way too under powered. On actual rescue/fire boats, they can spray solid jets of water literally hundreds of feet while moving several knots. Spraying while moving in the game really hurts your range and it's already not that great to begin with. These sprayers IRL are extremely powerful. they blast them from sea level on top of oil rigs when needed. So it needs a strength boost of a good 10-12x. 

6. Flames. The fires need big thick towers of smoke and much louder burning sounds. The boats in distress should occasionally be accompanied by oil spills around the boat and even water soaked with gas and oil thats on fire around the boat. The smoke is not only a visual necessity but a great visual cue to where the distressed boat is if you are navigating lots of sand bars and islands and can't spend a bunch of time looking at the map while you weave around hazards to reach the boats.

Those are my biggest concerns. The gameplay itself in regards to progression and what not is a different topic and probably a bit more subjective so I am not gonna get into that. I'm sure there is plenty of work going towards that area already to begin with. Some smaller things I personally would like to see are as follows:

1. More detailed cockpits when applicable. I like buttons, lights, screens, controls, things to fiddle with and get more of a realistic full fidelity control experience with each ship. It already is pretty good. But I'm picky. As many buttons, switches and things to tinker with as possible is great. Even light switches in each room, actual engine rooms with valves and control panels, kind of like some of the stuff you see built in the game Stormworks (Very different game, but still can be learned from).

2. Some of the ships from Deadliest Catch, whether they are replicas or ships inspired by the real ones. Crab/ Lobster fishing with pots in general would be SO COOL. And getting to toss out a hook and rope in each pot from the buoy than dumping all the crabs out onto the table, etc. I've seen a lot of people really wanting crab and lobster fishing added, and I know there is a crab boat in the roadmap. But getting to use some of the boats from Deadliest Catch would be really fun.

3. Ropes for towing boats, tethering to your buddies ships things like that, great feature that could be used for a lot of mission stuff and expand into towing barges of supplies, oil rigs, etc. Similarly would be tug boats to push and pull larger ships to assist them in docking or in rescues. 

4. Give windshield wipers a little squeaky noise when the seas are relatively calm and quiet but its raining. 

5. FOV adjustment. In first person the ships feel a tiny bit too in your face. Interiors feel a little claustrophobic as well. Could also be that the human characters are ever so slightly big too, and maybe need a slight hitbox adjustment.

6. BIG SHIPS. I know plenty more ships are coming and many much larger, so I just want to add emphasis. A great fleet of dozens of very diverse ships will be amazing and allow for so many different things to do in the game and especially multiplayer.

7. Missions based off of/inspired by real events. A good example would be an oil rig emergency mission based off of the Deepwater Horizon disaster. 

8. Potentially submarines

9. Coast Guards ships.

10. Emergency transport helicopters. (potentially a slippery slope that might take too much attention away from the boats and the ocean, so it should not be a priority for a good long while but it would be cool).

11. Maybe some heelies for my character or a skateboard. Takes too long to walk to the fishery at Rost lol.

12. Detailed unloading of caught fish/crabs at the docks.

13. I have not yet played multiplayer, but if it does not have proximity chat, I'm gonna need that added asap. Prox chat makes so many games exponentially better and hilarious.

14. Diverse horn sounds for different ships.

15. Increase the range at which you can start hauling buoys out of the water by a few yards just for some better usability and rougher water conditions.

16. Ice forming on the ships rails and edges in cold and windy conditions just like IRL. Accompanied by sledgehammers to remove it.

17. Brief and simple but enjoyable animation for climbing up and down ladders or boarding onto boats for a bit more realism and immersion. Same goes for NPC's. 

18. Fully interactable environments on ships and at docks. For example, any chairs/benches should have an option to sit on them, lie down in beds, etc. 

19. Maybe a manual docking feature where you can tie the ropes yourself. (Potentially a feature in settings for the players who prefer the current automatic docking mechanism)

Vorab: Ich weiß das Game ist schon über ein Jahr alt und es ist auch bereits ein neues erschienen, weswegen dann der Bilder-Upload für dieses Game eingestellt wurde. Aber ich halte es für mich persönlich trotzdem mal für angebracht ein "neutrales" Feedback abzugeben.
Desweiteren ist alles, was ich nachfolgend verfasse, rein mein Standpunkt der Sicht und Dinge über dieses Spiel und spiegelt nicht die Meinungen anderer "unbedingt" wieder.

Nun zum wesentlichen. Ich kategorisiere diese Rezension in 2 Hauptgruppen. Zum einen die Non-Creative (nicht kreativen) Ansichten und zum anderen die Creative (kreativen) Ansichten des Spiels.

Non-Creative Ansichten:
Dieses Game ist für alle Spieler eigentlich sehr gut spielbar. Kaum Bugs, Lags, Glitches, whatever. Zumindest habe ich bisher nur ein Bug kurzweilig gehabt. Sowas wie die KI rennt auf ein zu, die Gegner-KIs stossen zusammen und wiederholen sich in der Sache. Hatte ich aber auch schon in den WWE 2Kxx Games auf xBox360. Machen die zum Glück selten. Auch gibt es genug Modis und Matchtypen, dass Gamern nicht langweilig wird (mit einer Ausnahme, aber dazu komme ich bei den Creative Ansichten). Viele Originale, Titeln, etc. Rundum gesagt... für 0815 Spieler (Spieler die auf eigene Erstellung von Wrestlern, Schildern, Logos, etc. verzichten können) ist das Game ein komplett funktionsfähiges Game geworden. Wäre zu empfehlen für sie.

Creative Ansichten:
Ja wo fange ich da an? Gut ich fange mal mit der "Ausnahme" an, wie beim Non-Creavtive Ansichten erwähnt.
Ganz simple gesagt, für welche die auf Kreativität stehen und lieber mit CAWs (Create A Wrestler (zu dt.: Superstar erstellen)) in eigenen Shows, mit eigenen Logos im hochqualitativen Design zocken, wäre das Game nix mehr. Hat 2 Gründe warum.
1.) Wie bei "Vorab" erwähnt, neigt 2K/WWE/... dazu nachdem ein neues WWE Game erscheint, die Uploadseite für das dann auslaufende Game einzustellen, um es für das Neue zu verwenden. Was schwachsinnig ist. dazu später mehr.
2.) Das integreierte Bild-Erstellungs-Programm (BEP) ist noch schlechter als das von den WWE Games der xBox360 Konsole (ob bei Playstation das selbe drin war wie bei xBox360 weiß ich nicht). Dort konnte man immerhin Pixel für Pixel arbeiten und auch Pixel entfernen. Geht in diesem Spiel überhaupt nicht. Auch der so genannte Schlagschatten Effekt ist absolut für die Tonne. Um es für Leute ohne Bildbearbeitungskenntnissen bildlich vorstellbar zu erklären. Schlagschatten ist ein Farbverlauf von einer Farbe zu Transparenz (durchsichtig) in der Form der Schrift/Logo/Symbol/Motive/usw. Bei denen ist Schlagschatten folgendes: Schrift und dann einen ganz dicken Filzstift nehmen und versuchen einen Rahmen entlang der Schriftlinie zu zeichnen mit zittrigen Händen. So in etwa stellen die sich einen Schlagschatten Effekt vor scheinbar.

Bleiben wir beim BEP. Da dieses das von mir am meist zu beanstandenste Problem dort ist und dann geht es nochmal kurz zu der 2K Bild Uploadseite.
Was beim BEP noch zu negativ aufstieß bei mir ist der enorme Mangel an Schriftarten. Vor allem an unterschiedlichen Schriftarten. Wenn ich Lügen darf, ich glaub es sind maximal 10 Fonts (Schriftarten) eingebaut in das Game für Logos und Schilder etc.. Viel zu wenig. Wäre wenigstens die Möglichkeit gegeben Fonts die man auf der Festplatte hat hochzuladen (Ingame wohlbemerkt) wäre es ja noch ok. Dann wäre es kein Drama. Aber so.... nee nee. Es wäre auch schön gewesen, wenn man das Material während der Logo/Schild/... Erstellung auswählen könnte statt prinzipiell nur für Titel/Koffer/usw.
Ich könnte mich da noch weiter verlieren bei dem Bild-Erstellungs-Programm, aber ich denke mal, man hat verstanden.

So. Jetzt noch einmal kurz zu der 2K Bild Upload Geschichte und dann Zusammenfassung.
Ich verstehe nicht... ich wiederhole... ICH... VERSTEHE... NICHT... wieso 2K/WWE/... die Bild-Uploadseite jedes Jahr auf's Neueste für ältere WWE Games schliesst. Das ist so sinnfrei, wie keine Ahnung was. Stattdessen wäre es sogar "profitabler", wenn Sie diese offen ließen. Es ist ja nun mal kein Geheimnis, dass manche WWE Games schlecht ausfallen und dann manche wieder gut. Also warum immer nur auf das neue Pferd setzen, wenn das alte Pferd noch durchaus was zu bieten hat. Oder halt hätte. Aber dadurch verbaut man sich das. Ich wünschte mir echt, dass die eine Uploadseite machen, wo man Auswahlmöglichkeiten hat, für welches Spiel das Bild hochgeladen werden soll. Am Ende könnte es immernoch (worauf die ja aus sind und ebenfalls kein Geheimnis ist) gut Geld einspielen für Ihre Geldbörse.

Lange reden kurzer Sinn... die Zusammenfassung.
Für einfache Spieler die einfach nur spielen wollen und auf Kreativmodis pupen können, ist dieses Spiel im ganzen TopFit. Habt Spass mit.
Für die Spieler die Kreativ sich austoben wollen würden und das ohne Uploader... rate ich dringends davon ab. Ihr werdet überhaupt nicht glücklich werden. Ich wurde es auch nicht.
Dennoch empfehle ich das Game, weil es im gesamten komplett spielbar ist.

Darksiders II: Deathinitive Edition — Величие и Грусть Воплощенного Хаоса

Общая оценка: 8/10 — Великолепный представитель жанра action-adventure с огромным миром и глубочайшей проработкой главного героя, которому, однако, не чужды технические и дизайнерские шероховатости.
Кому понравится: Поклонникам Zelda-like игр, метроидвании, фанатам первого Darksiders, тем, кто ценит мрачный фэнтези-сеттинг и кастомизацию персонажа.

Сильные стороны:

1. Игра за Смерть — это невероятно.
Главное достоинство игры— это её протагонист. Если Война из первой части был грубой силой, то Смерть — это элегантная смертоносность. Его анимации, манеры речи и боевой стиль (парные камаки-серпники) создают ощущение невероятной мощи и грации. Он харизматичен, циничен, но при этом его мотивация (искупить вину брата) делает историю глубоко личной и трогательной.

2. Глубина геймплея и прокачка.
Darksiders 2— это не просто "клинок-да-загадки". Это полноценная Action/RPG с обширным деревом талантов (две основные ветки — воин-заклинатель и ассасин), системой лута (оружие и броня имеют характеристики и случайные свойства), и крафтом. Возможность собрать свой уникальный билд, подходящий под стиль игры, добавляет десятки часов к реиграбельности.

3. Огромный, разнообразный мир.
В отличие от более линейного первого Darksiders,здесь вас ждут несколько масштабных миров-хабов (Царство Мёртвых, Забытые земли и др.), которые исследуются в духе "метроидвании". Вы постоянно будете возвращаться к старым локациям с новыми способностями, чтобы открыть потайные области. Это создаёт прекрасное чувство прогресса и освоения мира.

4. Классические дангеноны и головоломки.
Формула"The Legend of Zelda" здесь соблюдена на отлично: вы находите новый гаджет (например, Призрачный Клинок), который не только помогает в бою, но и является ключом к головоломкам в подземельях. Сами подземелья продуманы великолепно, а боссы в конце — это масштабные и зрелищные испытания.

5. "Deathinitive" — достойный апгрейд.
Издание включает в себя все DLC,переработанную графику (более детальные текстуры, улучшенное освещение), все заклинания и костюмы изначально в игре. На ПК и современных консолях игра выглядит и работает стабильно.

Слабые стороны:

1. Технические несовершенства.
Даже в"Deathinitive" издании остались баги. Изредка встречаются вылеты, проблемы с камерой в узких пространствах, а на некоторых платформах могут проскакивать провалы в FPS. Это не катастрофа, но может раздражать.

2. Затянутость середины игры.
Особенно это чувствуется во второй половине.Некоторые квесты носят откровенно "фетч-квестовый" характер ("принеси 3 предмета", "активируй 4 камня"). Чувство эпического путешествия иногда сменяется ощущением рутины.

3. Баланс сложности.
При правильной прокачке и удачном луте Смерть может стать непобедимой машиной,что снижает вызов в конце игры. С другой стороны, некоторые боссы на высоких уровнях сложности могут требовать излишнего гринда.

4. Не все головоломки одинаково хороши.
Хотя большинство головоломок интересные,находятся и такие, решение которых неочевидно и может заставить надолго застрять, прерывая поток игры.

Вердикт:

Darksiders II: Deathinitive Edition — это культовая игра, которую должен попробовать каждый любитель жанра. Несмотря на технические огрехи и некоторую затянутость, её достоинства с лихвой их перевешивают.
Это игра с душой, с одним из самых харизматичных протагонистов в игровой индустрии, с гениальным миксом экшена, РПГ и исследования. Вы на десятки часов погрузитесь в мрачную и величественную вселенную, где самый младший из Всадников Апокалипсиса доказывает, что даже у Смерти может быть честь и чувство долга.

Ставлю твердую "четвёрку" и рекомендую к покупке со скидкой, если вас не пугают небольшие технические шероховатости.

With nearly 100h in, I finally decided to write a short review: 

What I like about the game: 
- different heroes with very different abilities and troops. Each plays very differently and allows different strategies
- the maps are fantastic and I love that positioning your units is key to be successful
- the artwork (I am talking about the finished art) is just beautiful
- there is a time-out, that pairs you with the AI, if you cannot find a PVP match within a certain period of time (really important due to the still limited playerbase)
- the generous login rewards and in game rewards (but see comment on lootboxes in general below)
- no seasons (yet); you rank up permanently, if you win enough games and as such play against opponents with similar skill/collection

What I don't like about this game:
- I more and more dislike lootboxes/microtransactions. I bought the steam summer sale. It allowed me to have a better collection from the start and a better playing experience than starting from scratch, I think. So far, so good...
However for potential expansions,  I would prefer to pay a fixed amount and get the full expansion set. The cards could be unlocked while playing the game, giving you long-time motivation, instead of anxiety opening what you don't want or need to improve your current deck. 

On a sidenote:
- that the art is unfinished doesn't impact play
- I don't think the game is unbalanced (anymore). Sure some matchups are harder than others, but that's part of the package having heroes with different abilities and armies. I play mostly green, but not because it is particularly strong, more because its suits my playstyle.

The story is sprinkled with corporate infighting, extramarital affairs, and of course murder. There's also some whimsy, with lots of animal pictures to sort through and some unique gimmicks, like fake Slack messages to sift through.

If I had to criticize, it'd be these things, keeping in mind that this is still definitely a game worth trying:

- They should've leaned into the animal theming in the story. It starts with the wacky premise of a corporation trying to make technology that lets you talk to animals, but it doesn't really go anywhere. So you end up with a fun but very grounded story about corporate intrigue, and then sometimes you see a picture of a horse. Given the setup, the story could've felt more special.
- There are perhaps too many clues for a few of the solves. There were a few times when I thought I made a really clever inference based on limited info, but then it was confirmed by a redundant clue that made it feel less special. I wanted to feel like I was making a stretch.
- The ending is a difficulty spike, which I can respect, but the logic and evidence is very fiddly, which I didn't like.

《A Case of Fraud》是一款有趣的类《[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2754380/The_Roottrees_are_Dead/]The Roottrees are Dead[/url]》推理解谜游戏。

“宠物翻译”技术初创公司Zoolingo的女总裁失踪了，而作为私家侦探的主角，必须在不能亲自问询相关证人的情况下，破解这一桩谜案，而要破解案件，就要从理解Zoolingo的公司结构开始。核心目标确实就和《The Roottrees are Dead》（以下简称《Roottree》）差不多，只不过推的不是“家族树”，而是公司内部的“职位层次树”。而由于这是一个和宠物有关联的公司，所以员工们的宠物当然也是重要的公司成员，因此它们也在要推理的范围之内。

每正确推理出三个人物/宠物的身份和对应位置，游戏就会确认这三个身份正确，很经典的“[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/653530/Return_of_the_Obra_Dinn/]奥伯拉丁[/url]”模式，也被《Roottree》沿用。而本作大致分成几个阶段，当推理出的身份数量到达了一定阈值，就能获得新的证据，这点也很像《Roottree》。

但是除了这些相似之处之外，我认为本作和《Roottree》有一个核心的不同。《Roottree》的玩法循环中一个核心部分是“[b]检索[/b]”，也就是需要玩家自行提取相关关键词并在“搜索引擎”中进行检索，只有在正确的地方搜索正确的词才能获得新的关键证据，而本作中并没有这样的玩法，玩家只需要深入阅读、理解和分析手里的证据即可。

虽然我不认为两种做法有什么绝对意义上的优劣之分，但至少我个人在玩有“检索”玩法的推理作品时，总会有些检索环节把我卡住。在这类游戏的前期，玩家什么都不知道，所以搜什么都可以出来新东西，这个时候是这类玩法最新鲜有趣的时候，但在后期，玩家往往有确切的想要知道的信息，但是又不知道要怎么搜，游戏中的“搜索引擎”也不可能灵敏到真的能理解你具体想要什么。就算你想要一步步“逼近”，有些时候游戏能给玩家的反馈就只是“没搜到”或者“搜到”，毕竟不可能真的有那么多时间精力去设计更多的“中间”搜索结果。

这就是这种特定的“检索”玩法最本质的矛盾：能不能搜出来东西完全取决于设计师有没有在这个关键词后面放东西，所以本质上“不可预测”，在真的去搜之前，你可能永远不会知道会搜出来什么样的结果。除了靠直觉，或者什么都搜一遍，好像也没什么很好的解决“卡关”的办法。

而本作没有检索环节，自然也就没有这个问题。嗯，所以上面这一段完全就是我借题发挥，这点我承认，但是把这个写出来也是希望抛砖引玉，虽然我个人觉得要突破这个核心瓶颈，要么需要设计一种完全不同的玩法框架，要么可能就必须得用AI等数据科学的方式去填补上面所说的“中间结果”才行。说不定已经有人用AI试过了，但目前至少好像没有成功到能传递到我耳中程度的作品。

那么说完这个问题，接下来就谈到本作具体的推理谜题设计。虽然我之前说本作分了几个阶段，但本作在大体上还是非常“非线性”的，在所有39个身份中，只要解出15个就能获得全部证据，所以至少也有20多个是可以按任意顺序推理的，当然这里只是指不会缺证据，具体当然还是有些比较容易，有些只能后面用排除法推。要解开所有身份，除了利用表面上的文字和图像等信息，有些看似“隐形”的信息也很重要，比如[b]证据的发现位置[/b]。

从纯推理谜题的角度来说，我觉得本作的设计是很出色的，线索给得很足，线索之间基本不会有单一的“弱联系”，要么就有很多弱联系来佐证这种联系不是巧合，要么就有一条虽然难找，但是却具有决定性的强联系。由于我很喜欢本作的谜题设计，我还写了一个（英文）指南，详细阐述我的推理过程，如果感兴趣的话可以看一看：

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3604054999

（当然为了写指南，我重新游玩并整理了一遍整个流程，因此游戏时长比实际要长，实际上初见差不多4小时左右）

但是还有一个方面，那就是叙事。在谈到《Roottree》这款游戏时，有些玩家觉得那款游戏的剧情不太突出，一切都只是经典的“豪门风云”。怎么说呢，我并不认为没有传统意义上的悬疑叙事就不能做推理解谜，但我还是好奇本作会做到什么程度。在本作中，玩家最后是真的需要破解我一开始所说的那个案件，而不只是推理身份，但这部分推理和前面的身份推理并没有衔接得很好，因为本作犯人的作案手法和动机还是很简单，我感觉有一大堆人的身份都不用推，都可以看出来是谁干的，并没有很好地建立起“在破案前必须推理身份”的这个理由，所以感觉两者就是分开的。

总而言之，本作从纯谜题设计的角度来看，在推理解谜作品当中可以说是比较出色，主要值得称道的是给出线索的严谨性。不过在推理玩法和叙事的结合上，感觉还是有提升的空间。

结论：[b]推荐[/b]。

A great detective game with total number of 200 written and unique cases to be solved. However, your experience can vary much depending on what mode you gonna play. It nicely combines detective aspect and home invasion elements — you solve the cases during your run but still try to survive. It also had kinda fun ending, now it's replaced. The next mode I would love to talk about is detective mode which disables the killers so you could totally dive into detective stuff without any threats. It makes the game so relaxing, and the great addition to it is the paused menu music — lovely ambient. This mode is actually hard, it's gonna take a lot of runs before you finally beat it but the process feels great unlike following modes. Normal mode turns the game into paranoia where you fully focus on threats, making non-stop defensive actions, minimizing solving of cases which causes the lack of enjoyment. It requires from you to create a complete list of all the cases solved in advance to use it each run without thinking 'cause you just have to know all the answers otherwise you have no chance to beat it. And yeah, there're no saves whilst every run takes 3–3,5 hours. Speaking of nightmare mode, I don't know why it even exists. It's absolutely unbeatable 'cause each run is 4–5 hour long, bugged, hella RNG based, without right to make a slightest mistake. I've beaten it only by backing up game save files, that is ridiculous how unbalanced and unfair the mode is. If you really want to enjoy the game, you should play only casual and detective modes, they're great but the others... well, good luck.

Back in the late 90's and early 00's you used to be able to buy a gaming magazine that would come with a disk. On that disk would be demo's of various upcoming games. Before the release of the original Sudden Strike game, I had TWO demo's of it and I replayed them many times.

The original was fantastic. Its biggest and most obvious flaw to me was that the AI seemed to not suffer fog of war, and so you'd often get shot up before you could see the enemy. But it was still an awesome game.

Then Sudden Strike 2 came along in 2002 and oh boy... Everything great about Sudden Strike but better. AI fog of war issue resolved, more accurate damage models for tanks, and a few other features that just made the game more enjoyable.

Steam didn't even exist back then, but I guarantee I put thousands of hours into both games.

Sudden Strike 3 came along a few years later... I can't really give it a fair review as I only played it for a short spell. I didn't enjoy it, the graphics seemed to be painful to the eye, and it would crash or bug out on me.

When Sudden Strike 4 released on Steam, I was very excited to see what it would become.

... It's shite. Sorry, I can't bring myself to enjoy this game.

I have installed and uninstalled Sudden Strike 4 a total of three times now, and each time I just end up getting frustrated with some really simple issues and then going off to burn a few hours in one of the older titles.

The only way I can describe it in short is that they took a working formula and somehow broke it. The gameplay feels like they're trying to keep some of the original charm of Sudden Strike but with modern graphics, which should work, but it just sort of... doesn't. I am going to push through some more missions just to see if things get better, but at this stage I'm not seeing it.

Today was my third attempt at giving Sudden Strike 4 a try, and here are *some* of my findings:

1. The voices are genuinely awful.

When you play the tutorial, you are given a German half-track full of German infantry... but the commander who is narrating/instructing you is American, and when you complete the tutorial you get an anecdote that is read out by someone who is British. And yet when you select your troops and move them around, they sound German as you'd expect. How do you f that up??

2. The mission briefings make me feel sad inside.

Go back to Sudden Strike or Sudden Strike 2 and look at the briefings. You would receive a relatively detailed (but not overcooked) explanation of the situation and the mission, and then given your objectives. In Sudden Strike 4, the second Allied mission brief literally goes like this: "Secure the left flank. Secure the right flank. Capture the village." Zero effort went into this, and it killed part of my soul to go through it.

3. Some of the ammunition figures are... mental.

Submachinegunners carrying over 1,000 rounds of ammunition. Do you have any idea how heavy ammunition is? For a Tompson SMG, one bullet weighs about 15 grams. So you're suggesting they are carrying 15 kilograms of ammunition, and I have no idea where they plan on stashing it. For a belt-fed MG that would be a substantial load. Modern day troops tend to carry around 300 rounds depending on the situation etc. I appreciate that the infantry ammunition count on the original Sudden Strike games was probably a bit off, but we should be getting this at least close to being correct by now.

4. The maps and the missions have shrunk in the wash.

Everything seems so enclosed. The OPERATION OVERLORD map for example is minuscule; they crammed the paratroopers that did the behind enemy lines bits into the same mission/map as the beach landings, and it's done poorly. You don't feel like there is any grand scale to it. In fact, the objectives that the paratroopers captured are basically just around the corner from the bunkers that the beach landing troops push through. I'd also like to complain about the rather pathetic number of troops that you get on the beach. If you're going to make a D-Day themed mission, you either need to make it focus on one particular area or - in the case of Sudden Strike - make it feel like a grand scale battle as it should.

5. Multiplayer/Skirmish feels like I'm playing DOTA.

When did this tug-of-war point-scoring type of game mode become popular? Did I miss the memo? When I play a multiplayer game of Sudden Strike, I expect to be spending a lot of time moving various units around a vast map with a realistic expectation that I'm going to be sitting in this chair for a couple of hours. My first Skirmish battle against the AI was over in about 10 minutes (literally) because the enemy AI won on points. I didn't even lose any troops, let alone get caught up in any sort of campaign or firefight. And get rid of this thing of spending points to spawn more units - I captured a train station and then apparently I can spend currency (that automatically fills up from what I can tell) to spawn a Tiger tank that gets delivered by train. You have no idea how uncool this mechanic is when compared to the earlier Sudden Strike games.

Conclusion:

On the whole, this game took what made Sudden Strike good and somehow broke it by turning it into what they think the fans want. The only reason (as far as I can tell) that this has worked is because most gamers of today weren't even born when the original title was released. Seriously - many of my work colleagues are post-2000 babies, and it makes me feel old.

I would like to clarify that this is more than a nostalgia hit. Sudden Strike and Sudden Strike 2 have not aged well at all. But this genuinely feels like Sudden Strike 4 could have taken all of the goodness from the earlier games and slapped some decent graphics on it to create an absolute win, but instead it's been dumbed down and turned into some sort of Hollywood-like mess.

I am a die hard Sudden Strike fan who virtually grew up with it and learned a lot of what I know about World War 2 weapons/vehicles/etc from it, and I cannot recommend Sudden Strike 4. I see Sudden Strike 5 on the horizon, and I remain optimistic.

AKIBA’S TRIP: Undead & Undressed is a quirky action role-playing game developed by Acquire and set in the vibrant district of Akihabara, Tokyo’s real-life hub of otaku culture. The game combines beat-’em-up combat with satire, humor, and social commentary, delivering a bizarre yet memorable experience. It’s a mix of urban exploration, character interaction, and unconventional combat that makes it stand out among Japanese action RPGs.

The story follows a young man named Nanashi, who is transformed into a “Synthister” — a kind of modern vampire that feeds on the life energy of others. To survive, he joins a group of vigilantes who hunt these creatures across Akihabara. The premise is as absurd as it sounds: the only way to defeat Synthisters is by exposing them to sunlight — achieved by stripping off their clothes during combat. Despite its silliness, the narrative surprisingly touches on themes of identity, connection, and the subcultures that define modern youth.

Gameplay revolves around exploring a faithfully recreated Akihabara, filled with real-world shops, billboards, and eccentric characters. Players can visit cafés, buy anime merchandise, or engage in random street fights. The city acts as both a playground and a social hub, immersing players in otaku life. Dialogue choices and relationship-building with party members add a visual novel flavor, providing multiple endings depending on the player’s decisions.

Combat is fast-paced and deliberately over-the-top. Players target enemies’ clothing — head, torso, and legs — using quick attacks to weaken and strip them. Each battle becomes a mix of timing, positioning, and managing multiple opponents. Though the concept is comedic, the system has genuine depth thanks to equipment upgrades, weapon variety, and combo chains. However, the mechanics can feel clunky, and camera control occasionally hinders precision in crowded fights.

A defining aspect of Undead & Undressed is its humor. The game constantly pokes fun at Japanese pop culture, fandoms, and gaming tropes. Characters are self-aware, dialogue often breaks the fourth wall, and absurd situations are treated with a straight face. This tone won’t appeal to everyone — what some find witty and daring, others may see as juvenile or repetitive — but it undeniably gives the game its charm and personality.

Visually, the game captures Akihabara’s energy with colorful settings and recognizable landmarks, though its graphics and animations feel dated even for its release period. The soundtrack complements the quirky atmosphere, ranging from upbeat J-pop to techno battle themes. Voice acting, available in both English and Japanese, adds to the game’s comedic appeal, with characters leaning fully into the absurdity of the premise.

Ultimately, AKIBA’S TRIP: Undead & Undressed is a niche but entertaining title that thrives on its weirdness. It’s part parody, part love letter to otaku culture, and part chaotic street brawler. While its gameplay lacks polish and repetition sets in, its humor, unique concept, and eccentric world make it a cult favorite. For players seeking something unconventional, it delivers a wild, unapologetically strange experience that could only come from Japan.
