[b]1. 기자를 경험해볼 수 있는 독특한 컨셉[/b]

게임 타이틀 그대로, 이 게임은 플레이어가 한 언론사의 ‘편집장’이 되어 기사를 제작하고 내보내는 과정을 중심으로 진행된다. 기사 하나를 완성하기 위해 제목, 사진, 본문 등 모든 요소들이 유기적으로 맞물려야 하며, 이런 점들이 현실감을 더해준다. 자연스럽게 “이렇게 작성하면 내 의도가 제대로 전달될까?”, “이런 방향이라면 대중들이 좋아할까?” 같은 고민을 하게 만들며, 플레이어를 실제 편집장의 입장에 몰입시킨다.

특히 기사 작성을 위한 사진을 획득하게 되면, 플레이어는 ‘판매 이익을 중시한 선정적인 기사’를 낼 것인지, 아니면 ‘편집장으로서의 사명감을 갖고 진실을 알리는 기사’를 쓸 것인지를 스스로 선택해야 한다. 이처럼 단 하나의 사진이라도 어떤 의도로 접근하느냐에 따라 전혀 다른 방향의 기사로 이어질 수 있다.

예를 들어, 게임쇼의 수상 사진으로 게임 홍보 모델을 하고 있는 여성의 의상 노출을 중심으로 기사를 쓰거나, 자녀의 과로사로 시위 중인 부모를 담은 사진을 이용해 해당 기업을 오히려 칭찬하는 식의 기사도 작성 가능하다. 현실에서 있을 법한 왜곡 보도들을 체험하는 과정은 때론 불쾌감을 유발할 수 있지만, 바로 그 점에서 게임이 말하고자 하는 바가 선명해진다. 플레이어가 정직한 편집을 선택할 수도, 악의적인 방향으로 왜곡할 수도 있다는 자유도는 이 게임의 핵심 매력 중 하나다.

또한, 플레이어의 선택은 메인 스토리에도 큰 영향을 미친다. 행동에 따라 스토리는 여러 갈래로 나뉘며, 총 9종류의 엔딩을 제공한다는 점에서 분기형 구조의 재미도 충분히 느낄 수 있다. 다만 아쉬운 점은, 이 엔딩들이 겉보기엔 다양해 보여도 실제로는 A, A′, A″ 정도의 유사한 전개가 많아 극적인 차이는 크지 않다는 것이다. 그럼에도 불구하고 수집 요소로서의 만족감은 확실히 존재하며, 전 엔딩을 모아보는 재미도 제법 쏠쏠하다.

[b]2. 실제 성우를 기용한 풀더빙[/b]

이 게임은 텀블벅 펀딩을 통해 개발되었으며, BIC(Busan Indie Connect)와 같은 전시회에도 참여한 바 있는 1인 개발 작품이다. 이런 배경 때문에 처음에는 큰 기대 없이 플레이를 시작했지만, 사운드 면에서 예상보다 훨씬 풍부한 완성도를 뽐내고 있어 굉장히 놀랐다.

최근 AI 기술이 비약적으로 발전하면서 게임 개발에도 많이 도입을 시도해보는 추세인지라 자연스럽게 성우 대신 AI 기술이 사용되었을 거라 생각했는데, 비하인드 인터뷰를 통해 모든 음성이 실제 성우들의 녹음으로 제작되었음을 확인할 수 있었다.

플레이어가 조작하는 ‘편집장’을 제외한 모든 인물들이 풀더빙으로 표현되어 있어, 텍스트 기반 게임에서 흔히 느껴지는 루즈함이나 단조로움이 상당 부분 해소되었다. 무엇보다도 편집장의 선택에 따라 전개되는 다양한 상황 속에서 등장인물들의 감정, 분위기, 심리 상태 등이 음성을 통해 보다 직접적이고 생생하게 전달되다 보니, 몰입감이 크게 상승했다.

결과적으로 집중력이 끊기지 않은 채로 장시간 플레이를 지속할 수 있었고, 캐릭터 간 상호작용과 서사의 밀도 역시 음성 덕분에 더욱 견고하게 다가왔다. 사운드 퀄리티와 성우 연기의 힘이 얼마나 게임 경험에 영향을 줄 수 있는지를 다시금 실감하게 만든 요소였다.


단점

[b]1. 너무 기괴해서 마치 공포게임 같은 그래픽[/b]

이 게임의 시대적 배경은 1996년으로, 신문의 영향력이 상당했던 시기로 설정되어 있다. 이 때문인지 전체적인 그래픽은 흑백 톤으로 연출되어 시대적 분위기와 잘 어우러진다. 등장인물들도 실사에 가까운 그래픽 스타일로 표현되어, 게임의 아날로그 감성과 맞물리며 특유의 현실감을 형성하고 있다. 이런 표현 방식은 게임의 콘셉트와도 어울려 굉장히 좋은 방향성이라고 느껴졌다.

하지만 완전히 실사에 가깝지는 않은 탓인지, 일부 장면에서는 다소 기괴하다는 인상을 받기도 했다. 예컨대, 단순히 편집장과 두 명의 인물이 식사를 하는 장면임에도 불구하고, 묘하게 불쾌하고 오싹한 분위기가 느껴진다거나, 각 챕터 시작 시 자주 등장하는 아침 회의 씬에서 특정 기자가 공허하게 시선을 던질 때면, 의도하지 않은 공포감이 은근히 밀려온다. 게임을 플레이하면서도 몇 차례 흠칫 놀라는 순간이 있을 정도다.

다행히도 더빙이 들어가 있어 인물들의 목소리가 전달되면서 그 기묘한 분위기가 어느 정도 완화되었지만, 만약 음성까지 없었다면 공포 게임을 하고 있다는 착각마저 들었을 것 같다. 물론 이 부분이 게임 진행에 있어 치명적인 결함이나 오류는 아니다. 다만 개인적으로는 강한 호불호가 갈릴 수 있는 요소로 느껴졌기 때문에, 단점으로 언급했다.

[b]2. 직관적이지 않은 회차 분기점[/b]

앞서 언급했듯, 해당 게임에서는 여러 갈래의 엔딩을 경험할 수 있다. 그렇기에 1회차를 완료한 후의 일반적인 행동 패턴은 크게 두 가지로 나뉜다. 하나는 기존에 클리어한 챕터 중 마음에 들지 않는 결과를 수정하기 위해 재도전하는 것이고, 다른 하나는 새로운 엔딩을 보기 위해 분기점을 찾아가는 방식이다.

이 게임에서 분기점은 주로 새벽일보의 대표나, 초반부터 꾸준히 등장하는 보좌관등 중요 등장인물들과의 대화 속에서 형성된다. 따라서 1회차를 정독하며 플레이했던 유저라면, 분기점 이전의 대사들은 이미 모두 숙지하고 있어 굳이 다시 볼 필요는 없다.

때문에 자연스럽게 N회차 플레이에서 가장 강하게 드는 니즈는 “분기점이 발생하는 선택지로 곧바로 이동하고 싶다”는 것이다. 그러나 문제는 이 게임이 분기점이 어디에 있는지를 명확하게 표시해주지 않기 때문에, 유저가 직접 대화를 하나하나 넘기며 그 지점을 찾아야 한다는 데 있다.

이러한 불편함은 초반 1~2개의 엔딩을 수집할 때까지는 그리 크게 다가오지 않지만, N회차 플레이가 누적될수록 피로감이 급격히 증가한다. 개인적으로는, 이러한 문제를 해결하기 위해 시나리오 플로우 차트를 도입해 분기점으로 바로 이동할 수 있도록 하는 방식을 고려해볼 수 있다고 생각한다.

이는 메인 화면에서 지원해도 좋고, 게임의 분위기와 조화를 맞추기 위해 편집장의 방 안에 특정 오브젝트(스크랩북이나 캐비닛같은 오브젝트..?)로 설치하여 1회차를 완료한 유저에게만 제공하는 식의 접근 방식도 괜찮을 것 같다. 이처럼 소위 '딸깍' 시스템을 도입하여 반복 플레이의 번거로움을 줄이는 장치가 있다면, 엔딩 수집의 즐거움은 더욱 배가될 수 있을 것이다.


[가격]
​
정가 15,000원. 필자는 50% 할인된 7,500원에 구매했다. 개인적으로 생각했을 때 가성비를 중요하게 생각하는 게이머라면, 정가 구매는 다소 부담스러울 수 있다. 모든 도전과제를 클리어하더라도 약 6~7시간 정도의 플레이 타임밖에 나오지 않으며, N회차 성향이 아닌 게이머라면 1~2시간만에 엔딩 1개를 보고 더 이상 손대지 않을 확률이 높다.

다만 독특한 게임 방식, 자국 인디 게임이라는 점, 그리고 전반적으로 긍정적인 평가들을 고려했을 때 흥미가 생긴다면 할인 기간을 노려 짧고 굵게 즐기는 전략도 괜찮은 선택이 될 수 있다. 평가를 올리는 시점이 25년도 여름 할인인데, 지금도 50% 할인을 진행하고 있으니 게임에 조금이라도 흥미가 느껴졌다면 할인 타이밍에 구매하여 라이브러리에 넣어놓는 것도 좋은 선택이 될 수 있을 것 같다.


[도전과제]
​
난이도 - 下
필요 회차 - 9회차+

편집장의 도전과제 난이도는 전반적으로 어렵지 않은 편이다. 다만 앞서 단점 항목에서 언급했듯, 일정 수준의 노가다는 필수 불가결하다. 총 17개의 도전과제 중 무려 9개가 엔딩과 직접적으로 관련되어 있어, 최소한 9회차는 진행해야 전부 클리어할 수 있다.

워워, 여기서 9회차라는 키워드에 찍혀서 지레 겁먹을 필요는 없다. 특정 챕터부터 시작할 수 있는 기능을 지원하기 때문에 매번 처음부터 새로 시작할 필요가 없어 반복 플레이의 피로도가 그렇게 높은 편은 아니니 걱정하지 않아도 괜찮다.

엔딩 관련 도전과제를 하나씩 클리어하다 보면, 나머지 업적들도 자연스럽게 해금되는 경우가 대부분이라 따로 신경 쓸 필요는 없다. 따라서 1회차는 부담 없이 자유롭게, 자신의 선택에 따라 플레이하는 것이 좋다. 이후 분기점을 직접 탐색하고 싶다면 자율적으로 도전하면 되고, 빠르게 모든 엔딩을 보고 업적 수집을 마무리하고 싶다면 공략을 참고하면서 플레이하는 방법도 있다.

필자의 경우에는 [url=https://blog.naver.com/ladycalla/223244737882]LadyCALLA님의 공략[/url]을 참고했다. 해당 공략은 전체적인 흐름을 잘 설명하고 있으나, 일부 엔딩 루트는 잘못 표기된 부분도 있으니 주의가 필요하다. 잘못 설명되어 있는 루트의 경우 스팀 가이드의 댓글란을 통해 쉽게 해결이 가능하다. 도전과제 올클도 굉장히 수월하고, 플레이 타임도 짧고 간결하기 때문에 도전과제 수집을 중요하게 생각하는 유저라면 라이브러리에 추가해볼 만한 가치가 충분한 작품이다.


[총평]

[b]원인불명의 이유로 사망한 국회의원의 진실을 파헤치는 편집장이 되어보는 2D 포인트 앤 클릭 게임[/b]

이웃 블로거분의 포스팅을 우연히 보고 흥미가 생겨 구매했지만, 막상 손이 잘 가지 않아 3~4개월간 창고처럼 묵혀두었다가 이번 6월 중순이 되어서야 부랴부랴 꺼내 플레이를 마쳤다.

개인적으로는 신문보다는 네이버 실시간 검색어와 같은 온라인 뉴스에 더 익숙한 세대임에도 불구하고, 게임이 전달하고자 하는 메시지의 핵심은 명확하게 와닿았다. 흔히 말하는 ‘펜으로 사람을 죽인다’는 문장이 말하듯, 이 게임은 언론사의 권력과 그에 따른 책임, 그리고 하나의 기사로 인해 발생하는 대중들의 다양한 반응을 통해 언론인이 겪는 고충과 고뇌를 효과적으로 보여준다.

가장 인상 깊었던 부분은 편집장과 함께 일하는 세 명의 동료 기자들이다. 정의와 진실을 신념처럼 외치지만 정작 자신의 안전이 위협받는 상황 앞에서는 두려움에 흔들리는 이 기자, 자극적인 내용이라면 사실 여부를 떠나 조회수만을 좇는 현 기자, 그리고 정체를 의심케 할 만큼 특정 단체에 깊이 연루되어 있을 듯한 분위기를 풍기는 권 기자. 많지도 적지도 않은 세 명의 캐릭터들이 매 챕터마다 회의실에서 기사를 놓고 벌이는 논의는 현실감을 불러일으키기에 충분했다.

개발자의 비하인드 인터뷰에 따르면, 중동 지역을 배경으로 스파이 활동을 벌이는 기자 이야기나, 사람의 기억 속으로 들어가 조작과 편집을 하는 판타지 콘셉트 등 다양한 차기작 아이디어가 준비 중이라고 한다. 이후 작품도 이번 작품처럼 포인트 앤 클릭 장르를 유지할지는 아직 확실치 않지만, 이번 게임에서 보여준 강점들과 차후 개선될 요소들을 바탕으로, 더욱 확장된 세계관과 개성 있는 캐릭터들을 통해 데카트리게임즈만의 고유한 색채가 분명하게 자리잡길 기대한다.

This game has an interesting and unique aesthetic, really great character design and 2D animation, the menus and UI are fantastic, and the opening movie is a delight. It's another indie RPG where those are the best things about it. 
Visually, the 3D portions don't really stack up to its ambitious design choices and end up making the experience disjointed and meandering. Artifacting in cell-shaded character textures in the final release of a game is pretty egregious. It would literally have been a matter of exporting them again at a higher resolution. Crisp character portraits don't belong next to models whose textures look like they were exported from a resized image in MS Paint. Even putting a low-res pixelation filter over the 3D portions to create some visual unity and hide things like artifacts in textures and corners that don't connect would have saved it from many of my complaints.

Gameplay is very slow in the early portions. I haven't gotten past the first few areas but the general lack of selection in abilities and repeated animations makes the length of the RPG battles punishing. The open-level flying potions are somehow both too big and confining. Too much open space with not enough happening.  The character exploration segments are pretty okay but it makes me wonder why it's not just a menu since the character models aren't used for any animations. It seems like it was just another aspect that could have been cut in favor of making the rest of the game more fun.

I feel like this game is brushing up against greatness, it just doesn't push over in any of the categories that would give it a handhold to pull itself up by. The game needed the attention to detail in the finishing steps that just wasn't in the budget. It tried to be too many games at once and thusly failed at being a passable version of any game. More testing and time spent on thing like pacing of battles and levels would have saved this game.

Future War Tactics: SOF vs Alien Invasion aims to deliver a compact, grounded turn-based strategy experience centered around a small Special Operations Forces team confronting a steadily escalating extraterrestrial threat. QuadCom Interactive frames the conflict in a near-future setting tinged with mystery—reports of disappearances, strange atmospheric readings, and anomalous disturbances across the Ural region provide the ominous backdrop. The narrative setup is promising, creating an early sense of unease as your squad ventures into forests, derelict military buildings, and isolated rural zones that have become sites of alien interference. Although the story opens with intrigue, it quickly becomes clear that the game uses its narrative primarily as connective tissue between missions rather than as a fully fleshed-out dramatic arc. The tone is functional rather than cinematic, serving more to justify the alien incursions than to provide deep lore or character development.

The gameplay leans heavily into traditional turn-based tactics with familiar but dependable mechanics. You guide each soldier across gridded maps, managing action points, seeking cover, maintaining firing lines, and using a predictable class structure to define roles. The medic stabilizes wounded allies, the grenadier handles clustered enemies, the scout maneuvers quickly to flank, and the technician brings utility to the squad with gadgets and support tools. These archetypes aren’t groundbreaking, but they give the squad enough variety to form a cohesive strategic rhythm. Missions typically revolve around short, objective-driven deployments: clearing an area, holding a position, investigating alien structures, or surviving waves of hostiles. The smaller scope keeps the pace brisk and approachable, and the straightforward mission design may appeal particularly to players who prefer contained tactical challenges over sprawling, multi-layered campaigns.

However, this streamlined structure also reveals the limits of the experience. Maps often share similar visual identity, which can make missions blur together over time, and the fixed camera angle occasionally makes it harder to assess sightlines or enemy placement. The environments, while thematically consistent, lack the depth, dynamism, and tactile polish seen in bigger-budget tactical games. Combat encounters rely more on predictable patterns than emergent surprise, and the repetition becomes noticeable over the course of the campaign. The progression system mirrors this minimalist approach as well: upgrading gear and unlocking new perks provides small incremental improvements rather than dramatic, build-defining shifts. It’s enough to give a sense of forward motion, but it never transforms your squad into anything radically new.

Despite these limitations, there is an earnest charm to the game. The gritty military aesthetic, the muted color palette, and the understated sound design contribute to a sense of grounded tension. The aliens, though not revolutionary in their behavior, add enough variety to force occasional adjustments in tactics. The game’s difficulty curve is fair, leaning more toward accessibility than unforgiving challenge. This makes Future War Tactics suitable for strategy players who enjoy the genre but don’t necessarily want to commit to systems-heavy complexity or punishing stakes. The campaign’s modest length, likely sitting around a dozen hours, also helps prevent the repetition from becoming overwhelming.

Where the game struggles most is in production polish. Animations, environmental detail, and localization quality vary in consistency, occasionally breaking immersion. The story sequences lack dramatic impact, partly due to flat dialogue and partly due to the game’s overall restraint in presentation. These issues don’t render the experience unenjoyable, but they do reinforce the impression that this is a smaller project with limited resources—a title that focuses on core mechanics first and treats everything else with minimal embellishment. For players who value polish, storytelling, or audiovisual richness as much as strategic content, these shortcomings will stand out.

In the end, Future War Tactics: SOF vs Alien Invasion is a serviceable, straightforward turn-based tactical game that knows its scope and stays within it. It doesn’t reinvent the genre or push tactical depth to new heights, but it offers a contained, approachable campaign with reliable mechanics and a grounded tone. It’s the kind of game that scratches a tactical itch without demanding long-term investment, perfect for players who want the structure of an X-COM-like experience without the sprawling management layers or emotional gut punches. While its repetitive environments, modest presentation, and thin narrative keep it from rising above the pack, it fulfills its role as a compact, military-themed strategy title that delivers dependable tactical engagements against an alien threat.

[h1]94年に出ていた…かもしれない「Wolfenstein 3D」クローン[/h1]

[b]世にも珍しい「スペイン内戦」を題材とした、ファシスト軍団を薙ぎ払うレトロ風FPS。[/b]
とは言っても史実のスペイン内戦はファシスト、すなわちフランコ側が勝利しているし、対する共和国軍サイドは裏にソ連がいるしで連合vs枢軸(ナチス)のような勧善懲悪ではないので中々描くのが難しい。
本作でも「ファシストをぶちのめせ」的なコトは言っているものの、実際は謎のカルト教団およびファンタジー要素を盛り込むことで政治的主張は雑にぼかされている。
その結果、明確にスペイン内戦と言える要素は「主人公の武器がスペイン製のアストラ600やイギリスから輸入されたヴィッカース機関銃」「所々にファランヘ党のマークがある」ぐらいしかない。概ねWWIIゲームといった感じなので、そのあたりはあまり期待しない方が良いかもしれない。

[h1]Wolfenstein 3Dが『DOOM』の技術力で正統進化を遂げていたら…？[/h1]
本作は1990年代にアメリカで発売された…風の内容となっており、グラフィックなどもそれ相応の出来映え。流石に操作性やなんかは現代的にできるが、レベルデザインなどは当時っぽい感じの鍵集め型になっている。
またマップは主に正方形で構成されており古めかしい印象。もともとWolf3Dの次回作である『DOOM』が1993年に、Wolfenstein 3Dとなるはずだった『Rise of the Triad』が1994年に発売されているので、本作は「もしid SoftwareがDOOMを作らずに続編を作り続けていたら…？」「もしRise of the Triadが二次大戦FPSのまま完成していたら…？」というifに近いものがある。

当時のid software製ゲームの例に漏れず、本編を構成する3つのエピソードはそれぞれ独立して存在する方式。ゲームは任意セーブ・ロードが可能で、各エピソードごとに所有武器はリセットされる。
非線形のオープンフィールド型マップ、リロードシステム、パーティクルによるゴア表現なども90年代当時ぎりぎり実現できそうな技術が使われており、それっぽさのクオリティはそこそこ高い。

[h1]他ではあまり見慣れない、テーマならではの変わった武器種[/h1]
主人公は共和国サイドの兵士として、フランコ率いるファシスト反乱軍とその裏にいる謎のカルト勢力を倒すべく各地を戦い抜いていく。
武器としては銃剣、ピストル、サブマシンガン、ショットガン、ライフル、火炎放射器、マシンガン、ライフルグレネード、ダイナマイトの9種類が登場。ピストルがアストラ600という現在ではややマイナーな拳銃だったり、ライフルがボルトアクションだったりと時代相応のラインナップとなっている。
90年代FPSにしては珍しくプロジェクタイル弾で処理され、リロードシステムも完備。ショットガンは弾数が少なく、ライフルは装填が遅く、火炎放射器は巻き込まれやすく、マシンガンは取り回しが悪い…といった、武器それぞれの癖もあり、使いこなすのが楽しい。

[h1]良くも悪くも忠実にリスペクトされた、出来不出来の差が大きい各種エピソード[/h1]
本作は基本的に見た目通りのWolfenstein 3Dクローンであり、Wolfenstein 3Dのクローンとはつまり平面的な迷路マップをひたすら進むだけの殺風景なゲームである。本作もエピソード1の終わりごろまではまさにそういった感じで、正直なところ今遊んでもあまり面白いと感じられる内容ではない。
しかしエピソード2あたりからたまにオープンフィールドで塹壕戦や軍事基地攻略を行うパートが用意されるようになり、これはきちんと面白い内容。機銃掃射を避けながら塹壕を駆け抜けてトーチカを焼き払ったり、時折現れる戦車に苦戦したり、時には友軍と共に進軍したり…と、かの「メダルオブオナー」の楽しいパートのようなゲーム体験を味わうことができるようになっている。

しかしそういった楽しいマップも割合としては少な目で、後半になってもステージの多くは平坦な迷路構成。
部分的に「そうでない場所」がよく出来ているだけに、「Wolf3Dのクローンゲームであること」に惜しさを感じてしまう内容だ。

[h1]悪くはないけど、愛を受け止められるかが問われる[/h1]
特徴的なグラフィックや一部マップの楽しい野外環境など、楽しめる要素は用意されている一作。
ただし「90年代風」というテーマに囚われているが故の問題点も部分的に見受けられ、そういった部分ではやや難があるかもしれない。
また敵兵のすり抜けバグなどもちらほら存在しており、初期設定ではフリーエイムが無効になっているなど微妙に遊びづらい内容。

『Wolfenstein 3D』や『DOOM』、『Rise of The Triad』といったタイトルのお約束を良くも悪くもきちんと守っているので、適切に評価するには先にそのあたりの理解を進めておく必要がある。が、分かっている人であれば開発陣のやりたかったことはダイレクトに伝わってくるだろう。見た目の割にやや敷居の高いタイトル。



[b]ゲームを快適に遊ぶための諸設定[/b]
本作はインターフェイスが日本語に対応している。日本語に切り替えたい場合はメインメニュー左下の国旗をクリックして日の丸を選択することで切り替えが可能。
また、デフォルト設定のままゲームを始めると上下視点変更ができないのだが、開始時に「垂直マウスルック(Vertical Mouselook)」をオンに切り替えておくことでマウスを用いて快適に遊ぶことが出来るようになる。
たぶん開発陣としてはフリーエイムなど90年代には存在しない！という意志があったと思われるが、正直これがあるとないとではオープンフィールドでの快適さが大違いなのでなるべくオンにしておこう。

Very closely follows the Wolfenstein 3D formula, but is a much comfier experience. Wolf 3D, especially on higher skills, is an endurance test. By contrast, everything about this game feels cozy. The art style, the music, the design aesthetic, and the combat especially. It all makes for a very relaxing experience; but not a very challenging one.

I do have one little niggle. There are probably a few too many guns for a game this easy. You've got your pistol, SMG, shotgun, rifle, flamethrower, and machine gun, as well as dynamite and a knife. The game doesn't really need most of these. The SMG is more than capable of taking down every enemy, the pistol has utility for its headshot mechanic, and the shotgun is useful when you just need to delete something. The rifle, and especially the heavy weapons like the MG and flamer are really not needed. This isn't Wolf 3D, where you're rocking the chaingun from the word "GO!" until you run out of ammo. Having the extra weapons doesn't hurt or anything, but it definitely feels like clutter. That's really my only minor complaint.

On the flipside, I CANNOT sufficiently express my appreciation to the developer for including the option to play as a girl. It's such a little thing, but in games where there is almost no story or voicelines, being able to just... choose your gender, since it doesn't effect gameplay, is a wonderful addition. In such a male-dominated genre, I am super grateful.

「Sakura Hime」はロマンティックコメディを主体とするビジュアルノベルです。読書体験が主要要素であり、主人公と複数ヒロインの出会いおよび日常的な場面を中心に構成されています。

物語は簡潔です。対立は短時間で解消され、対話が進行を支えます。深度は限定的ですが、構造は安定しています。

音楽は穏やかにループします。注意を妨げません。効果音は最小限です。

ゲームプレイは標準的です。選択肢が関係性とエンディングに軽微な影響を与えます。インターフェースは理解しやすい設計です。

作品のトーンは軽快でややフレンドリーです。深刻なドラマはほとんどありません。短時間で中断可能です。

総合的に「Sakura Hime」は落ち着いたロマンティックノベルを好むユーザーに適しています。馴染みある形式と予測可能なテンポを提供します。

My Island is a tranquil yet ambitious survival sandbox developed and published by SnowBaby Games, designed to transport players into an open-world archipelago where crafting, exploration, and self-sufficiency intertwine. The premise is simple: you begin adrift in a vast ocean, washed onto the shores of a deserted island, and from there, you must survive, adapt, and create a home of your own. The game blends survival mechanics with peaceful simulation, offering a more relaxed approach to a genre often defined by constant struggle. Rather than placing the player under relentless threat, My Island focuses on creativity and discovery, allowing you to shape your surroundings, cultivate the land, and explore the beauty of a tropical wilderness at your own pace. It’s an experience that invites reflection and patience, asking players to appreciate the process of rebuilding from nothing in a quiet, untamed world.

Visually, the game captures the allure of isolation with a warm and natural palette. The open ocean stretches infinitely in every direction, shimmering under a dynamic day-and-night cycle that subtly transforms the tone of your environment. Each island is unique, with its own arrangement of trees, wildlife, and topography, offering a refreshing sense of exploration as you sail from one to another. The environmental design, while not cutting-edge in technical detail, succeeds in evoking atmosphere through light, sound, and space. The sound of waves breaking against the shore, the distant cry of birds, and the rustle of wind through the palm leaves lend a meditative quality to the experience. The world feels alive in its stillness, designed less to overwhelm and more to calm. There’s a certain handmade quality to it all—simple textures, uneven models, and modest animations—that somehow enhances the sense of charm rather than detracting from it. This balance between realism and minimalism gives My Island a distinctive identity among indie survival games.

The gameplay structure combines elements familiar to the genre—gathering, crafting, hunting, and building—but integrates them with a more serene pacing. You collect resources from the environment, plant crops, build houses, and hunt or fish for food. Over time, your humble island evolves into a self-sustaining haven with farms, furniture, and tamed animals. One of the game’s defining features is the sheer range of customization it offers, allowing players to choose their character’s appearance and body proportions, and to design structures freely using multiple material types. The farming system, though simple, feels rewarding; planting and harvesting fruits, vegetables, and grains becomes a rhythmic activity that breaks up the flow of exploration and crafting. Sailing between islands adds another layer of satisfaction, creating a sense of adventure as you uncover new biomes, resources, and building opportunities. It’s clear that SnowBaby Games aimed to create an experience that emphasizes personal expression—where success is not measured by survival against harsh odds, but by the creation of a life worth living.

However, the game’s ambition often stretches beyond its technical grasp. While the world is expansive, it can feel repetitive once you’ve explored several islands, as many share similar layouts and resource distributions. The building system, though flexible, sometimes struggles with precision, and the crafting menus can be cumbersome. Players have reported that the mechanics, while functional, lack refinement and depth, with some features feeling unfinished or underdeveloped. The wildlife interactions, for instance, add life to the environment but rarely impact gameplay in meaningful ways. Likewise, the combat and hunting systems are serviceable but shallow, offering little beyond the basics. Despite these shortcomings, the game’s relaxed nature softens the sting of its limitations; it isn’t meant to be a hardcore survival simulator but rather a space for slow progression and personal creativity. Still, players seeking complexity or tightly designed systems may find the experience too simple or repetitive after extended play.

Where My Island shines most is in its tone and atmosphere. It offers a rare kind of solitude, the kind that feels restorative rather than lonely. Its pacing allows players to unwind, to watch the sun set over the water after a day of building or farming, and to enjoy the gentle satisfaction of self-made progress. It occupies a comfortable middle ground between games like Raft and Stardew Valley—lacking the tension of one and the depth of the other, but borrowing the best parts of both to create something quietly compelling. The game’s imperfections are easy to spot, but its sincerity is equally impossible to miss. It feels like the product of a small studio that poured genuine care into its creation, even if the end result doesn’t always reach the heights it aspires to. My Island may not revolutionize the genre, but it offers something many modern games overlook: space to breathe, to create without pressure, and to find peace in simplicity. For players who value that meditative quality over perfection, it is an imperfect but heartfelt journey that rewards time, imagination, and a willingness to embrace quiet adventure.

es como una conbinacion entre Halo y la estética de Minecraft.
multijugador shooter de ritmo rápido que introduce un giro significativo: los entornos son completamente destructibles y construibles.
Acción FPS Clásica y Entornos de Vóxeles: La mezcla de disparos rápidos con la capacidad de destruir y construir estructuras en tiempo real añade una capa estratégica única al combate.
Modo Infección: El modo Zombi es la estrella del juego, ofreciendo caos y diversión multijugador.
Aunque en su momento debió ser muy divertido, el juego actualmente depende demasiado de su multijugador. Como todo juego más antiguo, no hay tantos servidores disponibles y carece de jugadores activos. esto afecta la experiencia la verdad, ya que el juego resalta y se hace mas divertidocuando hay gente en línea.

Los gráficos son intencionalmente simples, al estilo de vóxeles, lo que le da una apariencia distintiva que, honestamente, es lo único que puede atraer a algunos jugadores hoy en día, si se jugara sería solo por ese estilo.

Si bien "Murder Miners" no tiene nada que envidiar a otros juegos de su estilo en cuanto a la fórmula de juego (la fusión de FPS y construcción funciona sorprendentemente bien), la realidad es que sin una base de jugadores activa, la experiencia se desinfla por completo.

Es un juego con una rejugabilidad enorme y gran potencial, pero la falta de servidores y de gente para jugar hace que sea difícil recomendarlo en su estado actual, a menos que solo se quiera echar un vistazo a los gráficos o tengas un grupo de amigos que lo jueguen contigo. No lo recomiendo.

Terra Nova: Strike Force Centauri, developed by Looking Glass Studios and republished by Nightdive Studios, is a tactical first-person shooter that combines strategic planning with fast-paced action, set against a richly imagined sci-fi backdrop. Originally released in 1996, the game introduced players to the Alpha Centauri star system, where humanity has colonized distant planets to escape a crumbling Earth. Its ambitious mix of squad-based tactics, immersive storytelling, and innovative technology made it a standout title of its era, earning critical praise even as it struggled commercially, ultimately achieving cult classic status among dedicated fans.

Players assume the role of Nikola ap Io, commander of an elite strike team tasked with confronting pirates, hostile factions, and the oppressive Hegemony that threatens humanity’s foothold in the new worlds. Gameplay revolves around the use of powered battle armor (PBA), which grants enhanced mobility, firepower, and tactical versatility. Equipped with features such as jumpjets for short bursts of flight, infrared and zoomed vision modes, lock-on targeting, and energy shields, the PBA allows players to adapt to rapidly evolving combat scenarios. Squad management adds another layer of complexity, as players must issue commands to AI-controlled teammates to coordinate attacks, hold positions, and execute strategic maneuvers, making each mission a careful balance of reflex-driven action and planning.

The game’s technical achievements were remarkable for the mid-1990s. Using the TED engine, Terra Nova rendered expansive 3D outdoor environments with dynamic elements, such as real-time water reflections and simulated physics, which enhanced immersion and realism. While its graphics may appear dated today, they were pioneering at the time, creating a sense of scale and atmosphere rarely seen in shooters of that era. The combination of varied terrain, interactive environmental features, and procedurally animated elements helped the game stand out in a crowded market and contributed to its unique gameplay experience.

Audio design in Terra Nova complements its tactical and immersive gameplay. The soundtrack underscores tense moments and high-stakes combat, while sound effects provide critical feedback for player actions and enemy movements. Voice acting enhances narrative engagement and aids in tactical decision-making, giving the impression of a living, reactive battlefield. These audio cues work in tandem with visual information to immerse players fully in the experience and reinforce the game’s strategic depth.

Despite its innovations, Terra Nova faced commercial difficulties upon release. Its complex mechanics, while praised by critics, may have been intimidating to a broader audience, and it entered a competitive market filled with more accessible shooters. These factors contributed to its modest sales, but over time, the game has been recognized as a trailblazer that influenced subsequent tactical shooters and immersive sci-fi games. Its blend of squad tactics, PBA combat, and expansive environments laid groundwork for many modern titles in the genre.

Today, Terra Nova: Strike Force Centauri is celebrated as a pioneering work that pushed the boundaries of game design in the 1990s. Its ambitious integration of narrative, technology, and tactical gameplay provides a deep and rewarding experience for players willing to invest in mastering its systems. For fans of tactical shooters and science fiction alike, Terra Nova offers not only a glimpse into the evolution of the genre but also an enduring, challenging, and highly engaging journey through humanity’s frontier in the Alpha Centauri system.

Rating: 9/10

Cute yet spooky, story-focused game.

The art style reminds me of painted paper dolls and is a joy to look at. The music fits the mood beautifully and surprised me with how elaborate it gets at times.
Since the story is based on a Russian fairy tale, it's all narrated by one VA and kind of like being read a bed time story. Now, I don't understand Russian, but I could at least appreciate the different voices and inflections that were used so it was still fun to listen to.

As for the gameplay itself, it's mostly walking and whacking, with the occasional jumping. It switches between Vasilisa - who is quite lovable - and her helpful little doll. The doll takes care of combat which is ... fine. I found the mobs to be a tiny bit frustrating because they don't have the most discernible tells in when they will attack sometimes, but their movements are funny and puppet-like and their designs, like the rest of the game, very interesting and also a bit spooky.
The boss fights were fun though, if not very difficult, but that's not what the game is about anyway.

The first part of the game has most of the walking, where Vasilisa has to make her way to the Baba Yaga's hut and go through a variety of environments, where she meets a number of Slavic folklore creatures and monsters, most of which get an entry in the in-game encyclopedia. (Only gripe with this is, while it's very interesting to read, the music stops dead in the menu, but that's a very minor nitpick.)
At Baba Yaga's hut, Vasilisa gets to do chores - or rather, her doll does, since Vasilisa sleeps all day and goes through Yaga's maze of a basement at night.

It's all fairly linear with only a handful of optional things to find, which makes sense since this is telling a story.

Overall the game is well crafted, well told and well presented, and definitely worth playing.

[b]⭐ My Verdict[/b]
“If you’re looking for a short but engaging interactive thriller with real stakes and multiple outcomes, this one delivers.”

[b]👍 What I Liked[/b]
+The premise grabbed me: after a catastrophic bio-weapon attack in London you’re trapped in a locked-down lab with the clock and air running out.
+It’s full live-action cinematic style, with real actors and a film-like production, which gives it a different feel than your standard game.
+The multiple endings are a major plus. Depending on your choices you’ll be steered toward one of eight different outcomes. 
+I appreciated the “relationship tracking” and “personality tracking” systems — your decisions don’t just choose dialogue options, they affect how your character is read and how others respond.
+For a budget indie/interactive-movie type, it does a solid job of suspense and keeping you on edge. The stakes feel real, and you feel the ticking clock.

[b]👎 What Could Be Better[/b]
-It’s relatively short. Because it’s an interactive film more than a full open-world or deeply mechanical experience, you’ll likely finish it in one sitting and then maybe replay to explore the other endings.
-If you prefer rich gameplay mechanics (stealth, combat, open exploration) you might feel the lack — this is very story/choice driven.
-Some choices feel like they don’t always have wildly different effects: you may notice only subtle divergences on a first run, so the “eight endings” claim might underwhelm if you expect dramatic branches for every decision.
-Since it’s live action, you’re limited by film sets & filming quality — if you’re very picky about visuals or acting, then some moments might feel a little off.

[b]🎮 Who Should Play It[/b]
+Fans of interactive movies / FMV (full motion video) games who want a thriller vibe and decent production value.
+Players who like story-rich experiences and are comfortable with choice-based branching rather than heavy control mechanics.
+Anyone who has maybe an hour or two and wants a contained experience with replayability via multiple endings.

[b]🚫 Who Might Skip It[/b]
-Hardcore gamers who want deep gameplay systems, long campaigns, or sandbox freedom.
-Those who dislike live-action video games or think FMV style is too limiting.
-Anyone expecting the length of a full AAA game — this isn’t it.

[b]📝 Final Thoughts[/b]
Overall, I’d say The Complex is a worthy pick for what it sets out to be: a condensed interactive thriller with meaningful choices and decent replay value. It has some limitations compared to traditional games, but if you go in with the right expectations it delivers a compelling story experience. I give it 4 out of 5 stars — go in with an open mind about the format, and you’ll enjoy the ride.

Из плюсов можно выделить:

- Интересный сюжет.
История цельная и последовательная, в ней тяжело запутаться и не возникает вопросов к логике: любой выбор ведёт к последствиям без отклонения от основной линии сюжета. Нет вихря из случайных твистов и локаций, нет абсурдных сцен и ветвей сюжета (спойлер): [spoiler]даже если учесть прохождение для достижения "Kindar Surprise", концовка органично вписывается в сюжет[/spoiler]. Сюжет гибок и интересен до самого конца.

- Отличная игра актёров и персонажи.
Все, за исключением главной героини (подробнее о ней в минусах), достойно смотрятся в кадре, им хочется верить, их хочется слушать, на них хочется смотреть. Среди действующих лиц нет одинаковых персонажей, у каждого есть свой индивидуальный шарм. С характерами персонажей тоже точное попадание: нет перебора в чертах и эмоциях, есть обаятельность, строгость, недоверие... Актёры играют свой образ полностью, не перегибая, не переигрывая и не скрывая своё мастерство.

- Пройденные фрагменты можно пропускать.
Всегда выделяю этот пункт либо в плюсах, либо в минусах. Если сначала пройти цепочку событий "A B D E", а при повторном прохождении получить цепочку "A C D E", то фрагменты "D" и "E" можно пропустить до принятия следующего решения. Комфортно проходить историю заново. В моменте действия в конференц-зале может показаться, что нельзя, однако в разных путях видны разные последствия, так что это не упущение.

- Приятная картинка.
Нет некачественной графики, нет игрушечных декораций и костюмов, локации кажутся тем, чем пытаются казаться, будь то палатка на пляже или лабораторный комплекс под землей.  Операторская работа тоже приятна - нет перегрузки для глаз, кадр информативный и приятный.

- На экране нет характеристик.
Если верно понимаю, каждое решение влияет на характеристики главного героя, а именно: честность, храбрость, любопытство, интеллект и чувствительность. Ни один из показателей не влияет на ход сюжета и их изменения не показываются на экране. На них можно посмотреть через меню паузы или после прохождения истории. Думаю, это сделано лишь для того, чтобы показать игроку то, какой личностью показывают принятые им решения. Бесполезны, но, главное, что не мешают.


Теперь о минусах:

- Главная героиня.
В Эми недостаёт всего: ни раскрытия, ни чёткой актёрской игры, ни подходящего образа. Игравшая её Michelle Mylett будто не испытывает эмоций, на протяжении всей истории она либо нейтральная, либо пускает слезу. Особенно сильно это заметно на контрасте её дуэта с Al Weaver, игравшим Риса - харизматичный персонаж, отыгрывающий весь спектр эмоций и вечно спокойный, холодный персонаж, реагирующий на любые события лишь голосом - это картина, оставляющая неприятное пятно на погружении в атмосферу. Также хочется отметить, что персонаж Эми совсем не похожа на доктора. Думаю, если рассматривать её вне контекста, быстрее всего придёт впечатление того, что она - руководитель, но никак не практик. 

- Маленькие оплошности.
Некоторые ошибки всё же есть, однако, их очень легко пропустить. Например: человек, печатающий на выключенном ноутбуке. Это не портит впечатление, просто забавные упущения.

This was always a drag because I no longer had anything to aim for in that game, and so the prospect of repeating that process another 5 or 6 times was pretty lame. Some of the negatives regarding the game (specifically the undercooked teams mechanic, and the monotony of grinding) can largely be mitigated by approaching the game with a casual mindset.

Nice little short story, defintely worth a quick look. This short and charming 10 minute animated VR film has a touch of WALL-E as you follow a decapitated robot head who is stuck with a broken voice box. While it cleverly uses the medium of VR to draw your attention 360° around the space, my main (and only) crticism is the VR film utilizes cuts that work in traditional film, but in VR it's really jarring. I would suggest fade in / out during transitions or having the player on a moving platform that narratively worked in the world, to mitigate the jerky feeling of unanticipatedly being teleported.

This was an otherwise enjoyable short VR film! I'd suggest watching it sitting down in a swivel chair, or know that your viewpoint will be moving in the film while you stand still. WOW! Just watched this. Amazing work. I think this is the first VR short film I've ever seen using the VIVE.

It is difficult to give this work a fair review. On one hand, every technical aspect works very well. It plays smoothly, and all the pieces preform what they are supposed to. It is meant to be a purely passive experience. As a free product, it delivers a properly working product.
Unfortunately a Passive experience lives and dies on the contents of the story, and it is impossible to not compare this to Wall-E, a bar that this animation is in no way capable of living up to. The design is simple, yet uninspired and unexpressive, the character has only a single line, and yet nothing is done to use that line to convey an actual sense of dialog. Wall-E, Groot, and other characters with similarly limited vocabulary still use that minimalism to convey entire paragraphs of context.
As for the story itself, it is either too vague, and I am missing it entirely,(which rarely happens) or it is so over simplified as to not even be recognizable as a story. There was a head, there was a problem, he met another head and together they pressed a button, and the problem was solved. For some reason that is meaningful?
Perhaps all of this could have been ignored if there was something added by making this a VR experience. If any of this somehow showcased how a regular experience can be made more impressive by using VR as the medium, I would at least be able to say it's worth trying, but I don't feel anything like this.

This feels like a school project where the student was busier checking to make sure they met all the stupid structural criteria to qualify for the grade, and then making sure they didn't write anything too difficult to animate, that making sure the story was actually enjoyable was never factored into the equation.
I don't usually do this to a free product that has no actual technical issues, but I just can't recommend this one.

《Tokyo Dark》是一款侧重心理叙事的点击式冒险游戏。玩家扮演东京警探伊藤，调查失踪搭档的下落。玩法结合调查、轻量解谜与对话选择，整体基调现实而阴郁，并逐步引向心理惊悚。

核心机制为“S.P.I.N”系统，涵盖理智、职业度、调查力与神经质四项指标。玩家决策会影响数值变化，并在后续解锁或限制路径，形成实际后果。选择简洁直接，影响会随剧情推进逐步显现。

探索流程清晰。玩家在二维场景中移动、收集线索并与角色交流。谜题逻辑明确且耗时短，设计重在叙事推进而非难度堆叠。节奏平稳，有效维持紧张氛围。

叙事是本作优势。剧情融合犯罪、神秘元素与心理压力，形成多分支结构。结局因S.P.I.N数值与关键抉择而异。主题涉及创伤与职责，文本精炼，不依赖廉价刺激。

画面采用日式动画风格，背景干净，角色表现力强。音乐以低调曲目烘托不安情绪，整体氛围始终统一。

总体而言，《Tokyo Dark》适合重视分支叙事与决策影响的玩家。游戏体量紧凑，可重复游玩，决策后果明确，心理主题聚焦。

Assassin’s Creed Chronicles: Russia is a 2.5D stealth-action game developed by Climax Studios and released in 2016. It is the final entry in the Assassin’s Creed Chronicles trilogy, following China and India. The game combines side-scrolling stealth gameplay with light combat and platforming, set during the Russian Revolution of 1918.

The story follows Nikolai Orelov, a weary Assassin seeking to escape the Brotherhood and flee Russia with his family. His final mission involves stealing a powerful artifact—the Precursor Box—from the Bolsheviks. Along the way, he encounters Anastasia Romanov, a survivor of the royal family, who becomes entangled in the struggle between Assassins and Templars. The narrative blends historical events with the series’ mythological lore.

Gameplay continues the stealth-driven design of previous Chronicles titles. Players use shadows, cover, and tools such as smoke bombs and rope darts to bypass guards. The game emphasizes precision and timing rather than open confrontation. Light puzzles and environmental traps add variety, while the occasional use of a sniper rifle introduces ranged mechanics unique to this entry.

The 2.5D level design is intricate, with multiple paths and vertical layers. Each stage rewards patience and observation, encouraging silent infiltration and nonlethal takedowns. Combat remains secondary—effective but risky. The game rewards ghost-like playstyles with higher scores and unlockable upgrades.

Visually, Chronicles: Russia adopts a distinctive art direction. The monochrome palette, accented by red and muted tones, mirrors the bleakness of the revolution and sets it apart stylistically from the vibrant color schemes of China and India. The aesthetic supports the somber tone of Nikolai’s personal story.

Performance is stable, with smooth animations and responsive controls, though some players found the stealth detection inconsistent. The pacing occasionally suffers from trial-and-error design, but the tight level structure and varied objectives maintain engagement.

In summary, Assassin’s Creed Chronicles: Russia delivers a compact, atmospheric stealth experience that closes the trilogy on a darker and more emotional note. While limited in scope compared to mainline Assassin’s Creed games, it succeeds as a focused and stylistically coherent side story, appealing to players who value deliberate, puzzle-like stealth gameplay over large-scale exploration.

This game doesn’t just tell you about love it shows you how people grow, how they break, and how even small choices can change everything. A simple otome turned out to be a story full of emotion, reflection, and human nature. 

Cyrus, the main character, is someone many people misunderstand. If you look at her story closely, it makes sense why she changes. She starts as a noble girl who knows nothing beyond kindness and justice, living under the strict rule of the temple. Then, everything falls apart her promotion is canceled, her engagement breaks off, her parents are murdered, and she’s sent to the depths as a criminal. Anyone would crumble under that, but she still tries to live and move forward. That’s the message I love most, if you stay stuck in the past, you’ll only get the bad ending but if you move forward, you’ll find hope.

Elt’s route, honestly? There wasn’t much chemistry. He’s sweet, sure, but being a womanizer makes me question his sincerity. I skimmed through most of his endings the only one that really caught my heart was the one where Fin “takes” me. Strangely, I preferred Elt’s normal ending maybe because Saint Yune appears there? His happy ending was nice too, mostly because he finally stood up for himself.

Now, Ulrik… I had high hopes after seeing everyone call him “best boy,” but halfway through his route, I started to feel disappointed. Early on, I actually interacted more with Elt than Ulrik. It even felt like Ulrik saved me not because he cared deeply, but because Elt said I was special. Maybe there was some care there, but it was clear his bond with Elt mattered more.

I wanted more sweet, romantic moments with Ulrik. Elt had far more bonding scenes, even with Cyrus! I still can’t believe we got so many beautiful CGs with Elt but barely anything for Ulrik. His route felt shorter, and even his normal ending was sad while Elt somehow gets a happy one every time. Unfair.

Some people said Adage’s ending was “just about killing,” but I don’t see it that way. I actually liked it, even though I expected a more dramatic plot twist about why Cyrus was sent to the depths. When you think about it, though humans are such mysterious beings. Sometimes, there doesn’t need to be a huge twist, just understanding their emotions is enough. seriously, what was that, Adage?! He was waiting for Cyrus to come back, and then—bam! That sudden shift in emotion caught me completely off guard. Still, I loved their exchanges, especially the ending with Ines. It felt abrupt, yes, but I liked the little detail that Cyrus knows how to cook, and the parallel from “I’ll devote my life to you” to “Why don’t you devote your life to me?” That line hit me hard. But then again Adage took care of us  It was the only time I didn’t feel anxious about danger or survival no hounds nearby, no stress about what to eat next.

Ines... I felt so alone at the start of his route just waiting for him to come. Doing his route right after finishing Adage’s made me miss having someone by my side all the time. I don’t have much to say , but I liked all his endings especially the happy one, mostly because Fin was there. (We also got justice here)

Fin’s route really struck me. Seeing the contrast between his versions the innocent boy versus the darker “Hound” side was painful yet fascinating. Many people prefer his yandere side, but for me, that Fin already had his ending. The route where he’s living in the Sanctuary District showed another side of him quiet, broken, but still human. It left me imagining what could have been, and I love that feeling of bittersweet possibility. And maybe now I understand why Sachen took a liking to Fin. They’re similar in a way both timid souls who were twisted by circumstances, turning toward darkness.

Then there’s Yune (I PLAYED HIM LAST). His route wrecked me emotionally in the best way. I didn’t expect to cry so much. There’s something about his voice and how he carries himself that feels sacred, fitting for a saint. His story had the justice Cyrus deserved(In the bad ending though....). The fact that he reformed the entire system for her, changing the country itself, made me love him even more. He’s not just a love interest, he’s a symbol of hope and change. Yune is, without question, best man.

The more I played, the more I realized this isn’t your usual otome game. It’s not just about romancen it’s about people, choices, and the mystery of being human. The way it shows multiple perspectives makes every character feel real. And the voice acting? Amazing. You can even hear how their tones change as the story progresses especially Adage and Fin. It’s such a subtle detail, but it adds so much depth.

One thing I noticed right away is how the voice acting subtly changes as you progress through each route. When you first meet Adage, his voice sounds almost robotic calm, collected, a little distant. But the more time you spend with him, the more emotion starts to seep through. It’s such a small detail, yet it completely changes how you see him. The same goes for Fin, his tone changes the most noticeably. You can really hear the emotional shifts as you get closer to each character.

I love the little visual details red in the Bodyguard route, green in the Warder route. In Yune it's violet. Those subtle touches really make me appreciate the effort put into this game. 

By the end, I found myself reflecting on the message that keeps repeating throughout the routes: don’t be trapped by the past. Move forward. Every character carries this theme differently, but they all lead you to the same truth growth comes from pain, and happiness is something you choose.

I didn’t expect to find something so profound in an otome game. But here I am, moved beyond words. Yune and Fin best men, both.

I've beaten the game on hard, it's kind of a mixed bag. 

The writing, the story, are superb, the game is definitely a stand out compared to your average video game or even an crpg.

There is a ton of reading. The English used is quite sophisticated, it's very book-like, with a lot of terms you won't usually encounter, the game tells the story almost exclusively through text descriptions and dialogues, so it's definitely on the harder end to understand everything, or even most, for non native speakers.

The visuals are also very decent, only bit that aged are the 3D models (it's not big deal, it doesn't look terrible or anything like that), but other than that, the game looks very good and will age like fine wine.

The soundtrack is also very memorable, albeit maybe a little too repetitive at times. Still, it's great at creating the right atmosphere.

Now it's time for the bad. A lot of poor decisions when it comes to equipment management of your teammates. The accuracy rates are a guideline at best, and will often cause frustration. No idea why they made them this way, but no can do about it. There were at least a few instances where the game would soft lock while in the matrix for whatever reason. There was also this bug which would allow you to equip an extra weapon in some cases. 

So... in general, it's a fantastic game, it's just flawed with some technical level issues which can be forgiven, and some a bit frustrating balancing decisions... 

It's definitely worth your time.

It took me a surprising while to realise that this was made by the same people that made Monark, haha. When I saw the opening, I noted that it reminded me of Monark, the Character Songs for the boss battles which I loved also reminded me of Monark, though not quite at the same level. Then when the Player gains their Tyrant Form, that's when it fully clicked for me of the Monark connection.

The characters and story isn't especially revolutionary, but I didn't need them to be, i enjoyed the game for what it was and enjoyed my time with them. The SSS activities were quite boring, though I get the desire to have gameplay connections to the context, the main enjoyable part of these were listening to character conversations, particularly loved that some future story characters / context is hinted at early on, things like Emri's appearance and Taiga's script, I had a bit of a laugh with some of the side characters like the failing actor who ended up in the power rangers show, or the 3 guys who discovered they were `dating` the same girl.
Though it was probably just me enjoying the small things in a largely flawed experience.

Animations are probably where I can obviously see the budget of this project, being somewhat rough in a number of places, I enjoyed the turn based combat mechanics of a timeline, breaks and interruption resource though as some other comments said, it's a simpler twist on Caligula's, which isn't a bad thing. 
The UI was quite stylish, it was clear what they were going for, particulalry during the Stun / Blitz Ultimates, though the animations there again let it down quite a bit. Maybe because of all the Slow Downs / hit stops, I ended up with alot of time to appreciate some of the VFX when I ended up liking quite a bit.

I appreciated that the Glitch dungeons were often designed as puzzles rather than straight combat, where if you engaged in it properly, you could speed up how long you had to spend fighting, they were hard enough that sometimes I had to stop and think, but not too long to figure it out, which I appreciate since I can't enjoy being stuck on puzzles like I used to because of time.

Less of a review and more of a message to the devs, I really enjoyed this game, and like Monark, I want to cheer on the mid-sized devs who create such games. Obviously not reasonably comparable to much larger budgets like Persona, this is a flawed game but at times, quite enjoyable.

For people who do want to give it a try, I'd probably suggest waiting for a sale.

The game has a really good plot twist, but there are details in the game development that makes me feel that the dev doesn't care about the game or the player's experience.

[h3]Big problems[/h3]
[list]
    [*]Spoiler: [spoiler]When you're hiding from the security, you're obligated to fail twice. You CAN'T hide on the sofa before being caught in the corridor and under the table.[/spoiler] Makes me feel that the game is trying to make me spend more time to not get a refund.

    [*]Spoiler: [spoiler]The end where you kill Jiwoo is stupid. Not because of the story (I liked both endings), but because there's a flashy green bottle on the table that the player sees from the beginning. But the RIGHT "weapon" to use is a black wine bottle in a cellar in the wall (that I thought was just texture at first), that you almost never see because there's a table or a wall in front of it (depending on whether you're coming from the corrido or the living room).
Again, it makes me feel that the game is trying to make the player spend more time trying to discover how to grab the green bottle (because it was SO flashy that I thought that was bugged or I was in the wrong position to grab it), and/or trying to find where the right "weapon" is.
Maybe the dev knows that's a problem, since the Steam description says that you need to find a "weapon", and your character also says the same, even if it makes more sense to wait for the timer.[/spoiler]

    [*]The rhythm mini-game is bad as hell. You need to use WASD when the buttons appear randomly on the screen (like OSU), but this style is not intuitive, and that's not fun to play it. Not counting that major buttons aren't in the music's rhythm (or appear even without any music at all). I know Sasaeng is a horror game, not a rhythm game, but if you'll put an obligatory rhythm mini-game, at least make it fun.

    [*]Jiwoo songs are AI and the dev don't make it clear. In the Steam description, it only says "AI was used for pre-rendered assets" without saying exactly what was made with it. And that's ok, I know that being an indie dev is hard, and AI can help to make the work faster, but at least make it clear for players. I hate it more when an AI user tries to pretend they didn't used it.
I'm sure that Jiwoo's songs are made by AI because these songs don't exist in any place, only on Youtube, but referencing Sasaeng (so we can assume they were made for the game). But no one knows who the singer is, even though her voice is so beautiful and talented, and the game doesn't credit anyone for the music (only for background sounds). And I really tried to find any information saying that it was not AI, because I really liked Venomous and Burn Me Down.
(I know there's people who don't care about it, but I think we can agree that's no reason to hide it from player who cares).
[/list]

[h3]Minor problems[/h3]
[list]
    [*]The models are ugly (I don't care about graphics, but some character looks like melted Play-Doh).
    [*]Some assets don't connect with each other (like misaligned walls with big spaces between them).
    [*]There's a character with no texture in his hair.
[/list]

I was ready to ask for a refund, but the only reason I didn't make one is that I made a video about the game (as I said, I really liked the plot twist), and my viewers sent me money through my Sasaeng video. Since the video about the game paid for the game itself, I don't think that's fair to refund it.

Natsuki Chronicles feels like it addressed a lot of problems I had with this team's previous game, Ginga Force, but it lost some of the cinematic flair and memorability in the process.

+Pros:
+The music is full of bangers, much like this team's previous games. It's Yousuke Yasui, you oughta know.
+I actually liked the story here the best out of their previous efforts. Ginga Force was a little too generic, but I found myself caring for Natsuki as an actually decent lead protagonist. Most shooters don't have great stories, so I appreciated them making a prequel game for this character.
+The weapons have some nice variety, and you don't feel as weak at the start as you did in Ginga Force. The ability to customize your ship in Story Mode between levels is really neat, and you're progressively getting stronger the more you play.
+There's actually an Arcade Mode this time around that lets you play the stages in order instead of one at a time! I don't know why this wasn't in Ginga Force, but it's here now!

-Cons:
-Stages are not very memorable at all, outside of the final 3. There's not as much room for cool setpieces like there was in Ginga Force. It's clear this team hasn't made a horizontal shooter before, and didn't do much to vary up the levels or enemy patterns. I think now that they have this experience under their belt, they could make an even better one next time.
-The bullet visibility is still not great, but it's slightly better than Ginga Force. I appreciate the "bullet lines" that you can toggle on to help track where they're going.
-It's still not as good as Eschatos. It doesn't have that "instant classic" factor, and took a little bit to grow on me.

Overall, I liked this one more than Ginga Force, but I wish it did a little more to stand out. История, которую игра в них рассказала была цельной, единой и что самое главное - законченной. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3596392141 [b]Проблемная часть: [/b]

[b]Сюжет: [/b]
Syberia 3 — это прямое продолжение второй части, но вместо мистики, путешествий и “мамонтовой” магии на этот раз тебе сразу подсовывают историю про противостояния Кейт с «клюквенными злодеями» и сопровождения племени юколов. 
Проблема даже не в том, что я хотел продолжения оригинальной сюжетной линии. Всё, за что любили ранние части — меланхолия, загадочность, чувство личного поиска — все это уходит на второй план. 

Проблема в том, что сюжет Syberia 3 не цепляет: он вторичен, зануден и быстро начинает утомлять потоком схожих дешевых сцен. Старые темы (поиск себя, взросление, одиночество) уступают место дежурному спасению надоедливых NPC с их диалогами, которые скорее раздражают, чем увлекают. Все драматические приёмы и “ персонажи для галочки” в Syberia 3 настолько предсказуемы и банальны, что сюжет буквально тонет в унылом мономифе (ты явно где-то всё это уже видел, но даже не хочется вспоминать где). 
Нету душевных или хорошо срежиссированных драматичных моментов.

А финал — окончательно выбивает из колеи: вместо настоящей «загадки» (как те же мамонты в прошлой части) или эмоционального катарсиса тебя ждёт разве что формальная точка маршрута (“ну всё, юколы дошли — спасибо, до свидания”). Более того, концовка возвращает Кейт на ту же позицию, с которой всё начиналось: ядро сюжета никуда не продвинулось, а всё проделанное ВО ВСЕЙ игре оказывается банальным филлером. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3599703425 [b]Оптимизация: [/b]
Главное “новшество” — переход на Unity и 3D. В теории это должен был быть шаг вперед. Но на практике…
— Камера дёргается, частенько стоит под не удобным углом, сама Кейт дрыгается во время бега. Выглядит все это очень бедно.  
— Фреймрейт нестабилен: местами идёт вполне плавно, потом в кат-сценах или во время исследования локаций — резкие просадки.
— Бедная анимация и ужасная мимика, выглядят даже беднее, чем в печально известной ME: Andromeda; всех ещё и показывают вблизи, тогда как первые две части умели скрыть сырость издалека.
— Графика местами совершенно устарела: текстуры плоские, освещение скудное даже на максимуме, всё дополнительно размазывается мыльной билинейной фильтрацией.
— Легендарная для PC-серии мышка теперь почти бесполезна, Кейт цепляется за каждого NPC на открытых локациях, иногда не может банально добежать до нужного объекта. А в комбинации с кривой камерой – на мышке невозможно зайти в части локации, которые находятся в «слепой зоне», только стрелочки клавиатуры помогут дойти.

А вот сейчас будет комбо из проблем, которые в совокупности утраивают фрустрацию от получения всех ачивментов в игре:
— Наведение на активные области - чистая лотерея; курсор часто “с нихуя” пропадает в головоломках, что делает простую задачу настоящей пыткой на терпение.

Syberia 3 arrives burdened by expectation. Benoît Sokal’s early entries were modern adventure game classics: elegant, melancholic and intricately clockworked. This third chapter tries earnestly to rekindle that magic, but its reach consistently exceeds its grasp, resulting in an experience that is narratively sincere yet technically troubled.

The shift to full 3D environments should have been a renaissance. Instead, it exposes the game’s weakest points. Movement feels imprecise, interactions are awkwardly placed and the camera transitions - often abrupt, often obstructive - frequently sabotage the sense of immersion the series once commanded effortlessly. When the game asks you to perform delicate actions with clumsy controls, frustration becomes your most reliable companion.

And yet, hidden beneath the roughness, there remains a pulse of charm. The art direction - snowbound settlements, weather-beaten caravans and steampunk relics - still carries Sokal’s unmistakable signature. Likewise, the soundtrack exudes a wistful, wandering quality that lends Kate Walker’s journey the emotional weight the systems struggle to support.

Narratively, Syberia 3 is uneven but earnest. The Youkol tribe and their migration offer a refreshing thematic pivot, yet the script wavers between thoughtful and stilted, rarely landing with the elegance of the earlier games. Kate herself remains compelling, though the story around her feels oddly detached from the sweeping mythos that once animated the franchise.

Puzzles - a cornerstone of the series - range from engaging to baffling, and not always for the right reasons. When they work, they echo Syberia’s mechanical poetry; when they don’t, they feel like busywork grafted onto unreliable interactions.

In the end, Syberia 3 is a flawed resurrection: heartfelt but hampered by technical instability, clumsy mechanics and an identity caught between tradition and reinvention. Fans may appreciate its sincerity (and I certainly did...), but newcomers will likely wonder what all the reverence was about.

GalGun Returns* is a remastered version of the original GalGun*, developed by Inti Creates. It updates the 2011 rail shooter with improved visuals, smoother controls, and additional content while maintaining its light arcade structure. The game focuses on shooting targets across branching routes in a first-person, on-rails format.

Gameplay follows the standard rail shooter formula. The player automatically moves through levels, aiming and firing at incoming targets using either a controller or mouse input. Scoring is based on speed, precision, and accuracy. The gameplay rhythm is quick and reactive rather than strategic, emphasizing arcade-style timing.

Mechanically, GalGun Returns* refines aiming responsiveness and user interface design. Camera transitions are smoother than in the original, and targeting is more precise. Each stage ends with performance ratings and unlocks, giving incentive for replaying levels to improve scores.

Visually, the remaster delivers cleaner, higher-resolution textures and sharper character outlines. The environments are bright and stylized, supporting fast readability rather than realism. The presentation remains consistent with anime aesthetics—simple geometry, vivid color, and high contrast.

Audio features energetic background music, brief voice segments, and sound effects that support fast-paced shooting feedback. The sound mix is clean, though limited in variation across stages. The tone is upbeat throughout, fitting the game’s casual rhythm.

The remaster also includes previously released content and quality-of-life improvements, such as expanded routes and customization options. It runs smoothly on modern systems, with short load times and minimal performance issues. Save and replay systems function reliably, supporting quick play sessions.

Overall, GalGun Returns* is a technically solid remaster of a straightforward on-rails shooter. It modernizes controls and visuals while preserving the simplicity and structure of the original. For players who enjoy short, score-driven arcade experiences with light visual-novel framing, it performs competently within its genre.

There are a couple systems that are unfortunately a product of this being the first game (The stat system being tied to doki doki mode) Which can make it really annoying to get endings, alongside some of the achievements being straight grindfests.

the classmates also having unique names and entries instead of being indistinguishable fodder also surprised me

It's a puzzle game with a factory theme. It's pretty close in feel to Zachtronics games. Space is cramped, and you have a limited budget for machinery. Your machine also needs to complete within a set time limit.

The problem is that the restrictions are too tight. I got totally fed up with getting a solution that worked, but which was still a failure because I used too many parts or didn't complete the solution on time.  Instead of enjoying myself, I was frustrated and angry with the completion of each puzzle.

The game already has bonus objectives, where you score additional points for completing a puzzle with fewer parts or in a faster time, and a leaderboard where your solution gets ranked compared to other players. That rewards players who want to optimize their solutions. The problem is the *minimum* required has to be highly optimized. A perfectly valid, straightforward solution isn't good enough.

- Rewarding exploration that fits well into the gameplay loop where you find mods for weapons, resources to upgrade your homebase and artifacts to enhance your build/gameplay style
- Cool boss battles

Cons:
- Almost no real sidequests
- Low variety of enemies and many reskins
- At endgame a special mission opens up for some endgame weapons. Hello friends,

Today we will be reviewing the game Fantasy Life I: The Girl Who Steals Time. This is a continuation of the game made on the Nintendo 3ds. Having never played that version of the game, this review will only be talking specifically about this version of the game.

This is a life sim, similar to games like Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon. The difference that there are 14 life's, or jobs, a player can level up and use in the game. This makes leveling them all up to max a great endeavor that should only be done post game, after beating the full storyline. The storyline is a interesting time traveling twist where the character lives his life's in the past. Then use these to explore the present day. Be aware that some sections of the game require life's to be a specific level to continue the story, so it may require grinding out the levels to get past the story section.

Even after beating the story, the post games stuff is many and lots. For example, finding new recipe's to make things, finding new weapons to forge, finding new furniture to make, even finding new items and monsters. Most of the post game stuff should be done in multiplayer, as the game allows this after a certain event in the game is done. Also, people tend to cause issues with random people who join their game. For example, i seen to personally got "kicked" out alot of the games on purpose, even though i was not doing anything bad. You can read about me asking about it here:

https://steamcommunity.com/app/2993780/discussions/0/604170759802432386/

The error when your kicked alot manifests as a "communication error". This happened to me at least 30 times in random games i joined with others just to have fun. Because of this issue, it is recommended you only play with friends. Also, people can make private rooms with a password, so it is possible to keep bad people out of your maps and runs.

Included in the post game, is a dungeon called the Treasure Grove, where it is only possible to get items and recipes for certain weapons and things. Many times people go here to farm the items as this location is the only place to find xxx item or weapon. Be aware the same issue posted above is also found when exploring the treasure groves, and player may kick others if they do not like them. Anyways, here is my pros and cons list:

PROS:

- A life sim where the player can choose any life, up to 14 of them.

- Each life has it's own recipe's and skills to learn. They must be leveled each.

- A storyline consisting of time travel.

- Dragons, which i like alot.

- Post game activities and multiplayer fun with others. Be aware of my above warning though about being kicked alot.

- Slow and methodical game. Not high powered hunting monsters or anything. Each life takes time to perfect to certain points too.

CONS:

- Kernal Anti Cheat program EASY. This did not bother me in any way. Some people have reported it slows down their game. I seen no slowdown, and only issue i personally had is being kicked from many games i tried to join.

- Being kicked from many people's games. Yes, this is a negative point because it happened to me personally 30+ times. Feel free to see how many times you get kicked from a random person's game when trying to collect legendary items you need to make weapons or level.

- Grinding can be a real hassle, especially at the end of the game. This has caused burnout issue with people, including a person i friended while playing the game.

- Multiplayer mode is timed. Many people do not like this, but i believe this was put into the game to prevent cheating and other nasty things that happen in online games.

Do i recommend this game? Yes, if you like stardew valley or harvest moon. This is not a monster fighting game, although it does include it. The game is very slow and methodical, so if you do not like relaxing and slow going games, avoid this game at all costs. The fact that people tend to purposely kick players off their multiplayer game makes this game annoying to play online, especially when farming for legendary items to make post game items. This aspect makes me, the writer of this guide, almost not consider this game. It does not make the game fun when trying to grind and farm for legendary items, then get kicked when your about to get them. If possible, i suggest players wait for a sale, if there is any at all.

🏺 Egypt Frontiers — когда песок реалистичнее людей

Я большой любитель Древнего Египта, и любая игра, обещающая окунуть меня в ту эпоху, автоматически получает шанс. Но Egypt Frontiers — это тот случай, когда отличная идея утонула в песке неуклюжей реализации.

NPC двигаются, будто их суставы из ивовых прутьев, лица напоминают восковые маски, а перевод на русский звучит так, будто писался через сон. Когда древнеегипетский рабочий говорит тебе: «Чувак, я устал» — это уже не история, а чистый сюрреализм.

И всё же, за этой забавной внешней оболочкой чувствуется искреннее старание. Разработчики действительно пытались воссоздать архитектуру и быт Египта — храмы, деревни, дома, внутренние дворики, даже оформление улиц выглядят с душой.
Ты чувствуешь, что они копались в источниках, искали визуальные решения, пытались передать атмосферу жаркого песка и света, а не просто “сделать пустыню с пирамидой”.

Некоторые механики удивляют:
— добыча камня — не тупое “бей киркой”, а забивание клиньев для раскола глыбы, что выглядит неожиданно реалистично;
— крафт — собирание предметов из деталей, а не магическое материализование из воздуха;
— система перков — пусть и с забавными названиями вроде “Сандалии 3”, но работает.

Сам геймплей — неспешный, почти медитативный. “Принеси, подай, построй” — но без раздражения.
Песок, тёплое освещение, пирамиды на горизонте — всё это создаёт настоящее ощущение Египта, пусть и окружённого анимациями уровня 2008 года.

И всё это за пять долларов.
Да, проект далёк от идеала, но за такую цену — это не провал, а искренний эксперимент, в котором гораздо больше души, чем в большинстве безликих ААА.

Вердикт:
🟢 Атмосфера Египта передана с любовью: архитектура, пейзажи и детали — действительно хороши.
🟡 Механики простые, но с приятными находками.
🔴 Анимации и перевод — боль, но забавная боль.

⚖️ Итог: хорошая идея, похороненная под глиной технических ограничений, но с теплом и уважением к эпохе.

[b]My experience[/b]

I have put 29 hours into this game so far, and still going strong. I personally love this game, and it has scratched the RTS itch I have been stuck with for sometime now. It combines my two favourite genre's and creates a replayable competitive experience.
The playerbase is currently quite small, but I do not have any issues getting a game (EU) during peak hours.



[b]What is this game?[/b]

Simply, it's a top down moba, with RTS elements. You control 3 rigs (all with abilities you choose and unique passive/"ultimate" ability.
You try and put 3 Rigs together, that will give you the best synergy and then you farm nests for core, and dunk them in the middle, whilst putting pressure on your opponent to slow them down. There are also 3 "optional" objectives that give you points, if you are the first to complete them. 
I.e capture all vision points.


I would like to note, this is a multiplayer, competitive game. This does not contain a campaign mode. 

Games are either:

1v1 or 2v2.

There is an infestation mode, which is basically survival mode. Survive against waves of enemies.

[b]Is it complex?[/b]

To begin with, the game offers you a lot of options.
You have up to 4 classes:

Mechanic (Support)
Gunner (DPS)
Tank
Summoner (Utility)

Each class has 3 rigs with a unique ultimate and passive ability.
Each class also has a "bank" of abilities and passives, which you can fit to any rig within that class. Just to make it clear, you can run 2 mechanics and they can be outfitted exactly the same, only difference being their ultimate and main passive abilities.

The game feels overwhelming in the first couple of hours, but after a few rounds (15 minutes each) and a good read through the different abilities, you very quickly learn what works and what doesn't.


[b]Does the game have strategic depth?[/b]

The Gameplay itself has depth, specifically around your decisions in game.

It's very Micro intensive.

Setting up your "Rigs" or "Squad" however is lacking a bit of depth. There is a very clear meta at high level play at the moment, but the developers will be adding more gear/abilities and a new class over the course of the Early Access, along with balance changes so I do expect this to change.

Для игроков, заставших или изучавших библиотеку легендарной Sega Genesis, не секрет, что платформа могла похвастаться своими небольшими, но мощными сериями, которые, почему-то, часто становились именно трилогиями. Так было с Golden Axe, Desert/Jungle/Urban Strike, Streets of Rage и... Road Rash. Кажется, именно Road Rash 3 стал одним из моих первых спонсоров безумного кооп угара в ущерб сну. В целом гонки с применением оружия я полюбил, наверное, с тех самых пор, как познакомился с этим поджанром, вероятно, ещё в Fire & Forget 2. И великолепных представителей этого поджанра существует великое множество. Одна беда - именно наследников мотоциклетных гонок, где участники вооружались всякими цепями, дубинками и прочими инструментами для телесной коммуникации с оппонентами, как-то почти и не сыскалось. Да, у Road Rash и за пределами шестнадцатибитной Сеги были свои представители. К тому же, ещё в 90-ых на аркадных автоматах вышла годная футуристическая Motor Raid. Но уже даже в нулевые на этом попроще я не могу припомнить ничего. Во всяком случае, стоящего внимания. Так продолжалось и в десятые вплоть до появления наконец-то нового достойного байкерского мордобоя, Road Redemption.

Но достойным он стал отнюдь не сразу. Уродилась игра натуральным гадким утёнком с ужасными менюшками, чем-то невразумительным в качестве музыки, с каким-то невнятным сырым обрубком вместо кампании и... на удивление бодрым базовым геймплеем. Да, в игре даже на старте было весело катить на своём стальном коне и раздавать пинки с тумаками налево и направо. К чести разработчиков, игру они не оставили в таком непотребном состоянии и стала она в итоге... взрослым гадким утёнком. Но всё равно заметно похорошевшим и прилизанным. Наконец-то кампания обрела какой-то адекватный облик и стала напоминать что-то в духе FTL, только без выбора дальнейшего задания. Структура её довольно простая - вас кидает на случайную карту текущей территории, где вам необходимо выполнить одну из случайных целей. Например, уничтожить достаточное количество представителей сопернической банды или прийти в первой тройке к финишу (что, опять же, можно сделать, устранив конкурентов). В случае невыполнения условий вы получаете шиш с маслом и жирный штраф к максимальному уровню здоровья. А в случае выполнения - порцию опыта и денег. Деньги можно тратить между миссиями в магазине на всякие расходники для пополнения здоровья или нитро, или на апгрейды в рамках текущего забега. А вот опыт вам пригодится, когда заезд закончится вашей гибелью. При его достаточном количестве, можно вкачать какой-нибудь навык, который облегчит вам следующие забеги в кампанию. То есть да, мета-прогресс тут есть. Заодно понемногу будут открываться новые мотоциклы и гонщики. Вроде бы звучит всё круто, верно? Почему же тогда перед нами именно гадкий утёнок, а не лебедь? Уф, с чего бы начать.

So, on the one hand, this is really impressive. It's not a little tactics game, it's a full pixel art crpg. A lot of the world is procgen, in ways that hinder gameplay, but it's still a big undertaking and it runs pretty smooth.

On the other, the other reviews are not wrong. It's very punishing. You need to grind a bunch of levels before you can do ANYTHING, and those levels don't help. Exp gain is also bonkers slow. You do drown in random equipment, 99% of which is vendor trash, and you can put points into talents---I'm in sword and shield, which isn't great because high level sword locks you out of using shield. But can you use shield with anything else? No.

The result of all of this is a VERY flat, very hard game that's difficult to get into. And I don't know that there's much that would help it that isn't fully replanning the talents system to let you have builds rather than just monofocusing your weapon.

I don't like thumbing down what is clearly a substantial project, but I think you have to have an appetite for punishing indie clunk that vastly exceeds my own to get to the diamond part of this rough.

The characters, writing, and art all seem fine. And when the procgen isn't telling you to find and dig a random tile on a map full of identical looking nonsense, it's okay too. The core gameplay is just more like if Rogue was a survival horror title, and less like a fantasy adventure rpg. If it could lean into that funk, it would be more engaging.

Edit: Oh, yeah, absolutely not. Sweated my way through the first couple dungeons, got all epics and legendaries in my gear slots, took one step outside the starting region to pursue the main quest, got mulched by a single random enemy. If the fights were interesting I wouldn't mind but the only thing I did wrong here was not full potioning on a two round cadence. Hard is fine if there's depth to the gameplay, but hard and boring I can't recommend.
