Sword art online - Lost song is part visual novel, part action game. In the action parts you are supposed to play as Kirito. I sad supposed, because by the second island nothing prevents you to switch out the party leader to any of the characters, or indeed make a new character of your preference. Still, the events are centered around Kirito, and if he isn’t the party leader, or at least in the party, he won’t gain the levels required to progress through level gated fights.

While not immediately apparent, a lot of the mobs will be reused at various stages. Notably the winged orb things will be present in a lot of places, just at different level and with a slight change in texture. And not just mobs, a lot of mid-level, and even high level bosses will be reused later. Their skillset might be different, but the appearance will be largely the same. Eventually, (literally) higher level places will be unlocked in the first 3 islands. At that stage you have to return to these previously unreachable parts of these maps to continue with the main quest, but it still feels as yet another reuse of the assets.

The voice acting in the game is excellent, but the sound file quality feels compressed. Not surprising, the game has tons of voice acting, and it was released for Playstation Vita too, where size should matter. Still, higher quality sound files would have been nice for the PC version. All the visual novel parts will be fully voiced by the original voice actors, including high profile ones, like the one for Kirito. In case you wonder, the 2 songs licensed were “Cynthia no hikari” form Eir Aoi, and “Yoru no niji wo koete” from Luna Haruna, both high profile singers. Too bad those song voices didn’t blend well with the voice actor in the visual novel parts.

A core game feature is flying. And not just as a means of travel, you will be fighting enemies in the air. Even if you want to avoid the air fight parts, some of the mandatory boss fights will take place there – and it wasn’t easy for me to control the combat in the air. Free flying as a method of travel is fun. Hover fighting was clunky for me. I played the game with the controller. It didn’t help that ascending was A, descending was double pressed A, which I messed up regularly. Honestly, LT should have been a direction toggle instead of multiplayer messaging – in a single player game I had literally no use for that. But by holding it down before pressing A for descend would have helped. In dungeons the flying / hovering is disabled, but still there are floating enemies. You are supposed to jump / double jump to reach them, then by keeping attacking them you sorta kinda maintain your floating. All in all it was an annoying mechanism. 

The game has auto save, it will save after important events, whatever those might be. There is no feedback whatsoever when an autosave has happened. So I just always returned to the bed in the inn, and saved there, to have a controlled hard save. That is the only place where a manual save is possible. There are a few slots to save into, though I only recycled the first 3.

The skills are unlocked as you level up. The same is true for all members of the party. Using a skill will level them up, making them more potent. Merely swinging your weapon is a skill in itself, which will level up too – for the weapon type equipped. It feels right to manage Kirito’s, and perhaps the custom created character’s skills. But you will have to manage the skill tree of all the rest of the roster – they won’t equip newly acquired skills, and as such, won’t gather proficiency in them either. Theoretically the levels and skill levels go up all till 1000, though on a normal playthrough I reached only levels in the low 400s. To reach up till the hard limit, a new game plus should be started, the enemies there will be higher levels. You will start the new game plus with the state at the end of your normal playthrough. 

Early on I intended to level up the full roster. Eventually, around the middle of the second island I gave up. From then on, I just focused on my main party : Kirito, Asuna, Rain. This way I had access to a high level party for the boss fights. In the visual novel parts supposedly the rest of the roster is present too, but during the fights, only your party will participate.

There is a store, where you can buy weapons and accessories. As you progress in the story, higher rank weapons will become available, though they will be plain weapons. The ones from drops / chests will have bonus properties. Some of them will be even of higher attack power. The weapons can be upgraded, but requires materials to be grinded. No point in leveling them up beyond a few levels, new tiers will appear soon, and a new rank weapon is on par with a +10 (i.e. max)  leveled up weapon of the previous rank, making higher level upgrades not worth it. The accessories help a bit, but they are not that important. Later in the game their cost won’t be a problem.

The drops from the field are unidentified, you will have to identify them in the store, to reveal their properties. It can be done in bulk. This mechanism makes it impossible to equip a (potentially) better weapon just found in the field, on the run.

The game is a bit grindy. If in a dungeon, I cleared it all the way to the boss room, and on the way out too, and still didn’t match the level of enemies on the higher maps. Early on I even tried to level up each possible party members, but after reaching level 160 with them I just gave up. It took a lot of pointless grinding to level up everyone. True, Kirito gained some extra levels in the process, but those were rendered moot, as the experience gain tappers out. By the end of the normal playtrough I was still below level 500. By default each character is equipped with the skills for only one weapon, but are capable of equipping a few types of weapons, depending on their race. If you want to change their weapon type, do it so right at the beginning of the character acquisition, and stick to that weapon for the rest of the game. Notably, there won’t be any spear users by default. If you want one, you will have to switch a compatible character to that weapon type, or make the custom character of a race able to use it.

Once you reach the second island, you will be able to make a custom character. It will look like one of the people wondering around in the town. Though the protagonist of the game will be still Kirito. He will have to fight some duels to progress the story, so he should always be included into the party, to level him up for those mandatory fights for progress. The most annoying duel was with Sumeragi. His special attack had a wide range, and can easily cause a damage more than a third of the healthbar.

There are a few side character storyline achievements. You don’t have to level or bond specially with those characters, their story will be experienced as you progress with the events. You just have to interact with the exclamation mark characters in the town. It is a bit confusing, but some of those side stories finishes only after the end credits rolled. It means the game doesn’t end with that final fight. There are a few hours of more content, mostly visual novel stuff. But those are gated behind yet another duel, though not so hard as the Sumeragi one. Also, only after the credits is the arena unlocked. There you can duel with your party members. Their AI will be upgraded in this part, each character having a different playstyle. I only fought a few of those, and eventually got a dagger, which when identified turned out to be a rank 10 one, my only such high level weapon. Before and after the fight there will be a visual novel part, though not sure if that is repeated for each duel, I didn’t fight the same character twice.

The game was stable, it didn’t crash for me.

Really digging what I’m playing after a couple of runs. The battle system reminds me a bit of Monster Train, but with some fun twists. It’s a 3-on-3 style fight where your team lines up against the enemy’s line. Once you kill of the enemy team, you can start hitting the enemy champion in the back. Once you take them down you win the match.

One interesting thing is there’s no mana or resource limit. Sometimes you can just play every card in your hand if you want, though that’s not always the smartest move. Some cards have unique conditions for when they can be played — like only after casting a spell or using a hero power.

I’m just starting to get into the battle gem system, where you can upgrade cards with effects like death touch, stun, freeze, etc. It takes a few minutes to wrap your head around the nuances, but once it clicks, there’s a surprising amount of depth here. Definitely worth checking out if you’re into Slay the Spire or Magic: The Gathering.

Este jogo é um Visual Novel em que o jogador é o tutor ou a tutora reais dos três príncipes de um reino muito recente, em que o rei morreu a pouco tempo. Seu personagem é o ou a alquimista pertencente ao conselho e já no primeiro momento que você chega ao reino, tentam te matar. E isso é interessante porque o jogo tem dois modos, o história e o aventura e no aventura você, jogador, pode colecionar mortes (são uns CGs bem fofinhos por sinal). Eu joguei o aventura e eu tive que refazer várias vezes minhas escolhas para conseguir não morrer e encerrar mais cedo a jornada, mas no modo história não tem mortes. I'm not sure if there are multiple routes to this game as mentioned, or how many of those have been implemented into the full game, as I just finished my first playthrough. However, I guarantee I had a really fun time with the game overall. While not perfect. the Murder Hotel was a delightful fun time, and I'd love to keep exploring this world further, with a promised update.

So, the Pros and Cons.

Pros:

-The graphics are rather nice. Of course, they're in an 'RPG Maker' style, with pixel art, mostly simplistic environments and more, but the character portraits, their visual identity and more are rather fun. I liked what is presented, knowing about the limitations that often come with narrative-first games.

-Soundtrack: The soundtrack was a delight. Very nice songs, that enhance most of the scenes they've been in, and help to immerse myself in the setting. I really enjoyed it.

-Plotline up to the middle of chapter 4: The premise is very interesting, and the characters are very fun! The protagonist is very well-written, and many of the side characters that you meet up on all cases are so unique and fun that I wanted to spend more time with them. 

-The cases themselves: As a good chaptered murder mystery, you have different acts/chapters, each one with a different case. The premise seems to be very much focused on locked room mysteries, but each one of those was set up rather uniquely, and even if not revolutionary, the manner you unravel them all is a highlight to the game itself.

Now the cons:

-Rushed endgame: Be from the lack of a 'true ending' as it stands, or be with problems with development from promises of deliveries, the end of chapter 4, the final chapter, felt... weaker than the rest of the game. While some plot points were fun to answer, it felt lacking compared to the rest of the plot, and the ending itself was rather anticlimactic. Maybe another revision of the final case, with its culprit(s) being more built up during the game, and the final debate being harder and also more... engaging, would be good.

-Rushed relationships: Be from the setting or more, something that was a bit shocking in the hotel is how... well, the main character has unmatched levels of Rizz. I played this with my friends watching me and I can say that a common joke was how everyone in the hotel wanted to sleep with us. And in plotline, we've been together for like 2-3 days. It wasn't a big issue as some of the relationships (especially with two specific girls in the cast) were well-written if you bought into the premise that 'we are skipping the stuff about meeting each other'

-Some plot beyond the cases: Of course, there is an overall narrative, but in some aspects, it does get a bit confusing and overwhelming. Some of the plot points that come up beyond the cases, and a few of the characters that were introduced for the more demon heavy plotline were a bit... much. Also another thing that is hurt by the lack of the true ending, but still.

Overall, given where I wanted this game to go, I'd give it a solid 8.5/10, with does very much get my recomendation, I'd love to see the few issues I had with the plot and pacing solved a bit, especially the final chapter, but beyond that, it's still very much a fun time, especially if you've played other games of the genre, especially Ace Attorney and Danganronpa and you've enjoyed them.

Это уже четвертая игра inkle, которую я прохожу. Наверное, рано или поздно попробую все.

Удивительное.
Хотя перед нами чисто текстовая игра, у нее есть очень серьезное отличие от классических визуальных новелл: время и пространство. На корабле есть множество локаций, а некоторые даже просматриваются из других. По этим локациям все время снуют персонажи. И в зависимости от времени и места вы получите либо нежелательных свидетелей, либо неожиданных союзников. Все прохождение - это кропотливое выстраивание сцен, в которых можно выгодно себя проявить, и не менее важный подбор реплик. Дело не только в том, что героиня может кого-то оскорбить или проболтаться в своем преступлении, - в игре отлично реализована механика фактов, так что хороший игрок-преступник должен помнить свою линию защиты и не должен путаться в показаниях. Иначе вас моментально выведут на чистую воду. Рано или поздно вы сможете все выстроить так, чтобы сбежать с корабля, но тут игра вежливо намекнет вам, что этого недостаточно, и предложит достичь дополнительных целей, чтобы полностью замести следы.

Плюсы.
- Сюрреалистические концовки с дельфинами и почившим мужем.
- Интересные достижения, которые вынудят штудировать время и пространство игры вдоль и поперек.
- В игре есть хорошая система подсказок и намеков для зашедших в тупик.
- Интересная рисовка, классический и джазовый саундтрек (включая русские мелодии!) и множество отвлеченных диалогов, рисующих эпоху.

Минусы.
- Я так и не нашел возможности сохраниться. Любая ошибка выбора на пути вынудит идти по своим следами раз за разом сначала. Это утомляет.

Интересный анти-детектив, где мы должны не вывести преступника на чистую воду, а замутить ее окончательно, чтобы выскользнуть на свободу. Но слишком камерный, и концовки либо скучные, либо безумные. Рекомендуется любителям интересных текстовых механик.

This could be so much better.  It might not just up and crash while looting after battles.  It also might not advance mob levels so fast that it is very, very difficult to get past even level 1 of the dungeon.  If I wanted frustrating, I would not have gotten a game that billed itself as being easy to pick up and put down.  I'd like to be able to feel like progress (dungeon depth) and use of game features (transforming items) were relatively easy to experience.  I'm beginning to think that it is non-trivial to get more than a few battles in to dungeon level one without some serious brain off grinding of the first easy-peasy mob of the first dungeon level; where's the fun of doing one or two non-challenging mob hits, exiting the dungeon, repeatedly, just to get enough cash to make it possible to visit the low inventory store enough to hoard up an insane number of potions to last a dungeon level?  (Whoever heard of an RPG store that, for example, only carries one healing potion per visit most of the time?) The store has so few items, even if you saved up the funds over a number of trips, you could not hope to get enough potions for a long crawl without meaningless in-and-outs of the dungeon so restocks of the store permit getting quantities needed.  I can't really even fathom what this must be like at higher levels to get through more than one level of the dungeon - since mobs auto-level quickly (more than one level per encounter) with the lowest level encounters such that the player is on-level with the second encounter and under-level on the third.  Level one of the dungeon should not be so challenging to get through!  Disappointing to have paid for this experience.  I had hopes for a fun time waster, but it's proving to be a put-off instead.  Another reason for this is that the whole alchemy thing of transforming loot to other items appears way too difficult to try out.  The sheer number of items needed puts this feature largely out-of-reach for casual players (unless, perhaps, one just saves up money and store visits to buy alchemy items), but then  buying things to transform seems a bit silly).  In the end, this review asks who really wants a grind of a time waster anyway?

* Mob level progression is far too fast.
* Potion unavailability seems quite pointless.
* Transforming items could be improved by allowing mixed rarity levels (high rarity items treated as the lowest rarity item in the list).
* It should not be necessary to exit the dungeon before mobs are challenging just to get another set of store items, or to just try to stock up on potions so one can make it past over-level mobs (before facing a boss).

On the other hand, the following seem well thought out:

* Graphics / sound.
* Not having to walk back to the dungeon exit.
* Linear progression for sake of making short sessions possible.
* Ability to buy item levels does at least offset the paltry inventory count of the store.
* The amount of gold loot per battle seems reasonable (sadly negated by the store lacking sufficient potions per store visit).

A deeply terrible game. To call it "cozy" is like calling Super Meat Boy "casual" - aside from the cute graphics, it is extremely tense! You need to constantly manage your resources, particularly because failures are punished with unclear setbacks, which cost dearly! At one point my setup was reduced to half, while I was sure that I was somewhat safe in the reset.

Speaking of reset - you can force a reset (i.e. death), and you may need to do so, because the fast travel system can put you in a spot, from which you just cannot exit anymore. Meaning, in my case, that one gets set back a painful amount through no fault of one's own. Similarly, you can drop some of your stuff on purpose (but annoyingly not every item), and you can put it where you cannot pick it up again.

Everything in the game is very randomized, and this also applies to the fast travel points. You may be on the hunt for one travel points forever, but then again, you may get three on the same screen! The same applies to virtually everything you may want to find - you may encounter a wasteland without that one thing in sight, or a whole bunch of them in one cluster. This is particularly problematic in the beginning, where resources are scarce(r), and one struggles to move ahead.

Your second main enemy is the tiny inventory. Or to be more precise, the tiny inventories, because you have three distinct bags for different resources. The main one is already annoying as hell, because tools that provide resources have tiny stacks (e.g. an axe in the beginning has two uses, and even the top tier axe has eight), and the resources need to be crammed into the same space as the tools themselves. Yes, the resources stack well, but managing a collection of, say, 40 of something becomes a real nuisance. The other two inventories are for currency-like items, and you will find (especially in the beginning) that you either have zero of those items, or receive a bunch of them at the same time, making the crucial resources go to waste. At the same time, you cannot waste items from the main inventory directly, so you often need to throw something out, pick a different item collection up, throw the item you wanted to waste away, and then pick up the original item again. Fun.

Finally, there is the upgrade/crafting system, which is poorly explained, and buggy. For example, you will get a lot of rewards that seem to indicate that your inventory or light capacity will go up, but they won't, because they are capped (light at 220, coins at 60). Some crafting stations need upgrades first, before you can craft the thing, you actually wanted, others may have upgrades, but those may be optional in the sense that you can still proceed without the upgrade. Unfortunately, there is no way to look up, what is crafted how, and where - there is no in-game option, and no wiki. Rain on Your Parade is a wonderfully chaotic and whimsically creative indie game that stands out by embracing pure, unapologetic mischief. Developed and published by Unbound Creations, it casts you as Cloudy, an adorable cardboard cloud with a single purpose: to ruin as many days as possible. What begins as a simple ability to rain on unsuspecting bystanders quickly expands into a toolbox of unconventional weather powers that let you wreak havoc across increasingly absurd scenarios. From the very beginning, the game makes it clear that it isn’t interested in realism or seriousness—it thrives on playful anarchy and comedic surprise.

The visual style is one of the game’s immediate charms. Everything is designed to look handcrafted, like a child’s diorama brought to life: cardboard buildings, painted paper characters, felt-tip marker outlines, and cut-out scenery that gives each level a cozy yet quirky aesthetic. This scrapbook presentation pairs wonderfully with the game’s tone, making every scene feel like a playful joke. The animations are simple but effective, with characters reacting in humorous and exaggerated ways when Cloudy unleashes rain, thunder, snow, or far more chaotic elements. The music and sound effects reinforce the lighthearted atmosphere, offering upbeat tunes and silly audio cues that make the game feel welcoming even as you’re causing mass panic.

The structure of Rain on Your Parade is built around a sequence of short, highly varied levels, each introducing a new gimmick, genre parody, or comedic twist. No two stages feel quite alike. One moment you’re drenching wedding guests just to spoil their big day, and the next you’re sneaking through a facility in a tongue-in-cheek stealth mission or fighting waves of enemies in a level styled after classic action games. The constant shift in tone and mechanics keeps the experience fresh, and the game seldom lets an idea overstay its welcome. Even the objectives vary from simple “soak everything” tasks to more specific puzzle-like goals that require paying attention to characters, props, or environmental interactions.

As Cloudy gains new abilities, the gameplay becomes more unpredictable and entertaining. Rain transforms into a multi-purpose tool that can douse flames, melt snow, or fill objects with water. Thunder can scare or disable machines, while tornado powers let you fling objects around in delightfully destructive fashion. Some liquids Cloudy absorbs create chaotic consequences, such as pouring oil to start fires or splashing coffee to energize NPCs into unhinged behavior. This broadening set of tools adds depth without becoming overwhelming—the game wants players to experiment, not micromanage.

Despite its charm, Rain on Your Parade does carry some limitations. The very randomness and playfulness that make it entertaining can also make it feel inconsistent. Some levels are brilliant, tightly designed, and packed with clever jokes, while others feel more like brief experiments that don’t land quite as well. The difficulty can fluctuate unexpectedly, with a few stages requiring precision or timing that may frustrate players expecting a purely casual experience. The overall campaign is also relatively short; though filled with variety, it doesn’t offer extensive replay value beyond optional goals, hidden secrets, and cosmetic customization for Cloudy.

Yet even with these minor drawbacks, the game shines through its personality. Cloudy can be customized with hats, colors, and even hand-drawn faces, giving players a chance to add a bit of their own humor to the character. The writing leans into silly jokes, meta references, and playful narration without trying too hard, making it accessible to younger audiences while still offering winks at older players. It’s a rare game that feels both wholesome and mischievous at the same time—an experience built around lighthearted creativity rather than competition or complexity.

Ultimately, Rain on Your Parade is a joyful dose of interactive comedy that succeeds because it embraces absurdity without restraint. It’s charming, unpredictable, and crafted with a genuine sense of fun, offering a series of imaginative levels that invite players to experiment, laugh, and cause harmless chaos. Although it may not offer long-term depth or intense challenge, it delivers exactly what it promises: a humorous, inventive adventure starring a mischievous little cloud who just wants to make the world a little soggier. For players seeking a breezy, feel-good game full of personality and surprises, Rain on Your Parade is a delightful choice.

[h1]In-Depth[/h1]

You're sitting in your car, driving across the asphalt and overtaking one opponent after another. You might think: "Why is this so boring?".. Yes? Then you're just like me. The more realistic the simulation, the more I start to yawn. However, there are two things that can quickly wake me up again: Either we delete the word "simulation" and replace it with "fun" (Mario Kart sends its regards), or we leave the road and head for the water (like in Wave Race on the N64). I've been hooked on jet ski racing ever since I raced my first laps over waves in Wave Race 64. But other developers are struggling to recreate this feeling in their games. So, is Riptide really that good? Spoiler: yes, but be prepared for a steep difficulty curve and a repetitive racing track experience that may prove challenging for some.

[h3] Story [/h3]

The setting is the first surprise for us and got me hooked immediately. Instead of tropical beaches with dolphins and steel drums, we find ourselves in a rather bleak future. Illegal hydrojet races are held in flooded ruins, and you must navigate one of these until you are caught by the police. Having been betrayed and expelled from the "Riptide GP" league, you must race one race after another to restore your reputation and build a new crew. You will face both human and robotic opponents, as well as waves and police officers who will also get in your way.

[h3] Gameplay & Stunts [/h3]

Sometimes we glide smoothly over calm waters; at other times, huge waves fly us into the air, inviting us to perform spectacular stunts that you can unlock for SP (Level ups). In some places, choosing the right route through the ever-changing landscape is crucial. Should we glide smoothly along the wave or let it slow us down to perform stunts? Although it's not as varied or old-fashioned as the genre's role model, Wave Race, it definitely gets the job done. There, forward and backward movements also influenced the sharpness of the turns or the position of the jet ski in the air. In Riptide GP: Renegade, the controls are more" two-dimensional", not bad or unsuccessful, but not perfect either.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3586835141

You can also discover shortcuts to help you gradually master the routes. Occasionally, police officers will try to block your way or slow you down with their jet skis. However, this is only a minor annoyance, as they won't be able to stop or handcuff you unlike in Need For Speed: Most Wanted. Furthermore, when you come into contact with your opponents, you won't fall into the water, that's one big exception at least. Usually, you'll feel a slight "bump" in the battle for position, but it won't stop you completely. I really like that because it's not easy to reach the top of the field later on anyway. A fall can set you back, but the risk of this is particularly high with failed stunts.

When you are launched into the air by high waves or ramps, you can perform stunts using different combinations of the two sticks. These take varying amounts of time to complete. The crucial question is whether you will complete the stunt before landing back in the water. Depending on your speed, the height of the waves and the environment's design, you will have different amounts of time to complete the stunt, so you should think carefully about whether to attempt one. In some familiar spots, it's a sure thing, but in others, where the environment changes dynamically, it can be a gamble. You may realise while in flight that an even more complex stunt would have been possible. Or you may realise before landing: "Whoops, this isn't going to work"  If you are successful, your turbo bar fills up – more for complex stunts than simple ones that take less time. With the push of a button, you get extra speed until the bar is empty again.

[h3] Pacing & Variety [/h3]

The gameplay is ultimately successful and enjoyable, albeit not perfect. In career mode, it is spiced up with a variety of challenges. Sometimes, you compete against seven opponents in classic races, most of which consist of two or three laps. However, there are also slalom courses where your mistakes are added to your overall score, as well as your time. In freestyle races, you must perform as many different stunts as possible within a set time to earn the most points. You will not be rewarded for repeatedly performing the same stunt, as this results in you losing points. In elimination races, the countdown runs repeatedly until the last driver is eliminated. Finally, there are "boss battles" where you have to race against a special character. You are simply challenged to a one-on-one duel and must use all your skills to be the first to cross the finish line. One mistake could cost you the victory.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3583515326

[h3] Criticism [/h3]

Your turbo is a one-use item, no matter how full the bar is. You can't control it, and once activated, you'll use it until it's empty again. The "mobile" implementation is definitely noticeable in many areas, as it would be much smoother if you could control how long the boost lasts. The difficulty curve in the middle of the game is also rather steep for some reason. It feels like a mobile game without microtransactions. At some point, it feels as though you're forced to spend money or grind in order to get a faster jet ski and improve your speed enough to win. This might be problematic for some people who aren't "gamers" like me and prefer a more casual approach. My third and final criticism is the lack of variety in the tracks. I played this game for seven hours and only saw eight tracks in total. Yes, eight. Players have to complete these eight levels a hundred times in different challenges to finish the story mode. To be honest, if the game were half the size with the same variety of eight tracks, it would be an objectively better game. It's tedious and unnecessarily long, with the same thing repeated over and over again.

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]

Riptide GP: Renegade is a relatively small title, but it's a fairly successful jet ski racing game. While it doesn't quite measure up to the legendary Wave Race series, it's highly recommended for fans due to the lack of alternatives.

Up to four players can compete against each other via split screen. There is also an online mode which suffers somewhat from a small player base and uneven duels due to players having different jet skis. However, the upgrade system works much better in single-player mode, providing challenging yet motivating tasks. The lack of variety in the courses and repetitive elements is somewhat offset by spectacular events on the tracks and the successful jet ski feel. If you're ready to face a variety of challenges in choppy waters, give Riptide GP: Renegade a try, especially since it only costs 0,50€ / 1,00€ on a sale.

Quando Blake Stone: Aliens of Gold chegou em 1993, a Apogee tentou apresentar ao mundo um novo ícone dos FPS, Blake Stone era um agente do British Intelligence enfrentando o maluco Dr. Pyrus Goldfire, um cientista que transformava pessoas em mutantes grotescos para construir um exército próprio, o jogo apostava em ficção científica pulsante, cheia de lasers, robôs, criaturas deformadas e instalações futuristas, quase como se um quadrinho pulp dos anos 80 tivesse virado um videogame.

Havia ambição, havia energia e havia uma tentativa sincera de ir muito além da fórmula de Wolfenstein 3D, a ideia central era simples, mas charmosa, explorar bases científicas, sobreviver a mutações bizarras e impedir que Goldfire espalhasse sua “visão dourada” pelo universo.

[b]“Se Wolfenstein era aço e concreto, Blake Stone era neon, mutações e paranóia científica.”[/b]

[h2]2. A evolução de Wolfenstein presa no passado[/h2]

Mesmo usando o motor de Wolfenstein 3D, Blake Stone tentava empurrar tudo ao limite, ele adicionou mapas mais variados, painéis tecnológicos, salas laboratoriais, ambientes que pareciam realmente funcionais, e até NPCs aliados. algo raríssimo em FPS da época, os inimigos eram mais diversificados, indo além de soldados genéricos e trazendo monstros verdadeiramente memoráveis, mas a engine limitava tudo, os corredores eram planos, a movimentação era rígida, a variedade visual tentava mascarar a repetição estrutural, o jogo queria ser moderno, mas sua fundação pertencia ao passado, mesmo assim, as intenções eram claras, dar mais vida e mais identidade ao mundo, Blake Stone não era só um tiro em corredor, era um tiro em corredor, laboratório, sala de teste, câmara de experimento e área de pesquisa.

[b]“Blake Stone queria correr… mas o motor Wolf3D só deixava ele caminhar.”[/b]

[h2]3. O brilho da atmosfera sci-fi e seus monstros[/h2]

Onde Blake Stone se destaca é na personalidade visual, os mutantes de Goldfire têm designs marcantes, a paleta de cores parece saída de uma HQ psicodélica e os laboratórios transmitem a sensação de um mundo vivo e funcional, cada corredor metálico, cada sala repleta de painéis piscando e cada câmara com experimentos grotescos reforçam o charme retrofuturista do jogo.

É um sci-fi colorido, exagerado, quase caricatural e exatamente por isso é tão divertido, mesmo limitado, o jogo se esforça para parecer maior do que realmente é.

[h2]4. Jogabilidade. ambição que tropeça em suas próprias pernas[/h2]

O ponto mais controverso do jogo é sua jogabilidade, há boas ideias, os NPCs inocentes que você pode poupar, sistemas de segurança que podem ser desligados, armas futuristas, exploração recompensadora, mas o ritmo é lento, os inimigos são resistentes demais, os mapas são grandes ao ponto de parecerem arrastados e a repetição estrutural, típica da engine, pesa após algumas horas.

O jogo tinha ambições de modernidade, mais do que a plataforma podia entregar, ele queria oferecer liberdade, narrativa contextual e variedade… mas sempre esbarrava no “pavimento plano” do motor Wolfenstein, ainda assim, a experiência carrega charme, por trás de seus limites, há um jogo tentando honestamente fazer mais do que podia, Wolfenstein como ponto de partida, mas Doom como ponto de queda.

Se compararmos apenas a Wolfenstein 3D, Blake Stone é uma evolução gigantesca, mais conteúdo, mais personalidade, mais mecânicas, mais variedade, ele é praticamente Wolfenstein com esteroides científicos, mas o problema de Blake Stone não foi ser melhor ou pior que Wolfenstein, o problema foi o calendário, Doom lançou apenas seis semanas depois e quando Doom explodiu com sua iluminação dinâmica, mapas verticais, monstros avançados e velocidade alucinante, Blake Stone instantaneamente pareceu velho, ele não perdeu por falhar, perdeu porque Doom inaugurou uma nova era no exato momento errado.

[b]“Blake Stone não foi derrotado pelo que fez… e sim pelo que Doom fez.”[/b]

[h2]5. Da recepção morna ao status cult[/h2]

O jogo vendeu decentemente, mas nunca empolgou o suficiente para competir, acrítica disse: “é bom, mas já nasceu datado”, os jogadores migraram rapidamente para Doom, e Blake Stone caiu no esquecimento, mas o tempo foi gentil, com a onda retrô dos anos 2000 e 2010, fãs de FPS antigos revisitaram o game e perceberam seu valor, humor bizarro, estética única, design exagerado, trilha curiosa, e aquele charme “tecnológico de laboratório dos anos 90” que não existe mais.

[b]Hoje, ele é cult.
Hoje, ele vive na memória dos fãs do gênero.
Hoje, ele é o último suspiro da era Wolfenstein antes da era Doom.[/b]

[h2]6. Conclusão. Um herói esmagado pela história, mas não apagado[/h2]

Blake Stone: Aliens of Gold é um jogo que importa não pelo que mudou, mas pelo que tentou ser, ele marca o fim de uma era, a era dos corredores planos, dos sprites simples, dos mapas quadrados, e o início de outra, que ele não pôde acompanhar, é um retrofuturismo involuntário, uma ficção científica colorida presa no corpo de um motor antiquado, uma tentativa sincera de evolução que foi atropelada por uma revolução, mas, visto hoje, é exatamente isso que o torna especial.

[b]“Blake Stone não venceu sua época, mas resistiu a ela, e hoje brilha como ouro nostálgico.”[/b]

Beyond the Mountains is a lovely top-down adventure game reminiscent of the GameBoy Color classic, Zelda: Link's Awakening DX. Although it isn't a very long game to go from start to finish with only 4 dungeons, it's a charming experience that the developer, VerdLife Games (Eric) clearly cares about and has put a lot of passion and love into. The world, art, story, and even the game engine itself was hand-crafted by him (and I assume a couple friends, based on the credits) to create a fun and unique experience that's both familiar to Zelda fans, but with some fun twists too.

When I first purchased the game it had a couple rough edges, like most indie games do. Play testing is hard, and--as any software developer knows--users will do things in ways you couldn't even begin to imagine, breaking everything and encountering strange and weird quirks. Within a day, the next patch came out and Eric had polished up and fixed the things that were pointed out by myself and other players. He's done an excellent job engaging with the community and supporting Beyond the Mountains post-release, and I have no doubt that he will continue doing so.

[h1]TL;DR:[/h1]

It's a wonderful homage to The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening, and while it doesn't feel [i]exactly[/i] like a Zelda game and is a fair bit shorter than Link's Awakening, was a fun experience in its own rights. The developer very clearly cares about his game, and has been very open with community feedback and post-release support.

Even if you don't like top-down adventure games or don't intend on playing Beyond the Mountains, [i]I strongly encourage you to pick up the game anyways just to support Eric/VerdLife Games[/i]. For the price of one and a half cups of coffee, he deserves the recognition and support for being such an excellent example of a developer who genuinely cares about his game and those who play it.

PAW Patrol: Grand Prix, developed by 3DClouds and published by Outright Games Ltd., is a bright, accessible kart racing game aimed squarely at younger players and fans of the hugely popular children’s TV show. It takes the familiar world of Adventure Bay and its surrounding regions and translates it into a light-hearted, arcade-style racing experience where kids can take control of their favorite pups in races packed with power-ups, shortcuts, and vibrant tracks. While it doesn't try to revolutionize the genre, it succeeds in providing an approachable and fun experience for its target demographic.

The game features a fairly robust selection of characters straight from the show, including Chase, Marshall, Skye, Rubble, and other recognizable faces. Each pup rides in a uniquely designed vehicle that fits their personality and role on the team, and the attention to detail here will definitely be appreciated by young fans. The track designs are pulled from locations seen in the series, such as Adventure Bay, Jake’s Mountain, and the Jungle, with environments that are colorful, full of movement, and easy to navigate. These tracks are simple in layout but contain enough variety in visuals and mild obstacles to keep players engaged, especially those new to the kart-racing genre.

In terms of gameplay, PAW Patrol: Grand Prix operates much like a simplified version of more complex kart racers like Mario Kart. Races are driven by straightforward mechanics—accelerate, steer, collect pup-themed power-ups, and avoid obstacles. The game smartly includes adjustable difficulty settings and accessibility features, such as automatic acceleration and simplified controls, making it easier for younger players to enjoy the experience without needing refined motor skills. There’s also a “hard mode” for older or more experienced players, though even at its most challenging, the game remains family-friendly and never overly punishing.

A standout feature is its support for local split-screen multiplayer, allowing up to four players to race together. This makes it a solid pick for family gaming sessions or playdates, where kids can share the couch and compete with one another. Unfortunately, there is no online multiplayer component, which slightly limits its longevity for older players looking for broader competition, but for the game’s intended age group, local co-op is more than sufficient.

Customization is present in a light form—players can unlock stickers and cosmetic items to decorate the pups’ vehicles, adding a small layer of personalization. Power-ups collected during races range from confetti blasts to snowballs and other lighthearted tools to gain the upper hand or disrupt other racers. These items are easy to use and well-balanced for casual play, though they lack the variety and impact found in more advanced racing games. Mayor Humdinger, a familiar antagonist from the show, occasionally shows up to throw in obstacles or disrupt races, adding a bit of character-driven chaos that ties the gameplay more closely to the show’s world.

One of the game’s major strengths lies in its presentation. It captures the look and feel of the PAW Patrol universe effectively. The characters are animated faithfully, voice lines are used liberally throughout races, and the environments mirror the TV show’s art style. That said, the voice lines can become repetitive over time, with characters frequently repeating the same phrases, which may become grating during extended play sessions. The soundtrack is cheerful and fits the tone, though it lacks variety and doesn’t quite reach the memorable levels of similar titles.

There are, however, a few limitations to keep in mind. The track selection, while thematically varied, is fairly small in scope, and races can begin to feel repetitive after a while. The base game includes eleven tracks, and although they are split into different environments, their layouts often feel familiar. The addition of DLC, such as the Barkingburg Cup and Pup Treat Arena, introduces new gameplay modes and environments, extending the game’s shelf life, but without them, the base experience might wear thin more quickly for older players or families playing regularly.

Performance across platforms is generally smooth, though minor bugs and occasional hiccups have been noted by players. These issues don’t break the game, but they do remind you that this is a mid-budget title made for a specific age group. Still, it manages to provide a stable and polished enough experience to satisfy its core audience. Load times are brief, the menus are easy to navigate, and there's very little downtime between races, which is a critical design feature for keeping younger players engaged.

Ultimately, PAW Patrol: Grand Prix does exactly what it sets out to do—it provides a fun, colorful, and accessible racing experience for younger gamers. It’s not trying to compete with the technical complexity or polish of higher-end kart racers, and it doesn’t need to. For its price point and audience, it offers solid value, particularly when purchased as the Complete Edition with its additional content. The inclusion of familiar characters, simple mechanics, and local multiplayer ensures that it’s a title families can enjoy together, especially those with children who are already fans of the franchise. It’s a charming, if limited, racing game that understands who it’s for and delivers an experience tailored just for them.

UKI-UKI-TENGOKU2 is a horizontal shmup which takes place under water with a pretty unique art style. Gameplay is a bit unusual with inertia, oxygen meter and attack mechanics that require some practice but overall it's a challenging shmup with lots of bullets. A bit weird but fun.

You can choose between three characters, a penguin, a fish and a human. There are two difficulties: Normal and Hard. According to the in-game guide there are six stages.

One of the oddest shmups I've had the joy of playing lately. 

Simple yet extremely difficult. Beautiful yet somewhat disorienting.  Uki-Uki is oddly compelling in the sense you'll feel the need to get just a bit further with each run all while trying to master its unique attack systems. Some of the challenge here also stems from the games visuals. Detirmining what is dead or alive through the busy pixel animations and rudimentary lighting makes things... interesting.  Scoring gives room for player growth as well with points detiremined by chaining different types of attacks and how close to enemies you are when you dispatch them.  I will 1cc this game!  It's just going to take some practice.  :)

UPDATE: The dev has added fixed camera and no screenshake options. The game is not nearly as disorienting now. Also, be sure to read the guide in the options menu.  Things will slowly start to click as you practice more.

It has Pac-Man Arrangement (1996), the single best maze game, therefore it is an easy recommend. It perfected the formula with cornering, a fifth ghost that  powers up the other ghosts but with the added benefit of higher scoring potential, and more varied maze design. There are jump and dash panels, bigger dots that causes you to decrease speed (some of them even change sizes in intervals), and even a boss fight at the end! If you want to experience the magnum opus of the Pac-Man series, this is it.

Other games include:

Pac-Man: The original arcade game. A masterpiece.

Pac-Mania:  Pac-Man, but you jump. The zoomed in camera makes it an unnecessarily frustrating time.

Pac in Time: It's a very janky platformer. It's bad but in a fun way.

Pac n Roll Remix: You Pac and you roll.

Pac Attack: A certified good time. It is the SNES version, however, rather than the superior PS1 remake.

Super Pac-Man: You'll either love or hate this game. I'm a certified hater.

Pac & Pal: Basically a sequel to Super Pac Man but without the super power pellet. The only thing I like about this game is actually the illustration with Pac-Man yelling "Give it back!" to Miru.

Pac-Land: It's a pioneer of the platforming genre. Somewhat bland but still important.

Pac-Man 256: Imagine Pac-Man but if endless runner and bad.

Pac-Man Championship Edition: A decent game, although its charm wears off quickly. It's similar to the OG Pac-Man except that it's more streamlined and is about getting as many points as you can within the time limit.

Pac-Man Arrangement (CS ver.): This game does not deserve to be called Pac-Man Arrangement as it is nowhere near as good or polished. It is basically a declaration of war against the original game, and it loses in every single way. The game is too easy as the ghosts move so slow and navigate throughout the mazes like they've been lobotomized. The mazes are not designed that well either. There are gimmicks, but they're bad. For example, there are doors that periodically close, and there are platforms that go up and down. Very riveting gameplay. The bosses are absolutely terrible as they amount to you eating a power pellet which turns them into a whole bunch of ghosts, and you tediously have to eat every single one. It is not fun. Take a look at Pac-Man Arrangement or even Shadow Labyrinth's MAZE mode for better Pac-Man boss design.

Battle Royale is so bad that it's hardly even worth mentioning. Pac-Motos is here too.

Definitely some stinky poo poo games in this collection, but also some great ones.  I also haven't noticed any input lag, so if any exists, it's minimal.

Other recommendations: Pac-Man World 2 Re-Pac, Pac-Man Championship Edition DX, and Pac-Man Championship Edition 2!

[h1]あの子を探して三千里[/h1] 
前作である夜廻が非常に雰囲気の良いゲームだったため、本作も購入。
今回はとある理由で離れ離れになってしまったとても仲の良い2人の少女を主人公に、視点をザッピングしながら物語を進めることになる。
はぐれた少女たちが、異形さまよう夜の町でお互いの影を追い求めるゲームです。

[h1]良かったところ[/h1] 
[list]
[*]前作以上に濃密になった夜の表現
前作に引き続き基本的に音楽はなし。ただし、アスファルトの道路を歩けば乾いた足音が響き、廃屋を歩けば床がじっとりと軋むなど、環境音がより丁寧に作り込まれていた。
鮮明さを増したグラフィックと相まって、自らがそこを歩くという没入感がさらに増している。
[*]自らの体験として心に残るシナリオ
序盤から一気に物語へ引き込まれ、テンポよく進む展開に最後まで惹きつけられた。
自分の手で進めていくゲームという媒体だからこそ、より濃くシナリオを味わうことができ、深く心に残った。前作に何か響くものを感じた方には特にプレイしてほしい。
[/list]

[h1]気になったところ[/h1]
[list]
[*]ファストトラベルの調整
本作では要所に中ボス的なイベントがあり、良いアクセントになっていた。ただ、チェックポイントが前作より少なく、お化けやボスに倒されるたびに同じ道をひた走ることになるのはやや煩わしかった。さらに、前作にあった主拠点の自宅へ戻るメニュー機能も削除されたため、効率よく移動するためにチェックポイントへデスルーラを繰り返すことに。町中を歩き回って欲しい意図は理解するし、それだけの完成度はあるのだが、バランス調整の難しさを感じた。
[/list]

[h1]まとめ[/h1]
前作以上に作り込まれた深夜の町並みは、より一層の没入感を与えてくれ、重みのあるシナリオと共に感情を揺さぶってくれる。収集要素込みで20時間もあればクリアできると思う。後悔はさせないので、ぜひ夜の町で一緒に情緒ガタガタになってほしい。よろしくお願いします。

I recommend this game with caution. The story is fun, the characters are great, the concept is intriguing, and there are lots of little moments that fans of just about every genre will enjoy. This game was made by geeks and nerds for geeks and nerds.

HOWEVER, the gameplay peaks at 2005 Nintendo. The only evolution is the graphics, as there is no real difference in combat or travel between any of the three eras you visit, and there definitely came a point where I wasn't playing because it was fun, but because I had put thirty hours into the game, I might as well finish it. Which, honestly, didn't give me a sense of accomplishment, but more of a sense of exhausted relief like I had finished deep cleaning my apartment before guests arrived.

The challenges and boss fights rely heavily (almost exclusively) on arcade and rouge-like style gameplay, which I generally am not a fan of. Some of the moments, both in combat and in story, toe the line between "homage" and "blatant ripoff", and it's very difficult to play without a controller.

There are some fun mini games that distract from the main plot like a CCG and some hidden gems I won't spoil, and having 30+ hours of gameplay makes it worth the money, but make sure you know what you're getting into first.

本质是个看片游戏，本作最大的特点就是通过游戏机制来进行的碎片化叙事，教科书级别的分镜，以及包含彩排、试演和试镜的影片。影片分镜特别标准、唯美，而且每个影片都是独立的固定长镜头，看得十分过瘾，我第一次打开游戏忍不住熬夜看了7个小时。碎片化叙事更是把游戏带上一个台阶，本质上是三个电影剪成碎片然后混合在一起，可能你上个片段是18世纪古典欧洲礼拜堂，下个片段变成现代大别墅。如果是其他游戏可能叙事已经崩了，但奇妙的是本作在这方面达到了绝妙的平衡。前后完全不着调的片段连续播放起来竟然使人完全没有违和感，而且有微妙的上瘾在里面，看完一个就想知道下一个讲了什么。《不朽》给了我体感非常好的、以前从未有过的观影体验。这种体验可以说不止游戏界，在电影界都是新奇的存在。

本作对我来说最大的影响就是它记录了部分拍电影的过程，因为一个只看电影，不真正在电影界工作的人是无从知晓拍电影的整个流程的，而《不朽》包含了剧本试读、试演、彩排、正式拍摄，以及导演在彩排中调整分镜、在镜头外用语言指示演员怎么表演的录像，完全一本拍电影入门指南，你甚至可以对部分有同一内容的彩排和正式拍摄部分进行对比（虽然这不在游戏要求内），体验一把当导演的感觉，这对我一个普通人来讲简直太棒了。

然而游戏的缺点正如我标题所说：本作几乎没有什么操作空间，对于一个不喜欢电影的、只喜欢打游戏的人来说简直是场灾难。在游戏后期，当你解锁了绝大多数片段、想要解锁剩下个位数片段的时候，游戏的纯随机播放机制简直就是让人坐牢，你只能反复播放然后祈祷噢上帝啊下一个最好是我没看过的，然后重复这个过程。最后一点就是本作的核心诡计，我只能说，稍微有那么点失望。

另：本作拿不到奖是正常的，因为本作包含反基督（重点）、裸露、脏话，白男们是不可能让这种作品登上大雅之堂的，不要因为在TGA等各路奖项没获奖就质疑它，能提名就是最大的认可了。

The first 25% of the game is one of the greatest games I've ever played. The remaining 75% is a trash fire. Folks: sometimes (often, in fact) less is more. The game dispenses with all of its brilliant subtleties and decides to explain so much as to make the story completely mundane. The first quarter of the game is filled with surprises. The last three are filled with doldrums. Enormously frustrating on those grounds. This could have very well been one of the most compelling video games ever made.

It's aight.

It is five stages of Arcade style Castlevania. Go left to right (and sometimes in other directions to collect keys), whip the things that pop up in front of you, use sub-weapons to cover your bases. It has pretty much every facet of the classic Arcade formula represented and it is all done serviceably.

Is it perfect? No. It is direly unpolished in a lot of places, and enemies are paced poorly. Most of them take one or two hits too many to kill, and there isn't enough variety, so you'll be slogging through the same foes throughout the game. The subweapons are of limited usefulness and the alchemy arts (item crashes) take far too much mana for what they do, so you'll be doing this largely by whip-whip-whipping.

By the end of the fifth (and final) stage my patience was already being tested, I don't think I could have done the harder difficulty which boasts even more enemy spawns.

But for what it was, it was worth $5.

1988 was a very cool year, with stylish music and fashion, and cool computers like the Amiga that could commandeer all the powers of multimedia. Scumm games were the state of the art back then and felt like real interactive cartoons, unlike any game of the time, and the novelty effect would help you cope with the tiring Lucasart "humour" and the nonsensical puzzles of which even the game's coverart makes fun of.
In order to really demonstrate the engine capabilities, the game uses a lot of different locations, way too many.
What really makes this a thumb down is the fact that it's very easy to get softlocked and unable to progress for one reason or another, and only realize you're stuck hours after you've made the mistake. So you're limited to either strictly follow a walkthrough, or waste an unreasonable amount of time trying to solve this unfunny game.
The story is not even interesting enough to watch a longplay on youtube.

I have played a few of this developers games now as I am very much pulled in by the graphics/art style and overall "chill" vibes of the games they have to offer. I like them for the most part they're affordable, simple and fun but... it's becoming very clear that the devs really are more "quantity over quality" and I'm starting to feel like by purchasing these games, I'm very much just contributing to a cash grab scheme.

The games are always buggy at some point with a few never even being addressed. All the games are super short and repetitive with very little to no replayability and they run on an extremely similar track. They're basically all the same thing in a different font. Oh, this one is witchy, this one is cute etc.

Carefully Stamped really solidified all of the above for me. The second the game loaded it was buggy, lol. I literally can not even progress in the game from the get go because there is NO TEXT. All the dialogue boxes are just blank with a random tick or cross where I am presumably supposed to make a choice or something? I have about 15 minutes "played" and all of those minutes are me trying to start the game, reloading, guessing where to click to try to get some progress to be able to start. 

I just can't with this dev studio anymore. They are starting to pump out games way too fast and too often. If you look at their profile, they have sooo many games coming out one after the other. There are currently TWENTY TWO confirmed games coming soon? All of them are just the same thing with a different theme, its crazy. It's clear they found their "niche" but it's a testament to the fact that very little effort is put in and goes back to it being quantity over quality with them. Having similar themed games isn't an issue, I would still enjoy that personally but when they're being churned out constantly and they're forever filled with bugs and issues - that's a problem. 
 There is no way these devs test their games or play through them themselves for the games to be shipping in the states they do and if they do... it's just further proof that they're here to make a quick buck and they do NOT care. 

I saw a dev response on another review claiming they spend a couple of months on games or whatever... that isn't anything to be bragging about imo. A couple of months per game and constantly pushing them out/announcing them one after the other is NOT a flex. Especially when they are a studio of "30 devs" with at least 22(!) games currently in development, wtf?
 Spend time and effort on the games and actually play and test them before taking people's money? 

I'm fed up of these games now, they're no longer fun and in this case - unplayable. Hoping the devs can calm down and make something good with actual stories and a decent playtime in the future. Oh, and of course no game breaking bugs on release?

This game is a gem. I can't believe it doesn't have more reviews. It is an excellent couch co-op game for the family. Reminds me of Fuzion Frenzy for Xbox, only Knight Squad has less variety but better, deeper game play in each game type. With Knight Squad keeping everyone on one screen, you really can play 8 people on the tiny Steam Deck screen all the way up to your TV.

I bought the game simply to see if the steam deck could handle 8 players. It can. Easily. I did have to change a setting on the steam deck itself or in the game to get more than 4 controllers recognized. Don't remember what it was. But I have had 7 people playing at it is a blast.

There are really two games here. The first is the one Knight Squad with default settings. It is okay, sometimes a little slow. I played for 30 minutes, thought that was nice, then put it down for a couple months. 

The second game is when you turn on max tier pickups on the shortest timer possible. My son and I randomly tried Knight Squad again, found the modifiers, set them for the extreme, and had an absolute blast! An hour later my entire family is sitting on the couch playing along. The matches become much faster paced, even frantic. No one can dominate for long because everyone is one pickup away from taking out the leader. You owe it to yourself to play max modifiers . It is a whole new game.

You can unlock new knights and a new sword for each knight. It is cosmetic only, but still nice to have some reward for playing.

Thank you Chainsawesome Games for this fun family friendly masterpiece. We need more games like this for the SteamDeck.

Which could be true but I've never played those. But this game reminds me of nes classics like Zelda, Final Fantasy and Uncle fester's quest(music wise). The music is really good in this game. Really captures the feel of the 8 bit era. The game is not super hard but challenging enough. The puzzles really challenge your common sense. I can even use a Dog whistle to signal a partner for my battle. Overall. It's a fun game. I recommend playing this especially for $4.99. It's really worth it.

Необычный формат судоку, где присутствует что-то похожее на сюжет и битвы с монстрами, где нужно драться с помощью как раз правильного заполнения клеточек в уже привычных нам квадратиках.

На что хочу обратить внимание тех, кто пришёл за идеальной игрой – забудьте про артефакты. Их нет. Ну или, конечно, можете пользоваться, но будьте готовы к тому, что убрать их не выйдет. Хоть я и знала, что для того, чтобы стать настоящим Судоку Мастером, нужно убить последнего босса без помощи артефактов, но примерно в середине игры я вдруг подумала: "Интересно, а что за плюшки они дают? Как оно вообще работает?".
Лучше бы не думала. Взяла артефакт, захотела его снять, а он не снимается. Пришлось идти проходить всё заново.

Сама же игра – это быстро успевать ставить правильные цифры и таким образом бить врагов. Если не тормозить, то враг не будет успевать отвечать, и именно это нам и нужно для того, чтобы набирать комбо и проходить противников на три звезды.
Можно покупать улучшения, зелья, всякие полезные штуки, которые могут помочь в прохождении. Про артефакты я уже упоминала выше, но не вижу смысла в их использовании, если есть желание получить все достижения. Если же на это всё равно, то они могут сильно помочь.
Также есть крайне неприятный момент. На последней локации в каждом бою можно допустить ошибку из-за того, что может быть несколько правильных решений, однако у этой игры правильное решение только одно, и тут нужно или пользоваться свитками для открытия рандомных клеток или надеяться, что вы угадаете правильно. Конечно, подобное крайне неприятно и можно отнести к серьёзному минусу.

Если вы любите судоку, то это может быть неплохой игрой на вечер или несколько, особенно по скидке.
Если же к судоку вы равнодушны (или вообще не любите), то, возможно, игра покажется скучной или даже сложной, если проходить без артефактов.

FlatOut — это серия аркадных гонок, впервые выпущенная в 2004 году, которая славится своей высокой динамикой, разрушительной физикой и яркой, эпичной атмосферой. Игра сочетает классические гонки с элементами экшена и безумных трюков, предоставляя игрокам возможность не только соревноваться за время, но и разрушать окружающую среду и автомобили.

Основные особенности
1. Геймплей и механика
Аркадные гонки:
FlatOut — это не симулятор, а именно аркада. Основная цель — выиграть гонку, используя скорость, ловкость и трюки. Игра славится быстрой динамикой и хаосом на трассе.

Разрушения и физика:
Одна из ключевых особенностей — разрушательная физика. Возможно разрушение частей автомобиля, разбивание препятствий, повреждение трассы и даже столкновения с другими машинами, приводящие к комичным эффектам.

Мини-игры и трюки:
В игре есть уникальный режим — "Мяч" (Stunt mode), где игроки могут выполнять прыжки, трюки и даже выбрасывать пассажиров из машины, что добавляет юмористического элемента.

Экстремальные ситуации:
Внутри гонок встречаются зомби, ловушки и другие фантасмагорические элементы, делающие каждую гонку непредсказуемой.

2. Графика и стиль
Графика яркая, насыщенная и с немного мультяшным оттенком, что подчеркивает комедийную и безумную атмосферу.

Детализированные модели автомобилей и эффектные взрывы позволяют ощущать масштаб разрушений и экшена.

3. Режимы и разнообразие трасс
В игре множество разнообразных трасс, от городских улиц до загородных трасс, каждая с уникальными препятствиями и уклонами.

Есть одиночные гонки, чемпионаты, режимы с разрушением и мини-игры.

Возможность выбрать разные автомобили с разными характеристиками.

Почему стоит играть
Экстремальный и веселый геймплей:
Высокий уровень хаоса, разрушений и свободной экшена создаёт ощущение веселья и безумия.

Разнообразие:
Различные режимы, трассы и автомобили позволяют запускать игру снова и снова, ко всему добавлена элемент неожиданности.

Ностальгия и стиль:
Для тех, кто любит классические аркадные гонки с физикой разрушений и юмористическим дизайном.

Мультиплеер:
В последних версиях появляется возможность соревноваться с друзьями или другими игроками онлайн, что делает игру ещё более захватывающей.

Минусы:
Иногда может казаться слишком хаотичной и менее стратегической.
Некоторые версии игры могут быть технически устаревшими или требовать доработки современных устройств.
Ограниченность контента в базовых версиях — больше внимания к физике и развлечениям.
Итог:
FlatOut — это яркая, мощная и безумная гонка, которая дарит массу положительных эмоций благодаря разрушительной физике, необычным трассам и веселому стилю. Игра отлично подойдет любителям динамичных и экшен-соревновательных гонок, жаждущим испытать моменты безумия и разрушений на трассе.

The Smurfs 2: The Prisoner of the Green Stone is a colorful, energetic 3D action-platformer developed by OSome Studio and published by Microids, offering a lively adventure that blends familiar family-friendly charm with a stronger emphasis on combat and exploration. This time, the Smurfs must retrieve the scattered fragments of the powerful Green Stone and stop a new villain, Stolas, whose corrupting influence is spreading chaos across the land. The twist comes from the Smurfs joining forces—begrudgingly—with their longtime foe Gargamel, who happens to be the only one capable of repairing Handy’s new invention, the SmurfoMix. The setup is simple but effective, giving the campaign a light narrative thread that supports the action without overshadowing it. Characters retain their trademark humor and personalities, creating a tone that remains faithful to the franchise’s gentle, playful spirit.

From the first moments, the game’s presentation stands out. The visuals are bright and expressive, with richly colored environments that give each location its own mood. Levels range from lush meadows and enchanted forests to volcanic caverns and icy wilderness, each packed with details that make them feel alive. Character models are polished, animating with an exaggerated expressiveness that fits the Smurfs’ cartoon origins. The world design strikes an attractive balance between accessibility and charm, making the environments appealing to younger audiences while still visually pleasant for adult players who appreciate clean art direction and smooth animation.

Gameplay mixes platforming with substantial action elements driven by the SmurfoMix, a multifunctional weapon that defines much of the experience. Rather than relying solely on jumping and traversal, players deploy various ammo types—glue-like shots, energy lasers, sticky projectiles and more—to both dispatch enemies and solve environmental puzzles. These mechanics add depth and variety, particularly as upgrades unlock new functions and interactions. Levels are noticeably more open than in the previous Smurfs game, encouraging exploration as you hunt for collectibles, clear corruption crystals, and discover optional challenge portals. Each area feels like a compact playground where movement, combat, and puzzle-solving intertwine.

However, despite its energetic design, the game’s loop can become repetitive. Many levels follow a familiar structure: enter a themed zone, clean up corruption, battle waves of enemies, gather the necessary fragments, and repeat. While the environments differ visually, the underlying mechanics don’t evolve enough to keep the experience consistently fresh. The increased focus on combat occasionally overshadows the platforming, with some battles feeling drawn out due to enemies acting as bullet sponges. Younger players may not mind the repetition, but those seeking more nuanced level design or inventive platforming challenges may feel the mid-game begin to drag.

Technically, The Smurfs 2 performs well overall, though it’s not entirely free of issues. Occasional minor bugs, such as odd physics reactions or brief drops in performance, can appear but rarely derail the experience. Control responsiveness is solid, making movement and aiming intuitive even for players with less experience. The game also includes difficulty settings that allow players to tailor the experience to their comfort level—an appreciated feature for a title aimed at a broad age range.

In terms of content, the game offers a respectable amount of adventure for its scope. The campaign lasts roughly six to eight hours depending on how thoroughly you explore, with extras and optional challenges providing additional playtime. While it doesn’t try to reinvent the platformer or action-adventure genres, it remains an enjoyable, polished experience that excels in its target niche: a family-friendly, visually appealing adventure full of light humor and engaging action. It’s not meant to challenge seasoned platformer veterans, but rather to offer a joyful romp and a sense of accomplishment through simple but satisfying gameplay.

Ultimately, The Smurfs 2: The Prisoner of the Green Stone is a spirited and competent entry in the franchise, expanding on the previous game with larger levels, more mechanics, and a more dynamic sense of progression. Its strengths lie in its charming presentation, accessible gameplay, and imaginative use of the SmurfoMix to blend action with exploration. Its weaknesses—repetition, occasional technical roughness, and a reliance on similar combat encounters—keep it from being a standout platformer, but it succeeds as a fun, wholesome adventure that fans of the Smurfs and younger players will appreciate.

Rating: 7/10

Man. This is friggin awesome. There has been some arcade racing games trying to capture the feel of arcade racing games from the 90s, but I'm yet to find one that gets it better than SPGP, but adding the modern touches a game like this needs.

The handling is amazing fun, the cars are twitch enough that you fell like you are battling them but never like it's unfar or an impossible battle. You don't need to use a brake a lot on circuits (in some you can easily flat-out the whole lap), so the focus is always on speed and doing the best racing lines. I've played a lot of the original Virtua Racing (and Daytona USA? Shit, probably the game that ate most of my quarters after Street Fighter 2), and I can honestly say the cars here handle better, they don't skid easily (unless you crash), but you need precision to control them. And an analog controller gives you enough precision for that. The game really shows a lot of love towards it, with lots of nice details on the tracks, which change every lap and small things like that.

And damn, this is still EARLY ACCESS. I wonder wha'ts coming up, but I am already having tons of fun with it.

The game does have some small flaws, like it's sometimes hard to know where you going to (mostly on cockpit camera - which is the most fun to play), the UI is kinda wonky, I wish some races were a littler shorter (5 minutes long races on arcades were common... but I can live with that), all to be expected on an Early Access game.

I hope the dev adds split screen suppport but, overall, if you want a good arcade racer, you really can't go wrong with SPGP . One of the best racing games I've played recently, and I do play a lot of them. Amazing how Rozz can pull it off and by himself make a game that's better than experienced gamedevs are doing.

Intentado dar un pantallazo de este gran juego en una reseña breve debo decir que me lleve una grata sorpresa con el mismo. Si bien no era ajeno al juego anterior "Ara fell" del cual continuan con algunas ideas las mismas las realizan con mejor resultado en esta nueva entrega, logrando asi un juego JRPG solido con una estetica "retror" a lo SNES, con actualizaciones en sus sistema jugable, calidad de vida, efectos y una historia que aun con sus conveniencias de guión esta bien llevado  y que paradojicamente aunque en pequeño, grandes empresas por rebuscar demasiado las mismas logan cosas menos organicas.

Conclusión: Recomendado

Si necesitan o les interesa algo que no me gusto, me incomodo o bien hubiera preferido diferentes serian:


- La decisión de usar 3 de 8 personajes en combate no es la que me gusta, prefiero los grupos de 4 que dan más variedad a estrategias y demas aunque lo entiendo debido a como estan configurados los combates y enemigos, aunque algunos se sienten desequilibrados a favor y otros en contra
- Algunas habilidades o hasta personajes senti que resultaban utiles SOLAMENTE en algunos combates y ambientes particulares.

- Para lo bien planteado que esta la historia, creo que hay partes que fueron forzadas o apuradas y no quisieron darle un desarrollo más organico, pero no quita que sea un buen cuadro en general

I can never bring myself to thumbs down a JRPG but I'm giving this a thumbs-up with some caveats.

Pros: 
- The pixel graphics are really solid. I don't really care for the dialogue portraits personally (not pixelated, they're weird and just don't really fit imo), but this might be a pro to some.
- Music is pretty good. Not "I have to download this" levels of good, but I'm not complaining. Battle theme kinda has a 'pirate-y' thing going on.
- Combat is really good. It's NOT perfectly balanced, but honestly I don't want a JRPG to be perfectly balanced, I want to find ways to break it/the best combos/items/characters to use.
- Equipment system is interesting. I can't say that I absolutely love it (I would've liked a bit more variety/equipment slots), but they tried something new. There's also some crafting but it's minimal and straightforward.

Cons:
- I only really have one here, but man it's a big one - the dialogue is so.... tryhard I guess is the best way to put it. It just oozes with this "I'm trying so hard to be Chrono Trigger/FF 6/Lufia 2", but it just isn't. This is broken down into two main issues I have with it - 
  1) The party will often get themselves into some sort of "high stakes" situation in a cutscene, and then it's as if the writer didn't know how to resolve it, and a character will just magically pull a rabbit out of a hat and all the sudden it's resolved. It makes the stakes so low whenever you're witnessing something you know should be important, because after you watch "something big is happening!" become "oh, literally nothing happened, why did I even watch that cutscene?" several times, you just stop caring. The worst part is that the resolutions for these dramatic events typically fall into 2 categories - 1) all the sudden, person/group A who is super mad at person/group B are ALL THE SUDDEN swayed by a few sentences and just decide to like, not do whatever they wanted to; or 2) just a weird joke thrown in and [b]BOOM[/b] situation resolved.
  2) All the relationship dialogue. Now I'll preface this by saying I literally could not care less about relationships in video games, I just don't care about fake romance with pixels on a screen, but it's really annoying here because of the way it's potrayed - "oooh you like Person X, don't you!!" "NUH-UH, SHUT UPP!"  It's what I'd imagine a high school girl's diary to contain. Not only this, but [spoiler] A vast majority of the eventual relationship choices in the game are objectively terrible and essentially make no sense [/spoiler].

Главный минус с точки зрения изображения — слабоватый (ограниченный, оригинальный) рендеринг от эмулятора syrup, который использует ядро pancake c software renderer, т.е. полностью повторяет работу GPU PS1 с нативным разрешением, с одной стороны это хорошо - архаично, с другой - без поддержки pgxp (fix тряска лиц) и upscale (fix лесенок). [b]Но при этом очень быстрая![/b] - должна эмулироваться без лагов даже на слабом ПК. Хоть как-то скрыть расплывчатую, неясную картинку и улучшить вид - [b]добавлены разные crt эффекты[/b], что хорошо.
Включены также — широкоформатность, 60fps, quicksave/load state и перемотка.
В-третьих, официально и при этом легально стали выпускать PS1 игры - благодаря разработчикам этого эмулятора syrup. Это круто, Implicit Conversions молодцы!
В целом, эмуляция игры очень хорошая, но было бы отлично иметь поддержку hw renderer с различными супер улучшениями и кастомными настройками хотя бы для PC, так как эмулятор кросс-платформенный.

О самой игре, это футуристичная (-киберпанк) экшен игра 2000 года.
Название игры отсылает к индикатору "страха", которая играет здесь важную роль - она заменяет счётчик здоровья. Урон, "страх", стрессовые моменты добавляют стресса, пульc учащается и индикатор окрашивается в красный, если при стрессовых моментах, в том числе при победе над врагами при незначительном уроне, индикатор старается возвращаться на место, то при серьезном уроне нужно выжить до определенного момента; бесшумность, скрытность, тихо устранённые противники, а также неполучение урона оставляют спокойствие.

Star Ocean: The Last Hope – 4K & Full HD Remaster is an updated version of the 2009 action RPG, offering enhanced resolution, sharper textures, and improved lighting while preserving the original game’s structure. The narrative functions as a prequel to the earlier entries, exploring humanity’s first ventures into deep space after a catastrophic conflict on Earth. Its tone mixes science-fiction discovery with character-driven drama across a wide range of planets.

The story centers on Edge Maverick and Reimi Saionji, members of an exploratory fleet seeking new worlds for humanity’s survival. Their journey expands into a larger conflict involving alien civilizations, infectious anomalies, and questions of responsibility in shaping interplanetary relations. While the writing is often earnest and occasionally melodramatic, the overarching plot provides consistent momentum through its combination of exploration and crisis.

Character development plays a major role, with a diverse party gathered from different worlds and species. Each character has a dedicated arc expressed through Private Actions, optional scenes that allow for deeper personality insight. These moments add emotional context, helping balance the game’s heavier themes with lighter interpersonal beats. Although some characterizations can feel uneven, the ensemble offers varied dynamics.

Combat uses a real-time system centered on mobility, combo timing, and positional tactics. The Blindside mechanic allows players to evade and counterattack by exploiting enemy focus, creating a high-speed rhythm that rewards timing and awareness. Characters specialize in different roles—ranged, melee, support, or magic—and the ability to switch between them mid-battle adds flexibility. The system remains one of the game’s strongest mechanics.

Exploration spans multiple planets, each featuring its own environments, enemies, and progression arcs. Areas range from natural landscapes to urban centers and mechanical complexes. While level design varies in complexity, the steady introduction of new regions keeps the journey feeling expansive. Crafting and item synthesis add extra layers of depth for players interested in optimization.

Presentation benefits significantly from the remaster’s visual improvements. Higher-resolution models, clean textures, and stable performance give the environments and battles sharper definition. The art style retains its original aesthetic, combining bright science-fiction designs with fantasy influences. The soundtrack mixes orchestral and ambient tracks that support both dramatic story moments and atmospheric exploration.

Star Ocean: The Last Hope – 4K & Full HD Remaster delivers a refined visual update of a large-scale sci-fi RPG centered on real-time combat, interplanetary travel, and character-based storytelling. Its strengths lie in its battle system, variety of locations, and the breadth of its ensemble cast. For players seeking a lengthy action RPG with a mix of exploration and fast combat, the remaster provides a polished and accessible way to experience the game.
