Very much an improvement over hiragana battle, in several ways.

Firstly, the difference in presentation is clear: most RTP map assets have been replaced by custom ones, there's voice acting and large portraits of characters, and sourced royalty free music is used in place of RTP music. The game does not feel like your average hobbyist RPG anymore, though there's some beginner mistakes like the music often not looping correctly, the sound effects of multi-hit skills being very loud, and some dungeon exits being handles improperly (for example, the train station dungeon exiting into the old train station). Nothing game breaking though.

Secondly, the educational content is better, and there's more of it. The main story is longer, so you have more opportunities to practice your knowledge against enemies, and there's more sidequests which will teach you vocabulary in both hiragana and katakana.

Thirdly, combat sees a major improvement. The mana bar has a reason to exist, meaning every character gets a variety of spells to use. A good compromise is that you cannot defeat an enemy with a spell that deals damage, you have to deal the finishing blow with a kana skill. There's also boss battles now, which are just a series of kana stuffed into one enemy that deals a lot more damage.

It's not perfect though.
The game is longer, but it contains a lot of dialog that has nothing to do with japanese whatsoever. Your party members (all 7 of em) have something to say in most scenes. It's entertainment value varies from bad to decent.
Also can I just ask: why does this game have heart-to-heart events? It's really just filler, a sort of distraction from the learning part. It wasn't for me, maybe someone else will feel different about it. And there's more than 20 of these events? If it would've included some vocabulary or some japanese cultural things I would've appreciated it more, but alas.

The most important question is: do I remember anything after playing it?
I think I can write about 80% of the katakana from memory, and I remember some new words in katakana. I did try learning katakana before starting this game, but that kinda failed as katakana does not seem to want to stick around for long. This is because they seem a bit confusing at first, some looking alike or similar to hiragana but sounding completely different.
If anything, this game is definitely a less painful way of learning katakana than any tool out there is, at least in my opinion.

So I've been following the author for this game for some time, and they've seemed pretty proud of this one. Naturally I've been excited and considering their influence from LSD Dream Emulator, I was anticipating some pretty striking visual design and cool ideas.

That is somewhat achieved here, in part. I love the purposeful clunkiness. The dated controls are cool to get used to and work around and demand a fuller attention, which can better invest the player into the game's atmosphere. Starting the game, I had put it down after failing a number of times to pass some of the starting areas because of how aggressively punishing it is. By design, the game utilises your HP in a way. Sorta like a half key system where you need more HP to survive, but there's also many traps you will most definitely take damage on, even if you're doing as much as you possibly can to dodge certain obstacles. This is because enemies in this game damage you by proxy of a damage radius, which will continuously damage you until you exit that radius. It's kind of novel, but very disheartening when you lack the means to control it at times.

The environments are overall very barren and often lacking in thematic variety, as the majority of the game maintains a liminal interior design. In some ways, I'm inclined to think this is a big part of the experience, as is the aforementioned punishing nature of the damage and control systems, but the more you wander the repetitive halls opening doors and hopelessly running out of consumable keys that lead you into little rooms with not so much as a couple collectables, you really start to wonder "Where's the line between art that punishes, and an enjoyable experience? Is this REALLY worth my time, and am I going to get anything out of this?" This is where we introduce the game's more hidden aspect:

[spoiler]The ARG on the connected company website.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]When I first encountered this, I was pretty damn excited. I love multimedia experiences where you investigate more than a game to solve puzzles, or to simply learn more about it, and to the credit of... "Apparatus Exanimus" (which is a title my friends and I have coined as comparable to a Harry Potter spell and makes me laugh the same way "Morbius" does) it does offer both a fictitious history background and various puzzle elements that are both written in a very natural way that I enjoyed. Can't complain in that sense. But what I can complain about is how much this game never really delivers much of anything all that significant. One could argue that the journey is ultimately what one experiences a piece of media for much more than a destination, but when your journey culminates as wandering through repetitive halls, facing off against maybe three kinds of enemies total, getting lost dozens of times and feeling a constant sense of dread because maybe you missed something important and you need to reset the game, turning to a website to read about death reports and solving puzzles, you might hope for something a bit more exciting to happen in the game or on the site that makes you go "WOAH! That was SO fucking cool! Holy shit." and that never happens. The experience maintains a very consistent acceptable level of engagement from start to finish and seldom escapes its comfort zone of mazes, doors and keys. It's a level of horror that's not very engaging, it's an ARG that's okay, the endings all lead to unique rooms with a sign or something, there's not much music to talk about besides like one track that plays in the end areas, and by the time I got done seeing the endings, it really felt like my time was wasted and I got next to nothing to think about after all was said and done. The ARG itself is based on the development of the game and various anomalies surrounding disappearances of the developers, and while that's cool, I think an experience like this demands more philosophical questions and geometric diversity in the game worlds than what was offered.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]Oh, and one other thing about the ARG. This game is to become dated inherently by the time the author can't pay for the website domain. This means any puzzles the game utilises won't work once this domain inevitably goes down. So if you're intending to play this and see all connected ARG material, you better get on it soon before they stop hosting the site.[/spoiler]

Ah, CastleMiner Z. One of those ~68p ($1USD) Xbox Live Indie Games on the 360 (80 Microsoft Points back in the day) that completely ate my free time. It blew up on Xbox Live Indie Games, became the best-selling game on the service and was the first XBLIG title to break a million paid downloads – not bad for a £0.65 indie survival game.

Then it went quiet for years. No real updates, just nostalgia… until the dev suddenly came back to dig it up from the grave and start resurrecting it again. Honestly, it’s not “just another Minecraft clone” – it has its own personality and gameplay style. It leans way more into survival horror, guns and dragons, with a much darker vibe and atmosphere than the original CastleMiner.

I remember spending hours on Xbox 360 with this and the other cheap DigitalDNA games. A big part of the charm was how little they cost and how some of them had redeem codes you could use in other games by the same dev to unlock extra items – proper “indie ecosystem” stuff (shame that scene is dead). I grabbed a few of those games purely for that reason; they were all fun in their own way, but none of them hit like CastleMiner Z. Avatar Laser Wars, the original CastleMiner – both good, but CastleMiner Z was the one that really stuck with me.

If I remember right, the original CastleMiner had some surprisingly nice lighting, especially reflections on water, but Z definitely has a much darker, grimmer feel overall. It absolutely shows its age now, but using your Xbox avatar as your character was a really neat touch at the time – and honestly, a Steam avatar option today would still be a cool feature.

On Steam it’s about a fiver right now, and personally I’d love to see it closer to the £2.99 mark, but whatever – it’s a classic. Definitely worth picking up, and the 4-pack is a no-brainer if you’ve got a few mates to drag along for only about double the price.

A Game with potential, but many letdowns and missed opportunities. 
I had 2 playthroughs, 1 on easy as CIA and one on Medium as [spoiler] Mossad [/spoiler]. While i had a good enough time on the first playthrough to start the second, the second "extended" one was quite the dissapointment and i cannot recommend going for a second playthrough for the things you "missed"

The bones of the gameplay are solid but are hampered in many aspects. While the mechanics work pretty fine, for the first 2/3rds of the game your agents wont have enough AP/FP to actually utilise a lot of mechanics to it's potential or intention, and you need a guide for the body engineering to reach those milestones.  The stealth works well enough, but become a bit tedious, the game pushes you to play loud (you get 50% xp on stealth kills, so if you focus on stealth all your agents will be underleveled) and that too works reasonably well if you adapt to the setting. "Frontal assaults" usually end up being a well setup ambush to take out half the enemies on a map, then mop the rest up on the next turn, rush to objectives and exfiltrate before reinforcements arrive. 
The Enemy AI did not seem to change between difficulties, the enemies just got more hp and damage, often leaving enemies with 3-10 hp left, which is incredibly frustrating if you dont have more than one FP, and didnt really add much to my normal difficulty playthrough either in forms of challenge nor fun. No mission has more than 9-10 enemies, 3-5 of which are usually just absolute trashmobs + reinforcements, which also doesnt really give you the feeling of storming a base of anything. The weapons are balanced in a weird way, where there is always half of the available inventory which is straight up useless or hopelessly outclassed, but which class of weapons this is changes as the game progresses ( Shotguns and pistols are great in the beginning, Shotguns, Snipers and SMG in the midgame, and Assault Rifles in the Lategame, LMGs are always useless)

The story itself is intruiging on the first playthrough until you realize everything is completely scripted through as it has to align with historical events and reach the quite unsatisfying ending. All story is strictly communicated through brief voicelines during the mission and are at times quite easy to miss, not that you are missing a lot as most of the times it is just another breadcrumb. Even in the end the big unbelievable threat you have to stop to save the world lacks any sense of urgency or drama as it is just another mission where you push a button on a terminal.  The "extended" playthrough seemed to add exactly one 5-10 minute mission in the very end to clear up the REAL mastermind behind Beholder, and with as little as the story actually changes you figure out halfway through the second playthrough anyways who it is. 
The additional faction you unlock after the first playthrough [spoiler] Mossad [/spoiler], has no real unique spin or perspective, nor uniqute mechanics to add to the game. It baits you early with plotpoints about a chemical weapon attack on [spoiler] Isreal [/spoiler] but seems to forget about that plot halfway through. It also dangles hunting down infamous nazi [spoiler]Jospeh Mengele[/spoiler] in your face, but he ends up just standing around motionless in a big open room in a mission as a side objective with no real buildup and exactly 3 lines of dialog after you kill him, and that is basically all the story missions in a nutshell. 
The Information gathering system is interesting the first couple of times, but quickly becomes an unbearable chore. While the files have 8-10 pieces of intel it is fine i guess, but it will later load you with 15-20 pieces of intel, each with red herrings on them, and expect you to do DOZENS of them, and character progression is locked behind them in the form of body engineering recipies. Also you will notice on your 3rd File or so that all the actual pieces of intel are completely identical, with random blacked out parts and names switched, so you wont get any additional lore from them either. And often times you will just spend your time micromanaging 30 agents since you can't actually put actions in a queue

If you enjoy the tactical approach and setting you will have fun with 75% of one playthrough and its worth picking up on sale. Just dont expect anything but a strictly linear story with a handful of story mission and a ton of random filler. Replayabilty is pretty much 0 in my opinion, so dont get baited into the second playthrough iif the first left you slightly dissapointed, that feeling wont go away.  All in all it is not enough to give a thumbs down in my opinion, but it could have been so much more!

[h2]📜Описание[/h2]
[b]Terminator: Dark Fate – Defiance[/b] — это ваш личный билет на самое неудачное пост-апокалиптическое свидание с искусственным интеллектом, который явно обделен чувством юмора. Это стратегия в реальном времени, где вы — не суперсолдат-одиночка, а этакий "менеджер среднего звена на Судный день", который должен не только выжить, но и вести за собой разношерстную армию таких же, как и вы, невольных участников этого тотального барбекю от Легиона. Ваша задача — возглавить "Основателей" и доказать, что человечество заслуживает второго шанса, даже если для этого придется в сотый раз переигрывать миссию из-за одного неудачно брошенного вражеского снаряда.

[h2]🎨Графика и звук[/h2]
Игра скромно напоминает, что конец света — это не только экзистенциальный ужас, но и эстетическое наслаждение. Визуальный ряд — это палитра, где преобладают оттенки выжженной земли, ржавого металла и багровых вспышек плазменных выстрелов. Техника и разрушаемость окружающей среды проработаны с любовью, достойной истинного машиниста: вы с замиранием сердца будете наблюдать, как модуль за модулем отказывает в вашем основном танке, превращая его из грозной машины в беспомощную мишень. Звуковое сопровождение — это симфония апокалипсиса. Скрип гусниц, треск автоматных очередей, оглушительный рёв взрывов и металлический скрежет терминаторов сливаются в идеальный саундтрек, который не просто погружает в атмосферу, а заставляет инстинктивно пригибаться к монитору.

[h2]🎮Геймплей[/h2]
Это не просто RTS, а симулятор выживания для тактических мазохистов. Здесь вас ждет главный парадокс: вы управляете целой армией, но каждый солдат и каждая единица техники на вес золота. Ваша тактика и каждый выбор на поле боя имеют глубокие последствия: другие фракции и персонажи либо присоединятся к вам, либо станут врагами, а определенные миссии будут доступны или недоступны в зависимости от ваших действий. Вы будете не просто строить базы и кидать ордами юнитов на врага, а кропотливо собирать свою армию, переходя с карты на карту, бережно сохраняя ветеранов и латая дыры в броне уцелевшей техники. Это игра, где можно выиграть сражение, но потерпеть стратегическое поражение, потратив на победу слишком много бесценных ресурсов.

[h2]📖Сюжет и атмосфера[/h2]
Сюжет кампании служит идеальным каркасом для ваших собственных тактических триумфов и провалов. Вы — командир "Основателей", одной из последних организованных сил человечества, и вам предстоит сорвать планы Легиона по тотальному уничтожению. Атмосфера — это главный козырь игры. Это чувство постоянного напряжения, когда вы осознаете, что против вас воюет не просто глупый ИИ, а расчетливый и безжалостный противник, не знающий усталости и сомнений. Это мир, где каждая победа дается с трудом, а потери ощущаются как настоящие. Вы будете принимать решения, от которых зависит судьба целых отрядов, и именно это создает тот самый, неповторимый драматизм войны за выживание.

Was für ein Indiegame-Highlight! Nachdem ich die Demo von SCHROTT bereits gezockt hatte, habe ich den Early Access direkt zum Release gekauft und in den ersten 6,5 Stunden eine richtig geile Zeit gehabt.
Obwohl es sich noch um Early Access handelt, gibt es schon jetzt viel zu entdecken: Perks, Rig-Teile und Achievements motivieren zu immer neuen Runs. Die zwei aktuellen Maps haben es schon ordentlich in sich, und laut Roadmap kommen bald weitere, noch schwierigere dazu.
Die Fähigkeiten sind abwechslungsreich und müssen klug eingesetzt werden, das Fahrgefühl ist rasant und die Hindernisse sind auch nach vielen Runden noch challenging.
Besonders freut mich, dass es eine globale Bestenliste gibt, auf der man sich mit anderen Spielern messen kann – das spornt zusätzlich an. 
Die Grafik erinnert schon etwas an Borderlands und passt daher perfekt zum chaotischen Rennspiel-Feeling.
Der Fortschritt ist schnell, aber fair: Perks und Rig lassen sich stetig verbessern und erleichtern [spoiler](oder erschweren!)[/spoiler] die kommenden Runs.

RICOSHET: ФЕНОМЕНОЛОГИЯ СОВЕРШЕНСТВА

Введение

Среди всех проектов корпорации Valve Corporation — от Half-Life до Portal — существует один,
настолько самодостаточный, что его можно считать идеей игры в чистом виде.
Речь, конечно же, о Ricochet (2000) —
не просто аркаде, а философском трактате о падении, возвышении и круговороте дисков.

⸻

I. Метафизика прыжка

Когда игрок совершает прыжок в Ricochet, он буквально отрывается от догматов индустрии.
Это не просто механика — это акт самопознания.
Ты не знаешь, куда приземлишься, но делаешь шаг.
Так рождается чистая вера в геймдизайн, свободная от HUD, квестов и туториалов.

«В момент падения человек ближе всего к пониманию Valve.»
— Гейб Ньюэлл, вероятно.

⸻

II. Геймплей как метафора капитализма

В Ricochet нет экономики, нет шопа, нет микротранзакций.
Это единственная игра, где невозможно купить преимущество,
потому что преимущество — это ты сам.

Каждый матч — рынок идей,
где побеждает не тот, у кого круче скин ножа
а тот, кто вовремя отпустил левую кнопку мыши.
Это идеальный антикапиталистический баланс,
в котором даже Маркс бы сказал:

«Да, здесь человек действительно свободен.»

⸻

III. Архитектура агонии

Геометрия арен Ricochet — не просто полигоны.
Это архитектурная поэма,
в которой платформа — это алтарь,
а пропасть — метафора провала современного геймдева.

Каждое падение — не поражение, а постигнутая истина.
Именно здесь игрок впервые осознаёт:

«Я не умер. Я — стал частью уровня.»

⸻

IV. Сообщество как монашеский орден

Ricochet — не массовая игра.
Это не Dota, не CS, не Team Fortress.
Это элитарная обитель избранных,
где онлайн в 3 человека уже считается международным чемпионатом.

Игрок Ricochet — это монах интерактивности:
он не ищет матчмейкинг,
он ищет смысл.
Он заходит на сервер не чтобы победить,
а чтобы почувствовать связь с диском.

⸻

V. Эстетика минимализма как протест против гиперреализма

Valve предсказала будущее.
Когда все стремились к графике и RTX,
Ricochet уже понимал: совершенство не нуждается в текстурах.
Фон — чернота космоса.
Ты — светящийся силуэт.
Это не арена. Это внутренний мир игрока.

Гейб Ньюэлл мог бы сказать:

«Ricochet — это когда ты играешь не в игру, а в отражение самого себя.»

⸻

VI. Философская интерпретация диска

Диск в Ricochet — символ.
Он вращается, летит, возвращается.
Это не оружие. Это цикл жизни.
Ты бросаешь диск — как доверяешь миру себя.
Он возвращается — как опыт, иногда по лицу.

Это акт доверия и разочарования одновременно.
Сократ им бы гордился.

⸻

VII. Почему Ricochet — вершина эволюции Valve

Half-Life подарил нам сюжет.
Portal — метафору.
Но Ricochet подарил абсолютную истину:
игра не должна ничего объяснять,
чтобы быть совершенной.

Valve могла закрыть проект,
но не сделала этого —
потому что закрыть Ricochet — всё равно что закрыть смысл.

⸻

VIII. Заключение

Ricochet — это не игра. Это чистая идея.
Это пик, после которого всё стало просто повторением.
CS2? — торговля.
Dota 2? — мета.
Ricochet? — философия.

⸻

“Когда диск падает в пропасть — падает и человечество.
Когда он возвращается — начинается надежда.”
— неизвестный игрок Ricochet, 2003 год.

Entspanntes Spielen für Zwischendurch.

Wer die Serie kennt, kommt eh nicht dran vorbei.
Alle anderen, die mal ein Spiel zur Entspannung spielen wollen, sollten es einmal versuchen und mit dem ersten Teil der Serie starten.

Man ist wie immer irgendein Bauerndepp im Mittelalter, der wie in jedem guten Märchen im Laufe vieler Ereignisse zu einem angesehenen Helden wird.
Dazu klickt man sich durch allerlei starrer Kartenschnipsel, die nach und nach freigeschaltet werden.
Dort redet man mit Personen, bekommt Aufträge, sammelt Gegenstände ein, klöppelt auf Monster und Gegner ein, und so weiter.

Das ist jedoch kein normales Adventure- oder gar Actionspiel, nein, denn das Gameplay setzt strategisches Vorgehen mit Ressourcenmanagement vorraus.
Das Umfeld macht nichts, nur man selbst wandert schrittweise umher, oder führt irgendeine Aktion aus, die dann etwas bewirkt.

Jede Aktion kostet irgendeine Ressource, man ist also ständig damit beschäftigt für geplante Aktionen zuerst einmal die dafür benötigten Waren zu besorgen und. ggf zu craften, oder gegen andere Waren mitunter mehrmals mit Gewinn einzutauschen, oder teuer beim Händler zu kaufen.
Es kann sich also durchaus lohnen, bei einem lukrativen Warenkreislauf selbst gut daran zu verdienen, ehe man sich weiter ins Abenteuer wirft.
Denn nichts ist ärgerlicher, wenn man später für ein Schwert seine gesamten letzten Ressourcen beim Händler für ein paar Münzen abgibt.
Dann darf man sich darauf einstellen, dass es erst einmal ziemlich zäh weitergehen wird, weil jede weitere Aktion sicher etwas benötigen wird, was man gerade nicht mehr hat. 
Also wer schon im echten Leben schlampig ist und sein Geld einfach so raus haut, für den ist dieses Spiel auch nichts.
Wer gerade etwas knapp bei Kasse ist, der sollte womöglich mal wieder dringend die ganzen Karten absuchen, denn zwischendrin gibt es auch immer wieder mal neue versteckte Ressourcen zu finden, wie z.B. Eier, Pilze etc..

Die Grafik ist seit Teil 1 von vor langer Zeit nicht besser geworden.
Was damals schon eher zweckmäßig war, hätte längst nachgebessert werden sollen, denn das ist gefühlt optisch so alt wie ein Sacred 1 oder Age of Empires 2.
Ok, Grafik ist nicht alles, aber für kommende Generationen sollten die Entwickler echt mal für eine Frischzellenkur ausschau halten, so etwas verkauft sich dann auch wieder gleich viel besser.

Die Errungenschaften sind alle wieder gut machbar und kann man in einem Durchlauf mitnehmen, wunderbar!
Der Schwierigkeitsgrad ist für Casual Gamer gedacht, man soll einfach nur einige Stunden Spaß haben, was ich auch hatte.

Fazit: Eins, zwei, drei - im Gras liegt noch ein Ei. Einsacken! :-)

[i]Леди и Джентльмены, представляю Вашему вниманию Dragon Age 2 – это игра с динамичной боевой системой и более камерным сюжетом, сосредоточенным вокруг одного города[/i]
Далее будет разбивка на блоки в которых я укажи плюсы и минусы данной игры
[h1]Сюжет и атмосфера[/h1]
[b]Сюжет:[/b] В Dragon Age II игрокам предстоит выступить в роли Хоука, нищего беженца, которому предстоит стать самым важным персонажем в мире Dragon Age. Легенда о возвышении героя, пережившего Мор, ставшего Защитником Киркволла, окружена множеством слухов и мифов. В новой игре, сюжет которой охватывает 10 лет истории этого мира, игрокам предстоит принимать непростые решения, искать поддержки опаснейших союзников, наживать богатство и славу и завоёвывать себе место в легендах. От Вас зависит, какой будет история, навсегда изменившая мир Dragon Age.
[b]Повествование:[/b] Сюжет охватывает десятилетие жизни Хоука, фокусируясь на его пути к власти и богатству и последующих последствиях его решений.
[b]Противоречивость:[/b] Несмотря на скучный сюжет в начале и однотипные задания на 4 одинаковых картах, игра содержит интересные моральные дилеммы и непредсказуемый финал, особенно во второй половине игры.
[h1]Геймплей и боевая система[/h1]
[b]Динамика:[/b] Боевая система стала более динамичной, с большим количеством врагов, более короткими и насыщенными схватками. Но при этом стала и проще, нет такого разнообразия скилов и комбинаций. По сути у Вас 2 боевых ветки и 3 вспомогательных + выбор 1-ой из 3 специализации (хотя можно выбрать 2, но это не очень целесообразно)
[b]Упрощение RPG-элементов:[/b] Убраны некоторые RPG-элементы, такие как не боевые навыки (убеждение, воровство), а экипировка отряда вообще не управляется. Теперь Вы только можете одевать и подбирать экипировку только гл. Герою! Максимум со партийцам теперь Вы выберете бижутерию.
[b]Боевые механики:[/b] Боевые способности стали более активными, с улучшенными пассивными навыками. Маги и воины получили новые возможности. Бои стали более эффектными, зрелищными
[b]Повторяющиеся локации:[/b] Их тут 10-11. Вы просто будете всю игру ходить по ним кругами. Только в конце игры добавят 1 или 2 новых. И то это уже будет финальная битва… Хоть и местами локации выглядят шикарно. Тот же Киркволл или Подземные тропы с прожилками Лириума – красота!
[b]Побочные квесты:[/b] Просто ворох однотипных заданий, встречаются конечно что-то интересное, но в целом: принеси, убей. 
[h1]Персонажи и компаньоны[/h1]
[b]Со партийцы:[/b] Ну тут Bioware держит планку – все персонажи с своей историей, нравами и темпераментом. У каждого есть личный квест и им сопереживаешь. Без романтики нас так же не оставили – все в лучших традициях. Но есть ложка дёгтя – Себастьян – этот персонаж добавляется в DLC. Задел хороший на историю, но сам персонаж скучный и скилы у него так себе, Варрик или Изабелла – в разы интереснее
[b]Система диалогов:[/b] Диалоговая система получила систему как в  Mass Effect – колесо с 3 видами диалогов (добрый, сарказм, злой), которая упрощает взаимодействие с NPC, но теряется отыгрыш. Когда ты не знаешь к чему все приведет и перечитываешь не сколько раз что ответить. А ту примерно понял кто что любит (к кому – то нужно по доброму, к кому – то с сарказмом) и клацаешь, даже не читаю ответ. А как его читать когда его нет, только Иконки на выбор?! Это минус Господа
[h1]Резюме[/h1]
Игра все же шикарна! Конечно не вызовет тот восторг как Origin, но все же шикарна. Особенна вторая половина игры: тут и дилеммы, нравственный выбор и финты сюжета! Но первую половину игры это: скучно, однообразно. Игра часто продается Бандлом – если Вы любитель RPG и хороших сюжетов, интересных персонажей, темного фантази – то обязательно к приобретению!

Прошло немного времени и вот мой честный обзор на Dragon Age II. А знаете почему немного? Да потому что было довольно интересно играть, и не так сложно (да простят меня любители тактик и стратегий DAO). 
Игра начинается как обычно не с интро, а с того, что в этот раз она решила тупо не запускаться. Да, я уже привык, что надо идти копаться в файлах игры минут 20, перед тем как начать игру, но в этом ничего супер страшного нет, просто хотелось бы запустить и играть. 

В меню же нас встречает прикольная надпись "Попробуйте демо Mass Effect 3", но суть больше в другом. Вопрос, нах** нужно регистрировать учётную запись к сервису, который уже не работает, так ещё и подгружает этот аккаунт минуты 2. Мой совет, отключите это и не регистрируйте ничего. 

Итак, вот мы зашли и выбор класса. Тут конечно фанаты первой части отчасти правы, это вам не 25 прологов и 75 разветвлений, тут есть выбор между классическими классами и полом, рас больше нет. Кто-то скажет урезали, а я скажу, зато в этом случае получился некий командор Шепард, который имеет свой характер и озвучку, что важно, таким образом персонаж воспринимается намного лучше. Чем-то жертвуем, но получаем взамен что-то также очень интересное. На этот раз я решил попробовать себя в роли мага, так как они меня жесть как замучили в первой части, да и во второй им противостоять сложнее всего. Скажу только одно, класс "магесса" меня очень сильно удивил, такого слова до этого я не встречал, и нет, это не мизогиния.

Дело доходит до сюжета, локаций, персонажей и геймплея, начну с основы. Место действия у нас уже, так скажем, другое государство, а именно город-государство Кирквол, но мы, по факту беженцы из того же Ферелдена, убегали с семьёй от Мора, сестрёнка к сожалению по пути того. Сама локация, как и графика в игре очень даже ничего, учитывая, что игра 2011 года. Да, конечно разнообразия локаций, как в Origins нет и это проблема, там старались всегда удивить новой локацией, но здесь, они очень часто повторяются. Об этом не сказал только ленивый и по началу было вроде нормально, но когда узнаёшь, что игра состоит из актов, а действия их крутятся как раз во всех этих локациях, то под конец тебе уже просто надоедает бегать по одним и тем же местам.

Сюжет уже не такой глобальный, как было до этого, мы не помогаем устранять Мор, который грозит всему миру, а решаем локальные проблемы между храмовниками и магами, которые по итогу, возможно выльются в окружающую среду и, я так подозреваю, это будет основной темой Инквизиции (как будто это логично), но пока ещё не здесь. Сам сюжет делится на акты, как я говорил и в каждом акте мы решаем определённую проблему, но спойлерить не буду. 

Каждый раз, начиная говорить о персонажах, стоит просто упомянуть - это старые BioWare, здесь в этом плане всё очень круто. По началу я думал, что разочаруюсь, потому что, допустим Карвер меня изначально бесил, и я отлично понимал, что в конце может встать выбор - брат против брата, за основу не взято. Но, как оказалось, по итогу раскрытия мне симпатизировали многие, кроме тех кого можно сосчитать по пальцам: Фенрис, Карвер, и какого-то хе** Андерс, который ультанул под конец. Диалоги во время перебежек между персонажами что-то с чем-то, я действительно смеялся, если собрать правильную компанию. У меня всегда был практически один стак: Авелин, Изабелла, Фенрис и мой пёс Дебик. Фенриса приходилось брать только лишь потому, что в этой игре нельзя поменять класс своим сопартийцам, поэтому нужен был хоть кто-то кто может впитывать урон, пришлось терпеть его нытьё. Но Изабелла и Авелин, просто поставьте их рядом и вам будет очень весело. И, кстати да, стоит упомянуть, что квесты сопартийцев очень даже интересные. 

Что же до геймплея, системы диалогов, то это наверное одно из самых больных мест фанатов первой части. Геймплей сильно упростили, очень даже, я пробежал всю игру, спокойно сражаясь со всеми (а может потому что я был магом). Да, есть пару просто очень жирных врагов, но сражаться с ними легко, просто долго. Боевая система стала намного динамичнее, красивее, зрелищнее. Врагов на квадратный метр также дофига как и раньше. Прокачка стала легче и интуитивно понятнее, что может быть и минусом, а кому-то наоборот. Самое главное теперь не нужно 40 минут разговаривать с персонажами, узнавать лор, а потом буквально 3 часа драться с мобами. Здесь выдержали "золотую середину", 20 минут разговоров, потом 20 минут драк. Тебе не успевает надоесть. Система диалогов сменилась в сторону Mass Effect'a, теперь уже не 10 вариантов ответа на один вопрос, но она мне понравилась. Она стала живее что ли, можно как быть типом, который старается везде всё решить мирно, можно прикалываться над всеми, а можно просто раздавать по щщам, выбор за вами. Да и сама режиссура диалогов огонь, в этом конечно BioWare молодцы. По поводу отношений с тем же полом, что и вы. Да блин и в первой части это было, да практически в любой игре от этой студии, главное, что это опционально и я замутил с Изабеллой, всё.

Под конец, ещё не подводя итог, хотелось бы рассказать про звуковое сопровождение и дополнения. Музыка в игре моё почтение, как и в первой части, но, на самом деле, меня это уже так сильно не удивляет. Я уверен, с вероятностью 90% в третьей части с музыкой проблем не будет и атмосферу выдержать она сможет, да ещё и засесть в душу. Про дополнения много говорить особо не буду, а тут как будто и не надо, это же не Пробуждение из первой части на 20 часов. Дополнение с "эльфийкой" довольно весёлое, оно даёт расслабиться и познать культуру Орлейской аристократии, после него мне даже было бы интересно видеть в одной из частей Орлей своими глазами. Второе же более мрачное, загадочное, а мне такое нравится, где ты по крупицам собираешь детали и в конце сражаешься, наверное, с самым сложным боссом этой части. Мой вердикт: и то и то классно, надо пройти оба и не пожалеете.

【嗯……第一篇评测就给《饥饿地城》辣23333~】

【第一印象】
发现这个游戏的时候是我真的闲的无聊看看免费游戏，结果就发现了！
本人很喜欢像素风（8-bit）的游戏！还有RPG类型的！
开始玩的时候，新手教程是“老练囚犯”，当时就觉得这个人物好好玩。
接着又打了几盘人机。电脑跟你打从来不怂的，1V3的时候经常有，开局一会儿就三杀了。每次死了一两次后都会想“要不我也像电脑那样不怂？试试看”，结果每次都是送送送……
最后一盘就是占领祭坛（反正我是这样叫的），每次都有电脑跑去站，然后我就一直骚扰，每次都把他打死在祭坛里面，还是占领不了……心疼自己智商。

【游戏趣味性】
1.像素风（8-bit）。如果有一点点信仰的玩家第一眼都会喜欢的吧。
2.游戏模式。稍微有一点点枯燥，就是杀杀杀，DieDieDie。希望官方以后出一点娱乐模式or剧情模式（就像RPG类做任务）~

【好评的理由】
1.免费游戏好伐？！这都不给好评？游戏素质也还算不错！
2.像素风（8-bit）这点就给很多信仰玩家加分！
3.很多人物，很耐玩。
4.电脑的智商在我的眼里还算蛮高的。
5.DLC40R良心好伐？不想花钱玩人物的也可以在游戏里刷游戏币买啊！
6.很多关卡、很多技能、武器，应该来说玩不腻。（上面我说的游戏模式枯燥指的是单纯杀杀杀枯燥啊……）
7.占的内存很少……300MB，对于我这种渣渣宽带来说so easy。
8.支！持！简！体！中！文！

【差评的理由】
1.服务器问题真的很大好伐。欧洲服务器300ping，到亚洲服务器直接到了600ping，突然感觉我是欧洲人了呢！（并不，还是非洲的）
2.人物、技能平衡性有点差。具体什么情况还是自己玩玩，就知道了。

【总结】
大概就差不多了~反正我很喜欢这个游戏，已经准备花钱购买人物了。

毕竟作者花了这么多时间去做游戏，开放是免费的，也就只有DLC赚赚钱。还是一句话，支持作者，让作者有把游戏完善下去的动力！

한줄로 평가하면, 기본 골자가 완성된 게임이자 아직 살이 안붙은 갈비같은 게임이다.

잡고 먹을만해 보이는데, 뜯어먹을게 없다.

일단 장점을 언급하면, 네크로댄서마냥 블록단위로 움직이며 던전을 해쳐나가는 게임이다. 가장 큰 차이점은 이건 리듬게임이 아니라는 것정도. 

플레이어블 캐릭터도 3명에 스토리도 준수하다.  캐릭터별로 2가지 스킬이 있는데, 뭘 선택하냐에 따라 다른 플레이를 즐길 수 있다. 

연격이라는 재밌는 스텟이 있어서 쓰는 맛도 있다.

스테미나까지 고려하고, 회피를 적당히 써야하는 것도 게임의 몰입에 도움이 되는 것같다.

다만....  

엔딩을 보려면 난이도를 높혀가며, 다회차 플레이를 해야하는데 캐릭터 말고는 해금할게 없다.

정령이나, 전송기, 함선 커스터마이징, 스톤, 물약업그레이드 모두 난이도와 상관없이 반복 플레이 하다보면 전부 초반에 해금될뿐더러 이런 소울라이크 게임에 기본 골자같은 것들이라 특색처럼 다가오는 건없다.

그나마 스톤과 함선 커스터마이징은 참신하다. 

스톤의 기본스텟이나, 커스터마이징에 혜택이 들어가 있는건 처음보니까. 대신 후자의 경우에는 그 혜택때문에 멋대로 커스터마이징 할수 없다. 외관과 성승을 따로 선택할수 있었으면 좋겠다.

이 스톤도 아쉽다. 타르코프마냥 죽으면 팬티에 있는것만 가져오는데, 그걸 보관할 보관함이 있어서 파밍하는 맛이 있는것도 아니다. 그냥 좋은 거 5개 얻으면 그 5개에서 추가하고 뺄것만 생각해야한다. 

그렇게 올린 스텟 중에서도 특정 스텍이 중요한데, 치명타 확률이랑 연격은 걍 높으면 장땡이다. 다른게임도 치확 높으면 그냥 깬다! 할수 있지만, 여긴 유물과 스톤,정령으로 치명타 확률이 확보가 되는데, 특정빌드에서는 그게 너무 강하다. 다른 스텟이 무의미해 질 정도로. 개인적인 경험일수도 있겠지만, 그러다 보니 다른 빌드에 손이 잘 안가기도 한다.

또, 툴팁이 조금 짜증난다. 정령을 예로들면, 바람 정령이 질주를 부여한다. 그럼 질주가 뭘까? 그건 알려주지 않는다. 대충 효과를 보고 짐작만 할 뿐이다. 최소한 내가 받는 버프가 뭔진 알아야되는 것 아닌가?

정령도 3마리를 랜덤으로 받는데 이중 선택권이 없다. 즉, 5개들고 있는게 고정인 스톤, 랜덤으로 받는 정령, 능력이 정해진 커스터마이징=> 소울라이크 게임인데 내가 무슨 빌드를 가고싶다고 갈수 있는 것도 아니고, 그런 기능이 해금되지도 않는다. 

또 캐릭터가 3명이 있지만 3명의 스토리가 모두 존재하는 것도 아니다. 오로지 메인 스토리 뿐이며 다른 캐릭터를 들고와서 이야기를 진행해도 NPC는 고정된 대사를 말한다. 

무엇보다 중간저장이 없다. 한번 시작하면 40분, 30분 걸리는 게임이 스테이지마다 한번 저장 만들기가 어려웠나? 이건 진짜 썩나가는 부분이라고 생각한다

또 자동공격 이거 내가 보는 대상이랑 다른거 때릴때 그것때문에 손해보는 경우도 많다. 좀 짜증나는 부분.

그리고 HP다는 UI속도가 느려서 급한 상황에서는 저 적이 죽었는지 살았는지 모르겠어서 공격 헛칠때도 있다. 이것도 상당히 거슬린다.

또 전송기나 몇몇 상호작용 하는 기능이 나오면 그 기능이 뭔지, 도움말에 선택지에 대한 설명이 남아있기는 해야할것같다. 한번 까먹으면 뭔 기능인지 감으로 때려맞추는것도 피곤하다.

황혼난이도? 까지 오면서 느낀점은 이정도이다. 그래도 게임사가 할만한 게임을 만들었고, 뼈대자체는 튼튼해 보이니 개추준다.

The most unexpected sequel I could ever imagine— went from a horror story game to a Metroidvania, and yet it's the best I could ever ask for.
I'm not a Metroidvania enjoyer or anything of sorts— in fact, I don't like Metroidvania at all, including big titles like Hollow Knight and Dead Cells. This game however, managed to push beyond those boundaries, as here I am having 100%'ed it. The UI sucks and is very simple, but you can get used to it. Aside from that, it's a very story-rich and content filled game with more than 15 bosses and a pretty big map with multiple enemies and characters.
It is made in such a way that you don't need to play the past game, as the events are explained very summarized to you, although I really suggest playing if you like.

Needless to say, it's totally worth the price, and the cute character design makes the mood feels light despite the heavy background story, and you will find yourself exploring every single location of the map just to have it filled out.
If you're the kind of player that likes 100%'ing games just like me, then you just found the right thing, as it feels very rewarding due to the challenges you'll face— they don't feel impossible or headache inducing, but doable with time, really feeling your advancements as you play.

That's it, I can't say much without giving spoilers, just know that Nyaruru and Lily are the best :)

A continuação mais inesperada que eu poderia imaginar— passou de um jogo de terror para um Metroidvania, e ainda assim é mais do que eu poderia pedr.
Eu não sou fã de Metroidvania nem nada— na verdade, eu não gosto de Metroidvania, incluindo grandes títulos como Hollow Knight e Dead Cells. Este jogo, no entanto, conseguiu ir além, já que aqui estou eu, tendo platinado ele. A interface é ruim e muito simples, mas você se acostuma.
É um jogo com uma história rica e conteúdo extenso, com mais de 15 bosses e um mapa bem grande com vários inimigos e personagens.
Ele é feito de uma forma que você não precisa jogar o jogo anterior, já que os eventos são explicados de forma bem resumida, embora eu realmente recomende jogar se você quiser.

Nem preciso dizer que vale totalmente o preço, e o design fofo dos personagens deixa o clima leve apesar da história profunda, e você vai se ver explorando cada lugar do mapa só pra completar.
Se você é o tipo de jogador que gosta de platinar jogos, assim como eu, então você acabou de encontrar o jogo certo, porque a sensação é muito gratificante por causa dos desafios e lutas— eles não parecem impossíveis ou que causam dor de cabeça, mas sim superáveis ​​com o tempo, e você realmente sente seu progresso conforme joga.

É isso, não posso dizer muito sem dar spoilers, só saiba que Nyaruru e Lily são as melhores :)

For me, Ikaruga is more than just a game, but a work of art. Every bit of progress feels like a victory.

Ikaruga (斑鳩, spotted dove) often comes into mind when I see birds, reminding me of this game I bought a decade ago but never able to finish. Back then, I hadn’t heard the term Souls-like, but Ikaruga should be my first encounter with high difficulty.

Ikaruga stands out with its unique mechanic: instead of choosing an aircraft focused on attack or defense, you control a single aircraft switching between blue and black.

This polarity system is the heart of the game, matching your polarity to the color of enemy bullets you absorb to power up your attacks, while switching to the opposite polarity maximizes damage against enemies. The game is mostly about strategy and reflexes due to numerous bullet-hell moments, often you’re switching polarities not to attack but to survive, you must know extratekt where to position in the chaos.

What makes Ikaruga a game of art is symmetry. Enemies often appear in pairs, following identical attack patterns but with opposing blue and black bullet colors, creating visually stunning and harmonious patterns. When you find the perfect position to survive and strike back, it’s immensely satisfying.

Steam records show I completed the Chapter 1 boss in 2015, and I managed to finish the bosses in chapter 2 and 3, a personal milestone, but no chance in Chapter 4. Every bit of progress feels like a victory in this game.

By today’s standards, Ikaruga remains a unique and timeless gem.

The concept of this game is brilliant - on paper. I'm afraid that I have to hesitate a little bit to call it a game. The potential for a game is here, but the technical hurdles involved in getting this to work, combined with the incredibly short amount of content really makes this more of a proof of concept than a game, per se.

The largest issue, by far and large, is that this game does NOT support Internet play. When hosting or finding a game - it's all done across the Local Area Network. So if you and your co-player of choice aren't on the same network (at home, in a dorm, at work, etc) - you're going to need to setup a VPN service to make this work. Some people have reported success with services like Hamachi - that didn't work for me, but I was able to setup a VPN on my particular brand of router, and get myself and a friend connected.

Once you DO get the game up and running - the entire content of the game can be played in under 30 minutes. For all the trailer talks about "solve puzzles" - there was only one puzzle to be solved. 

A very unique experience, and one worth seeking out - IF you are tech-savvy enough to get past the hurdles. I'd love to see the concepts provided here fleshed out a bit more, and for more of a game to result.

TL; DR: a fun side-scrolling SHMUP/visual novel whose story is surprisingly heavy and with mechanics that will likely satisfy most casual and hardcore audiences, but leave neither blown away with its otherwise standard gameplay.

Pros:
-bright and alluring art style that both pleases and lulls the player into a false sense of calm, allowing the story to hit all the harder when the reveal times come
-voice acting, while sparse, is done well
-once you get into the flow of the combat loop you hit that "fun zone" that games like Doom:  Eternal like to tout
-somehow the story makes the existence of plane waifus make sense
-the plane waifus have some of the strongest writing in the game, as well as character development that fits their backgrounds and what happens during the story

Cons:
-small gripe, but:  you can't rename the protagonist (not exactly a standard VN feature, but would be welcome here)
-numerous grammar & spelling mistakes (at least in English)
-by the end the gameplay gets more repetitive than most SHMUPs simply because it lacks the same level of depth, with some mechanics (especially one particularly fun time-slowing ability) introduced and used only in that one stage
-the writing can forget itself sometimes, i.e. you'll have a conversation with a character and have resolved a situation, only in a scene directly following to be as if that conversation never happened...it only happens a few times, but is frustrating as it yanks you right of the otherwise good immersion; the story also leaves a LOT of questions unanswered, and much of it seems like it will never be explored

Overall, this is quite a good indie effort with fun gameplay, interesting characters, and a good amount of playtime (took me about 10 hours to reach my first ending, and there are eight endings in total).  While it doesn't really do anything special in either the SHMUP or VN genres, it ends up being more than the sum of its parts to create a compelling narrative that drives you to see how far down this plane waifu rabbit hole goes.

Influent is a language learning game where you try to explore an apartment to learn words related to the stuff inside. Most of these are nouns for household objects, but there are some verbs and adjectives included as well. I mostly used it for Russian (I'm upper beginner) but I also tried it in Spanish (I'm upper intermediate).

To play the game, you walk around the apartment to find vocab words. When you click on the objects, you can add the words to your vocabulary list. You can add nouns just by finding them, but you'll need to earn stars to unlock the adjectives and verbs. To earn a star, you can either add 10 words to your list or master one of your words. To master a word, you have to pass all five star challenges, which each give you a different prompt and have you find the object or choose the vocabulary word.

It takes a little while to get the hang of the controls, but once you do the game is pretty easy to play. Some of the words are a bit hard to find, as some of them are inside of cupboards or are parts of a larger object. Long sessions tended to get kind of boring, but I enjoyed short sessions of 10-20 minutes each.

Influent is like a more dynamic version of a flashcard app, and does have some strengths. All of the words have native speaker audio recordings, and if your target language has a different script than your native language, you can toggle between the actual script or a transliteration. The words taught correspond to normal household items, but aren't limited to the most common ones. As an upper intermediate learner, some of the words were not yet familiar to me, but they are objects I see every day. There are a lot of different languages available, including some languages that are less common languages to learn.

The game doesn't let you reorganize your word list, so once you add a word it stays where it is. If you want to review specific words on your list, you have to pick the page they're on, and you can't move words around to drill them in a more customizable way. The adjectives and verbs are each tied to a specific object. You can't just pick any green object, you have to choose the object where the game gave you the word, and some of those were harder to remember than others. 

Inlfluent is a niche game with a pretty narrow purpose. If you are no longer a total beginner in your target language, but most of the words on the word list are still pretty new to you, I think Influent is an engaging way to learn them. If you're getting into the intermediate stages, it's too limited to be useful, and you'd probably have more fun learning/practicing any words you don't know in a different way. It's also good for getting a taste of a lot of different languages, and you get the best value if you sample a few of them. 6/10

As others may have already said this is more or less a flashcard-like program, and honestly you will get as much out of this game as you put into it. You can continually amp up the difficulty as you go, especially with Japanese as you can progress from Hiragana to Katakana then to Kanji (good for beginners to intermediate learners). What I don't think people appreciate enough is connecting words to visuals (rather than your native language), and associating verbs with objects (both of which this game does).

If you're serious about a language and are still learning, I would honestly suggest this game as a fun supplemental word collector. This is an underrated and underappreciated language aid. Cheers to Rob Howland for an awesome game!

Freddi Fish 3: The Case of the Stolen Conch Shell, developed by Humongous Entertainment and re-released by Nightdive Studios, stands as one of the most polished and beloved entries in the classic point-and-click adventure series. Like the other titles in the franchise, it immerses players in an underwater mystery filled with colorful characters, clever puzzles, and a generous dose of charm. The story begins with Freddi and her loyal sidekick Luther arriving for the Founders’ Day Festival, only to discover that the Grand Conch Shell—an important artifact used to open the celebration—has been stolen. When Luther’s Uncle Blenny is falsely accused of the crime, Freddi and Luther take it upon themselves to uncover the truth, setting the stage for a whimsical detective adventure that perfectly balances humor, logic, and child-friendly storytelling.

What makes Freddi Fish 3 special is how it handles its mystery through playful interactivity rather than exposition. The player is given freedom to explore an expansive undersea world made up of dozens of interconnected areas, each packed with secrets and surprises. Every screen is brimming with detail, from background animations and hidden jokes to clickable objects that react with delightful sound effects or quirky mini-gags. This interactivity helps bring the underwater setting to life and keeps younger players engaged as they explore. The game’s art direction, hand-painted backgrounds, and expressive character animation remain vibrant even decades later, evoking a timeless cartoon aesthetic that has aged gracefully. The underwater world feels cozy yet adventurous, filled with personality in every corner.

The gameplay follows Humongous Entertainment’s traditional point-and-click formula but refines it into one of the series’ most cohesive designs. Players collect and use items, solve puzzles, and talk to various fishy inhabitants to uncover clues about the stolen conch shell. The puzzles are cleverly designed to encourage logical thinking without becoming frustrating, ensuring accessibility for younger audiences while still being satisfying for older players revisiting the game out of nostalgia. One of the standout features is the randomization system—each new playthrough can feature a different culprit and varied item placements, which gives the game a surprising amount of replay value. This simple but effective mechanic keeps the adventure fresh and encourages players to replay it multiple times, something uncommon in children’s adventure games from the 1990s.

Freddi Fish 3 also benefits from exceptional writing and voice acting. The characters are distinct and memorable, each with their own quirky personality and mannerisms. Freddi’s calm intelligence contrasts nicely with Luther’s endearing clumsiness, creating a dynamic duo that feels authentic and engaging. The dialogue is lighthearted, often humorous, and sprinkled with small lessons about friendship, responsibility, and curiosity. While clearly written with children in mind, the humor and pacing have enough universal appeal to entertain older players as well. The voice performances, particularly by Donna Williams as Freddi and Mike McAuliffe as Luther, give the characters warmth and personality that elevate the story far beyond simple text-based narration.

From a technical standpoint, the remastered release by Nightdive Studios ensures that the game runs smoothly on modern systems while preserving its original charm. The interface is clean and intuitive, using clear icons and responsive cursor feedback to guide players naturally through interactions. The music deserves equal praise—its light, jazzy tunes and atmospheric sound effects create a soothing, immersive experience that complements the gentle pace of exploration. Every click, bubble, and splash feels deliberate and satisfying, further drawing players into the undersea mystery.

Although it is a children’s game, Freddi Fish 3 possesses an impressive level of craftsmanship and design maturity. Its puzzles never condescend to players, its writing never feels forced, and its pacing ensures that curiosity is always rewarded. The sense of progression is subtle yet rewarding, with each solved puzzle and new clue bringing Freddi closer to the truth. The conclusion—where the real thief is revealed—offers a satisfying resolution while reinforcing the game’s themes of fairness, friendship, and perseverance. Even after completion, players can return for another playthrough to experience alternate scenarios or simply enjoy the world’s cozy charm.

If there’s one limitation to mention, it’s that the game’s simplicity and short length might leave some modern players wishing for more. Experienced adventure game fans will likely breeze through it in a couple of hours, and the puzzles, while charming, are designed with accessibility in mind rather than complexity. Yet these qualities are part of its appeal—Freddi Fish 3 was crafted as an introduction to adventure games, and in that regard, it remains one of the most effective examples ever made. Its ability to encourage critical thinking, exploration, and observation in a non-threatening environment makes it a standout in children’s entertainment.

In the end, Freddi Fish 3: The Case of the Stolen Conch Shell is a delightful underwater adventure that embodies the best qualities of Humongous Entertainment’s golden era. It combines clever design, memorable characters, and enduring charm to create a game that continues to entertain both children and nostalgic adults decades after its release. Its blend of humor, gentle mystery-solving, and interactive storytelling remains unmatched in its genre, and the remastered version ensures that a new generation of players can experience it as vividly as ever. It’s not just a nostalgic trip—it’s a timeless reminder of how creativity, simplicity, and warmth can turn a small adventure into a classic that never loses its shine.

测评一下
1、技能。作为类银河恶魔城游戏，技能是非常成熟的。本作其实也不例外，而且有一定的创新，就是将技能分别划分在不同的地方：二段跳（植入体）冲刺（植入体）；弹射（拳套）螳螂爪（拳套）；上撩（剑）下劈（剑）；钩锁（锤子）下砸（锤子）
这个设计初看还有点新颖，但是玩多了发现其实只是换汤不换药而已。而且在使用组合技能时，还因为分布在不同的武器中，增加了玩家的操作难度（切武器）。
因此综合来看，整体有点创新但不多，且没必要难为玩家。-1分

2、武器技能树。我认为这是本作的最大优点。三种武器其实都有自己的特点，而且技能树有所取舍，使得玩家有了自己的战斗风格。技能树的深度也不错。+1分

3、地图。地图设计中规中矩。如果非要挑个毛病，就是存档机制不支持sl，这和主流的类银游戏是有区别的。

4、任务系统。给我的感觉是庞杂凌乱。支线剧情交织在一起，再加上人物众多，使得任务不够明确。而且有些剧情是要给剧情锁的。分别举正反两个例子，例如沼泽蛤蟆格伦德尔，因为毒沼拦路（剧情锁），所以必须跟着剧情才能打到这个boss。相反找部族帮忙的几个任务，帮助部族消灭的boss，就完全可以先杀boss，后面再接相关的任务。导致给玩家的感觉，就是两件不相关的事。有些跑图任务找npc一次就差不多了，没必要来回来去跑。点名蟹人和复仇寡妇。-1分

5、锁。上面提到的剧情锁不再赘述。这里是想说的探图的地图锁。其实这个设计非常考验开发者的水平。优秀的开发者一般使用技能锁和剧情锁，相反则是简单粗暴的门锁（单纯的放一个门，任务完成自己开门）。我认为本游戏有些简单粗暴，我甚至不知道这个门锁是因为哪个任务打开的。-1分

6、战斗数值
首先想说的是贪婪这个植入体，是不是忘了设置加成上限。当然了，多亏了这个植入体我才能顺利通关，推荐大家使用。但是仅从战斗数值上讲，是不是有问题。其次是困难难度与普通难度，小怪和boss的伤害数值。困难难度就是单纯的将伤害增加了接近10倍，纯数值碾压。而后期小怪打人不掉血，boss打人又扛不住。这样的战斗数值，那么请问技能树里加血减伤的技能到底有没有用？不加小怪也打不死我，加了也扛不住boss打3下。因此我认为是战斗数值设置有问题。-0.5分

7、剧情 
整个剧情非常简单，没什么出彩也没有逻辑问题。支线也有丰满剧情的作用。甚至还根据不同选择有多结局。虽然多结局也没特别惊艳吧。

总结：以上7点，最后得分是7.5/10。良作，推荐喜欢类银的玩家入手游玩，价格方面可以等一个小折扣或者全价入都可以。

I discovered Carter’s Quest through Twitter and was immediately intrigued by its queer Zelda vibes. I'm not a fan of Zelda titles post-Twilight Princess, but this game still felt like it was made for someone like me. Having played through the current build, I can confidently say I love it. That said, this review will be highly critical; not because I disliked the game, but because I genuinely want to see it reach its full potential once it leaves Early Access. It’s easier to articulate what needs improvement than what already shines, so please know: I think this game is a diamond in the rough. Spoilers ahead.

[Combat]
- The combat system is the most enjoyable part of the game. Floaty combos, varied attacks, and a decent weapon selection make for engaging encounters.
- Unfortunately, the four magic spells you unlock feel underwhelming. Only the lightning spell stood out; largely because it’s overpowered. I couldn't get the wind spell to function as shown in the update trailer.
- None of the pause-based combos ever worked for me, despite repeated attempts. It felt like I was missing out on a significant portion of Carter’s arsenal.
- Locking on to enemies would feel more intuitive if mapped to the right trigger instead of the bumper. Since the bow is mostly used for puzzles, swapping these controls could improve comfort and flow.

[Boss Design and Mechanics]
- The flying-rock segment of the Malformed Homunculus: Urgum boss fight felt clunky. It’s almost a shoot-’em-up, but the delayed attack strings break the rhythm. A hold-to-fire mechanic would suit it better.
- The King Lanky boss and its later reskins were awkward. The perspective and some cheap moves made the fight feel unrefined, though I did improve with each iteration, which felt rewarding.

[Character Design and Naming]
- Some character names are jarring. "Carter" feels generic, evoking the vibe of someone renaming Link to Kevin. "Kelly Ai" unintentionally evokes AI discourse, which is distracting. "Games Goblin" could easily be "Gambling Goblin," a missed opportunity for stronger alliteration.
- Several characters are referred to by generic titles rather than names, which breaks immersion.
- Villagers all share the same dialogue string.
- The blacksmith mentions a child who never appears.
- The clothing shopkeeper criticizes Carter’s outfit while she strongly resembles his second look.
- The wizard outfit is uninspired and overpriced at 25 currency. Why would I replace Carter's new look with something so plain? Worse, it clips through Carter’s backside.
- There’s a noticeable lack of body diversity. Most characters share the same height and build, and a lot of the characters look too similar face-wise. While the art style is cohesive, it restrains needed individuality.

[Narrative and Character Presence]
- Goba’s disappearance after the first area felt abrupt. He seemed poised to be a recurring character.
- Helga and her counterparts currently feel narratively disconnected. It might make more sense for Goba to guide the player instead. Their designs also feel less polished compared to other characters.
- Kelly’s absence during her fight with Ryval greatly strains believability. Her village collapses while she delays confronting a weak opponent, which undermines her entire character arc.
- In Carter’s memory cutscene, he wears his current outfit instead of his original cargo shorts. This breaks continuity.
- Carter’s father and presumed brother could benefit from stronger visual designs. It's the main character's family, but they look overtly generic.

[Bugs and Technical Issues]
- A recurring bug causes Carter to turn in the opposite direction when entering void-style doorways. I think it's when flipping into them.
- The physics in rat-folk fortresses, those above the pit or near the ocean, are glitchy and need refinement.
- The broomstick clips through Carter’s legs at certain angles and looks overly plain. A more stylish upgrade later on would be welcome.
- Carter’s flip is the main travel mechanic before acquiring the broom. It could be enhanced; think Lara Croft’s acrobatics as a traversal mode.
- Carter could benefit from action-based vocalizations, similar to Link’s grunts. Real-life mutes still make sounds, and this could add personality.

[Customization and Visuals]
- Yooba’s customization menu is buggy. Face options bleed into wing options, and the bottom palette can become cut off.
- It would be great to apply those unlocked colors to Carter’s outfits.
- Carter’s hairstyle should be customizable independently of his costume. His loose hairstyle sometimes disappears, giving the impression of a shaved head in certain terrain.
- Earlier builds featured a pixelated, posterized graphic style that worked well. Unless the current level of rendering and details are upgraded, that older style would be preferable.
- Environmental detail is lacking. Dungeons and fields often feel empty. If the game world remains sparse, consider scaling back the size to maintain cohesion.

[Items and Upgrades]
- The weapon designs are unremarkable.
- The heart-piece equivalents feel too derivative. Comparatively, magic upgrades represented by hourglasses are a nice touch. More creative choices like this would elevate the game.

[Final Thoughts]
Carter’s Quest is brimming with charm and potential. Its combat, queer aesthetic, and Zelda-inspired structure make it a standout indie title. But to truly shine, it needs polish across systems, narrative cohesion, and visual diversity. I’m rooting for this game and hope my feedback helps it evolve into the masterpiece it’s clearly striving to be.

Currently, i'm in a very difficult spot for how I feel about the game. I think it nails the atmosphere tremendously well and feels like it could easily challenge phas for the horror game in my friend group. I think the ability to tweak how your investigator to be better with certain items and be worse in other regards is really cool. Being able to have the truck friend feel as effective as everyone else if they get scared easily is great. The relics you receive give minor buffs to using certain items. I've received one that increases the aoe of UV and a second for aoe of flashlight. 

Yet in this comparison, we must also look at the gameplay loops of the two games. I will preface this that I haven't been able to do any of the roguelite mechanics in this.
Both games focus on gathering evidence to figure out the ghost. The primary difference is that in NOX you also banish the ghost. In concept, this is easy and even with the 'punishments' for getting it wrong, its still process of elimination. 
The problem lies in evidence. In phas, you can remove evidence as you find or fail to find certain types. I am also aware that the spirit box is bugged right now so i'll put that to the side for now. The other evidence types are difficult to confirm. Motion camera feels iffy at best, emf being a perfect item in phas feels flawed here, ultraviolet is useful but hard to know where to check, recording feels the most consistent but i either have not received any confirmed ones or i'm incorrect in my guess, ghost writing also feels consistent but i will explain why that is concerning in a moment. 
I'm sure I missed one but the other thing phas does is that there is a room for the ghost to sit in. I think that's true here as well but i think its only visible when the ghost hunts.

speaking of hunts.... The ghost hunts in this game as well, starting with a loud musical sting. Well, let me rephrase from my experience. The ghost enters a seeking phase, looking for the player, upon seeing a player a musical sting activates then the hunt begins proper. The ghost then advances towards the player. If the player has a crucifix out, they burn over the course of around 5-10 seconds then (presumably) return to their starting location. Note: the ghost can still grab you if its not fully burned. After a few moments, couldn't get a time, the ghost returns to a dormant state. The hunt amounts increase as sanity burns. Simple, no? Well, lets look at a certain thing I said. It seeks, then when it sees you, the musical sting happens. So far, I have lost a life 3 times to turning a corner into the ghost and couldn't whip out that crucifix fast enough. You can burn your personal relic to prevent dying to the ghost but you only get those once a day or by finding the coins. 

Ah yes, coins. These give you bonus lives but there's 2 problems with them. You can find them naturally or by picking up the tabby on each map then placing it. The cat should point towards where the coins are but from my experience, much like a normal cat, it stares off in a direction. You also only receive these coins if you succeed at banishing the ghost. If you leave early, you don't receive them. Nothing wrong with that but the difficulty of the game means that its easier to learn what you can and leave. It still randomizes the area, reduces the free gear you get and reduces the money you receive. Makes sense for a roguelike. 

In addition to all of this, I'd like to talk about the dowsing stick. This is a small plumbob on a string that glows and (I think?) points in the area of cursed objects. Now, wendigo does say it can't make cursed objects. The problem for this is that the dowsing stick. Has. Physics. I can move 2 cm and it spins faster than an industry grade fan and that is with low bobbing on the character. Simple fix would be removing its physic and have it spin while its trying to find the cursed object before locking into a direction. I'm not a game programmer so I could just be mean on that for barely any reasons. 

Finally, lets talk about the sanity system. This is something I cross referenced with my friend who i'm going to duo in this with (and I currently duo with her in phas). There were times where both of us chill in the house for upwards of 5 minutes with minimal drain. Then we see or barely hear an event and drop to 60. There's also fuse boxes. Supposedly. Both of us played a total of 6 maps? and she only found it on a hotel type map. The beginner maps to learn how to play are old houses that seemingly don't have fuse boxes which means you can never turn on lights. Which means you have a constant sanity drain you can't deal with. Frustrating to say the least. 

Now, that's a lot of negatives and even to me, its a bit disheartening. I do see a lot of promise however. Things just need to be tweaked to be more consistent. Less physics on certain items, easier ways to tell if an item worked or not, guaranteed closets and fuse boxes on every map (like 1, please), maybe a practice house for ghost hunting proper with 5-7 rooms and helps you learn how to properly use the items in the field. I think this is legitmately one of the biggest contenders to fight against phas but more groundwork needs to be put in. As we get updates, I will be streaming it but at this moment, I cannot say that anyone should buy it. You should try it! If I could give a mixed review I would. Please don't consider this to be a hate message or a contrarian review. I would love to love this game but its hard

게임 자체의 난이도가 높지는 않은데, 짜증나게 하는 요소들이 종종 있음. 미이라 치와와가 진짜 저혈압치료제임. 달려들어서 몸에 붙어 체력 야금야금 갉아먹는데 떼어내도 타겟팅 이런게 없다보니 휘둘렀는데 헛칼질하면 다시 몸으로 달라들어 피가 한 줄씩 날라갈때도 있었음. 그리고 공략 없이 하면 사실상 도전과제 100% 불가능한 구조. 투탕카멘으로 전환하고 싶어도 할 수 있는 방법이 없어서 오닉스 코인 놓쳤으면 다시 해야함.

No Delivery, developed and published by oates, is an atmospheric indie horror RPG that transforms the familiar setting of a pizzeria into a surreal, unnerving descent into madness. Beneath its unassuming retro exterior lies a game that fuses psychological horror, roguelike mechanics, and cryptic storytelling into a singular, haunting experience. At first glance, it resembles a lighthearted job simulator, tasking you with working shifts at a struggling pizza restaurant. However, as you delve deeper into the nightmarish corridors and decaying side rooms of this establishment, it becomes clear that the job is far from ordinary. No Delivery uses nostalgia and simplicity as a disguise, concealing a deeply disquieting narrative about exploitation, decay, and the horrors that lurk behind a smiling mascot.

From the moment the game begins, the atmosphere is heavy with unease. The pixel art and VHS-style visual filters evoke the look of an old, damaged recording, as though you’re watching a game that shouldn’t exist. The visuals flicker, distort, and occasionally blur in ways that make the world feel unstable. The pizzeria itself is both familiar and alien—an empty dining hall, a broken arcade, a flickering kitchen—all rendered in a style that recalls retro RPGs but tainted by grime and static. There is something inherently wrong about everything you see, yet the game rarely resorts to outright jump scares. Instead, it cultivates dread through absence, through the quiet moments between actions where the player feels most exposed. The sound design amplifies this tension with distant hums, looping background noises, and unsettling silences that stretch longer than they should. When the music does emerge, it often feels dissonant or warped, enhancing the dreamlike quality of the experience.

The core gameplay combines elements of traditional turn-based RPG combat with roguelike progression. You play as an employee navigating shifts and “Wrong Turns,” which function as procedurally generated dungeons. Each shift presents a new layout filled with hazards, strange NPCs, and cryptic objects that hint at the pizzeria’s sinister secrets. Combat encounters play out through a familiar turn-based system, but resources are limited, and every action feels consequential. Characters can die permanently, and losing one means hiring a replacement to continue the job. This mechanic reinforces the game’s themes of disposability and corporate dehumanization, as employees are treated as interchangeable assets rather than individuals. The system creates a subtle form of tension that goes beyond traditional horror—every decision carries weight, not because of fear of a monster, but because of the cost of survival in a system designed to consume its workers.

Exploration in No Delivery is equally compelling and unnerving. The pizzeria serves as both a hub and a labyrinth, filled with locked rooms, strange machines, and hidden areas that only reveal themselves after multiple playthroughs. The “Wrong Turns” serve as excursions into nightmarish distortions of familiar places, where enemies and scenery morph into grotesque versions of normal life. These sequences are not only the game’s combat arenas but also narrative devices, representing the deeper psychological rot beneath the pizzeria’s cheerful surface. Each new area feels like peeling back another layer of a corrupted memory. The writing leans heavily on implication rather than exposition, leaving players to piece together the fragmented story through item descriptions, environmental clues, and strange encounters. This lack of explicit direction can feel disorienting, but it also invites curiosity and engagement. The more you explore, the more you sense that the horror isn’t just about what’s happening inside the restaurant—it’s about what the place represents.

The game’s retro aesthetic works to its advantage, bridging nostalgia with discomfort. The low-resolution sprites and dim lighting create a claustrophobic sense of place, while the VHS overlay adds an uncanny authenticity, as if the game itself were an artifact from a forgotten era. Every detail, from the flickering neon signs to the looping animations of mechanical mascots, contributes to the sense of unease. There’s a deliberate contrast between the cheerful, colorful branding of the pizzeria and the decaying reality of its interiors. It’s a visual metaphor for the way the game presents its horror—not through overt violence, but through the rot that festers beneath a smiling façade. The attention to aesthetic detail is remarkable, and it captures a kind of analog dread rarely seen in modern horror games.

Mechanically, No Delivery rewards patience and experimentation. Because much of the game’s content is hidden behind procedural generation and player choice, no two playthroughs feel exactly the same. There are multiple endings, secret areas, and subtle variations that only reveal themselves through repeated exploration. Some runs might feel manageable and even optimistic, while others descend into complete chaos, with new enemies and corrupted spaces replacing familiar ones. This replayability gives the game a sense of mystery that persists long after completion. At times, however, this design can feel opaque or even frustrating. The lack of clear guidance, combined with the game’s intentionally cryptic systems, can make it difficult to discern how to progress. Yet this ambiguity feels purposeful—it mirrors the confusion of the protagonist and reinforces the feeling of being trapped in an environment that refuses to make sense.

Thematically, No Delivery goes beyond surface-level horror to explore the dehumanizing effects of modern labor and consumer culture. The endless cycles of work, replacement, and failure reflect a grim satire of corporate life. The pizzeria becomes a microcosm of a system where human effort and identity are consumed in the pursuit of meaningless productivity. Even as you succeed, the game constantly reminds you that your victories are temporary and your survival inconsequential. This undercurrent of existential dread gives the game a philosophical weight that elevates it above standard horror fare. It’s not just about monsters or jump scares—it’s about the quiet horror of being trapped in an unending loop of expectation, failure, and erasure.

No Delivery is a haunting and unconventional experience that challenges the boundaries of what an RPG can be. Its blend of psychological horror, surreal world-building, and roguelike mechanics creates an atmosphere that is both deeply unsettling and strangely compelling. It’s a game that doesn’t explain itself easily, demanding players engage with its mysteries on their own terms. Though it may frustrate with its opacity and rough edges, these imperfections contribute to its authenticity and charm. For those willing to embrace its strangeness, No Delivery offers a truly original exploration of fear—not the fear of the unknown, but the fear of familiarity twisted into something grotesque and unrecognizable. It’s a modern cult classic in the making, a surreal nightmare that lingers long after the credits roll.

The Afterglow of Grisaia is a kinetic visual novel set within the broader Grisaia universe, focusing on a self-contained story that emphasizes character interaction and emotional tone rather than player choice. Unlike the mainline entries, it does not feature branching routes or decision-driven progression, instead presenting a linear narrative designed to enrich the setting and provide additional perspective on familiar characters.

The writing centers on personal dynamics, introspection, and quieter moments that fill in the space between larger events in the series. Its pacing is steady, prioritizing atmosphere and character presence over dramatic plot shifts. This approach makes the experience accessible to returning players who want more context and emotional depth, while being less suited for those seeking heavy conflict or complex narrative branching.

Presentation follows the series’ established style. Character sprites, background art, and interface elements are polished and consistent, relying on clean illustrations and expressive poses. Visual effects are modest but effective in emphasizing tone during key scenes. The artwork maintains the aesthetic identity of the franchise without pushing toward significant stylistic changes.

Audio design supports the atmosphere with a restrained soundtrack built around soft tracks and ambient pieces. Voice acting is a notable component, adding nuance to character interactions and reinforcing emotional beats. The overall soundscape remains low-key, matching the narrative’s reflective focus.

Because the story is linear and relatively short, replay value is limited. The experience is designed as an expansion piece within the Grisaia world rather than a standalone, choice-driven visual novel. Its strength lies in additional characterization rather than structural depth.

The interface is streamlined and easy to navigate, with standard visual novel features such as text logs, skip options, and adjustable settings. Performance remains stable, and the game requires minimal system resources.

Overall, The Afterglow of Grisaia offers a concise, character-focused narrative intended for players already familiar with the series. It provides a polished, atmospheric side story that complements the main titles, aiming more at emotional continuity than at expansive storytelling or interactive complexity.

You waste so much time trying to interact with every single element on the screen, pressing random buttons, because the game offers no visual feedback or hint about which objects are actually usable and which are not. This constant “push and pull” completely breaks immersion.

Actions feel shallow, and the abilities you gain amount to little more than simple “switches” with no real sense of progression, making the experience flat. The control system is imprecise, and the engine suffers from heavy aliasing even at maximum settings, apart from the design, it’s technically quite poor.
The atmosphere is the only redeeming quality; visually it’s a good game and probably even tells a good story, but the gameplay is so frustrating that it’s hard to see it through to the end.
