This might be the worst Duck Life yet. 

For starters, its runtime (3-4 hours) is SUPER padded. A significant portion of that runtime is just watching your duck slapfight the other duck until one of them dies of old age. The number of minigames is somewhat higher than previous entries, which the game thankfully accounts for by having them be comically bad. I genuinely cannot stress enough how poor the quality of the minigames are, and the few passable ones are direct rips from other, better games (Swords and Souls absolutely blows this game out of the water).

It is baffling that this is the 7th Duck Life game, and yet the same sloppy bugs keep coming back year after year. I played a good 15% of this game with no music, simply because it just decided to cut out for minutes at a time. Thankfully I was not missing much.

The combat mechanics are also weirdly cryptic for how simple they are. You'll get a weapon that says "30 lightning" and be left more or less in the dark as to what that might mean. There is a rock-paper-scissors type matchup system (that also has no chart or the like to reference, so it relies on trial and error), but in reality there is little point in engaging with said system. The reason for this is that tournaments are against three consecutive opponents, and so the time and effort spent grinding for gear that matches up well against every opponent would be much better served just levelling up to the cap immediately.

Herein lies the biggest issue of this game. There is so little margin for error against the tournament opponents that your two best options are 1. Level up to the cap, or 2. Specifically set up a build to counter certain ducks, and then grind the gear and money to do so. The latter option is unintuitive, painstaking, and longer, and so the result is that most of the game's mechanics only serve to get in the way. The sidequest items, for example, are so quickly obsoleted that they are a waste of time to even bother collecting, let alone spend coins to level them up.

I do want to mention that there are a couple of funny moments in the game. The first is that one of the first enemies you fight suggests that he's going to hang himself if you don't take his rope item, and the second is learning that the city area is a No-Fly-Zone, which has all sorts of weird implications.

Anyways, this game is not worth your time or money. I will continue to review every duck life game though because it is my ordained mission.

BloodRayne — малоизвестный алмаз своего времени, а ныне попросту невозможный для воссоздания продукт: кровавый, мясной, дикий. Рыжая стерва Рейн с язвительными шутками прорубает себе путь через солдат рейха, зомби-деревенщин, древних демонов, вампиров и даже божеств.

За собой она оставляет потоки крови, омывающие полы и стены. Враги, однажды услышав её ужасную симфонию резни и предсмертные вопли, спешат спрятаться кто куда.

[hr][/hr]

[b] Тёте Рейн на момент первой части — около 60–70 лет. [/b] Она не злодей, но и не герой. Балансирует на острой грани, оставаясь антагонистом и служа Ликвидатором у тайного общества Бримстоуна.

[b] Как говорит сама Рейн [/b]: “[i] Я не прочь разрубить вас на части и выпить всю кровь, но так я поступаю только с плохими людьми”. [/i]

Она не вампир в классическом смысле, а полукровка (Дампир): жажда её не одолевает, но кровь исцеляет и приносит удовольствие. Бой также доставляет Рейн весомую часть кайфа, особенно если удаётся лишить врага конечности, сопровождая потуги того остановить хлещущую кровь остроумной насмешкой: “[i] О-о бедняжечка! Кажется, ты что-то потерял? [/i]”

[hr][/hr]

Мир BloodRayne — альтернативная история с ретро-футуризмом. Так что не удивляйтесь повстречать тут: киборгов-нацистов, древних существ и даже примитивных роботов. 

[h2] Рейн вот не удивляется вовсе. [/h2]

Своими корнями, игра уходит к Nocturne, где уже были Дампиры. Но BloodRayne — отдельная история, да и права на неё теперь не у оригинальных создателей. А сами создатели, давным-давно уже не у дел… 

[hr][/hr]

[h3] Даже в 2025 году, несмотря на свой почтенный возраст, BloodRayne остаётся стильным и действительно кровавым экшеном. [/h3]

Да BloodRayne кому-то может показаться устаревшей, но важно помнить следующее: то была эпоха, когда геймдизайн только становился на ноги. А потому, попробуйте полюбить BloodRayne такой, какая она есть.

BloodSaint, developed and published by Walter Machado, is an unapologetically old-school action shooter that delivers a concentrated dose of high-speed combat and pixelated carnage. Built as a spiritual continuation of Machado’s long-running Ubermosh universe, the game takes place thousands of years after that series, preserving its core philosophy of minimalist design and pure mechanical intensity. Rather than expanding into modern complexity, BloodSaint condenses its ideas into a tightly wound experience that demands precision, reflex, and rhythm from the player. It is a game that celebrates mastery over excess, the kind of project that feels handcrafted for players who crave challenge over accessibility.

From its very first moments, BloodSaint makes its intentions clear. The presentation is bold, pulsing with the energy of classic arcade shooters while filtered through a contemporary indie sensibility. The pixel art style is dense and stylized, combining dark neon palettes with streaks of crimson and glowing white effects that create an atmosphere of raw aggression. The screen constantly pulses with motion—bullets, enemies, and explosions painting a chaotic tapestry that’s as visually stimulating as it is disorienting. The soundtrack, dominated by heavy rock and industrial beats, amplifies that adrenaline. Every encounter is underscored by rhythmic percussion and electrified riffs, reinforcing the sensation of controlled chaos. It’s the kind of game that pulls you into its tempo and refuses to let go until you’re either victorious or dead.

Gameplay in BloodSaint adheres to the tight, uncompromising philosophy of arcade design. It uses a top-down perspective, and your goal is simple: survive waves of relentless enemies while cutting through them with speed and precision. There’s no exposition, no tutorial, and no wasted motion. Every element serves a singular purpose—to push the player toward that satisfying state of flow where instinct takes over. The controls are snappy and immediate, emphasizing reflexive movement and rapid targeting. The combat design encourages both aggression and caution; while the player feels empowered, one mistake can mean instant failure. As with many of Machado’s previous works, learning enemy patterns and balancing offensive bursts with defensive movement becomes the key to endurance. Each session plays out like a self-contained test of skill, and with every death, the game subtly teaches adaptation and timing.

What sets BloodSaint apart from other indie action games is its complete rejection of modern padding. There are no elaborate upgrade trees, cinematic cutscenes, or open-ended exploration. Instead, it’s pure distilled gameplay, built around repetition and improvement. Every run feels like a short, brutal lesson in precision. This minimalist approach is both its strength and its limitation. On one hand, it allows the core mechanics to shine without distraction; on the other, it can make the experience feel narrow, particularly for players accustomed to broader progression systems. The game’s structure—short runs, escalating challenge, and little room for error—means that its replayability depends entirely on one’s enjoyment of the core loop. For those who thrive on mechanical mastery, it’s endlessly addictive. For those who prefer variety and exploration, it may feel thin after a few sessions.

The difficulty curve in BloodSaint is steep but fair. Early runs are punishing, demanding quick learning and steady composure. Enemies are fast, aggressive, and merciless, and their attack patterns force the player to constantly adjust positioning and prioritize threats. However, as familiarity sets in, what once felt overwhelming transforms into a kind of hypnotic rhythm. Dodging, shooting, and chaining kills begin to flow together seamlessly, creating moments of clarity amid chaos. The game rewards that perseverance not with cinematic rewards or stat boosts, but with the visceral satisfaction of survival. It’s a purist approach to challenge—one that harks back to the arcade era where skill alone determined success.

In terms of atmosphere, BloodSaint carries a strange sense of reverence beneath its violence. Though minimal in narrative, it hints at a larger mythology connected to the Ubermosh universe, set ten millennia after its predecessor. The world feels post-human, populated by the remnants of a civilization long past redemption. The title itself—“BloodSaint”—suggests the fusion of brutality and devotion, a warrior’s spiritual ascension through combat. This subtle lore adds an intriguing texture to the experience without ever intruding on the gameplay. The sense of continuity between Machado’s works gives the game a mythic weight, as if each new release represents another fragment of a larger cosmic saga rendered in neon and gunfire.

While BloodSaint succeeds in delivering an intense and satisfying arcade experience, it isn’t without its shortcomings. The minimalist design that fuels its immediacy can also limit its longevity. The environments, though visually striking, can feel repetitive, and the enemy types, while distinct in behavior, lack variety over extended play. The short average playtime reflects this—most players will extract the bulk of the experience within a few hours. However, this brevity is not necessarily a flaw in the traditional sense; it aligns with the game’s design philosophy of pure, condensed action. Rather than stretching itself thin with filler content, BloodSaint offers a compact, replayable challenge loop that remains focused on intensity over duration.

Ultimately, BloodSaint is a love letter to arcade purity—fast, punishing, and exhilarating. It refuses to compromise its identity for accessibility or spectacle, delivering an experience that values precision and control above all else. Every pixel, sound, and frame of motion contributes to a singular goal: immersion through action. It’s not a game that caters to everyone, but for those who appreciate the art of mechanical mastery, it’s a rare gem. Walter Machado once again demonstrates his commitment to creating small, self-contained worlds of challenge and style. BloodSaint stands proudly among them as a testament to the enduring appeal of stripped-down design and the timeless thrill of a perfectly executed run.

As a fan of monster girls, I have to say—I approve of this game. However, it still has a few flaws worth mentioning.

First off, this isn’t a hentai game. It does have some sexual content and innuendo, but it’s pretty tame overall, so don’t expect anything explicit.

You play as Mia, a human warrior who’s deeply in love with her husband, Fernando. One day, Fernando is captured by monster girls, and Mia sets out to rescue him. To save her beloved, she has to travel across different kingdoms and defeat each monster girl boss holding him hostage. It’s your classic “save the princess (or prince)” kind of story—simple, but it gets the job done.

The pixel art is absolutely gorgeous and full of charm, reminding me of the good old days of retro gaming. The monster girls themselves are cute, sexy, and full of personality. You’ll meet all kinds of them—a dwarf, elf, orc, oni, fairy, salamander, unicorn, slime, and more. Each one is beautifully designed, and you can view their details in the gallery. You can even “punish” them if that’s your thing—no judgment here.

The music is decent, in my opinion. Not breathtaking, but not bad either. It’s catchy enough to stick with you for a while. I personally like the shop’s theme.

The gameplay is your standard platformer: you can jump and attack at first, and later unlock new abilities like blocking, dashing, and shooting arrows. The controls can feel a bit stiff, especially if you’re using a keyboard. The keybind options are also limited—you can’t even bind dash to the Shift key, which is a bit of a bummer. I’d recommend using a controller if possible, since it feels better suited for the game.

Each level can take around half an hour to an hour to complete, depending on how thorough you are with collecting everything and dealing with traps or challenges. A lot of players say it’s hard, and while it can be tricky at times, I think it’s fair overall—even when playing on keyboard. Some achievements, like Ymir’s challenges, can take a while to finish, though.

Overall, it’s a short but enjoyable experience. The beautiful pixel art, charming monster girls, and solid gameplay make it worth checking out, even if it’s a bit rough around the edges. Expect about five to ten hours (or more) of playtime if you’re aiming for full completion.

Technicity approaches the city-building genre from an unconventional angle, placing the player directly inside a vast open world instead of observing it from above. The experience begins not with spreadsheets or zoning tools, but with the tactile act of shaping land, driving construction vehicles, and assembling buildings piece by piece. Osaris Games builds the foundation around creative freedom: you are encouraged to sculpt terrain, design your own modular construction blocks, craft custom furniture, and assemble entire structures from scratch. The world itself is huge, filled with empty spaces and rough-cut landscapes that invite experimentation. Rather than limiting the player with early-game restrictions or a traditional resource system, the game hands you powerful tools from the start and says: build the city you imagine.

The highlight of Technicity is the act of building itself. Designing original structures becomes surprisingly absorbing thanks to the flexible block-creation system, which lets players sculpt detailed architectural elements and share them through the Steam Workshop. Factory setups further expand the creative loop, allowing players to mass-produce custom pieces and use them across multiple projects. Driving vehicles, laying roads, and physically traveling between distant build sites adds a sense of scale that few other city-builders attempt. This first-person perspective and hands-on approach make the process feel more personal, as though you are an architect and engineer working inside the space rather than a distant overseer. For players who love constructing large-scale projects, this sandbox-centered design can become deeply satisfying.

Yet the game’s ambitions often exceed the maturity of its underlying systems. While it offers the appearance of a city-builder—fire stations, hospitals, police buildings, and other civic structures—their functions are minimal or nonexistent. Many of the buildings operate more as decorative set dressing than meaningful components of a simulation. There is no crime system for police stations to influence, no health mechanics for hospitals to improve, and no complex simulation driving the behaviour of NPC populations. This leads to a disconnect between the aesthetic promise of a functioning metropolis and the mechanical reality that much of the city lacks depth beyond its visual presentation. For players expecting a simulation on the level of traditional city-builders, this absence becomes a noticeable gap.

Terrain and infrastructure tools, though generous in scope, can also feel rough around the edges. Road construction in particular tends to be finicky, with slopes that snap into strange angles and intersections that lack polish. Terrain transitions may appear abrupt, and the world’s natural geography sometimes feels more like a rough draft than a cohesive landscape. These issues don’t ruin the creative experience, but they do add friction, especially when attempting more precise or realistic city layouts. The game’s visuals and NPC animations similarly reflect the limitations of an independent project, functioning well enough to support creativity but lacking the refinement expected from larger-budget titles.

Even with these shortcomings, Technicity has a clear identity and appeals strongly to a certain type of player. Those who value open-ended building, architectural design, terrain shaping, and large-scale experimentation will find plenty to enjoy. Its cooperative mode also adds a layer of social creativity, letting friends build entire neighborhoods together in a persistent world. And because the game doesn’t impose demanding simulation rules, it becomes an ideal canvas for relaxed, long-form construction sessions. However, players seeking deep urban management or a complex interplay of economic and civic systems will quickly notice the emptiness behind the city’s façade.

Ultimately, Technicity stands somewhere between a creative sandbox and a light construction simulator, offering impressive freedom but limited systemic depth. It succeeds best when embraced as a hands-on building toy rather than a full-featured city-management experience. The tools it provides are powerful, the world is large, and the ability to create and share custom content gives it lasting appeal. With more development polish and richer simulation layers, it could evolve into something truly exceptional. For now, it remains a distinctive and engaging choice for players who find joy in constructing, shaping, and designing entire cities from the ground up—one block, road, and blueprint at a time.

This is a thumbs sideways review, but ever slightly more to the positive side.

I really enjoyed the setting, and story of the game. There were some cliché moments here and there, but also some unexpected events that made it worthwhile.

The writing is good, and the gameplay is passable. There are unfortunately a lot of essential features missing from such an RPG. The tracking of quests is not done well, and it was often difficult to remember the locations of NPCs who originally gave me a quest. 

The quests also lacked a lot of important information, and only displayed the initial goal. Once the quest was updated, and there was a next step, the quest information didn't reflect that.

The biggest annoyance with the game, is at times, your party members would spontaneously decide to disappear on their personal missions. The big problem with that is they took all the gear you gave them, and you couldn't take it back unless you knew the moment before they would leave.

The store page also claims there are "hundreds of magical items to find". Okay, sure...hundreds of absolute garbage magical items, yes! I struggled to find anything actually useful, as every item or enchantment has something like +5% melee damage, or +10% protection against poison damage. Such useless attributes which didn't make my characters feel any more powerful in the slightest.

You also get scarabs, which are kind of like magical charms that give you abilities. I might as well have glued trash to myself instead, the little good they did. And so few scarabs, as well! Throughout the game, I had found only enough to fully equip 3 characters. I might have had one extra.

Finally, the last two or three quests in the game are insufferable in terms of combat. Every corner you turn, another enemy awaits. I had done quite some internal screaming each time I encountered yet another wizard with charm, knockback, or stun spells. 

Perhaps I built my character incorrectly, because the struggle was real. I became a potion addict, chugging multiple bottles at the same time, and still being stun-locked into death at the very end of the game. It soured the experience, which up until the end, was rather positive.

To get the best experience out of this game, I'd suggest looking up some character builds.

好久了，我第一次玩到这个游戏是2017年，那是用我爸的旧手机玩的，给幼小的我带来了深深的震撼。老实说我当时（10岁左右）天真地认为这个游戏里的每一颗星球都会像《无人深空》那样独一无二，现在再玩一遍发现可以探索的星球应该不多，并且也稍微比其它的星球亮一些大一些，很好找。这款游戏放到现在来说应该也不值得这个价位了，记得当初在手机上玩的时候还有很多种付费版本可以选择，现在的我也是为了补票，为了找回那段童年回忆（比那段时间更早我还玩了泰拉瑞亚，也补票了）再花钱买了这个游戏，游戏性很浅，画面放到如今来看也算是比较粗糙，剧情其实也非常非常简单，其实从一开始（下有剧透）[spoiler]就能隐约感受得到lisa博士因太空病离世了[/spoiler]，另外找地球这方面也存在一定的问题：Lisa已经找了上万课星球，我们艾姆只找了几百颗就找到了。不过这在一定程度上也能圆回来，也许Lisa已经把自己剩下的猜想写在了代替自己的智能程序，程序可以自己寻找地球，而选择辅助艾姆寻找地球这本身也是制作者们的一种巧思，体现的是Lisa这个人物的人文关怀面。依稀记得这部作品有一定思考人工智能与人类关系的话题在，也聊的比较浅。
  玩下来这部作品的不足还是很多的，可以看得出来的SIGONO确实是初出茅庐，不过就是很巧，那样年幼的我遇上了这样“年幼”的公司，最后情节对于那时候的我来说足够精妙，“[spoiler]我们一直要找的地球居然在以Lisa命名的恒星之后！？[/spoiler]”，这也为我对宇宙浪漫的感受埋下了一颗需常常幻想才会慢慢发芽的种子，是的，我记得我小时候对天文知识很感兴趣，很小的时候就能记全（相对于很多同龄孩子来说)太阳系八大行星的顺序（我隐约记得那几年有争议冥王星算不算太阳系的行星），还有他们的特点，卫星，气候，地貌啊什么的......那时候也不喜欢尤其不喜欢历史这门学科，想着以后可能真的要当天文学家。不过后来因为学业、特长之类的经历太过繁忙，我也渐渐遗落下了对宇宙的强烈幻想，转而投身于各样的烦恼中了。可是这颗种子还在，他也随着我对于身边环境的感受慢慢发芽了，也就是为什么我总是对与星球、宇宙相关的电影比较感兴趣（事实上只看过几部很经典的），也直到高二前那个暑假，我第一次看了《星际穿越》之后，我对宇宙间的浪漫、跨越时空的情感之类的愈发敏感，这种情感后来也从小时候那种对物理学意义上天文的好奇，转变为了一种地理、历史层面的文明进程的感受，火箭变成了一种模糊的意象，失重感、真空也变成了可以描述现实遭遇的奇妙感受。这些与宇宙相关的元素，慢慢推进着我对于时空理解的构建，这也多亏了我在小时候玩到了这款简单的小游戏——地球计画（我玩的时候名字里就是“画”而非现在的“划”）
  还有一些值得提及的是，这部作品比较明显是为移动端开发的，他的人物可活动区域是竖向的，飞船界面也是竖向摆放的，这与OPUS的下一部作品有明显差异（因为下一部作品是横向的），我玩起来时感受得到有些小细节放到PC来说明显不如手机的呈现，但不管怎么样，这是Sigono的第一个作品，它的完成度已经很高，值得我为之赞叹，并且这部作品的音乐制作非常好，我相信在游戏性与叙事表达中倾向后者的这一类游戏，音乐是一定需要占大头的设计，或者无论哪一类游戏，音乐都是侧向传达情绪的强力手段，而地球计画的音乐真的很好，个人认为最抓耳的是最终飞船快坠入Lisa恒星的配乐《HOPE》，还有游戏结束时的谢幕配乐《Beyond》。
 希望我继续对宇宙充满幻想，也许再过几十年，我也可以真正用自己的躯体去感受宇宙。

Здесь не найти интересный геймплей, запутанную историю или прорывные идеи, но это — первый шажок инди-студии SIGONO в их долгом и тернистом путешествии по созданию милых, фантастичных и чувственных историй. Игра изначально создавалась для телефонов, но, тем не менее, это не слишком сильно отнимает от экспириенса, который хотели создать разработчики, уставшие от современных ААА-игр, над которыми издеваются менеджеры и маркетологи. Взяв за фуллпрайс, скорее всего, разочаруетесь, но хотя бы по скидке можно поддержать первые начинания. Или же вернуться сюда после их последующих игр и посмотреть, с чего всё началось.

Din’s Legacy is a sprawling, systems-heavy action RPG that embraces the unpredictable. Developed and published by Soldak Entertainment, it continues the studio’s signature design philosophy: dynamic worlds, procedural storytelling, faction-driven conflict, and player builds shaped as much by chaos as by intention. Rather than offering a scripted narrative or tightly choreographed campaign, the game throws you into a living environment where monsters scheme, towns collapse or thrive based on your involvement, and your own character evolves through a mutation system that constantly opens new possibilities. It is a game built for players who enjoy complexity, unpredictability, and deep mechanical experimentation.

You begin as a member of the Mutated, a race created by Din—an immortal god known for forcing mortals through cycles of trials. This framing sets the tone: your character is not a fixed entity but an unfinished experiment. Din’s Legacy builds its identity around this concept, allowing your character to mutate into different class combinations as you gain experience. Rather than selecting a single class at the outset, you evolve through the use of mutation points, which let you add new skills, alter existing ones, or adopt entirely different specializations. A mage might sprout barbarian traits, a rogue might gain summoner abilities, and hybrids emerge in surprising, sometimes chaotic ways. This system invites endless tinkering, rewarding players who enjoy crafting strange, powerful, or unconventional builds.

The world itself is equally dynamic. Each scenario generates a new region with its own towns, factions, and monster commanders who actively work toward their own victory conditions. These factions aren’t passive—they launch raids, sabotage settlements, develop technologies, and escalate plans that can reshape the region if left unchecked. The game constantly updates you with evolving threats, giving the sense that everything is happening in real time whether or not you intervene. Towns you are meant to protect can fall under siege, NPCs can die or turn hostile, and monster plots can spiral into full-blown crises. This creates a uniquely reactive experience—your successes and failures directly influence the world’s stability, leading to scenarios that feel earned rather than scripted.

Combat follows traditional hack-and-slash design, but the dynamic environment and mutation system keep it fresh. Skills come from multiple class trees, and enemies vary widely depending on which factions dominate the region. Some foes strike in disciplined groups; others rely on brute-force numbers or unusual magical tactics. Because the world evolves independently of you, threats can escalate quickly, leading to moments where the difficulty spikes or where you are forced to adapt your build on the fly. Loot plays a major role in progression, and while equipment follows familiar RPG conventions, the sheer variety of modifiers—combined with mutated skills—encourages constant refinement of your loadout.

Beyond combat, players can tailor their experience through extensive world customization. Before generating a scenario, you can adjust world size, monster density, faction aggressiveness, environmental modifiers, and more. This flexibility allows you to craft a fast-paced gauntlet, a sprawling sandbox, or something in between. These settings enhance replayability, which is already built into the game’s DNA. No two worlds unfold the same way, and even a similar build can feel drastically different depending on the threats and factions present in a given scenario.

Despite its ambition, Din’s Legacy does exhibit shortcomings. The visual presentation reflects the studio’s modest resources: environments are colorful but lack detail, character models can feel dated, and animations are functional rather than cinematic. The storytelling is also minimalist—little more than framing to justify the world’s constant upheaval. Players seeking narrative depth, emotional arcs, or polished cutscenes will not find them here. Likewise, the sheer density of systems can be overwhelming at first. Between mutation effects, class trees, faction politics, world events, and loot management, newcomers may feel like they are managing a dozen mechanics at once. The game also suffers from occasional imbalance, with sudden difficulty spikes or world events that progress too quickly, leaving you struggling to keep pace.

Yet for its intended audience, these rough edges become part of its charm. Din’s Legacy is unapologetically mechanical, designed for players who enjoy dissecting systems, adapting rapidly, and watching chaotic interactions play out. Its dynamic world simulation and build flexibility give it a sense of life rarely seen in the ARPG genre. Where many games emphasize perfect control and directed experiences, Din’s Legacy revels in the unexpected—monsters can outmaneuver you, towns can fall without warning, and your character can evolve into something you never planned but eventually grow to love.

Ultimately, Din’s Legacy is a unique hybrid of hack-and-slash combat, emergent storytelling, and open-ended character evolution. It offers a depth of replayability far beyond most ARPGs, and its sandbox structure gives players extraordinary agency. It may lack the polish, graphical appeal, and narrative cohesion of mainstream titles, but it compensates with ambition, creativity, and an ever-changing world that demands clever thinking and strategic adaptation. For players who crave originality and unpredictability over gloss, Din’s Legacy provides a rich and consistently engaging adventure.

It's hard to give airbuccaneers a fair review. It really is. Why? Because as of writing, both servers up right now have 0/32 players.

I really doubt anyone will even read this review, only because this is a game time forgot. I bought it when it first came out on steam, and since nothing has changed since other than going free to play (with no bonus for people who previously bought, something that would anger most people but I had my fun with it so I feel it's only fair) all I can do is reminisce on previous times I've played this game in 2013 when it wasn't horribly dead.

I feel like AirBuccaneers is a game that if it had a thriving playerbase it wouldn't be at "mixed" of 60% positive ratings. It's rough around the edges- but not in a way that negatively impacts the game. The game works like most air combat simulators, you fly around in airships and shoot different types of weapons at the enemy while the pilot tries to steer you out of the way of projectiles incoming so you don't horribly crash and burn to your pitiful death. What makes AirBuccaneers different than guns of icarus? Ground combat. It's a lie to say you can walk to your enemies base and kill them via one on one fistfights as the ground is covered in poisonous mushrooms, but in AirBuccaneers you spawn in your home base and can choose what ship to board either by walking onto a docked one or using an hangglider to get to one in the air. But how does this equate into ground combat? You have free movement and aren't locked onto your ship, meaning it's a legitimate strategy to either dismount your hangglider in mid air and jump onto the enemy's ship or to jump from your own and engage in proper swashbuckling- or just take their helm and drive their ship into a cliff. You can also use one of the diverse ship types like the Kamikaze ship that instantly destroys anything when touched (but it horrendously underarmoured) or the massive, immobile fort that has a huge cannon on it but can only move via air maneuver which takes a long time to recharge.

Another great thing about airbuccaneers is the perks and flaws system. I found this very unique at the time, and it still sticks out to me as one of the only multiplayer games that has something like this. There are very overpowered perks in each level progression tree that you can pick to make yourself better suited to one role, but there are negatives in that tree (or other trees) you must choose from as well. This would be just OK if the perks were something generic like "move 10% faster" or "repair 20% slower", but they're all mostly fun stuff like "you're drunk and your screen is tilting", "you don't take fall damage", "you have an eyepatch over half of your screen", and "your gun works like russian roulette and has a random chance of killing you". I didn't get that far in the perk tree as this game died pretty quickly, but it was the main thing that kept me playing and I really wish another multiplayer game would pick up something similar.

So all that positive said, do I recommend AirBuccaneers? Hell yes, if you can find players. It's free to play now, and is a great arcadey game with an interesting character creation system. I just really wish it wasn't dead.

[h1] [b]「我会一直伴你左右，祈祷你的未来将会开满无数幸福的花朵。」[/b] [/h1]
感动、满足、愉悦、幸福……我无法找到一个词来最准确地概括完成这部游戏时的心情。如果要我进行一个最贴切的形容，我会用“解脱”。
推完这部游戏是在凌晨的三点，本想趁着热乎写完这篇评测再去安心睡觉，没想到往床上一躺就再也没有起来，穿着衣服不盖被子就这样睡着了。再醒来便是中午十二点，浑身疼的我起了床吃了点东西于是开始着笔评测。
说了这么多，其实我想要传达的意思只有一个：游玩本作给我的精神带来了相当的疲倦。此前游玩的五彩斑斓系列也同样给了我如此感受，只是那时资历尚浅的我无法指出到底是哪一环节出了问题，只是抱着奇怪的心情机械地通关了游戏。现在我明白了：漆原雪人的叙述水平太烂了。

在游玩本作的途中，我不止一次产生了如下想法：前一句台词是如何承接下一句台词的？前一个场景是怎么发展到下一个场景的？事情为什么会变成这个样子？这到底是什么类型的叙事？。若是其他知名脚本的作品，我会怀疑是作品本身过于烧脑或者我的理解能力缺乏锻炼，但这个作品让我确信：如果我感觉这个故事很复杂很难懂，那一定是他的表达方式有问题。
我严重怀疑雪人的大纲就是先写一条大概的主线以及一张复杂的角色关系网，然后上手想到什么写什么——反正最后角色之间的联系能串起来、剧情能回归到主线，一切有所谓的没所谓的都能归于角色塑造与剧情铺垫。不然我实在是想不到，类似本作推着主线、突然又衍生支线、然后插入回忆讲述角色故事、时不时来点哲学讨论/观点说教、冷不防地在本就不清晰的主线上添砖加瓦这样毫无章法的叙事是如何出现在一个制作偏成熟的商业作品上的。我感觉我不是来看小说的，是来看随笔的，故事是跟着脚本想法走的，他简直是在写意识流。
他从没有在意过剧情节奏，不然也不会做出肆意穿插回忆、大篇输出不知所云的观点这样大幅增加阅读难度、让人连看懂都觉得困难的行为，某种意义上我觉得他可能真的很享受写作，只是一味地写而已……我在游玩时体会到的正面情绪反馈几乎都源于剧本本身的优秀，这可能能证明他的想法确实不错吧，但这样的剧本换个叙事显然能有更好的效果。

在游玩本作之前，个人还去看了雪人的一部轻小说，叫做《如果明天，这个世界就会终结》。实际上，相比本作而言，舞台更为箱庭的小说带给我的观感要好上不少，其中更为通畅的语言表达和富有想象力与美感的环境描写一度让我以为雪人的写作水平突飞猛进了，直到我游玩了本作。目前，包括本作在内的许多游戏会将剧本的文字量当作宣传，意在宣扬故事的体量之大、内容之丰富。实际上这样的宣传就如同雪人的小说与游戏给我的不同感受，小说的篇幅更为短小但也能明显感受到对文字表达的精简与叙事节奏的把控，而游戏却一味追求大体量反而诞生了无数冗杂的叙述与无意义的复杂。如此庞大的文字量当中，有效信息到底有多少呢？现在我去苹果自带的阅读里边打开一本书，一卷异世界厕纸普遍500-800页，一本严肃文学的长篇小说却只有不到400页，虽然这样的对比有些欺负人，但我认为文字的凝练毫无疑问要比体量更为重要。毕竟实际上，雪人有了篇幅的限制不也能写出小说那样的精炼文字吗？
相较于老资历而言，本人体验过的雪人作品只有鸟鸟三部和一本轻小说以及本作而已，想来是不足为道的。然而就光是这几部作品当中，雪人所写下的元素就有相当严重的同质化趋向——戴罪之人如何追求幸福、身边一定有透明之人相伴、人要有希望才能活着、言语的力量、祈祷幸福等等……说好听点叫作家个人风格，难听点就叫没活了。写角色就是“因为某种纯粹的愿望而不幸”——“被百般折磨并坚持/黑化”——被爱拯救/解放消散”；写事件就是“异常发生”——“寻找解决办法”——“决战后陷入回忆”——“原来你一直在我身边/我只是渴望爱而已”。这样的写法就算不谈其他作品，光是在本作中就屡屡出现，实在是有点审美疲劳，可能也是单纯的个人不太吃这套吧。不管怎么说，作为一个脚本家，故事的创意始终还是首位，就算这些元素将会成为雪人一生的命题，我也希望他能做到不舍弃这些的同时，为玩家带来更为丰富的体验。

[i] [b]「生命本没有意义或价值，就算你不能成为伟人。就算你无法帮助他人。这一切都无所谓。成就伟大事业对生命来说真的只是微不足道的小事。只要你答应我一件事就够了——不管一生中经历多少悲伤和痛苦——在最后的日子里。希望你能说出『这一生很快乐』」[/b] [/i]
企鹅这个角色，可能是我近期见过的最有人性的神了。嗯，虽然她说自己不是神。灵魂留世或转生，途径旅馆收获温暖的话语，得知有一名高位的存在一直默默地看着自己，祈祷着幸福。暖意流过，只是鼓励的话语却含有难以言喻的说服力。

整个游戏的剧情，几乎就是建立在这样充满着爱与温暖的基调之上的。虽然途径之事曲折离奇阴暗磨难，角色的身世背景也一定伴随着不幸的遭遇，但在故事的主题上雪人一直致力于传达爱这一方面是我很欣赏且喜欢的。在本作中，雪人用“爱”这一主题规避掉了“红绪家所致力的真正的幸福”与“一人的牺牲”这个电车难题，用红绪终这一角色癫狂的塑造和主角仅仅是为了所爱之人的幸福这两点来让剧情的走向逐渐变得一边倒，这种仅是为了一人而非强行宏大的写法同样是我所喜爱的。因此本作的情节可谓是非常合我胃口，也难怪在如此差劲的叙事之下我也能收获这般感动。
红绪祀在苦难之中坚强不屈，向着天空高喊命运小儿；非人注定不为人所爱的命运被拯救，心中的谢意与爱意驱使其世世相追；橘才怀着想成为人类的渴望拼命收集心，为了母亲和妹妹放弃自己的幸福……不同角色的命运在不断的轮回中交织变化，不管是谁都在竭尽全力追寻自己的爱与幸福，这样不惧痛苦勇敢追求苦尽甘来充满希望与陪伴的故事也许就是雪人笔下真正的魅力所在吧。

可惜的是，除了上述列出的角色以外，其他角色的故事与作用都稍显单薄。在这个看似双男主一女主的封面之下，本作所写的重点实际是非人与橘才的一对一。祀作为串通起两者的桥梁也获得了相当程度的重视，其定位是“过去的主角”、“现今的锚点”，前者联系角色，后者展开剧情，角色作用大于角色塑造。至于另一位男主龙起，就是各种层面的惨了。剧情中出生便是公共厕所开局，从外面主动潜入红绪家当卧底，背景无比强大还有个天下无敌的师傅，剧情中一直在说要突破要超越到头来打团造成的有效伤害几乎没有，从来都只是个肉盾的同时还是个只堆生命不堆护甲的肉，随随便便被打一下就是真伤，剧情始于他被橘才撞飞，最后埋下的伏笔也不了了之，舔了一整个游戏的祀最后也不知道有没有结果，用于塑造的笔墨也没有多少，其作用更多是作为橘才不在时的视角摄像头而存在。说实话，前期橘才的塑造真的很不讨喜，出场便是手染无数鲜血的变态杀人魔，看过祀的记忆之后还不忘来几句嘲讽，人好心帮他也只是被他解读为玩善人游戏，就这样一个烂人要和龙起抢女主、还当人面对着人心爱的人告白，这一套下来确实有够憋屈而且恶心，相当劝退，结果发展到后面龙起成小丑了橘才成圣人了，好端端男主之一成了躺赢狗，不知道雪人到底在写什么。

显然，这是一部问题远多于亮点的作品，叙事与文笔上的巨大缺陷令我几乎是以一种“折磨”的心态来通关这部游戏的，“雪氏老方”的情节及人物设计也凸显出其缺乏新意的遗憾，逐渐走向极端的人物资源分配也使其中的不少角色工具感显著。然而，这篇故事带给我的感性体验使我不禁以一种宽容的心态来看待这部作品。在众多描写角色不幸与痛苦遭遇的作品中，雪人的作品总是以一种追求爱与幸福的执着打动我，这种追求中透出的力量堪称“傻劲”，纯粹且童话，却总能导向一个幸福的结局，一个充满着爱与希望的五彩斑斓的世界。他笔下的文字不知所云又繁琐到令人皱眉，但他的故事却如魔力般吸引着人。也许我已经是个大人，因为我学习了理论与知识，能够写下批判与评论的文字；也许我还是个孩子，会对故事中的真善美产生触动与共鸣，对那爱与幸福的童话有种近乎痴愚的喜爱。
[i] [b]「活着本身，就是一场玩笑，没有意义，每一秒只是无色透明地度过。但既然反正也是没有意义的人生。向所爱之人献上诗歌，这样活着。为自己的内心绽放花朵，这样活着。像这样，为自己方便地创造意义就好——去培育有活下去的价值的东西就好。感觉充斥着整个世界的什么东西，暗暗地对我说着……如果决定了自己应该怎么活着，尽可能多地享受快乐的时光，才划得来。我也能纯粹地这样想。」[/b] [/i]

Adorable Witch is a short, puzzle-focused title built around simple mechanics and a light fantasy theme. Its structure centers on small, self-contained stages where the player guides a witch character through environmental hazards using basic movement and object interaction. The design emphasizes quick comprehension and minimal mechanical complexity.

Level layouts rely on timing, switches, traps, and enemy positioning. Solutions tend to be straightforward, and most stages can be cleared with brief trial and error. The difficulty curve remains mild throughout, making the game accessible but offering limited challenge for players seeking deeper puzzle design.

Visual presentation uses bright colors and a soft, cartoon-inspired style. Character animations are minimal but consistent with the game’s small scope. Backgrounds and effects are simple, supporting clarity rather than detail. The overall aesthetic is cohesive even if it does not push beyond basic expectations.

Audio design is functional, featuring short music loops and limited sound effects. While not memorable, it supports the general tone without detracting from the experience. The soundtrack maintains a light atmosphere that aligns with the game’s visual identity.

The gameplay loop is brief, and the total playtime is limited. This structure suits players looking for a compact experience but may feel insubstantial for those expecting extended progression or mechanical depth. Replay value is minimal once all stages are completed.

Controls are responsive, and the game runs smoothly on modest hardware. Its simplicity helps avoid technical issues, and the interface is intuitive enough that players can start immediately without tutorials.

Overall, Adorable Witch delivers a small-scale puzzle experience built around clear mechanics, light presentation, and approachable difficulty. It works as a short, casual title but does not aim for intricate puzzle design or substantial narrative content.

Spy Fox Opération Milkshake est un jeu que j'avais longuement écumé dans sa version CD-ROM lorsque j'étais encore une enfant. Ne possédant pas de lecteur de CD-ROM sur mon ordinateur actuel, j'étais frustrée de ne pas pouvoir retrouver ma Madeleine de Proust − jusqu'à ce que je remarque qu'il avait été aussi publié sur Steam.

Je me suis donc décidée à télécharger cette version, et à mon grand bonheur, j'ai constaté que ma joie de jouer à Spy Fox était demeurée intacte.

Il faut dire qu'outre son intrigue (qui parodie de manière amusante les histoires à la James Bond), ce jeu bénéficie d'un humour omniprésent, dont on apprécie parfois même mieux les subtilités lorsqu'on y joue en tant qu'adulte. Le gameplay, de type pointer-cliquer, s'appuie sur des puzzles, des relations entre personnages, mais ce qui m'amuse le plus, c'est la possibilité de cliquer à peu près n'importe où dans une scène donnée pour y trouver une multitude de petites surprises visuelles et de mini-gags.

Le portage en français est efficace ; et même si l'on devine que quelques jeux de mots de la version originale n'ont pas pu être traduits depuis l'anglais, d'autres ont été adaptés avec brio par l'équipe de traduction. De manière globale, le doublage en français est très amusant, et donne un vrai relief à une galerie de personnages déjà hautes en couleurs (quoiqu'une ou deux caricatures fussent inutiles, par exemple l'accent du poulet spécialiste d'arts martiaux). Mention spéciale au doublage du rôle-titre qui accentue à la fois son élégance à toute épreuve et son côté franchement snob : c'est un vrai régal.

Un autre petit défaut de la version Steam par rapport à la version CD-ROM est l'enchaînement des lignes de doublage, qui ne respecte pas certaines pauses du format original (respire un peu pendant ton monologue d'ouverture, Cabri !)

En dépit de ces quelques détails, Spy Fox reste tout de même un jeu fichtrement amusant, avec un point fort qu'il faut impérativement souligner : sa rejouabilité. Car il existe plusieurs moyens de déjouer les plans de Cabri O'Lait ! Si vous lancez une deuxième partie de Spy Fox Opération Milkshake, il y a de très fortes chances que le jeu ne vous propose ni les mêmes puzzles ni les mêmes interactions que lors de votre première partie.

Agent Morgane, terminé !

Alright, so... I've been playing ADOM since around 2004, give or take. I was in primary school and my mum got me my first PC. Back then it was ASCII only. In 2015, ADOM got a Steam release, and along with it came some nice tiles and sprites to make the game more approachable.

ADOM is a top-down, turn-based, traditional roguelike RPG that is EXTREMELY difficult and brutal. I think ADOM is a fantastic example of why older games are just better — the game is longer, the systems run deeper, and there's so much more customization.

You will die, many, many, many times. There’s even an area in the game that is literally blocked off by the devs until you’ve lost 100 characters. That alone tells you what to expect.

To me, ADOM is the quintessential fantasy RPG. Give it a proper go — once you start getting the hang of it, you'll see that very few games come close to how awesome ADOM is.

It's the best game ever made, at least to me. And I've played thousands of games.

In the 90's and 2000's I spent well over 1000 hours on ADOM.  That's a very conservative estimate. And over the past 15 years I've bought dozens of roguelikes, trying to recreate the experience that this game gave me. And some of those roguelikes were very good - but they never did what this did. 

Every single roguelike I've owned since around 1998, my first instinct is to compare how it does things to how ADOM does things and the other roguelike always comes up short. The balance, the world, coming up with inventive ideas to get out of seemingly impossible situations. It's the gold standard imho.

So yeah, I'd recommend this. It's alright.

At this moment I have played the game for 6 hours, before the two hours struck, I have to admit I was in doubt if I should keep the game, or refund it. I have decided to keep it, and I have decided to recommend the game. But with some reservations.

The game is played on a single map (divided by portals which you can freely move between). It is a pretty hardcore game, in which you can lose everything and can be forced to reset. In many ways making this a survival game. In this game you will be able to meet hundreds or even thousands of other players all trying to expend their empire.

This is personally something I love, no instance based RTS, but one massive world. Everyone connected to each other. For that reason alone, this game gets a massive plus, as there are very few games like this and even less that succeeded. It is a genre that needs to be tamed, as a true MMORTS is something I have been longing for for years.

The basics are there and they work. The pathfinding is not perfect, but your units do get from A to B. Building works correctly and your resource gathers work as they should. 

There is however not much beyond this point. The amount of buildings, resources and troops is limited. When it comes to war, generally the player that is online the most wins, as he can gather more resources. The developers have mentioned that more resources are on the way and hopefully more unit and building variaty will be added as well.

The game is also lacking a real objective, as there is no way to 'win' the game. This might not be seen as a negative for everyone however, as some prefer the sandbox gametype.

There is a lot to like about this game, but there are 2 fundamental problems. 1) You fight aliens, gather resources and upgrade your gear but then what? Nothing- you just do that again over and over. 2) Resources are scarce. No matter how well you do on missions, you are likely going to be able to refill your ammo and not much more. Unless you use the weakest weapons and gear in the game, but even then the rewards are just enough to keep your team going and maybe upgrade a piece of gear every so often.

As such, this is a rat race. Kill shit. Recover. Kill shit. Seems like they could have done a lot more with this.

Deathspank – игра, которая высмеивает жанр ролевых игр, культуру американского общества, и берёт самое лучшее из игр серии Diablo. За те 10 часов, которые уйдут у игрока на полное прохождение, игра не успевает надоесть, оставляя после себя приятное послевкусие и неожиданный финал, который полностью ломает представление о мире игры.
Звуки электронной гитары будут сопровождать игрока по картонному, вымышленному и карикатурному миру средневековья, от одного чудаковато-то задания к другому. Чего только стоит задание с нахождением пропавших сирот и помещением их в мешок, или помощи местному Индиане Джоунсу с зачисткой пещер, в которые он сам не может пойти из-за боязни узких пространств, темноты и пауков.
Снаряжение, что герой будет находить на протяжении всей игры выглядит красиво и эстетично, как если бы его комплекты продавались отдельно в виде дополнений, в лучших традициях тех же Electronic Arts. В мире также полно оружия с разными характеристиками, начиная с мечей, жезлов, арбалетов и заканчивая каким-нибудь молотом, который не наносит урон демонам, но, в буквальном смысле, выбивает из них дерьмо.
“Мультяшность” мира DeathSpank позволила ему хорошо сохраниться в наше время. Каждая локация имеет свой тон повествования. Перемещение между которыми происходит через деревенские сортиры.
Настоятельно рекомендую проходить игру на английском языке, не используя кривой русификатор от команды ZoG Forum Team, из-за которого теряется львиная доля юмора, что есть в диалогах, и использовать контроллер для более комфортного прохождения.

Итоговая оценка – 9/10.
Игра была пройдена на Lenovo Legion GO s.

前言：我是玩完了续作《神树残响》再回来玩前作的，所以下面的评价主要基于两作的区别重点评价，先说结论，建议玩家先玩《神树》再玩本作，理由我会在下面详谈：
（另外我是通过家庭共享玩的神树残响的，所以库里没有，库存警察勿扰）

游戏性方面：本作属于是常规的RPG宝可梦回合制对战玩法，各个分系统丰富度比续作《神树残响》要丰富，有完整的伙伴战力，各种工会，采集系统也更丰富，烹饪和烘焙系统全程可用，支线委托也非常多，还有昼夜交替，续作《神树》反而是阉割了很多功能，但事实上，体感上确实《神树》更好玩，当然卡牌系统带来了更多的乐趣，但不得不说多而杂的系统带来的是给玩家带来的是更多的麻烦，而非增益。

剧情上，《虚构未来》这作，只谈真结局，概括的讲就是女主为了拯救和自己朝夕相处了半年的小女友（女同向）不惜付出一切最后拯救成功的故事，而事实这个小女友只是把你当工具人最后还背叛了女主，故事非常传统也非常圣母，从立意高度上就远远低于讲赫卡特为主角的《神树残响》的，《神树》完全是从个人救赎，到家国救赎，再到人类这个种族的救赎，立意可以说非常高了，两篇故事读下来，《神树》给人以一种十分畅快的感觉，而读完《神树》再读《虚构未来》就完全是在《神树》的阴影下，只想把本作作为《神树》世界观的补充去了解杀人鬼时期的赫拉特，而对于女主被背叛再去舍命救赎的“感人”故事，就完全无感了。

另外，世界观的营造我认为本作是不全面的，很多世界观是我从读了续作《神树》的剧情，变的理解的，这也是为什么我建议先看《神树》，因为在《神树》剧情临到最后是梳理了一遍类似红莲之主到神树一系列的神权更替的，脉络就很清楚，而本作事实上是没有完全说清楚的，无法想象在没看《神树》的前提下，是如何对这个怎么理解了。

结语：说了那么多，只是想说本作全面不如续作《神树残响》，也没什么大惊小怪的，前作不如续作，不是很正常嘛，所以还是推荐大家玩一玩的，无论是作为独立的作品去看，还是作为续作世界观的补充，本作的内容是非常值得一玩的，特别一提，在这两作的比较中，不妨可以代入作者的思考，对于各系统的取舍以及制作思路，可能会有不一样的收获。

标准的中规中矩剧情类rpg，不过不管是量上还是情节安排上确实都比社团续作神树差不少，糖度也差点意思
游戏数值设计上也差了点，很多资源需要刷一下才行，该叮就叮吧 反正是看剧本的
总评价是合格 可以买来看看，但远不比进步幅度明显的续作神树来的惊艳

『Sakura Swim Club』は、高校の水泳部に所属した主人公が、チームメイト2名との関係を深めていく短編ビジュアルノベルです。物語は一般的な展開に沿って進行し、競技要素よりもキャラクター同士の交流に重点が置かれています。選択肢は少なく、ストーリー展開に大きな影響を与えることはほとんどありません。

アートワークは高い完成度を持っています。キャラクタースプライトおよびCGシーンは鮮やかで整っています。背景は静的ながら、必要十分な水準です。アニメーションはジャンル特性上限定的ですが、全体的な表現品質は安定しています。

ストーリーテンポは明快で、対話がテンポよく進行し、関係性の構築に焦点を当てています。物語自体は軽めで、大きな意外性はなく、過度なドラマ性を求めるユーザーには向きません。シンプルなロマンス要素を求めるプレイヤー向けと言えます。

ゲームプレイの介入要素は最小限です。テキストを読み、数少ない選択肢を選び、CGを閲覧する程度で、パズルやサイドアクティビティは存在しません。分岐が限定的なため、リプレイ性は低いです。

動作性能は安定しています。起動は迅速で、幅広い環境で問題なく動作し、基本的な設定が用意されています。サウンドトラックは穏やかですが、やや単調です。

総評として、『Sakura Swim Club』は、短時間で楽しめるロマンス重視のビジュアルノベルであり、魅力的なアートと簡素なメカニクスが特徴です。軽いドラマ性を求めるユーザーには適していますが、価格に対し内容が薄いと感じる場合もあります。

Bad North delivers a fast, accessible tactical strategy experience that fits perfectly into short sessions without sacrificing depth. Each island introduces new layouts, demanding positioning and meaningful decisions, from choosing where to deploy your troops to deciding which commander to risk in order to protect your homes. The minimalist visual style, paired with a calm soundtrack, contrasts beautifully with the tension of the Viking invasions.

For those looking for a light yet engaging strategy game to enjoy in short bursts, Bad North is a solid choice. It doesn’t try to reinvent the genre, but it executes its ideas with precision and offers a satisfying experience from start to finish.

A very cool game with lots of potential, but not worth its price.

Bad North feels more like a mini game than a real game, it lacks depth and is extremely limited.
I would love to play this game for hours and hours if it had more replayability, more items, more classes, more spells etc.
But the sad reality is, I played 4 hours, and I already discovered everything the game has to offer in terms of gameplay. This is not a rogue-like you can lose yourself in for hours and find creative ways to have fun in.
I played one campaign, cleared it, and now what ? There is nothing more to do, and the gameplay does not allow you to be creative, so there is no reasons for me to go for an other run.
Only 3 classes, one spell per class, and a few items that don't even have any synergy with anything prior ? That is very weak :/

To me, the game is clearly unfinished, but could be reaaally fun if it contained way more content. I see the potential, and I will keep an eye out if the content ever comes so I can change this review.
In this state, I would argue it is worth $3 or $5 at most, but clearly not $15.

I would still recommend it, it is still a good game, but definitely not at this price.

This a wonderful little game that has obviously had a lot of effort put into it! My hat goes off to the small team who made it!

To summarise, Radix Chronicle is a hybrid turn-based tactics/puzzler that slowly and carefully introduces new strategies to the player, easing in those less familiar with the genre into, by the end, pulling off wild combos and synergies to obliterate the battlefield.

The battles are short and sweet, and thanks to the Ring Trial system, devoid of frustrating RNG and 5% miss chance bullshit. Now you can only blame yourself if you miss that essential attack! The real fun comes in once you start going for the optional objectives, and even secret ones! Doing these earns you more loot for more unique plays, but thankfully aren't 100% necessary to make it to the end if its too much of a grind for you.

While simple graphically, it oozes 16-bit charm and some catchy music I find myself humming sometimes. It thrusts a conflicted cast of characters thrust into a plot that slowly reveals itself even beyond the first playthrough! My only gripe is that there is not enough of it!

What it feels like: A mash-up of FF Tactics and Disgaea, crossbred with a Puzzle game.

QoL Recommendations:

- Would be nice to mouseover terrain and see what effects it has. Same with status ailments. Getting to the manual is a pain while in game.

- Being able to see your stage score on previous attempts would be nice.

Overall: Strongly Recommend if you enjoy Turn-based Strategy games.

An absolutely delightful game! As someone who is totally new to the bullet hells, picking this up finally made the genre really click for me. An outstanding look into the future of shmups! Takes the Touhou formula into something very uniquely special with its abstract fantasy setting and exquisite world-building discoverable due to the scanning mechanic. Despite it's advances into the potential of the bullet hell genre, it's actually very easy for a bullet hell! It makes this a great introduction for new players that would want to explore this genre as it's quite forgiving with it's amount of lives as well as bullet patterns which make this very approachable for something of this caliber before getting into the harder difficulties. The cast of characters are great! The playable characters all have unique special attacks and their perks that are worth a try although Empitts is hands-down the easiest character to do a full run with as she gifted with bonus lives and the best balance of speed and utility. The bosses and the enemies are unforgettable with their surreal appearances and multi-media visual style that tell vast stories with their looks alone, which applies to the boss spell cards as well. (When was the last time I've seen rotting teeth being used as projectiles in a bullet hell? Let alone any game!) Learning about each of the colorful characters and their settings throughout playing the game and unlocking journal entries is really fun and worth a look into the vastness of this universe's themes of mortality and time. The music deserves a shoutout for being wonderful and a PERFECT match to this colorful visual style. My favorite songs being the Stage 2 Boss Fight (Audrey), the Extra Stage, and the nostalgia-inducing beauty that soundtracks the Journal pages. I can't recommend this game enough! Despite a bug here and there, (nothing game-breaking as far as I found, just some visual or input hiccups.) as well as lack of controller support and volume options, this game is absolutely worth it! It's supplied with a lot of content to chew on despite being an arcade bullet hell. I'm endlessly excited to see what Ethereal Airport does next to add to their already diverse collection of indie games. Check it out!

[b]Story:[/b] As I said, the strengths for this game lie for one in how they set up the history of the MC and how you explore and interact with the mysteries of who you are. Each romanceable character (route) has specific insight into your heritage, story, and issues the current world is going through. You are left guessing in one route but get another clue in another route, and so on. It's very replayable and seems to encourage going through again. I do wish some routes focused more on the two main issues (our heritage and the Energy Crisis) but I assume this is an artistic choice and suspect the Fae routes will help fill in the blanks. I have not come across any choices that lock me out of an ending, aside from very very very slow quick time events necessary to fail and get the 'bad end' of your route. The world is intriguing but doesn't seem to have coherent culture. I would love to see it explored more and explained! 
[b]In summary:[/b] Love the storytelling aspect, wish for a more cohesive world, would love to see a more tidy ending on some routes. Tragic ends are A+, particularly recommend Druk's as it evokes a rather sad fairytale type end. 

[b]Art:[/b] Lovely. The backgrounds are a delight to look at, soft and comforting and detailed. I want to live in MC's room and walk around the library and flower fields. I love what we see of the fae courts and want to see more! Character design is interesting, particularly of the fae, and you can pick out personality for the most part by looking at them. I do hesitate to say this, but I have to be honest, the main sprites for the LI's are lacking a little. Some are rougher than others, and I fully believe the artist probably did these early on and has gotten better because most of the CG's are lovely but the main sprites for some are...not great. Druk suffers the most from this, but I find Fenir also to look slightly off, along with Kimura and the anatomy for Kayn, and Kuna'a's neck. I don't think Etza looks bad at all, Aisa is so-so. Mom looks okay. I hate to say this but I feel like this is what drags Alaris back the most. These sprites don't match the detail in which the Fae like [spoiler] in the dawn court and Tar, I think, in the forest [/spoiler] have, and it can be super jarring and takes me out of the story when they share screen with a differently rendered sprite. Paricularly because we look at them the most. I don't want to dunk on Alaris, I think it's one of my preferred VN's already, I enjoy it greatly, and the dev has done amazing work. I just want to see Alaris shine. 
[b]In summary:[/b] Backgrounds are perfection, in love with all the designs, the main cast looks very shaky. 

[b]Romance:[/b] Intriguing that it is actually plot relevant! Each route has it's own issues and foray and way to get closer to your LI of choice. I tested this and you can romance anyone with any personality trait, they will just make different comments and some like certain things better [spoiler] Kuna'a and Kayn seem to like a flirty protag, for one. [/spoiler]. All LI's have a distinct personality and past and way of reacting to you, making them engaging to explore. If you're looking for super lovey, hands-on romance, this isn't it, it feels appropriately like getting to know someone you're coming to really like. (Even Kayn is pretty chill. We'll see how Kuna'a behaves). 
[b]In Summary:[/b] Very sweet LI's with their own personality and perspectives on plot. No critcisms. 

[b]MC customization:[/b] Not overly dramatic. Pronouns/gender/a quick quiz to determine some traits. The traits don't make a huge impact on story, and I sort of wish some choices would lock out other LI's or make some tasks harder. I feel it could make some difference. Essentially you will come to your choice of route and (assuming you're playing a central route because that's what released) you are nearly guaranteed any of them to be into you if you've been halfway interested in them. Or even if not. 
[b]In summary:[/b] Lacking, but also that isn't the focus of the game. Just keep expectations decent. 

[b]Gameplay:[/b] Easy to understand and navigate. VERY appreciative of a decent skip system. Never had any issue with saves. Actively tried to cause problems on purpose and all I could manage to do was get two songs to play at once by scrolling back and forth. Impressed by lack of bugs in EA. I do find navigating the communicator a little clumsy (Mouse and computer) as sometimes I have to click a couple times to get a message to generate and sometimes it just pops up. The quick time events are a little too slow, I appreciate it not being too fast but I wish it wasn't so long. 
[b]In summary:[/b] Easy, non-bugged gameplay, some preferences. 

Overall, I really enjoy this game. I follow along various socials to keep an eye on it and hope it releases to great success. You can see the time put in and the care. The characters and interesting world building are definitely strengths, and if you like a VN with replayability this is your thing.

[b]Foreword[/b]

Let's revisit the developer and the first episode before moving forward. Apart from Kathy Rain, we have the excellent [i]Whispers of a Machine[/i] available from the same team, also a point and click video game. As for KR: I remember checking it out when it became free (the game was released almost a decade ago!) and I purchased the director's cut which included some enhancements (released 5 years after the original).

[b]Story[/b]

In this sequel we continue to control Kathy as the protagonist. 3 years have passed since the events of the first episode and Kathy has become a private investigator. We learn that she used to work with Lucas but moved on to offer her own PI services. In terms of clothing and haircut style there have been no changes. I liked the idea of moving forward in time as this Kathy seems to be more mature now. 

Unfortunately, money is (still) an issue so Kathy decides to pick up a case that comes with a nice little sum as reward. A serial killer called Soothsayer is terrorising the citizens of Kassidy and Kathy decides to put an end to all this. The story is quite interesting and it is told in 6 days (consider every day a chapter). Important parts are introduced by cutscenes and as Kathy has nightmares between the chapters you just know that there will be references to the events that happened in the first game.

Did I like the plot? I still feel the ending was rushed (similarly to its predecessor) and I'm still not sure whether or not I like the supernatural approach the game takes. I just found Kathy's character so interesting and likeable throughout the game that I would have just moved on with a more standard thriller / crime investigation direction.

[b]Gameplay[/b]

This is a point & click game alright! Controlling Kathy is quite easy. We just use the left click to interact with objects and if items are needed for this from our inventory, we just need to drag those but first we need to click on the bag in the lower-left corner of the screen. For the majority of dialogues Kathy uses her notebook. A diamond symbol at the bottom is available which allows us to ask questions pertaining to interactable objects in the location where we are. Honestly, this could not be better in any way. No annoying HUD, no unnecessary action wheel.

Leaving a location always shows Kathy on her [i]katmobile[/i] driving on the road. As we progress with the story, new and new places are added and they are available in the upper left corner. This being a sequel we now have almost 20 areas! Not all of them are available at the same time, though. I enjoyed seeing Kathy on her bike as the time of the day as well as the weather (and even the traffic behind us) keep changing as the story unfolds.

The game has a lot of achievements and many are related to the story and to some silly (optional) thing we can try to do (e.g. using our lockpick set to steal different vehicles). This is something that was added in the first episode (only in the Director's Cut). I didn't mind these but I certainly did not miss the different skins for our bike. And what about the puzzles? They are interesting but I struggled with the one where decoding / sending messages via a pager was a must. I'm fine with using a guide for the sake of immersion so this was not really an issue. 

[b]Summary[/b]

Kathy Rain 2 is an example of how a sequel must be done. I found Kathy's new storyline more interesting and appreciated the increased length a walkthrough took this time. Growing up in the '90s I also liked that the story takes place in 1998. Answering machines? CRT displays? Making phone calls via landlines only? When we visit Eileen (Kathy's best friend) at the newspaper company, there is a CRT display in the lower-right corner with the 3D Pipe screensaver running. Do you remember this? 

This is a must have for point & click game fans. Anything I missed? A developer's commentary option would be great!

[h2] Upon Impression:[/h2] 
Kathy Rain 2: Soothsayer is one of the best sequels I have ever played for any game. Not much is taken away from the original; Kathy is still equipped with her lighter, taser and the notes journal. Most of the puzzles are pretty much the same, where you have to use your head and be creative with how to solve them, thinking outside of the box sometimes. Some important characters from the original game are still relevant, but many more new ones are introduced and fleshed out, making Kassidy City more of a prevalent place with depth. 

[h2]In relation:[/h2] 
This game also ties in with Kathy Rain, explaining most of the unanswered questions, doing a good job of having an explanation to do with some antagonist and their motive, making it a surprise twist that makes sense and more than it seems.

I suggest playing the previous game first, especially as this one's ending and conclusion will be a lot better than without playing it. Mind you, if you're one of those people who played the first game but can't remember much of it, this one has a short recap before starting it, so don't worry too much about it, but some things will make a lot of sense in the final days if you find yourself questioning certain things. 

[h2] What is Kathy Rain 2: Soothsayer?[/h2]
Like before, this is a point-and-click adventure game. A sequel that takes place a couple of years after the end of the first game, now Kathy Rain has a license and her own office to be a full-time private detective. The only problem is that she is desperate for a quick amount of cash to not be evicted from her apartment/office, taking it upon herself to find out who the Soothsayer is. A criminal seemingly killing random civilians, leaving a calling card behind in every crime scene for months.

[h2]The differences:[/h2]
Otherthan Kathy Rain becoming more badass over time, the stakes are higher with some weapon violence, some drunken use, swearing and gore as there is a dangerous killer on the loose whose motivation is unclear yet, so it could be anyone (even Kathy's best friend, Eileen, right)?

Another major thing that is different between the 2 games, and someone can pinch me if I'm wrong on this, it's the cinematic cutscenes. There aren't many of them, and they go by quite quickly, but when they hit, they hit, going by so quickly you want to rewatch them again if that's possible in the moment.  Selling the tension and the adrenaline rush for how much they stand out and how insanely well calligram it is for a point-and-click adventure game. 

[h2]The beauty:[/h2]
You don't tell me this doesn't look visually appealing, beautiful, and impressive.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3583168948 
And yes, each location is vast and different, all of which an unique and look like an upgrade to Kathy Rain. 

The pixels for this game, like this location, look like it is taken out of colour theory books, or they could make their way into one. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3582434382 

And if you're one of those people who like to interact with everything and get a dialogue out of it, well, you are looking at one game that allows you to do it, and the bonus is you may gain an achievement out of it. 

[h2]Conclusion:[/h2] 
If there's something I want people to take away from this review, Kathy Rain 2: Soothsayer is a game that just has the right balance of every component incorporated into it. A really solid game. Anyone who thinks otherwise should at least play the game for themselves to see if I'm overhyping it.

1万回クリックするまで終われないクリッカースリラー。

あなたは、あるホテルの一室のベッドで目覚める。その傍らにはチンパンジーのお面をかぶった男が座っていた。男はあなたに集計カウンター（クリッカー）を渡し、大枚を見せびらかしながら、こう告げる。「10000回クリックしろ。そうしたら、このカネをくれてやる」。

基本的にやることは、クリックのみ。ひたすらクリックしつづける。と、いってもいちいちカチカチする必要はなくて、長押しでもカウントしてくれる。なんなら、キーボードのスペースバーを押してもカウントしてくれる。ただし、押しっぱなしの場合は10秒あたり50クリックほどしかカウントしてくれないので、最速クリアを目指す場合は手動で高速連打しまくろう。

クリックしているあいだ、ちょくちょく男からの指示がはいる。カーテンを開けろ、いややっぱ閉めろ、テレビをつけろ、やっぱり切れ、こっち来い、こっち来んな、絵を見ろ、部屋の温度を変えろ、クリックの速度を落とせ……その合間に男は自分自身についての謎めいた語りを挟んでくる。「俺だって昔はクリックが巧かった。だがいつしかこの手が……」

ビデオゲームにおいてクリックは物事を進行させるための手段だ。本作はその「クリックによる進行」を強調し、前景化させることで、ある種の異化効果を発揮する。クリックするだけで数十分から1時間ほどのプレイスルーはとても長い。ダレる。クリックはむなしい。だが、やめられない。クリックしつづければいつか報酬がもらえるというのがゲームの法だから。

その期待を本作は見事に裏切る。
奇妙で不穏な雰囲気のまま進んでいき、すっきりしたオチなどは与えてくれない。謎は謎めいたまま残る。だが、これがクリッカーにハマったわたしたちについての寓話だとするならば、すこしはわかるようになるのかもしれない。

I want to like this game, and there's plenty good here. The first 3-4 hours of it were quite fun. Progressing through the normal difficulty and unlocking new things. But as soon as you need to get to the higher difficulty, it is absurdly reliant on RNG, or metaprogression grinding to even challenge anything. The bonus difficulty goals are near impossible to get (you can have it all go relatively well, to where it looks like you might finally land one of them, only to have RNG shaft you at the end by not giving you the choices you need). It's honestly pretty frustrating. 

The builds and synergies are... unbalanced. There is basically no point in upgrading towers. Just build more towers. Many of the unlocked weapons and towers are inferior to ones you already have, and end up clogging up the available pools. 

And, as mentioned earlier, the difficulty increase at even hard is just unmanageable. Your towers basically do no damage. You basically do no damage (unless you get lucky with plenty of weapon chests, and that those weapon chests drop rare or better upgrades). Even the basic enemies end up having too many hitponits, meaning you're relying almost entirely on the knockback inflicted by your axe to at least keep them away from your city (rather than actually killing them). 

And finally, metaprogression just isn't very interesting. The new city types are fun, and change up the gameplay, sure, and there's unlocks of new towers and weapons that will come naturally, yes, but most of those unlocks simply aren't very good. And the stat increase progression is simply an uninspired grind. If beating the higher difficulties requires investing hours of time into getting +4% attack speed, or +4% tower range, then sorry, but I ain't interested. 

So yeah, I think this game is fun for a few hours, and the basic principles of it being a tower defense/city builder/roguelike is cool. The art style is nice. But the balancing is, quite frankly, pretty bad, and makes it far more frustrating than fun after the first few hours. 

So my verdict is give this one a pass unless it gets some serious rebalancing. And I think it can be rebalanced, and can be salvaged, because the framework of the game is good. So let's hope that happens.

I gave it a long, honest look as someone who loves this type of game and I have to be honest;

For the time being, stay away. 

It's far too undercooked. The difficulty, balance, metaprogression, even basic QoL stuff that's standard in this flavor of Roguelite is so below par that playing the game makes me feel like I paid to alpha test for them.

For example; 

This game doesn't even have Bans/Lock ins for level up choices as a mechanic, yet in order to progress to higher difficulties, some levels will make you do challenges like "Complete a run on Hard using only 4 types of buildings" with no actual way to narrow the pool down enough to make it conceivably doable, especially if you've unlocked other content.

As far as meta progression, it's a looooong grind for small, boring percentile increases: 5% at most and sometimes as low as 3%. No Second Wind, no actual abilities, just "4% attack speed, 5% hp" that scales up in cost exponentially and makes winning a run for the first time not actually feel rewarding or like a big satisfying thing like in Vampire Survivors, Ball X Pit, etc.

The potential is definitely there, and it's got incredible music and a fresh concept. But as of right now I'm left with a bad taste in my mouth

Anyway, I got this to play on the Steam Deck because it was cheap and it said it was verified. It did not work properly on my steam deck. Then again, I was a new Steam Deck user so it could have been my bad.

Anyway, I guess my problems with the game are largely around the typical tropes for a game of this style. There's too much dialogue to read, there's lots of silly set up and preamble that feels meaningless.  In Fire Emblem on the GBA, you were a commander that Lyn encountered in the wilderness. She was this cool badass, facing off against potentially stronger, meaner, and just really obvious bad *guys*. It worked for me. You meet some characters early on that are interesting, and fun to play in battle. I wanted to like Dark Deity, but apart from I guess the saucy character designs in their portraits, they all seemed kind of generic to me.  Anyway, this game has a lot of fluff and I found myself not interested nor caring about it.

Oh well, I guess I'll wait to see if Eternal Legend is more on my wavelength.

The game is decent, I highly recommend it, especially for rhythm game lovers.
The art style is cyberpunk, and if you play the original missions, the music really highlights it. CYBRID is reminiscent of a mix between Beat Saber and Pistol Whip, but there are some subtle differences in the mechanics. You don't have to think about whether to swing swords or shoot; it offers a variety of playstyles. There's fitness, melee, and ranged combat, all set to the perfect beat of the music.
You also need to be able to switch between swords and pistols. You can use a sword in one hand, a pistol in the other, and use the sword to deflect incoming bullets. You know what this game reminds me of, not so much a visual novel, but more like those text adventures from the 1980s where you have to navigate narrative death pits to find various endings - a text game with some nuances, such as having a proper item to progress. However, I am not exactly sure why you are allowed to keep items between the different runs, logically you would find and use them during the same playthrough, but it's not the case for whatever reason, and I am pretty sure some paths don't allow you to do that. I won't pretend that I read every page in this game, not that I didn't enjoy the writing, it just takes a lot for a game to get my attention, but at least it managed to keep me interested for 2 hours. I couldn't do the 100% completion, I found the main 6 endings or letters as they called, plus most of the optional deaths, and yet I am still missing something. The game does not have any voice acting aside from those specific endings, and I kinda wish that it did because I enjoyed those moments. I know the voice acting can also hurt the game, but it also adds to the atmosphere if done well, and those few letters that were voice-acted were my favorite parts of the narrative.  

I thought the illustrations were nice, kind of a unique style I would say, were they made specifically for the game? The reason I ask is that I see a lot of games being made for the artwork, and not the other way around - which is weird to me (but I assume it's original to the game, more credit to you if it is). Good choice of music overall when it does not overlap the last scene, although it does overlap pretty often. I don't believe there is a save feature but you can use a bookmark as a shortcut. 

[h1] Pros: [/h1]

(+) I just like the formatting of this game because text games can be pretty ***** dull, it reminds me of how they used to make text adventures in the past, giving the player a choice after every scene and just killing you constantly. You had some interesting ideas with the items, although the carryover is a strange mechanic, it can be confusing. Honestly, I did not read all of the pages, I read some, and I enjoyed the lighthearted endings, I wish you had more voice acting, even if it was not professional. I liked the choice of music, and I think the art was very nice as well.

(+) Now the game advertises a ton of endings, most of them are more like insta kills, but there are at least 6 main endings with an interesting conclusion.


[h1] Feedback: [/h1]

[u] Nitpicks [/u] - It's a bit unfortunate that you reused some of the pictures, and I kinda wish all scenes had a unique look. You keep the items between the runs which is confusing, I assumed those are only for one run, and you even need to replay with items to get some of the paths. Music would sometimes overlap the last theme. I don't have any issues with the writing, but I thought the paths looped in a very unpredictable way, if at all, sometimes it just made no sense.

Almost forgot, some of the death choices do not have a red border in the UI, probably a mistake.

[b] Overall Thoughts: 7/10 [/b]

I mean for a $2 text game, you still managed to keep me playing, overall I like how you packaged a narrative game with choices and item mechanics, even if they are somewhat negligible. The NEOGEO POCKET COLOR SELECTION Vol. 2 is another fantastic release that continues SNK’s wonderful effort to preserve its handheld legacy. Like the first volume, this collection is packed with charm, great gameplay, and an authentic retro feel that perfectly captures what made the Neo Geo Pocket Color so special.

The emulation quality is excellent once again — the games run smoothly, the presentation is clean and stylish, and the optional Neo Geo Pocket frame gives everything that nostalgic handheld touch. SNK really nails the presentation, and the inclusion of lesser-known titles shows genuine care for the company’s history.

However, there are a couple of drawbacks worth mentioning. Several of the included games remain Japanese-only, with no English translation options. It’s disappointing because these titles have a lot to offer, but the language barrier makes them difficult to fully enjoy for non-Japanese players. Even a simple in-game translation or subtitle option would’ve gone a long way.

Another noticeable omission is SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters 2, one of the most beloved and unique games on the Neo Geo Pocket Color. It’s strange that it wasn’t included, especially since the first Card Fighters Clash was part of Vol. 1. Having the sequel here would have made this collection truly complete.

Still, NEOGEO POCKET COLOR SELECTION Vol. 2 is a joy to play and an excellent continuation of SNK’s retro revival. It’s a must-own for fans of classic handheld gaming, even if it leaves you wishing for just a little more.

[h1]●ゲームの概要等[/h1]

　ネオジオポケットシリーズのタイトルを10個いれたコレクションの第2弾。前作は格闘ゲームとアクションが多めだったが、今回はスポーツ系が多めで、カードバトル、RPG、スゴロク、パズル等が収録。
　収録タイトル自体はストアページを参照して欲しい。



■ゲームの要素

▼プレイ時間は各ソフトでバラバラ。またクリアの基準も曖昧なので明記しないが、実績獲得は10時間前後で可能なはず。一番長いのは「ガンバレねおぽけくん(仮)」か『SNK VS. CAPCOM 激突カードファイターズ』で両者クリア自体は10時間前後だが、やりこみは20時間前後だと予想。運によって前後する。100時間以上プレイしているが、これは寝落ちと各種検証に費やした時間。

▼『SNK VS. CAPCOM 激突カードファイターズ』以外のタイトルでは、トレードや通信対戦等は行えない。

▼ネオジオポケット自体の操作が電源等を除くとジョイスティック、オプション、Aボタン、Bボタンぐらいしかない為、ボタンの長押しや複雑な操作で対応させるタイトルが多いのも特徴。

▼フルスクリーンをゲーム内で設定できない為、フルスクリーン化したい場合はAlt＋Enterを押す事で対応可能。

▼全体的なオプション項目等は存在しない。



[h1]●良い点[/h1]

[b]・巻き戻し機能で効率化[/b]
　カードバトルだと勝利後のドロップの厳選。難しい難易度のタイトルでも、ミス等を補える為、快適なプレイをしやすい。


[b]・SNK VS. CAPCOM 激突カードファイターズ[/b]
　メイン要素としてはこれ。DS版よりもバランスが良く、今回通信対戦専用カード等も収集できるため、応用が効きやすく快適なプレイがしやすい。
　２つのバージョンの両方とも収録されているのも良く、各バージョンでセーブデータが独立している。

　またドロップやHPが可変式。弱い敵と強い敵で分けられ、それに応じてドロップ数も３と５に分けられるが、どちらにせよ他のカードゲームよりもアンティでの獲得数が多い為、かなり効率的に集められるのが良い。



[h1]●悪い点[/h1]

[b]・ガンバレねおぽけくん(仮) [/b]
　このタイトルだけは非常に不愉快だったので注意が必要。以下理由を箇条書き

▼好感度の上昇するイベントの発生がランダムで冗長。中には下がるイベントもある為、巻き戻し機能を使わない場合は数時間以上も粘る事になる可能性が高い。

▼好感度が高い時に発生するゲームの開発進行度を進めるイベントの発生がランダムで冗長。このゲーム開発度が100％にならないとミニゲームは追加されず、数度、このイベントを発生する必要がある。これも巻き戻し機能である程度改善するが、無かったら数時間も不快で退屈な画面を見る羽目になる。

▼ミニゲームの内容が既存のゲームの改悪かつ、プレイ時間が1時間近くの物も存在して拷問の様な退屈さと高難易度でイライラしやすい。

▼単純操作系に加えて、じゃんけん等の完全運要素、連打系と方向キーガチャガチャ系の操作が多い。ちなみに筆者はそれで手の皮がむけた。退屈で肉体的負荷と精神的負荷が強い。

▼主人公とサブキャラが気持ち悪い。下ネタ（特に股間タッチ）や放屁、脱糞、鼻くそ、ほくろ毛。これらの単語に拒否反応があるとキツイ。正直上記の冗長さに合わせてこのようなシーンを延々と見せられるので非常に不愉快だった。

　以上が、主な不快な要素だが、好き嫌いがあるにしても現在のコンプライアンスや価値観に置いて、非常にセクシャルかつ身体的特徴の揶揄等、あまり気持ちの良くない表現が多すぎた。
　当時このゲームを買っていたら、冗談抜きにしてカセットをハンマーで粉砕していた。

　ちなみに連打系はコントローラー設定からSteam入力を有効にしてAボタン等をターボ化すれば、簡易化する。それでもレバガチャ系は多分この設定じゃ対処できない為、下手にやり込もうとすると同じように手の皮がむけてしまうかもしれない。

　ちなみにこのゲームのセーブ方法は、最初の部屋に戻ってオプションボタンに該当するキーを押すとセーブできる。ソフトリセットで消える場合はこの方法でセーブしてからでないといけない。かなりややこしいセーブの仕方だ。


[b]・ネオジオカップ'98PLUS [/b]
　以下の点からちょっとゲームバランス等に不満があるが、人によって気にならないかもしれない。

▼チームによって能力の強弱がありすぎる。また弱いチームに弱いなりの特典がない。

▼敵NPCの連携が強すぎる。決勝戦になると、敵が敵のゴール前からこちらのゴール前まで空中戦でパス。他にも3人がかりでこちらの操作選手を取り囲み、精密な操作も難なく行うため、巻き戻し機能が無いと対処できない難易度。あと一部のチームのゴールキーパーのブロック率が高すぎて、通常のシュートではゴールできない事がある。

▼逆に味方NPCはポジションを守らない。操作キャラがゴール前にいても味方はサポートする気もなく、センターライン付近に存在する事が多い。また味方NPCが近くに複数いると操作がおかしくなる。このせいで敵の様に取り囲んだりしない。ゴールキーパーも敵側よりも防がない事が多いと味方の操作性や連携が弱すぎる。

▼タックル、ヘディング、シュートの判定が曖昧。想定してボタンを押すと別の事をする事が多い。これはレベルによる判定範囲の問題ではなく、基礎システムの判別が曖昧なのが理由だと思う。

▼ランダムイベントの選択肢のどれを選んでも結果が悪くなるしかない事が多い。これは巻き戻し機能でも対処不可能。

▼ミニマップ等がない為、パスするにも味方の正確な位置情報が分からない。それなのに敵側は的確なパスが多い。一応マーク自体は表示されるがかなり出鱈目で距離も状況も不明。

▼放置するとソフトリセットされる。されると進行データが消える。苦労して勝利した後に数分休憩を挟むとすぐにリセットされるため、苦労が水の泡になる。正直かなり萎えた。しかも自動的にいつでもされる可能性がある為、休む暇もなくリラックスしてプレイできない。

▼店売りのアイテムのデメリットが強力かつ、販売価格が高すぎる。結果リーグを2回ぐらい優勝しないと上位のアイテムを購入できない。

　以上が主なデメリットだ。操作性による難易度への影響はチームの強さでいくらかカバー可能で、巻き戻し機能の使用でも対処可能だ。それでもフェアとは言い難いゲームバランスで、日本チームで始めたりすると50戦近く勝利し、育成が整った段階でも巻き戻し機能に依存しないと勝てない様な試合が殆どになってしまう。
　カメルーンやブラジルチームの様な中堅から強豪を使えば、巻き戻し機能なしでも余裕でクリア出来たりもするが、結局チームを育てているんじゃなくて、強いチームを借りているだけでつまらなく感じる。
　しかも勝利に喜んでトイレ休憩でも挟もうものなら、勝手にソフトリセットされるため、ゲームデータが進行しづらい。この不快さが分かるだろうか？


[b]・通信対戦やトレードが出来ないタイトルが含まれ、一部コンプリート不可能かもしれない。[/b]
　カードバトルのタイトルではコンプリートが達成できるのは非常に良いのだが、『バイオモーター・ユニトロン』も主人公キャラの選択によって入手できるパーツが異なるはずだ。

　だから通信機能がコンプリートに恐らく必要なので、このタイトルでコンプリートしたい場合はあきらめるしかないと思う。


[b]・オートセーブのタイミングがおかしく、フリーズが多い為、経過を失いやすい[/b]
　主に追加されたエミュレーター用のメニューを開くとフリーズする事が多い。筆者は50時間プレイした中で、10回前後のフリーズを経験した。

　フリーズが起きるとセーブデータの保存がされない為、小まめにゲーム選択メニュー。最初の起動するタイトルメニューに戻って進行データを保存する必要がある。ちなみに各ゲームのタイトル画面ではない。

　最初のプレイの１時間程度でフリーズしたり、その後数十時間のプレイしてもしなかったりと条件は不明。かなり前のデータに何回も戻されてかなり不快だった為、注意が必要。かなり高い減点項目だと思う。またゲーム保存の方式も分かりにくいのが良くない。下手にゲーム内でセーブせずにリセットされると、セーブが消えてしまう事がどのソフトでもあり得るのも減点要素。


[b]・巻き戻し機能が使いにくい[/b]
　偶に暴発して、記録している最も古いタイミング戻る事があり、少し使い勝手に疑問点が多い。



[h1]●お薦めな点・感想等[/h1]

　まず言いたいのは悪いタイトルじゃないという事だ。ただ復刻タイトルに巻き戻し機能や中断セーブを設けるのであれば、正しく機能して欲しいというのが個人的な感想だ。

　特にフリーズの多発は容認しづらく、正直これさえ修正してくれればお薦めとして評価できる。それくらいには不快度の中で一番高い項目だ。また巻き戻し機能があるのであれば、加速機能も同様に欲しかった。結構待ち時間が多いタイトルが多い。

　ゲームバランスとして、類似ジャンルと比べるとどれもかなり劣っている。そういうことを前提に好きなタイトルがあれば購入するのはありだと思う。しかし悪い点に書いたように不快な表現や、不快な仕様が多いタイトルも多い為、注意が必要。

　ちなみに筆者は『SNK VS. CAPCOM 激突カードファイターズ」と『ポケットテニスカラー』と『ロックマン バトル＆ファイターズ』辺りが楽しく感じた。他は悪い点に挙げたソフト以外はあっさりし過ぎ、パワプロとかの比較的最近のタイトルに慣れていると物足りなさを感じる。楽しめたタイトルも最近の類似ジャンルが飛躍的進化をしていないのも理由かもしれない。

　ちなみにお薦めにしない事にした要因としては、数時間の進行データとセーブデータを失うリスクが高いこと、不快なタイトルの収録、機能がそれほど充実していないのにコストパフォーマンスが悪い点、最近のゲームよりもかなり見劣りするタイトルばかりというのが主な理由。ちなみにコストパフォーマンスは原価基準の為セール時にワンコイン以下になった際はコスパは良くなる。

　正直もう少し軽いエミュレーターを使ってほしかった。というのも下手に3D処理をかけて重めな画面外設定や説明書を演出するという必要のない機能を付けるくらいなら、この辺を軽量化してフリーズを防いでほしかったからだ。他にもオプションやUI・UXの向上も期待したかった。
　それにもしかしたら巻き戻し機能でメモリ占有と処理が複雑化してフリーズしている可能性もある為、クイックセーブ＆ロードを採用した方が良かったかもしれない。

　好きなタイトルがあれば遊ぶことは出来るので、決して購入するなとは言わないし、事実楽しかった。あくまでエミュレーター周りと全体的な評価として、採点が個人的基準を下回ったので形式的にお薦めしないだけ。

　もっと欲を言えば『SNK VS. CAPCOM カードファイターズ2 EXPAND EDITION』も収録して欲しかった。
