The game is broken.

Even in the demo, it was noticeable how little attention was paid to the code and technical aspects of the game, but I hoped those were just demo problems. After all, the game was in development for 3 years; surely, by release, they fixed all the technical issues, right?

Wrong. Touching a bonfire opens the menu after about 5 seconds, and during that time, you can run anywhere and break the game by opening the bonfire menu in places where it's not allowed, including skipping boss fights. After some time, the game goes into slow-mo mode for no apparent reason or purpose, but everything around you slows down several times. However, you speed up and can run faster than a horse. I didn't understand why this happens or how to activate it intentionally, but sometimes when you jump, the game literally changes its physics and breaks.

Pressing the Tab button opens the menu, but pressing it again doesn't close it; you have to close it with the mouse.

The combo attack inputs are broken; I was literally pressing the wrong combos, but the game still registered ones I didn't actually perform.

In many places, you can stand and look through textures, discovering all the game's secrets.

The game has 7 types of resources that drop, and in 2 hours of playing, I genuinely didn't understand what they are for, if every enemy dies from one fist combo and resources aren't consumed.

Moreover, it's unclear why there is even weapons in the game, if fists kill EVERYTHING, and so effectively that it's almost impossible to die while using them.

The horse is a separate meme. I never figured out if it was intended to be so useless or if it's the developers' joke, as they themselves wrote that the horse is not needed to complete the game. And yes, the horse is indeed unnecessary. Furthermore, traveling on horseback is slower than on foot, and its only use is to break the game even more by allowing you to reach places you're not supposed to, thanks to a buggy flying horse.

All the menus are broken. Why does the soup menu have buttons for quitting the game, resetting the location, and going to the main menu? In Souls, the bottom button exits the bonfire menu, and more than once, out of habit, I pressed the bottom button in the menu and fell for it.

Why does pressing the Tab button while viewing armor colors open the combo list?

Why are the weapon equipment menu and the ability/ring equipment menu two different buttons, and why aren't they tabs in the same menu? I literally couldn't figure out how to equip anything until I checked the settings and discovered that the game has THREE EQUIPMENT MENUS: equipment for colors and the horse on Tab, weapon equipment by holding the weapon button, and secondary weapon equipment by holding the secondary weapon button. Seriously, why isn't this one button with a nicely and logically designed menu that would be convenient to use?

Why, if I want to check my weapon upgrades, do I have to equip it, approach a bonfire, wait 5 seconds for the menu to deign to open, open the upgrade menu, see that it opens the combo list, exit the upgrade menu, exit the bonfire, open the combo menu, check the combos, and only then do I have all the information to decide whether I want to upgrade it or not. And what's even more stupid and ridiculous – if you want to do this for another weapon, you have to start over: open the equipment menu (remember, it's not a single key press but holding a button, so it's not instant), select the weapon, equip it, and watch the soup animations again. So much fun.

[*]Maps design is GREAT! This is where the game really shines. I love the art and the secrets of this game, exploration is rewarding in Dead Wells! There are some awesome map reveals where the game really starts to pick up and make you realize its true size, those are the moments I seek in these types of games and they are truly well executed here!
[*]Choices of builds: Zerker (2 handed bastard sword), knight (sword and shield), mage (spells) or gunsman (yay! Shadow Tower Abyss gameplay!)
[*]The more I play, the more I feel this game grow on me. This game, despite its flaws, has really great ideas and a LOT of love put into it. I think its worth getting since its inexpensive, if you're into this type of games (Lunacid, Kingsfield, Shadow Tower, etc), especially now that the dev has announced working on improvement patches on it! Excited to see these improvements in the future!
[*]❤Soup Pot weapon❤

[b]Downsides:[/b]

[*]Bugs. At moments, even though I had a full stamina bar, my attacks were locked. No idea why or how. After spamming block and attack, ends up unlocking, but pretty annoying.
[*]Sound. For "retro feels" reasons, I'm guessing, the cut-scenes and SOME of the sounds go through a bit-crusher effect, as if you were playing through a Commodore Amiga. Doesn't make much sense since everything else is PSX referenced, and even less sense when only SOME of the sound is bit-crushed. It gets annoying quickly because it makes everything really high-pitched and distorted. I would not play this game with earphones. So my suggestion to the dev(s); either make this effect togglable, or tone it WAY the fuck down, because this game isn't going for Commodore Amiga feels. If you wanna go for low-fi, maybe just make the audio low-res like PSX used to have limitations for sound, but lay off the bitcrushing. It's gonna drive me nuts in the long run. For sure.
[*]U.I. needs help. Glad that UI is only like 10-20% of the game's experience, but yikes. Layout should be easier to understand/navigate.
[*]Map progress. There are some areas that are way bigger than others that require switches to be pressed to open a gate. Those are longer runs where, if you're only holding 1 potion (and no Soup Pot), you'll eventually have to run back to a campfire, restore and level up, only to realize that the progress has reset. Perhaps it was because I went to the hub where I can travel to different parts of the maps (never explored it before so I went to check it out), but anyways, once I came back, all the switches had been reset. Which is a little frustrating. The treasure chests were all reset to unopened too, so I doubled all the loot of the map, which feels like something very exploitable.
[*]It's messy. There's a bunch of stuff shown on screen that I do not understand at all. Top right corner shows a bunch of numbers and icons, they go up and down -- what are they? Heck if I know. Absolutely clueless. I have a bunch of stats I can upgrade, it makes other stats go up too. What does it do? I dunno. There should be a reference sheet for this available in the leveling up menu, explaining what each stats affect/do. I don't understand what "Flows" are and I don't know how to upgrade my attack points (if I even can). Picking up new items can sometimes lead up to confusion solely from the text pop up that is sometimes a headache to read through and try to understand. I think there's balancing to do on how much information is given and at what pace. I'm not sure where to go if I want to re-read on something I picked up, because some of it seems to change the gameplay, but I dunno what.
[*]General polishing needed. The state of the game doesn't feel final at all. Short example: Health bar is RED, Stamina bar is GREEN. Health pickups are GREEN and stamina pickups are RED. Why? Simple fix would do the trick!

Dev's really got something good going. I really really hope they look into these issues to make the game even better. I like this game, but I don't LOVE it in its current state. I believe this game could be a 10/10 with enough post-release care! Don't give up yet, dev!!!

Wonder Ball is a 3D platformer where you jump, dash and shoot lightning at robots... and that's about it. There's a good foundation for a game here, but it reeks of being a prototype without properly fleshing out its mechanics, world or characters. What you see is exactly what you get. Nothing more and nothing less.

Pros:
+ Tight controls. Easy to pick up and understand what button does what, and how you use them for things.
+ UI is clean, readable and doesn't interfere with the main gameplay.
+ The dev is a decent programmer, I didn't run into any big problems and the mehcanics are solid.

Cons
- My main issue is that Wonder Ball lacks personality. You should hire an artist, a character designer, or a writer. Somebody who can give this world some actual *character,* because right now Wonder Ball has none. It's just a platformer where you play as a ball, that has these abilities seemingly "just because" and it doesn't even have rolling physics. You could replace this sphere with an actual character with some equipment or a sidekick and you'd have something far more interesting than this. If you're going to make a simple game in this day and age, you have to give it some kind of identifying feature that grabs people right away.
- The lightning attack makes no sense, I don't know why you have it other than to break boxes you can't normally reach, and it having a cooldown meter makes no sense either. If the idea was to limit our combat abilities and just have something to hit enemies with while we pass them (because you cannot dash into them, for some reason), maybe make the combat actually fun, instead.
-The collection radius for your character could stand to be a little bigger. It's very easy to miss stuff you feel like you should have rolled over.
- Hub worlds are barren. Just the same trees and rocks everywhere, and it takes too long to travel between levels. Think Yooka Laylee but much worse.
- No reason to collect all the boxes in a level (it's just more coins and gems you find everywhere anyways) and there are far too many.
- You can't move the camera upwards, so if there are boxes above you, you will not be able to see them.
- No character feedback when you get hit. Your health goes down, but that's it.

It can be fun if you like this kind of game, but there are several things holding it back from being good, and ultimately it's nothing special. 5/10

Fight School Simulator is a hybrid management-and-action experience that attempts to merge the satisfaction of running a martial arts academy with the thrill of stepping into the ring yourself. Developed and published by Queen Developer, the game begins with a simple but appealing premise: you are the master of a fledgling dojo with big aspirations, responsible for both day-to-day operations and the combat reputation of your school. From the earliest moments, it becomes clear that the game wants to strike a balance between hands-on building, strategic planning, and direct physical engagement. You’re not just decorating a gym and passively watching students train—you’re fully invested in shaping them, teaching techniques, and representing your own school when conflicts erupt.

The management layer provides the backbone of progression. You start with modest equipment and a modest space, gradually expanding your facility by placing new training stations, adding utilities, customizing layouts, and upgrading various elements to improve the efficiency and appeal of your dojo. Students arrive with differing abilities, needs, and potential, and part of the game’s charm comes from molding them into fighters who reflect your chosen training philosophy. Whether you want a dojo full of disciplined kick specialists, balanced all-rounders, or unconventional brawlers, the tools available allow for meaningful variation. The financial loop—collecting tuition, investing in gear, maintaining facilities—creates a familiar but rewarding rhythm. However, the depth is lighter than full-scale simulation titles, and seasoned management-sim players may find systems somewhat simplistic after extended play.

Where the game distinguishes itself is in allowing the player to jump directly into combat. You aren’t limited to watching your students fight—you are an active martial artist whose abilities grow alongside the school. Combat involves both melee and ranged options, with new techniques learned through tasks, training sessions, and challenges issued by a Grand Master figure. The movement and attack mechanics favor a slightly arcade-like feel: quick strikes, evasive movement, counters, and the satisfaction of delivering decisive blows. Beyond standard sparring, the world introduces escalating threats—rival schools that challenge your dominance, formal tournaments, and even criminal factions that attempt to intimidate or sabotage your dojo. These encounters give the game a narrative throughline and help break up the pacing between administrative tasks.

The systems are ambitious, but they also reveal the rough edges of an indie production. The dual nature of the game—half management sim, half fighting adventure—results in neither side reaching the complexity of genre leaders. Training cycles, recruitment, and facility maintenance are engaging at first but begin to show repetition as the school grows. Similarly, the combat system, while fun, lacks the depth and precision found in dedicated martial arts or action games. Some players have reported bugs and inconsistencies, such as tasks failing to register or navigation quirks in upgraded school levels. These issues don’t make the game unplayable, but they interrupt immersion and remind you that the experience is built on a smaller-scale foundation.

Despite its limitations, there is a clear enthusiasm behind the design. The developer’s vision of giving players a dynamic dojo life—juggling school reputation, student progress, and street-level challenges—comes through in the game’s structure. When everything aligns, the loop becomes genuinely satisfying: train your students in the morning, negotiate fees and upgrades in the afternoon, and step onto the mat at night to defend your dojo’s honor. Watching your facility grow from a humble training hall into a flourishing academy creates a sense of accomplishment that anchors the game’s progression. The action elements add personality and prevent the experience from feeling too static or overly managerial.

Visually and technically, the game adopts a functional, straightforward approach. Character models, environments, and animations are serviceable rather than striking, but they convey the necessary information clearly. The Unity-based presentation leans toward a clean, slightly stylized look rather than realism. Performance is generally stable, though some users have noted occasional glitches or UI hiccups, particularly on handheld devices like Steam Deck. On standard PC setups, however, the experience remains smooth enough for extended play sessions.

Ultimately, Fight School Simulator succeeds as a niche but engaging blend of two genres. It isn’t deep enough to satisfy players seeking a full management epic, nor refined enough to rival dedicated action combat titles, but it offers a distinct experience that lies somewhere between the two—a space few games explore. For players who like the fantasy of running their own martial arts academy, mentoring fighters, and backing up their teachings with their own fists, the game provides a unique and entertaining route to fulfilling that fantasy. It’s a mid-scale indie project with ambition, personality, and room for refinement, but its core loop is enjoyable enough to make the journey of building and defending your dojo well worth taking.

Max Payne 2 The Fall of Max Payne - это игра в стиле нуарном шутере от 3-его лица. Это продолжение истории Макса Пейна, детектива, который спустя большое время возвращается к работе, но оказывается втянут в смертельный заговор. связанный с роковой женщиной, Моной Сакс. Проиграв в данную игру могу написать что центром внимания становится от части мрачная, также трагическая история любви и предательства. Говоря про трагическую историю любви мы говорим про Макса и Мону когда они встретились спустя большое время в не очень хорошой ситуации, и идя дальше по сюжету мы можем увидеть как Макс переживает за Мону отличным примером это станет Строй площадка когда Уинтерсон выходит со спины наведя оружие на Мону что по итогу получается Макс стреляет в Уинтерсон тем самым спасая себя и Мону хотя и сам падает в яму (От этого как раз момента это и название The Fall of Max Payne это как нехая метафора к личности Макса), Но и по итогу все заканчивается все не очень хорошим концом, Мона погибает от рук Владимира. Играв в игру еще с самого детства она затянула своей гнетущей атмосферой, вечно дождливым Нью-Йорком и постоянным ощущением некой безысходности и фатализма. Так же что все повествования ведутся через меланхоличные внутренние монологи Макса и хорошо сделанные комиксы. Добравшийся до геймплея можно понять что основной механикой игры является Bullet Time (Замедление времени) это уже не просто какой то обычный эффект а уже отьемлемый элемент выживания и тактики. Так же прекрасные динамичные и эффективные перестрелки смотря на это обновленная физика (Ragdoll) делает эпичные и динамичные сражения еще более красочными. Под водя итог могу сказать что Макс Пейн очень трагичная личность которая не может отпустить смерть своей жены и ребенка гнобя себя в этом. Max Payne 2 - это не просто шутер а интерактивный нуар-фильм, она берет лучшие элементы первой части и доводит их до совершентсва, предлагая более зрелый, кинематографичный и трагичный опыт.

I will start off saying that my overall recommendation is mixed:

As someone who really enjoys metroidvania style games as well as action style combat. This game certainly hits both of those check boxes quite well. But it is not a perfect game and i will list my pros-cons-other thoughts below.
Pros -
-Plenty of items find via exploration in the world
-Various environments and platforming challenges
-Combat that allows you to be fairly creative with combos
-Semi-modifiable play style with sigils that allow you to enchance choice of combat method
-Every boss and many enemies give challenges that may force you to change up your style - keeping things varied
-*Biased pro* - a Very NICE soundtrack - One of my absolute favorite music bands have multiple songs in this game and that makes me very happy. The music not tied to said band is also quite good! And i barely found any tracks to be poor in style or to my tastes.

Cons-
-Story feels rushed and many plot points feel unresolved or just pushed aside for the next issue in story line.
-NPCs in towns repeat the same lines throughout the various chapters - offering little to the story or world building.
-The metroidvania aspect feels fairly railroaded - can only explore so much and sometimes the story forces you to leave locations or not allow you back into them until later. 
-Some of the hidden items in exploration are basically impossible to find naturally without a guide or a post game item that gives you a hint an item is in the area. Many require tools you wont get until very late into the game despite looking similar to other obstacles.
-Storyline guidance can be obtuse in some areas - causing confusion on what to do or where to go
-Lack of side quests/objectives outside of some race and combat challenges.
-the game needs more fun non story moments between the characters and story NPCs (there are a couple here and there but many that could use more interactions to build more character investment.

other factors that others may find important-
-The game sports a anime style and includes humanoid people with animal traits, so if you dislike that kind of stuff that may deter you.
-Lack of DLC content - No extra stories and super challenge fights outside of a few within base game.
-The tone of this game is more "dark/edgy" compared to Rabi-Ribi but Tevi does have lighthearted moments too and a sense of humor so its not all edge. If you only want cute and silly stick with the previous game.

All in all - i rate the game a solid 6/10. It kept me entertained well enough and the music kept me motivated to push through many of the toughest fights. Also CC is absolutely adorable and love her design!

[h2] 兔娘！二次元！弹幕！银河城！ [/h2]

对于这款游戏，我是抱了很大期待的。《Rabi-Ribi》可以算是我正式使用steam的入坑游戏了。实际玩下来呢，《TEVI》并不像我想象那般优秀，倒不是说这游戏不好，只是没有达到我的期望，抛开前作滤镜，这款游戏也算是一款可圈可点的良好作品。

[h3] 战斗部分 3.5/5 [/h3]

和前作一样，这作战斗最核心的部分基本都集中在Boss战上，杂兵战基本都很普通没什么可讨论的。核心其一是华丽的，变化莫测的，形式多样的，攻击方式丰富的弹幕是Boss战的特色，我更愿意称其为横版弹幕动作类银河城。核心其二是主角丰富的连招，攻击方式和搓评分打法，就像《鬼泣》一样，在战斗中一边闪转腾挪，一边考虑怎么打出不同连招把评价打上去。结合在一起，这游戏就像回合制一样，Boss发招发弹幕，然后会有一段真空期，玩家就上去各种连招输出。《TEVI》在这部分也是下了很多功夫的，游戏内有足够多的Boss战，Boss战弹幕华丽，变化多端，各有特色。但是本来想给4分的，但是最后考虑还是只给了3.5分，主要是这作难度感觉偏低了，我玩游戏一般都是普通难度开的，但是这作是我开了困难难度依然觉得简单，大部分Boss我都没太摸清楚攻击方式，就靠着硬打莽过去了，我也不是嗑药莽的，就纯靠肌肉临场反应打，可惜了这么华丽的战斗设计了。

[h3] 关卡设计 3.5/5 [/h3]

地图够大，场景够多，地图收集要素非常多，隐藏点够多，是这个游戏关卡设计最大优点了，但是和前作《Rabi-Ribi》的超精彩的关卡设计，N多秘密通道，特殊打法相比，《TEVI》设计太平庸了。地图场景非常多，探索路线看似很多，游戏每个阶段都有很多地区都能去，但实际上都有能力锁限制，你最后还是要按照主线的指引去玩（不过就算有能力锁，能探索一部分捡捡道具啥的也不错）。很多隐藏道具也是能力锁限制获取，强制你后面再来探索（这里就要吐槽下了，这游戏地图标记功能不太便利，图标也少），隐藏道具解谜上感觉有些偷懒，大部分都做得很普通，没有太多难度。这些就是关卡设计上主要掉分的地方了。还有一个有些微妙的地方，就是地图单向通行点太多了，有很多地方你一旦错过了就得绕一大个圈子才能回去，就很烦。

[h3] 装备设计 4/5 [/h3]

这作在徽章设计上更加丰富了，徽章数量非常之多，种类也十分丰富，而且大部分都是技能、连招相关的特殊徽章，不是纯数值向的设计，套路看上去很多，能搭配很多种玩法，让人眼花缭乱。不过数量太多也算是有些缺点了，很多徽章乍看之下根本不知道有什么用，学习成本有些高了，大部分设计有些浮夸，或者难以触发，过多的选择导致有些不会选择了。不过这游戏难度并不算打，按照自己喜欢掉分方式去选择就好，游戏流程也足够长，能给玩家足够的时间去探索。

[h3] 剧情故事 3/5 [/h3]

剧情十分普通，有些二次元游戏剧情的通病，节奏有些奇怪，角色设计有些刻意套模板了，前期有些谜语人，然后后期一股脑信息输出。游戏剧情相比其他银河城游戏，剧情量也算多的了，游戏内有很多设定说明帮助玩家了解游戏世界观，不过应该没几个人能认真看完吧。NPC数量过多，导致大部分角色登场次数有限，戏份不多，塑造也不多，很多角色感觉完全没有存在感，有的角色行为动机就没啥铺垫，感觉就很突然就变成反派了，有些角色噶了也完全伤心不起来。剧情上很多发展都感觉有些奇怪，主角一开始偷了盗贼团的星尘齿轮跑了，按理来说中间会因为这件事和盗贼团发生冲突才对，结果这事就没下文了，盗贼团也不派人来找主角麻烦，盗贼团到了最后才开始正式有戏份；还有一个是主角要去天界找给正太恶魔治疗妹妹的方法，结果去了发现天界根本没有方法，然后立马就被另一件事带走了，此后再也没人提过治疗这件事，太奇怪了，正太恶魔出来就是为了找治疗手段的。这种奇怪的地方不止一处，玩着感觉就很奇怪。不过看在主角团还是很可爱的份上，好歹给个及格分，游戏也基本把事情讲清楚了，虽然不够精彩，但也没啥太掉分的情况，只是很多细节还需要多打磨。

[h3] 美术表现 4/5 [/h3]

画面基本算比较精美的了。所有有点戏份的NPC都是又精美立绘的，各种表情差分也不少，有美女也有帅哥，有御姐也有正太，种类繁多，总有一个合你口味，特别是主角，十分可爱，超级棒。游戏场景相对一般一些，但是游戏场景数量很多，每块区域都是不同风格的场景，虽然达不到优秀，但是基本那个良好是没问题的。作为二次元游戏怎么少得了剧情CG呢，这个游戏CG蛮多，基本都画得很棒，也算是加分项了[strike] 虽然剧情本身不太嘻嘻 [/strike]。其他的UI表现上啊，图标设计啊，这些基本都还不错，看着舒服就行了。

[h3] 游戏音乐 4.5/5 [/h3]

音乐部分是我最满意的部分了，因为游戏场景多，Boss战多，剧情多的原因，游戏内也给每个场景，不同Boss战，不同剧情配置丰富的音乐，音乐丰富而且大部分音乐都挺不错的。这作有很多场景音乐都让我影响深刻，打完游戏后立马找了游戏原声来听了（雪山啊，熔岩区域啊，幻想花园啊我都十分喜欢）。不过Boss战的音乐我倒是没几个有印象的[spoiler] 可能是大部分Boss都是一遍过 [/spoiler]。

[h3] 吐槽一下 [/h3]

First things first: This is not a clasic turn-based rpg, let's just get that clear (I have no idea what that other review is talking about). This is styled very much like those games but there is no character progression, no army/party building, no skills, etc. TBS game maybe, rpg definitely not. 

This is really a puzzle game using some mechanics from tactics style games. Think of it like playing challenge mode in chess games. There is a board setup and you basically have to figure out a strategy to solve it. 

General graphics/audio: Very barebones, you basically get to toggle fullscreen, lighting & shadows (I have no idea why in the hell anybody would turn off lighting and shadows unless they were trying to run this on a rig from 20 years ago), music and sfx. The game is locked to 60fps but I'm not even sure 60 is necessary considering what is happening. 

Story: Somewhat amusing story which I did not expect at all. I don't mean an actual plot because there is barely a story, there aren't really characters and stuff but the overarching narrative basically makes fun of tactics style games. Every couple of centuries sky-people who aren't really sky people go into a world where everybody is getting along and just makes them all fight on these square floating islands for their amusement. It's accompanied with little bits of text at the start of every level that are somewhat amusing. 

Gameplay: Very straightforward tactics-style mechanics thrown into a puzzle. Units move on a grid, they have basic stats and attack stuff, enemies have movement preferences and if you mouse over them it shows exactly where the enemy will go. Some boards have a very specific way to beat and is basically trial and error. Most of the time a wrong move will ruin everything and you gotta restart or hit the turn back button. One mechanic I'd definitely recommend turning off is the one where when enemies attack your units it pauses the game and you have to click for the attack to go through. Since you can't press the turn back button this serves no real purpose, units move  quickly and there's no actual need to see when the enemy attacks, if it does and you didn't know it was coming odds are you f*cked up. 

My main complaint would be the weird difficulty curve(?). With most puzzle games you expect it to start easy and then slowly and consistently ramp up until it is ridiculously hard. With Monstro the difficulty goes up and down, every once in a while you hit a hard level but in between them are levels that are not only much easier but also don't require a specific way to solve (a lot of the easier ones just require you to gather your guys up and wait for the enemy to walk in and get slaughtered). 

Overall: Would recommend as a casual strategy/puzzle game. If you are looking for a new Tactics Ogre/Final Fantasy Tactics then this is definitely not for you unfortunately. There is decent enough value for the money, The first Human wing took me about an hour and there is a monster wing and a ++ wing for both races.

本作的一大特点是男主的大篇幅的心理描写，详细描写了男主的心路历程。不过在后期让人感觉有点拖沓了，回忆的部分其实不需要这么多，心理描写的部分在男主转变之后应该略写或者不写，联系到最后的樱花作战男主还在迷茫，要女主角们来帮助，就让人感觉有点抽象。我知道，在剧情上，男主没法做其他的操作，但这样的演出和节奏毫无疑问是会拉低风评。

A streamlined Majesty-like experience with fun combat AI and satisfying progression for heroes. 

Combat AI is pretty good. Ranged units properly kite enemies instead of just standing still while enemies pound on them. Wizards teleport out of danger (once you unlock the spell). Melee units dodge roll and change position in combat. It's all very fun to watch.

Upgrades are meaningful. Rogues can get backstab damage multipliers and 10X damage against wounded enemies. Archers can get armor piercing arrows. Drakeguards can learn to breathe fire, paladins can learn to passively heal other heroes, warlocks can drain life from their foes, bladedancers can learn to imbue different elements into their swords.

Each guild contributes a unique item to the marketplace for all hero classes to buy and the items have helpful effects like a chance to dodge attacks, do more damage against undead, resist fire damage, add poison or elemental effects to their weapons, etc. A lot of your heroes' power will come from accumulating these accessories. This is in addition to the selection you can unlock in the marketplace such as potions, rings of regeneration, and equipment.

The game comes with a sandbox mode that generates a random map, as well as a survival-style sandbox mode where enemies get stronger. It also has a small selection of handmade scenarios to challenge you.

Feels pretty polished so far, with only a few minor bugs and some balancing issues like the scaling of building prices that can be easily remedied.

The experience is very streamlined compared to Majesty. Tax collectors have been replaced with passive income and a cut of marketplace sales. There are no builder units, just passive regeneration on buildings and a Repair spell that can fix them in a jiffy. Buildings are built instantly and heroes are recruited instantly with no timers or build animations. I didn't mind, but some players may be looking for a more immersive simulation experience.

There's also no exploration flags, only attack flags, but this is compensated for by the heroes exploring actively in their downtime.

As someone that has been playing the original Majesty for years, this scratches the itch of recruiting heroes, helping them get stronger and slowly conquering the map from the enemy. Highly recommended to Majesty fans. The screenshots don't do it justice, I would try the demo to get a good feel for it.

众多大佬已经把AIR分析烂了，感觉我怎么写都是在献芹，但又忍不住。观铃是我最喜欢的角色之一，《AIR》是我最喜欢的番剧和游戏之一，这篇文章也是我写的最久的一篇。此文仅是我与往人、观铃、晴子和小空共同的“夏之记录”，刍荛之见，各位不吝赐教。

[h2] AIR的三重枷锁[/h2]

[h3] 情感的淡化[/h3]

人与人情感的联结，再怎么紧密，过了一代直接砍大半。或许你还记得童年时的玩伴，或许你还记得亲戚家的小孩。然而长大后还保持联系的能有多少？即使是同一代人，若不常联系，情感也会被时光冲淡。而到我们的下一代、再下代，甚至可能形同陌路。

我们亲身体验了AIR，也许被其故事深深吸引。AIR能短时给我们鼓舞，振奋人心，但过几天呢？再过几个月呢？再过几年可能连剧情都忘记了。剧情再丰富，情感再真切，散发的光芒再耀眼，也终将会随时间变黯淡。

[h3]抽象与具体[/h3]

越容易传播，越失去血肉；越拥有温度，越难逃消亡。可歌可泣的故事即使被记载，但也很难被共情。翼人的故事传到往人这一代，已经简化为“天空中的女孩”“悲伤”“翅膀”等抽象的概念和符号。女孩是谁？为什么悲伤？我需要怎么做？往人一概不知，又何谈拯救？
仅强调宏大而抽象的历史、集体，忽略个性，最终受伤的是渺小的个体。朝廷说翼人是为国家而战，实则是被迫成为战争机器；就连柳也，最初的守护者，连让神奈的“真实”在历史的画卷中留下一笔都无法做到，他用尽最后的生命火光所编写的《翼人传》最终也杳无音信。在历史巨浪中，个体穷尽一生所激起的浪花刹那间便会烟消云散。

[h3] 传承的诅咒[/h3]

传承下来的，便对么？翼人从承载梦想与希望的种族，变为厄运、痛苦和诅咒的源头，他们每一代的转生者都要经历无数悲伤的梦，最终在孤独中死去。这份被诅咒的传承，是否应该重新审视？而即使是现实，当今时代，都仍有多少陋习、文化糟粕？
不仅如此，当传承和当前的幸福冲突了又怎么办？值得传承的东西，应该牺牲当下的幸福去传承？如果要牺牲个人的幸福才能拯救世界，换作是你，你愿意吗？

[h1] 如何打破枷锁？[/h1]

这三个问题，我会倒着回答，因为AIR的终点也是起点。

[h3]  以幸福为利刃，斩断诅咒重铸传承[/h3] 

面对诅咒，往人母亲给出了最温柔又最锋利的答案：

> “我不想强迫你去做这件事。你要找到属于你自己的幸福。因为人活着，就是为了寻找自己的幸福。想要如何使用它，都是你的自由。单纯操控它来赚钱也可以。不再旅行也可以，把人偶丢掉也可以。忘记天空中的女孩，继续自己的生活也可以。”

不道德绑架，不强迫传承。往人的母亲教会我们，如果是以牺牲自己的幸福为代价，这种传承不要也罢。

主动选择，重新定义传承。传承幸福也是一种传承。我们歌颂勇敢与正义，我们赞扬温柔与善良，我们将其汇聚成属于自己的幸福，再把幸福传递下去。

[h3]  以心灵为箭矢，贯穿迷雾抵达真实[/h3] 

历史是死的，人是活的。与其拯救虚无缥缈的传说，不如珍惜现在，守护好眼前的人。

观铃虽然笨拙，但吃苦耐劳，做饭扫地洗衣服从无怨言；

观铃虽然学习成绩不好，还老是逃课，但是她还机智地选择课间再偷偷进去（好孩子不要学）；

观铃虽然每次一遇到麻烦，就“みすずチン、ピンチ！（观铃亲，大危机！）”，但也会努力鼓励自己：“观铃亲，fight！”“みすずは強い子（观铃是坚强的孩子）”。

往人刚遇到观铃时还嫌烦，在日常相处过程中，才逐渐发现，这个会犯蠢、会平地摔，却依然用“nia哈哈”面对苦难的普通女孩竟如此生动和具体。往人最后的愿望也不再是打破轮回、终结宿命等宏大议题，仅仅只想回到第一次见面的时候，再真心实意陪伴一次观铃。

> “我哪里都不会再去了，我要和你待在一起，看你露出笑容我就非常幸福。可以的话我想从和她相遇的时候开始重新来过，然后这次一定要……一直和观铃……”

而对晴子来说，观铃是什么？起初，观铃是一种强行赋予的、抽象的责任。晴子既不知如何将抽象的责任转化为具体的爱，也害怕“过家家”般的母女之情终会消散，只能靠疏离来逃避抽象的责任和注定离别的悲伤。这十几年的相处如同囚禁她们二人的镜像监牢，既不能逃脱，也不能相见，只能隔网相望。观铃每一次“嘎哦”和“nia哈哈”都是对晴子精神的凌迟。

然而，十多年来，观铃的一个人玩扑克、一个人喝“奇怪果汁”开始在晴子心中化为箭矢。随着往人出现，这支箭彻底打造完成。与其害怕离别而推开，与其害怕责任而逃避，不如用真心实意对抗虚假迷雾，即使下跪10天又如何，晴子誓必亲手用心灵之箭射穿这监牢，将爱意传达，与眼前这个真实的女儿紧紧相拥。所有迟到但并未缺席的爱最终凝聚成那声“妈妈”，这既是对晴子的最高的回应，也是给晴子最深刻的救赎。晴子：

> “教会了我怎么和别人一起生活下去……不就是你教会了又傻又没用的我吗……教会了那个只懂得靠喝酒寻找幸福的我吗……你教会了我和家人一起度过每一天的意义……”

[h3] 以愿望为羽翼，划破苍穹传递希望[/h3] 

往人：

> “你接下来不要记做过的事，而是要写想做的事。”

观铃：

> “我很庆幸自己努力过了。虽然有时也很痛苦，很难过....但是真的很庆幸自己努力过。因为在终点.....伴随着幸福。”

面对必死终局，观铃积极面对，没有放弃。无论结局如何，自己努力的过程是有意义的，死而无憾。

终点虽是肉体的终点，但也是幸福所在。所以，即使观铃肉体死亡，纵使我们体验AIR之后的感动消散又如何？观铃努力的精神、承载的梦想由玩家来传承。只要我们没有遗忘AIR，只要未来还有人愿意了解AIR，无论过去多久，AIR都一直是我们心中的天空，抬头便能望见，即使遥远，也依然有力量照亮我们心中的大地。

[h2]  打破枷锁，迎接胜利[/h2] 

观铃在前往Goal途中，用尽最后力气比了三个“V”。一个送给往人，是携手往人斩断诅咒的“胜利”；一个送给晴子，是伴随母亲从抽象责任到具体之爱的“胜利”；一个送给自己，是观铃展翅冲破云霄，让鸟的歌声响彻青空的“胜利”。

If you are expecting a true garden simulator or a game with an interesting story, then you will be quite disappointed on both counts I'm afraid. However, if you are one of those people who likes to take the barest hints of story and setting and weave your own tale from them then there's hope. I don't know if there's a way to win this game or not, though I'm pretty sure there isn't. There's a story mode and an endless mode which implies that the story mode does reach a conclusion at some point, however after the 2.5 hour mark (roughly) you're pretty much guaranteed to fail no matter what you do. 

For me, the true entertainment in this game came from figuring out how to cheat the system in humorous ways. For example, in order to progress in the game you have to continue to buy and send bowls of fruit to the village. In order to do that you must make money. In order to do that you must grow fruit. In order to do that you must either continuously hit a wooden platform with a pair of mallets (I'm telling you this because the game doesn't, so you're welcome one person who's ever going to read this review), or buy an auto clicker to click the platform for you (at a much slower rate than you can do it yourself). It's simple enough until you realize that inflation is no joke in this village's economy. That's when you either fail repeatedly, wave your arms until they fall off and still fail repeatedly, or start discovering the way to cheat the system. Turns out, you can attach as many planters as you want to one auto-clicker as long as the planters aren't touching one another. This makes it unnecessary to grow any fruit yourself and you can pretty much just sit at the bottom of your cave doing nothing but occasionally buying absurdly overpriced fruit bowls until you feel like you've got your money's worth of this game.

The voice actor for the guy who drops you little updates over the intercom is pretty good and the "village gossip" tidbits are interesting at first, so if you've read the essay above and are still eager to save an entire village from starvation single handedly by simply waving your hands like a madwoman for a couple minutes and then just sitting on your ass then, by all means spend your money!

I have mixed feelings about this game. There is some serious disbalance of difficulty in levels or even parts of levels. Some feel too easy, other are just stupidly difficult. I was playing on hard and got an achievement for finishing it on hard, which only a bit more than 1% has (and overall the game was finished by something like 20%, which also is quite low). There are sections that are just poorly designed, especially when they throw dozens of enemies all of which can and will shoot you in a head the second you put your nose out of cover. But there are other sections, where very similar combat situations somehow play much easier. As if enemies have different accuracy depending on a level. It took me really long to be patient enough and go through the harder encounters and I'm not really sure if it was worth it.

The beginning of the game is very weak, probably the worst of it, so don't judge too quickly, it gets better. But the last 2 levels (or maybe 3) weren't bringing much new and had all the issues mentioned above.

The graphics are quite dated too, although definitely not the worst and there are some interiors that are actually very well crafted. 

The main aspect, of course, is the gunplay and it's actually quite decent. Weapon handling is fun and headshots are satisfying (although sometimes animations and/or hit registration make it look stupid) and there are sections which felt really cool as a good old shooting gallery, but this time in VR. There are some other short sections of using heavy machine guns on planes and stuff like that, mostly not fun, but some actually were.

Overall it feels more like a tech demo. They clearly didn't get enough time to balance it all out, keep parts that work well and remove those that don't, so instead we get this crazy mixture as if different levels of the game were developed by entirely different teams.

I'm not going to bother even criticizing the story, it's just terribly bad. But then again, it kinda doesn't get in the way too much, and the game would definitely be worse without it, so yeah, at least we have some story going. But don't expect any memorable/likeable characters or any realistic dialogues. 

Worth mentioning is the game size of around 200GB, most of which is apparently spent not on the game itself, but on some MOV short documentaries and 360 degrees footage of some places from WW2. It was actually interesting to watch, but it's nothing special either.

The only reason I would give it a thumbs up is that there are very few realistic WW2 shooters with a story for VR, so surprisingly this game is actually a rare type in this format for some reason. If you want a shooting gallery it's probably one of the best ones on VR in general. But we should push for better quality of VR games (especially PCVR), not dumb down the acceptance criteria because of this scarcity. 

So no recommendation from me here and I hope the devs will do better next time.

プレイフィールはローグライクと言うより、普通のアクションRPGに近い。
・地道なプレイで経験値が溜まってレベルが上がり、拠点で永続パワーアップが得られる。
・各ステージにある飯屋での食事で基礎ステータスが上昇する（その冒険中は永続、重ねがけ可）
・レアな武器は単純に強いから強い。
これらの要素で地味ぃ～に攻撃力を上げて敵殲滅を早め、HPや防御力を伸ばして死ににくくする。各ステータスの意味を理解する必要はあるが、基本的に大きい数字の力でゴリ押しするゲームであり（普通にクリアするだけなら）アクションの腕前はあまり要求されない為、カジュアルに遊べると言える。

反面、装備枠が限られているため、使用アイテムは厳選する必要があり、別々の周回でも最終装備が似通った物になりやすい。ネタ武器やロマン武器も多く用意されてるが、クリアだけを目指すなら、これらの出番は殆ど無いのが残念である。そして装備枠が限られてる以上、集めたアイテムの能力が全て反映されるわけではないため「うはｗｗｗあの変な能力と、この頭おかしい武器がシナジーして無双になったｗｗｗｗ」状態がおきにくい（あることはある）そういう意味で「ローグライクらしいゲーム」を求めているなら本作は不向きと言える。

なお、↑上記はゲーム中盤以降の話であり、序盤は少し事情が異なる。
初期状態だと1～3体目のボスがちょっと強すぎるのだ。真面目にアクションゲームの反射神経で乗り越えるか、強力なレア武器を手に入れるまで死亡を繰り返すガチャゲーに頼ろう。中盤のボスを超えた辺りで「銃」カテゴリの武器や、衣装（≒キャラクターチェンジ）要素がアンロックされて、ゲーム全体がグッと楽になる。

過去レビューによると、相当バランスが悪かった時期もあったようだが、現在（2025年）では2023年の最終パッチによって快適にプレイできるようになっている。少なくとも私自身は不便を感じなかった。なお過去の攻略では最強とされた「ソルベオの血」が現在ではナーフされてる事には注意されたし。

Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night is a solid Igavania, crafted by the man himself, and it wears that legacy proudly. The map design, soundtrack, and progression all hit the right nostalgic notes, and it absolutely feels like the spiritual successor to Symphony of the Night we’ve been begging for. The problem is, it just doesn’t quite sing like the old days.

Miriam is fine, but she’s no Alucard. The story is campy even by Castlevania standards, the dialogue feels like it was written during a sugar rush, and the game has more jank than a flea market laptop. It’s fun, don’t get me wrong, but between the floaty combat, weird pacing, and occasionally ugly visuals, it’s hard not to wish it had a little more polish and soul.

As for people whining that it’s too easy, that’s on you. Nobody’s forcing you to use the busted shards or the overpowered weapons. You made your own easy mode. Go swing a knife and suffer like the rest of us.

Despite the rough edges, it’s a damn respectable effort. It’s not Symphony of the Night 2, but it is a decent "Spiritual Successor" (God they loved that term in the Peak Kickstarter Era, didn't they?) closer to the DS Castlevanias, maybe even a bit below them. Still, it’s stylish, playable, and dripping with charm where it counts.

Verdict:
Janky, and occasionally goofy, but still worth playing for diehard Castlevania fans. 
7.5/10  not quite a symphony, but definitely a solid composition (although perhaps not as much of an earworm as we had hoped after so long.)

En effet, il m'a posé certaines difficultés autant au niveau de la compréhension de l'histoire (peut être due à mon vocabulaire Anglais pas assez étendu dans les thèmes abordés), qu'à mon exploration des différentes scènes de l'environnement où les chemins possibles ne sont pas tracés et donc pas des plus intuitifs, sans oublier les puzzles qui nécessitent une certaine aisance en ce qui concerne la logique, les mathématiques ou encore retranscrire des notes de musique sur un piano.

La toute première chose qui émane de ce jeu est que l'on ne vous prendra pas par la main pour vous guider, vous devrez vous triturer les méninges et composer avec ce que vous voyez à l'écran ainsi qu'avec les notes recueillies, ou votre sens de la déduction, et il en va de même pour certains succès à débloquer.

Pour ce qui est de l'histoire, vous incarnez (enfin je crois) une petite fille brune perdue dans des bois sinistres où des obstacles épineux vous barrent la route... Les premières énigmes vous attendent d'entrée de jeu jusqu'à ce que vous rencontriez une autre petite fille blonde et atterrissez dans sa famille qui est pour le moins étrange.
L'histoire et l'ambiance (aussi bien visuelle que musicale) sont troublantes.

Les deux fins diffèrent légèrement, les objets collectés ou non m'ont semblé avoir un impact sur le dénouement.
Il faudra 2 parties distinctes pour débloquer tous les succès. 
Le jeu peut se terminer en quelques heures (surtout lorsque l'on bute sévèrement sur les puzzles) ou en quelques minutes (après avoir compris comment débloquer certains succès) [spoiler] si l'on va droit à l'essentiel. [/spoiler]

Pour conclure j'y ai apprécié l'ambiance et la patte graphique, mais j'ai pesté sur les énigmes que je n'ai pas su résoudre seule, et j'ai eu du mal à suivre l'histoire avec ces notes (qui sont ces gens ? Des Illuminatis, des parents éplorés devenus fous ? ou de dangereux psychopathes ? ou alors des entités errantes qui n'auraient pas su trouver la paix ? Bonne question.

A prendre en promo pour ceux qui aiment utiliser leurs cellules grises.

Okay so I gave up on Story Mode. There were just too many places where the game would crash or get stuck and I got sick of having to ALT TAB out so that I could manually close the game down.

Then I decided to try my hand at the Survival Mode. I did not have to play very long before I was annoyed by some of the developer's terrible decisions. The setting of the game is that you are trying to survive in a place that obviously had humans living in it back in the 1800s. You will find old run down remnants of buildings, old wagons, blocked entrances to old mines and things like that.

Unfortunately what you will also find are invisible walls preventing you get to areas that the developers did not want you to go but they did not have the foresight to create something to block your path. You will also find plenty of buildings that would make perfectly good bases for your first few days of survival that you cannot use because the developers have made them boarded up. So despite the fact that they look like they were boarded up a century ago and you have an axe, you cannot get into them.

I found a wooden chest that looked like it could contain stuff but you cannot open it because it has a rope tied around it. I have both an axe and a knife but no the developers chose to fill this game with objects that should be interactable but which are just garnish. This game is filled with garnish. The things that you find that are not garnish do not make sense. I found an old destroyed building with a broken western style horse drawn wagon in it. In the back of it I found two bottles of anti psychotic pills and a box of Valium tablets.........in a building that existed way before the invention of Valium and before psychopathy was even a recognized condition, let alone had medication to cope with it.

This is one of those pretty games with very poor mechanics and ridiculous ideas, created by developers who took way too many shortcuts. If you could take the graphics of this game and put them on The Long Dark, a real survival game, then you would have an awesome game. 

If you like the look of this game because of the survival aspects of it then do yourself a favour and go buy The Long Dark. Thank god I got this while it was on sale.

I want to start off with saying that I am a huge fan of Roboquest. It’s easily one of the best rogue-likes I’ve ever played. So, it must be a little jarring to see me leaving a review of not recommending this VR port.

My main complaint is lack of binding controls. At the moment it’s a little rough to get into this game if you require certain inputs to be bound in your preferred control scheme. The default controls aren’t so good. Important inputs such as jump and crouch bound to joystick will always be a minus for me. 

Aiming. Very rough. You have some control of where the gun is positioned on the Y axis in settings but the X axis is fixed in such a way that is slightly off angle. I love the implementation of adjusting your gun axis to be more comfortable for the user but I’m confused as to why it’s only on one axis of adjustment. 

Throwing. Holy… throwing in VR is never fun but this really makes a rough mechanic in VR even worse. You’d think throwing would be natural in VR considering the peripheral’s capabilities but it’s actually quite hard to throw accurately in VR due to several factors. One of the biggest limiting factors is tracking of headsets. In this case, if your using a Quest your going to find it a bit rough to throw accurately as you can’t reach behind your back without losing tracking.

Lack of leaning into the platform. This game sticks too close to the desktop version of the game and I would’ve loved to see things lean into VR as a platform more. This lack of commitment detracts from the VR port as opposed to the desktop version. I wouldn’t be able to recommend this game for VR when I know the desktop version is objectively better in every way. There isn’t anything added that makes the VR version better than the desktop versions. 

It’s just Roboquest, but more expensive and in Vr. 

Not 

Roboquest but helped by VR and pushed to the next level. 

But all hope is not lost. The devs need to cook a little longer on this and as a Roboquest fan I am anxiously awaiting the next couple of updates to see what they are bringing to the table. I’m assuming they meant to release this in early access as even the released version isn’t a “1.0” version. It’s clear they ran out of time. 

The lack of multiplayer on release is a bit disappointing but I’m hoping they can have customizable bindings and multiplayer soon. If these two things can be done it’ll go a long way to improve my opinion of this vr port.

In the meanwhile if people ask me which version they should pickup I will have to point them towards the desktop version of the game for now until the VR version is finished.

You can also customize your car, record replays and export your time as a file so that other people can race against your ghost.

Now, about performance, it is amazing. I get over 500 FPS with uncapped FPS playing the game on the highest graphics settings, but that may just be because I have a beefy PC.

I would 100% recommend this game to anyone who likes racing games. 

One more thing I would like to say, is that this game works perfectly with Linux using Proton Experimental, in my experience. It is also rated Platinum on ProtonDB, so that is nice too.

Vor zwei Tagen im Sale gekauft mit 50 % Preisnachlass und dafür ist es wirklich ein nettes kleines Aufbaugame, welches sich noch im Early Access befindet (seit einem Jahr) aber schon mehrere größere Updates erhalten hat.

Man startet - bestenfalls im Coop - mit einer kleinen Zwergenstation, sucht Holz und Erze und baut nach und nach Technik und Ausrüstung auf. Die Kämpfe gegen Wildschweine, Orks und anderes Gesocks sind ziemlich hölzern, da die Gegner halt dann doch etwas Pech beim Denken zu haben scheinen. Im Grunde ist das aber auch nur Beiwerk, denn im Grunde geht es natürlich eher um das Entdecken der Welt und den Aufbau seiner Basis.

Hierfür gilt es nach und nach neue Maschinen freizuschalten, sodass man nach kurzer Zeit nicht mehr händisch Erze farmen muss, sondern dampfbetriebene Maschinen dafür einsetzen kann. Damit die funktionieren braucht es natürlich Kohle. Also suchen und eine kleine Produktion aufbauen. Und so setzt es sich Stunde um Stunde fort.

Grafisch dürfte das Game auch auf schwächeren Systemen laufen, denn Texturen und so sind eher ein Fremdwort. Es kommt da bei Weitem nicht an Enshrouded oder Satisfactory oder so heran, muss es aber auch nicht. Auf nexusmod gibt es ein Reshade-Preset für das Game, welches das Spiel in seiner visuellen Qualität deutlich verbessert (schärfer und kontrastreichere Farben) und ist absolut zu empfehlen.

Wir haben es heute erstmals im Coop gezockt und hatten Spaß dabei, auch wenn die Bedienung manchmal etwas fummelig ist, wenn man sich nach unten in eine Höhle baut.

Toll sind die zahlreichen Bauelemente, ob Holz, ob Stein, Fenster, Türen und so weiter, da ist ne Menge dabei, um der Basis die persönliche Note zu verpassen.

Fans des Genres können und sollten bedenkenlos zugreifen!

游戏美术、音乐和交互逻辑没什么毛病，在我这里算加分项。主要来讲讲这个自走棋构筑的问题：

先说结论，作为肉鸽游戏，数值平衡失败，单局体验同质化严重，主要原因如下：
1.单局游戏中，随机单位出现顺序、随机宝石抽取、随机事件、随机饰品对玩法并无显著影响，甚至可以说约等于无；
2.大多数角色升级，技能倍率无显著提升，仅有攻击力1->1.5->3的倍率提升，物抗魔抗及血量提升；
3.然而本游戏辅助根本不吃攻击力，升级某些辅助对阵容提升几乎没有帮助（基本为了提升一击线）；
4.合成金星单位获得的宝珠强度大多平平无奇，有些与角色甚至没有联动；
5.高等级羁绊基本无质变，仅有数值的线性提升；
6.游戏不同阵容差距显著，游戏存在物伤、法伤、技能伤、dot伤，上述伤害可以复合。平A只有物伤，而本游的逆天平A拐：宝石雷霆黄玉、逆天物伤拐：升星技能倍率几乎翻倍的桂榴石，完爆其它所有伤害拐；
7.游戏爆伤无视双抗，收益显著。然而提升暴击率只有两种方法，使用宝石天使之石直接提升暴击率，或者提升速度（速度直接影响暴击率），然而游戏提升速度手段相当有限，这使得单位红宝（金星宝珠+30速）强度飙升。

综上所述，我们得到了一套逻辑自洽的完美公式，红宝+玉髓+桂榴石+雷霆黄玉，强度全程在线，满配红宝两脚踹出9999*2极其残忍。几乎所有金卡的强度与这套1蓝卡+2白卡的组合相比都相形见绌（游戏的金卡合金星极为困难，基本配合流浪宝珠商店+提升金卡出率的香水+变形虫可以正常食用），于是地牢之旅就变成公公又式式的三人行+可有可无的前排。

游戏其余伤害类型衍生的流派素质欠佳，不仅联动困难而且养成难度更高，过渡绝对称不上丝滑（受卡得要死的经济系统限制，点名丰收之角）。

最后再提一些小建议：
1.联机站位受限，1p固定奇数位2p固定偶数位，站位调整困难，建议直接改为自由站位；
2.局内事件可以设计得更大胆，对玩法有冲击；
3.贴纸更换事件设置为常驻1次；
4.优化中文翻译文本，明确效果对象；
5.诸君，我喜欢大数字。

Внимание! Я поставил Heavy Memories позитивную оценку в первую очередь как произведению искусства - экспериментальной "не-игре" об отчаянии и бесконечной фрустрации, которую практически невозможно пройти до конца без усиленного абьюза эксплойтов (вроде "Alt+F4 в опасной ситуации") или прямого вмешательства в ее код. Если вы ищете "просто игру на пару вечеров", проходите мимо: HM можно порекомендовать либо поклонникам необычных геймдизайнерских решений (как пародию на "игры про войну"), либо самым безумным хардкорщикам, готовым потратить десятки часов на попытки пройти маленькую, но крайне строптивую инди-разработку.

Heavy Memories - пример "анти-игры", которая знакомит игрока с элементарными правилами и геймплейными механиками, а затем ставит его в настолько невыносимые условия, что пройти ее даже до середины смогут немногие. И речь здесь не о "сложном, но справедливом" геймплее - речь о намеренно завышенном количестве мощных противников при остром недостатке аптечек.

Схожий прием использовался в NAM (1998) от TeamTNT, концепция которой была близка Heavy Memories, только терпеть ее было немного проще благодаря возможности сохраняться после каждого убитого вражеского солдата. HM суровее: это вольный римейк Battle City с обширными картами, в которых одинокий танчик противостоит десяткам оппонентов. Четыре попадания - минус одна "жизнь" и откат к началу уровня; израсходованы все "жизни" - прогресс теряется, а игра начинается с самого первого уровня (на старте есть три попытки; дополнительные изредка выпадают из уничтоженных врагов наряду с прочими бонусами). При этом каждая из вражеских машин также гибнет с четырех попаданий (оставляя каркас, на уничтожение которого для получения бонуса требуется еще один выстрел), их поведение непредсказуемо, а карты ими просто кишат. Изредка встречаемые "точки ремонта", во-первых, обычно целиком спрятаны за разрушаемыми стенами без намека на свое присутствие, а во-вторых восстанавливают "здоровье" танка лишь при первом использовании (по факту, это одноразовые аптечки).

Как будто этого мало, многие схватки происходят ночью: игрок видит противников в радиусе кольца света вокруг танка и ламп, но ничто не спасет его от пули, прилетевшей из темного угла карты. И, чтобы разнообразить причины Game Over'а, в проект добавлены мины да статичные огневые точки, стреляющие теми же снарядами, что вражеские танки.

По итогу: сохраняться здесь нельзя, израсходование всех жизней обнуляет сейвфайл, и дотерпеть даже до финала третьего уровня (из десяти) - это уже челлендж. Да, здесь все еще можно исхитриться и выйти из игры до того, как ваш танк уничтожат на последней попытке (тогда уже завершенные уровни не придется проходить заново), но это эксплойт, который лишь смазывает впечатления игрока от проекта. Ибо, судя по левел-дизайну и общему упадническому настроению HM, игрок здесь должен страдать - как на настоящей войне. Ибо на войне нет ни "справедливости", ни "правил", ни "баланса"; более того - чем чаще вы попадаете на поле боя, тем ниже вероятность, что вы увидите ее "концовку". В идеале после первого поражения HM вообще должна была бы удалять себя с компьютера и блочить возможность повторного запуска: как говорит танкист с экрана Game Over'а, "Что сгорело, то не вернуть".

И это действительно крутой арт-хаусный концепт - правда, как и в случае с NAM, на практике играть в него оказывается просто невыносимо (или еще невыносимее - там сохранность прогресса зависела от самого геймера, а HM оставляет его ни с чем после пары ошибок). Окончательно деморализовать игрока призваны ачивки в духе "попасть снарядом в 100 летящих вражеских снарядов", "уничтожить 500 вражеских танков" и "взорвать 1000 бочек" - на фоне сюжета о перебинтованном танкисте, который не может успокоиться без постоянных инъекций от врача из лазарета, работают они на "отлично".

При этом играть в HM все еще веселее, чем в тот же NAM - цветовая палитра не утомляет однообразием, карты действительно интересно исследовать, а геймплей кажется "честнее", чем в детище Team TNT (эти обстоятельства и повлияли на выставление позитивной оценки). I had beaten Blue Fire a while back and saw this new expansion that was also a stand alone game, and I have to say, at the low low price of FREE, you just won't find a 3D platformer of this caliber anywhere. 

I could go on about the actual Blue Fire game, but let me just speak about the stand alone Void Maker game, since that’s why you’re here. Sit back and settle in, this one meets the word count for that 6th grade English final. 


PROS:

The character movement. Controlling the character just feels fun. It feels as good as if Super Meat Boy finally got made into a good 3D platformer. Quick, snappy, very responsive, and easy to control the character with a high skill ceiling but easy to pick up intuitively. Genuinely the best 3D platformer character-controller I’ve seen from an indie developer. Hat in Time feels sluggish and uninspired compared to this. Void Maker can stand on its own separate from the main game with no story or progression due to this movement, it feels that good. 

A very in depth level creator that I admittedly have not sunk my teeth into as much as I should, though it is extensive and very powerful. Like Mario Maker but 3D and very expansive. It is a straight up way to practice 3D level design on the scale of nearly making your own game in a user friendly way. It has the ability to create levels with even metroidvania style elements, where as you progress you unlock the various movement mechanics and unlock the next challenge. Or just start with everything and fly through the pure platforming challenges. I’ve dabbled with it and it definitely seems like it will let you create nearly exactly what you want, and anything not in the game yet has the potential to be added due to the….

Developers support and engage with their player base. There is an active discord that you can join from the home screen. The community is small right now from what I’ve seen but definitely has the room for competition.

It looks good. This is a personal preference but the game looks great. It’s no AAA Unreal 5 rendered game, but it has a simple beauty that also clearly conveys through color and art the information the player needs to intuit the meaning of unknown objects. Big red spikey thing? Prob gunna kill me.

The music is great. Again, preference here, but it has a calming atmospheric lost-soul sort of vibe to it. Makes me feel nostalgic, which I like when I’m playing a modern old school 3D platformer 

User generated content. I keep coming back daily and finding new levels to play. Not all are the best, just like with Mario Maker, but honestly there are some gems. And beating a level with .45% completion rate and getting a world record is SATISFYING. 

The devs are still supporting it. The last update listed on their Discord was 5 days ago. They are committed to this and I don’t see this passionate team stopping until this expansion is as polished as can be. 


CONS:

The current menus for the Browsing Levels in the game are very bare bones and a bit buggy. I have gotten a few records that did not show the next time I logged in on the stages I got the records on. 

There is no Personal Stat screen or character screen. Skins to unlock or customization, or even just a personal page that tells you stats like all deaths and all the levels you’ve cleared would be great. Like in Halo, everyone loves their Service Record. 

The community is small. There are not, at the time of writing, too many content creators for the game. Both creating content like on YouTube and creating Maps. There are a handful of very good level designers though. I personally have not found the content list to be small enough to complain though it could be an issue if you get super addicted.

Unless you’ve played Blue Fire and memorized the icons, you won’t know what powers you are starting a level with. Currently, how this is shown is by listing the icons of the items that grant movement abilities, and highlighting the ones that active. This doesn’t convey to you what they do unless you already know their meaning. That being said, 7 seconds of pressing buttons fixes that. Still this could be fixed with the next point… 

No tutorial level. This is a free game, not every player will have an understanding of how Blue Fire works as many are coming here to try out BF before buying the main game. I personally would not have thought that my third jump came from holding and charging the Attack button to get a spin attack in air, but it is vital to know this for several of the player made levels. 


This is clearly an early version of the Void Maker game but my god is it so worth your time. It is one of the only games I can pick up and just spend 10 minutes trying a level or 3 hours playing on accident. The actual game is smooth and mostly bug free. The user interface outside of the game play could use some polish but I would be shocked if any of my concerns are even valid in a few months with how fast they are updating and patching the game. 

I love indie games, and this one takes the cake as the most fun free one I’ve played on Steam. It’s criminal that it is not more widely known.  

For the low low price of FREE, just get the game and make your friends play it and beat their scores.

Beneath the Cherry Trees CTRL+C/CTRL+V/ 桜の樹の下には   è...Non lo so!

Onestamente non è un gioco, non è una visual novel. Sinceramente facevano prima a metterlo come video sul tubo. 

Anche se è solo una dimostrazione tecnica delle potenzialità del software AIRNovel, direi che è una pessima dimostrazione. Il gioco ha una risoluzione non adattabile sui monitor 16:9 (quelli del portatile per intenderci), dura manco 10 minuti con un pessimo inglese. 


L'ho giocato perché era gratuito, se fosse stato a pagamento, sarebbe stato il gioco dove avrei richiesto il rimborso per la prima volta.

p.s. Ho impiegato più tempo a scrivere questa recensione che a completare il gioco.

¡Bajo los cerezos hay cadáveres enterrados! 

Así es como empieza esta obra de poesía literaria centrada en el poema "Beneath The Cherry Trees (1928)" de Motojirō Kajii, el cual se centra en la belleza de los cerezos cuando florecen, aunque lo hace de una forma bastante "peculiar", por no decir directamente que es perturbadora a más no poder.

Esta visual novel es muy corta, y cuando digo que es corta es que dura 5 minutos y gracias. Tal y como se comenta en la descripción la hicieron para demostrar la capacidad del motor con la que se ha realizado, el AIRNovel, así que no buscaban profundizar y crear una visual novel al uso.

A nivel artístico cumple. Los paisajes son bonitos, de estilo fotorrealista y el script de la joven chica que aparece está bien diseñado y lleno de detalles, sobretodo teniendo en cuenta que lo que tenemos entre manos es una novela visual sin coste alguno.

En cuanto al audio no es una locura, pero está bien y creo que ayuda a matizar y darle más drama a ciertos momentos.

Por otra parte decir que el juego viene traducido a varios idiomas, entre ellos el español, cosa que se agradece porque no es nada habitual en cuanto a visual novel se refiere. Eso sí, el juego no viene doblado a ningún idioma, pero vamos que tampoco lo encuentro necesario.

No disponemos de logros ni cartas, algo previsible siendo un juego gratuito, pero un logro por terminarlo no hubiera estado mal.

Nada más, sobretodo porque he tardado más en escribir este análisis que en terminarme de leer la novela XD.

Si tuviera que darle una puntuación sería un 5 y porque es gratis, sino... Igualmente es recomendable, ya que te la lees en nada y es una experiencia nueva y diferente a lo que estamos acostumbrados.

PD: Gracias a todos por haber destinado unos minutos en leer mi análisis. Espero que os haya servido y para cualquier cosa nos vamos viendo por steam n.n

I can't recommend this now, or really ever. Even if the bugs were squashed, its still not good. As far as current technical issues go:
- Performs poorly on a 3080 Ti with a Ryzen 9 cpu (my coop partner had the same experience with his gaming pc)
- Room culling rarely works properly, so you'll see through the world very frequently.
- The portals clip player character models, and cause janky transitions between sides (They use render method of painting a wall with a view from a different part of the level, but don't appear to display models half-way through the portal correctly). You also get quick flashes of the outside of the levels while passing through if your camera is at any angle other than orthogonal to the door frame.

Gameplay reasons not to buy this:
- The game's coop and puzzles are very half-baked. The first variety of puzzle is: fire-brigading items across barriers that the other person can't move through. There's just not a lot of thought to it, just "it is your turn to carry the Olympic torch over the orange threshold." The second variety is sharing information with your buddy which will tell him exactly what button to hit. Pretty simple, but at least there is some simple pattern recognition required. Then the third variety: needing to press something at the same time. On the level of LEGO synchronized lever pulling.
- These puzzle mechanics can work, but here's the kicker: The game doesn't develop any particular implementation, dismissing them pretty quickly after using them, and rarely layers them. The two most engaging puzzles only layer two of these: One requires you to relay information and then synchronize lever pulling; the other requires you fire brigade items across barriers and match sequences, then fire brigade items. The final "puzzle" is [spoiler] a synchronized lever pull. You unlock doors for your buddy by passing the character barriers then one player can sit back until two key items are acquired for the lever pull.[/spoiler] Puzzle game endings can be difficult, but this was really disappointing.
- The non-euclidean parts of the game amount to just wonky level design. Most of the time they are just a wow factor (and probably what is tanking the framerate and causing all of the weird level culling). Anytime they do matter they are statically determined, not controlled by the player characters, and just mask players' views from the puzzle solution to require that the other player take part in the information exchange puzzle variety. There's nothing you couldn't do in this game that you couldn't do with normal level design, where a game like Portal depends on the mechanic. Its main reason for being in this game is that it is relevant due to the plot.

There's also a story. I listened to it because I had a friend who voice acted in this. One or two voice logs in you can map out every plot point in your head.

The game can be completed in about an hour to a hour and a half. I won't be getting my $8.50 back however, because the game was bugged at launch and caused me and my friend to enter a fugue state for 20 minutes, one synced lever pull from completing the game. Then we played it again for the voice actor friend in less than an hour.

For 8.50, you could do worse and you could do better. I hope they take some lessons from this endeavor and hone their craft a lot more before releasing another game. This needed a serious QA pass, and desperately needs a more interesting puzzle experience.

Cette évaluation risque de s'étoffer avec le temps : 

LE MESSIE EST DE RETOUR :-) 

- Midair est le succésseur de Tribes , beaucoup plus dans l'esprit Tribes 1 et 2 que Tribes Ascend . j'ai du mal a me souvenir de Tribes 2 , donc je dirais que ce jeu est une version plus puriste de Tribes ascend . 

- Pour les nouveaux c'est simple, Midair est un Tribes like, 3 Armures Disponible , légère (plus de vitesse , plus de maniabilité , moins de vie) Medium ( le compromis) et heavy ( plus de vie , plus de jetpack mais plus de loudeur , moins de maniabilité) . le jetpack et pouvoir skier a des vitesses démente


- Aucune armes n'est en hitscan , en résumé il faut prévoir la trajectoire , le distance de son adversaire pour le touché , c'est vraiment le gros point positif sur ce jeu , tout est basé sur l'expérience, le skill et la récompense de bien faire . même le snipe , qui as un projectile rapide certe, doit s'appliquer .

- tournant sur unreal engine 4 , bien optimiser , graphiquement très épuré , on remarque quand même des différences de qualité dans les cartes du jeux , en clair les dernières cartes sont plus belles que les premières, tout ceci sera sûrement réglé dans le temps .

- le voice command est présent , en clair en appyant sur V vous lancer la commande de tchat préenregistrer pour communiquer avec les alliés et les ennemis , Pour exemple En appuyant sur V-A-F je lance la commande " Get the ennemy flag " et ainsi de suite , comme sur Tribes en sommes . 

- Un netcode excellent , je n'ai jamais rencontré un jeu ou je peux jouer sur un serveur US a 140 de ping sans en ressentir la latence , je ne sais pas comment ils ont reussi cet exploit , mais c'est tout simplement génial , d'après les dires des devellopeurs , tant que vous jouer a - de 150 de ping, vous ne ressentirez aucun lag .

Problem #1: Physics are stiff and counter-intuitive, and level layout makes it difficult to glide around Tribes-style. You have to "GIT GUD" before you manage to do so, which is why this game is turning off new players, and is basically dying. Tribes:Ascend wasn't easy to grasp, but gliding around the hills was easy to get a hang of, as the level design was generous and straightforward in that regard even in its worst maps.

Problem #2: This problem is shared with Tribes: Ascend. Unreal engine is strained by the networking requirements of FPS-Z shooters. Both MidAir and Tribes: Ascend inaccurately draw object positions when your ping is above 30. Yes, you can "GIT GUD" and adapt to this problem, but it is a symptom of bad netcode in Unreal Engine. Older games like Quake Wars didn't have this problem. In fact, even older Unreal games (UT2003, UT2004) had seemingly better netcode, or maybe they just worked better due to two-dimensional movement. 

Problem #3: As part of awful level design, bases have a weird, disconnected layout. The importance of deployables and generator is downplayed. Tribes: Ascend had superficial base design compared to original Tribes 1/2 already. Original Tribes games had its own "indoor game" on some levels, where you could spend the entire game just being an engineer who maintains the base, and it would be both important and fun. That angle is lost here. Nobody's ever inside the base.

Problem #4: The game shipped without a voice announcer! No "Your team's flag was taken" here! The UI is cumbersome. The ammo counters for weapons are not prominent. 

Problem #5: Developers are slow and largely oblivious to feedback.

UNSIGHTED — крайне приятная игра, в нее просто-напросто интересно играть.
Красивые пиксельные локации радуют глаз, а незамысловатый, но приятный саундтрек дополняет атмосферу. В целом весь визуал очень классный, за исключением дизайна пары боссов (три летающие лысые женские головы, почему???) и некоторых персонажей. Хотя касательно NPC намного более актуальна другая проблема — они не просто картонныe, они деревянные. Они не интересные, не имеют никаких доп активностей или разнообразия диалогов, ни о каком развитии отношений также нет речи. Они просто существуют, они просто могут дать что-то взамен на твои деньги или повторить в 10-й раз одну и ту же фразу, ну а также вручить нам что-либо в благодарность, если мы подарим кому-то три мешочка заветной метеоритной пыли, увеличивающей везунчику жизнь на 24 часа. После вступительной части свой отсчет начинают внутриигровые часы, периодически забирающие в небытие различных NPC, когда их время подходит к концу, но для меня как для игрока это ничего не значит, и единственная причина увеличить кому-то жизнь — это получить от него благодарственный подарок, а остальное — потратить на пару дополнительных хилок и продление собственной жизни (мы тоже имеем таймер, и, насколько я знаю, по его истечении происходит перманентное поражение на сейве). На самом деле я чутка стемнил, и был все-таки один персонаж, которого я тащил до конца, на то есть пара причин, но я умолчу о них, чтобы избежать любых спойлеров. Честно говоря, я в целом не вижу особого смысла в том, что механика ограниченного времени здесь существует, есть хорошие способы пополнить свое время, его вполне хватает для спокойного прохождения, но при этом оно все равно психологически подгоняет, что не дает полностью насладиться миром, миром реально интересным, хоть и не особо большим. При первом прохождении игра может показаться чуть ли не линейной, но уже на втором, зная некоторые крафты и механики (некоторым из которых игра, к сожалению, не обучает, а самому догадаться анрил), игра может быть пройдена, побеждая основных сюжетных боссов (не считая финального разумеется) в обратном порядке и в рамках одного часа, а местный аналог амулетов позволяет собирать мощнейшие билды и убивать некоторых боссов двумя комбинациями "парирование + атака". Парирования тут очень приятные и простые, даже PERFECT!-парирования имеют неплохое окно для реакции. На самом деле, так можно сказать про всю игру: она вся довольно простая и не вызывает трудностей, за исключением разве что одного опционального босса (и то из-за саммонов), а также некоторых ачивок (боссраш из 9 боссов за 10 минут — сказка). Подводя итог: игра не идеальная, но очень хорошая и, повторю снова, крайне приятная.

未経験者向けに解説。

古い携帯ゲーム機からの移植が3作品＋おまけの1作品（さらに古い時代の作品）という4本セット。
携帯機と侮ってはいけません。高いアクション性と十分なボリュームが両立されています。
当時の説明書もついてくるし、海外版もついてきます（海外版は若干ゲームバランスが異なる部分も存在）。

↓気になると思われる点をいくつか解説↓

・BGMは評価の高い楽曲が揃っています。しかし元が古い携帯機なので音質には難があります（おまけタイトルのみ別ハードにつき比較的良好）。
・バグ技が有名なシリーズですが、普通のプレイで致命的なバグに遭遇することは極めてまれです。仮に遭遇しても『巻き戻し機能』があるので回避できます！
・今の時代に遊んでも十分に楽しめます。古くなったのは解像度と音質（移植で多少改善？）だけです！
・上達する喜びがあります。アクションRPGですが、上手くなるとすごい速さでクリアできます。

↓ここから作品ごとの簡単な紹介↓

『悪魔城ドラキュラ サークルオブザムーン』
携帯機3作品の中で、もっとも王道となる物語を体験できます。雰囲気も良いです。
シビアながら優れたゲームバランスを持っていて、やり込むほどに新たな攻略法が見えてくる良作。
シリーズ未経験者に最初にお勧めしたい作品です。

『キャッスルヴァニア 白夜の協奏曲』
携帯機時代の事情で、色調が強調されている画面になっています。
BGMは音質がよくないせいで評価されていませんが、楽曲そのものは魅力的です。プレイ後にカバー曲を聴いてみよう！
ボスの種類が豊富で、大型のボスが多いのが売り。マップも広大。
難点はゲームバランスが後半になるほど雑で、また後半はやや作り込みが足りない部分も。
バグ技を駆使したRTA動画で有名なゲームでもあります。
2番目にプレイすることをおすすめします。わかりにくい部分もあるので、詰まったら攻略サイトをみるのもアリ。

『キャッスルヴァニア 暁月の円舞曲』
これも携帯機時代の事情で色調が強調されています。
この作品は世界観が特殊で、これだけが現代（近未来）が舞台になっています。
実はこの作品はある過去作から繋がった世界観を持っているのですが、未プレイでも問題ありません。
他の収録作品にはぜったいに出てこないような個性的なアイテムがたくさん登場して面白いです。
舞台設定の特性上、また完成度から言っても、携帯機3作品の中で最後にプレイすると一番楽しめると思います。

『悪魔城ドラキュラXX』
おまけの１作品。この作品だけ純粋なアクションゲームで、RPG要素はありません。
一番古い作品で、シリーズの雰囲気を知るには良いのですが、凶悪な難易度で悪名高いタイトルでもあります。
操作性もあまりよくないので、レトロゲーム好きでなかったら無理にプレイしなくてもいいかも……？
実績の対象にもなっていますが、恐ろしい難易度には『巻き戻し機能』で対抗する手段もあります！

The first volume of the Battle Network collection, Vol. 1 is a good introduction but offers imo less bang for their buck. If you're going to get this one, I'd recommend grabbing both volumes together.
As a collection, it does everything you want it to do: the first 3 games (plus Battle Network having access to both Blue & White), a gallery with promotional art, a music player, and even a title screen voiced by the anime's original Voice Actor. The only other addition is a maxbuster mode, making grinding a breeze with it.

There is a multiplayer element too to do battles and compare libraries but it's at this point abandoned, so unless you have friends to play with good luck getting use out of it.

As for the games themselves, they're still fun but these are definitely the growing pains of the series, lacking some of the later features such as souls, emotion window or even many e-reader cards. Still a decent introduction though to the deckbuilding and other mechanics, but lacking in a lot of depth.

If you're going to get it, I would recommend going for both collections at once by getting the bundle. It is still a good collection but the weaker of the two.

正直、諦め半分だった流星コレクションが出ると聞いて久しぶりにテンションが上がり、ここはロックマンシリーズで唯一ちゃんと触れていなかったエグゼも履修しておこう、とセール時に購入。

確かに広義ではアクションゲームなのですが初代ロックマンやX、ゼロZXのようなジャンプアクション、ハイスピードアクションとは根本的に違うものです。
自身で構築したチップフォルダ（カードゲームでいうデッキ）を的確に運用することで爽快感を得るゲームで、Xやゼロのようにキャラの直感的なアクションによって爽快感を得るゲームではない、というのが大きな違いかと思います。
少なくとも自分は、初代ロックマンやX、ゼロ、ZX等よりも動きの癖や敵の挙動の見極めが難しいと感じます。

救済措置のバスターマックスと配信チップがあるとは言え、令和に遊ぶには少々不親切だったり不便だったり意地悪だなぁという印象があります。
流星シリーズはリアルタイムで遊んでいましたが、エグゼを遊んでいると流星の戦闘システムの快適さが恋しくなります…エグゼの積み重ねがあってこその流星だったんだなぁと実感しました。

以下、各タイトルの感想。

■エグゼ
記念すべき1作目でシステムやゲームバランスはまだ粗削り。
戦闘終了後にHPが回復するから良いものの、雑魚戦ですらチップの引きが悪いと戦いづらく、マップは構造がわかりづらい上にエンカウント率も高い。
しかし、今作のロックマンがどういう成り立ちのキャラクターなのかを知るためには避けて通れない1本。

■エグゼ2
エンカウント率やマップのわかりづらさ、チップの選びづらさといった前作の不満点を大きく改善…したかと思いきや、ストーリー終盤では前作にも勝るとも劣らないエンカウント率や面倒なマップが待ち構えています。
自分の戦い方によってロックマンが変化するスタイルチェンジがおもしろい。
今作からのレギュラーチップに加えて同名チップも今作は5枚まで入れられるので、1～3の中ではプログラムアドバンスが一番使いやすい。

■エグゼ3（WHITE版をプレイ）
ストーリーではデカオや炎山の掘り下げがあったり、1と2のストーリーを踏まえて主人公の成長が見られるものになっていて、ストーリーは今作が一番おもしろかった。
…しかし、一部のマップのわかりづらさ（無駄な回り道の多さ）は健在。
ボスの難易度調整が他に比べてイマイチな印象で、前半に戦うビーストマンやバブルマンは「もう二度と戦いたくねぇ！」と思った一方で、その後のデザートマン、プラントマン、フレイムマン、ドリルマンはびっくりするほど緩慢な攻撃パターンで拍子抜けしたり。

3の最大の特徴になる強化システム『ナビカスタマイザー』はパズル的なおもしろさがあるものの、せっかく手持ちでベストなカスタマイズをしていてもストーリー進行によって組み込まなければならないプログラムがあり、半ば強制的に組み替えなければいけないので、ややめんどうくさいシステムになっていると思いました。

さて、次は後半の4以降をプレイ…と思ったけど、少しエグゼの戦闘に疲れてしまったので、また少し間を空けてから遊ぼうと思います…

Remnant Records est un jeu d’enquête horrifique… mais pas du tout dans le style Phasmophobia. Ici, pas de chasse au fantôme classique : on explore un lieu chargé d’histoire, et tout le gameplay repose sur la compréhension de ce passé.

On fouille, on lit des notes, on reconstitue des souvenirs, et on essaie d’identifier les objets qui correspondent le mieux au drame vécu par le “protagoniste” de la mission. Chaque partie raconte sa propre histoire, et ça fonctionne vraiment bien.

Chaque personnage possède des compétences uniques qui apportent une vraie profondeur au gameplay. Et n’oubliez pas : c’est un jeu d’horreur. Vous n’êtes pas seuls dans ce bâtiment… et ça, vous allez vite le comprendre.

Que ce soit en solo ou à plusieurs, la découverte est super agréable. Le jeu se démarque vraiment des autres titres d’enquête paranormale, et ça fait du bien d’avoir un concept différent.

Petit défaut tout de même : après 10 à 15 heures de jeu, la sensation de découverte s’atténue. On fait assez vite le tour des histoires, ce qui réduit un peu la fraîcheur des parties sur le long terme.

Malgré ça, Remnant Records reste une belle surprise et un jeu que l’on recommande chaudement !

올바른 위치에 타일을 배치해서 가로줄과 세로줄의 숫자 합을 일치시켜야 되는 퍼즐 게임.

Aggregator Elevator System 은 숫자 타일들을 적절하게 배치하여 퍼즐들을 풀어나가야 하는 게임으로, 가로줄 그리고 세로줄의 숫자들을 보고 “어떻게 해야 이 줄에 해당하는 타일들의 숫자를 모두 합한 게, 이 퍼즐이 원하는 수치가 될 수 있는가?” 를 생각하면 되는 방식의 게임이다. 퍼즐 메커니즘은 앞 문장에 말한 것처럼, 가로줄과 세로줄에 적혀 있는 숫자를 보고, 그 줄에 해당되는 타일의 수를 모두 더한 게 일치하도록 숫자 타일들을 배치하면 되는 방식이다. 첫 레벨에는 순수하게 숫자가 적힌 타일들을 던져 주기 때문에 “아 ㅋㅋㅋ 이거 네모네모 로직처럼 단순하게 풀어 나가면 되네 ㅋㅋ” 라고 생각할 수 있지만, 게임의 엔딩까지 60 레벨만 풀면 됨에도 불구하고 30% 정도만 들어가도 머리가 지끈거리는 걸 느낄 수 있을 것이다. 그 이유는, 당연하지만 게임이 숫자만 적힌 타일 말고 다른 특이한 타일들을 던져 주기 때문이다. 게임 내 특이한 타일들은 총 10 종류가 있는데, 인접하는 타일에 직접 숫자를 더해주는 타일 / 숫자의 수치를 직접 10 으로 만들어 버리는 타일 / 수치가 X 축과 Y 축에 따라 결정되는 변수 타일 등등, 정해진 수치가 있는 타일이 아니라 변하기 쉬운 수치를 지닌 타일이라서, 특이한 타일들은 모두 어디다 타일을 배치하느냐가 매우 중요한 타일들이다. 게임 레벨 자체의 크기 또한 작은 편이 아니고, 한 레벨에 타일을 6 ~ 10 개 던져주는 게 기본이라 경우의 수가 보기보다 매우 많아서, 난이도가 절대 낮은 퍼즐 게임은 아니라고 생각한다.

이 게임은 특이하게 게임을 시작하면 바로 레벨 1로 들어가는 게 아니라, 플레이어가 시드를 입력해서 해당 시드에 해당되는 레벨들이 생성된다. 즉, 두 플레이어가 서로 다른 시드를 입력하면, 60 레벨까지 갈 때까지 서로 다른 레벨들을 풀게 될 거라는 것이다. 이 시스템의 장점은 일반적인 퍼즐 게임과 다르게 매우 많은 가짓수의 레벨들 – 이론적으로 무한대의 레벨들 - 을 볼 수 있을 것이라는 점이지만, 단점으로는 시드 별 난이도 상승 곡선이 다르기 때문에 몇몇 시드에서는 레벨 배치가 악질적으로 느껴질 수 있다는 점이다. 이 게임에 뼈를 묻고 몇 백개의 퍼즐들을 풀어 갈 재미를 느낀다면 이러한 시스템이 긍정적으로 느껴질 것이지만, 개인적으로는 한 번 엔딩까지 보고 만족한 입장이어서 “차라리 레벨 종류는 고정하고 레벨 개수를 더 늘리지 …” 라는 생각이 들었다. 그래도, 퍼즐 게임에 퍼즐의 개수가 많은 게 단점은 아니라, 매우 부정적으로 느껴지지는 않았다. 게임을 시작하면 시드를 입력하는 것 말고 난이도 선택 및 컨트롤 선택이 있는데, 컨트롤의 경우 게임이 의도한 “엘리베이터 조작” – 타일들을 화면 좌측의 엘리베이터로만 움직일 수 있고, 자유로운 조작이 불가능하다 – 및 편의성 패치 이후 추가된 “직접 조작” – 타일들을 드래그만 하면 원하는 위치로 바로 옮길 수 있다 – 이렇게 두 조작 모드가 있다. 말만 들어도 알겠지만, 엘리베이터 조작으로 게임을 진행하면 안 그래도 어려운 퍼즐 때문에 머리가 지끈거리는데 조작까지 원하는 대로 안 되어서 더 빡칠 수 있으므로, 직접 조작 모드로 플레이하는 걸 권장한다.

퍼즐 외적의 요소는 사실 그렇게 특별한 건 없다. 비주얼은 정말 최소한의 요소를 갖춘 정도이며, 사운드도 매우 특별하지는 않아서 게임 중반부터는 그냥 유튜브로 원하는 음악을 틀면서 게임을 진행하였다. 그나마 귀여웠던 두 가지 소소한 디테일을 적자면, 레벨을 클리어할 때마다 독특한 그림이 화면 좌측 하단 및 레벨 선택창에서 보이며 – 그림이라고 적었지만, 사실 네모네모 로직을 풀어서 나온 그림처럼 자잘한 픽셀 오브젝트에 더 가깝다 – 화면 우측 상단의 여자아이가 한 레벨에서 오랜 시간을 소비할 때마다 라면을 먹는다던가, 잠을 잔다던가 하는 식의 방치 애니메이션이 있다는 점이다. 퍼즐 외 요소가 매력적이지는 않았지만, 퍼즐 게임에 중요한 건 퍼즐이므로 이에 대해 큰 실망감을 느끼지는 않았다. 


결론적으로, 단순해 보이는 메커니즘이지만 다양한 타일을 추가함으로써 플레이어가 생각해야 할 가짓수를 늘려서, 직관적인 디자인에 난이도 있는 퍼즐들을 잘 넣어 만든 좋은 게임이라 추천. 업적의 경우 한 시드에 배정된 모든 레벨들을 힌트 없이 클리어해야 해서 난이도가 있는 편이지만, 다행히 스팀 가이드에 업적 100% 를 달성하기 쉬운 가이드가 있으니 너무 걱정할 필요는 없다.

여담) 업적 100% 를 노리는 사람들이 주의해야 할 두 중요한 특징이 있다. 먼저, 게임의 패치 노트와는 다르게, 아직도 업적이 게임을 진행 중에는 달성 표시가 뜨지 않고 끄고 나서야 달성이 된다. 업적이 안 뜬다고 안절부절하지 말자. 두 번째 특징은 훨씬 더 중요한 특징인데, 게임 내 설정에 레벨을 클리어 할 수 있는 타일 배치를 완성하면, 원래는 레벨이 자동으로 클리어가 되는 게 아니라 Submit 버튼을 눌러서 레벨을 제출해야 하는데, 설정 중 자동으로 Submit 을 누르는 설정이 있다. 이 설정을 절대 !!!!!!!!!! 켜지 말아라. 왜 그런지는 모르겠는데, 이 설정을 켜고 게임을 진행하면 이후 업적들이 죄다 달성되지 않는다. 이후 업데이트로 고쳐 질지는 모르겠지만, 웬만하면 켜지 않는 걸 권장한다.

In 'Tower Bombarde' you play a little worm-like virus which has the mission to hack the enemy by destroying various towers, there are also hazards in this game that try to hinder you from terminating all the turrets. 

There are 10 levels in this game, where in each of them are 10 small stages which you have to complete in order to finish one of the levels and in every 10th stage there is a bossfight. The bosses of the first two levels have a moderate difficulty and take a little longer than the 'normal' stages. One Level takes you around 10-15 minutes to finish. 
If you go game over, you have to restart the level entirely.
I'm not aware if there's any bonus content, since I only played the first two levels, so the game might be a little longer and has a hard mode of some sort if you finish all 10 levels.

This game has very simple controls and is easy to understand. You move your character with the mouse and a left-click, you can see the turrets range by pressing the middle-mousebutton and you can use a shield by right-clicking, the shield reflects the bullets of enemy-turrets and assists you in killing them. The first few levels are beginner-friendly and help you learn the game faster.

Bugs, Freezes and Lags weren't noticed by me, so this game has been polished well and you don't need a NASA-PC to play this game it seems.
The music in this game is fitting with the action and doesn't sound bad in my opinion, if you don't like you can turn it off in the options-menu.
