You’re unlikely to come across a horror FPS quite like this: within its first hour, you’ll battle bizarre monsters, endure some outlandishly cheap jump scares, and, if you’re lucky, get lectured about communism by a bird creature. It’s a unique combination only possible via pure indie ambition—perhaps more ambition than experience, though.

Let’s get the major stumbling blocks out front. The game’s menus and most text are locked to Russian, with in-game dialogue in English, which leaves non-Russian speakers fumbling in the dark. There are no options to change the language. Almost all voices are clearly AI-generated, and the results are inconsistent and occasionally broken (at least one female character inexplicably shifts to a male voice for a line). The writing is, at times, overly verbose and just as clearly machine-written. Subtitles rarely match what you’re hearing. The introduction can set you up for failure—enemies might swarm your bike before you can pick up a weapon, which forces a death you can’t skip or easily recover from.

If you do push past these rough edges, you’ll find that enemy AI doesn’t follow normal rules: monsters never stop chasing you, even phasing through buildings and fences. Once armed, you’ll discover heavy balancing issues—every enemy takes two shots, regardless of type, and firing your weapon seems to summon the entire map’s enemy population. Some parts of the world are just bizarre in scale, making navigation even stranger (spot the triple-sized beds).

Despite this, there’s a beating heart beneath the jank. The developer has carved out a surprisingly large, open map with side quests, secrets, and a storyline you slowly unravel. For the price—more of a dollar impulse buy than a full-fledged release—there’s genuine curiosity and effort behind the worldbuilding. With about 2 hours of play you might only be scratching the surface, and you may catch glimpses of the potential the developer is trying to realize.

Those positives are almost paradoxical, though: there’s passion here, but every step is tripped up by technical issues, lack of polish, and an overreliance on AI-generated everything—from text and icons to voices and artwork. The environments, story, and that bird philosopher all suggest there was more in mind than just another disposable horror release.

Right now, it’s difficult to recommend outright, even at a rock-bottom price, unless you’re a fan of so-bad-it’s-good indie projects or want to experience one of the more surreal budget horror games on Steam. If the developer addresses the language barrier, AI abuse, and general playability, this could actually be a hidden gem. As it stands, you’re buying a wild experiment—often broken, sometimes fascinating, and absolutely rough around every edge. Proceed only if you know exactly what you’re in for.

どちらかというとハクスラ好きで、ヴァンサバ系は本家のみやったことがある程度のユーザーの感想です。初めてゲームレビューを書きます。
この作品はヴァンサバとハクスラ系のいいとこどりしたような作品でとても楽しめた。
まだ開発途上の作品ではあるが、現時点でも十分おもしろく、おすすめできます。
戦士キャラと弓キャラのみをある程度やり込んだ時点でのレビューです。

■良いところ
・ヴァンサバ系の要素を取り込んだことでハクスラ系にありがちな冗長で退屈な戦闘がひたすら続く感じがなく、毎回短期的に劇的に強くなるスリリングな戦闘が楽しめる。
・逆にヴァンサバ系と比べると地道にキャラを強化していく楽しみがあり、装備構成をあれこれ考えるのも面白い。一度戦闘にでると大量に装備を獲得できるので、何度も繰り返し戦闘をしたくなり、中毒性が高い。
・ver1.8でやりやじめ現在1.9だが、敵の強さなどのバランスは悪くないと思う。理不尽と感じる点はそうない。

■残念なところ
・王道ハクスラ系に比べるとビルドの多様性、やりこみ要素がかなり劣る。
・逆にヴァンサバと比べると戦闘終盤の派手さや異常なインフレ感がなく、スキルの効果がレベルに応じて大きく変わったりもないので、そのあたりは割と地味かもしれない。
・基本的に戦闘で取得したいスキルは決まってくるので、あまりその戦闘での一期一会のスキル同士のシナジー的な面白さはない
・キャラ固有の基本攻撃と特殊攻撃が他のスキルに比べ火力が高いので、ひたすらそれを強化してしまえば終わりだったりする。
特定のスキルを強化するレジェンダリ効果はあるが、戦闘でそのスキルを早々に取得して強化できるかには運がからむので、貴重なレジェンダリ効果枠を特定のスキルにつかうより、基本攻撃と特殊攻撃を強化した方が無難ということになりがち
・武器に関しては武器攻撃力アップのボーナスが重要すぎて、それがついてないとすべてゴミになる。

■期待するところ
・個人的には祭壇でのスキルの成長要素やキャラのスタッシュ、ダンジョンレベルの解放などは完全にキャラで分けてほしい。別のキャラを触りだすときにすべてのダンジョンが解放済みだとあまりモチベーションが上がらない
・ビルドの多様性がもっとほしい。
・ユニーク装備が大してユニークじゃないので、個性的な効果がもっと出るとうれしい。
・レジェンダリ装備は終盤割とぽこぽこと落ちるし、装備を組み合わせて作ることもできるので、あまり有り難みがなくなってくる。その事自体に不満はないが、家宝になるような装備を見つけてそれを軸にビルドを考える楽しみをもう少し強化してもらえると嬉しい。

The gameplay, while mostly competent, does leave a few things lacking. It tries to blend beat-em-up crowd control with the intimacy and technicality of a fighting game. This mostly works; the combat system does feel satisfying when you get going, and the ever-escalating combo sound is delightful. When you time your reactions and flawlessly convert a punish into strings, the game really sings. Enemies, however, have no need to plan and react to you. They can just kinda throw out hitboxes or command grabs and corner carry you left to right to left again with no finesse. The expectations of precision on the player do not hold for the opposition, and that can feel really unfair. I got strongly soured in the last few stages of the game because there were ten straight seconds of attacks that simply could not be reacted to. The system gets messy when pushed to its limits.

That's really part of the appeal, though. It's not perfect, but certainly glad it's here.

Initial Thoughts: I have just completed Far Cry, it took me just under 9 hours to finish. 

Story: This game feels straight out of a 2000s action-adventure flick; think XXX with Vin Diesel, Pierce Brosnan’s James Bond, or even the DOOM movie. It’s packed with cheesy clichés and doesn’t take itself too seriously, which actually adds to the fun and humor. It’s your classic ex-special-forces hero saves the day and gets the girl setup. Without spoiling anything, the ending is one of the most anti-climactic I’ve ever seen, almost a zero-payout after the punishment you endure in the final mission.

Characters: They’re bland and lifeless, with voice acting that borders on parody. The main character sounds like that surfer guy from the viral interview describing waves, it’s comically bad. His partner doesn’t sound anything like she looks, which only adds to the disconnect. But let’s be honest, this game wasn’t built for its story; it was built to show off the Crytek engine.

Gameplay & Mechanics: Far Cry can be downright unfair, even on the easiest difficulty. It wants you to approach missions stealthily; going into it full run-and-gun as I did will get you punished fast. Some missions and boss fights, especially the infamous final one, are absurdly difficult unless you cheese your way through them. That being said, driving sequences are fun, and weapons are satisfying to use, each with their own advantages. The MP5SD is a standout here. The rocket launcher, however, is extremely underwhelming, it’s slow and weak compared to the one enemies use (theirs absolutely wrecks you).

Graphics: Crytek is crushing it in 2004. The graphics and physics are stellar in most areas, the water effects are especially impressive, and the game still looks good by today’s standards. The only downside is the limited draw distance, which can break immersion a bit.

Final Thoughts: Far Cry stands out as a unique entry in the series; it feels more like a Crysis prototype than a traditional Far Cry sequel. It’s a not-so-serious, action-packed adventure that fits right into that early-2000s hero-movie itch.

Score: 7.0/10. As true a 7 as it gets. It does just enough right to rise above average, but the uneven balance and weak storytelling keep it from going any higher.

但又不得不提的是就像我最开始说的，我只是当作手机小游戏的免广告版，而这游戏也确实做到了，但问题是去掉广告之后并没有把材料的获取变得更轻松，只是单纯去除了广告，材料依然需要刷，我98个小时里面，实际游玩时间应该是一半左右，可玩部分是不少的，但也需要差不多刷一半时间的材料，我觉得这部分还是真值得改进，时间是有点太久了，进入新地图后基本上就是先找个刷材料方便、东西靠在一起的位置先刷个半小时，然后再推进地块，这部分真值得再改改，不过话又说回来，这类本来就是解压游戏，不能太功利性的去玩，轻松一点就好
无论如何，总而言之，打折后是值得入手的，特别是当你电脑里没有一个慢节奏的游戏时，这个游戏能让你从其他游戏中回过神来，并且能带来还算不错的体验，当成主力游戏是无聊了点，但当作一款辅助型游戏，那么这游戏是可以给出8/10的，值得推荐一玩的游戏

In Response to Common Complaints: 
(For context, I am currently 60 hours in, have nearly 1k hours in Satisfactory, a sizable chunk in Shapez/Zachtronics-verse/Atrio, and no less than three separate therapy appointments that have used the fact that I refuse to buy Factorio, because I don't like the visuals, as a metaphor for why I think I'm going to die alone.)

TL;DR
This is not Conveyor Belt Automation. This is secret Programming Automation wrapped in adorable visuals. There's an optional Minecraft-style Redstone dynamic to provide efficiency, flexibility, and less line spaghetti. 

I can spend three hours writing a text wall about my complicated feelings, or I can spend 15 minutes drawing a flowchart that explains how (I think) my brain works, and then lose myself for 16 hours making that flowchart both readable and pretty.

This game is for me.

If you just want more conveyor belts (Satisfactory, Shapez, and I assume Factorio) then you might find this game annoying and limiting. That's totally fine. That's what those games do very well, and they're all amazing.

If you, like me, have Programmer's Brain, but are such a violently visual thinker that text-only programming is a struggle, it's a treat. 
-If have Rock? Go right. If no have Rock? Keep walking. It's relaxation therapy for people who like to label everything.
-Are your little dude going down the wrong paths? That's a bug report.
-Are your little dudes running in circles and looking insane? There's ways to give them a rest.
-Did you clear-cut and strip mine the map before finding infinite resource generators? You can regrow that. 
--You can even set up harvest/growth cycles if you're into that.

The game literally weaponizes your empathy to push you towards more efficient, sustainable solutions. But, it also lets you ignore all of that and just infinite-resource your way through everything. There is a lot of flexibility, but instead of providing it to you through more and more machines, it provides it to you with sparks (your dudes), and the layout of the world itself. 

Some minimun-spoilery things to help avoid frustration:
[spoiler]-The game proceeds through wood, stone, and then metal. (If there's more, I haven't gotten there yet)
-Either hold off on massive factories until you're in stone (you'll know when).
--Or, always build with a mind towards converting to one-way paths overs long distances or high-traffic areas.
-Combat gets exponentially easier with each stack of active sparks.
--Manual combat will (for the most part) only ever be necessary for short spurts as you reach a new infinite harvestable.
--- I know there's a tower defense portion at the end of the game, I've yet to reach it, and can't apply the above to that portion. I'll update this review to reflect that portion when I reach it. Especially as I loath tower defense, and am curious how they approach it[/spoiler]

Please do yourself a favor and pay attention to the fact that the first spark you get is literally a log. Stubby legs, no arms. If that doesn't tell you everything you need to know about the intelligence of the sparks, and the humor of the visuals, nothing else will.

I'm not about to complain about a small experimental game being 'too short' when it's functionally more like buying a ticket to a virtual museum/art installation. Wanted to open with that since it's something people tend to be negative about for no reason, and I think even games I don't like deserve to be criticized fairly. 

With that in mind, let me critique the installation. It's a small grotto of neon plants and objects in the middle of a seemingly infinite black lake. If you stand in specific spots, you will either hear a looping music track or hear a spoken-word bit. Music tracks seem very deliberately placed to allow you to enjoy particular imagery while you listen, but the spoken-word parts are delivered through speaker-looking visualizers that stick out no matter where they're placed. There's also an alien tripod creature walking around for... reasons, and you can also walk through 5 columns of floating crystals that give you the ability to throw them? and when you've collected all 5 you can press F to teleport to the credits.

The reason that I can't recommend this is because it left me feeling... flat. I'm sure the artist meant to express something personal with it, but it doesn't come through. The visuals and music are too far in one direction, a sort of 'dark whimsy' where the imagery doesn't really seem to... evoke anything related to bipolar disorder? The music is good, but it's just fun experimental synth. Now, normally 'i don't understand this' is a bad critique of modern art, but the issue here is that 'subtle' doesn't seem to have been the goal, since all the spoken word content is completely on the nose. It's either one of those rhythm-less couplets written by someone who doesn't seem to be all that poetic; stuff on the level of "When I'm depressed it really sucks/ but being manic totally f**cks". Or literally just giving an explanation of the emotional color wheel while standing on a giant emotional color wheel. 

This feels mean to write because of how this game was clearly not something cynical, but if you're going to make representational art you open yourself to art critics. And I do think it's more important to *do* art criticism for 'notgames' and 'interactive albums' like this, instead of just going "dis not real game it don't have gameplay where's my gun." But taking it seriously in that way comes with the risk of finding it lacking.

This is very polished and the sound design is clean, immersive, and really well done. I enjoyed the colorful visuals and the interactive nature of the installation. I am definitely excited to see more experimental games like this. If you like what you see, support the dev here by picking up the game or the soundtrack.

您好，我是人工智能稼轩5000，请问有什么可以帮您的？
[h2]本作是什么玩法？[/h2]
     这款游戏的玩法让我想到了[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/470260/Event0/]Event[0][/url]和[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/368370/Her_Story/]Her Story[/url]，游戏剧情推进主要是靠与海默“对话”和在数据库中检索过去的对话记录，用找到的一个又一个小event拼凑出their stories。

     这个玩法算是一把双刃剑，优点是大大增强了我在游玩过程中的沉浸感，仿佛我真的化身为了前往希望家园执行任务的弗兰克，玩家自身能充分参与到调查的过程中。而且虽然海默并非一个真正的AI，但和他的对话内容也十分丰富，许多问题作者都有考虑到，对话体验很棒。[spoiler]甚至考虑到了玩家想把海默变成猫娘喵XD[/spoiler]

     那么缺点呢？缺点就是来自这句“玩家自身能充分参与到调查的过程中”，换个说法就是，如果你调查不出来，那么就卡着吧。没有什么提示，你所能依靠的就是你掌握的对话。当然大部分时间还是不会卡的，哪怕随便试也能试出来。但个别资料实在是难以检索到，比如卡我时间最长的61和79，我根据上下文把自己代入情景，来来回回试了好多遍才终于试出来了关键词，当时属实是有点红温。虽然说不需要100%也能通关，但对于一款主要看剧情的游戏，有一段剧情空着看不了还是让我很难受。可是话又说回来，这也不算很大的问题，这个玩法总的来说还是很棒的！
[h2]那么剧情又如何呢？[/h2]
     如果想看看对本作艺术性的赏析，可以看看[url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198279159118/recommended/3255860/]这位仁兄的评测[/url]。很遗憾的是，我并没有这么高的鉴赏水平，也没有读过石黑一雄的书，所以我玩完之后并没有这么深的感受，也就不过多分析本作的内涵了，只简单聊一聊本作的文字带给我的直观上的感受。

     本作的故事分为明暗两条线展开，明线是海默2000所记录下的对话，这些是明面上的故事线，而我们还要做的就是在地图各处找到各式“人脸”并了解背后的暗线故事。明线故事理清脉络，暗线故事填充内容。这样做的好处是即使我意外通过“检索”了解到了后面的故事也不会感到被剧透，反而是能激发我探索的好奇心，推动我前进，体验还是不错的。

     再来说说文笔方面，明线上多为比较正式的对话，故多透着一种淡淡的压抑和冷冰冰的严肃。暗线的故事则更有生命力一些，让我们得以窥到每个人物真实的一面，但细品也可以感受到其文字之后有着隐约的伤感。明线的对话和配乐以及画面营造出了淡淡的忧郁氛围，而暗线的故事就像一束月光，带着我们前进，但同时也不偏离整体郁郁的基调，通篇看完很舒服。
[h2]tlnr，来个总结！[/h2]
     综上，本作值得一玩，但可能不太适合期待着惊天阴谋or巨大反转的的玩家。本作需要你耐心地阅读他们的故事，挖掘他们的故事，拼接他们的故事，走进他们的故事。但是……
[b][i]请不要温和地走进那个良夜[/i][/b]

This is a very simple to learn RTS, with good level design (thus far), a pretty good base mechanic, and a brilliant art style (literally and figuratively, the lighting is a bit intense).

The basic premise is that you control a constantly-spawning highly mutable lifeform, and by taking and holding various points around the map you gain access to different sets of abilities for your units. Basic units spawn at a constant rate, and the biggest challenge lies in determining what to turn them into and where to attack. Resource management boils essentially down to "how long do I wait before expanding", which is a simple enough thing to measure.

The good stuff:

As I've said, the art design is excellent. Seriously, everything is pretty clear in its function at a glance and the game looks gorgeous.

It's got a really intuitive interface. Even novice RTS players should be able to pick this up and figure out just about everything extremely easily.

Speedy matches aren't something I'm used to in any RTS. It's nice to be able to knock out a quick game or two instead of an hours-long slog sometimes.

It's quickly engaging, and the additional features that are supposed to make that even better.

The downsides:

If you're looking for something with a lot of depth, look elsewhere. There aren't lots of resources to juggle, there's no campaign, it is exactly what it appears to be.

It's really heavy into micromanaging units for a sizeable portion of each game. Towards the end it can get a bit more macro, but misplacing half a dozen guys (not tough to do) can have pretty dire consequences early on.

Momentum is massively important. This isn't a negative thing necessarily, but it becomes pretty clear pretty quickly who has the advantage in a battle. It's possible to come back if you're behind, but there's an obvious tipping point.

You can't control units while you're zoomed out. That's a bit of an odd design decision and I'm sure there's a reason for it, but it's a little bit frustrating.

All in all this is extremely well done, and for the price you seriously can't beat it for entertainment value.

This is a fantastic puzzle game! About 4.5 to 5 hours (depending on if you are slow like me). Ran extremely well on PSVR2 via PC adapter with no hiccups or glitches. If you like The RoomVR, Myst, Riven, Ghost Town, or slower Escape room style / puzzle adventure games, then this is the game for you. Lots of creative 3d puzzles, beautiful Renaissance era environments, with moody shadows and lighting (looked great on OLED!). Very pretty game. Nice, atmospheric, and subtle music. Pretty decent level and puzzle design, and animations. 

Gameplay mainly consists of teleport to move, back and forth between preordained areas. Puzzles are of the typical puzzle adventure game style where you finish a puzzle to get a piece to figure out how to unlock the next puzzle.

A lot of Japanese wooden box and blacksmith variety puzzles, some moving tile and matching puzzles, and some arithmetic/combo puzzles. Story is pretty light, told through environment and letters scattered throughout, but was serviceable for this type of game, budget, and size of studio.

Some of the pieces require manipulation and combination, which tripped me up several times, but led to an "aha" moment when I finally figured out what I was supposed to do. Some of the areas/puzzles also tripped me up with trying to passing over things that were interactive. This did not happen often, as most of the interactive items are intuitively designed in the in-game logic or machinery of the world (similar to something like Riven).... but it did lead to me haphazardly trying to grab, turn, and yank at anything and everything when I would get to a spot, just to make sure I didn't miss something. Some puzzles I brute forced accidently, without really finding or understanding the clues first. Game has a hint system, but I do not think I used it.

I know it is a real pain for developers, but I really think puzzle games need to be designed for the option to add randomization of solutions on playthrough, and there should be increasing difficulty settings with more complexity added to each of the puzzles for more veteran puzzlers, or folks who want to go through multiple times with more of a challenge. 

Overall, I enjoyed it a lot! I think VR really suited this game well, and I think the developer did an excellent job utilizing the format to maximize immersion and enjoyment that I would not have had otherwise with a Flatscreen experience.  I give it a full-throated endorsement, and I am really looking forward to whatever they may come up with next in VR!

I have played this game for a short amount of time but I feel like I can already provide an accurate review.

The games soundtrack is somewhat mediocre.  I highly suggest listening to your own music over the top.

The gameplay is pretty good, it's a great concept but needs some improving.  Here are some suggestions:

> Higher tolerances for missing.  This isn't real life, not everyone can smack a tiny target with a sword in the opposite hand with ~1 seconds notice.  I understand there must be a skill curve, but I feel allowing for small errors would be great.

> When the sheild is used to deflect an item, it should not be allowed to roll back and cause you to lose a life.  This screwed me on many occasions.  Instead I suggest having the sheild "smash" the projectiles on impact.

> Longer sword.  Some projectiles are out of reach for sitting players/people that stand still.  I do have room-scale enabled but if I was a stationary player I would certainly struggle to hit some of the targets.

> Power ups.  I feel like there is little to no reward for performing well in this game, and the combo system in place doesn't accurately represent or reflect your performance.  I would suggest rewarding the player with perks for high combos/low miss rates in the form of power up projectiles that you slice to gain a temporary advantage (such as seeing where projectiles are going to go, or a magnetic sheild that pulls projectiles towards it).

TL;DR Game is 6/10, needs improvements but I would reccommend.

[h1] 3D Adventure-action game with a Metroidvania style of progression and horrific atmosphere [/h1]


Please note that I haven't played the original game on any version. This review will be based on the game as is and not the Remastered parts.

As the title implies, you play as Michael LeRoi aka the Shadow Man, a voodoo warrior whose main goal is to protect Liveside, the world of the living, from the Apocalypse. To do so, he must journey into Deadside, the world of the dead and gather 120 Dark Souls which serve as the game's main objective and source of power for Shadow Man.

The early game will be spent in Deadside, collecting Dark Souls and voodoo artifacts that will allow the player to progress further into the levels. These artifacts also serve as weapons against the enemies met in Deadside. Shadow Man's fighting system is close to classic Tomb Raider games, Michael aims automatically at the closest enemy to him, all you have to do is press the corresponding key/button to the weapon equipped. Two weapons can be equipped at the same time although in practice the regular gun will probably be your main weapon throughout the game due to its unlimited ammo unlike the voodoo weapons taht work on limited yet rechargeable magic energy. The battles start off as dull but get more and more dynamic as you advance thanks to the new weapons you collect and Dark Souls raising the amount of available magic energy. To balance things out, the number of enemies let in previously visited levels will raise every time you find a certain amount of Dark Souls.

While not as smooth as games like classic Tomb Raiders, Shadow Man has you exploring large levels via platforming. Jumping in this game is a bit weird, Michael's entire body has to land on the platform platform you're trying to jump on otherwise he will automatically grab on the edge and you'll have to climb it before continuing. This might seem like an unimportant detail but it becomes more and more apparent and irksome as you progress and have to slow down and wait for Michael to climb up every platform on your way.

While failing some jumps can lead to immediate death, there is no proper game over in this game. When your health drops, you're brought back to the beginning of the level with every collectibles, weapons, items and Dark Souls collected and killed enemies don't respawn unless you get to another level. You can warp to any level anytime you want, the warp screen even indicates you what item, weapon and how many Dark Souls you should aim for. Every time you acquire a new artifact or ability, the warp screen is updated and lets you kow what your newly acquired buff gives you access to. You will often come back to previously visited levels to uncover hidden portions so you better get used to backtracking. Kingdom of Atham: Crown of the Champions (KoA: CotC) is an ambitious indie title that blends elements of survival, RPG, and base-building genres. Developed by Sofa Mauve Studio, the game invites players into the mystical world of Atham, where they assume the role of a divine champion tasked with cleansing the land of corruption. The game offers a rich tapestry of features, including crafting, combat, magic, and exploration.

KoA: CotC presents a multifaceted gameplay experience:

-Character Progression: Players can choose from various races, each with unique bonuses, and specialize in skills ranging from melee combat to magic and crafting. The skill progression system is designed to cater to different playstyles, allowing for a personalized experience.

-Crafting and Building: The game boasts an intricate crafting system that enables players to forge weapons, armor, and tools. Base-building is a central aspect, with players constructing strongholds to withstand the encroaching darkness. Recent updates have introduced features like mounts and automated repair systems to enhance the base-building experience .

-Combat and Magic: Combat is dynamic, offering options for melee, ranged, and magical engagements. The magic system includes six distinct schools, such as Fire, Holy, and Summoning, each with its own set of spells and abilities. Players can dual-wield weapons, enchant gear, and summon creatures to aid them in battle .

-Exploration: Atham is a vast world divided into diverse biomes, including forests, mountains, and ruins. Each area presents unique challenges, resources, and enemies. Dungeons and caves are scattered throughout, offering opportunities for loot and adventure.

The game's visuals are a blend of stylized fantasy and realism. While the graphics may not rival AAA titles, they effectively convey the game's atmosphere. Recent updates have improved visual fidelity and performance, with optimizations such as DLSS support for smoother gameplay .

KoA: CotC has cultivated a dedicated community on platforms like Steam and Discord. The developers actively engage with players, addressing feedback and implementing updates. However, some users have expressed concerns about the game's longevity and the pace of updates .

Pros:
-Deep and engaging gameplay with multiple systems to explore.
-Rich lore and world-building that immerse players in the setting.
-Regular updates introducing new content and features.
-Active community and developer engagement.

Cons:
-Some technical issues and bugs persist, affecting gameplay.
-Steep learning curve for new players.
-Occasional balance issues with certain skills and mechanics.

Conclusion
Kingdom of Atham: Crown of the Champions offers a compelling blend of survival, RPG, and base-building elements. While it may not be without its flaws, the game's depth and the passion of its developers shine through. For players seeking a rich, immersive experience in a fantasy setting, KoA: CotC is a title worth exploring.

国产RPG游戏有这种素质，我很惊奇。
绝对不是贬低国产游戏的意思。尽管这游戏的确有许许多多的bug，不足，以及挖下来的一大堆坑又没填，但我觉得这种素质级别的，而且是RPGmaker出产的，我到现在都没见过那么几个。
先来说说好：一、羊皮纸风格，画面绝大多数手绘，诚意很足，这方面能够打趴多数同类作品。
二、BGM很出彩。
三、背景故事规模宏伟，有一个完整的大世界观。而作者也表示想要继续做下去，做一个大系列的游戏。会有更多的剧情更多的分支。
接着就是不足，尽管我很喜欢这个游戏，但不可否认它现在是“不完整的”、“破漏着的”：
一、steam成就解锁有问题，大多数人都只能在前几次游戏中解锁相当有限的几个。
二、游戏应当未开发完，许多地方进入都只是提示地图未完成并不能进入发展剧情。而本篇故事剧情篇幅很短，（或许这才是免费的原因？）
三、背景故事设定相当宏伟，这是优点，但如果故事细节处理不当，只会让这个设定成为一个空谈“大饼”，或许这也应该归入到未完成？但我觉得故事叙述可以再细化一点，情节再多一点。
四、游戏细节体验会有点糟糕，比如新提出的时刻点以及做事消耗的时刻并不那么亲民也不随时显示，使得新玩家对时间把握相当困难；马车看笔记碎片全程使用键盘，但却毫无提醒；战斗敌人光标选定相当的困难，多数敌人情况下键盘更好选择目标但却从来没有任何相关教程；有些对话看似已经说完但实际底下还有，但单击鼠标左键只会让你进入下一段对话，剩下的对话犹如隐藏剧情一般，而这一切解决方式只需要增加一个滚动条又或者直接将内容放至下一段就可以解决。
五、游戏难度分布相当不均匀，从魔王刚刚苏醒钓条鱼遇到几个史莱姆都能让全军艰难作战付出一定代价勉强胜利到闯入人类地盘肆意杀虐也就不到一个月的事情，虽然开头有以回复诅咒的前提，但这个变化或许太快了？

虽然在本作宣传上有些出处将本作跟《废都物语》相提并论，但除了画风风格相似，较为出彩的音乐，以及相当壮丽宏伟的背景设定以外，本作在很多方面还需要改进学习，但也不可否认即便拥有不算少的缺点，这作还是诚意与其他素质都是满满的，非常期待该作完成的那天，又或者说拯救大魔王3？

[i] My Experience [/i]

I really enjoyed playing Moonshot, and inserting the fictional nation of Ustria into the space race. There were a few missions that tripped me up, but you'll be a lot more competent (both because of your experience and skill unlocks) at the end of your time with the game. Although the gameplay is fun, there's also typically only one, circuitous way to proceed in each level. I would welcome a bit more "immersive sim" into the experience.

A few other points:
[list]
[*] One particular tricky section involves timing how long it takes a guard to cross a room, so that you can emerge when his back is turned. Your screen turns black when you climb inside the cupboard to hide. Although this was definitely tricky, it also made me feel like a super spy.
[*] When you drop from one level to the one below, you will always fall in the center. This can make you accidentally set off infrared alarms that you thought you'd dodged.
[*] Lockpicking is tricky, even with the upgrade. This could probably stand to be a bit more intuitive and less random.
[*] When you retry a level, you (for some reason) keep the money that you acquired in your failed attempt and can collect it again. Therefore, you can (sort of) grind out enough cash to buy all the upgrades relatively early in the game. I did this unintentionally, just failing the same level over and over.
[*] I wish the game didn't have the pixelated breasts on the screens in the game. Not because I was offended, but because as far as I know, that's the only NSFW aspect of the game. Since Steam often censors NSFW games by default, fewer players are seeing this game than it deserves.
[*] Purchase the taser upgrade first. Although you don't need it much in the earlier levels, that extra charge will soon be a lifesaver.
[/list]

If you're a fan of this 2D style of stealth game (or you played Trilby: The Art of Theft and loved it), I'd recommend Moonshot. It's a little rough around the edges, but this sort of game isn't released very often.

Can't believe that I, an IT Specialist, paid to play IT Specialist Simulator.
First ticket was a wallpaper change. It's just as irritating in real life to deal with end users as it is in the game. 
Second ticket was a printer job, I wanted to quit immediately. 10/10 simulator, can confirm it's realistic.

If you work in IT, this game is very interesting and overall fun. If you do not work in IT, this is a very close simulator with things you have to deal with in a real working environment. 

However, it is incredibly buggy. Even with the sale, I do not think it is worth buying at the moment. For example, your PDF reader app stops working and you no longer can access any documentation you need to complete tasks if you do not have them memorized or screenshotted onto your computer. On day 2, you lose access to your email app on your desktop and rely on reading emails off your tablet. On day 3, your bootable pendrive has to be set up again because for some reason your pendrive wipes itself when you go into a new day. You set the correct address mapping for a printer, but the game doesn't recognize it, and you get penalized. You can't use the enter key on your numpad when trying to ping the router. If you change password requirements in the terminal, you have to do so in a specific order otherwise the terminal throws an invalid number error (even if you enter the correct number). The list goes on.

As for gameplay and not bugs, tasks repeat pretty frequently and sometimes interrupt what you are doing. For example, I'm working on someone's permission issue and the computer completely turns off and get a new tasks on the same computer saying that their TPM chip is messed up. There are no actual other NPCs walking around, so the game feels unalive / empty. You are doing these tasks and your rewards is advancing in your career, and maybe I didn't get around to the point in the game, but there are no ways to spend the money you are making. 

This game has potential to be fun and entertaining for those in the IT world, and informative to basic troubleshooting and networking to those outside the IT world. I was really looking forward to this game, but ultimately couldn't finish day 3 because of how buggy the game is. I had to stop playing once I found myself looking up if the things I were doing were reported bugs on the steam discussion pages.

Jeśli uwielbiasz serię „Ace Attorney”, chemię między postaciami, błyskotliwe dialogi, dramatyczne konfrontacje i dreszczyk emocji towarzyszący odkrywaniu prawdy. To „Stories from Sol: The Gun-Dog” wyda Ci się dziwnie znajome, i to w najlepszym możliwym sensie.

🚀 Ta sama energia „Aha!”, która towarzyszy odkrywaniu sprzeczności. Chociaż to nie jest Visual Novel z sali sądowej, narracja w stylu śledztwa i powolne odkrywanie prawdy zaspokajają tę samą potrzebę, co przekopywanie się przez zeznania świadków w „Ace Attorney”. Każda rozmowa wydaje się znacząca. Każdy szczegół wydaje się mieć znaczenie później.

👥 Jedną z przyjemności „Ace Attorney” jest nawiązywanie więzi z jego ekscentrycznymi, serdecznymi postaciami. „Stories from Sol” również to doskonale oddaje. Załoga Gun-Doga jest pełna osobowości, ciepła, pełna wad, zabawna i zaskakująco emocjonalna.

🛸 Fani Ace Attorney wiedzą, jak sceny potrafią w ciągu kilku sekund zmienić się z absurdalnej komedii w szczerą, pełną emocji opowieść. Ta Visaul Novel doskonale oddaje ten ton. W jednej chwili się śmiejesz, a w drugiej uderza cię cicha, emocjonalna kwestia, która zapada w pamięć.

📚 Podobnie jak w najlepszych sprawach w Ace Attorney, tempo akcji jest tu napięte. Bez wypełniaczy, bez zbędnych scen, bez zbędnych naświetleń. Po prostu mocna, wciągająca narracja, która szanuje Twój czas.

🌌 Stories from Sol: The Gun-Dog to pozycja obowiązkowa dla fanów powieści wizualnych, a szczególnie idealna dla każdego, kto uwielbia styl opowiadania historii Ace Attorney. Jest inteligentna, pełna emocji, dowcipna i pełna niezapomnianych momentów z udziałem bohaterów.

Jeśli lubisz odkrywać prawdę poprzez dialogi, nawiązywać więzi z sympatyczną obsadą i przeżywać emocjonującą zagadkę science fiction, rozważ tę powieść wizualną jako swoją kolejną świetną przygodę.

Hard to explain, but I enjoy the game. 
The core conceit is that it takes five minutes to play, unless you die earlier. This makes it a rather niche game I suspect, but it works for me.
The core concept is that you are humanities last hope, and trying to terraform planets to save the human race. The game mechanics are very simply, you  fly around looking for solar systems, which oddly enough consists of a bunch planets in he same orbit around a star, and look for planets worth using your limited supply of terraforming gas on. 
The information you get is limited, the population potential, and the percentage change of success. Completing the terraforming consists solely of holding down the left mouse button, nothing more. While on the planet however, it is worthwhile zipping around exploring it, as you can find repair nodules (red dots) and schematics for upgrades (boxes with question marks on them)  or alient artifacts.
There are times when you will drop down on to a planet you don't want to terraform to grab these, that is cool. 
The upgrades so far include better weapons, a speed boost, and faster terraforming. You need parts, little bolts dropped by one kind of enemy ship, to install.
The alien artifacts change basic factors in the game, and at the start of each game you get to pick one. So far I have seen one that makes you harder to detect and one that gives you more terraforming gas at the start. I think there are eight or ten total.
One of the things I like is that the things you find are persistent between games. 
One downside in my mind is there is no score. You do get a rundown of how your run was, including the percentage of humanity saved, which I uses as my own personal measure, but an actual score would be nice.
I have to give high marks to the visuals, the sense of 3-D, when it is there, is awesome. All of your flight and combat is on a 2-D plane, but zipping around the planets, and looking at the asteroids is top notch.
The sound is also pretty nice.
Another negative for me was the controls though, and I feel I need to mention this. The game allows for mouse and keyboard, or controller, but both feel awkward. In the end, I found learning mouse and key-board easier, but you will have to decide for yourself which you prefer. 
All in all though, a lot of fun. I suspect once it is beaten once or twice, it will quickly be uninstalled, but I am getting my moneys worth.

Dear Combat Cat Studio Team,

I want to start by saying I've invested a significant amount of time into your game—my hours and achievements on file reflect that dedication. It's clear from my play history that I've been a committed player, and I truly appreciate the engaging PvP mechanics and creative design elements that initially drew me in.

That said, I've noticed some concerning trends that seem to be impacting the overall health and enjoyment of the game for long-term players like myself. Player levels appear to be dropping steadily, which has led to frustrating experiences in matches. For instance, in 20v20 team games, it's becoming common to have fewer than 10 human opponents, with the rest filled by bots. Custom matches were a great addition to extend the game's longevity, but tying them so closely to premium purchases can feel limiting. 

Similarly, limited-time events like deathmatch are seeing queues stretch to two hours or more due to low player turnout, which diminishes the excitement and accessibility these modes are meant to provide.

These issues point to a broader challenge: sustaining an active, diverse player base. From my perspective as an English-speaking player, the official developer Discord could play a pivotal role in bridging community feedback to the development team, but it sometimes feels like certain voices or suggestions aren't being fully represented. For example, there's an emphasis on community events in platforms like VRChat, which, while fun, may not align as well with the core demographic interested in this PvP title—particularly when compared to established furry and art-focused communities. This shift can make the space feel less inclusive and more niche, potentially alienating players who thrive on larger, team-based interactions.

Additionally, the moderation approach in the English Discord has occasionally come across as overly restrictive for non-harmful feedback. Bans or removals for things like profile choices (e.g., AI-generated images) or perceived "annoyance" can discourage open discussion, especially on critical topics like game balance or event ideas. While I understand the need for a positive environment, fostering a space where constructive criticism is welcomed—even if it's tough—could help surface valuable insights that benefit everyone.

On a brighter note, the game's art and cosmetic direction shows real promise as a marketing strength. Outfits like the Halloween set, maid ensemble, and bikinis add a fun, appealing layer to character customization that resonates with many players. However, I've observed some inconsistency in how related feedback is handled in community channels—positive comments or innocent suggestions (e.g., adding stockings to a maid outfit) sometimes get moderated out, which might unintentionally stifle enthusiasm for these features and create friction between the creative team and the community. It gives the impression that the English speaking moderators feel ashamed of the obvious -- the characters are meant to be attractive, and wish to discourage it from being acknowledged positively by players.  This isn't a new art direction either, before the game even launched, the opening movies include one where a character is tied up in a questionable fashion with questionable camera angles. The studio, the actual developers, are trying to embrace this and have done so from the beginning. The community team should not be trying to discourage the very people who would by 90% of the thus-far released skins. I feel like they may want to consider abdicating their roles, as volunteers, if Marquez doing her shake emote makes them uncomfortable. Or if Akai Hime's voice lines, emotes, or outfits make them squirm? Same thing. Maybe not the discord or game you should filter feedback for. 

To help turn things around and revitalize player engagement, I'd love to see more targeted outreach to aligned communities. Partnering with popular art platforms like DeviantArt, Pixiv, or Weasyl could be a game-changer—perhaps by offering limited-time badges or rewards for playing during collaborative events. Collaborating with animal-themed VTubers and Twitch streamers is another strong avenue: providing them with keys to distribute, or custom promo codes tied to streamer-branded badges, could draw in fresh audiences and boost concurrent players during peak times.I'm sharing this feedback here because I care deeply about the game's potential and want to see it thrive. The English-speaking community team has a unique opportunity to amplify these ideas and help steer the game toward greater success. By creating a more open, inclusive feedback loop and focusing promotions on spaces that match the game's vibrant, furry-inspired vibe, you can rebuild momentum and keep dedicated players like me coming back for more. I have only seen the international team bothering to partner with "kemono" steamers thus far. Obviously they're willing, they just need the English speaking community moderators and volunteers to point them at a high-profile performer rather than personal friends.  

Now I do know steam guidelines require I not make accusations so I'll just say this; the game's official discord has a moderation log. It includes bans for Ai profile pictures. It includes bans for people being thirsty. It includes bans for being "annoying", and this is all verifiable fact so these aren't accusations, they're verifiable fact. Further, the VRchat community nights are also announced there to verify that claim as well. 

It's a shame but such a stifling environment makes me feel like I only have my game review as an option, or I contact my old gamedev friend from NEU and ask him if he can pass on my feedback and concerns, written in Chinese, to the rest of the development team. I prefer to see the English speaking community team do right by the developers and align with their goals, interests, and desires, however.

堅実な作りのゲームで十分に遊べはしますが、一部の点が足を引っ張っているのが残念なポイント。

[h3] 問題点 [/h3]

[list]
    [*]敵がやや硬い
　　一部のレビューで「敵が硬い」と指摘されていますが大体その通りです。
　　最も一般的な敵であるゲオルギーUSNのHPが88(難度ノーマル)に対し、ARの初期火力は一発8です。
　　つまり撃破に11発必要ですが、ゲオルギーのHS倍率は5倍なのでHSなら3発で倒せます。
　　要は弱点を狙えるかどうかで必要弾数が大きく変わる大味な調整なんです。
　　他にもロマノフN型はHP1500に対し、HSは2倍かつ282ダメージで頭部破壊（破壊後1分で自爆）できる、
　　ロマノフF型はHP1300に対し、背中のボンベは240ダメージで破壊（破壊すると即死）等の
　　知っているかどうかで大きく違うのに教えてくれない要素が多すぎます。
　　自分は公式ガイドブックを購入して知りましたが、できればゲーム内で教えてほしかった。
    [*]QTE
　　基本的にボスはHPを減らすとQTEが発生し、失敗すると即ゲームオーバーです。
　　失敗できるものも（わずかに）存在しますが、初見では失敗してみるまで区別はつきません。
　　雑魚にもQTEがあります。何なら上記のゲオルギーUSNもロマノフN型もQTEを持っています。
　　ゲオルギーは足を破壊すると使用（失敗すると即死）、ロマノフN型は掴まれると発生（失敗すると即死）
    [*]武器周りのシステム
　　弾薬が満タンの状態で同じ武器を拾うと階級ラインが1本増え、3本目で階級が上がり強化されます。
　　このシステムのせいで強化したい武器をしばらく温存しなければならず、好きな武器を使いにくい。
　　またゲーム開始時は初期状態のため、好きなステージからプレイを開始しづらくなっています。
　　ノーマル以上の難度ではコンテニュー時のペナルティで弱体化もあります。
　　（ノーマルでライン1本、ハードで階級1つ、ゴッドハードでは強化自体できません）
　　無条件に強化できるアイテムもドロップしますが、稀に拾えない位置にドロップします。
    [*]ボタン表記がXboxのみ
　　PS3でも販売されてましたよね？なんでPS表記が無いんですか？
[/list]

全体的に「ちょっと…」となる要素は多いのですが、致命的な不具合もなく軽く遊べるゲームです。
定価の¥2180では微妙ですが執筆時最安値の¥547くらいなら十分オススメできます。
繰り返しプレイするというよりは1週サクッと消化して次のゲームに行くのに向いてるカンジですね。

Invisible apartment is technically one (prohibitively short) VN, but is also the name of the series, with a prologue and two sequels being folded in as DLC to the original. It's recommended by the devs to buy the other games as DLC, so that's what I did, and I'll be reviewing all of them here together because of that.

The "presentation" or UX of this VN immediately stands out as...atrocious. It was made using a custom-designed engine for some unknown reason (Ren'py has been free and widely available for years, first created nearly 15 years ago according to Wikipedia), and lacks some really, [i]really[/i] basic features that I could put together in a freaking WinForm application in less than a day. These features include things like a "backlog," configuration settings (text speed, audio levels), skip/auto functionality...these are all extremely, extremely basic things that even other VNs using really rudimentary engines (like Himawari) support. About 10 minutes into the first story (IA 0) the game crashed on me repeatably, and I found through the forums that this was because of the music being on. I turned it off and never decided to turn it back on. You get a set of saves per game, but it's only six each--not enough to cover all of the choices available for the last two stories.

The art's a bit better than the standard for OELVNs. As you can see from the main page it's set in a futuristic world, so the clothing designs are usually interesting. The artist also clearly has a penchant for hair, because the main character goes through like 5 different styles (usually at least 2 (sometimes 3) during a story). It's a nice touch in a medium where a character frequently has one outfit, two if they have a route.

"Gameplay mechanics" are standard VN fare--you pick choices. It treats "wrong" choices very strangely however: during the earlier VNs (and possibly during the later ones, I didn't go through every permutation), when you pick a wrong choice you travel down that path for a little bit, then when it ends poorly you're immediately booted back to the point of the original choice, with the "right" choice already chosen for you. It's very disorienting. The story has a habit of disorienting scene shifts during the regular story as well. Speaking of which...

There are a few different elements to the story that are worth separating: the writing quality itself (things like grammar and syntax), the plot (or the sequence/design/logic of events that you go through), and then the "execution" of story elements or a character's portrayal.

The first is substandard ESL, and I apologize if that sounds harsh, but as a writer it's always been very obvious. It makes the experience feel stilted and a little unemotional. After a scene shift, frequently a character will painstakingly describe the process that brought them to their new location in a manner that doesn't at all fit an "internal monologue" a person might have.

The second is mediocre to poor. If you look at the entire plot across the series, it's made up of a bunch of actors putting each other into situations and then doing nothing when they're there. Entire swaths of time where a character has the ability to act, but does nothing. Their actions belie their motivations. The main character comes off as...I can't think of the word right now, but several times she takes an action and then, 5 minutes in real-world time, she goes back and does what she was avoiding with her first action. One character is said to have been "building a personal army," but they do absolutely nothing with this so-called army so this (also) feels half-baked. Spoilers here, but the entire "conflict" is resolved by a third party with no interaction with any of the "main" characters until the last 5 minutes or so of the final VN--he's acting largely of his own volition, and he has no reason whatsoever to resolve the conflict.

The final aspect, the portrayal of these events or characters, was okay. At one point a character spends a bit of time interacting with a surveillance AI in the shape of a parrot, and for some reason I found these sections pretty funny. Most character interactions feel okay, though a couple times they're deliberately molded to fit a plot contrivance and feel bad. The specifics of certain scenes also work okay-to-well, tying back to things (characters or events) across each VN.

All in all this was a very weak experience.

Playing this after WWE 2K22, I have to say — it’s still the best one in the series. I’ve enjoyed WWE 2K24 and WWE 2K25 very much, However there are still dispite it going in the right direction ,still many flaws and outdated gameplay:

✅ The Good:

- Chain wrestling makes a return.
- Massive roster.
- New hairstyles in the Creation Suite (especially happy they brought back some older ones).
- Graphics are really solid.
- The AI is a lot smarter now — they actually complete taunts before going for moves, etc.
- New game modes have been added and are a nice touch.

❌ The Bad:

- The Island content is limited to "next-gen" consoles — PC is next-gen too!

- Creation Suite limitations:
I’m pleading with 2K — please overhaul this mode. It’s extremely outdated, especially with the face scans and morphs. We need: More customization options, More hairstyles, More clothing options for female wrestlers, Fixes for attire parts that glitch based on hairstyles, Ability to customize in-game characters (hair, makeup, face paint, lip gloss, eyelashes, eyes, body morphs, etc.), This is such a core part of the game, and it’s overwhelmingly disappointing that after four games, there’s still no major improvement.

- Universe Mode:
What have the developers done here? Respectfully — it’s a mess. I want to build rivalries, pick actions, and shape stories. Instead, it’s repetitive, copy-paste matches with no triple-threat rivalries. Royal Rumble rivalries feel flat. They have all the tools to make this the best mode in the game — even better than Showcase. I want to feel like I’m running the company: booking surprise returns, hearing commentary react to comebacks or injuries. Please bring back custom promos — make them interactive! It doesn’t need voice acting, just immersion. You can do it, 2K. I believe in you.

- MyFaction:
Terrible. Full stop. Locked behind paywalls for “persona cards” that take forever to earn. It’s boring and pointless. We all wanted Road to WrestleMania (RTWM) — instead, we got this. Get rid of it. If you want monetization, just do a £10 battle pass for cosmetics — not this grindfest.

- Showcase:
It’s okay. I’m a hardcore women’s wrestling fan (as you can tell from my Creation Suite rant), but that one random ladder match for MITB? Easily the worst Showcase match. Not terrible overall, but please — more women’s matches next time.

- The Island (again):
Oh wait… we can’t even play it on PC. If you’re advertising a “new mode,” there should be a price difference if we can’t access it. I’ve watched gameplay and reviews — doesn’t look like we missed much though.

- MyRise:
First year I didn’t finish it. I just don’t like intergender wrestling — not because of the gender dynamic, but because it doesn’t happen in WWE now. Instead of two separate stories, they merged them lazily.
Here’s an idea, 2K: stop releasing yearly games and actually spend time making something inventive.

- AI improvements to matches and gameplay:
Managers are hopeless at supporting during matches. Please amend the rope-break animations so the referee can always see them, and stop the referee from colliding with a wrestler’s head during pin counts — the ref should get there in time to make the count. Make managers interfere more dynamically: have them interact with each other, perform shady actions at ringside, and play believable win/lose reactions (e.g., an animation of disbelief when their wrestler loses a pin). The Blue Box is six interesting game concepts compiled into a single package.  Every game in the Blue Box is simple to pick up and enjoy without enduring tutorials or pages of documentation.  Three of them feature Twitch IRC integration (Ostriches, Llama, and Snapshot) which make this a great purchase for streamers looking for something new and interesting to share and play with their viewers.

These are "game jam" games with time constraints and smaller teams but still manage to execute some fairly impressive technical feats and present some entertaining moments.  Oligocene Snapshot in particular is a promising Pokémon Snap clone for people who were disappointed that it was never followed up.  Further levels for that game are still in development but even in its current state it's fun to play.

The Blue Box is worth it for the variety of simple but fun game concepts on display, but it's also a great purchase for the aforementioned Twitch integration.  There's plenty to appreciate in this package.

German review, English below

Auf den ersten Blick wirkt das Spiel sehr süß und gemütlich. Und tatsächlich hat das Team sich offenbar sehr viel mit den Grafiken beschäftigt. Leider wurde meiner Meinung nach zu viel Zeit und Energie in den oberflächlichen Anschein gesteckt und zu wenig in die Story und Funktionalität. 
Das Spiel ist unglaublich langweilig, da man nicht mehr machen kann, als seine Energie in die Feldarbeit zu stecken, Tiere zu streicheln, ein paar Muscheln zu sammeln und einmal am Tag den zur Farm gehörenden Laden zu öffnen. Wozu der Angelsteg gedacht sein mag, erschließt sich mir nicht, denn man kann einfach nicht angeln in dem Spiel und auch sonst gibt es keine Abwechslung im tristen Farmalltag.
Die Steuerung ist bisweilen hakelig, die Hitboxen zu winzig. Schon im Tutorial wird erwähnt, dass es 'frickelig' werden kann, die richtigen Kacheln zu treffen, was einen wirklich stutzig werden lässt. Wieso weißt man als Entwickler in einer Vollversion darauf hin, dass die Steuerung schwierig ist und weist lieber eine Fokustaste  (zum vermutlich besseren Zielen) zu, statt dafür zu sorgen, dass die Steuerung wirklich problemlos funktioniert?
Die Beschreibungen für einige Feldpflanzen sind unvollständig und je nach Sprache heißen Saat, Pflanze und Frucht unterschiedlich. Die Lokalisierung war wohl auch nicht unbedingt weit oben auf der Liste, wenn solche Fehler mehr als einmal unterlaufen. 
Was die Story betrifft, beginnt sie eigentlich sehr interessant. Leider wurde auch hier gespart, denn es gibt keine nennenswerte Weiterentwicklung der Geschichte im Verlauf des Spiels. Die wenigen NPCs sind langweilig und ohne Tiefe. Interaktionen mit ihnen machen keinen Spaß und auch hier fehlt jede Entwicklung. Die wenigen Unterhaltungen, die ich mit ihnen geführt habe, waren flach und unergiebig. 
Die jeweils finale Belohnung für das Beenden einer der Tierinseln (Wieso ist hier die Rede von einzelnen Inseln, wenn man auf der Insel strandet und es kein Fortkommen gibt?) ist nicht viel wert. Es gibt eine Auszeichnung (Steam), einen Brief, der einem das Offensichtliche (nämlich, dass man die Tierinsel vollständig von den Dornen befreit hat) mitteilt und dann kann man sich dort niederlassen und, während dort eine Schleifenanimation läuft, auf's Klo gehen, Tee kochen, Abendessen zubereiten, Wäsche aufhängen... Beendet man diese Animation schließlich hat man lediglich echte Zeit totgeschlagen oder im besten Fall irgendetwas Sinnvolleres getan, als sich die Animation wieder und wieder anzuschauen. 
Die Musik ist zwar nett anzuhören, jedoch weiß ich nicht, ob mir das Hauptthema des Harvest Moon/Story of Season - A Wonderful Life Soundtracks in dem Kontext wirklich zusagt (das Spiel hatte schon vor über 20 Jahren weit mehr Tiefe als dieses hier). 

Fazit: sehr schön gestaltetes Spiel, wenn mal gar nicht mitdenken und/oder Zeit totschlagen will.

English:
At first glance, the game seems very cute and cozy. And indeed, the team has obviously put a lot of effort into the graphics. Unfortunately, in my opinion, too much time and energy was spent on superficial appearances and too little on the story and functionality. 
The game is incredibly boring, as there is nothing more to do than put your limited energy into field work, pet animals, collect a few shells and open the farm shop once a day. I don't understand what the fishing pier is for, because you simply can't fish in the game, and there is no other variety in the dreary everyday farm life.
The controls are sometimes clunky and the hitboxes are too small. Even in the tutorial, it is mentioned that it can be “fiddly” to hit the right tiles, which really makes you wonder. Why would a developer point out in a full version that the controls are difficult and assign a focus key (presumably for better aiming) instead of making sure that the controls work smoothly?
The descriptions for some field plants are incomplete, and depending on the language, seeds, plants, and fruits have different names. Localization was probably not high on the list of priorities either, given that such errors occur more than once. 
As far as the story goes, it actually starts off very interestingly. Unfortunately, corners were cut here too, as there is no significant development of the story over the course of the game. The few NPCs are boring and lack depth. Interacting with them is no fun, and here too, there is no development whatsoever. The few conversations I had with them were shallow and unproductive. 
The final reward for completing one of the animal islands (why are we talking about individual islands when you are stranded on the island and there is no way forward?) is not worth much. There is an award (Steam), a letter telling you the obvious (namely, that you have completely cleared the animal island of thorns), and then you can settle down there and, while a looping animation plays, go to the bathroom, make tea, prepare dinner, hang up laundry... When you finally finish this animation, you've just wasted real time or, at best, done something more meaningful than watching the animation over and over again. 
The music is nice to listen to, but I'm not sure if I really like the main theme of the Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons - A Wonderful Life soundtrack in this context (the game had far more depth than this one over 20 years ago). 

Conclusion: beautifully designed game for when you feel like playing without thinking and / or feel the need to kill some time.

🦖 Динозавры в кубиках
- В обычном ARK динозавры выглядят грозно и реалистично.  
- В PixARK они похожи на милые фигурки LEGO, которые всё равно хотят тебя съесть.  
- Ты приручаешь их не ради выживания, а ради того, чтобы твой кубический Т-Рекс выглядел круче, чем у соседа.  

⛏️ Кубический крафт
- Строишь базу? Отлично. Только теперь твоя «супер-крепость» выглядит как домик из детского конструктора.  
- Но не переживай: кубический дизайн делает даже провалившийся проект выглядящим «стильно минималистично».  

🤯 Сложность
- Игра обещает «выживание», но на деле ты чаще умираешь от того, что забыл поесть, чем от динозавров.

- Это ARK, но в стиле «детский сад».

Got my hands on the game and here are my thoughts with things I would like to see at the end.

Music is there but nothing to brag about as of yet. Outside of banger theme we heard in the trailer. 

The gameplay is very intuitive but a flawed. We get a random map and set up our units. Each unit will have different stats like initiative (when they act), movement range and attack range. 
We move cute chibis on the map and engage in 1v1 combat where we see full sprites and lots of fan service (I approve)
So far, the units are NOT created equal. I already cheesed some hard maps with setting up 2 soldiers in a choke point backed up by medic. But the clear winner so far is the, I think her name was bullwark. Tough to kill and she will 1 shot you if you dare to sit anywhere near water, ledge or any other hole. She will push you into it and insta kill your beloved grunts. And once a unit bites the dust it's over for them for the entire run.... along with their artifacts (just had to kick the man while he was down, huh?)
AI is rutheless. And I mean it. It will go after your units and set you up for big AOE attacks. The saving grace so far is that the AI does not really use ultimate commander skills which can help but again they are not game winning (unless you manage to pop off PUNKZ ultimate and start one shotting everything). 
I think I lost 3 first runs. Well it is a roguelike but it still stung. 

So, with all that said I can recommend the game, just make sure you are ready for difficult battles. Oh and if you dare to approach sth called "deadly battle" then understand before hand that difficulty spike is vertical. As a veteran of Project Moon I sorta approve though I initially expected a casual game.

1. Difficulty modes, with such gorgeous art style you are bound to draw casuals, doubt they will stick around after getting their ass handed to them
2. Random enemy. At this point I choose my opponent, I would like to be surprised, though that can come later since there aint many factions for now 
3. A crazy game mode. Look, not sure if it can work but hear me out: what if we make the map bigger, remove artifacts or I dunno make some tech tree and pit all factions against one another. Like, player selects one faction and all the others settle in some remote points of the map. Then AI and Player take turns and try to take over other territories. Initially maps could be just gray, occupied by random mercs, once a faction takes hold of it they can defend it with their main army, a little bit like campaign in Dawn of War Dark Crusade

6. Let me check enemy abilities, it's a bit painful to learn how units act the hard way so I would like to click and see what they can do (unless I missed it, then sorry)
7. let me check my units, I keep forgeting which artifact is on which soldier
8. remind me to check if I geared up before battle or let me put artifacts after I enter the map in the setting up phase 
9. Explain what buildings do, yes you highlighted that they are important but I dont know why, then enemy captures medic base and they heal like crazy each turn
10. For the love of all that is holy: let me attack after I move or let me cancel an action, I keep moving first expecting I can shoot someone but my turn ends after unit finishes moving, pissed me off the first few runs

The first true bullet-hell (aka “danmaku”) arcade twin-stick shooter, a masterclass in design, and a new standard for the genre…If you can stomach it. 
———————-

Please note that while I was a playtester for over a year for this game, I decided to have my game key rescinded so I could buy the game.  All of my thoughts on the game I will share free of any bias. I’m not affiliated with the dev nor do I benefit in any way; the dev was kind enough to let me be a playtester and listen to my endless and annoying feedback, so now here I am to tell you exactly what I think of Sektori

Also note that my positives and negatives may not apply for everyone, they’re simply my opinions to do my best to help you decide if the game is for you. 
————————————————————
POSITIVES:

✅ Not a Geometry Wars clone but evokes a familiar feel while providing a legitimate, unbroken campaign arcade run instead of levels, tying it closer to real arcade design. Think Kill Knight or Nex Machina. 

✅ Maybe the first arcade run-based twin stick shooter with true forward progression.  In most twin sticks, the game doesn’t progress forward until you clear all enemies in a wave. In Sektori, the game continuously progresses and spawns new enemies like a scrolling shoot-em-up whether you’re killing or not.  Again, this creates more legitimate arcade design. You can’t just turtle and run around enemies. 

✅ True forward progression also means true snowball-based design. Because enemies spawn without being stopped by wave based soft locks,  enemies and enemy attacks pile up more and more, forcing the player to constantly act and strategize in dynamic ways.  In fact, sektori has some of the best executed snowball based design in all of gaming and warrants study. 

✅ The game isn’t afraid to introduce soft and hard “checkmate” scenarios, but they never feel cheap, which is incredibly hard to pull off in a game this dense.  What this means is like in chess, the game is not afraid to put the player into extremely tight scenarios that can lead to getting hit or losing the run.  In soft checkmates, you get put into brutal dodge scenarios but can potentially dodge your way out with enough skill and reading the enemies intelligently enough in the moment.  Hard checkmates occur when you’re essentially forced into a hit that you can’t avoid. Both types never feel cheap because they typically involve either a cascading series of many small decision making mistakes, or ~1-3 fatal ones in a succession.  The game gives you a recharging invulnerable explosive dash that often helps with soft checkmates, but hard checkmates often involve being forced to use your dash and then still in a situation to get hit before it restores.  

 ✅ Because the game is so dense with enemies, the explosive dash is perhaps the best example of an invulnerable dash so far.  It never really feels like it invalidates the enemy or bullet pattern design but acts as an open-ended tool to help manage the onslaught.  Very rarely does it feel like there’s an obvious time and place to use it. Immense accomplishment there as most invulnerable dashes in games like this get used in more scripted “dash here now” ways. 

✅ Easily the best bosses seen in the genre yet. If they seem too easy at first, keep playing and you will see their potential. The bosses tow an elegant line between mixing dynamic and linear patterns, while also putting the player in tricky checkmate scenarios if you aren’t careful that can both frustrate and make you smile for being so precisely done to create those scenarios.  Legitimate and brutal bosses have never been done like this for the twin stick genre. 

✅ Plentiful modes to keep you busy with a robust leaderboard system. Leaderboards are separated by which ship and mode you use. There’s even an optional fork in the campaign mode- you can play a standard campaign with or an “arcade campaign”. The arcade campaign removes the optional roguelite perk system. Both forks have a separate scoring tab.  

✅ Some of the best useof RNG in arcade games ever. The optional rogue lite perks don’t make the game feel like a rogue lite due to how the perks are balanced and allow for some freedom of control on how they appear. You select which perks will appear, somewhat like a pre-run loadout system. The enemy waves spawn in familiar but slightly randomized ways that makes each run unique, but not to the point that scoring meta feels intangible or random.  The RNG cascades on itself in ways over the 40 minute run time in ways that don’t really allow luck to be a factor, memorization becomes secondary to pure skill, and each run truly does feel familiar yet different in a way that creates beatifully rich and deep snowballing gameplay. The RNG is also kept in check by the level design.  Every now and then the arena changes shape/size, and all enemies out of bounds die, which prevents snowball RNG from becoming too random.  

✅ Insane skill ceiling and replay value.  Clearing the game on hardest settings in all modes will push even seasoned gamers to their limits. Don’t be surprised to expect dozens if not hundreds of hours for the hardest clear.  The scoring meta is rich and only extends the difficulty more.  If you could only choose one twin stick to live with forever, this would be in my opinion the one to choose. 

—————————-
NEGATIVES (please note these may be subjective and may not apply to everyone)

💔 Doesn’t commit enough to its aesthetic.  The art style and overall look of the game pops beautifully and looks great. It just doesn’t commit enough aesthetically.  Its style is kind of like geometry wars with a moody/mysterious or even subtly ominous or edgy undertone, but it plays its own style too safe in fear of looking too busy and loses some of its emotional pull. We need MOAR MOOD. GRUNGE. MYSTIQUE. 

💔 Randomized song and background order was in my opinion a tragically poor artistic decision. Some tracks do appear at certain points, and the stages do alter their visuals some, but on the whole, the music tracks and art backdrops (which look awesome) are largely randomized. This doesn’t give the players enough emotional hooks or identity to latch onto.  The full OST itself has a clearly defined emotional identity as it transitions from track to track, and that’s hurt by the randomized song order. 

💔 Easiest difficulty is perhaps a tad too hard. This is more of a warning than an a negative criticism and not an issue for me specifically, and may not be an issue for you. Just be warned that even on the easy difficulty, it is still a very dense and busy game as the game is designed around a super high enemy density.  I think the easy mode could have been a bit less dense just to ease players into the game more. 

💔 Some minor visual inconsistencies. There’s a player hurtbox viewer (awesome), but at times it can be hard to see depending on your ship color and hurtbox color you choose due to the animation of the ship/shield.  There are options to customize your ship, but there could be more options here I think.  The text for the UI is also painfully generic to me and attempts to give the game a mature feeling, but over time it sort of makes the game feel more lifeless when it feels like it needed more aesthetic intensity and boldness.  
 
💔 Some enemy spawn design could be improved. Minibosses and arena size/shape changes are not utilized to their full potential to create more bold and memorable set pieces as the game could have.  Overall excellent but there was room to push the envelope here, especially with miniboss spawn design as they’re usually spawned in the same way. Would have liked to see more moments where the arena becomes small for extended periods and/or used more creatively. 
————————

Overall: 9 to 9.5. Absolutely incredible game that sets a new benchmark for the genre on almost all fronts.  If you give it enough time to sink its hooks, there’s a strong chance you’ll agree it’s the best twin stick ever.

Sektori is a maddeningly good arcade twin-stick shooter the likes of which we rarely get to see.  Top-tier action and design, with fun nooks and crannies, a lot to pay attention to, and several play modes.  This is a core, gameplay-first type of game, and it deserves to be experienced by any arcade-style twin-stick fans, but especially those wanting an intense, high-engagement experience (and not just because the developer and their testers have no concept of what lower difficulty feels like or is for ;).

So, several modes to unlock (including the old Geometry Wars passive mode where you trigger exploding gates instead of any shooting), three ship types, and various modifiers (for the "classic" side mode) and upgrades (for the main, campaign mode).  You do have to pass the first boss to be allowed to unlock more, and that is no trivial feat, as the lowest difficulty is still pretty bonkers and bosses here come directly from hell as far as I can tell, but after that hurdle, the path to side mode unlocks is pretty friendly (you basically just need to play a new side mode to unlock the next side mode), and at least you don't get the same boss every time in campaign (always a nice feature to see) so maybe you'll get one of the less-savage ones sometime...  The ship types do seem like restrictive unlocks though, and mutators require accumulating achievements, which becomes hard to add to quite quickly.  I expect a good number of players won't get to enjoy all the toys the game has to offer, simply because the dev closed the gates on them (for reference, check the "Transcendent" achievement for stats on how many buyers have all three ships unlocked).  That said, apparently there's some konami code nonsense thrown in one can use to skip the unlocking, but I don't know if it has other consequence yet.

Also, while there are some roguelite-style aspects to play with via upgrade "decks" there is also the option for pure arcade runs.  Upgrade decks are sixteen preset card trios (half start unlocked, the rest come fairly easily from achievements), and you take exactly eight into a campaign run to draw from when you catch evolution powerups in a variation on the ever-invasive pick three gimmick.  Note that cards don't repeat here, though, so while you can randomly get "rare" card versions with different stats, your decks offer a fixed set of upgrades that come in a varying order, not an unlimited/ever-increasing power stack.  Rather inexplicably, "arcade" mode is triggered not by selection but by manually discarding each of your available decks instead of taking upgrades, which takes three evolutions to accomplish, so it's a very strange option, but it's fully supported by the game, with its own leaderboard (and that's without even offering separate leaderboards for the three difficulties despite the huge run differences).  Of course, arcade mode is quite tough since you just throw away your bonus upgrades and then play the same game.

On caveats, I've never liked the Gradius style upgrade system, where upgrade pickups are like currency, increasing your available upgrade tier until you "activate" the upgrade to take what comes from that tier.  I dislike it especially because people [i]always[/i] put speed on the first tier and start with deliberately crippled movement, so you waste time and upgrade points getting the appropriate baseline movement just to play the game and otherwise it's a dead option you have to pay to build past every single upgrade, which just feels lame on both counts.  Sektori is no different on that, but it's a minor pain point when the rest of the game is such sheer fun, and I have to give credit that making activating an upgrade recharge your slam attack is a brilliant little touch to pull activation into the action.

I don't know what possesses a dev to dedicate such effort to making a game [i]this[/i] good in such a niche space, but I'm so grateful we get the occasional crazy to cast another gem.  Pay them, and don't forget to grab your upgrades, especially some speed.

I wish there was a mixed option instead of just positive/negative on Steam. Fatal Falls is an indie psychological horror game with a lot of ambition, but unfortunately, its execution falls short in some areas (no pun intended). While it has an intriguing premise and some moments of genuine tension, for instance in the sewers-like chapter, the game has a few issues.

1. Puzzles
Some are well-designed and even embedded in well-written dialogues, but others rely too much on backtracking or finding tiny, hard-to-spot details in dimly lit environments.

2. Inventory
The way items are handled is clunky. Certain objects don’t save correctly across chapters, and using something like a battery for the camcorder feels like it was tacked on rather than a meaningful survival mechanic.

3. Performance
The game runs smoothly in some areas but chugs in others, especially during the later chapters. It feels unoptimized, with occasional stuttering and frame drops despite good hardware.

Fatal Falls has potential, but it feels like a game that’s trying too hard to be deep without refining the core gameplay. The horror elements are undercut by tedious puzzles. However, if you love psychological horror, a decent story and are patient enough to deal with its flaws, you might find something worth experiencing.
